entries.summary: Mutable Water, ruled by Jupiter/Neptune—dissolution, compassion, and mystical union.
entries.description:
Pisces, the Fishes, is mutable Water ruled traditionally by Jupiter (and in the modern scheme by Neptune)—the final sign, of dissolution, compassion, imagination, and mystical union. In 777 it corresponds to the letter Qoph and the path of the Tarot trump The Moon (path 29), the dark journey through illusion and the deep before dawn. It governs the boundless, the sacrificial, and the return of all things to their source.

The two fishes bound and swimming in opposite directions figure the tension of soul and body, spirit and matter, ever pulling apart yet joined—the last lesson of the wheel before it begins again. Pisces’ gift is empathy, devotion, and visionary art; its shadow, escapism and self-loss. As the closing sign it dissolves the year’s forms back into the ocean of potential.

10-iklil.summary: al-Iklil, 'the crown' — the diadem on the Scorpion's brow, the lunar mansion at Libra.
10-iklil.description: al-Iklil, 'the crown,' is the arc of stars on the forehead of Scorpio, the Mansion of the Moon set in 777 in the path of Libra (Lamed). A station of dignity and of binding, it was read as favourable for love and for the laying of foundations, and as potent in works of constraint — the regal circlet poised above the Scorpion's dangerous heart.
tables: CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon

10-jabhah.summary: Jabhah (10° sub-position) — the 'Lion's Forehead' lunar mansion at its earlier-degree station on the Cheth/Cancer path.
10-jabhah.description: In Crowley's table CLXXIV the lunar mansions are sometimes listed at multiple sub-degrees within the same zodiacal path, reflecting the manzil's spread across more than one decanic sub-division. '10° Jabhah' is the earlier-degree station of the ninth Arabic lunar mansion Jabhah (Lion's Forehead, anchored on Regulus), placed at the 10° mark of the Cheth/Cancer path. The mansion itself is treated in full under the canonical Jabhah entry; this slug records the additional 10° sub-position. See also: Jabhah, Lion's Forehead.
tables: CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon

10-saad-al-sa-ad.summary: Sa'd al-Sa'ud (10° sub-position) — 'Luck of Lucks' at its earlier-degree station on the Ayin/Capricorn path.
10-saad-al-sa-ad.description: '10° Sa'd al-Sa'ud' is the earlier-degree station of the twenty-fourth Arabic lunar mansion Sa'd al-Sa'ud — the 'Luck of Lucks,' the most beneficent of the four 'luck' mansions of the winter sector. It is placed at the 10° mark of the Ayin/Capricorn path; the canonical 30° entry carries the full description. See also: Sa'd al-Sa'ud (30°), Luck of Lucks.
tables: CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon

10-suraya.summary: al-Thurayya, 'the abundant one' — the Pleiades, the most celebrated of the lunar mansions.
10-suraya.description: Among the most beloved of the twenty-eight mansions, al-Thurayya is the shimmering cluster of the Pleiades, 'the abundant' or 'the many,' set by Crowley in the path of Aries (Heh). Across cultures this glittering seven-fold knot of stars has signified plenty, gathering, and the seed-multitude; the Arab astrologers counted it a mansion of increase, of fortune in trade, and of the flourishing of all things sown. Its soft fire is fecundity made visible in the night sky.
tables: CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon

20-fargh-the-former.summary: Fargh the Former (20° sub-position) — the lunar mansion at its earlier-degree station on the Tzaddi/Aquarius path.
20-fargh-the-former.description: '20° Fargh the Former' is the earlier-degree station of the lunar mansion Al-Fargh al-Awwal (الفرغ الأول, 'the first/former emptying'), one of the great square-of-Pegasus mansions (marked by α and β Pegasi) sometimes attached to the Aquarian portion of the lunar zodiac. The canonical entry at 30° carries the description; this slug records the additional 20° sub-position on the Tzaddi/Aquarius path. See also: Fargh the Former (30°), Fargh the Latter.
tables: CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon

20-hakah.summary: Hak'ah (20° sub-position) — the small-group lunar mansion in the head of Orion, on the Vav/Taurus path.
20-hakah.description: '20° Hak'ah' (الهقعة, 'the white spot') is a sub-position entry for the fifth Arabic lunar mansion Hak'ah, marked by the three stars of Orion's head (λ, φ¹, φ² Orionis) — the small bright cluster from which the constellation rises. In traditional mansion-magic Hak'ah governs the favour of friends, the safe return of travellers, and the prospering of voyages. Crowley fixes it at the 20° mark of the Vav/Taurus path. The canonical Hak'ah entry (if any) carries the principal description.
tables: CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon

20-sarfah.summary: Sarfah (20° sub-position) — the eleventh lunar mansion (at the lion's hind quarters), on the Teth/Leo path.
20-sarfah.description: '20° Sarfah' is the earlier-degree station of the eleventh Arabic lunar mansion Sarfah (الصرفة, 'the changer/turner'), marked by β Leonis (Denebola) at the tail-end of Leo. In mansion-magic the 'turning' refers to the season-pivot the mansion marks; its influence is associated with the breaking of patterns, separations, and partings. The canonical 30° entry carries the full description. See also: Sarfah (30°).
tables: CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon

20-shaulah.summary: al-Shaula, 'the sting' — the raised tail of the Scorpion, the lunar mansion in Scorpio.
20-shaulah.description: al-Shaula, 'the sting' (the upcurved stinger of the Scorpion), is the Mansion of the Moon set in the path of Scorpio (Nun). An emphatically martial and dangerous station, it was reckoned potent in works of strife, siege, and binding — the venomous point at the end of the Scorpion's tail.
tables: CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon

30-fargh-the-former.summary: al-Fargh al-Muqaddam, 'the former spout' — the upper mouth of the Urn, in Pisces.
30-fargh-the-former.description: al-Fargh al-Muqaddam, 'the first (upper) spout' of the great Bucket or Urn (two corners of the Square of Pegasus), is the Mansion of the Moon set in 777 in the path of Pisces (Qoph). The 'spouts' pour out the celestial waters; this former one was read as a station of union and of increase, and as potent in works that bind and join.
tables: CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon

30-hak-ah.summary: al-Haq'a, 'the white spot' — the lunar mansion at the head of Orion, in Gemini.
30-hak-ah.description: al-Haq'a, 'the white spot' or whorl, is the small triangle at the head of Orion, counted as a Mansion of the Moon and placed by 777 in the path of Gemini (Zayin). The Arab astrologers held it a station of hunting and of the binding of tongues and affections, its airy, dexterous nature consonant with the mutable-air sign of the Twins.
tables: CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon

30-iklil.summary: Iklil (30° sub-position) — the 'Crown' lunar mansion at its later-degree station on the Nun/Scorpio path.
30-iklil.description: '30° Iklil' is the later-degree station of the seventeenth Arabic lunar mansion Iklil ('the Crown'), at the 30° mark of the Nun/Scorpio path. The mansion itself is described in full under the canonical Iklil entry (and its English gloss 'Horns of Scorpio'); this slug records the additional sub-position. See also: Iklil (10°), Horns of Scorpio.
tables: CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon

30-jabhah.summary: al-Jabha, 'the forehead' — the brow of the Lion about Regulus, the lunar mansion in Leo.
30-jabhah.description: al-Jabha, 'the forehead of the Lion,' is the sickle of stars crowning Leo (its brightest, Regulus, being the Lion's heart), the Mansion of the Moon set in the path of Leo (Teth). A station of royal and forceful character, it was held to favour love, building, and the strengthening of dominion — the solar majesty of the Lion concentrated in its lifted brow.
tables: CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon

30-sa-ad-al-sa-ad.summary: Sa'd al-Su'ud, 'the luck of lucks' — the most fortunate of all the lunar mansions, in Aquarius.
30-sa-ad-al-sa-ad.description: Sa'd al-Su'ud, 'the luckiest of the lucky,' is the most auspicious of the twenty-eight mansions, set in 777 in the path of Aquarius (Tzaddi). Rising with the softening of winter, it was the great mansion of goodwill, marriage, alliance, and flourishing — a station under which all undertakings were held to prosper, the very crown of the four Fortunes.
tables: CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon

30-sarfah.summary: al-Sarfa, 'the changer' — Denebola, herald of the turning season, the lunar mansion at Virgo.
30-sarfah.description: al-Sarfa, 'the changer of the weather' (Denebola, in the Lion's tail), is the mansion set in 777 in the path of Virgo (Yod); its heliacal rising and setting were held to turn the seasons and break the summer heat. The old astrologers reckoned it a station of cutting and severance — good for the pulling down of what must end and the harvesting of what is ripe.
tables: CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon

30-shaulah.summary: Shaulah (30° sub-position) — the 'Tail of Scorpio' lunar mansion at its later-degree station on the Samekh/Sagittarius path.
30-shaulah.description: '30° Shaulah' is the later-degree station of the eighteenth Arabic lunar mansion Shaulah ('the raised tail'), at the 30° mark of the Samekh/Sagittarius path — the point at which the scorpion's sting gives way to the archer's bow on the great wheel. The mansion is described in full under the canonical Shaulah entry (and its English gloss 'Tail of Scorpio'). See also: Shaulah (20°), Tail of Scorpio.
tables: CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon

30-suraya-dabaran.summary: Suraya / Dabaran (30° sub-position) — the Pleiades and Aldebaran, taken together at their later-degree station on the Vav/Taurus path.
30-suraya-dabaran.description: '30° Suraya. Dabaran' is the later-degree station combining two of the most famous fixed-star markers in the lunar zodiac: Ath-Thurayya (الثريا, 'the chandelier' — the Pleiades) and Al-Dabaran (الدبران, 'the follower' — Aldebaran, α Tauri). Both fall in the Taurean section, the Pleiades at the bull's shoulder and Aldebaran at his eye, and the mansion-tradition treats them in close succession. The canonical entries (the-pleiades, alldeboran) carry the full descriptions; this slug records the combined 30° sub-position on the Vav/Taurus path. See also: the Pleiades, Alldeboran.
tables: CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon

a-bag-in-his-hand.summary: Detail of the magical image of the 1st decan of Aquarius: a bag held in the hand.
a-bag-in-his-hand.description: ‘A bag in his hand’ is a detail of the magical image of the ascendant (first) decan of Aquarius—‘A man with bowed head, and a bag in his hand’—from the classical decan tradition in Liber 777. The bag signifies the keeping, carrying, or distribution of goods, an emblem of resource and exchange suited to the social, gathering nature of the water-bearer. The full figure served as a talismanic image ruling ten degrees of the zodiac.
tables: CXLIX. Magical Images of the Decans (Ascendent)

a-bearded-ancient-seen-in-profile.term: A bearded ancient seen in profile
a-bearded-ancient-seen-in-profile.displayTerm: A bearded ancient seen in profile
a-bearded-ancient-seen-in-profile.summary: Liber 777's design for the Fool (Aleph): a bearded ancient seen in profile.
a-bearded-ancient-seen-in-profile.description: In Liber 777's column of ‘Correct Design of the Tarot Trumps,’ the image set at the path of Aleph—Atu 0, the Fool—is ‘A bearded ancient seen in profile.’ The figure carries the paradox of the trump: the numberless beginning shown not as a youth but as the Ancient of Days, for the pure spirit that steps into the void is at once the oldest and the youngest of things, alpha and omega in a single face. Seen in profile, he looks ever onward, the eternal wanderer whose folly is the highest wisdom and whose every step is a fresh creation.
tables: CLXXXI. Correct Design of Tarot Trumps

a-beautiful-naked-man.summary: Magical image of Yesod: a beautiful naked man, strong and vital.
a-beautiful-naked-man.description: ‘A beautiful naked man’ (the full image adds ‘very strong’) is the magical image of Yesod, the ninth Sephirah, the Foundation, sphere of the Moon. Yesod is the seat of the vital and generative forces, the astral foundation upon which the material world rests, and its image is the beautiful, powerful, naked figure—the body of vitality and the reproductive power of nature laid bare. He embodies the lunar, fertile energy that gathers all the higher influences and transmits them into manifestation.
tables: CXX. Magical Images of the Sephiroth

a-beautiful-naked-woman.summary: Magical image of Netzach: a beautiful naked woman.
a-beautiful-naked-woman.description: ‘A beautiful naked woman’ is the magical image of Netzach, the seventh Sephirah, Victory, the sphere of Venus. Netzach is the realm of desire, instinct, feeling, and natural beauty, and its image is the unveiled goddess of love—the magnetic, alluring power of nature that draws all things toward union. She is Venus made visible, the principle of attraction and emotional force that animates the lower, personal triad of the Tree.
tables: CXX. Magical Images of the Sephiroth

a-beautiful-woman-with-her-two-horses.term: A beautiful woman with her two horses
a-beautiful-woman-with-her-two-horses.displayTerm: A beautiful woman with her two horses
a-beautiful-woman-with-her-two-horses.summary: Magical image of the 1st decan of Gemini: a beautiful woman with her two horses.
a-beautiful-woman-with-her-two-horses.description: ‘A beautiful woman with her two horses’ is the magical image of the ascendant (first) decan of Gemini, drawn from the classical decan tradition transmitted through Picatrix and Agrippa into Liber 777. The two horses fittingly echo the twin nature of Gemini, the sign of pairs and duality, while the beautiful woman who governs them embodies the airy, mutable grace of the sign. Such decan images were used as talismanic figures, each ruling ten degrees of the zodiac.
tables: CXLIX. Magical Images of the Decans (Ascendent)

a-beautiful-woman-wreathed-with-myrtle-s.term: A beautiful woman wreathed with myrtle. She holds a lyre
a-beautiful-woman-wreathed-with-myrtle-s.displayTerm: A beautiful woman wreathed with myrtle. She holds a lyre
a-beautiful-woman-wreathed-with-myrtle-s.summary: Magical image of the 2nd decan of Cancer: a myrtle-wreathed woman holding a lyre.
a-beautiful-woman-wreathed-with-myrtle-s.description: ‘A beautiful woman wreathed with myrtle, she holds a lyre and sings of love and gladness’ is the magical image of the succedent (second) decan of Cancer in the classical decan tradition gathered into Liber 777. Myrtle is the plant of Venus and love, and the lyre and song of gladness express the tender, joyful, musical mood of this watery decan. As with all the decan figures, the image served as a talismanic emblem ruling its ten degrees of the zodiac.
tables: CL. Magical Images of the Decans (Succedent)

a-black-crane-with-a-sore-throat-he-flut.term: A black crane with a sore throat - he flutters
a-black-crane-with-a-sore-throat-he-flut.displayTerm: A black crane with a sore throat - he flutters
a-black-crane-with-a-sore-throat-he-flut.summary: The magical image of Naberius — a fluttering black crane with a hoarse voice — Goetic Marquis of the third decan of Scorpio.
a-black-crane-with-a-sore-throat-he-flut.description: Naberius (Cerberus, Naberus), the twenty-fourth spirit of the Goetia and a valiant Marquis, appears as a black crane (in some accounts a three-headed dog) that flutters restlessly about the circle, speaking with a hoarse and raucous voice. In 777 he rules the third decan of Scorpio by day. He makes men cunning in all arts and sciences, especially rhetoric, and restores lost dignities and honours. The hoarse, agitated bird of black plumage fitly haunts the deep, secretive final face of the Scorpion, where reputation is lost and won again.

a-calf.summary: Detail of the magical image of the 3rd decan of Taurus: a calf among the beasts.
a-calf.description: ‘A calf’ is a detail of the magical image of the cadent (third) decan of Taurus—‘A swarthy man with white lashes, his body elephantine with long legs; with him a horse, a stag, and a calf’—from the classical decan tradition in Liber 777. The calf, young of the bull, is a fitting beast for the earthy sign of Taurus, one of the herd of animals attending the strange composite figure. The full image served as a talismanic figure ruling ten degrees of the zodiac.
tables: CLI. Magical Images of the Decans (Cadent)

a-calf-s-rides-on-viper.term: a calf s. Rides on viper
a-calf-s-rides-on-viper.displayTerm: a calf s. Rides on viper

a-child.summary: Magical image of Tiphareth: a child (also a king, a sacrificed god).
a-child.description: ‘A child’ is one of the magical images of Tiphareth, the solar centre of the Tree, given as ‘a majestic king, a child, and a sacrificed god.’ The child is the newborn or reborn divine son—innocence, fresh life, and the promise of the future—the Holy Child who is the harmonised self at its dawning. With the king and the sacrificed god it completes the threefold solar mystery: the god who is born, who reigns, and who dies and rises at the heart of the cosmos.
tables: CXX. Magical Images of the Sephiroth

a-conventional-figure-of-justice-with-sc.term: A conventional figure of Justice with scales
a-conventional-figure-of-justice-with-sc.displayTerm: A conventional figure of Justice with scales
a-conventional-figure-of-justice-with-sc.summary: The magical image of Adjustment (Atu VIII)—the figure of Justice with sword and scales, the perfect balance of Libra.
a-conventional-figure-of-justice-with-sc.description: This image—a figure of Justice holding the balanced scales, often with an upright sword—is the magical figure of the trump Adjustment (the older Justice), attributed to the letter Lamed and the sign Libra. The scales weigh every act and its consequence with absolute precision, while the sword stands ready to enforce the verdict; together they declare the cosmic law of exact equilibrium, that every action is answered by its due and that truth is the perfect balance of opposing weights. Libra is the cardinal-air sign of equipoise, and this card is its very soul. Esoterically the figure of Justice with the scales figures the inexorable law of balance and karmic adjustment—the precise weighing by which all things are brought to equilibrium, the truth that nothing is unaccounted and that right action consists in restoring and maintaining the perfect poise of the scales.
tables: CLXXXI. Correct Design of Tarot Trumps

a-crowned-priestess-sits-before-the-veil.term: A crowned priestess sits before the veil of Isis between the Pillars of Seth
a-crowned-priestess-sits-before-the-veil.displayTerm: A crowned priestess sits before the veil of Isis between the Pillars of Seth
a-crowned-priestess-sits-before-the-veil.summary: Liber 777's design for the High Priestess (Gimel): a crowned priestess before the veil of Isis.
a-crowned-priestess-sits-before-the-veil.description: Liber 777's design for Atu II, the High Priestess (path of Gimel, the Moon), is ‘A crowned priestess sits before the veil of Isis between the Pillars of Seth.’ She is the lunar guardian of the inner sanctuary, enthroned between the black and white pillars of mercy and severity, the gateway of the mysteries. The veil of Isis is the curtain of the unrevealed—the secret of nature and of the goddess that only initiation may part. Crowned and seated, she keeps the threshold of the longest path, the silver road that crosses the Abyss toward the Crown.
tables: CLXXXI. Correct Design of Tarot Trumps

a-crucified-god.summary: Magical image of Tiphareth: a sacrificed (crucified) god.
a-crucified-god.description: ‘A crucified god’ is one of the magical images of Tiphareth, the solar heart of the Tree, whose images are ‘a majestic king, a child, and a sacrificed god.’ The sacrificed and risen god—Osiris, Christ, Dionysus, the slain and reborn sun—is the central mystery of this Sephirah: life given up that it may be renewed, death at the centre that is the seed of resurrection. It is the deepest face of Tiphareth's solar symbolism, the heart that is wounded and made glorious in the same act.
tables: CXX. Magical Images of the Sephiroth

a-dark-man.summary: Magical image of the 1st decan of Libra: a dark man bearing a spear, laurel, and book.
a-dark-man.description: ‘A dark man’ opens the magical image of the ascendant (first) decan of Libra—‘A dark man, in his right hand a spear and laurel branch, and in his left a book’—from the classical decan tradition in Liber 777. The spear and laurel signify martial honour and victory, the book learning and judgement, fitting the airy, balancing sign of the scales. Such decan figures were employed as talismanic images, each governing ten degrees of the zodiac.
tables: CXLIX. Magical Images of the Decans (Ascendent)

a-dog-with-a-gryphons-wings.term: A dog with a gryphons wings
a-dog-with-a-gryphons-wings.displayTerm: A dog with a gryphons wings
a-dog-with-a-gryphons-wings.summary: The magical image of Glasya-Labolas — a winged dog fledged with a gryphon's wings — Goetic President of the first decan of Sagittarius.
a-dog-with-a-gryphons-wings.description: Glasya-Labolas, the twenty-fifth spirit of the Goetia and a mighty President, comes forth as a dog bearing the wings of a gryphon. In 777 he rules the first decan of Sagittarius by day. He teaches all arts and sciences in an instant, is named the author and captain of manslaughter and bloodshed, tells things past and to come, conciliates friends and foes, and can make a man go invisible. His swift winged hound is the very emblem of the Archer's arrow — knowledge and slaughter loosed together and flying straight to the mark.

a-fair-youth-with-winged-helment.term: A fair youth with winged helment
a-fair-youth-with-winged-helment.displayTerm: A fair youth with winged helment
a-fair-youth-with-winged-helment.summary: Liber 777's design for the Magician (Beth): a fair youth with a winged helmet.
a-fair-youth-with-winged-helment.description: ‘A fair youth with winged helmet and heels’ opens Liber 777's design for Atu I, the Magician, on the path of Beth (Mercury). The winged helmet is the unmistakable attribute of Mercury-Hermes, the swift messenger of the gods, marking the magician as the agent of intellect, speech, and rapid transmission of will. Youthful and beautiful, he is the eternally fresh creative mind; the wings show that his thought outruns the body, flying between the worlds to carry the divine word into act.
tables: CLXXXI. Correct Design of Tarot Trumps

a-flame-clad-god-bearing-equivalent-symb.term: A flame-clad god bearing equivalent symbols
a-flame-clad-god-bearing-equivalent-symb.displayTerm: A flame-clad god bearing equivalent symbols
a-flame-clad-god-bearing-equivalent-symb.summary: Liber 777's design for the Emperor (Heh): a flame-clad god bearing equivalent symbols.
a-flame-clad-god-bearing-equivalent-symb.description: Liber 777's design for Atu IV, the Emperor (path of Heh, Aries), is ‘A flame-clad god bearing equivalent symbols.’ Clad in the fire of Aries—the cardinal, kindling sign of the ram—he is the sovereign solar-martial power, robed in flame as the emblem of his authority and energy. The ‘equivalent symbols’ he bears (orb and sceptre, the regalia of rule) declare his office: the establishing of order, dominion, and law over the manifest world, the masculine will that frames creation within bounds.
tables: CLXXXI. Correct Design of Tarot Trumps

a-girdle-of-leaves.summary: Detail of the magical image of the 1st decan of Cancer: a girdle of leaves.
a-girdle-of-leaves.description: ‘A girdle of leaves’ is a detail of the magical image of the ascendant (first) decan of Cancer—‘A man with distorted face and hands, a horse's body, white feet, and a girdle of leaves’—from the classical decan tradition in Liber 777. The leafy girdle binds the strange composite figure with a token of vegetable life and fertility, suited to the nurturing, watery sign of the crab. The full image served as a talismanic figure ruling ten degrees of the zodiac.
tables: CXLIX. Magical Images of the Decans (Ascendent)

a-grave-man-pointing-to-the-sky.term: A grave man pointing to the sky
a-grave-man-pointing-to-the-sky.displayTerm: A grave man pointing to the sky
a-grave-man-pointing-to-the-sky.summary: Magical image of the 2nd decan of Pisces: a grave man pointing to the sky.
a-grave-man-pointing-to-the-sky.description: ‘A grave man pointing to the sky’ is the magical image of the succedent (second) decan of Pisces in the classical decan tradition transmitted through Liber 777. The solemn figure directing his gaze and gesture heavenward suits the contemplative, spiritually aspiring quality of this watery decan, turning the mind from the deep toward the high. As with all the decan images, it served as a talismanic figure ruling ten degrees of the zodiac.
tables: CL. Magical Images of the Decans (Succedent)

a-green-clad-woman.summary: Magical image of the 2nd decan of Aries: a green-clad woman.
a-green-clad-woman.description: ‘A green-clad woman, with one leg bare from the ankle to the knee’ is the magical image of the succedent (second) decan of Aries in the classical decan tradition gathered into Liber 777. The green raiment suggests fresh growth and the burgeoning vitality of spring, the season Aries opens, while the figure's poised, half-revealed stance marks readiness and movement. Such decan figures were used as talismanic emblems, each ruling ten degrees of the zodiac.
tables: CL. Magical Images of the Decans (Succedent)

a-hermaphrodite.summary: Magical image of Hod: a hermaphrodite, uniting the sexes.
a-hermaphrodite.description: ‘A hermaphrodite’ is the magical image of Hod, the eighth Sephirah, Splendour, the sphere of Mercury. Hod is the realm of intellect, language, and the analytical mind, and its Mercurial nature is fittingly imaged as the hermaphrodite—the union of male and female in one form, the androgyne of the alchemists. Mercury is the messenger who moves between all opposites and partakes of both; the hermaphrodite expresses the reconciling, dual-natured intelligence that names and orders the world.
tables: CXX. Magical Images of the Sephiroth

a-horse.summary: Detail of decan magical images (Taurus and Scorpio): a horse among the attendant beasts.
a-horse.description: ‘A horse’ appears as a detail in two of the classical decan images gathered into Liber 777: in the cadent (third) decan of Taurus, where a horse, a stag, and a calf attend a swarthy elephantine man, and in the cadent decan of Scorpio, whose image is simply ‘a horse and a wolf.’ In the older talismanic tradition such attendant beasts each carried their own symbolic weight; the horse signifies vigour, swiftness, and noble strength. These figures ruled ten degrees of the zodiac apiece.
tables: CLI. Magical Images of the Decans (Cadent)

a-horses-body.summary: Detail of the magical image of the 1st decan of Cancer: a horse's body.
a-horses-body.description: ‘A horse's body’ is a detail of the magical image of the ascendant (first) decan of Cancer—‘A man with distorted face and hands, a horse's body, white feet, and a girdle of leaves’—from the classical decan tradition in Liber 777. The equine body fused to a human form makes the figure a composite, monstrous emblem of mingled natures, of the kind common among the older talismanic decan images. The full figure ruled ten degrees of the zodiac.
tables: CXLIX. Magical Images of the Decans (Ascendent)

a-knight-with-lance.summary: The magical image of Eligos — a goodly knight with lance, ensign and serpent — Goetic Duke of the third decan of Leo.
a-knight-with-lance.description: Eligos (Abigor), the fifteenth spirit of the Goetia and a great Duke, appears in the form of a goodly knight bearing a lance, an ensign or banner, and a serpent. In 777 he rules the third decan of Leo by day. He discovers hidden things, knows things to come and the outcome of wars and how soldiers shall meet, and procures the love of lords and great persons. The mounted knight beneath his banner befits the royal, martial Lion in its final, lordly face — war foreseen and dominion won.

a-majestic-king.summary: Magical image of Tiphareth: a majestic king (also a child, a sacrificed god).
a-majestic-king.description: ‘A majestic king’ is one of the magical images of Tiphareth, the sixth Sephirah and the solar heart of the Tree, whose images are ‘a majestic king, a child, and a sacrificed god.’ The king crowned in glory is the harmonised, sovereign self enthroned at the centre of the personal universe—the radiant ruler in whom all the surrounding powers are reconciled. He is one face of the threefold solar mystery of Tiphareth: majesty, innocence, and sacrifice united in the reborn god of the Sun.
tables: CXX. Magical Images of the Sephiroth

a-man.summary: Detail of the magical image of the 2nd decan of Libra: a man, dark yet delicious of countenance.
a-man.description: ‘A man’ opens the magical image of the succedent (second) decan of Libra—‘A man, dark, yet delicious of countenance’—from the classical decan tradition in Liber 777. The figure's dark but pleasing aspect suits the airy, harmonising sign of the scales, in which grace and attraction temper every quality. As with all the decan images, it served as a talismanic figure governing ten degrees of the zodiac.
tables: CL. Magical Images of the Decans (Succedent)

a-man-arrayed-like-a-king.term: A man arrayed like a king
a-man-arrayed-like-a-king.displayTerm: A man arrayed like a king
a-man-arrayed-like-a-king.summary: Magical image of the 2nd decan of Aquarius: a man arrayed like a king, full of pride.
a-man-arrayed-like-a-king.description: ‘A man arrayed like a king, looking with pride and conceit on all around him’ is the magical image of the succedent (second) decan of Aquarius in the classical decan tradition transmitted through Liber 777. The regal but vain figure expresses the fixed, self-assured, and sometimes haughty quality of this airy decan. As with all the decan images, it functioned as a talismanic figure governing ten degrees of the zodiac.
tables: CL. Magical Images of the Decans (Succedent)

a-man-crowned-with-a-white-myrtle-wreath.term: A man crowned with a white myrtle wreath
a-man-crowned-with-a-white-myrtle-wreath.displayTerm: A man crowned with a white myrtle wreath
a-man-crowned-with-a-white-myrtle-wreath.summary: Magical image of the 2nd decan of Leo: a man crowned with white myrtle, holding a bow.
a-man-crowned-with-a-white-myrtle-wreath.description: ‘A man crowned with a white myrtle wreath, holding a bow’ is the magical image of the succedent (second) decan of Leo in the classical decan tradition gathered into Liber 777. The white myrtle crown signifies honour and love, the bow strength and aim—fitting the proud, vital, sovereign nature of the fiery sign of the lion. Such decan figures were employed as talismanic images, each ruling ten degrees of the zodiac.
tables: CL. Magical Images of the Decans (Succedent)

a-man-holding-a-book-which-he-opens.term: A man holding a book which he opens
a-man-holding-a-book-which-he-opens.displayTerm: A man holding a book which he opens
a-man-holding-a-book-which-he-opens.summary: Magical image of the 3rd decan of Capricorn: a man opening and shutting a book.
a-man-holding-a-book-which-he-opens.description: ‘A man holding a book which he opens and shuts’ is the magical image of the cadent (third) decan of Capricorn in the classical decan tradition transmitted through Liber 777. The opening and closing of the book suggests study, deliberation, and the measured weighing of knowledge—suited to the earthy, Saturnine reserve of the goat. As with all the decan images, it served as a talismanic figure governing ten degrees of the zodiac.
tables: CLI. Magical Images of the Decans (Cadent)

a-man-holding-in-his-right-hand-a-javeli.term: A man holding in his right hand a javelin
a-man-holding-in-his-right-hand-a-javeli.displayTerm: A man holding in his right hand a javelin
a-man-holding-in-his-right-hand-a-javeli.summary: Magical image of the 1st decan of Capricorn: a man with a javelin and a lapwing.
a-man-holding-in-his-right-hand-a-javeli.description: ‘A man holding in his right hand a javelin, and in his left a lapwing’ is the magical image of the ascendant (first) decan of Capricorn in the classical decan tradition gathered into Liber 777. The javelin marks determination and martial drive, the lapwing a creature of the field and of wary cunning, together expressing the ambitious, persevering character of the earthy goat. Such decan figures were used as talismanic emblems, each ruling ten degrees of the zodiac.
tables: CXLIX. Magical Images of the Decans (Ascendent)

a-man-in-mail.summary: Magical image of the 3rd decan of Gemini: a man in mail, armed with bow and quiver.
a-man-in-mail.description: ‘A man in mail, armoured with bow, arrows, and quiver’ is the magical image of the cadent (third) decan of Gemini in the classical decan tradition transmitted through Liber 777. The armoured archer expresses readiness, skill, and the swift, far-reaching action proper to the airy, mutable sign of the twins. As with all the decan images, it functioned as a talismanic figure governing ten degrees of the zodiac.
tables: CLI. Magical Images of the Decans (Cadent)

a-man-in-sordid-raiment.summary: Magical image of the 1st decan of Leo: a man in sordid raiment with a nobleman, bears, and dogs.
a-man-in-sordid-raiment.description: ‘A man in sordid raiment, with him a nobleman on horseback, accompanied by bears and dogs’ is the magical image of the ascendant (first) decan of Leo in the classical decan tradition gathered into Liber 777. The contrast of the lowly figure with the mounted noble, attended by beasts of the chase, evokes the wide range of fortune and the lordly, animal vigour of the fiery sign of the lion. Such decan figures were used as talismanic emblems, each ruling ten degrees of the zodiac.
tables: CXLIX. Magical Images of the Decans (Ascendent)

a-man-leading-another-by-his-hair.term: A man leading another by his hair
a-man-leading-another-by-his-hair.displayTerm: A man leading another by his hair
a-man-leading-another-by-his-hair.summary: Magical image of the 3rd decan of Sagittarius: a man leading and slaying another by his hair.
a-man-leading-another-by-his-hair.description: ‘A man leading another by his hair and slaying him’ is the magical image of the cadent (third) decan of Sagittarius in the classical decan tradition transmitted through Liber 777. The violent scene expresses conquest, dominance, and the ruthless edge of the fiery archer's drive toward its target. As with all the decan figures, it served as a talismanic image governing ten degrees of the zodiac, and like several of these older emblems it carries a harsh, martial character.
tables: CLI. Magical Images of the Decans (Cadent)

a-man-leading-cows.summary: Magical image of the 2nd decan of Sagittarius: a man leading cows, with an ape and a bear.
a-man-leading-cows.description: ‘A man leading cows, and before him an ape and bear’ is the magical image of the succedent (second) decan of Sagittarius in the classical decan tradition gathered into Liber 777. The herdsman with his cattle and following beasts evokes mastery over the animal nature and the husbanding of resources, tempering the fiery archer's energy with practical guidance. Such decan figures were used as talismanic emblems, each ruling ten degrees of the zodiac.
tables: CL. Magical Images of the Decans (Succedent)

a-man-of-grave.summary: Detail of the magical image of the 3rd decan of Pisces: a man of grave and thoughtful face.
a-man-of-grave.description: ‘A man of grave’ opens the magical image of the cadent (third) decan of Pisces—‘A man of grave and thoughtful face, with a bird in his hand, before him a woman and an ass’—from the classical decan tradition in Liber 777. The grave, contemplative figure suits the deep, reflective, spiritually-burdened nature of the final decan of the zodiac. The full image served as a talismanic figure ruling ten degrees of the zodiac.
tables: CLI. Magical Images of the Decans (Cadent)

a-man-of-like-figure.summary: Magical image of the 2nd decan of Taurus: a man of like figure, with cloven ox-hoofs.
a-man-of-like-figure.description: ‘A man of like figure (to the ascendant), with cloven hoofs like an ox’ is the magical image of the succedent (second) decan of Taurus in the classical decan tradition transmitted through Liber 777. The ox-hoofed man directly evokes the bull of Taurus, the patient, earthy, generative force of the fixed earth sign. As with all the decan images, it functioned as a talismanic figure governing ten degrees of the zodiac.
tables: CL. Magical Images of the Decans (Succedent)

a-man-riding-a-camel.summary: Magical image of the 2nd decan of Scorpio: a man riding a camel with a scorpion in his hand.
a-man-riding-a-camel.description: ‘A man riding a camel, with a scorpion in his hand’ is the magical image of the succedent (second) decan of Scorpio in the classical decan tradition gathered into Liber 777. The scorpion held openly is the very emblem of the sign, signifying control over its venomous, transformative power, while the camel suggests endurance through harsh and desert places. Such decan figures were used as talismanic emblems, each ruling ten degrees of the zodiac.
tables: CL. Magical Images of the Decans (Succedent)

a-man-riding-on-an-ass.term: A man riding on an ass
a-man-riding-on-an-ass.displayTerm: A man riding on an ass
a-man-riding-on-an-ass.summary: Magical image of the 3rd decan of Libra: a man riding on an ass, preceded by a wolf.
a-man-riding-on-an-ass.description: ‘A man riding on an ass, preceded by a wolf’ is the magical image of the cadent (third) decan of Libra in the classical decan tradition transmitted through Liber 777. The patient ass and the leading wolf set humility beside cunning and appetite, a pairing of opposites suited to the balancing, relational nature of the airy scales. As with all the decan figures, it served as a talismanic image governing ten degrees of the zodiac.
tables: CLI. Magical Images of the Decans (Cadent)

a-man-with-3-bodies-1-black.summary: Magical image of the 1st decan of Sagittarius: a man with three bodies—black, red, and white.
a-man-with-3-bodies-1-black.description: ‘A man with three bodies, one black, one red, one white’ is the magical image of the ascendant (first) decan of Sagittarius in the classical decan tradition gathered into Liber 777. The threefold body in the alchemical colours—black (nigredo), red (rubedo), and white (albedo)—suggests the stages of the Great Work and the expansive, multiple, philosophical reach of the fiery archer. Such decan figures were used as talismanic emblems, each ruling ten degrees of the zodiac.
tables: CXLIX. Magical Images of the Decans (Ascendent)

a-man-with-a-lance-in-his-right-hand.term: A man with a lance in his right hand
a-man-with-a-lance-in-his-right-hand.displayTerm: A man with a lance in his right hand
a-man-with-a-lance-in-his-right-hand.summary: Magical image of the 1st decan of Scorpio: a man with a lance and a severed human head.
a-man-with-a-lance-in-his-right-hand.description: ‘A man with a lance in his right hand, in his left a human head’ is the magical image of the ascendant (first) decan of Scorpio in the classical decan tradition transmitted through Liber 777. The lance and the severed head are stark emblems of death, conquest, and the cutting power of the sign, fitting Scorpio's nature as the realm of dissolution and regeneration. As with all the decan figures, it served as a talismanic image governing ten degrees of the zodiac—one of the grimmer of these old martial emblems.
tables: CXLIX. Magical Images of the Decans (Ascendent)

a-man-with-an-ape-running-before-him.term: A man with an ape running before him
a-man-with-an-ape-running-before-him.displayTerm: A man with an ape running before him
a-man-with-an-ape-running-before-him.summary: Magical image of the 3rd decan of Capricorn: a man with an ape running before him.
a-man-with-an-ape-running-before-him.description: ‘A man with an ape running before him’ is the magical image of the cadent (third) decan of Capricorn in the classical decan tradition gathered into Liber 777. The ape going before its master suggests imitation, instinct led, and the lower nature put to service—an apt figure for the disciplined, ambitious earth of the goat that harnesses base forces to its climb. Such decan figures were used as talismanic emblems, each ruling ten degrees of the zodiac.
tables: CL. Magical Images of the Decans (Succedent)

a-man-with-bowed-head.summary: Magical image of the 1st decan of Aquarius: a man with bowed head and a bag in his hand.
a-man-with-bowed-head.description: ‘A man with bowed head, and a bag in his hand’ is the magical image of the ascendant (first) decan of Aquarius in the classical decan tradition transmitted through Liber 777. The bowed head suggests thought, humility, or burden, and the bag the keeping or carrying of goods—together evoking the reflective, accumulating, socially-minded character of the airy water-bearer. As with all the decan figures, it served as a talismanic image governing ten degrees of the zodiac.
tables: CXLIX. Magical Images of the Decans (Ascendent)

a-man-with-distorted-face.summary: The talismanic image of the first decan of Cancer — a man with a distorted face.
a-man-with-distorted-face.description: “A man with distorted face” is the magical image of the ascendent (first) decan of Cancer, in the old decan tradition behind Liber 777. The twisted or distorted features lend a note of strangeness and hidden feeling to the watery, moon-ruled sign of the Crab, whose nature is changeable and inward. As a decan talisman the figure encodes the moody, concealing quality of this first face of Cancer.
tables: CXLIX. Magical Images of the Decans (Ascendent)

a-man-with-two-bodies.summary: The talismanic image of the first decan of Pisces — a man with two bodies.
a-man-with-two-bodies.description: “A man with two bodies” is the magical image of the ascendent (first) decan of Pisces, from the decan tradition. The doubled body suits the dual, twofold nature of the sign of the Fishes, which face in opposite directions — the pull between the worlds, the divided self of the watery, dissolving sign. As a decan talisman it marks this first face of Pisces with the theme of duality and the meeting of two natures.
tables: CXLIX. Magical Images of the Decans (Ascendent)

a-mighty-crowned.summary: The magical image of Chesed — a mighty, crowned, and throned king.
a-mighty-crowned.description: “A mighty crowned [and throned king]” is the magical image of Chesed, the fourth Sephirah, the sphere of Jupiter, mercy, and beneficent rule. The crowned and enthroned king embodies majestic, ordering authority exercised with generosity — the benevolent sovereign whose reign is law and abundance. He is power at its most stable and gracious, the merciful lawgiver who governs the manifest order from his settled throne.
tables: CXX. Magical Images of the Sephiroth

a-mighty-warrior-in-his-chariot.term: A mighty warrior in his chariot
a-mighty-warrior-in-his-chariot.displayTerm: A mighty warrior in his chariot
a-mighty-warrior-in-his-chariot.summary: The magical image of Geburah — a mighty warrior in his chariot.
a-mighty-warrior-in-his-chariot.description: “A mighty warrior in his chariot” is the magical image of Geburah, the fifth Sephirah, the sphere of Mars, severity, and martial power. The armed warrior riding to battle embodies the disciplined, destructive force of the sphere — strength, courage, and the just exercise of might against disorder. He is the necessary severity of the Tree, the divine power that breaks down what must be broken and defends the order established by his counterpart, the merciful king.
tables: CXX. Magical Images of the Sephiroth

a-prophet.summary: Design detail of the Lovers (Zayin): a prophet.
a-prophet.description: ‘A prophet’ opens Liber 777's design for Atu VI, the Lovers (path of Zayin, Gemini): ‘A prophet, young, and in the Sign of Osiris Risen.’ The prophet presides over the mystery of the card—the hierophant or oracle who blesses the union of opposites and pronounces the choice. Gemini is the sign of duality and discernment, and the prophet is the inspired voice that discriminates and weds, the Children of the Voice taking counsel of the Oracle of the Mighty Gods.
tables: CLXXXI. Correct Design of Tarot Trumps

a-restless-man-in-scarlet-robes.term: A restless man in scarlet robes
a-restless-man-in-scarlet-robes.displayTerm: A restless man in scarlet robes
a-restless-man-in-scarlet-robes.summary: The talismanic image of the third decan of Aries — a restless man in scarlet robes.
a-restless-man-in-scarlet-robes.description: “A restless man in scarlet robes” is the magical image of the cadent (third) decan of Aries, in the old decan tradition. Scarlet is the colour of Mars, ruler of Aries, and the restlessness suits the fiery, impatient, pioneering nature of the Ram at its final face. As a decan talisman the agitated, red-clad figure encodes the burning energy and driving urgency proper to this third of Aries.
tables: CLI. Magical Images of the Decans (Cadent)

a-sickle.summary: The reaping blade of Saturn—Cronos's curved scythe, the harvest and the cutting of time.
a-sickle.description: The Sickle is attributed to Saturn (the path of Tav, the Universe), and it is the curved blade of the reaper—the scythe of Cronos-Saturn with which the old god both castrated his father and mows down the generations of men. As Saturn's instrument it is the weapon of time and ending: the tool that cuts the ripe from its stalk, gathering in the harvest and severing what has run its course. It speaks of limitation, of the cycle completed, of the inevitable cutting-down that makes room for the new. Esoterically the Sickle is the principle of necessary ending in the magician's hand—the disciplined reaping that gathers the fruit of a cycle and clears the field, the blade of Saturn that turns time itself into a tool of the Work.

a-skeleton-with-a-scythe-mowing-men.term: A skeleton with a scythe mowing men
a-skeleton-with-a-scythe-mowing-men.displayTerm: A skeleton with a scythe mowing men
a-skeleton-with-a-scythe-mowing-men.summary: The magical image of Death (Atu XIII)—the skeleton-reaper of Scorpio mowing down the generations, change through dissolution.
a-skeleton-with-a-scythe-mowing-men.description: This image—a skeleton wielding a scythe to mow down men—is the magical figure of the thirteenth trump, Death, attributed to the letter Nun and the sign Scorpio. The reaper cuts down all that lives without exception, kings and commons alike falling before the blade, yet from the severed ground new shoots spring: Death is not annihilation but transformation, the necessary dissolution that clears the old to make way for the new. Scorpio's threefold power of scorpion, serpent and eagle is the secret of this card—putrefaction that becomes regeneration. Esoterically the skeleton with the scythe figures the great law of change through death—the mowing-down of the outworn self and form so that life may be renewed, the dissolving power of Scorpio by which what has ripened is reaped and the buried seed is freed to grow again.
tables: CLXXXI. Correct Design of Tarot Trumps

a-small-headed-man-dressed-like-a-woman.term: A small-headed man dressed like a woman
a-small-headed-man-dressed-like-a-woman.displayTerm: A small-headed man dressed like a woman
a-small-headed-man-dressed-like-a-woman.summary: The talismanic image of the third decan of Aquarius — a small-headed man dressed like a woman.
a-small-headed-man-dressed-like-a-woman.description: “A small-headed man dressed like a woman” is the magical image of the cadent (third) decan of Aquarius, from the decan tradition. The blending or reversal of male and female suits the airy, unconventional, boundary-crossing nature of the Water-Bearer at its final face. As a decan talisman the curious figure encodes the eccentric, role-confounding quality of this third of Aquarius.
tables: CLI. Magical Images of the Decans (Cadent)

a-smiling-woman-holds-the-open-jaws-of-a.term: A smiling woman holds the open jaws of a fierce
a-smiling-woman-holds-the-open-jaws-of-a.displayTerm: A smiling woman holds the open jaws of a fierce
a-smiling-woman-holds-the-open-jaws-of-a.summary: Liber 777's design for Strength/Lust (Teth): a smiling woman holds open the jaws of a fierce lion.
a-smiling-woman-holds-the-open-jaws-of-a.description: Liber 777's design for Atu VIII/XI, Strength—Crowley's Lust—on the path of Teth (Leo) is ‘A smiling woman holds the open jaws of a fierce and powerful lion.’ She masters the beast not by violence but with a smile, her courage and joy taming the raw leonine fire. The image is the very emblem of spiritual strength: vital, instinctual power (the lion, Leo) embraced and directed by the serene, ecstatic will rather than suppressed. It is mastery through union, the rider one with her mount.
tables: CLXXXI. Correct Design of Tarot Trumps

a-soldier-in-red-apparel.summary: The magical image of Zepar — a soldier in red apparel and armour — Goetic Duke of the first decan of Virgo.
a-soldier-in-red-apparel.description: Zepar, the sixteenth spirit of the Goetia and a great Duke, appears in red apparel and the armour of a soldier. In 777 he governs the first decan of Virgo by day. His office is over love: he inflames women with desire for men and brings them together, though it is said he can also render them barren. The martial red of his image marks the heat of passion enlisted, paradoxically, in the service of the cool and chaste sign of the Virgin.

tables: CLI. Magical Images of the Decans (Cadent)

a-star-in-a-pentacle.summary: The magical image of Decarabia — a star within a pentacle — Goetic Marquis of the third decan of Aquarius (by night).
a-star-in-a-pentacle.description: Decarabia (Carabia), the sixty-ninth spirit of the Goetia and a great Marquis, appears first in the figure of a star set within a pentacle, and afterward, at the operator's command, in the shape of a man. In 777 he is the nocturnal ruler of the third decan of Aquarius. He knows the virtues of all birds and precious stones, and can make the likeness of every kind of bird to fly before the magician and to sing and drink as living birds do. The bare geometric sign — a star caught in the pentagram — fitly opens the abstract, pattern-loving sign of the Water-Bearer, where spirit first shows itself as figure and number before it takes on flesh.

a-strong-man-in-human-shape.term: A strong man in human shape
a-strong-man-in-human-shape.displayTerm: A strong man in human shape
a-strong-man-in-human-shape.summary: The magical image of Foras — a strong man in human shape — Goetic President of the first decan of Aquarius.
a-strong-man-in-human-shape.description: Foras (Forcas), the thirty-first spirit of the Goetia and a mighty President, appears plainly as a strong man in human shape. In 777 he rules the first decan of Aquarius by day. He teaches logic and ethics, the virtues of all herbs and precious stones, makes a man witty, eloquent, invisible and long-lived, and discovers treasures and recovers things lost. His wholly human form — unmixed with beast — befits the humane, rational sign of the Water-Bearer, whose gift is knowledge in the service of mankind.

a-strong-man-with-a-serpent-s-tail.term: A strong man with a serpent's tail
a-strong-man-with-a-serpent-s-tail.displayTerm: A strong man with a serpent's tail
a-strong-man-with-a-serpent-s-tail.summary: The magical image of Bathin — a strong man with a serpent's tail upon a pale horse — Goetic Duke of the third decan of Virgo.
a-strong-man-with-a-serpent-s-tail.description: Bathin (Bathym, Marthim), the eighteenth spirit of the Goetia and a mighty and strong Duke, appears as a strong man with the tail of a serpent, seated upon a pale horse. In 777 he is set at the third decan of Virgo by day. He knows the virtues of herbs and precious stones, and can carry men suddenly from one country to another. The vigorous man trailing a serpent's coil — bearer of herb-lore and of swift transport — images the earthy sign of the Virgin as keeper of natural secrets and of hidden roads.

a-swarthy-hairy-man.summary: The talismanic image of the third decan of Leo — a swarthy, hairy man.
a-swarthy-hairy-man.description: “A swarthy hairy man” is the magical image of the cadent (third) decan of Leo, in the old decan tradition. The dark, hirsute figure lends a note of brute strength and animal vigour to the regal, solar sign of the Lion at its final face. As a decan talisman it encodes the raw, powerful, leonine quality of this third of Leo.
tables: CLI. Magical Images of the Decans (Cadent)

a-swarthy-man-with-white-lashes.term: A swarthy man with white lashes
a-swarthy-man-with-white-lashes.displayTerm: A swarthy man with white lashes
a-swarthy-man-with-white-lashes.summary: The talismanic image of the third decan of Taurus — a swarthy man with white lashes.
a-swarthy-man-with-white-lashes.description: “A swarthy man with white lashes” is the magical image of the cadent (third) decan of Taurus, from the decan tradition. The striking contrast of dark skin and white lashes marks the figure with an arresting, earthy distinctiveness suited to the final face of the fixed earth sign. As a decan talisman it encodes the solid, sensual, and singular quality of this third of Taurus.
tables: CLI. Magical Images of the Decans (Cadent)

a-swift-footed-person.summary: The talismanic image of the third decan of Cancer — a swift-footed person.
a-swift-footed-person.description: “A swift-footed person” is the magical image of the cadent (third) decan of Cancer, in the old decan tradition. The quickness of foot lends a note of restless movement to the watery, tidal sign of the Crab at its final face — the ebb and flow made nimble. As a decan talisman the fleet figure encodes the changeable, mobile quality of this third of Cancer.
tables: CLI. Magical Images of the Decans (Cadent)
CXLIX. Magical Images of the Decans (Ascendent)

a-tower-struck-by-forked-lightning.term: A tower struck by forked lightning
a-tower-struck-by-forked-lightning.displayTerm: A tower struck by forked lightning
a-tower-struck-by-forked-lightning.summary: The magical image of the Tower (Atu XVI)—the fortress of Mars shattered by lightning, the sudden ruin that liberates.
a-tower-struck-by-forked-lightning.description: This image—a tower struck and broken by forked lightning, its crown blasted off and figures falling from its height—is the magical figure of the sixteenth trump, the Tower (or House of God), attributed to the letter Pe and the planet Mars. The lightning is the sudden, violent descent of force that shatters every structure built in pride and false security, casting down what the ego has raised against the heavens. Martial and catastrophic, it is destruction that is also deliverance: the prison-tower must fall for the prisoner to go free. Esoterically the lightning-struck Tower figures the sudden, shattering intervention of higher force—the necessary demolition of every rigid, self-made structure that has shut out the light, the violent liberation by which what is false is thrown down so that the truth may break in.
tables: CLXXXI. Correct Design of Tarot Trumps

a-virgin-clad-in-linen.summary: The talismanic image of the first decan of Virgo — a virgin clad in linen.
a-virgin-clad-in-linen.description: “A virgin clad in linen” is the magical image of the ascendent (first) decan of Virgo, from the decan tradition. The pure linen and the figure of the virgin perfectly suit the chaste, harvest-tending sign of the Maiden at its first face — purity, modesty, and the careful order of Virgo. As a decan talisman it encodes the clean, virginal quality with which the sign begins.
tables: CXLIX. Magical Images of the Decans (Ascendent)

a-wheel-of-six-shafts.summary: The magical image of the Wheel of Fortune (Atu X)—the turning six-spoked wheel of Jupiter, the rise and fall of all things.
a-wheel-of-six-shafts.description: This image—a great wheel of six shafts or spokes, with figures borne up and down upon its rim—is the magical figure of the tenth trump, the Wheel of Fortune, attributed to the letter Kaph and the planet Jupiter. The wheel turns ceaselessly, lifting up what was low and casting down what was high, the very emblem of fortune, fate and the cyclic changes of existence; about it ride the kerubic and Typhonic powers of rise and fall. Yet at its hub is a still point that does not move. Esoterically the Wheel of six shafts figures the turning of fortune and the cycles of manifestation under Jupiter's rule—the endless revolution of gain and loss, ascent and decline, and the wisdom of seeking the unmoving centre, the Sphinx upon the axle, from which the whirling rim can be watched without being ruled by it.
tables: CLXXXI. Correct Design of Tarot Trumps

a-winged-goddess-stands-upon-the-moon.term: a winged goddess stands upon the moon
a-winged-goddess-stands-upon-the-moon.displayTerm: a winged goddess stands upon the moon
a-winged-goddess-stands-upon-the-moon.summary: Liber 777's design for the Empress (Daleth): a winged goddess standing upon the moon.
a-winged-goddess-stands-upon-the-moon.description: ‘A winged goddess stands upon the moon’ completes Liber 777's design for Atu III, the Empress (path of Daleth, Venus): ‘Crowned with stars, a winged goddess stands upon the moon.’ Winged and luminous, she stands upon the lunar crescent—Venus presiding over the tides of generation, the heavenly feminine set above the changeable waters of nature. The image fuses the planet of love with the powers of fertility and growth: the great mother who, between the Supernal Father and Mother, brings all forms to birth.
tables: CLXXXI. Correct Design of Tarot Trumps
CLI. Magical Images of the Decans (Cadent)
CXLIX. Magical Images of the Decans (Ascendent)

a-young.summary: Liber 777's design for the Chariot (Cheth): a young and holy king.
a-young.description: ‘A young’ is the opening of Liber 777's design for Atu VII, the Chariot (path of Cheth, Cancer): ‘A young and holy king under the starry canopy.’ The charioteer is shown as a youthful, consecrated king—the soul in the prime of its disciplined power, enthroned within the vehicle that bears it across the waters of Cancer. His youth is the freshness of victory; his kingship and holiness the conquest of the lower nature by the will that carries the Grail in triumph.
tables: CLXXXI. Correct Design of Tarot Trumps

a-young-woman.summary: The magical image of Malkuth — a young woman, crowned and throned.
a-young-woman.description: “A young woman, crowned and throned” is the magical image of Malkuth, the tenth Sephirah, the Kingdom and the realised, material world. As the bride of Microprosopus and the daughter of the supernal Mother, she is the divine feminine fully descended into manifestation — sovereign of the visible world, the queen in whom all the forces of the Tree are gathered and made real. Crowned and enthroned, she is the glory of creation as the throne of the divine presence on earth.
tables: CXX. Magical Images of the Sephiroth

aaron.summary: Aaron — at Hod; the priest and spokesman, voice of the divine word.
aaron.description: Aaron is attributed to Hod, the Mercurial sphere of intellect and communication. As the first High Priest and the appointed mouth of Moses before Pharaoh, he embodies the office of mediating speech and ritual order that belongs to Hod. His was the work of articulation and ceremony — the splendour of the priestly word giving form to the wisdom received from above.
tables: XCI. The Saints or Adepts of the Hebrews

abandoned-success.summary: Eight of Cups — Abandoned Success; Saturn in Pisces, Hod of Water: joy left behind.
abandoned-success.description: Abandoned Success is the Golden Dawn name for the Eight of Cups, Hod of the watery suit, Saturn in the first decan of Pisces. The cups stand half-full beneath a darkened, marshy sky; the seeker walks away from emotional fulfilment that has lost its meaning. It signifies disenchantment with what has been won, the quiet relinquishing of pleasures grown hollow.
tables: CXXXIV. Titles and Attributions of the Chalice Suit

abdaron.summary: Angel of the second face of Aquarius, where thought clarifies into science and reason.
abdaron.description: Abdaron governs the middle decan of Aquarius (10–20°), attributed to Mercury and the Six of Swords, *Science* — ordered intellect, the passage from troubled to clearer waters. Mercury, at ease in Aquarian air, lends method and measure. Abdaron is the angel of disciplined reason, of the analytic mind that finds its way by system.

aboha.summary: Angel of the third face of Sagittarius, where fire overreaches into oppression and burden.
aboha.description: Aboha presides over the closing decan of Sagittarius (20–30°), where Saturn meets the Ten of Wands, *Oppression* — force pressed past its measure into a crushing burden. Saturn's weight collapses Sagittarius's flame upon itself. Aboha is the angel of the tyranny into which unchecked fire degenerates, the lesson that power without limit becomes its own load.

above-head.summary: Above the Head — the bodily seat of the crown centre, corresponding to Kether.
above-head.description: 'Above the Head' marks the seat of the highest centre (Sahasrara), set in 777 at Kether — the point a little above the crown where, in the yogic and magical traditions, consciousness opens beyond the body into the divine light. It is less a place in the flesh than the threshold where the personal touches the transcendent.

above-it-stood-the-seraphim-six-wings.term: Above it stood the seraphim: Six wings
above-it-stood-the-seraphim-six-wings.displayTerm: Above it stood the seraphim: Six wings
tables: XCII. The Angelic Functions in the World of Yetzirah

abrahadabra.summary: The eleven-lettered Word of the Aeon, the formula of the Great Work accomplished.
abrahadabra.description: ABRAHADABRA is the central Word of Crowley's New Aeon, given in Liber AL and unfolded at length in his commentaries. Eleven letters long—the number of magick, of the union of the 5 of the microcosm with the 6 of the macrocosm—it is built as a cipher of accomplishment: a pentagram of five A's interlaced about the central H, the breath of life, with the doubled HAD proclaiming the marriage of the Rose and the Cross. Crowley calls it "the Word of the Aeon," the glyph of the Great Work performed, in which the magician and the universe are made one. Attributed here to Cheth and the Chariot, it is the sealed cup that carries the Holy Grail of attainment across the Abyss.

abrahadabra-iao-inri.summary: The solar formula of Tiphareth: the accomplished Word joined to the gods of death and resurrection.
abrahadabra-iao-inri.description: At Tiphareth, the heart of the Tree, the Word of the Aeon ABRAHADABRA is set beside the twin solar formulae IAO and INRI. IAO is the Gnostic name of the godhead whose three letters spell the cycle of Isis the nurturing mother, Apophis the destroyer, and Osiris the slain-and-risen lord—the eternal pattern of birth, death, and resurrection that Tiphareth, the place of the sacrificed and reborn god, embodies. INRI, the title nailed above the cross, is read in the Golden Dawn as the formula of the elements and of L.V.X., the Light extracted through the gestures of Isis Mourning, Apophis Slain, and Osiris Risen. Together at the solar centre they declare the whole mystery of the dying god made the living Sun.

abraham.summary: Abraham — at Chesed; the patriarch of mercy, faith, and lovingkindness.
abraham.description: Abraham is attributed to Chesed, the sphere of Mercy and Jupiter. The first patriarch, called the friend of God and the father of nations, embodies the boundless lovingkindness (chesed) and generous faith that the fourth Sephirah signifies. His covenant, his hospitality, and his readiness to be guided make him the very type of merciful, expansive grace upon the Tree.
tables: XCI. The Saints or Adepts of the Hebrews

absinthe.summary: The bitter green spirit of Mars—wormwood's fire, the 'green fairy' of poets and visionaries.
absinthe.description:
Absinthe is attributed to Mars (Pe, the Tower)—the bitter, emerald spirit distilled with wormwood (Artemisia absinthium), whose very name in scripture stands for bitterness and the star that fell and poisoned the waters. Its martial fire and reputation for kindling visions and madness made it the muse and the ruin of a generation of poets and painters. Esoterically it is the burning, bitter draught of Mars, the severity that scours and inspires.

Caution: wormwood and the spirits made from it are toxic in excess (the thujone of wormwood is a convulsant), and absinthe is strongly alcoholic. This entry is historical and symbolic and is in no way advice for use.
absinthe.caution: Strongly alcoholic; wormwood (thujone) is toxic in excess. Historical/symbolic entry only — not advice for use.

absolute.summary: The Eighth Path — the Absolute or Perfect Intelligence of Hod, the hidden ground of splendour.
absolute.description: The Eighth Path is the Absolute or Perfect Intelligence (Sekhel Shalem), assigned to Hod, the sphere of Mercury and Glory. The Sepher Yetzirah says it is the means of the primordial which has no root by which it can cleave or rest, save in the hidden recesses of Gedulah (Chesed), from which its own proper essence emanates. 'Absolute' marks it as complete and self-contained — the perfected intellectual splendour of Hod, the ordering mind whose forms are finished and entire, drawing its sustenance from the merciful abundance above it.
tables: XIII. Paths of the Sefer Yetzirah

abundance.summary: Three of Cups — Abundance; Mercury in Cancer, Binah of Water: overflowing plenty.
abundance.description: The Three of Cups, Abundance, is Binah in the suit of Water and the second decan of Cancer under Mercury. The Mother's sphere receives the loving waters of the Two and brings them to fruitful increase — three pomegranate cups brimming over, the generous fullness of joy shared. It is plenty, hospitality, and the spilling-over of emotional good fortune, the spring of feeling flowing freely.
tables: CXXXIV. Titles and Attributions of the Chalice Suit

acacia.summary: The acacia of the resurrected god—Masonic emblem of immortality, shittim-wood of the holy ark, sacred to Tiphareth.
acacia.description: The Acacia is attributed to Tiphareth, the solar sphere of the sacrificed-and-risen god, and it is pre-eminently the tree of resurrection and immortality. Its hard, incorruptible wood—the biblical shittim—framed the Ark and the Tabernacle; in Freemasonry the sprig of acacia marks the grave of Hiram Abiff and signifies the soul's survival of death. Esoterically the acacia is the green token of the deathless life at the heart of the Tree—the proof, laid upon the tomb, that the slain god rises.

accompanied-by-4-noble-kings.summary: The magical image of Barbatos — a huntsman attended by four noble kings and their troops — Goetic Duke of the second decan of Gemini.
accompanied-by-4-noble-kings.description: Barbatos, the eighth spirit of the Goetia and a great Duke, appears (when the Sun is in Sagittarius) attended by four noble kings and their great companies of troops. In 777 he rules the second decan of Gemini by day. He gives the understanding of the songs of birds, the voices of other creatures and the barking of dogs; he breaks the treasures hidden by enchantment, and tells things past and to come. The retinue of kings befits the sociable, many-voiced sign of the Twins — knowledge that comes in concourse and conversation.

tables: CXLIX. Magical Images of the Decans (Ascendent)

ace.summary: The Ace of Wands: the root and seed of the fiery suit.
ace.description: ‘Ace’ here denotes the Ace of Wands within Liber 777's table of the Court Cards and their celestial dominion, attributed to the realm of Spirit (31bis) at the head of the suit of Fire. The Ace is the root of the powers of Fire—the pure, originating spark of will and energy before it divides into the numbered cards. It corresponds to Kether in the suit's little tree, the seed from which the whole fiery sequence unfolds.
tables: LXXI. Court Cards of the Tarot, with the Spheres of their Celestial Dominion - Wands

achodraon.summary: Nocturnal angelic Lord of Libra within the Airy Triplicity.
achodraon.description: Achodraon is the night-governor of Libra among the angelic Lords of the Triplicities. As the cardinal member of the Air trine by night, Libra's open scales are weighed in darkness — the private conscience judging itself when no one watches; Achodraon presides over this nocturnal, inward balancing of justice.

aclahayr.summary: A genius of the Nuctemeron's fourth hour, set by Crowley at Cancer.
aclahayr.description: Aclahayr is listed among the genii of the fourth hour of the Nuctemeron, the “Day Illumined by Night” attributed to Apollonius of Tyana and transmitted by Éliphas Lévi. He is reckoned among the genii of the fourth hour, but the tradition has not handed down a definite office for him, and none is here supplied. Crowley ranks these hour-genii along the zodiacal paths in 777 (Table CLXXIII), where Aclahayr stands at Cancer (Cheth).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

acquisitio.summary: Geomantic figure 'Gain' — attributed to Jupiter; profit, success, attainment.
acquisitio.description: Acquisitio, 'gain' or 'acquisition,' is one of the sixteen figures of geomancy, attributed to Jupiter and associated with Sagittarius. Its open, outward-flowing form is among the most fortunate of the figures, signifying profit, success, the attainment of what is sought, and the increase of worldly goods. It is the geomantic emblem of expansion and good fortune, the gathering-in of what one desires.
tables: XLIX. Lineal Figures of the Planets, &c., and Geomany

ad-al-akhbiyah.summary: Sa'd al-Akhbiya, 'the luck of the tents' — the last of the four Fortunes, in Aquarius.
ad-al-akhbiyah.description: Sa'd al-Akhbiya, 'the fortune of the tents' or 'of the hidden things,' is the fourth of the lucky mansions, set in the path of Aquarius (Tzaddi). A station of concealment and of homes, it was read as favourable for things kept secret, for the besieging and the freeing of the bound, and for the mending of estates — the sheltering fortune of the water-bearer.
tables: CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon

adeptus-exemptus.summary: 7°=4, the grade of Chesed — the Exempt Adept, master of the whole lower Tree.
adeptus-exemptus.description: The Adeptus Exemptus is the grade of the A∴A∴ attributed to Chesed, the sphere of Mercy and Jupiter. It is the summit of the second order, in which the adept has perfected the management of his life and powers and stands ready, having exhausted all that the manifest universe can teach, at the very brink of the Abyss. Before him lies the supreme renunciation: to surrender all he has built and attained in order to cross over and be reborn as a Master of the Temple.

adeptus-major.summary: 6°=5, the grade of Geburah — the Greater Adept; mastery of magical force.
adeptus-major.description: The Adeptus Major is the grade attributed to Geburah, the sphere of Severity and Mars. Here the adept, having attained the central vision of Tiphareth, develops and wields magical power and the strength of will, learning to direct force with discipline and severity. It is a station of considerable danger, for the energies now mastered can inflate the ego as readily as they serve the Work.

adeptus-minor.summary: 5°=6, the grade of Tiphareth — the Adept of the Knowledge and Conversation of the Angel.
adeptus-minor.description: The Adeptus Minor is the grade attributed to Tiphareth, the harmonising solar centre of the Tree. Its great task and threshold is the Knowledge and Conversation of the Holy Guardian Angel — the conscious union of the human self with its divine genius, toward which the operation of Liber Samekh is directed. Attainment of this grade marks the adept's true rebirth: the lower self is at last linked, through the heart of the Sun, to the light above.

adjuchas.summary: Rocks — the Nuctemeron genius of the eleventh hour presiding over rocks, set by Crowley at Aquarius.
adjuchas.description: In the Nuctemeron — the “Day Illumined by Night” ascribed to Apollonius of Tyana and preserved by Éliphas Lévi — Adjuchas is numbered among the genii of the eleventh hour, the spirit of rocks. He governs the rocks and the stony bones of the earth. Crowley arranges the twelve hours and their genii upon the paths of the Tree (777, Table CLXXIII), placing him at Aquarius (Tzaddi).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

administrative-intelligence.summary: The Thirty-second Path — the Administrative Intelligence of Tav, directing the seven planets.
administrative-intelligence.description: The Thirty-second Path is the Administrative or Serving Intelligence (Sekhel Neevad, the 'attending' Intelligence), attributed to the letter Tav and the planet Saturn, the path of The Universe (The World) joining Yesod to Malkuth. The Sepher Yetzirah says it directs and associates the motions of the seven planets, governing each in its own proper course. The last and lowest of the paths, sealed with the Saturnine cross of Tav, it is the great administrator — the ordering ground that ministers to the whole machinery of the heavens, completing the Tree and binding the worlds into one working order.
tables: XIII. Paths of the Sefer Yetzirah

admirable.summary: The First Path — the Admirable or Hidden Intelligence of Kether, the inconceivable Crown.
admirable.description: In the 'Thirty-two Paths of Wisdom' appended to the Sepher Yetzirah, the First Path is named the Admirable or Hidden Intelligence (Sekhel Muphla), assigned to Kether, the Crown. It is the primal radiance that confers the comprehension of the First Principle which has no beginning, and which no created mind can wholly attain — for to know it fully would be to stand outside creation altogether. Crowley keeps this title at the summit of the Tree as the marker of that which is admirable precisely because it is forever concealed: the Light that gives the very power to understand, yet remains itself beyond understanding.
tables: XIII. Paths of the Sefer Yetzirah

adonis.summary: Adonis, the beautiful dying-and-rising youth — beloved of Aphrodite, the slain god of vegetation.
adonis.description: Adonis is the beautiful youth beloved of Aphrodite, slain by a boar and mourned each year, whose death and return mirror the dying and reviving of vegetation. Spread across Malkuth, Virgo, and Tiphareth, he belongs to the great company of slain-and-risen gods — Tammuz, Attis, Osiris — whose passion marks the turning of the seasons. He is youthful beauty cut down in its prime and restored, the perennial emblem of nature's death and rebirth.

ae.summary: The diphthongal sound-value 'AE' — Crowley's English transcription for the Coptic letter set at Chesed in Liber 777 table LI.
ae.description: In table LI, Crowley extends the Hebrew alphabet's correspondences to the Coptic letters, listing each Coptic glyph's English phonetic value beside it. 'AE' is the Latin transliteration he assigns at the fourth position — Chesed, the merciful Jupiterian sphere — most plausibly representing the Coptic ligature for the alpha-epsilon diphthong (αε), which in late Coptic-Greek practice often stood at this place in the abjadic count. As a glossary entry it is not a name or god but a sound: the open, lifting vowel-pair, allotted by Crowley to the sphere of expansion and beneficence on the principle that the alphabetic and sephirothic columns of 777 must align rank for rank.
tables: LI. English Equivalent of the Coptic Alphabet

aecus.summary: Aeacus, judge of the dead — the just king who weighs the souls of the West, at Libra.
aecus.description: Aeacus is one of the three judges of the dead in the Greek underworld, a king famed in life for his piety and justice, set after death to judge the souls of Europe. Referred to Lamed and Libra, the sign of the balance, he embodies the weighing and judging of the departed. With Minos and Rhadamanthus he holds the scales of the afterlife, rendering to each soul its due.

agares.summary: The second spirit of the Goetia, a duke of Aries who teaches all tongues and turns back fugitives.
agares.description: Agares is the second spirit of the Goetia, a duke ruling in the East under the decans of Aries. His office is to teach all languages, to bring back those who have fled and to halt those in flight, to overthrow dignities both temporal and spiritual, and to cause earthquakes. He is shown as a venerable old man riding upon a crocodile and bearing a goshawk on his fist. As one of the spirits of the first sign he figures speech, motion and the sudden checking of flight — the power that gives and withholds the tongue and the road.

agate.summary: The banded chalcedony of Mercury — layered, protective, many-patterned.
agate.description: Agate, a banded chalcedony, is attributed to the path of Beth and Mercury — its endlessly varied concentric layers and figures (the famous 'eye' agates) suiting the Mercurial principle of multiplicity, pattern, and communication. Worn since antiquity as a protective and grounding amulet, it gathers the swift Mercurial virtue into a banded, earthbound stone; esoterically it is the gem of patterned intelligence and steady protection.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

agla-alhim.summary: The names of strength at Geburah: the everlasting might of God and the Elohim of severity.
agla-alhim.description: Geburah, the sphere of Mars, severity, and burning judgment, carries two divine names of power. AGLA is a notariqon of the Hebrew sentence Atah Gibor Le-Olahm Adonai—"Thou art mighty forever, O Lord"—a formula long used in protective and banishing rites, fitting for the warrior-sphere whose virtue is courage and whose work is the destruction of all that is impure. ALHIM (Elohim) is the plural creative name of the Godhead, the host of mighty ones through whom the divine will is enforced. Set at the fifth Sephirah, the two names gird the magician in the strength of the unconquerable, the sword that defends and the fire that purges.

agni.summary: The Vedic god of fire and the sacrificial flame; the elemental principle Tejas.
agni.description: Agni is the Vedic god of fire — of the hearth, the lightning, and above all the sacrificial flame — the divine priest who bears the offerings of mortals up to the gods and so mediates between earth and heaven. As an elemental power he personifies Tejas, the fiery Tattva, the principle of heat, light, and transformation. Ancient and ever-young, kindled afresh at every sacrifice, he is the living tongue of the divine fire that consumes and purifies.
tables: XXII. Small Selection of Hindu Deities

agni-bhawana.summary: Agni-bhāvanā — the meditation upon the fire-element, set at the path of Fire.
agni-bhawana.description: Agni-Bhawana is the 'cultivation of the fire-element' among the Hindu/Buddhist Results, attributed to the path of Shin and the element Fire. It is the concentrative meditation upon fire — its heat, light and transforming, consuming nature taken as the inward object — by which the mind enters absorption and gains the faculties associated with the element.
