One of the elemental bhāvanās, it answers to the fire-kasiṇa; set at Fire, it figures the meditator's union with the principle of energy and transformation.
tables: XXIV. Certain of the Hindu/Buddhist Results

ahapshi.summary: Ahapshi — one of the Egyptian decan/elemental names Crowley lists at the Earthy quadrant in table XIX.
ahapshi.description: Ahapshi appears in Crowley's table XIX ('Selection of Egyptian Gods') at position 32bis (Earth), alongside the more familiar Earth-attributions like Geb and Satem. Its precise Egyptian source is not securely attested in modern Egyptology — the name is plausibly a Hellenistic-Coptic distortion (possibly of Apep / Apophis, or of a local theophoric form) preserved through the magical literature Crowley drew on (Budge, Mathers's Egyptian sources, and the Sepher Sephiroth). The entry preserves it as it stands in 777: an Egyptian name fixed at the Earthy supernal quarter, whose deeper identity Crowley left unannotated.

aharph.summary: Name of the last decan of Taurus, where fixed earth grows heavy and Saturnine, and growth stalls.
aharph.description: Aharph is 777's name for the last decan of Taurus (20°–30°), where fixed earth grows heavy. Saturn rules this face and it bears the Seven of Disks—Failure—the fatigue of fertility overworked, growth that stalls and must be left fallow. Among the thirty-six Hermetic decan-faces it stands for the exhaustion that precedes the Bull's release into the airy duality of Gemini.
tables: CLXXII. Egyptian Names of the Cadent Decans

ahepi.summary: Hapi, a Son of Horus and namesake of the Nile flood, attributed to Aquarius, the Water-Bearer.
ahepi.description: Ahepi is a form of Hapi, the baboon-headed member of the Four Sons of Horus, guardian of the lungs in the canopic jars under the protection of Nephthys. The name is shared with Hapi the great androgynous god of the Nile inundation, bringer of the fertilising flood—and 777's placement at Tzaddi/Aquarius, the Water-Bearer who pours the celestial stream from his urn, plainly draws on that resonance of poured, life-giving water. Whether as the funerary genius or as the spirit of the flood, Ahepi belongs to the Egyptian mysteries of preservation and renewal through water.

ahoz.summary: Diurnal angelic Lord of Sagittarius within the Fiery Triplicity.
ahoz.description: Ahoz is the day-governor of Sagittarius among the angelic Lords of the Triplicities. As the mutable, far-ranging member of the Fire trine, Sagittarius by day is the questing flame of the archer under the open sky; Ahoz presides over this aspiring, outward-flying fire that seeks its mark in the light.

aib.summary: Aib — the heart, seat of conscience weighed in the judgment, attributed to the central Sephiroth.
aib.description: The Aib (Ab), the heart, is in Egyptian thought the seat of thought, will, and conscience — the part weighed against the feather of Ma'at in the judgment hall of Osiris to determine the soul's fate. Set in 777 across the central Sephiroth (Chesed through Hod, the realm of the reasoning soul), it is the moral and intellectual core of the being, the inner witness upon which all turns.
tables: CXVI. Egyptial Attribution of Parts of the Soul

aim.summary: The twenty-third spirit of the Goetia, a duke of Scorpio who makes men witty and sets cities ablaze.
aim.description: Aim (also Aym or Haborym) is the twenty-third spirit of the Goetia, a great and strong duke of the decans of Scorpio. He makes men witty and gives true answers concerning private matters, and he sets cities, castles and great places on fire. He appears with three heads — a serpent, a man bearing two stars upon his brow, and a calf — riding upon a viper and bearing a firebrand with which he kindles his flames. A spirit of the fierce water-sign, he unites cunning counsel with the power of conflagration.

ain.summary: The first Veil of the Negative: absolute Nothingness prior to all being.
ain.description:
Ain (Hebrew אין, “not” or “nothing”) is the first of the three Veils of the Negative that the Qabalah places ‘above’ Kether, before existence itself. It names not an empty space but the absolute absence of all attributes—no form, no number, no light, not even the potential for these. Where ordinary thought reaches for a first cause, the Qabalist instead posits a pure negation so complete that it cannot be said even to ‘be.’ Ain is the apophatic ground of the whole system: every positive statement about God is, at this level, dissolved.

In practice the Veils are a discipline of un-knowing. The aspirant who ascends the Tree finally confronts Ain as the recognition that the Source cannot be grasped by any faculty that grasps. Crowley aligned this with the Buddhist Śūnyatā and with the mystic’s ‘cloud of unknowing’—the point at which contemplation must surrender concept altogether.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

ain-soph.summary: The second Veil: the Limitless, infinity without boundary.
ain-soph.description:
Ain Soph (אין סוף, ‘without end / no limit’) is the second Veil of the Negative. If Ain is sheer Nothing, Ain Soph is that Nothing conceived as boundless—infinite extension without edge, quantity, or division. It is the classical Qabalistic name for the unknowable Godhead in its utter transcendence, the Limitless from which, by a self-contraction (the later doctrine of tzimtzum), room for a created cosmos is made.

The progression Ain → Ain Soph → Ain Soph Aur stages the unthinkable into the merely unimaginable into the first dawning of light, giving the contemplative a graded ladder down from absolute negation toward the Crown. Ain Soph marks the middle rung: being is not yet, but infinity already ‘is.’
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

ain-soph-aur.summary: The third Veil: the Limitless Light that concentrates into Kether.
ain-soph-aur.description:
Ain Soph Aur (אין סוף אור, ‘Limitless Light’) is the third and final Veil of the Negative, the threshold where boundless nothing first becomes radiance. Here the infinite concentrates itself to a single point—the primordial spark that crystallises as Kether, the Crown and first Sephirah. The image is of light withdrawing into a centre so as to shine outward as a created world.

The triad of Veils thus describes the descent from un-being to the brink of being: Nothing, Limitless Nothing, Limitless Light. For the practitioner it is the metaphysical preface to the Tree of Life, reminding us that the highest Sephirah is itself only the first condensation of a Light whose source remains forever veiled.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

air.summary: The mediating element of intellect, breath, and communication.
air.description:
Air is the element of intellect, communication, and the breath of life—warm and moist, mobile, mediating between Fire and Water. In 777 it corresponds to the letter Aleph and path 11, to the Tatwa Vayu (a blue circle), and to the eastern quarter. Its weapon is the Dagger or Sword, its archangel Raphael, its elemental king Paralda, its creatures the sylphs.

The Hebrew Ruach means at once ‘air,’ ‘breath,’ and ‘spirit,’ and the same triple sense runs through pneuma and spiritus: the invisible medium of thought, word, and life. Air is the realm of ideas in motion, of analysis and exchange, the swift connective tissue that carries one thing to another.
tables: CX. Elements and Quarters per the Sepher Yetzirah
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

ajna.summary: Ajna — the brow chakra, the third eye of command, attributed to Chokmah.
ajna.description: Ajna, the 'command' chakra between the brows, is the sixth wheel — the 'third eye' of inner vision, seat of the mind's higher light and of the union of the lunar and solar currents (Ida and Pingala). Set in 777 at Chokmah, the supernal Wisdom, it governs intuition, insight, and the direct perception that transcends the senses.

akasa.summary: Akasha — the fifth Tattva, Spirit or aether; the all-pervading subtle space.
akasa.description: Akasa (Akasha) is the fifth and subtlest of the Tattvas, the element of Spirit or aether — the all-pervading 'space' out of which the four gross elements proceed and into which they dissolve again. Its symbol is the black or indigo egg, and in the yogic scheme it is the matrix of sound, the field of hearing, and the ground of the deepest meditation (akasha-dharana). On the Tree it answers to the descent of pure Spirit, the quintessence that contains and reconciles Fire, Water, Air, and Earth.
tables: XXII. Small Selection of Hindu Deities

akel.summary: Nocturnal angelic Lord of Cancer within the Watery Triplicity.
akel.description: Akel is the night-governor of Cancer among the angelic Lords of the Triplicities, complement to the day-Lord Raadar. As the cardinal source of the Water trine by night, Cancer is the moonlit tide, feeling at its most receptive and remembering in the dark; Akel presides over this nocturnal, inward flow of the waters.

albus.summary: Geomantic figure 'White' — attributed to Mercury; peace, wisdom, clarity.
albus.description: Albus, 'white,' is one of the sixteen geomantic figures, attributed to Mercury and associated with Gemini. A figure of peace, purity, and clear-headed wisdom, it signifies favourable counsel, the settling of disputes, and the bright, reflective intelligence of the airy Mercurial nature. It is reckoned a mild and beneficent figure, good for matters of thought, learning, and reconciliation.
tables: XLIX. Lineal Figures of the Planets, &c., and Geomany

alchemy.summary: The earthy Great Work of transmutation, the perfecting of metal and soul alike.
alchemy.description: Alchemy, here attributed to Earth (32 bis), is the art of transmutation—of base metal into gold, and, on the inner plane, of the unredeemed self into the spiritual gold of the perfected being. Rooted in Earth as the matter to be worked, it is the laboratory science of the Western mysteries, its furnaces and vessels mirroring the operations of dissolution and coagulation by which the soul is purified. Crowley read its whole symbolism as a veiled manual of initiation, the Stone being the attainment itself.

alcohol.summary: The fermented spirit, attributed to Tiphareth and Sol; sacrament and intoxicant.
alcohol.description:
Alcohol is placed at Tiphareth and the path of Sol — the solar centre — for wine is the oldest sacrament of the dying-and-rising god, the blood of Dionysus and of the Eucharist, the 'spirit' (the word is no accident) drawn from the fruit by the alchemy of fermentation. In due measure it is the loosener of the tongue and the heart, the inspirer of poets and the visible image of solar joy; in excess it is the destroyer of the very self it seemed to liberate. Esoterically it is the two-edged solar fire, ecstasy and ruin in one cup.

Caution: alcohol is a toxic, addictive drug responsible for vast harm; dependence is a serious disease. This entry treats its symbolism, not its use.
alcohol.caution: Toxic and addictive; major cause of disease and harm. Symbolic/historical entry only.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

alder.summary: The water-tree of the Moon—the alder that bleeds red, guardian of fords and the lunar threshold.
alder.description: The Alder is given to the Moon (Gimel, the High Priestess), a tree of riverbanks and marshes whose wood resists rot underwater and whose cut flesh turns from white to a startling blood-red. To the Celts it was a tree of Bran and of prophecy, set upon watery thresholds and made into whistles and pipes. Esoterically it suits the lunar path of Gimel—the water-loving guardian of crossings and fords, the threshold-tree between the dry land of consciousness and the deep of the unconscious.

alexandrite.summary: The colour-changing chrysoberyl of Gemini — the very gem of duality.
alexandrite.description: Alexandrite is attributed to the path of Zayin and Gemini — and no stone could better suit the sign of the Twins, for it changes colour with the light, green by day and red by lamplight, a single gem of two natures. This dramatic dualism makes it the perfect emblem of Gemini's mystery of the two that are one, the pair held within a single substance. The stone of doubleness and of the union of opposites.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

alim.summary: The lunar formula ALIM, the 'gods' of Yesod and the astral foundation.
alim.description: ALIM (אלים) is a Hebrew word for "gods" or "mighty ones," attributed in the formulae table to Yesod and the Moon. Yesod is the Treasure-house of Images, the astral foundation where the powers of the higher Sephiroth are stored and reflected before they crystallise in Malkuth; its formula names the plurality of forces that move beneath the lunar tides of the unconscious. As a magical word it gathers the changeable, image-making energies of the ninth Sephirah—the silver root of vision and of dream—under a single name of divine multiplicity.

alinkir.summary: Angel of the third face of Cancer, where emotional plenty thickens into stagnant luxury.
alinkir.description: Alinkir presides over the closing decan of Cancer (20–30°), where the Moon, ruler of the sign, meets the Four of Cups, *Luxury* — pleasure grown heavy, satiety bordering on stagnation. The Moon in its own sign saturates feeling until it ceases to move. Alinkir is the angel of contentment that risks becoming inert, the warning that still water grows stale.

all-22-trumps.summary: The whole of the Major Arcana, the 22 Trumps, attributed to Spirit and the 22 paths of the Tree.
all-22-trumps.description: ‘All 22 Trumps’ names the complete set of the Tarot's Major Arcana, the Atu, attributed in Liber 777 to the realm of Spirit (31bis) that crowns and unites the elements. The twenty-two trumps correspond to the twenty-two letters of the Hebrew alphabet and the twenty-two paths that join the ten Sephiroth upon the Tree of Life. Taken together they form a complete map of the soul's journey and of the forces of the cosmos—from the Fool's first step to the Universe's final dance—the pictorial alphabet of the whole Hermetic-Qabalistic system.
tables: XIV. General Attribution of the Tarot

all-anaphrodisiacs.summary: The class of substances that quell sexual desire, attributed to Virgo — sign of chastity and restraint.
all-anaphrodisiacs.description: Counterpart to the aphrodisiacs, "all anaphrodisiacs" — the substances that diminish or extinguish the sexual appetite — are placed at Yod, the path of the Hermit and the virgin sign of Virgo, whose nature is continence, purity, and self-contained discretion. The logic of the attribution is the symbolism of the Virgin: the cooling, withdrawing, abstemious power set opposite Venus's heat. Agents historically classed here include camphor, the bromides, and various sedative botanicals. Esoterically the class embodies the principle of restraint and sublimation — the turning-inward of generative force that the Hermit's solitary path requires.
all-anaphrodisiacs.caution: Historical/symbolic entry only — not medical advice. Some agents of this class (e.g. camphor, bromides) are toxic in excess.

all-aphrodisiacs.summary: The whole class of substances exciting sexual desire, attributed to Venus — the planet of love and generation.
all-aphrodisiacs.description: Under the Vegetable Drugs Crowley gathers "all aphrodisiacs" as a single correspondence and assigns them to Daleth, the path of Venus and the Empress, the sphere of love, beauty, and generative heat. The attribution is transparent: as Venus governs desire and fertility, so the drugs that kindle the sexual appetite belong to her column. Historically the category has held a wide spectrum — the comparatively benign botanicals such as damiana, yohimbé, and the mandrake of folklore, alongside genuinely dangerous agents such as cantharides ("Spanish fly"). Esoterically the class figures the magical principle of attraction itself — the Venusian force that draws bodies and souls into union, the same current that, refined, becomes the love that moves the Tree.
all-aphrodisiacs.caution: Historical/symbolic entry only — not medical advice. Substances once used as aphrodisiacs range from harmless to acutely poisonous (e.g. cantharides), and several can cause severe injury or death.

all-beasts-of-burden.summary: The ox, ass and mule of Taurus—patient labour and the uncomplaining bearing of weight in fixed earth.
all-beasts-of-burden.description: The beasts of burden are gathered at Taurus, the fixed-earth sign of the patient bull, and they figure the principle of steady, enduring service: the ox under the yoke, the ass beneath its load, the mule on the mountain path. Theirs is the virtue of Taurus made flesh—strength expressed not in conquest but in patient carrying, the slow reliable power that bears the world's weight without complaint. Esoterically they mark the labouring body and the disciplined endurance on which all higher building rests, the humble strength that takes up the burden of the Work and does not set it down.

all-beasts-of-transport.summary: The horse and camel of Cancer—the bearers of motion, the living vehicles of the Chariot.
all-beasts-of-transport.description: The beasts of transport are attributed to Cancer, the path of the Chariot (Cheth), and they are the creatures that carry the traveller forward—horse, camel, and all the steeds that turn the wheels of the Chariot of the soul. Where the beasts of burden merely bear weight, these bear it onward; they are motion harnessed, the means by which the will is conveyed across the world. Esoterically they figure the vehicles of consciousness, the bodies and forces the adept yokes to the chariot of attainment, drawing the self toward its goal under the sheltering, lunar protection of Cancer.

all-carminatives.summary: The aromatic remedies that relieve digestive wind, attributed to Leo — the sun's warmth in the belly.
all-carminatives.description: "All carminatives" — the warm, aromatic substances that ease flatulence and settle the stomach — are assigned to Teth, the path of Strength and the fiery, sunlit sign of Leo. The attribution reads the gentle inner fire of digestion as a solar, leonine warmth: the carminatives kindle and order the heat of the belly. The class is among the most benign in the table, comprising culinary aromatics such as fennel, dill, caraway, ginger, peppermint, and anise. Esoterically these mild, comforting agents figure the well-tempered vital fire — Leo's heart-warmth applied to the body's economy, strength expressed as easy digestion rather than violence.

all-carrion-birds.summary: The vulture-kin of Netzach—devourers of death sacred to the Mother, returning the dead to life.
all-carrion-birds.description: The carrion birds—vultures and their kind—are placed at Netzach, the Venusian sphere of nature and love, an attribution that turns on their hidden maternal aspect. In Egypt the vulture was the very hieroglyph of 'mother' and the bird of Mut and Nekhbet, for the carrion-eater performs love's secret labour: it consumes the corpse and so returns the dead back into the living stream of nature, an act of fierce tenderness. Thus these birds, repellent on the surface, belong to the goddess of life and generation. Esoterically they teach that even decay is taken up into love, that nothing is wasted, and that the Mother reclaims all her children.

all-cereals.summary: The grain of the Kingdom—all cereals of Malkuth, the harvested bread of earthly life.
all-cereals.description: All cereals are attributed to Malkuth, the tenth Sephirah, the Kingdom and the manifest earth. Wheat, barley, and corn are the gift of Demeter and Ceres, the cultivated grain that feeds humankind and that, cut down and buried to rise again, became the central mystery of Eleusis. As the staff of life and the substance of bread, cereals are the very type of Malkuth's office: the divine reduced to daily nourishment, spirit eaten as bread. Esoterically the grain is the indwelling life of the Kingdom, slain and resurrected in every loaf.

all-cerebral-excitants.summary: The stimulants of mind and brain, attributed to Mercury and Aries — intellect and the head.
all-cerebral-excitants.description: "All cerebral excitants" — the drugs that quicken the mind and rouse the brain — are placed across Beth, the Mercurial path of the Magus (the sphere of intellect and swift thought), and Heh, the path of the Emperor in Aries, the sign that rules the head. The double attribution unites the organ (the Aries-governed head) with the faculty (Mercurial reason): together they make the seat of mental excitation. The class ranges from the everyday — caffeine, the xanthines of coffee, tea, and kola — to far more potent and hazardous stimulants. Esoterically it figures the kindling of the higher mind, the Mercurial spark that, well-governed, illuminates and, ungoverned, burns itself out in restlessness.
all-cerebral-excitants.caution: Historical/symbolic entry only — not medical advice. This class includes powerful and addictive stimulants that can cause serious harm, dependence, or death.

all-diuretics.summary: The substances that increase the flow of urine, attributed to Aquarius — the water-bearer.
all-diuretics.description: "All diuretics" — the agents that promote the passing of water — are fittingly assigned to Tzaddi, the path of the Star and the sign of Aquarius, the Water-Bearer who pours out the urn. The symbolism is direct: the sign that empties the vessel governs the drugs that flush the body's waters. The class includes such botanicals as juniper, dandelion, parsley, and uva-ursi. Esoterically it figures the principle of cleansing release and circulation — the Aquarian outpouring that carries away what is stagnant and renews the inner streams.

all-dull.summary: The dull, grounding odours of Earth—heavy, quiet scents that settle and root, the perfume-class of the material world.
all-dull.description: "All dull odours" are attributed to the element Earth (32 bis). Where fire's perfumes blaze and air's lift away, the earthy scents are heavy, muted, and grounding—the smell of soil, moss, root, and stone, fragrances that settle the senses rather than excite them. Esoterically these dull odours are the olfactory signature of Earth itself: the quiet, weighty, rooting scents of the manifest world, calling the attention downward and inward to the body and the ground.

all-emmenogogues.summary: The substances that promote menstrual flow, attributed to the Moon — ruler of the monthly tides.
all-emmenogogues.description: "All emmenagogues" — the agents that provoke or restore the menstrual flow — are placed at Gimel, the path of the High Priestess and of the Moon, which governs the rhythmic monthly tides of the body as it governs the tides of the sea. The attribution follows the ancient association of the lunar cycle with menstruation. The class is among the most perilous in the table, for many traditional emmenagogues — pennyroyal, rue, savin, tansy — were employed as abortifacients and are powerfully toxic. Esoterically it figures the lunar power over generation and its rhythms, the dark, regulating tide of Yesod and the veiled priestess.
all-emmenogogues.caution: Historical/symbolic entry only — not medical advice. Many traditional emmenagogues (pennyroyal, rue, savin, tansy) are powerful poisons and abortifacients; ingestion has caused organ failure and death.

all-evil-odours.summary: The foul odours of Saturn—dark, heavy, repellent scents proper to the saturnine sphere of death and dissolution.
all-evil-odours.description: "All evil odours" are attributed to Saturn (Tav, the Universe)—the foul, heavy, repellent scents (asafoetida, sulphur, the reek of decay) that belong to the saturnine mysteries of death, dissolution, and the underworld. In magic such odours were burned to repel, to bind, or to summon the darker powers, and they mark the sphere of Saturn as the lift of frankincense marks the Sun. Esoterically these are the perfumes of the dark threshold—the stench of putrefaction that is, in the alchemical work, the necessary first stage from which the gold is at last won.

all-exclusively-phallic.summary: A note on Yesod's deities — all of them exclusively phallic, expressing the generative Foundation.
all-exclusively-phallic.description: This entry preserves Crowley's note that the deities attributed to Yesod are “all exclusively phallic.” Yesod is the Foundation, the lunar sphere of the vital and generative forces, the seat of sexuality and the reproductive power on the Tree. Its gods are therefore figures of male potency and the seed of life — the divine generative current concentrated in the sphere that transmits the forces of the Tree into manifestation.

all-fiery-odours.summary: The fiery odours of the element Fire—hot, kindling, pungent scents that burn and rouse the spirit of Shin.
all-fiery-odours.description: "All fiery odours" are attributed to the element Fire (Shin). Hot, sharp, and kindling—pepper, dragon's blood, the resins that crackle and flare—these are the scents that rouse, inflame, and energise, the olfactory signature of the active, consuming, spiritual element. Esoterically the fiery odours are the perfume of will and ardour, the kindling smoke that lifts the spirit into the flame of Shin and drives the energy of the rite toward heaven.

all-fugitive-odors.summary: The fleeting odours of Mercury—volatile, quicksilver scents that rise and vanish like thought itself.
all-fugitive-odors.description: "All fugitive odours" are attributed to Mercury (Beth, the Magus). Volatile and swift, these are the scents that flash upon the air and are gone—the fresh top-notes, the quick herbs and citrus oils that will not be held—mirroring the mercurial nature: mobile, communicative, and never grasped. Esoterically the fugitive odours are the perfume of the quicksilver mind, the fleeting fragrance of Mercury that, like a thought or a spoken word, is bright in the instant and away upon the wind.

all-giant-trees.summary: The great enduring trees of Taurus—towering, slow-grown strength rooted in the patient earth.
all-giant-trees.description: All giant trees are attributed to Taurus (Vav, the Hierophant), the fixed earthy sign of slow, massive, enduring growth. The redwood, the oak, the cedar—trees that outlast empires—embody the bull's patient, generative power and the Hierophant's office as the stable trunk of tradition that bears the life of generations. Esoterically the giant tree is the firm, deep-rooted strength of Taurus made visible: that which grows imperceptibly yet immensely, and stands.

all-glorious-odours.summary: The glorious odours of the Sun—radiant, splendid, kingly scents that lift the heart toward the solar light.
all-glorious-odours.description: "All glorious odours" are attributed to the Sun (Resh). These are the radiant, splendid, magnificent perfumes—frankincense, cinnamon, the golden resins—whose smoke is the very breath of glory and worship, fit for the solar sphere of beauty, sovereignty, and the harmonised heart. Esoterically the glorious odours are the perfume of the Sun's own splendour, the fragrance of adoration and triumph that rises toward Tiphareth, gold made scent.

all-good-things.summary: Among the contents of the highest heavens — the sum of all good gathered above.
all-good-things.description: 'All good things' appears in the table of the contents of the heavens as a summary of the treasures stored in the supernal heaven — the totality of blessing, life, and peace held in Araboth and poured down upon creation. It names the highest heaven's character as the storehouse of every good, the source from which all benefit descends to the lower worlds.
tables: XCV. Contents of the Heavens of Assiah

all-hot-pungent-odours.summary: The hot, pungent odours of Mars—sharp, aggressive, biting scents that sting and rouse to action.
all-hot-pungent-odours.description: "All hot pungent odours" are attributed to Mars (Pe, the Tower). Biting and aggressive—pepper, the acrid resins, the scents that sting the nostril and quicken the blood—these are the martial perfumes of war, energy, and severity. Esoterically the hot pungent odours are the perfume of Mars's force: the sharp, rousing smoke that breaks complacency and drives the will to action, the olfactory edge of the sword.

all-narcotics.summary: The drugs of sleep, stupor, and dream, attributed to Pisces — the dissolving, oceanic sign.
all-narcotics.description: "All narcotics" — the substances that dull sensation and bring sleep, stupor, and dream — are assigned to Qoph, the path of the Moon (the trump) and the watery, dreaming sign of Pisces, the dissolution of waking consciousness into the oceanic deep. The attribution captures the narcotic's essential gesture: the drowning of the daylight mind in the Piscean waters, the descent into the lunar underworld of Qoph where forms melt and the sleeper drifts. The class includes opium and its kindred, and by extension the great hypnotics and soporifics. Esoterically it figures the seductive descent into the unconscious — the dissolving mercy that may open visionary depths or close in lethal oblivion.
all-narcotics.caution: Historical/symbolic entry only — not medical advice. Narcotics are among the most addictive and lethal of substances; overdose readily causes fatal respiratory depression.

all-odoriferous-roots.summary: The fragrant roots of Yesod—the hidden, earth-deep scents of the Foundation, vitality drawn up from the dark.
all-odoriferous-roots.description: "All odoriferous roots" are attributed to Yesod, the Foundation—the lunar storehouse of the vital and astral life. Roots are the hidden, sustaining part of the plant, drawing life from the dark; the fragrant roots (orris, ginseng, valerian) are the foundation-scents, deep and grounding, drawn up from beneath. Esoterically the odoriferous roots are the perfume of Yesod's secret vitality—the fragrance of what grows unseen and feeds the whole, the hidden generative base made scent.

all-poisonous-plants.summary: The venomous flora of Scorpio—poison-plants of Death, whose toxin is at once bane and the seed of transformation.
all-poisonous-plants.description:
All poisonous plants are attributed to Scorpio (Nun, Death), the sign of venom, death, and regeneration. Scorpio rules the serpent's bite and the alchemy of putrefaction by which life is broken down and remade; its plants carry the same double signature, for the poison that kills in one dose may heal or transform in another—the pharmakon that is both remedy and bane. Esoterically the poisonous plant is the Scorpionic mystery in vegetable form: the toxin that dissolves the old that the new may rise.

Caution: this is a symbolic correspondence. The plants it points to—nightshade, hemlock, aconite and their kind—are genuinely deadly and must never be handled or ingested.
all-poisonous-plants.caution: Refers to genuinely deadly plants (nightshade, hemlock, aconite, etc.). Symbolic correspondence only — never handle or ingest.

all-purges.summary: The purgatives that flush and empty the body, attributed to Water — the dissolving, cleansing element.
all-purges.description: "All purges" — the cathartics and purgatives that violently empty the bowels — are placed at Mem, the path of the Hanged Man and the element of Water, the dissolving, downward-flowing principle that washes away. The attribution reads purgation as a watery flushing, the body's tide turned to cleansing. The class spans the mild (senna, rhubarb, castor oil) and the drastic and dangerous (croton oil, colocynth, jalap, the resinous cathartics that can scour to the point of injury). Esoterically it figures purification by release — the Mem-water that drowns and dissolves the old in order to renew, the reversed posture of the Hanged Man who lets go.
all-purges.caution: Historical/symbolic entry only — not medical advice. Drastic purgatives (croton oil, colocynth, jalap) are violently toxic and can cause severe injury or death.

all-reptiles.summary: The cold-blooded creatures of Scorpio—serpent-kin of the lower waters, emblems of death and regeneration.
all-reptiles.description: All reptiles are attributed to Scorpio, the fixed-water sign of death, sexuality and regeneration, and they are the serpent-kin: snakes, lizards, crocodiles and their cold-blooded fellows that creep close to the earth and shed their skins to be renewed. Cold of blood and ancient of line, they belong to the oldest, most instinctual strata of life, the reptilian deep beneath the warm-blooded mind. Under Scorpio they carry the sign's double meaning—venom and healing, death and the casting-off of the old self. Esoterically the reptile is the primal life-force in its most archaic form, that which sloughs the dead skin so that the new may live.

all-sakti.summary: Shakti, the supreme creative power of the Goddess, seated in the supernal Mother Binah.
all-sakti.description: All Sakti—the Shakti—is attributed to Binah, the third Sephirah and the supernal Mother. In the Hindu system Shakti is the dynamic creative energy of the Godhead, the feminine power without which the static Shiva cannot act; she is the womb and the force of all becoming. Set at Binah, the great sea of Understanding through which the formless force of Chokmah takes its first form, she is the cosmic Mother in her aspect of active power, the divine energy that gives birth to the whole manifested universe.
tables: XXII. Small Selection of Hindu Deities

all-scarlet-flowers.summary: The flame-flowers of the element Fire—all scarlet blooms blazing with the spirit of Shin.
all-scarlet-flowers.description: All scarlet flowers are attributed to the element Fire (Shin, the Aeon / Judgement). Their burning red is the visible signature of fire among the plants—the poppy, the geranium, the hibiscus—each a small flame lifted upon a stem. As Fire is the element of spirit, energy, and the all-consuming will, the scarlet flower is its gentlest embodiment: beauty that burns. Esoterically these blooms are the fire of life flowering into colour, the ardour of Shin made visible in the field.

all-soft-voluptuous-odours.summary: The soft voluptuous odours of Venus—sweet, sensual, caressing scents that melt the senses into love.
all-soft-voluptuous-odours.description: "All soft voluptuous odours" are attributed to Venus (Daleth, the Empress). These are the sweet, sensuous, enveloping perfumes—rose, sandalwood, the heavy florals—that soothe, allure, and awaken desire, the very breath of Venusian beauty and pleasure. Esoterically the soft voluptuous odours are the perfume of love and the senses fulfilled, the caressing sweetness of the Empress that draws the soul gently toward union and delight.

all-sweet-virginal-odours.summary: The sweet virginal odours of the Moon—pure, fresh, chaste scents proper to the High Priestess and her silver light.
all-sweet-virginal-odours.description: "All sweet virginal odours" are attributed to the Moon (Gimel, the High Priestess). Light, fresh, and chaste—the pale florals, the cool clean sweetness untouched by heaviness or heat—these are the perfumes of purity and of the virgin Moon, fitting the sphere of the veiled Priestess. Esoterically the sweet virginal odours are the perfume of the chaste lunar mysteries, the clear and modest fragrance of the soul as yet unstained, the scent of the silver light behind the veil.

all-water-plants.summary: The flora of the element Water—all water-plants of Mem, life adrift upon the great deep.
all-water-plants.description: All water plants are attributed to the element Water (Mem, the Hanged Man). Rooted in the deep or floating free upon it—the lotus, the reed, the water-lily, the rush—they live wholly within the medium of feeling, reflection, and the unconscious that Water signifies. As Mem is the hanged, immersed consciousness that surrenders to the flood, the water-plant is the soul that takes its life directly from the great waters. Esoterically these plants are the vegetation of the astral sea, drawing being from the formless depths.

alldeboran.summary: Aldebaran, the Follower — the red eye of the Bull and a Royal Star, marking the mansion al-Dabaran.
alldeboran.description: Aldebaran (al-Dabaran, 'the follower,' so named because it follows the Pleiades across the sky) is the fiery orange eye of Taurus, here set in the path of Taurus (Vau). One of the four 'Royal Stars' of Persia, watcher of the eastern quarter, it has always borne a martial, kingly fire — a star of honour and eloquence, and of the perils that attend high fortune. As a lunar mansion it was reckoned potent for the building up and the casting down of estates.
tables: CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon

alloces.summary: The fifty-second spirit of the Goetia, a lion-faced duke of Virgo who teaches astronomy.
alloces.description: Alloces (Allocer) is the fifty-second spirit of the Goetia, a strong and mighty duke of the decans of Virgo. He teaches astronomy and the liberal sciences and gives good familiars. He appears as a soldier or warrior with the face of a lion, red and flaming, riding upon a great horse; his eyes blaze with fire and he speaks with a hoarse voice. A spirit of the earthy sign, he is the fiery-faced teacher of the stars.

almond.summary: The lunar almond—pale nut of the Moon's path, kernel of hidden sweetness and watchful waiting.
almond.description: The Almond is attributed here to the Moon (Gimel, the High Priestess), distinct from the flowering almond of Kether. As the first tree to wake in the year and the model of the menorah's cups, the almond keeps a lunar character of vigilance and patient expectancy—the Hebrew shaqed, "almond," puns upon shoqed, "watchful." Its hard shell guarding a sweet kernel makes it an emblem of the hidden interior life that the lunar mysteries conceal. Esoterically the almond on Gimel's path is the secret sweetness behind the veil of the High Priestess, the watchful seed of the Moon.

almond-in-flower.summary: The first blossom of the year—the almond in flower at Kether, Aaron's budding rod and the Crown's first stirring of life.
almond-in-flower.description: The almond in flower is attributed to Kether, the Crown, and to Spirit (31 bis)—for the almond is the first tree to blossom, breaking into white-and-rose flower while winter still holds, the very image of life stirring at the topmost point before all else awakes. It is Aaron's rod that budded overnight, and the model of the seven-branched menorah, whose cups were "made like unto almonds." Esoterically the flowering almond is the first pure flash of being out of the Negative, the Crown's silent watchfulness blossoming into the promise of the whole Tree to come.

almost-any-female-image-shows-some-aspec.term: Almost any female image shows some aspect of Binah
almost-any-female-image-shows-some-aspec.displayTerm: Almost any female image shows some aspect of Binah
almost-any-female-image-shows-some-aspec.summary: A note on Binah's imagery — almost any female figure shows some aspect of the supernal Mother.
almost-any-female-image-shows-some-aspec.description: This entry preserves the principle that Binah, the third Sephirah, is so purely the archetypal feminine that almost any female image expresses some facet of it. Binah is the supernal Mother, the great sea of form and understanding, imaged as “a mature woman, a matron.” The note reminds the student that femaleness as such — receptivity, form-giving, the womb of manifestation — is the signature of this sphere wherever it appears.
tables: CXX. Magical Images of the Sephiroth

almost-any-male-image-shows-some-aspect-.term: Almost any male image shows some aspect of Chokmah
almost-any-male-image-shows-some-aspect-.displayTerm: Almost any male image shows some aspect of Chokmah
almost-any-male-image-shows-some-aspect-.summary: A note on Chokmah's imagery — almost any male figure shows some aspect of the supernal Father.
almost-any-male-image-shows-some-aspect-.description: This entry preserves the principle that Chokmah, the second Sephirah, is so purely the archetypal masculine that almost any male image expresses some facet of it. Chokmah is the supernal Father, the first active outpouring of force, the Yod and the bearded sage; its specific magical image is “a bearded male figure.” The note reminds the student that maleness as such — force, initiative, the begetting power — is the signature of this sphere wherever it appears.
tables: CXX. Magical Images of the Sephiroth

aloe.summary: The bitter healer of Libra—aloes, whose bitterness purges and balances upon the path of Justice.
aloe.description: The Aloe is attributed to Libra (Lamed, Justice / Adjustment). Its thick leaves yield both a soothing balm and a famously bitter purgative, a doubleness that suits the sign of the balance: medicine and bitterness held in equilibrium, the corrective that restores measure. Esoterically the aloe is the bitter draught of Justice—the discipline that heals by adjustment, the cleansing severity that brings the soul back into true weight.

aloes.summary: The fragrant aloes of the Moon—sweet aloes-wood smoke rising upon the lunar path of Gimel.
aloes.description: Aloes, as a perfume, is attributed to the Moon (Gimel, the High Priestess). Whether the precious aromatic aloes-wood of scripture or the bitter aloes burned as incense, it carries a deep, slightly bittersweet character here drawn into the lunar sphere of the veiled Priestess. Esoterically the aloes is a perfume of the lunar threshold—a sweet smoke touched with bitterness, fit for the mysteries of the Moon that mingle longing and concealment.

aloyar.summary: Nocturnal angelic Lord of Capricorn within the Earthy Triplicity.
aloyar.description: Aloyar is the night-governor of Capricorn among the angelic Lords of the Triplicities. As the cardinal member of the Earth trine by night, Capricorn is the mountain in shadow, ambition working silently and ceaselessly while others rest; Aloyar presides over this patient, unseen ascent.

alpha.summary: Alpha — a letter of the Coptic alphabet (a), which Crowley attributes to the path of Aleph (Air).
alpha.description: Alpha is a letter of the Coptic alphabet — the script in which the Egyptian language was written in the Christian era, the Greek alphabet adapted to Egyptian speech. It is the first letter, from Greek alpha. Crowley folds the Coptic alphabet into the great correspondence of letters and paths in 777 (Table LI), assigning Alpha to the path of Aleph (Air) on the Tree of Life, so that the Egyptian-Christian script takes its station among the Hebrew letters and the keys of the Tarot.
tables: LI. Names of the Coptic Letters

alphun.summary: Doves — the Nuctemeron genius of the eighth hour presiding over doves, set by Crowley at Scorpio.
alphun.description: Among the genii of the eighth hour in the Nuctemeron of Apollonius of Tyana, Alphun presides over doves. He governs the doves, the gentle birds of Venus and of peace. Lévi gives the roll of the hour-genii in his Transcendental Magic; Crowley tabulates them along the paths of the Tree (Table CLXXIII), assigning Alphun to Scorpio (Nun).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

also-the-cross.summary: The cross — included by Crowley among the lineal figures of Chokmah, the supernal Father.
also-the-cross.description: In table XLIX the entry at Chokmah reads (in essence) 'the Line, also the Cross,' folding the cross into Chokmah's family of lineal forms alongside the straight line — both being figures of extension and direction rather than enclosure. The cross is the line crossed by another line, the simplest possible articulation of two intersecting forces; in Crowley's Hermetic reading it is the lingam in its barest geometric statement, the active, phallic counterpart to the yonic circle. Its assignment to Chokmah — the lightning-flash, the Yod of YHVH — fits this exactly: the cross is the formal sign of generative direction in the supernal masculine.
tables: XLIX. Lineal Figures of the Planets, &c., and Geomany

also-the-diamond.summary: The diamond (rhombus) — another lineal figure folded into Binah's yonic family in table XLIX.
also-the-diamond.description: Crowley's lineal-figures column at Binah reads as a list — 'the Plane, also the Diamond, Oval, Circle, and other Yoni Symbols' — recognising that more than one closed geometric form belongs to the Mother. The diamond is the rhombus standing on its point: a closed quadrilateral whose pointed apexes invoke both the vesica piscis and the standing lozenge of the Goddess in folk art. Crowley folds it among Binah's yonic forms because it encloses space symmetrically — receptive, formative, gestating — and because in Hermetic emblem-books it long stood for the matter perfected in the Great Work.
tables: XLIX. Lineal Figures of the Planets, &c., and Geomany

also-the-mysteries-of-the-crucifixion.term: also the Mysteries of the Crucifixion
also-the-mysteries-of-the-crucifixion.displayTerm: also the Mysteries of the Crucifixion
also-the-mysteries-of-the-crucifixion.summary: 'also the Mysteries of the Crucifixion' — Crowley's trailing reference at Tiphareth in table XLV.
also-the-mysteries-of-the-crucifixion.description: In table XLV the cell at Tiphareth — the heart-sphere of the sacrificed-and-risen god — closes with 'also the Mysteries of the Crucifixion,' pointing to the central Christian mystery as one of the Tiphareth-powers in Western mysticism. The placement is consistent throughout 777: Tiphareth holds the figure of the divine made flesh and the willing death-and-rebirth, of which the crucifixion is the most luminous Western expression. The entry preserves Crowley's pointer.

also-the-tao.summary: The Tao as Crown — the Way made first principle at Kether.
also-the-tao.description: Where the Tao proper is referred to the negative Veils, it is also set at Kether, the Crown — the first positive emanation, the One that is the Way become a point of light. Here the nameless Tao takes its first nameable form as the supreme unity from which the polarity of Yang and Yin (Chokmah and Binah) will divide: the Way considered not as boundless void but as the primal source of being.

altar.summary: The double-cube of Taurus and Tiphareth—the basis of the temple, the place where the work is offered.
altar.description: The Altar is attributed to Taurus and to Tiphareth, and it is the foundation-piece of the temple: the double cube upon which the weapons are laid and the work performed, the fixed and solid base that supports the whole operation. Its earthy stability suits Taurus, while its station at the centre, Tiphareth, marks it as the heart of the working—the place of offering and exchange between the operator and the powers above. Ten cubes high or made as a double cube, the altar represents the manifest universe raised up as a place of sacrifice. Esoterically the Altar is the consecrated centre of the work, the solid ground on which the elements meet—the heart's place where what is below is offered up and what is above descends to meet it.
tables: XCV. Contents of the Heavens of Assiah

amaimon.summary: One of the four cardinal demon-kings — here ruling the element of Earth.
amaimon.description: Amaimon is one of the four great demon-kings of the quarters in the Goetic and Abramelin traditions, named alongside Oriens, Paimon, and Ariton (Egyn). In this attribution he is set to the element of Earth, governing the spirits of the South in many of the old grimoires. As a 'king,' he commands lower ranks of spirits and was held to be among the most powerful and perilous of the infernal hierarchy, to be approached only with the strictest precautions.

amaranth.summary: The unfading flower of Chokmah—amaranth, the bloom that never dies, emblem of immortal Wisdom.
amaranth.description: The Amaranth is given to Chokmah, the sphere of the supernal Father and primal Wisdom. Its Greek name, amarantos, means "unfading"—the legendary flower that never withers, and so since antiquity the very symbol of immortality and undying fame. Set at Chokmah, the highest active power, it signifies the deathless, ever-flowing life of pure Wisdom. Esoterically the amaranth is the imperishable bloom of the eternal, the wisdom that does not pass away.

amber.summary: Fossil resin of Cancer — captured sunlight and the origin of 'electricity'.
amber.description: Amber — fossilised tree-resin, often holding ancient life within it — is set at the path of Cheth and Cancer, the lunar, watery, memory-keeping sign. Warm and golden, it is sunlight preserved from a vanished age, an emblem of memory and the deep past that Cancer rules. The Greek for amber, elektron, gave its name to electricity itself, for rubbed amber draws light objects: the stone that first revealed the hidden electric force. Esoterically it is the keeper of time and the spark latent in matter.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

ambergris.summary: The exalted scent of the deep—ambergris of Kether and Pisces, rare gift of the sea, crown of all perfumes.
ambergris.description: Ambergris is attributed to Kether and to Pisces. A rare, waxy concretion born within the whale and cured by the ocean and sun until it gives a warm, marine, almost indescribable sweetness, it is the most exalted of natural fixatives—precious as gold, drawn from the sea, the very type of a treasure refined out of the deep. Its place at the Crown and at the watery sign of the deep is exact. Esoterically ambergris is the supreme perfume of the heights and the depths at once—the priceless essence ripened in the great waters and lifted to the Crown.

amdusias.summary: The sixty-seventh spirit of the Goetia, a duke of Aquarius whose unseen music sounds and whose voice is thunder.
amdusias.description: Amdusias (Amdukias) is the sixty-seventh spirit of the Goetia, a great duke of the decans of Aquarius. He gives concerts at the operator's command, causing the sound of all manner of musical instruments to be heard though none be seen, and he makes trees to bend and bow at his will. He appears in human form (or as a unicorn), and his voice is like thunder. A spirit of the airy sign, he is the master of unseen music and of the bending of trees.

ameshet.summary: Imsety, one of the Four Sons of Horus — human-headed guardian of the liver and the South.
ameshet.description: Ameshet (Imsety, Mesta) is one of the Four Sons of Horus, the human-headed genius of the canopic jars who guards the liver of the deceased and watches over the South, protected in turn by the goddess Isis. With his brothers Hapi, Duamutef, and Qebehsenuef he upholds the four quarters of the embalmed body and, by extension, the four pillars of the sky — a guardian of the integrity of the soul's vessel as it passes into the afterworld.

amethyst.summary: The violet stone of Jupiter and the spirit—sobriety, devotion, and transcendence.
amethyst.description: The amethyst is a violet quartz attributed to Jupiter and, by its purple, to the spiritualised high reaches of devotion and rulership. Its name derives from the Greek amethystos, ‘not drunken,’ from the ancient belief that it guarded against intoxication—an apt emblem for the clear, sober mind in service of the higher will. The royal purple of amethyst long made it a stone of bishops and kings, of temperance, dignity, and the elevation of the lower nature toward the divine.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

amission.summary: Geomantic figure 'Loss' — attributed to Venus; loss, letting-go, things passing away.
amission.description: Amissio, 'loss,' is one of the sixteen geomantic figures, attributed to Venus and associated with Taurus. The mirror-reverse of Acquisitio, its form is one of outflow and release; it signifies loss, the slipping-away of possessions, and matters that pass out of one's grasp. Yet, being of Venus, it can be favourable where loss is desired — the ending of a burden or the freeing of what was held too tightly.
tables: XLIX. Lineal Figures of the Planets, &c., and Geomany

amnesia.summary: Loss of memory, set under Binah and Saturn — the eclipse of the faculty of recollection.
amnesia.description: Amnesia, the loss of memory, is placed at Binah, the Saturnine sphere of Understanding. Traditional medical astrology gives Saturn dominion over memory, the bones, and the slow consolidating faculties of the mind; amnesia is therefore read as a failure or eclipse of that retaining, structuring power — the dark Mother's vessel of memory broken or emptied. Esoterically it figures the soul cut off from its own past, a Saturnine forgetting that severs continuity of self.

amon.summary: The seventh spirit of the Goetia, a marquis of Gemini who procures love and reconciles enemies.
amon.description: Amon is the seventh spirit of the Goetia, a great and powerful marquis ruling in the decans of Gemini. He tells of things past and to come, procures love, and reconciles controversies between friends and foes. He appears as a wolf with a serpent's tail, vomiting flame, or as a man with the teeth of a raven or dog. A spirit of the airy twin-sign, he governs the binding and loosing of human bonds — the making of love and the settling of quarrels.

amoun.summary: Amoun (Amun), the Hidden One — the concealed creative breath, attributed to the supernal heights.
amoun.description: Amoun, the “Hidden One” of Thebes, is the great concealed god whose name itself means that which is veiled. In Liber 777 he is placed among the highest powers — touching Chokmah, Chesed, and the Veils of the Negative — as the unseen source from which all manifestation breathes forth. Originally a god of air and the invisible wind, he rose to become king of the Egyptian pantheon; his hiddenness makes him a fit emblem of the divine that can never be directly beheld, only known through its works.

amoun-ra.summary: Amoun-Ra (Amun-Ra), the hidden sun made king of the gods — the Jupiterian sovereign of Kaph.
amoun-ra.description: Amoun-Ra is the fusion of the hidden Amoun with the visible sun-god Ra, the supreme deity of imperial Egypt, in whom the concealed source and the radiant power are made one. Attributed to Kaph and Jupiter, he is the benevolent king of the gods, the expansive, ruling majesty of the heavens. The union of names declares the theology: the unseen creator and the blazing sun are two faces of a single sovereign power.

amy.summary: The fifty-eighth spirit of the Goetia, a flame-formed president of Scorpio who teaches astrology and betrays guarded treasure.
amy.description: Amy (Avnas) is the fifty-eighth spirit of the Goetia, a great president of the decans of Scorpio. He teaches astrology and the liberal sciences, gives good familiars, and betrays the treasures that are kept and guarded by other spirits. He appears first as a flaming fire, then takes human shape. A spirit of the watery sign, he is the teacher of the stars and the revealer of hoarded, spirit-guarded wealth.

an-ancient-walketh-bearing-a-lamp.term: an ancient walketh bearing a lamp
an-ancient-walketh-bearing-a-lamp.displayTerm: an ancient walketh bearing a lamp
an-ancient-walketh-bearing-a-lamp.summary: Liber 777's design for the Hermit (Yod): an ancient walks bearing a lamp.
an-ancient-walketh-bearing-a-lamp.description: ‘An ancient walketh bearing a lamp’ is the heart of Liber 777's design for Atu IX, the Hermit (path of Yod, Virgo). The aged wanderer carries his lantern through the dark—the light of the inner wisdom borne into the night of the world. The lamp is the hidden illumination of the seed-letter Yod, the spark of the Logos carried by the one who has withdrawn from the crowd; the Hermit lights the way for those who follow the path of return.
tables: CLXXXI. Correct Design of Tarot Trumps

an-archer-in-green.summary: The magical image of Leraje — an archer clad in green — Goetic Marquis of the second decan of Leo.
an-archer-in-green.description: Leraje (Leraikha, Loray), the fourteenth spirit of the Goetia and a mighty Marquis, appears in the likeness of a gallant archer clad and clothed in green, bearing a bow and quiver. In 777 he rules the second decan of Leo by day. He causes great battles and contests, and makes the wounds of arrows to putrefy. The green bowman amid the fiery Lion marks the martial vigour of the sign loosed in conflict — the hunter's keen eye and the festering shaft.

tables: CLI. Magical Images of the Decans (Cadent)

an-eagle-headed-man.summary: The talismanic image of the second decan of Gemini — an eagle-headed man.
an-eagle-headed-man.description: “An eagle-headed man” is the magical image of the succedent (second) decan of Gemini, in the old decan tradition. The eagle's head lends keenness of sight and loftiness of mind to the airy, intellectual sign of the Twins at its middle face — far vision joined to quick thought. As a decan talisman the eagle-headed figure encodes the sharp, soaring mental quality of this second of Gemini.
tables: CL. Magical Images of the Decans (Succedent)

an-old-man-leaning-on-a-staff.term: An old man leaning on a staff
an-old-man-leaning-on-a-staff.displayTerm: An old man leaning on a staff
an-old-man-leaning-on-a-staff.summary: The talismanic image of the third decan of Virgo — an old man leaning on a staff.
an-old-man-leaning-on-a-staff.description: “An old man leaning on a staff” is the magical image of the cadent (third) decan of Virgo, from the decan tradition. The aged figure with his supporting staff lends a note of experience, patience, and careful husbandry to the harvest sign of the Maiden at its final face. As a decan talisman it echoes the Hermit of the Virgo path, encoding the seasoned, prudent quality of this third of Virgo.
tables: CLI. Magical Images of the Decans (Cadent)

anahata.summary: Anahata — the heart chakra of air, attributed to the heart-centre of the Tree.
anahata.description: Anahata, the 'unstruck' chakra at the heart, is the fourth and central wheel, seat of the element Air and of love, compassion, and the meeting of the higher and lower. Set in 777 about Chesed, Geburah, and Tiphareth — the heart of the Tree — it is the threshold of the spiritual life, the centre where personal feeling opens into transpersonal love. Its name, 'unstruck,' denotes the primal sound that arises without two things being struck together.

analysis-into-4-elements.summary: The contemplation of the four elements (catudhātuvavatthāna) — the body resolved into earth, water, fire and air.
analysis-into-4-elements.description: Analysis into 4 Elements is catudhātuvavatthāna, one of the Forty Meditations, attributed to the path of Netzach. The meditator examines the body and resolves it into the four great elements — the solid (earth), the cohesive and fluid (water), the warming (fire) and the moving (air) — until the sense of a unified 'body' or 'self' dissolves into a flux of impersonal qualities. It is among the most analytical of the meditations, a discipline of insight as much as of calm: by reducing the apparently solid person to its bare physical constituents, it loosens identification and prepares the ground for the perception of not-self.

ananaurah.summary: Angel of the first face of Virgo, where patient skill is cultivated with prudence.
ananaurah.description: Ananaurah rules the opening decan of Virgo (0–10°), where the Sun meets the Eight of Disks, *Prudence* — careful, skilled application, the apprentice's diligence. The Sun lights Virgo's methodical labour and rewards attention to the small. Ananaurah is the angel of the prudent cultivation of craft, of mastery built one exact step at a time.

anchorite.summary: The solitary holy recluse of Virgo—the Hermit withdrawn, seeking the light by the discipline of solitude.
anchorite.description: The anchorite is set at Virgo, the path of the Hermit (Yod), and is the very type of that card: the one who has withdrawn from the world into the cell or the desert to pursue the inward light alone. The word means literally 'one who retires,' and the anchorite's solitude is not flight but discipline—the deliberate stripping-away of distraction so that the lamp of the spirit may be tended without interruption. Under Virgo, the sign of purity, service and exacting inner labour, the anchorite figures the seeker who has made of solitude a path. Esoterically he is the Hermit who carries his own small light through the dark, content to walk apart that he may walk toward the source.

ancient-bearded-king-seen-in-profile.term: Ancient bearded king seen in profile
ancient-bearded-king-seen-in-profile.displayTerm: Ancient bearded king seen in profile
ancient-bearded-king-seen-in-profile.summary: The magical image of Kether — an ancient bearded king seen in profile.
ancient-bearded-king-seen-in-profile.description: “An ancient bearded king seen in profile” is the magical image of Kether, the Crown and first Sephirah. The profile — showing only one side, the “face” that may be glimpsed but never fully beheld — perfectly figures the most hidden and exalted point of the Tree, of which only a partial vision is granted. As an aged, royal, bearded figure he is the Ancient of Days, the primal sovereign source from which all the rest of the Tree depends.
tables: CXX. Magical Images of the Sephiroth

and-one-cried-to-the-other.term: And one cried to the other
and-one-cried-to-the-other.displayTerm: And one cried to the other
tables: XCII. The Angelic Functions in the World of Yetzirah

and-prana-yama.summary: 'and Prana-yama' — Crowley's trailing note at Taurus in table XXIV, the breath-restraint practice of yoga.
and-prana-yama.description: In table XXIV the cell at path 16 (Vav/Taurus) ends with '... and Prana-yama,' closing the listed yogic practices with breath-restraint — the fourth limb of the eight-fold yoga of Patanjali, the disciplined direction of prana (life-force) through controlled inhalation, exhalation, and retention. Pranayama is the bridge between bodily and meditative practice and the foundation of all the higher dhyana attainments. The entry preserves Crowley's trailing reference; the principal Prana entry holds the broader description.
tables: XXIV. Certain of the Hindu/Buddhist Results

andras.summary: The sixty-third spirit of the Goetia, a raven-headed marquis of Sagittarius who sows discord and is deadly to the careless.
andras.description: Andras is the sixty-third spirit of the Goetia, a great marquis of the decans of Sagittarius. His office is to sow discord; and he is so dangerous that, unless the operator is wary, he will slay him and his assistants. He appears with the body of an angel and the head of a black night-raven or owl, riding upon a strong black wolf and brandishing a sharp and bright sword. A spirit of the fiery sign, he is the sower of strife and the most perilous of murderers.

andrealphus.summary: The sixty-fifth spirit of the Goetia, a peacock-formed marquis of Capricorn who teaches geometry and grants subtlety.
andrealphus.description: Andrealphus is the sixty-fifth spirit of the Goetia, a mighty marquis of the decans of Capricorn. He teaches geometry, mensuration and astronomy, makes men exceedingly subtle and cunning in argument, and can transform a man into the likeness of a bird. He appears at first as a peacock raising a great noise, then takes human form. A spirit of the earthy sign, he is the teacher of measurement and the giver of subtle wit.

andromalius.summary: The seventy-second and last spirit of the Goetia, a serpent-bearing earl of Pisces who punishes thieves and recovers stolen goods.
andromalius.description: Andromalius is the seventy-second and final spirit of the Goetia, a great earl of the decans of Pisces. He brings back both the thief and the goods that are stolen, discovers all wickedness and underhand dealing, punishes thieves and other wicked persons, and uncovers hidden treasures. He appears as a man holding a great serpent in his hand. The last of the seventy-two, this spirit of the watery sign is the avenger of theft and the restorer of what was taken — a fitting close to the catalogue of the Goetia.

angel-with-lions-head.summary: The magical image of Ipos — an angel with a lion's head, goose's feet and a horse's tail — Goetic Earl and Prince of the first decan of Scorpio.
angel-with-lions-head.description: Ipos, the twenty-second spirit of the Goetia, an Earl and mighty Prince, appears in the shape of an angel with the head of a lion, the feet of a goose, and a horse's tail (the grimoires more often give a hare's). In 777 he is set at the first decan of Scorpio by day. He knows all things past and to come, and makes men witty and bold. His chimerical body — angelic, leonine and base-footed at once — images the strange compounding of courage and cowardice that the searching sign of Scorpio lays bare.

angel-with-raven-s-head-rides-black-wolf.term: Angel with raven's head. Rides black wolf
angel-with-raven-s-head-rides-black-wolf.displayTerm: Angel with raven's head. Rides black wolf
angel-with-raven-s-head-rides-black-wolf.summary: The magical image of Andras — an angel with a raven's head astride a black wolf, a sharp sword in hand — Goetic Marquis of the third decan of Sagittarius (by night).
angel-with-raven-s-head-rides-black-wolf.description: Andras, the sixty-third spirit of the Goetia and a great Marquis, appears with the body of an angel and the head of a raven (in some accounts an owl), riding upon a strong black wolf and brandishing a sharp and bright sword. In 777 he is the nocturnal ruler of the third decan of Sagittarius. His office is to sow discords; he will kill the master, the servant and all assistants if the magician is not wary, and so is reckoned among the most dangerous of the spirits. The black-winged swordsman upon his wolf befits the fierce, far-shooting fire of the Archer turned to strife — the loosed arrow that wounds friend and foe alike.

angels-of-the-elements.summary: Angels of the Elements — the English name of the angelic choir Kerubim, the host of Assiah at Yesod.
angels-of-the-elements.description: In the Qabalistic angelology each Sephirah commands its own choir of angels; “Angels of the Elements” (Table CI, the Angels of Assiah given in English) renders into the vernacular the Hebrew order Kerubim, the host attributed to Yesod. These are the Angels of the Elements, the Kerubim who marshal the four elemental powers about the lunar Foundation. Crowley sets them at Yesod on the Tree, where the choir gives angelic form to the energy of that sphere as it acts in Assiah, the world of action.

angels-singing-in-divine-presence.summary: A content of the heaven Ma'on at Geburah — the angelic choirs that sing by night.
angels-singing-in-divine-presence.description: Among the contents of the heavens, the angels singing in the divine presence are placed in Ma'on, attributed to Geburah. The Talmud says that in Ma'on stand companies of ministering angels who utter song through the night and are silent by day for the sake of Israel's glory — the choiring host whose praise fills the residence-heaven.
tables: XCV. Contents of the Heavens of Assiah

anhalonium.summary: Peyote (mescaline cactus), attributed to Hod; sacramental visionary plant.
anhalonium.description:
Anhalonium Lewinii is the old botanical name for peyote, the small mescaline-bearing cactus of the North American deserts, attributed to Hod, the sphere of Mercury and of visionary intellect. For the Huichol and many other peoples it is a profound sacrament, the source of guided visions and healing; Crowley experimented with its extract and used it ritually, and it later became central to the mid-century investigation of the chemistry of mystical experience. Esoterically it is the wilderness teacher — the plant whose bitterness opens the inner eye, fitting Hod's office as the magician's workshop of vision and form.

Caution: mescaline is a potent hallucinogen, controlled in most jurisdictions, and peyote populations are endangered. This is a historical and symbolic entry, not advice for use.
anhalonium.caution: Potent hallucinogen; controlled substance; plant endangered. Historical/symbolic entry only — not advice for use.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

anhalonium-lewinii.summary: Peyote (mescaline cactus), attributed to Hod; sacramental visionary plant.
anhalonium-lewinii.description:
Anhalonium Lewinii is the old botanical name for peyote, the small mescaline-bearing cactus of the North American deserts, attributed to Hod, the sphere of Mercury and of visionary intellect. For the Huichol and many other peoples it is a profound sacrament, the source of guided visions and healing; Crowley experimented with its extract and used it ritually, and it later became central to the mid-century investigation of the chemistry of mystical experience. Esoterically it is the wilderness teacher — the plant whose bitterness opens the inner eye, fitting Hod's office as the magician's workshop of vision and form.

animal.summary: The animal nature itself at Virgo—the instinctual soul (nephesh) the Hermit must purify and discern.
animal.description: Placed at Virgo, the sign of discrimination and the path of the Hermit, the bare term 'animal' points to the animal nature in man—the nephesh or instinctual soul, the body of appetite and reflex that the seeker must come to know, govern and refine. Virgo is the sign of analysis and purification, exactly the faculty by which the higher self examines and orders the animal below it. Esoterically this entry marks not a single beast but the whole instinctual ground out of which consciousness rises: the creaturely life that is neither to be despised nor indulged but disciplined, made clean, and taken up into the work of the Hermit's solitary ascent.

anise.summary: The sweet liquorice scent of Cancer—anise, comforting and protective, perfume of the lunar home of Cheth.
anise.description: Anise is attributed to Cancer (Cheth, the Chariot). Its warm, sweet, liquorice-like fragrance has long been used to comfort, to protect against the evil eye and bad dreams, and to ward the threshold of the home—domestic, sheltering virtues fitting the lunar, protective water-sign of Cancer. Esoterically anise is the sweet guardian-perfume of Cheth's sheltering Chariot—the comforting scent that wards the inner sanctuary and keeps the night's terrors from the door.

anpu.summary: Anpu — the Egyptian Anubis, named here in Crowley's Adam Kadmon body-table XXI at the Mercurial path.
anpu.description: Anpu is the older Egyptian form of Anubis (Inpu / Anpu in transliteration) — the jackal-headed god of embalming, the guardian of the necropolis, and the psychopomp who weighs the heart in the Hall of Two Truths. Crowley's table XXI places 'Anpu' as a parenthetical guardian at path 12 (Beth/Mercury) — fitting, since both Anubis and Mercury are conductors of souls across the threshold between worlds, and both preside over speech, weighing, and judgement. The entry registers Anpu as Crowley's preferred Egyptological transliteration of the better-known Anubis, fixed at the Mercurial path.

anubi.summary: Anubis — the jackal-headed lord of the dead, guide of souls and weigher of the heart.
anubi.description: Anubis (Anpu) is the jackal-headed god of embalming and the dead, the opener of the ways who guides souls through the underworld and presides over the weighing of the heart against the feather of Maat. In 777 he is set upon the path of Qoph, the dark passage of the Moon between sleep and waking, life and death — fitting for the keeper of the threshold who stands, as Anubis of the East and of the West, at the gates of the Light and guards the perilous crossing between the worlds.

anubis.summary: Anubis, the jackal-headed guardian of the dead — psychopomp and master of embalming.
anubis.description: Anubis, jackal-headed lord of the necropolis, presides over death, mummification, and the weighing of the heart. In Liber 777 he is referred both to Hod and Mercury — for as guide of souls through the underworld he is a true psychopomp, the Egyptian counterpart of Hermes — and to the path of Aries. He embalms the dead and conducts them to judgement, the faithful keeper of the threshold between the worlds, and the patron of all who would travel safely in the realms of the dead.
tables: CLXIX. Egyptian Gods of the Zodiac (Succedent)

anus.summary: The fundament of the Perfected Man, the lowest gate of the body where waste returns to earth.
anus.description: The Anus is attributed to Malkuth, Capricorn, and Yesod in the body of Adam Kadmon—the nethermost outlet of the physical organism. As the gate of excretion it corresponds to the function by which the body casts off what is spent and returns it to the earth, the dark and humble end of the digestive descent. In the symbolic body it marks the final point at which the Tree's influence, having passed through every region, is released back into the material ground of Malkuth.

any-red-stone.summary: The martial correspondence of Pe and the Tower—any red stone burning with the raw force of Mars.
any-red-stone.description: The instruction "any red stone" is Crowley's correspondence for the 27th path, Pe, attributed to Mars and the Tower (Atu XVI). Where the system elsewhere names a single gem, here it gestures at a whole class—ruby, garnet, red jasper, bloodstone—any stone whose colour carries the scarlet signature of Mars, planet of war, destruction, and severity (Geburah). The redness is the point: the violent, breaking-down energy of the Tower struck by lightning, the force that shatters false structures. Esoterically the red stone is an amulet of martial power and protection, the condensed fire of Geburah worn against the heart.

any-solitary-person.summary: The one who stands apart—Virgo's lone seeker, the human form of the Hermit's withdrawal.
any-solitary-person.description: Any solitary person is attributed to Virgo, the path of the Hermit, where solitude is raised into a spiritual office. Where the anchorite is the formal recluse, this broader figure is anyone who, by temperament or calling, stands apart from the crowd—the wanderer, the contemplative, the self-sufficient soul who needs no company to be whole. Under Virgo and the Hermit such aloneness is not loneliness but a chosen ground of clarity, the quiet in which the inner voice can be heard. Esoterically the solitary person embodies the truth that certain stretches of the Path can be walked by one alone, and that the capacity to be wholly by oneself is itself an attainment.

apas.summary: The passive, receptive element of emotion, intuition, and dissolution.
apas.description:
Water is the element of emotion, intuition, memory, and the unconscious—cold and moist, receptive, descending, and formless save for the vessel that holds it. In 777 it answers to the letter Mem and path 23, to the Tatwa Apas (a silver crescent), and to the western quarter. Its weapon is the Cup, its archangel Gabriel, its elemental king Nichsa, its creatures the undines.

Mythically Water is the primordial deep from which creation rises and into which it dissolves—the waters of Genesis, the abyss of Tiamat, the river of forgetfulness. It governs the tides of feeling and the solvent power that breaks down rigid forms so that they may be reshaped. As the ‘universal solvent’ of nature it is also the alchemical agent of dissolution, the necessary death before reintegration.
tables: XXII. Small Selection of Hindu Deities
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

ape.summary: The cynocephalus of Mercury—the baboon of Thoth, sacred imitator and minister of the lord of writing.
ape.description: The ape is attributed to Mercury, and it is the sacred cynocephalus or dog-headed baboon of Thoth, depicted squatting in adoration at the rising of the moon and seated as scribe and minister beside the god of wisdom and letters. As the animal that imitates, the ape figures the mind's mimetic and reflective power—Mercury's gift of mirroring, copying and combining—as well as its restless cleverity. There is a double edge here: the ape is both the wise attendant of Thoth and the mocking parody, the trickster of the intellect. Esoterically it stands for the lower mind that, rightly disciplined, becomes the faithful scribe of the higher, but ungoverned descends into mere chatter and aping.

apep.summary: Apep (Apophis), the serpent of chaos — the great adversary of the sun, coiled in Scorpio.
apep.description: Apep is the monstrous serpent of primordial chaos, the eternal enemy of Ra who lies in wait each night to devour the sun as it passes through the underworld. Attributed here to Nun and Scorpio, the sign of death and the deep, Apep embodies the destructive, dissolving darkness that the solar order must perpetually overcome. Each dawn is a victory over him; yet he is never finally slain, for chaos is the necessary shadow against which creation renews itself.

aphrodite.summary: Venus—love, beauty, attraction, and art; ruler of Netzach and the path of Daleth.
aphrodite.description:
Venus is the planet of love, beauty, harmony, and desire—the magnetic force of attraction that draws all things toward union. In 777 she rules the seventh Sephirah Netzach and the path of Daleth (the Tarot trump The Empress), governing art, pleasure, fertility, and the green growth of nature. Her metal is copper, her number seven, her emblems the rose, the dove, the girdle, and the myrtle.

As Aphrodite–Ishtar–Hathor she is at once the goddess of earthly passion and of the higher love that orders the cosmos. Brightest of the planets to the eye, Venus as both morning and evening star long carried a double symbolism of Lucifer the light-bringer and the gentle evening lamp—union of the high and the low under the single law of love.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

aphruimis.summary: Name of the first decan of Leo, the Saturnine friction out of which solar sovereignty is forged.
aphruimis.description: Aphruimis is 777's name for the first decan of Leo (0°–10°), the entry into fixed fire. Saturn rules this face and its card is the Five of Wands—Strife—the friction of competing strengths as the Lion's flame first asserts dominion. Among the thirty-six Hermetic decan-faces drawn from Egypt's star-clocks, it names the contest out of which solar sovereignty is forged.
tables: CLXVIII. Egyptian Names of Asc. Decans.

aphut.summary: Name of the last decan of Virgo, where mutable earth brings the full harvest of wealth.
aphut.description: Aphut is 777's name for the last decan of Virgo (20°–30°), where mutable earth brings its harvest fully in. Mercury rules this face and its card is the Ten of Disks—Wealth—accumulated material abundance, the granary filled. Among the Hermetic decan-faces it stands at the close of Virgo, the consummation of patient earthly labour before the scales of Libra.
tables: CLXXII. Egyptian Names of the Cadent Decans

apis.summary: Apis, the sacred bull of Memphis — the living incarnation of Ptah and Osiris, at Taurus.
apis.description: Apis is the sacred bull of Memphis, worshipped as the living herald and incarnation of the creator-god Ptah and, in death, identified with Osiris as Serapis.
