Fittingly attributed to Vav and Taurus, the bull of the zodiac, he embodies fertile, generative strength and the divine made manifest in a living animal. The Apis bull was sought out by its sacred markings, honoured in life, and mummified with royal splendour at its death.

apo-bhawana.summary: Āpo-bhāvanā — the meditation upon the water-element, set at the path of Water.
apo-bhawana.description: Apo-Bhawana is the 'cultivation of the water-element' among the Hindu/Buddhist Results, attributed to the path of Mem and the element Water. It is the concentrative meditation upon water — its cohesion, fluidity and downward-tending nature taken as the inward object — by which the mind enters absorption and gains the faculties associated with the element. One of the elemental bhāvanās, it answers to the water-kasiṇa; set at Water, it figures the meditator's union with the principle of flow and dissolution.
tables: XXIV. Certain of the Hindu/Buddhist Results

apollo.summary: Apollo, god of the sun, music, and prophecy — the radiant Olympian of light and order.
apollo.description: Apollo is the luminous Greek god of the sun, music, poetry, healing, and prophecy, the very image of harmony, reason, and youthful beauty. Referred to Tiphareth, the solar centre, and to the path of the Sun and Sagittarius, he is the divine light made personal — the lord of the lyre, the far-shooting archer, and the voice of the Delphic oracle. He embodies clarity, proportion, and the illuminating power of the sun over both nature and the soul.

apollo-the-charioteer.summary: Apollo the Charioteer — the sun-god driving his chariot, at Cancer.
apollo-the-charioteer.description: “Apollo the Charioteer” is Apollo in his solar aspect as the driver of the chariot of the sun across the heavens, here referred to Cheth and Cancer. The image fuses the god of light with the daily course of the sun, the radiant power borne in triumph through the sky. It fittingly echoes the Tarot Chariot of the Cancer path — the sun-god enthroned in his moving car, master of the celestial journey.

apollo-the-diviner.summary: Apollo the Diviner — the oracular god of prophecy, at Gemini.
apollo-the-diviner.description: “Apollo the Diviner” is Apollo as the god of prophecy and oracles, master of the Delphic shrine where his priestess uttered the future. Referred to Zayin and Gemini, the sign of communication and the speaking voice, he is the divine source of revelation through speech. As diviner he opens the hidden to the mind, the luminous intelligence that pierces the veil of time.

apollo-the-pythean.summary: Apollo the Pythian — slayer of the Python, lord of Delphi, at Scorpio.
apollo-the-pythean.description: “Apollo the Pythian” commemorates Apollo's slaying of the great serpent Python at Delphi, after which he took the oracle as his own and was honoured with the Pythian Games. Referred to Nun and Scorpio, the sign of death and the serpent, the title marks his victory over the chthonic dragon — the triumph of solar light over the dark earth-power. As the Pythian he is the conqueror of the serpent and the founder of his greatest sanctuary.

apoltun.summary: Name of the first decan of Cancer, the Venusian opening of the watery world in love.
apoltun.description: Apoltun is 777's name for the first decan of Cancer (0°–10°), the cardinal initiation of the water-triplicity. Venus rules this face and it bears the Two of Cups—Love—the first meeting and mingling of feeling, the tide reaching for its mate. One of the thirty-six decan-faces by which the Egyptians read the night sky, it names the tender opening of the emotional world.
tables: CLXVII. Egyptian Gods of the Zodiac (Asc. Decans)

apophis.summary: Apophis, the chaos-dragon — the dark serpent whose name is the cry of destruction.
apophis.description: Apophis is the Greek form of Apep, the great serpent of chaos and the arch-foe of the sun-god. In Crowley's system the word also enters the formula I.A.O. as the middle term — Isis, Apophis, Osiris — the phase of death and destruction that stands between the nature-mother and the risen god. Apophis is thus not mere evil but the indispensable darkness of dissolution through which all things must pass to be reborn, the night that the new sun conquers.
tables: CLXXI. Egyptian Gods of the Zodiac (Cadent)

apoplex.summary: Apoplexy at Aries — the sudden Martial rush of blood to the head.
apoplex.description: Apoplexy (the older name for stroke) is set at the path of Aries, the sign that rules the head and is governed by Mars. Medical astrology read the sudden seizure as a violent, fiery congestion of blood in the head — the Aries-Mars temperament of heat and impetus turned destructive, the cerebral vessels overwhelmed by a Martial surge. As a symbol it is the danger of unchecked fire and headlong force striking at the seat of reason.

apoplexy.summary: Apoplexy at Sagittarius — seizure born of Jupiterian plethora and excess.
apoplexy.description: Apoplexy appears again on the path of Sagittarius, the Jupiter-ruled sign of expansion and abundance. Where the Aries attribution stresses the Martial rush to the head, the Sagittarian-Jupiterian reading stresses plethora — the apoplexy of over-fullness, of rich living and excess, the body so engorged by Jupiter's bounty that the vessels burst. It is the cautionary shadow of expansiveness, mercy and increase carried past their healthy bound.

apple.summary: The fruit of Venus—the apple of love and temptation, hiding the five-pointed star within its core.
apple.description: The Apple is attributed to Venus (Daleth, the Empress), and it is everywhere the fruit of love and desire: the golden apple of Aphrodite and of the Hesperides, the apple of discord that began the Trojan war, the fruit by which Eve woke to knowledge. Cut across, it reveals its five seeds set in a perfect pentagram—Venus's own star hidden in its heart. Esoterically the apple is the sweet, dangerous fruit of Venusian desire and knowing, the love that opens the eyes and overturns the established order.

apron.summary: The workman's badge of Hod—the apron of the craftsman-magician, sign of grade and protection in labour.
apron.description: The Apron is attributed to Hod, the Mercurial sphere of the intellect and of the magical crafts, and it is the badge of the workman: the garment worn by the mason and the artificer, both to protect in labour and to declare rank and office. In the Western mystery tradition the apron marks the initiate as one who builds, and its decorations signify the grade attained. Its place at Hod, the sphere of Mercury the craftsman and of skilled working, is exact. Esoterically the Apron is the sign of the magician as a worker in the temple—the consecrated craftsman who labours with skill and according to rule, girded for the practical work of the art and bearing upon himself the tokens of what he has achieved.

aput.summary: Aput — the divine guardian Crowley pairs with the Ear of Adam Kadmon in table XXI.
aput.description: Aput appears in Crowley's body-table XXI as the parenthetical guardian of the Ear at path 21 (Kaph/Jupiter) and 32 (Tav/Saturn). In Egyptian, 'Apuat' or 'Wepwawet' is 'the Opener of the Ways,' the jackal god who clears the path for souls; Aput may well be Crowley's shortened transliteration of this name, which would fit the ear's role as the organ through which a path or 'way' is heard and followed. The entry preserves Aput as Crowley fixes him — the guardian of hearing in the perfected body, set at the Jupiter-path and the Saturn-path.

aquamarine.summary: The sea-blue beryl of the element Water — the calm of the deep sea.
aquamarine.description: Aquamarine — the sea-blue beryl whose name means 'water of the sea' — is set at the path of Mem, elemental Water. Its pale ocean-blue is the very colour of the element it serves, and it was anciently the talisman of sailors and a charm for safe passage over the deep. Esoterically it is the stone of the serene, fathomless water, of emotional clarity and the calming of the tides.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

aquarius.summary: Fixed Air, ruled by Saturn/Uranus—humanity, innovation, and the poured-out waters.
aquarius.description:
Aquarius, the Water-Bearer, is fixed Air ruled traditionally by Saturn (and in the modern scheme by Uranus)—the sign of humanity, innovation, idealism, and the free circulation of knowledge. In 777 it answers to the letter Tzaddi and the path of the Tarot trump The Star (path 28), the figure pouring the waters of life beneath the stars; Crowley famously revised the older Tzaddi attribution, declaring ‘Tzaddi is not the Star.’ It governs the collective, the future, and the visionary.

The Water-Bearer pours not emotion but living wisdom, nourishing the whole of humanity—an appropriately airy ‘water’ that is really the outpouring of mind and spirit. Aquarius’ gift is originality, friendship, and altruism; its shadow, detachment and cold abstraction. It is the prophet and reformer of the zodiac, and gives its name to the coming Aeon in popular thought.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

ararita.summary: A seven-fold name proclaiming the One: 'One is His Beginning, One is His Individuality, His Permutation is One.'
ararita.description: ARARITA is a notariqon of the Hebrew sentence Achad Rosh, Achdotho Rosh Ichudo, Temurahzo Achad—"One is His Beginning; One is His Individuality; His Permutation is One." Seven letters for the seven planets and the sevenfold star, it is the great formula of the reduction of multiplicity to unity, used by Crowley as the mantra of the Hexagram and as the spine of his Liber ARARITA. Attributed to Netzach, the sphere of Venus and of the many-coloured rays of feeling and desire, it teaches that all the scattered fires of the heart resolve, in the end, into the single flame of the One.

arathron.summary: Olympic Spirit of Saturn, governor of the dark, time-bound provinces of heaven; lord of stone, lead, and the hidden.
arathron.description: Arathron (Aratron) is the Olympic Spirit of Saturn in the system of the Arbatel of Magick, the Renaissance grimoire that divided the visible heaven among seven planetary regents. Crowley sets him at Tav, the path of Saturn and of the great closing letter of the alphabet — the boundary, the threshold, the lead that is the alchemist's prima materia. To Saturn's nature the Arbatel ascribes to Arathron the rulership of the largest share of the celestial provinces, dominion over all things saturnine: agriculture, long life, the secrets of the earth and of the dead. He is said to convert any living thing into stone in an instant, to change quicksilver into lead, to grant invisibility and faithful familiars, and to teach alchemy and the magical arts. He governs on the Day of Saturn (Saturday). Esoterically he is the spirit of limitation made wise — the contraction and gravity of Binah's reflection in the world of forces, the patient intelligence that ripens slowly and keeps the keys of the locked door.

araziel.summary: Araziel, the angel set over Taurus — the assisting intelligence of the sign on the path of Vav.
araziel.description: Araziel is the angel attributed to Taurus in the Golden Dawn and Crowley's 777 (Table CXLIII, the Twelve Lesser Assistant Angels of the Signs). The name carries the Hebrew theophoric ending ‑el, “of God,” marking him as a ministering intelligence rather than a ruling archangel: the lesser angel who carries the governance of the sign into act. Set over Taurus (fixed Earth), he embodies the settled fertility and enduring substance of the bull; Crowley places him at the path of Vav on the Tree of Life.
tables: CXLIII. Twelve Lesser Assistant Angels in the Signs (Transl).

archatapias.summary: Name of the first decan of Pisces, the Saturnine face of weary withdrawal into the deep.
archatapias.description: Archatapias is 777's name for the first decan of Pisces (0°–10°), the entry into mutable water. Saturn rules this face and its card is the Eight of Cups—Indolence—the abandonment of feeling grown stale, the turning-away that begins the sign of dissolution. One of the thirty-six decan-faces inherited from Egypt, it names the weary withdrawal that opens the waters of Pisces.
tables: CLXVIII. Egyptian Names of Asc. Decans.

archer.summary: The Archer — the celestial bowman of Sagittarius, the aimed and aspiring force.
archer.description: “The Archer” is the figure of Sagittarius, the centaur-bowman who looses his arrow toward the heights, here referred to Samekh and Sagittarius (and echoed at Cancer). The drawn bow and the speeding shaft are emblems of aspiration, aim, and the directing of force toward a distant goal. As the Archer he embodies the questing, far-shooting energy of the sign — purpose loosed like an arrow at the mark.

archetypal-world.summary: The Archetypal World — Atziluth, the world of pure emanation.
archetypal-world.description: The Archetypal World is Atziluth, the highest of the four Qabalistic worlds — the realm of pure divine emanation, of the ten Sephiroth in their unmixed essence and of the four letters of the holy Name in their root. It is the world of archetypes nearest to the Godhead, where all things exist as ideal, undifferentiated principles before any descent into form. In 777's elemental scheme it is associated with primal Fire and the Father of the Tetragrammaton.

arepien.summary: Name of the last decan of Libra, the Jovial face of truce and reconciliation.
arepien.description: Arepien is 777's name for the last decan of Libra (20°–30°). Jupiter rules this face and it bears the Four of Swords—Truce—the rest and reconciliation that follow sorrow, balance restored through withdrawal. Among the Egyptian decan-faces it stands at the close of Libra, the airy peace before the descent into Scorpio.
tables: CLXXII. Egyptian Names of the Cadent Decans

ares.summary: Mars—energy, conflict, courage, and severity; ruler of Geburah and the path of Pe.
ares.description:
Mars is the planet of energy, war, courage, and necessary destruction—the cutting, driving force that clears the field for new growth. In 777 it rules the fifth Sephirah Geburah and the path of Pe (the Tarot trump The Tower), and embodies the principle of severity and decisive action. Its metal is iron, its number five, its emblems the sword, the spear, and the colour scarlet.

As Ares–Nergal–Horus the avenger, Mars is the warrior god whose aggression, rightly directed, becomes protection and justice; wrongly directed, it becomes cruelty and ruin. The magician learns from Mars the disciplined release of force—the surgeon’s knife rather than the berserker’s rage.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

aries.summary: Cardinal Fire, ruled by Mars—initiation, the first thrust of spring.
aries.description:
Aries, the Ram, is the first sign of the zodiac—cardinal Fire, ruled by Mars, marking the spring equinox and the explosive beginning of the solar year. In 777 it is attributed to the Hebrew letter Heh and the path of the Tarot trump The Emperor (path 15). It embodies pure initiative: the raw, pioneering thrust of will that breaks dormancy and starts the cycle anew.

Mythically the Ram is the golden fleece, the leader of the flock, the sacrificial yet ever-renewing head of the year. Its keywords are courage, impulse, and assertion; its shadow is rashness and self-absorption. As the first fire of the wheel, Aries is the spark of identity asserting ‘I am.’
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

arimanius.summary: Arimanius (Ahriman), the Zoroastrian lord of darkness — the principle of evil, at Scorpio.
arimanius.description: Arimanius is the Latin form of Ahriman (Angra Mainyu), the destructive spirit of Zoroastrian dualism, the dark adversary of the good Ahura Mazda. Referred to Nun and Scorpio, the sign of death and the deep, he embodies the principle of evil, decay, and opposition — the cosmic counter-force against the powers of light. His inclusion among the dark attributions marks him as a great mythic image of the destructive principle in the universe.
tables: CLXVII. Egyptian Gods of the Zodiac (Asc. Decans)

ariton.summary: One of the four cardinal demon-kings — Ariton (Egyn); here ruling the element of Fire.
ariton.description: Ariton, also called Egyn, is one of the four demon-kings of the quarters in the Abramelin tradition, ruling with Oriens, Paimon, and Amaimon. In this attribution he is set to the element of Fire. As a cardinal king of the spirits he presides over a numerous host and was counted among the chief powers whose names the magician must know to command the lesser demons beneath them.

tables: CXX. Magical Images of the Sephiroth

armilus.summary: Cupidity — the Nuctemeron genius of the tenth hour presiding over cupidity, set by Crowley at Capricorn.
armilus.description: Armilus is the Nuctemeron genius of cupidity. That “Night-illumined Day”, ascribed to Apollonius of Tyana and handed down through Lévi's Transcendental Magic, sets a company of spirits over each of the twelve hours of the magical day, and Armilus belongs to the tenth hour. He is the spirit of greed and covetousness, the unslaked lust for possession. In 777 (Table CLXXIII) Crowley redistributes these hour-genii across the zodiac, where this spirit falls at Capricorn (Ayin).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours
CLI. Magical Images of the Decans (Cadent)

arms.summary: A correspondence of Taurus and a detail of decan imagery: the shoulders and arms.
arms.description: ‘Arms’ appears both as a bodily correspondence and as a detail of the decan images in Liber 777. In the table of the Human Body the shoulders and arms are governed by the path of Vav (Taurus); and in the cadent decan of Aries the restless figure wears golden bracelets ‘on his hands and arms.’ The arms are the limbs of action and embrace, the instruments by which will reaches into the world—an apt member for the strong, productive sign of the bull and for the vigorous imagery of the fiery decans.
tables: CLI. Magical Images of the Decans (Cadent)

arnica.summary: The healer's flower of Jupiter—golden arnica, balm for bruises and the beneficent touch of Jove.
arnica.description: Arnica is attributed to Jupiter (Kaph, the Wheel of Fortune), the great benefic. Its golden, daisy-like flowers yield a famous remedy for bruises, sprains, and the shocks of the body—a gentle, restoring medicine fitting the planet of mercy, expansion, and good fortune. Esoterically the arnica is Jupiter's healing benevolence in herb-form, the kindly power that eases injury and turns the wheel back toward wholeness.

aroueris.summary: Aroueris (Haroeris), Horus the Elder — the far-seeing falcon of the heavens.
aroueris.description: Aroueris is the Greek rendering of Har-wer, Horus the Elder, the great sky-falcon whose eyes are the sun and moon, distinct from the child Horus son of Isis. Placed at Aries and Aquarius, he is the elder, cosmic aspect of Horus — the far-gazing lord of the sky whose vision spans the heavens. As one of the oldest forms of the falcon-god he represents the ancient, all-surveying power of light over the world.
tables: CLXVII. Egyptian Gods of the Zodiac (Asc. Decans)

arrow.summary: The dart of aspiration—the straight ray of Sol and the flight across the Abyss, will loosed toward its mark.
arrow.description: The Arrow is attributed to the Moon (the path of Gimel) and to the Sun (Resh), and it is the emblem of aspiration loosed and aimed: the straight line that is the shortest distance between the soul and its goal, the dart of will shot toward heaven. In its lunar attribution it is the arrow flying up the path of the High Priestess across the Abyss; in its solar one it is the directed ray of light. Once released, the arrow cannot be recalled—it figures the irreversible commitment of an aspiration fully launched. Esoterically the Arrow is the single-pointed will sent flying toward the divine, the act of aspiration made swift, straight and unrecallable, the soul's flight toward the mark it has chosen.

tables: CL. Magical Images of the Decans (Succedent)
CLI. Magical Images of the Decans (Cadent)

arsenic.summary: The classic poison, attributed to Netzach; the venom hidden in the Venusian green.
arsenic.description:
Arsenic is set at Netzach, the Venusian sphere — the most notorious of poisons concealed within the sphere of love and beauty, a reminder that Venus has her deadly aspect and that the green world holds venom as well as nectar (the lurid 'Paris green' and 'Scheele's green' pigments were arsenic compounds). Tasteless and slow, it was the inheritance-poison of legend. Esoterically it figures the poison hidden in pleasure, the toxic shadow of attraction.

Caution: arsenic is a potent cumulative poison and carcinogen. Scholarly entry only.
arsenic.caution: Potent cumulative poison and carcinogen. Scholarly entry only.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

art.summary: Atu XIV — Samekh / Sagittarius; alchemical combination of opposites into a new whole.
art.description: Art (the older Temperance) is trump XIV, attributed to Samekh and Sagittarius, the path from Yesod to Tiphareth—the central ‘arrow’ that rises straight toward the Sun. It is the great alchemical work of combination: the tempering and union of opposites (fire and water, the white and red, king and queen) into a new and perfected substance. Crowley’s androgyne pours the contraries into a single cauldron, the motto ‘Visita Interiora Terrae…’ (VITRIOL) encircling the work. Art teaches the patient blending of warring forces into harmony—the very method of the Great Work.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

artemis.summary: Artemis, the virgin huntress and moon-goddess — wild mistress of the chase, at the Moon.
artemis.description: Artemis is the Greek goddess of the hunt, the wilderness, and the moon, the chaste twin of Apollo who roams the forests with her nymphs and her silver bow. Referred to Gimel and the Moon and to Sagittarius, she is the cool, untamed lunar power, protectress of wild things and of maidens, swift and unyielding. As the divine huntress she embodies independence, the silver light, and the fierce purity of the untouched wild.

arteriosclerosis.summary: Hardening of the arteries at Tav and Saturn — the Saturnine rigidifying of the vessels.
arteriosclerosis.description: Arteriosclerosis, the hardening and stiffening of the arteries, is attributed to the path of Tav and the planet Saturn. Saturn is the lord of hardening, drying, and the slow imposition of rigid form; the calcifying of the once-supple vessels is the very signature of his work in the body. Esoterically it figures the Saturnine fate of all matter — the gradual loss of flexibility and flow, structure tightening at last into stone.

arthritis.summary: Arthritis at Capricorn — Saturn's affliction of the joints and bones.
arthritis.description: Arthritis is set on the path of Capricorn, the cardinal earth sign ruled by Saturn that governs the knees, the joints, and the skeletal framework. The inflammation and stiffening of the joints is read as a classic Saturnine malady: cold, dry, and constricting, fixing the body's hinges in painful rigidity. It is the disease of the bone-lord, the price exacted by time upon the structures that bear us up.

artificial-glass.summary: The made stone of the Star—sand transmuted by fire, art perfecting nature under Aquarius.
artificial-glass.description: Artificial glass is Crowley's striking correspondence for Tzaddi, the path of The Star (Atu XVII) and the sign Aquarius. Where the other stones are gifts of the earth, glass is humanity's own crystal—silica sand married to fire and breath, the first great act of conscious transmutation. This artifice befits the Star: the sign of the Water-Bearer and of the New Aeon's hope, where the human becomes a co-creator pouring out the waters of revelation. Esoterically glass is the perfected vessel, clear and light-bearing, the transparent medium through which the starlight passes—an emblem of the aspirant made limpid enough to transmit the divine.

aruparga.summary: Arūpa-rāga — the Pali name for the seventh fetter, craving for formless existence.
aruparga.description: Aruparga (arūpa-rāga) is the Pali for the seventh of the ten fetters, the craving for existence in the formless realms — the most attenuated longing for continued being, set at Kether. One of the higher fetters severed only at full liberation, it is the final residue of the thirst for existence. (Its English face appears under 'Desire for immaterial immortality'.)

as-air.summary: Cross-reference marker — 'as Air,' Crowley's editorial note in the deity tables for gods invoked in their airy aspect.
as-air.description: Crowley's deity tables (XXXIV in particular, for the Greek gods) sometimes mark a placement with 'as Air' — recording that the god named in that cell appears at this path in their airy, gaseous, mercurial, or breath-borne aspect rather than in their fuller mythic form. The slug preserves this cross-reference marker as it appears in Crowley's text: not a deity but the qualifying clause that fixes the deity's elemental face at this Tree position.

as-egyptian.summary: Cross-reference marker — 'as Egyptian,' Crowley's note in table III (Translation of the Names of the Paths) pointing to the Egyptian rendering of a path-name.
as-egyptian.description: In table III ('Translation of the Names of the Paths') Crowley occasionally appends 'as Egyptian' to a path-name — recording that the path-name at this cell can also be given in its Egyptian-mythological form (e.g. the path of Tav rendered in Egyptian as a name of Sokar or of the underworld). The slug preserves this cross-reference qualifier as it appears in the source. The full Egyptian path-naming itself is held in the dedicated Egyptian-deity tables (XIX, XX).
tables: III. Translation of the Names of the Paths

as-hanged-man.summary: Cross-reference marker — 'as Hanged Man,' Crowley's note in the deity tables for gods placed at the Mem/Water path under the Tarot Hanged Man.
as-hanged-man.description: In table XIX Crowley marks a placement at path 23 (Mem/Water) with 'as Hanged Man' — recording that the deity at that cell appears here in the suspended, sacrificial, descended aspect symbolised by the Tarot trump assigned to this path (XII, the Hanged Man). The slug preserves the cross-reference shard: not a deity but the qualifying clause fixing the god's mode as the inverted, water-immersed, willingly-bound one of the path.

as-incubus.summary: Cross-reference marker — 'as Incubus,' Crowley's note in the Christian-deity column for a placement at Yesod under the dream-incubus aspect.
as-incubus.description: In table XXXVI ('Selection of Christian Gods, Apostles, Evangelists, and Churches of Asia') Crowley marks a placement at Yesod with 'as Incubus' — recording that the figure at that cell appears here in the dream-visiting, nightmare-bringing aspect that the lunar/Yesodic sphere is traditionally associated with. The incubus (literally 'one who lies upon') is the demon of the sleeping mind; the cross-reference marker is Crowley's editorial qualifier rather than a separate deity. The entry preserves it as such.
tables: XXXVI. Selection of Christian Gods (10); Apostles (12); Evangelists(4); and Churches of Asia (7)

as-scarab-in-tarot-trump.summary: Cross-reference marker — 'as Scarab in Tarot Trump,' Crowley's note at the Qoph/Pisces path.
as-scarab-in-tarot-trump.description: In table XIX Crowley marks a placement at path 29 (Qoph/Pisces) with 'as Scarab in Tarot Trump' — pointing to the scarab beetle that, in Crowley's Thoth deck's design of trump XVIII (The Moon), creeps across the threshold between the dark towers, carrying the solar disc through the night of Qoph. The Egyptian khepri-scarab is the great symbol of the sun's nocturnal passage and emergence; the cross-reference marker pins this iconographic detail to the cell.

as-virgin.summary: Cross-reference marker — 'as Virgin,' Crowley's note in the deity tables for gods placed at the Virgo path in their unwedded aspect.
as-virgin.description: In table XIX ('Selection of Egyptian Gods') Crowley marks a placement at path 20 (Yod/Virgo) with 'as Virgin' — recording that the god named at that cell appears here in their virginal, unwedded, hermetic aspect rather than in their mated or maternal form. The marker is most often used for Isis-as-Virgin (Isis-Sothis before her union with Osiris), and for the parallel Greek Virgo-goddesses (Demeter-Persephone, Artemis). The entry preserves Crowley's aspectual qualifier as it appears in the source.

as-water.summary: Cross-reference marker — 'as Water,' Crowley's note in the deity tables for gods invoked in their watery aspect.
as-water.description: Across Liber 777's deity tables (XIX, XXII, XXXV, and elsewhere) Crowley frequently glosses a god's placement at a particular path or Sephirah with 'as [element/aspect]' — e.g. 'Isis as Water,' 'Neptune as Water' — recording the specific facet under which the deity occupies that position. The slug 'as Water' collects these cross-reference shards: it marks the aquatic, receptive, lunar-flowing aspect of whichever god is named at the cell. The entry itself is not a deity but Crowley's aspectual qualifier — the explanation that the placement holds the god in their watery mode.
tables: XXII. Small Selection of Hindu Deities

as-wisdom.summary: Cross-reference marker — 'as Wisdom,' Crowley's note in the deity tables for gods placed at Chokmah in their sapiential aspect.
as-wisdom.description: In table XX ('Practical Egyptian Gods') Crowley uses 'as Wisdom' to mark a placement at Chokmah — the second Sephirah, whose name 'Chokmah' means 'Wisdom' — recording that the deity named at that cell appears here in their sapiential aspect (Thoth as the writer of judgement, Hermes as the wise messenger, the great divine word). The slug preserves this cross-reference shard: not a deity but the qualifying clause fixing the god's mode at the supernal Wisdom-Sephirah.

asana.summary: Āsana — meditative posture, the steady seat that founds the inner work, set at Taurus.
asana.description: Asana is the yogic posture among the Hindu/Buddhist Results, attributed to the path of Taurus. In Patañjali's eight-limbed yoga it is the third limb: the firm, steady and comfortable seat that frees the body from agitation so that the breath and mind may be governed. Crowley devoted close attention to āsana in his own training, prizing the conquest of bodily restlessness as the indispensable foundation of all meditation. Its earthy, fixed Taurean attribution suits this discipline of stillness and stability in the flesh.
tables: XXIV. Certain of the Hindu/Buddhist Results

asar.summary: Egyptian god of death, resurrection, and the underworld; the slain-and-risen king.
asar.description: Osiris (Egyptian Asar) is the slain-and-risen god—king of the dead, lord of resurrection, and judge of souls in the hall of the underworld. Murdered and dismembered by his brother Set, reassembled by Isis, and reborn to rule the realm of the dead, he is the archetypal dying god whose story promises life beyond death. In 777 he is attributed to the solar centre Tiphareth, the place of the sacrificed-and-reborn god, and Crowley made the ‘Formula of Osiris’ (the slain god) the keynote of the superseded Aeon, now yielding to the Aeon of the child Horus. Osiris embodies the mystery of regeneration through death.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

asar-un-nefer.summary: Egyptian god of death, resurrection, and the underworld; the slain-and-risen king.
asar-un-nefer.description: Osiris (Egyptian Asar) is the slain-and-risen god—king of the dead, lord of resurrection, and judge of souls in the hall of the underworld. Murdered and dismembered by his brother Set, reassembled by Isis, and reborn to rule the realm of the dead, he is the archetypal dying god whose story promises life beyond death. In 777 he is attributed to the solar centre Tiphareth, the place of the sacrificed-and-reborn god, and Crowley made the ‘Formula of Osiris’ (the slain god) the keynote of the superseded Aeon, now yielding to the Aeon of the child Horus. Osiris embodies the mystery of regeneration through death.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

asentacer.summary: Name of the third decan of Aries, where cardinal fire is harmonised by Venus into completed work.
asentacer.description: Asentacer governs the third and final decan of Aries (20°–30°), where the cardinal fire of the sign comes to its first rest. Venus rules this face and it carries the Four of Wands—Completion, or Perfected Work—the harmonising of raw Martial energy into a finished, settled order. In the decan tradition that Hellenistic astrology drew from Egypt's thirty-six faces, this name marks the point where ignition becomes accomplishment before the wheel turns to Taurus.
tables: CLXXII. Egyptian Names of the Cadent Decans

ash.summary: The World-Tree—Yggdrasil the great ash binding the nine worlds, Saturn's axis of all things.
ash.description: The Ash is attributed to Saturn (Tav, the Universe) and to Tiphareth—and above all it is Yggdrasil, the world-ash of Norse myth whose roots and branches bind together the nine worlds and upon which Odin hung nine nights, wounded by his own spear, to win the runes. As Saturn's tree it is the axis and framework of the cosmos, the structural tree of time and limitation upon which all things are stretched; reaching to Tiphareth it touches the harmonised centre. Esoterically the ash is the spine of the universe, the tree of the cosmic ordeal and of hard-won wisdom.

asi.summary: Asi (Isis), the great goddess — the throne and mother, spread across the supernal triad.
asi.description: Asi is a name of Isis, the supreme Egyptian goddess of magic, motherhood, and resurrection, here spread across Kether, Chokmah, and Binah — the three supernal Sephiroth. As the throne (her hieroglyph) and the all-encompassing mother who gathered the scattered Osiris and conceived Horus, she is the archetypal feminine power at the highest reaches of the Tree. Asi is the loving wisdom and the boundless mother-love woven through the supernal heights.

asicath.summary: Name of the first decan of Taurus, the entry into fixed earth where fertility meets its first labour.
asicath.description: Asicath is the name 777 gives the first decan of Taurus (0°–10°), the entry into fixed earth where the fertile patience of the Bull meets its first toil. Mercury rules this face, and its card is the Five of Disks—Worry—the anxiety of material strain that tests the ground before it can bear fruit. One of the thirty-six Egyptian decan-faces later absorbed into Western astrology, it names the labour at the root of earthly stability.
tables: CLXVIII. Egyptian Names of Asc. Decans.

asmoday.summary: The thirty-second spirit of the Goetia (Asmodeus), a fire-breathing king of Aquarius who teaches the sciences and guards treasure.
asmoday.description: Asmoday (Asmodeus) is the thirty-second spirit of the Goetia, a great and powerful king of the decans of Aquarius, to be invoked bare-headed and with reverence. He gives the ring of virtues, teaches arithmetic, geometry, astronomy and all handicrafts, answers all demands fully and truly, makes men invisible, and guards hidden treasure. He appears with three heads — a bull, a man and a ram — a serpent's tail, the webbed feet of a goose, breathing fire and riding upon an infernal dragon, bearing lance and banner. A spirit of the airy sign, he is among the mightiest of the Goetic kings, master of the sciences and of buried wealth.

aspen.summary: The trembling tree of Air—the aspen whose ever-quaking leaves whisper with the restless element of Aleph.
aspen.description: The Aspen is attributed to Air (Aleph, the Fool). Its leaves tremble and whisper in the faintest breeze, hung upon flattened stalks that catch every current—the most airy of trees, never still. This perpetual quaking made it for the old mind a tree of fear, of the wind's voice, and of the restless, mobile element itself. Esoterically the aspen embodies the ceaseless movement and communicative whisper of Air, the element of Aleph that is everywhere in motion and never grasped.

aspergillus.summary: The sprinkler of lustral water at Aquarius—the implement of purification by sprinkling, cleansing the field of work.
aspergillus.description: The Aspergillus (aspergillum) is attributed to Aquarius, and it is the implement used to sprinkle consecrated water in the rite of lustration—the brush or perforated vessel that scatters drops of purifying water over the temple, the instruments, and the operator. Paired with the censer (which purifies by fire and smoke), the aspergillus purifies by water, the two together cleansing the working-space through the complementary elements. Its place at the airy, water-bearing sign of Aquarius befits its office of dispensing the lustral flood. Esoterically the Aspergillus is the instrument of purification by water—the means by which the magician cleanses and consecrates the field of the Work, washing away the profane so that the holy may safely descend.

ass.summary: The patient burden-bearer of Taurus and Capricorn, and the Typhonic Set-beast—humble earth and stubborn endurance.
ass.description: The ass is set among the decan images at Taurus and Capricorn, the earthy signs of endurance and labour, where its proverbial patience and sure-footed carrying of weight make it the emblem of uncomplaining service. Yet the ass has a darker face in the old mysteries: it was the beast of Set-Typhon, the red ass of the desert, an animal of the adversary and of obstinate, untamable force. Between these poles—humble carrier and Typhonic outsider—the ass holds the ambiguity of the lower earth: that which bears the spirit's burdens, and that which resists and tests it.

assaf-tida.summary: The 'devil's dung' of Saturn—asafoetida, foul and powerful, the great banishing incense of the saturnine sphere.
assaf-tida.description: Asafoetida (assaf-tida) is attributed to Saturn (Tav, the Universe). A resin of such pungent, fetid reek that it earned the name "devil's dung," it is the classic banishing and exorcising incense—burned to drive off evil spirits and break enchantments, its very foulness a weapon. Such an "evil odour" is proper to dark, saturnine Saturn. Esoterically asafoetida is the repellent perfume of the threshold-guardian, the stench that scatters the lower powers and seals the circle against intrusion.

assafoetida.summary: The fetid banishing-resin of Capricorn—asafoetida, the goat-sign's pungent ward against evil and the dark powers.
assafoetida.description: Asafoetida is attributed here to Capricorn (Ayin, the Devil). The same powerfully fetid gum-resin—"devil's dung"—burned for banishing and exorcism finds a fitting second seat upon the Devil's goat-path, where its acrid reek both names and repels the darker, carnal powers. Esoterically the asafoetida of Capricorn is the harsh perfume that confronts the Devil's own domain, the stench used to drive out what the path of Ayin sets as the soul's ordeal.

assicean.summary: The presiding name of the first decan of Aries—the fiery threshold of the zodiac, ruled by Mars and bearing the Two of Wands, Dominion.
assicean.description: Assicean is the name Liber 777 preserves for the spirit of the first decan of Aries (0°–10°), the very ignition-point of the zodiacal wheel. In the Hermetic decan system—the thirty-six “faces” the Egyptians read as star-clocks of the night and the Hellenistic astrologers inherited as rulers of ten-degree spans—this face is governed by Mars in his own cardinal-fire sign and answers to the Two of Wands, which the Golden Dawn titled Dominion: raw initiating will, the spark that asserts itself before any form exists to temper it. To name it is to name the threshold where pure energy first breaks into manifestation.
tables: CLXVIII. Egyptian Names of Asc. Decans.

asteroth.summary: The twenty-ninth spirit of the Goetia (Astaroth), a duke of Capricorn who reveals secrets and the fall of spirits.
asteroth.description: Astaroth (here Asteroth) is the twenty-ninth spirit of the Goetia, a great and powerful duke of the decans of Capricorn. He gives true answers of things past, present and to come, discovers all secrets, and makes men wonderfully learned in the liberal sciences; he will also discourse of the fall of the spirits. He appears as a hurtful angel riding an infernal dragon or beast and bearing a viper in his right hand; his breath is of so deadly a stench that the operator must guard his face with a magical ring. A spirit of the earthy sign, he is the revealer of secrets whose very presence is poison.

astiro.summary: Name of the middle decan of Aquarius, a Mercurial face of lucid intelligence with a stellar name.
astiro.description: Astiro is the name 777 keeps for the middle decan of Aquarius (10°–20°). Mercury rules this face and its card is the Six of Swords—Science, or Earned Success—clear, ordered thought that finds its way through difficulty. The name's stellar ring (Greek astēr, “star”) suits a face of the abstract, far-seeing zodiac; among the thirty-six Hermetic decan-faces it names the lucid intelligence at the heart of the Water-Bearer's sign.
tables: CLXX. Egyptian Names of the Succedent Decans

astr-a.summary: Astraea, the star-maiden of justice — who fled the wicked earth to become Virgo, at Saturn.
astr-a.description: Astraea is the Roman goddess of justice and innocence, the “star-maiden” who dwelt among mortals in the Golden Age but, as the world grew corrupt, withdrew to the heavens to become the constellation Virgo. Referred to Tav and Saturn — the lord of time and the end of ages — she embodies departed justice and the hope of its return. Her flight from the earth marks the passing of the age of innocence; her catasterism makes her the celestial emblem of righteousness.

astrology.summary: The art of reading the will of heaven in the motions of the stars, fixed at the path of the Star.
astrology.description: Astrology is set at Tzaddi and Aquarius, the path of the Star, whose figure pours the waters of heaven and gazes upon the constellations. As a magical power it is the science of correspondence raised to its widest scope—the reading of character, event, and destiny in the angles and aspects of sun, moon, and planets against the zodiac. It is the parent art from which much of the 777 system of correspondences itself descends, the great map by which the magician locates every force in space and time.

aswata.summary: The sacred fig of the Gita—Ashvattha, the cosmic tree rooted in heaven, set at the solar heart of Tiphareth.
aswata.description: Aswata (Ashvattha) is the sacred fig of India—Ficus religiosa, the pipal—here attributed to Tiphareth. In the Bhagavad Gita it is the great cosmic tree whose roots are above in the eternal and whose branches spread below into the world, the inverted tree of manifestation that the wise must "cut with the axe of non-attachment." Set at Tiphareth, the harmonising centre, it is the tree of the world-order rooted in the divine. Esoterically the Ashvattha is the Tree of Life seen from the East—creation depending from its source, the solar heart through which the eternal flowers into time.

ataxia.summary: Ataxia at Beth and Mercury — the breakdown of Mercurial coordination.
ataxia.description: Ataxia, the loss of muscular coordination and ordered movement, is placed at Beth, the path of Mercury. Mercury rules the nervous system, the relaying of messages, and the fine ordering of motion; ataxia is the failure of that swift Mercurial governance, the body's signals scrambled and its movements unstrung. As a symbol it is intelligence severed from execution, the messenger's lines cut.

atembui.summary: Name of the last decan of Pisces—the final face of the zodiac, where feeling is poured out and the wheel completes.
atembui.description: Atembui is 777's name for the last decan of Pisces (20°–30°), the final face of the entire zodiac. Mars rules it and it bears the Ten of Cups—Satiety—feeling brought to fullness and exhaustion, the cup poured out at the end of the cycle. Among the thirty-six Hermetic decan-faces it marks the dissolution in which the wheel completes itself and returns, through Aries, to the beginning.
tables: CLXXII. Egyptian Names of the Cadent Decans

aterechinis.summary: Name of the middle decan of Libra, the Saturnine face where balance breaks into sorrow.
aterechinis.description: Aterechinis is the name 777 records for the middle decan of Libra (10°–20°). Saturn rules this face and its card is the Three of Swords—Sorrow—the grief that enters when balance is broken and a bond is cut. Among the thirty-six Hermetic decan-faces inherited from Egypt, it names the wounding at the heart of the airy sign of partnership.
tables: CLXX. Egyptian Names of the Succedent Decans

athena.summary: Athena, goddess of wisdom and just war — the grey-eyed strategist born from the head of Zeus.
athena.description: Athena is the Greek goddess of wisdom, strategic warfare, craft, and the city, sprung fully armed from the head of Zeus. Spread across Chokmah, the path of Mars, and the airy signs, she unites intellect with disciplined force — the spear and aegis joined to the owl of wisdom. Patroness of Athens and of heroes, she is reason made sovereign over violence, the clear-eyed power of skilled and righteous action.

athor.summary: Diurnal angelic Lord of Aquarius within the Airy Triplicity.
athor.description: Athor is the day-governor of Aquarius among the angelic Lords of the Triplicities (not to be confused with the goddess Hathor, with whom it shares only a sound). As the fixed member of the Air trine, Aquarius by day is the clear daylight reason of the water-bearer, ideas held steady and shared; Athor presides over this lucid, settled intellect of the light.

atma.summary: Atma — the divine Self, the spark of the universal Spirit, attributed to Kether.
atma.description: Atma, in the Vedantic and Theosophical division of the human principles, is the Self — the pure, universal Spirit, identical with Brahman, the highest and most impersonal of the seven principles. Set fittingly in 777 at Kether, the Crown, it is the divine ground of the being, the 'I' that underlies all the lower vehicles and is one with the Absolute.

atma-darshana.summary: The Vision of the Self (ātma-darśana) — the realisation of the Ātman, set at Kether.
atma-darshana.description: Atma-darshana is the 'vision of the Self' among the Hindu/Buddhist Results, attributed to Kether, the Crown. In the Vedantic scheme it is the direct realisation of the Ātman — the true Self recognised as identical with the supreme reality, beyond name, form and the play of the mind. Set at the highest Sephira, it figures the summit of attainment in the path of knowledge (jñāna), where the seeker, dropping all that is not-Self, knows the Self alone; it is the Eastern counterpart to the Knowledge and Conversation of the Holy Guardian Angel raised to its non-dual extreme.
tables: XXIV. Certain of the Hindu/Buddhist Results

atropine.summary: The principal tropane alkaloid of belladonna, attributed to Geburah.
atropine.description:
Atropine is the isolated tropane alkaloid that gives belladonna and its kin their lethal and visionary power, placed at Geburah — the martial sphere of severity, the cutting and dangerous force. Pharmacologically it blocks the parasympathetic nervous system, dilating the pupil, racing the heart, and at higher doses producing delirium; in modern medicine it is a vital antidote and cardiac drug, a clear case of Geburah's destructive power turned to disciplined use.

Caution: atropine is highly toxic and dangerous outside precise clinical control. This entry is scholarly only.
atropine.caution: Highly toxic alkaloid; clinical use only. Scholarly entry — not advice for use.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

attis.summary: Attis, the castrated shepherd-god — consort of Cybele, the slain and reborn vegetation deity, at Virgo.
attis.description: Attis is the Phrygian shepherd-god, beloved and consort of the Great Mother Cybele, who in frenzy emasculated himself and died, to be mourned and reborn with the spring. Referred to Yod and Virgo, he belongs to the dying-and-rising gods of vegetation, his self-sacrifice marking the death and return of the green world. His ecstatic, blood-stained cult was among the great mystery religions of the ancient Mediterranean.

audere.summary: 'To Dare'—the watery power of the Sphinx, the virtue of courage.
audere.description: Audere, 'to dare,' is set at Mem and Water, the watery member of the Four Powers of the Sphinx. As the power of Water it is the virtue of courage—the boldness to enter the unknown depths, to face the terrors of the astral and the ordeals of initiation without flinching. The eagle-faced daring of the Sphinx, it is the heart's readiness to plunge in where knowledge has shown the way and will has chosen it, the audacity without which no magician crosses the threshold.
tables: L. Transcendental Morality (10 Virtues; 7 Deadly Sins; 4 Magic Powers)

aum.summary: AUM (Om), the sacred primal sound — the cosmic syllable, among the Veils of the Negative.
aum.description: AUM, or Om, is the supreme sacred syllable of Hindu tradition, the primordial vibration from which the universe is sounded into being. Referred to the Veils of the Negative, it stands at the very root of manifestation, beyond all the Sephiroth — the unmanifest sound that contains creation, preservation, and dissolution in its three letters A-U-M. To intone it is to attune the self to the fundamental hum of the cosmos, the Word behind all words.
tables: XXII. Small Selection of Hindu Deities

aumgn.summary: Crowley's deepened AUM: the mantra that binds creation, preservation, and the silence beyond death.
aumgn.description: AUMGN is Crowley's expansion of the sacred Hindu syllable AUM. Where AUM spans the A of creation, the U of preservation, and the M of dissolution, Crowley inserts the nasal GN to carry the sound past the stop of death into a resonant continuity—the silent hum that does not cease, the secret that destruction is not annihilation but transformation. Set at Nun and the sign Scorpio, the path of Death and of the deepest mysteries of putrefaction and rebirth, AUMGN is the word that conquers the grave by singing through it, dissolving the fear of ending into the unbroken vibration of being.

aur-pot.summary: Alchemical 'drinkable gold', attributed to Kether; the medicine of perfection.
aur-pot.description:
Aurum Potabile — 'potable gold,' drinkable gold — is set at Kether, the Crown, as the mineral counterpart of the Elixir Vitæ: the legendary alchemical preparation in which the perfect metal is rendered into a liquid medicine able to cure all ills and confer long life. It is the physical sacrament of the highest Sephirah, gold (the perfected solar substance) raised to the Crown and made a draught of regeneration. Esoterically it names the incorruptible perfection taken inwardly — the medicine that is the goal of the Work itself.

Caution: historical gold preparations were often toxic; this is an alchemical-symbolic entry.
aur-pot.caution: Historical gold 'medicines' were frequently toxic. Alchemical/symbolic entry only.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

auramoth.summary: Thelemic goddess of the element Water, invoked in the West in the Star Ruby.
auramoth.description: Auramoth is the goddess of the element Water in the Thelemic magical pantheon, invoked in the West in Crowley's Star Ruby (the cry 'ahh AURAMOTH'), paired with Thoum-aesh-neith, the goddess of Fire. Her name fuses the radiance of the aura with the great mother-goddess Maut (Mut), so that she presides over the deep, receptive, formative waters — the feminine, lunar-aqueous power of the West and of the path of Mem upon the Tree.

aurora.summary: Aurora, the rosy-fingered dawn — the goddess who opens the gates of day, at Tiphareth.
aurora.description: Aurora is the Roman goddess of the dawn, who rises each morning from the ocean to herald the sun and scatter the darkness with her rosy light. Referred to Tiphareth, the solar centre of the Tree, she is the radiant prelude to the sun's glory — the first blush of light that promises the full day. As the renewing dawn she is hope, beginning, and the daily rebirth of the world in light.

avarice.summary: The Saturnian vice of avarice, the grasping greed of the constrictor.
avarice.description: Avarice is listed among the vices at Tav and Saturn, the path of the Universe and the heaviest of the planetary forces. As the shadow of Saturn—lord of limitation, hoarding, and cold contraction—it is the miser's greed, the gripping accumulation that withholds and never gives. Where Saturn's higher gift is structure and patient endurance, its vice is the freezing of the heart into mere possessiveness, the soul shrunk to the size of what it clutches.
tables: L. Transcendental Morality (10 Virtues; 7 Deadly Sins; 4 Magic Powers)

avigga.summary: Avijjā — the Pali name for the tenth fetter, ignorance, root of the whole chain.
avigga.description: Avigga (avijjā) is the Pali for the tenth of the ten fetters, ignorance — the fundamental unknowing of the Four Noble Truths and of the true nature of things, set at Malkuth. It heads the chain of dependent origination and is the last fetter to fall; with its ending comes complete awakening. (Its English face appears under 'Ignorance'.)

avron.summary: Angel of the second face of Pisces, where feeling brims over into full happiness.
avron.description: Avron governs the middle decan of Pisces (10–20°), attributed to Jupiter and the Nine of Cups, *Happiness* — the wish fulfilled, emotional plenty and deep contentment. Jupiter blesses the Piscean sea with generous joy. Avron is the angel of complete and overflowing happiness, the cup of feeling filled to its brim.

awwa.summary: al-'Awwa', 'the barker' — the lunar mansion of the dogs of Virgo.
awwa.description: al-'Awwa', 'the barker' or 'the howlers' (a zigzag of stars in Virgo), is the Mansion of the Moon in the path of Virgo (Yod). Read as a station of benevolence and gain, of fruitful unions and good harvests, it belongs to the earthy, nurturing sign of the Virgin.
tables: CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon

azeph.summary: Forbidden names — the Nuctemeron genius of the tenth hour presiding over forbidden names, set by Crowley at Capricorn.
azeph.description: In the Nuctemeron — the “Day Illumined by Night” ascribed to Apollonius of Tyana and preserved by Éliphas Lévi — Azeph is numbered among the genii of the tenth hour, the spirit of forbidden names. His province is the insufferable or forbidden names, bound in the tradition to blasphemy and the misuse of holy words. Crowley arranges the twelve hours and their genii upon the paths of the Tree (777, Table CLXXIII), placing him at Capricorn (Ayin).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

ba.summary: Ba — the Egyptian soul, the human-headed bird, attributed to Binah.
ba.description: The Ba, depicted as a bird with a human head, is in Egyptian thought the personal soul or animating spirit that, after death, flies free of the body by day and returns to it by night. Referred in 777 to Binah, the supernal Mother and the womb to which the soul returns, it figures the individual essence that survives and journeys — the migrating soul-bird of the dead.
tables: CXVI. Egyptial Attribution of Parts of the Soul

ba-neb-tattu.summary: Ba-Neb-Tattu (Banebdjedet), the ram-god of Mendes — the soul of Osiris, at Taurus.
ba-neb-tattu.description: Ba-Neb-Tattu is Banebdjedet, the ram-headed god of Mendes, whose name means “the Ram, Lord of Djedet,” regarded as the living soul (ba) of Osiris and of the great gods. Referred to Vav and Taurus, the sign of generative animal strength, he embodies fertile, virile power and the indwelling soul of the divine. The sacred ram of Mendes was honoured as the very life-force of the gods made flesh.

babalon-vitriol.summary: The names of the Great Mother and the inward descent: BABALON the Scarlet Woman and the alchemical VITRIOL of Binah.
babalon-vitriol.description: Binah, the supernal Mother and dark sea of Understanding, takes the formula BABALON beside the alchemists' VITRIOL. BABALON is Crowley's spelling of the Woman girt with a sword, the holy whore who receives all and refuses none, in whose cup of fornication the saint pours every drop of his blood—the formula of the surrender of the ego across the Abyss into the womb of the Mother. VITRIOL is the acrostic Visita Interiora Terrae Rectificando Invenies Occultam Lapidem—"Visit the interior of the earth; by rectification thou shalt find the hidden stone"—the command to descend inward to the dark matrix where the soul is dissolved and re-coagulated. Both name the same mystery: the giving-up of self into the great darkness that understands.

bacchus.summary: Bacchus (Dionysus), god of wine and ecstasy — the liberator of the divine madness, at Tiphareth.
bacchus.description: Bacchus is the Roman name for Dionysus, the god of wine, vine, ecstasy, and ritual madness, the liberator who dissolves the bounds of the ordinary self. Referred to Tiphareth, Capricorn, and the place of Spirit, he is a dying-and-rising god whose mysteries promised rebirth through divine intoxication and frenzy. He is the joyous, dangerous power of release — the loosening of restraint that opens the soul to the god within.

back.summary: The back of the Perfected Man, the watery column that bears the burden of the body.
back.description: The Back is attributed to Mem and Nun, Water and Scorpio, in the body of Adam Kadmon. As the spine and back uphold the trunk and channel the nervous current from the base to the head, this region answers to the deep watery and Scorpionic forces that run, hidden, along the central axis of the body—the secret serpent-power that the Eastern traditions place along the spine, here cast in the watery language of the Western Tree.

back-of-head.summary: Qoph — 'back of the head'; the dim hindbrain of dream and instinct, path of The Moon.
back-of-head.description: Qoph means the 'back of the head' (and is linked to 'ape' and to the eye of a needle) — the hindmost, least conscious part of the skull, seat of the older, animal brain. In Liber 777 Qoph is the path of The Moon, attributed to Pisces, joining Netzach to Malkuth. The image is precise: the back of the head is the region of dream, instinct, and atavism, and the Moon's path leads through exactly this twilight — the dim, watery, fearful threshold of sleep and bodily formation through which the soul descends into and ascends out of matter.
tables: III. Translation of the Names of the Paths

bael.summary: The first king of the Goetia, set in the decans of Aries — a three-headed spirit who confers invisibility.
bael.description: Bael is the first spirit of the Goetia (the Lesser Key of Solomon), a great king ruling in the East, attributed to the fiery decans of Aries. He governs many legions and his chief office is to make the magician go invisible. Tradition gives him a strange triple form — heads of a cat, a toad and a man, or all three at once — and a hoarse voice. As the leading spirit of the seventy-two he sets the pattern of the whole order: a fallen power compelled by the divine names to serve the operator who knows how to bind him, here cloaking his summoner from sight.

baglis.summary: Measure and balance — the Nuctemeron genius of the second hour presiding over measure and balance, set by Crowley at Taurus.
baglis.description: In the Nuctemeron — the “Day Illumined by Night” ascribed to Apollonius of Tyana and preserved by Éliphas Lévi — Baglis is numbered among the genii of the second hour, the spirit of measure and balance. He presides over weight, measure and proportion, the equilibrium of all quantities. Crowley arranges the twelve hours and their genii upon the paths of the Tree (777, Table CLXXIII), placing him at Taurus (Vav).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

baie.summary: The Ba — the soul-bird of mobility, set at Binah, that flies between the living and the dead.
baie.description: Baie is Crowley's rendering of the Egyptian Ba, one of the chief parts of the soul in the Egyptian scheme, here attributed to Binah. The Ba was depicted as a human-headed bird, the mobile, individual soul that could leave the body and travel between the worlds, returning to the tomb by night and going forth by day. Placed at Binah, the supernal Mother and the sphere of the soul's higher understanding, it figures the part of us that takes wing — the personal soul capable of flight beyond the body toward the source.
tables: CXVI. Egyptial Attribution of Parts of the Soul

balam.summary: The fifty-first spirit of the Goetia, a three-headed king of Leo who gives invisibility and true answers.
balam.description: Balam (Balaam) is the fifty-first spirit of the Goetia, a terrible and powerful king of the decans of Leo. He gives true answers of things past, present and to come, and makes men invisible and witty. He appears with three heads — a bull, a man and a ram — with flaming eyes and a serpent's tail, riding upon a fierce bear and bearing a goshawk upon his fist; he speaks with a hoarse voice. A spirit of the regal fire-sign, he is the kingly giver of foresight and concealment.

balances.summary: Design detail of Justice/Adjustment (Lamed): the scales and balances.
balances.description: ‘Balances’ is a fragment of Liber 777's design for Atu VIII/XI, Justice—Adjustment—on the path of Lamed (Libra): ‘A conventional figure of Justice with scales and balances.’ The balance is Libra itself, the emblem of exact equilibrium, by which every deed is weighed against its consequence. Sword in one hand and scales in the other, the figure embodies the impersonal law of adjustment: nothing is added or taken from the cosmic account, and all things are brought, in time, to perfect poise.
tables: CLXXXI. Correct Design of Tarot Trumps

baldah.summary: al-Balda, 'the empty place' — the starless mansion of Sagittarius.
baldah.description: al-Balda, 'the city' or, by inversion, 'the empty district,' is the all-but-starless patch of sky in Sagittarius that forms the twenty-first Mansion of the Moon, set in the path of Sagittarius (Samekh). Its very emptiness gave it an ambivalent fame — a fallow, waiting ground, read as favourable for harvests, for the founding of settlements, and for the safe keeping of what is sown in barren times.
tables: CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon

banshees.summary: The wailing death-spirits of Irish lore, set at Gemini and Virgo — heralds whose cry foretells a death.
banshees.description: Among the Legendary Orders of Being, the Banshees (Irish bean sídhe, 'woman of the fairy-mound') are attributed to the airy and earthy paths of Gemini and Virgo. They are the keening spirits of Gaelic tradition, attached to old families, whose mournful wail in the night announces an approaching death. Half ancestral guardian and half omen, the banshee belongs to that twilight order of beings who move between the living and the dead; her cry is the voice of fate made audible, the messenger of an end already decreed.

banyan.summary: The one-into-many tree—the banyan whose endless aerial roots turn a single trunk into a forest, image of Kether's unity.
banyan.description: The Banyan is set at Kether and Yesod—the great Indian fig whose branches let down aerial roots that thicken into new trunks, so that a single tree becomes, in time, a whole grove sheltering thousands. It is the perfect natural emblem of the One unfolding into the many while remaining one living organism, the Crown's unity expressed in endless ramification; beneath such a tree sages sit and the divine is taught. Esoterically the banyan is the immortal, self-perpetuating life of the source—the single root whose canopy is a world.

barbatos.summary: The eighth spirit of the Goetia, a duke of Gemini who grants the speech of beasts and breaks enchantments.
barbatos.description: Barbatos is the eighth spirit of the Goetia, a great duke of the decans of Gemini, who comes with great power when the Sun is in Sagittarius, attended by four noble kings and their troops. He gives the understanding of the voices and songs of birds and of other animals, breaks open the hidden treasures laid by enchantment, and reconciles friends and those in power. A spirit of the airy sign, he opens the secret languages of nature and the sealed hoards of the earth.

barcus.summary: Quintessence — the Nuctemeron genius of the fifth hour presiding over quintessence, set by Crowley at Leo.
barcus.description: Barcus is the Nuctemeron genius of quintessence. That “Night-illumined Day”, ascribed to Apollonius of Tyana and handed down through Lévi's Transcendental Magic, sets a company of spirits over each of the twelve hours of the magical day, and Barcus belongs to the fifth hour. He rules the fifth essence, the subtle spirit distilled out of and above the four elements. In 777 (Table CLXXIII) Crowley redistributes these hour-genii across the zodiac, where this spirit falls at Leo (Teth).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

basilisk.summary: The king-serpent of Geburah—the lethal gaze, concentrated venom and terror, destructive martial power.
basilisk.description: The basilisk is placed at Geburah, the severe Martian sphere of destruction and judgement, and it is the legendary king of serpents whose mere glance or breath was said to slay. Hatched from a cock's egg and crowned like a tyrant, the basilisk is venom and death distilled to a single deadly look—an apt emblem for the terrible, blasting power of Geburah, the sword that destroys whatever cannot endure its severity. To meet its gaze unprepared is to perish; only the mirror, which turns its own death-dealing stare back upon it, defeats it. Esoterically the basilisk figures the destructive force that must never be confronted directly but only mastered by reflection and right understanding.

bathin.summary: The eighteenth spirit of the Goetia, a duke of Virgo who knows herbs and stones and transports men afar.
bathin.description: Bathin is the eighteenth spirit of the Goetia, a mighty and strong duke of the decans of Virgo. He knows the virtues of herbs and precious stones and can carry men suddenly from one country to another. He appears as a strong man with the tail of a serpent, riding upon a pale horse. A spirit of the earthy sign, he masters the secret properties of nature and the swift translation of bodies across the world.

bay.summary: The bay-laurel of the Sun—Apollo's solar leaf crowning the harmonised heart of Tiphareth.
bay.description: The Bay (sweet bay, the true laurel) is attributed to Tiphareth, the solar centre. It is Apollo's own tree, the evergreen of prophecy, poetry, and victory, whose leaves crowned the god, his seers, and his champions, and were chewed by the Pythia to bring on the oracular trance. As a solar plant it belongs to the radiant heart of the Tree, where inspiration and triumph meet. Esoterically the bay is the green token of the illumined and victorious self, the laurel of the achieved Work worn at the centre.

bear.summary: The mighty beast of Sagittarius and Mars—raw strength, primal ferocity, the brute power that must be aimed.
bear.description: The bear stands among the magical images of the Sagittarian decans and at Mars, a creature of overwhelming bodily strength and sudden ferocity. It is the type of untrained power: massive, slumbering, and terrible when roused, the martial force in its most elemental form. Under Sagittarius this strength is given direction, the arrow's aim lent to the brute, while at Geburah/Mars it is severity and the warrior's might. Esoterically the bear figures the great reserves of instinctual energy that the adept must master rather than slay—power to be governed and turned to the Work.
tables: CL. Magical Images of the Decans (Succedent)
CXLIX. Magical Images of the Decans (Ascendent)

beatific-vision.summary: The Beatific Vision, the rapturous solar experience of the perfected heart.
beatific-vision.description: The Beatific Vision, attributed to Tiphareth and the Sun, is the blessed sight of the Divine that fills the soul with unshakeable joy—the visio beatifica of the Christian mystics transposed to the solar centre of the Tree. At the heart of the harmonising sixth Sephirah, where the dying-and-rising god reigns, it is the experience of the redeemed self beholding its source in beauty and blessedness, the radiant peace that crowns the long work of the heart.

tables: CXLIX. Magical Images of the Decans (Ascendent)

beautiful-man-on-winged-horse.summary: The magical image of Seere — a beautiful man upon a strong winged horse — Goetic Prince of the first decan of Pisces (by night).
beautiful-man-on-winged-horse.description: Seere (Sear, Seir), the seventieth spirit of the Goetia and a mighty Prince, appears as a beautiful man riding upon a strong winged horse. In 777 he is the nocturnal ruler of the first decan of Pisces. He is wholly good of nature and indifferent to good or evil; he can pass over the whole earth in the twinkling of an eye to bring abundance or carry messages, and discovers thefts and hidden treasures. The fair rider upon his swift winged steed images the boundless, all-pervading flow of the sign of the Fishes — desire that goes everywhere in an instant.

beautiful-woman.summary: The magical image of Gremory — a beautiful woman with a duchess's crown about her waist, upon a camel — Goetic Duke of the second decan of Libra (by night).
beautiful-woman.description: Gremory (Gamori, Gomory), the fifty-sixth spirit of the Goetia and a strong and mighty Duke, appears as a beautiful woman with a duchess's crown girded about her waist, riding upon a great camel. In 777 she is the nocturnal ruler of the second decan of Libra. She tells of things past, present and to come, discovers hidden treasures and where they lie, and procures the love of women, young and old alike. The crowned and lovely rider befits the Venusian sign of the Balance — sovereignty worn at the waist, beauty enthroned upon endurance.

beauty.summary: Beauty—the sixth Sephirah; the harmonising solar centre, seat of the Holy Guardian Angel.
beauty.description:
Tiphareth (תפארת, ‘Beauty’) is the sixth Sephirah and the radiant centre of the Tree, the point of equilibrium where all the surrounding powers are harmonised. Its planet is the Sun, and its symbolism is overwhelmingly solar: gold, the rose, the lion, the child, and above all the figure of the sacrificed-and-risen god—Osiris, Christ, Dionysus—who dies and is reborn at the heart of the cosmos. Its God-name is Tetragrammaton Eloah va-Daath; its grade is Adeptus Minor.

In the Thelemic system Tiphareth is the seat of the Holy Guardian Angel, and its attainment—the Knowledge and Conversation of the Angel—is the central work toward which Liber Samekh and much of 777 itself are directed. As the meeting-place of the higher and lower selves, Tiphareth is where the human consciousness first touches the divine and is reborn as something greater.
tables: III. Translation of the Names of the Paths
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

bee.summary: The bee of Binah—the Great Mother's industrious swarm, the queen and hive of the supernal feminine.
bee.description: The bee is attributed to Binah, the supernal Mother, and the choice is rich: the hive is a single body ruled by its queen, a perfect image of the maternal sphere from which all the workers issue and to which all return. Sacred to the great goddesses—the bee-priestesses of Demeter and Cybele, the honey of immortality—the bee is industry, order, and the sweet fruit of disciplined collective labour. Honey, incorruptible and golden, is the gift of this Mother. Esoterically the bee figures the soul as worker in the great hive of Binah, gathering the nectar of experience and rendering it into the imperishable honey of understanding under the rule of the Supernal Queen.

beetle.summary: The scarab of Scorpio and Pisces—Khepri rolling the sun from death to dawn, the emblem of self-renewal.
beetle.description: The beetle—above all the scarab—is placed at Scorpio and Pisces, the watery signs of death, dissolution and rebirth, and it is one of the supreme Egyptian glyphs of resurrection. Khepri, the rising sun, was figured as the scarab that rolls its ball of dung as the god rolls the solar disk up from the underworld each dawn, the creature seeming to be self-generated from formless matter. So the beetle marks the secret of becoming: that out of corruption and the dark waters of Scorpio the new sun is born. Esoterically it is the promise hidden in every nigredo, the life that engineers itself anew from its own decay.

tables: CLI. Magical Images of the Decans (Cadent)
CL. Magical Images of the Decans (Succedent)

behahemi.summary: Angel of the second face of Aries, where raw fire steadies into established strength.
behahemi.description: Behahemi rules the middle decan of Aries (10–20°), where the Golden Dawn sets the Sun within the Ram and the Three of Wands, *Virtue* or Established Strength. The solar sub-rulership tempers martial impulse with steadiness and confidence: the initial flare of Aries finds a centre and becomes durable. Behahemi is the angel of strength that has proven itself and can now be relied upon — the consolidation that follows the first wild charge.

beleth.summary: The thirteenth spirit of the Goetia, a terrible king of Leo who compels love.
beleth.description: Beleth is the thirteenth spirit of the Goetia, a mighty and terrible king ruling in the decans of Leo, who rides upon a pale horse amid a great noise of trumpets and music. His office is to procure the love of any man toward any woman, or the reverse, until the operator's desire is fulfilled. So fierce is his coming that the magician is counselled to receive him with courage, the hazel wand pointed to the ground. A spirit of the regal fire-sign, he is the imperious compeller of passion.

belial.summary: The sixty-eighth spirit of the Goetia, a king of Aquarius in a chariot of fire who distributes high offices.
belial.description: Belial is the sixty-eighth spirit of the Goetia, a mighty and powerful king, said to have been created next after Lucifer, attributed to the decans of Aquarius. He distributes preferments, senatorships and high offices, gives the favour of friends and foes, and grants excellent familiars; but he must be presented with gifts and sacrifices to give true answers, and even then is not to be wholly trusted. He appears as two beautiful angels seated in a chariot of fire, speaking with a comely voice. A spirit of the airy sign, he is among the greatest of the infernal kings, the bestower of rank and office.

belief-in-a-personality.summary: The first fetter — the view of a self (sakkāya-diṭṭhi), belief in a real, abiding personality.
belief-in-a-personality.description: Belief in a Personality is sakkāya-diṭṭhi, the first of the ten fetters (saṃyojana) that bind beings to the round of rebirth, attributed to Hod. It is the deep-rooted conviction that there is a permanent, separate self standing behind or within the five aggregates — the 'I am' taken as a substantial thing. This is the most basic of the fetters and the first to be severed at stream-entry; its dissolution is the dawn of insight into not-self. Set at Hod, the analytic sphere of Mercury, it figures the mind's habit of construing a solid identity out of mere process.

belladonna.summary: Deadly nightshade, attributed to Binah; the witches' herb of Saturn.
belladonna.description:
Belladonna, deadly nightshade, is set at Binah, the dark formative Mother ruled by Saturn — a perfect attribution for one of the great Saturnian poisons, an ingredient of the legendary witches' 'flying ointments' said to induce sensations of flight and visionary sabbath. Its name, 'beautiful lady,' recalls its use to dilate the pupils for cosmetic effect, a small emblem of its power to alter perception. Esoterically it belongs to the bitter, death-bearing aspect of the Great Mother, the herb of the threshold between worlds.

Caution: belladonna is a deadly poison; the deliriant tropane alkaloids it contains have killed many who sought visions through it. This is a historical and symbolic entry only — it must never be ingested.
belladonna.caution: DEADLY POISON (tropane alkaloids). Fatal in small doses. Historical/symbolic entry only — never ingest.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

benzoin.summary: The sweet balsamic resin of Netzach—benzoin, warm and honeyed, a gentle Venusian incense of love and ease.
benzoin.description: Benzoin is attributed to Netzach, the Venusian sphere. The "gum benjamin," a sweet, vanilla-balsamic resin, burns with a warm, comforting, slightly sensual smoke long used to soothe, to purify, and to draw love and harmony—virtues proper to gentle, victorious Venus. Esoterically benzoin is the warm sweet perfume of Netzach, the honeyed incense of love, pleasure, and emotional ease that softens the heart and gladdens the senses.

berith.summary: The twenty-eighth spirit of the Goetia, a red-clad duke of Capricorn who turns metals to gold.
berith.description: Berith is the twenty-eighth spirit of the Goetia, a great and terrible duke of the decans of Capricorn (known also by the names Beale and Bolfry). He tells of things past, present and to come, turns all metals into gold, and gives and confirms dignities. He appears as a soldier clad in red apparel, wearing a golden crown and riding a red horse; he is a notable liar, to be commanded into the triangle. A spirit of the earthy sign, he is the giver of gold and rank, dangerous in his deceit.

beryl.summary: The water-clear stone of the element Water — the scryer's crystal of the deep.
beryl.description: Beryl is attributed to the path of Mem, the element Water — a clear, watery stone (the family that includes emerald and aquamarine) long used for scrying; the very word 'crystal-gazing' descends through the old practice of 'beryl-gazing,' divination in a polished beryl. Its limpid, water-pale depth suits the element of intuition, dream, and the unconscious. The stone of the seer's water-mirror.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

bestial.summary: 'The Bestial Ones'—the qliphothic order of Aquarius, humane reason degraded to the brutish.
bestial.description: In the Translation of the Orders of Qliphoth 'The Bestial Ones' is the averse order attributed to Tzaddi and Aquarius. As the demonic shell of the path, it is the shadow of Aquarius' humane, forward-looking intelligence: the rational benefactor of mankind degraded into the brute, the higher mind sunk into mere animal instinct.
