It names the corruption of enlightened humanity into the bestial, the water-bearer's gift of vision drowned in unreason.
tables: CXXIII. Translation of the Orders of the Qliphoth

beta.summary: Beta — a letter of the Coptic alphabet (b/v), which Crowley attributes to the path of Beth (Mercury).
beta.description: Beta is a letter of the Coptic alphabet — the script in which the Egyptian language was written in the Christian era, the Greek alphabet adapted to Egyptian speech. It is from Greek beta (Coptic vida). Crowley folds the Coptic alphabet into the great correspondence of letters and paths in 777 (Table LI), assigning Beta to the path of Beth (Mercury) on the Tree of Life, so that the Egyptian-Christian script takes its station among the Hebrew letters and the keys of the Tarot.
tables: LI. Names of the Coptic Letters

bethehon.summary: Diurnal angelic Lord of Scorpio within the Watery Triplicity.
bethehon.description: Bethehon is the day-governor of Scorpio among the angelic Lords of the Triplicities. As the fixed deep of the Water trine, Scorpio by day shows the lit surface over a hidden depth, feeling concentrated and intense; Bethehon presides over this daylight mastery of the deeper waters, the controlled face of profound emotion.

bethon.summary: Angel of the third face of Gemini, where thought reaches its limit and collapses into ruin.
bethon.description: Bethon presides over the closing decan of Gemini (20–30°), attributed to the Sun and the Ten of Swords, *Ruin* — the logical mind pushed to total breakdown, yet with the dawn implied by the Sun set beneath it. Bethon is the angel of intellectual collapse that exhausts a way of thinking and so clears the ground for a new day.

bethor.summary: Olympic Spirit of Jupiter, dispenser of dignity, treasure, and the friendship of the airy spirits.
bethor.description: Bethor is the Olympic Spirit of Jupiter in the Arbatel tradition, placed by Crowley at Kaph, the path of the Wheel of Fortune and of jovial expansion. As Jupiter is the bringer of mercy, increase, and good fortune, so the Arbatel grants Bethor the swift conferral of dignities and riches, the reconciling of the spirits of the air so that they answer truthfully, the transport of precious stones and medicines, and the prolonging of life. He governs upon the Day of Jupiter (Thursday) and presides over a great company of subordinate kings, princes, and ministering spirits. Esoterically he embodies the benevolent, magnanimous current of Chesed pouring into the world of action — the open hand, the prosperous tide, the genial authority that lifts and enlarges whatever it touches.

between-the-pillars-sits-an-ancient.term: Between the Pillars sits an ancient
between-the-pillars-sits-an-ancient.displayTerm: Between the Pillars sits an ancient
between-the-pillars-sits-an-ancient.summary: Liber 777's design for the Hierophant (Vav): between the pillars sits an ancient.
between-the-pillars-sits-an-ancient.description: Liber 777's design for Atu V, the Hierophant (path of Vav, Taurus), is ‘Between the Pillars sits an ancient.’ The aged hierarch is enthroned between the twin columns of the temple, the seat of teaching authority, mediating between heaven and the assembled aspirants. Where the High Priestess sits before the veil in lunar silence, the Hierophant sits in solar speech, the bridge-builder who transmits the eternal doctrine. His antiquity signals the venerable continuity of the tradition he embodies and confers.
tables: CLXXXI. Correct Design of Tarot Trumps

bewitchments.summary: The Piscean art of casting glamour and enchantment over the minds of others.
bewitchments.description: Bewitchments belong to Qoph and Pisces, the path of the Moon card, the deep watery realm of illusion, the unconscious, and the deceptive astral light. As a magical power it is the throwing of glamour—binding the perceptions, kindling love or fear, weaving the fascinations by which one mind is enthralled to another. Pisces' misty, dissolving nature makes it the natural seat of such sorcery, and the tradition warns that those who work in this water risk being drowned in their own illusions.

bhavani.summary: Bhavani, the life-giving Mother — a fierce and nurturing form of the Goddess, at Binah and Netzach.
bhavani.description: Bhavani is a form of the great Goddess Parvati-Durga, the giver of life and the bestower of being, worshipped both as nurturing mother and as fierce protectress. Referred to Binah, the supernal Mother, and to Netzach, the sphere of Venus, she joins the maternal and the passionate aspects of the divine feminine. As Bhavani she is the source of existence itself, the power that grants life and sustains the world.
tables: XXII. Small Selection of Hindu Deities

bifrons.summary: The forty-sixth spirit of the Goetia, an earl of Cancer who teaches the sciences and lights candles on graves.
bifrons.description: Bifrons is the forty-sixth spirit of the Goetia, an earl of the decans of Cancer. He teaches astrology, geometry and the other arts and sciences, the virtues of herbs, woods and precious stones; he moves dead bodies from place to place and seems to light candles upon the graves of the dead. He appears first as a monster, then takes human shape. A spirit of the watery sign, he is the teacher of sciences and the disturber of the tombs.

bigostry.summary: The Jupiterian vice of bigotry, the narrowing of faith into intolerance.
bigostry.description: Bigotry (Bigostry) is listed among the vices at Kaph and Jupiter, the planet of religion, law, and expansive belief. As the shadow of Jupiter's faith it is the hardening of conviction into intolerance—the zealot's refusal of any truth but his own, the corruption of devotion into prejudice. Where the Jupiterian virtue is a generous, ordering piety, its vice is faith turned tyrannical, the expansive principle perverted into the persecution of all that differs.
tables: L. Transcendental Morality (10 Virtues; 7 Deadly Sins; 4 Magic Powers)

bihelami.summary: Angel of the first face of Pisces, where feeling withdraws into weary indolence.
bihelami.description: Bihelami rules the opening decan of Pisces (0–10°), where Saturn meets the Eight of Cups, *Indolence* — abandoned pleasure, the turning-away from emotional surfeit. Saturn drains the Piscean waters and the soul leaves the feast unfinished. Bihelami is the angel of the melancholy retreat from what no longer satisfies, the first step of a deeper search.

bime.summary: The twenty-sixth spirit of the Goetia (Bune), a three-headed dragon-duke of Sagittarius who enriches and moves the dead.
bime.description: Bune (here Bime) is the twenty-sixth spirit of the Goetia, a strong and great duke of the decans of Sagittarius. He changes the place of the dead and causes spirits to gather upon their graves; he makes men rich, wise and eloquent, and gives true answers to all demands. He appears as a dragon with three heads — those of a dog, a griffin and a man — and speaks with a high and comely voice. A spirit of the fiery sign, he commands the dead and bestows wealth and eloquence.

birds-generally.summary: The birds of Venus—creatures of air and love, the singing life of the Empress's green nature.
birds-generally.description: Birds in general are attributed to Venus and the path of the Empress (Daleth), for they are the bright, singing, amorous creatures of the air, beloved of the goddess of love and beauty—the doves and sparrows of Aphrodite, the whole feathered chorus of nature in its courtship and song. As beings of the air that nest, mate and rear their young in the green world, they belong to the Empress's domain of fertile, sensuous nature. Esoterically birds figure the aspiring soul and the messages that pass between earth and heaven; gathered under Venus they are the loveliness and longing of natural life, beauty on the wing.

bismuth.summary: The heavy earth-metal, attributed to the 32-bis path of Earth.
bismuth.description:
Bismuth is attributed to the 32-bis path of Earth — a heavy, brittle metal whose oxide forms the iridescent, almost otherworldly stair-step crystals beloved of mineral collectors, and whose salts are a long-standing earthy remedy for the stomach. Its attribution to the elemental Earth suits a dense, settling, gut-soothing metal of the lowest path. Esoterically it belongs to the grounding, stabilising virtue of Earth.

Caution: bismuth salts are mild in normal medicinal use but not harmless in excess.
bismuth.caution: Mild in medicinal use; not harmless in excess.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

black.summary: 'The Black Ones'—the qliphothic order of Cancer, the nurturing depths gone lightless.
black.description: In the Translation of the Orders of Qliphoth 'The Black Ones' is the averse order attributed to Cheth and Cancer. As the demonic shell of the path, it is the shadow of Cancer's sheltering, watery depth: the dark womb of nourishment turned into a lightless gulf, the protective enclosure become a black and smothering prison. It names the corruption of the cherishing maternal water into engulfing gloom.
tables: CXXIII. Translation of the Orders of the Qliphoth

black-diamond.summary: The dark diamond of the Veils, Capricorn, and Spirit — light hidden in absolute night.
black-diamond.description: The black diamond is attributed to the Veils of the Negative, to Capricorn, and to the path of Spirit — the supreme stone of light rendered utterly dark, the brilliance of Kether veiled in the blackness of the Negative and of Saturnine Capricorn. It is a perfect emblem of the deus absconditus, the hidden God: the same incorruptible substance as the clear diamond, yet opaque, holding its fire within. The stone of the dark night that is also the highest light.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

black-egg.summary: The Tattvic symbol of Akasha — the black or indigo egg of Spirit.
black-egg.description: The Black Egg (often indigo or violet) is the Tattvic symbol of Akasha, the element of Spirit or aether. In the system of Tattvic meditation each element is visualised as a coloured geometric form, and the egg or oval of darkness represents the subtle, all-containing space from which the other four arise. Gazed upon, it serves as a gateway to the quintessence, the still ground that underlies and reconciles the gross elements.

black-pepper.summary: The hot grain of Aries—black pepper, biting and martial, a kindling spice of the Emperor's fire.
black-pepper.description: Black Pepper is attributed to Aries (Heh, the Emperor), the cardinal fire-sign ruled by Mars. Its sharp, biting heat is the very type of a hot, pungent, martial spice—rousing, aggressive, quickening the blood—fitting the warlike, initiating energy of the Ram. Esoterically black pepper is the kindling fire of Aries taken as scent and savour, the sharp heat that breaks inertia and spurs the will to its first bold motion.

bladder.summary: The bladder, attributed to Aquarius, the reservoir of the body's spent waters.
bladder.description: The Bladder is attributed to Tzaddi and Aquarius in this table. The reservoir that collects the water filtered by the kidneys and releases it from the body, the bladder belongs with the Aquarian governance of the body's fluid economy—the holding and measured pouring-out of the stream. It completes, with the kidneys, the system by which the organism regulates and discharges its waters.

blended-pleasure.summary: Four of Cups — Blended Pleasure; Moon in Cancer, Chesed of Water: ease before satiety.
blended-pleasure.description: Blended Pleasure is the Golden Dawn title of the Four of Cups, Chesed of the watery suit, the Moon in the last decan of Cancer. Four cups stand full beneath a calm lotus, fed but no longer overflowing: pleasure received and ordered, yet mingled with the first hint of its own decline. The card warns that emotional abundance, once it grows fixed and self-satisfied, begins quietly to lose its savour.
tables: CXXXIV. Titles and Attributions of the Chalice Suit

blessings.summary: Among the contents of the highest heavens — the stored treasuries of blessing.
blessings.description: In the table of the contents of the heavens of Assiah, 'Blessings' are reckoned among the treasures held in the supernal heaven Araboth. The Talmud lists, among the things stored in the highest heaven, the treasuries of life, of peace, and of blessing — the reservoirs of divine favour kept above and dispensed upon the world. Here they are gathered to the supernal triad as one of the precious contents of the topmost sky.
tables: XCV. Contents of the Heavens of Assiah

bloated-corpse.summary: The contemplation of the bloated corpse — first of the cemetery meditations on the body's decay.
bloated-corpse.description: The Bloated Corpse (uddhumātaka) is one of the ten asubha or 'foulness' contemplations of the Forty Meditations, the cemetery-meditations in which the practitioner steadies the mind upon a body in a stage of decomposition. Set here at the path of Virgo, it is the swollen, distended corpse — the form puffed and disfigured shortly after death. These meditations are not morbid for their own sake but a deliberate antidote to lust and to the conceit of permanence: by contemplating the inevitable dissolution of the body, craving for it is loosened and the mind turned toward dispassion.

blood.summary: The blood, attributed to Saturn in this table, the dark vital fluid of the body.
blood.description: The Blood is attributed to Tav and Saturn in this table of the Body. The red tide that carries life, warmth, and nourishment to every part is the most precious of the body's fluids, anciently held to be the very vehicle of the soul. Its attribution to Saturn—lord of the deep, the fixed, and the foundational—sets the blood among the grave and essential substances on which the whole organism depends, the dark river of life running through the frame.

blood-red.summary: The red kasiṇa — a disc of red taken as the object of one-pointed concentration.
blood-red.description: Blood-red is the red (lohita) colour-kasiṇa of the Forty Meditations, set at the path of Mars. As with its fellow colour-discs, a field of red is contemplated until it is internalised as the luminous counterpart-sign and the mind enters absorption. The Martial attribution suits the heat and vividness of the colour; yet the discipline is the same cooling, focusing work as the other kasiṇas — the fierce hue made a still point on which the meditator's whole awareness converges.

bloody.summary: 'The Bloody Ones'—the qliphothic order of Taurus, sensual appetite degraded to gross hunger.
bloody.description: In the Translation of the Orders of Qliphoth 'The Bloody Ones' is the averse order attributed to Vav and Taurus. As the demonic shell of the path, it is the shadow of Taurus' rich, generative earthiness: the fixed sensual strength of the bull corrupted into bloody, devouring appetite, the lust of the flesh turned cruel and gross. It names the perversion of fertile abundance into mere consuming hunger.
tables: CXXIII. Translation of the Orders of the Qliphoth

bloody-corpse.summary: The contemplation of the bloody corpse — a cemetery meditation on the body's corruption.
bloody-corpse.description: The Bloody Corpse (lohitaka) is one of the ten foulness (asubha) contemplations of the Forty Meditations, set at the path of Aries. The meditator dwells upon the image of a body smeared and oozing with blood, one of the graphic stages of decay through which the cemetery-meditations lead the mind. Like its companions it is medicine against sensual desire and the illusion of the body's beauty and permanence — a sober, unflinching gaze meant to cool craving and awaken urgency toward liberation.

blue-circle.summary: The Tattvic symbol of Vayu — the blue circle or sphere of Air.
blue-circle.description: The Blue Circle is the Tattvic symbol of Vayu, the element of Air. In the practice of Tattvic vision the elements are contemplated as coloured forms, and the smoky-blue disc or sphere stands for the mobile, pervasive principle of Air — breath, movement, and the medium of touch. It is used as a meditative gateway into the airy quarter of the subtle world.

bo.summary: The tree of awakening—the Bo or Bodhi tree under which the Buddha won enlightenment, sacred to the Wisdom of Chokmah.
bo.description: The Bo-tree (the Bodhi, Ficus religiosa) is attributed to Chokmah, the sphere of supernal Wisdom—for it is beneath this very tree that the Buddha sat through the night and attained perfect enlightenment. The sacred fig of India, long-lived and far-spreading, it is the tree of awakening par excellence. Esoterically its place at Chokmah is exact: it is the tree of pure illuminating Wisdom, the canopy under which the bounded mind opens into the unconditioned.

boar.summary: The tusked beast of Mars—blind charging fury, the destroyer that slew Adonis, war made animal.
boar.description: The boar is attributed to Mars, and it is among the most martial of beasts: armed with tusks, immune to fear, charging straight at whatever opposes it. In myth the boar is a famed destroyer—the beast that gored the beautiful Adonis to death, the Calydonian terror that laid waste a kingdom—so that it stands for war's blind, ravaging violence and for the sudden eruption of brute force. Under Geburah's planet it carries the destructive severity of Mars in its rawest form. Esoterically the boar figures the headlong aggressive energy that must be hunted and mastered, the furious power that destroys beauty when it runs unchecked.

boars.summary: The great monstrous boars of myth, set at Mars — savage tuskers loosed as divine scourges.
boars.description: Among the Legendary Orders of Being, the Boars are attributed to the path of Mars. Greek myth knew several monstrous boars — the Calydonian Boar sent by Artemis to ravage a land that had slighted her, and the Erymanthian Boar captured by Heracles — savage, tusked beasts loosed as instruments of divine wrath and hunted by gathered heroes. Their Martial attribution befits their ferocity and the bloody hunts they provoked; as an order they figure the brute, charging violence of nature roused to fury, the wild force that gods unleash and heroes must master.

bodily-desire.summary: The fourth fetter — sensual craving (kāma-rāga), the pull toward objects of the senses.
bodily-desire.description: Bodily Desire is kāma-rāga, the fourth of the ten fetters, attributed to Yesod, the lunar foundation of the appetites and the generative life. It is sensual craving — the relentless reaching of the mind toward pleasant sights, sounds, tastes, touches and the objects of desire. Weakened at the stage of the once-returner and uprooted only by the non-returner, it is among the most tenacious of the bonds. Set at Yesod, the seat of the instinctual and reproductive forces, it figures the gravitational pull of the senses upon the soul.

boils.summary: The Plague of Boils — the breaking forth of sores, attributed to Geburah.
boils.description: The sixth plague, the boils and blains that broke out upon man and beast, is referred in 777 to Geburah, the sphere of Mars and of severity. The eruption of burning sores — affliction in the flesh — belongs aptly to the harsh, martial, chastising sphere of the fifth Sephirah.
tables: CXXII. The Ten Plagues of Egypt

botis.summary: The seventeenth spirit of the Goetia, a president and earl of Virgo who reconciles friends and foes.
botis.description: Botis is the seventeenth spirit of the Goetia, a great president and earl of the decans of Virgo. He tells of things past and to come, and reconciles friends and enemies. He appears first as an ugly viper, then as a human with great teeth and two horns, bearing a sharp and bright sword in his hand. A spirit of the earthy sign, he is the revealer of time and the maker of peace between adversaries.

bow.summary: The bow of Luna and Sol—the tension that launches the arrow, Diana's lunar arc and the engine of aspiration.
bow.description: The Bow is attributed to the Moon and the Sun, and it is the implement that gives the arrow its flight: the curved, tensioned arc that gathers and stores power, then releases it in a single directed surge. As Diana's weapon it carries the lunar attribution—the cool, far-aiming huntress—while its pairing with the solar Arrow makes it the means by which the directed ray is sped. The bow teaches that aspiration requires not only an aim but a gathered tension, a drawing-back before the loosing. Esoterically the Bow is the disciplined gathering and concentration of force that precedes its release—the stored power of the prepared will, bent to the utmost so that the arrow of aspiration may fly the farther and the truer.

brahma.summary: Brahma, the creator of the Hindu trimurti — the demiurge who utters the worlds, at the heights.
brahma.description: Brahma is the creator-god of the Hindu trinity, the four-faced deity who brings forth the universe and the Vedas. Spread in Liber 777 across Kether, Chesed, and the path of Jupiter, he is the demiurgic power of origination, the first emanation that fashions the manifold worlds. Born from the cosmic lotus or the golden egg, he is the architect of creation, complement to Vishnu the preserver and Shiva the destroyer.
tables: XXII. Small Selection of Hindu Deities

brazen.summary: 'The Brazen Ones'—the qliphothic order of Scorpio, depth degraded to shameless effrontery.
brazen.description: In the Translation of the Orders of Qliphoth 'The Brazen Ones' is the averse order attributed to Nun and Scorpio. As the demonic shell of the path, it is the shadow of Scorpio's penetrating intensity and its mysteries of death and regeneration: the deep transmuting power degraded into hard, brazen effrontery—shamelessness, the metallic glare of passion without depth. It names the corruption of profound desire into blatant, unblushing impudence.
tables: CXXIII. Translation of the Orders of the Qliphoth

bread-and.summary: The Bread and Salt of Earth—the eucharistic food of the body, the sacrament of the material world.
bread-and.description: 'Bread and...'—the Bread and Salt—is attributed to the element of Earth (the 32nd path as Malkuth), and it is the sacramental food of the magician: the simple, sustaining substance of bread, the preserving and purifying virtue of salt, taken up as the holy nourishment of the body and the consecrated emblem of the material world. As the Pantacle is the disk of Earth, so the Bread is its food—the matter that feeds and sustains the operator, hallowed into a sacrament. To eat the consecrated bread is to take the manifest world into oneself as something holy. Esoterically the Bread and Salt figure the redemption and consecration of ordinary matter—the everyday substance of life raised, through the rite, into the body of the Work and the sustenance of the spirit in the flesh.

breakers-in-pieces.summary: Gash'khalah — the averse Chesed; devourers who shatter rather than build.
breakers-in-pieces.description: The Breakers in Pieces (Gash'khalah, the 'Smiters' or 'Disturbers') are the Qliphoth of Chesed, the sphere of Mercy. Against Chesed's building, ordering benevolence they set a greedy, ravening force that smashes and devours all structure — mercy curdled into rapacity, generosity inverted into the will to consume. They are the shells of a love turned to destruction.
tables: CXXIII. Translation of the Orders of the Qliphoth

breath.summary: The breath, attributed to Air, the vital spirit drawn in and rendered out.
breath.description: The Breath is attributed to Aleph and Air. The drawing-in and giving-out of the vital air is the body's most immediate commerce with the surrounding element, and its attribution to Air is exact: breath is the air made inward, the spirit (spiritus, 'breath') by which the organism is kept alive moment to moment. In many traditions the breath is the bearer of the life-force itself, the bridge between body and soul, the rhythm on which both meditation and life depend.

breathing.summary: Mindfulness of breathing (ānāpānasati) — the central recollection, attention resting on the breath.
breathing.description: Breathing is ānāpānasati, mindfulness of in-and-out breathing, the most universally practised of the Forty Meditations and attributed in 777 to Spirit, the quintessence. The meditator simply attends to the breath as it enters and leaves the body, neither forcing nor following it elsewhere, until the mind gathers and stills. Praised by the Buddha above all other supports, the breath is always present, intimate, and self-renewing — the bridge between body and mind, the conscious and the autonomic — and through it the practitioner may pass through the full range of absorption and insight. Its placement at Spirit befits the breath's ancient identity with the life-force itself.

brilliant-ones.summary: Brilliant Ones — the English name of the angelic choir Chashmalim, the host of Assiah at Chesed.
brilliant-ones.description: In the Qabalistic angelology each Sephirah commands its own choir of angels; “Brilliant Ones” (Table CI, the Angels of Assiah given in English) renders into the vernacular the Hebrew order Chashmalim, the host attributed to Chesed. These are the Brilliant or Shining Ones, the amber-gleaming hosts of mercy and majestic order proper to Jupiter's sphere. Crowley sets them at Chesed on the Tree, where the choir gives angelic form to the energy of that sphere as it acts in Assiah, the world of action.

brondeus.summary: Presiding god of the first decan of Aquarius, the Venusian face of cold defeat opening fixed air.
brondeus.description: Brondeus is the presiding god 777 assigns to the first decan of Aquarius (0°–10°), the entry into fixed air. Venus rules this face and it bears the Five of Swords—Defeat—the failure of an idea or alliance, the cold loss with which the Water-Bearer's sign opens. The name belongs to the Greco-Egyptian roster of thirty-six decan-rulers, the faces of the old astronomy.
tables: CLXVII. Egyptian Gods of the Zodiac (Asc. Decans)

bucaphi.summary: The stryges — the Nuctemeron genius of the tenth hour presiding over the stryges, set by Crowley at Capricorn.
bucaphi.description: Bucaphi is the Nuctemeron genius of the stryges. That “Night-illumined Day”, ascribed to Apollonius of Tyana and handed down through Lévi's Transcendental Magic, sets a company of spirits over each of the twelve hours of the magical day, and Bucaphi belongs to the tenth hour. He rules the stryges, the night-hags and vampire-witches of antique lore. In 777 (Table CLXXIII) Crowley redistributes these hour-genii across the zodiac, where this spirit falls at Capricorn (Ayin).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

buddhi.summary: Buddhi — the spiritual soul of intuition, attributed to Chokmah.
buddhi.description: Buddhi, the spiritual soul or faculty of pure intuition, is the vehicle of Atma — the principle of wisdom and direct, undivided knowing. Referred in 777 to Chokmah, the supernal Wisdom, it is the discriminating light just below the divine Self, the bridge by which the impersonal Spirit touches the individuality.

buer.summary: The tenth spirit of the Goetia, a president of Cancer who teaches philosophy and the healing virtues of plants.
buer.description: Buer is the tenth spirit of the Goetia, a great president who appears when the Sun is in Sagittarius, attributed in 777 to the decans of Cancer. He teaches natural and moral philosophy, logic, and the virtues of all herbs and plants; he heals every distemper of man and gives good familiars. He is figured in a wheel-like, radiating form, sometimes likened to the centaur-archer. A spirit of the nurturing water-sign, he is the great physician and teacher of the healing arts.

bull.summary: The Bull-Kerub of Taurus and of Earth—patient strength, fertility, the sacrificial ox.
bull.description: The Bull is the Kerub of Earth, emblem of the fixed earthy sign Taurus and one of the four holy living creatures of Ezekiel's vision and of the Sphinx. It is patient, generative strength: the plough and the herd, the slow power of the soil, the sacrificial ox whose blood feeds the gods—Apis of Egypt, the bull slain by Mithras from whose body the world's life springs. Esoterically the Bull is the stable, fertile ground of manifestation, the silent power of earth that bears all things; at Taurus it is also the dumb, enduring force that the aspirant must learn to yoke and direct.

bull-with-gryphon-s-wings.summary: Bull with Gryphon's Wings — a recurring composite magical image attributed across several decanic and Goetic placements.
bull-with-gryphon-s-wings.description: 'Bull with Gryphon's wings' is a composite magical image that recurs across several cells of Crowley's image-tables, naming the iconographic type of a winged bull — a fusion of the Taurean ox-form (strength, fertility, the earthy quadruped) with the eagle-and-lion wings of the gryphon (sky-mastery, royal predation, the union of celestial and earthly power). The compound is ancient, returning in the Assyrian lamassu, the Persepolis bull-capitals, the cherubim of Ezekiel, and the apocalyptic beasts of Revelation. As a magical-image class it stands for sovereign, winged earthiness — the chthonic power lifted into the air.

burners.summary: Golachab — the averse Geburah; flaming destroyers, force without measure.
burners.description: The Burners (Golachab, the 'Flaming Ones' or 'Arsonists') are the Qliphoth of Geburah, the sphere of Severity and Mars. The disciplined, just strength of the fifth Sephirah is here perverted into blind, consuming fire — violence and wrath divorced from any purpose but devastation. They are the shells of strength run wild, cruelty for its own sake.
tables: CXXIII. Translation of the Orders of the Qliphoth
CXLIX. Magical Images of the Decans (Ascendent)
XLVII. Kings and Princes of the Jinn
XXXVI. Selection of Christian Gods (10); Apostles (12); Evangelists(4); and Churches of Asia (7)

butatar.summary: Calculations — the Nuctemeron genius of the third hour presiding over calculations, set by Crowley at Gemini.
butatar.description: In the Nuctemeron — the “Day Illumined by Night” ascribed to Apollonius of Tyana and preserved by Éliphas Lévi — Butatar is numbered among the genii of the third hour, the spirit of calculations. He governs reckoning and computation, the working and mastery of numbers. Crowley arranges the twelve hours and their genii upon the paths of the Tree (777, Table CLXXIII), placing him at Gemini (Zayin).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

butayn.summary: al-Butayn, 'the little belly' — the second lunar mansion, in the body of the Ram.
butayn.description: The second Mansion of the Moon, al-Butayn ('the little belly'), lies in the body of Aries and in 777 is attributed to the path of Aries (Heh). A small triangle of faint stars in the Ram's flank, it was traditionally read as a station of hidden treasure and of finding what is lost, of foundations laid and seed buried — the latent fertility folded within the cardinal fire of spring.
tables: CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon

cactus.summary: The armed plant of the desert—the cactus of Scorpio, water and visionary life guarded behind a wall of spines.
cactus.description: The Cactus is attributed to Scorpio (Nun, Death), the intense, secretive water-sign that hides depth behind a hard surface. Thriving where nothing else can, the cactus hoards living water within a body sheathed in spines—desire and vitality fiercely defended, the Scorpionic union of the succulent and the piercing. Certain cacti, moreover—the peyote, the San Pedro—have been sacramental visionary plants of the Americas, opening the death-and-rebirth doorway that is Scorpio's own. Esoterically the cactus is hidden, well-guarded life: the sweet water of vision walled behind thorns.

caduceus.summary: Hermes's staff of balanced serpents—the supreme weapon of Mercury, polarity reconciled and message borne.
caduceus.description: The Caduceus is attributed to Mercury and is the herald's staff of Hermes: a winged rod about which two serpents twine in balanced, ascending coils. It is the great emblem of the Mercurial art, for it shows the opposed forces—light and dark, positive and negative, the two currents of the serpent-power—reconciled and made to climb together up the central wand. As the staff of the messenger-god it also signifies the safe passage between the worlds and the authority to cross every threshold. Esoterically the Caduceus is the magician's mastery of polarity: the power to hold the warring opposites in equilibrium and raise them as a single healing, illuminating force along the central channel—the balanced ascent that is the secret of the Work.

cahor.summary: Deception — the Nuctemeron genius of the third hour presiding over deception, set by Crowley at Gemini.
cahor.description: Cahor is the Nuctemeron genius of deception. That “Night-illumined Day”, ascribed to Apollonius of Tyana and handed down through Lévi's Transcendental Magic, sets a company of spirits over each of the twelve hours of the magical day, and Cahor belongs to the third hour. He is the spirit of trickery and guile, the whole art of the deceiver. In 777 (Table CLXXIII) Crowley redistributes these hour-genii across the zodiac, where this spirit falls at Gemini (Zayin).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

camaysar.summary: The marriage of contraries — the Nuctemeron genius of the fifth hour presiding over the marriage of contraries, set by Crowley at Leo.
camaysar.description: Among the genii of the fifth hour in the Nuctemeron of Apollonius of Tyana, Camaysar presides over the marriage of contraries. His province is the wedding of opposites, the reconciliation of natures contrary and at war. Lévi gives the roll of the hour-genii in his Transcendental Magic; Crowley tabulates them along the paths of the Tree (Table CLXXIII), assigning Camaysar to Leo (Teth).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

camel.summary: The beast of the path Gimel—the camel that bears the soul across the desert of the Abyss to Binah.
camel.description: The camel belongs to Gimel, the path of the High Priestess that crosses the Abyss from Tiphareth to Kether, and the attribution is exact, for the Hebrew letter Gimel itself means 'camel.' It is the animal that can cross the trackless desert without water, and so it is the perfect emblem of the soul's passage over the Abyss—that waterless waste where no ordinary sustenance avails—carried by the silver lunar power of the Priestess. To ride the camel is to be borne across the great gulf between the lower self and the supernal light; it endures, it remembers the way, and it does not perish in the dryness.
tables: III. Translation of the Names of the Paths

camio.summary: The fifty-third spirit of the Goetia (Caim), a thrush-formed president of Virgo who grants the speech of beasts.
camio.description: Caim (here Camio) is the fifty-third spirit of the Goetia, a great president of the decans of Virgo. He gives men the understanding of the voices of birds, of bullocks, dogs and other creatures, and of the noise of the waters, and he gives true answers of things to come. He appears first as a thrush, then as a man; he answers as if in burning ashes or coals of fire. A spirit of the earthy sign, he opens the languages of the animal world.

camphor.summary: The cool white scent of the Moon—camphor of Luna and Cancer, chaste, penetrating, and pale as moonlight.
camphor.description: Camphor is attributed to the Moon and to Cancer. White, crystalline, and intensely cool to the senses, its penetrating scent has always seemed lunar—chaste and cleansing, used to quiet desire, to preserve, and in the rites of the dead. Its coldness and pallor are the Moon's own. Esoterically camphor is the cool, purifying perfume of the lunar sphere, the white scent that calms the blood and clears the air, fragrance of the chaste and reflective Moon.

cancer.summary: Cardinal Water, ruled by the Moon—home, memory, nurture, and protection.
cancer.description:
Cancer, the Crab, is cardinal Water ruled by the Moon—the sign of home, family, memory, and the protective, nurturing instinct. In 777 it is attributed to the letter Cheth and the path of the Tarot trump The Chariot (path 18), whose armoured charioteer carries the Grail within his shell. It governs the tides of feeling and the deep continuity of the past.

The Crab’s hard shell and soft interior perfectly figure the Cancerian nature: fierce in defence of what it loves, tender within. Lunar and maternal, the sign rules birth, shelter, and belonging; its shadow is clinging and emotional self-enclosure. Cancer is the womb and the hearth of the zodiac.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

candidate.summary: The seeker at the threshold, at Malkuth — the soul awaiting initiation.
candidate.description: The Candidate is the one who seeks admission, standing poor and blindfold at the door of the Temple before being brought to light. Attributed to Malkuth, the Kingdom and the world of ordinary experience, the candidate represents every soul at the outset of the Work — unawakened matter awaiting the spark of initiation that begins its ascent.
tables: CXV. Officers in a Masonic Lodge

cannabis-indica.summary: The Indian cannabis variety, attributed to Netzach and Hod; visionary and sensory.
cannabis-indica.description:
Cannabis Indica appears at Netzach and Hod — the Venusian sphere of feeling and the Mercurial sphere of mind — reflecting the two faces of its action: the heightening of the senses and emotions on the one hand, and the loosening and acceleration of thought on the other. The same plant whose resin (hashish) Crowley set at Chokmah is here placed in the lower personality, where its effects are felt in ordinary consciousness. In the Indian tradition (bhang, ganja) it carries an ancient sacramental and Shaivite association.

Caution: this is a psychoactive drug with genuine risks and variable legality. The entry is scholarly and symbolic, not an encouragement to use.
cannabis-indica.caution: Psychoactive; legality varies; dependence and acute anxiety/psychosis risk. Symbolic/historical entry only.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

capricorn.summary: Cardinal Earth, ruled by Saturn—ambition, discipline, and the ascent of the mountain.
capricorn.description:
Capricorn, the Sea-Goat, is cardinal Earth ruled by Saturn—the sign of ambition, discipline, mastery, and the patient climb toward the summit. In 777 it corresponds to the letter Ayin (‘eye’) and the path of the Tarot trump The Devil (path 26), which depicts the generative, goatish force of matter and the bondage—and liberation—of incarnate life. It governs structure, achievement, and worldly authority earned through perseverance.

The strange composite of goat and fish marks Capricorn as the creature who climbs the highest peaks yet is born from the deeps—matter aspiring to spirit, the dark fertile root of the manifest world. Its strength is endurance and responsibility; its shadow, cold ambition and pessimism. Capricorn is the mountain the initiate must scale.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

caput-draconis.summary: Geomantic figure 'Head of the Dragon' — the ascending Node; thresholds and beginnings.
caput-draconis.description: Caput Draconis, the 'Dragon's Head,' is one of the sixteen geomantic figures, taking its name from the ascending lunar Node and associated with the benefics. It is a figure of beginnings, entrances, and good thresholds — the opening of a new matter and the favourable point of departure. Generally fortunate, it signifies increase and the auspicious start of an undertaking.
tables: CXXXIX. Planets Exalted in the Signs of the Zodiac

carbon.summary: The element of the Veils and of Spirit — the hidden root-substance of all life.
carbon.description: Carbon stands at the Veils of the Negative and at the path of Spirit — a striking attribution for the element that is the literal backbone of all organic life and that appears, in its allotropes, as both the blackness of graphite and the perfect light of the diamond. That a single element should span the basest soot and the most brilliant gem makes it a natural emblem of the hidden root from which all forms arise, the dark potential of the Negative that contains the Crown's light in seed. Esoterically carbon is the secret prima materia of the living world.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

carcer.summary: Geomantic figure 'Prison' — attributed to Saturn; binding, restriction, delay.
carcer.description: Carcer, 'prison,' is one of the sixteen geomantic figures, attributed to Saturn and associated with Capricorn. Its closed, boxed-in form signifies binding, restriction, confinement, and delay — limits imposed and movement checked. It is among the more difficult figures, though its very fixity can mean security, isolation for a purpose, or the stable containment of what must be held fast.
tables: XLIX. Lineal Figures of the Planets, &c., and Geomany

carrying-a-viper-trumpeter-with-him.displayTerm: carrying a viper. Trumpeter with him

caseara.summary: The purgative bark, attributed to Water; herb of cleansing and release.
caseara.description:
Cascara (cascara sagrada, the 'sacred bark') is placed on the path of Mem, the element Water, among the purges — a classic stimulant laxative whose action flushes and releases, fitting Water's dissolving, cleansing nature. Esoterically it belongs to the watery work of purification, the letting-go of what is held.

Caution: stimulant laxatives are habituating and harmful with prolonged use.
caseara.caution: Stimulant laxative; habituating and harmful with prolonged use.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

cassia.summary: The sweet aromatic bark of Taurus—cassia, warm and earthy, a spice of the holy oil and of the patient bull.
cassia.description: Cassia is attributed to Taurus (Vav, the Hierophant). A warm, sweet, cinnamon-like bark named among the spices of the holy anointing oil and the perfumes of the king's robes, it has a rich, grounded, sensuous sweetness fitting the fixed earthy sign of Taurus. Esoterically cassia is the warm earthy perfume of the Hierophant's sign—the sweet bark of consecration brought down to the fertile, sensuous ground, fragrance of blessing made solid.

casting-illusions.summary: The Piscean power of weaving false appearances in the deceptive astral light.
casting-illusions.description: Casting Illusions, also set at Qoph and Pisces, is the sister-power of bewitchment: the deliberate shaping of phantasmal appearances—sounds, sights, presences—in the malleable astral substance, so that others perceive what is not materially there. The path of the Moon card governs precisely this borderland of dream and deception, where the magician who has mastered the tides of glamour can paint upon the senses of the beholder. The same faculty, turned inward and upward, becomes the visionary's power to behold true astral forms.

castor.summary: Castor, the mortal twin of the Dioscuri — horseman and brother, at Gemini.
castor.description: Castor is one of the Dioscuri, the twin sons of Leda, the mortal brother of immortal Pollux, famed as a tamer of horses. Referred to Zayin and Gemini, the very sign of the Twins, he embodies one half of the great fraternal pair whose devotion was so deep that, at his death, Pollux shared his own immortality so they might never be parted. The twins became the constellation Gemini, eternal emblem of brotherly love.

cat.summary: The solar-leonine feline of Aries and Leo—sacred to Bast, sovereign, independent, and luminous.
cat.description: The cat is attributed to Aries and to Leo, the fiery and the solar signs, and it carries the leonine fire in a smaller, subtler vessel. Sacred to Bast, the Egyptian goddess of warmth, joy and protection, the cat is the domestic kin of the lion—self-possessed, luminous-eyed in the dark, sovereign and unservile. It keeps the dignity and pride of the Sun-beast while adding the lunar mystery of the creature that sees in the night. Esoterically the cat figures the magical will that remains its own master, allied but never owned, and the watchful guardian of the threshold between light and dark.

cat-s-eye.summary: The chatoyant stone of Leo — the living slit of the solar lion's eye.
cat-s-eye.description: The cat's eye is attributed to the path of Teth and Leo — a chrysoberyl whose single shifting band of light (chatoyancy) opens and narrows like the eye of a cat, fitting the leonine, solar sign of Lust/Strength. It is the watchful, vital eye of the great beast, the stone of guarded power and alert, courageous vision; long worn as a protective amulet against the hidden and the unseen.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

cauda-draconis.summary: Geomantic figure 'Tail of the Dragon' — the descending Node; endings and exits.
cauda-draconis.description: Cauda Draconis, the 'Dragon's Tail,' is one of the sixteen geomantic figures, named for the descending lunar Node and associated with the malefics. The counterpart of Caput Draconis, it is a figure of endings, exits, and thresholds passed; generally unfortunate, it signifies loss, dissolution, and the conclusion of a matter. Yet where an ending is sought, its outgoing nature may serve, releasing what must depart.
tables: CXXXIX. Planets Exalted in the Signs of the Zodiac

causub.summary: The handling of serpents — the Nuctemeron genius of the seventh hour presiding over the handling of serpents, set by Crowley at Libra.
causub.description: Among the genii of the seventh hour in the Nuctemeron of Apollonius of Tyana, Causub presides over the handling of serpents. He rules the charming and safe handling of serpents. Lévi gives the roll of the hour-genii in his Transcendental Magic; Crowley tabulates them along the paths of the Tree (Table CLXXIII), assigning Causub to Libra (Lamed).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

cedar.summary: The kingly wood of Jupiter—cedar of Lebanon, fragrant and incorruptible, perfume of Chesed's majesty.
cedar.description: Cedar is attributed to Jupiter and to Chesed. The great cedar of Lebanon—tall, fragrant, and famously incorruptible—furnished the beams of Solomon's Temple and the palaces of kings, the very type of noble, enduring majesty fit for the beneficent, magnanimous sphere of Jupiter; its warm, lasting scent repels decay and moth. Esoterically the cedar is the perfume of Jovial sovereignty and incorruption—the kingly wood whose fragrance endures, the dignity and mercy of Chesed made aromatic.

centaur.summary: The man-horse archer of Sagittarius—Chiron the wounded healer, the beast that aims its arrow at heaven.
centaur.description: The centaur is attributed to Sagittarius, whose very glyph is the centaur-archer, and it is the perfect emblem of that sign: half horse, half man, drawing the bow and loosing the arrow of aspiration toward the heavens. The centaur unites the animal and the human, the instinctual gallop of the lower nature with the aiming, far-sighted intelligence of the higher—a tension that is the whole drama of Sagittarius. In Chiron, wisest of centaurs and teacher of heroes, this union becomes the wounded healer whose own hurt is the source of his wisdom. Esoterically the centaur figures the soul that has not yet wholly transcended the beast but has learned to ride it and to aim it upward toward the divine.

centaurs.summary: The man-horse beings of the wild, set at Sagittarius — the very form of the Archer.
centaurs.description: The Centaurs are an order of legendary beings attributed to Samekh and the sign Sagittarius — fittingly, for the Archer of the zodiac is himself a centaur, drawing his bow. Half-man and half-horse, they unite human reason with animal force; most were wild and violent, but the wise Chiron, tutor of heroes, shows their nobler aspect. As an order they figure the path's own image: the aspiring arrow of higher purpose riding upon untamed animal power.

cereals.summary: The grain of the element Earth—cereals as the body's bread, the fruited substance of the material world.
cereals.description: Cereals are attributed here to the element Earth (32 bis), as elsewhere to Malkuth—doubly the plant of the material plane. As the cultivated grasses whose seed is bread, they are the very substance of earthly sustenance, the element of Earth made edible and life-giving. Esoterically the cereal is matter at its most nourishing and faithful: the grain that, sown in the dark ground, dies and multiplies, feeding the body that the spirit may dwell in it.

cerebral.summary: The cerebral organs, the brain attributed to Mercury, seat of thought and the nerves.
cerebral.description: The Cerebral system—the brain—is attributed to Beth and Mercury. As Mercury governs the mind, the nerves, and all communication, so the brain is its bodily seat: the organ of thought, perception, and the coordination of the whole nervous network. The swift, connective intelligence of Mercury finds its physical throne in the cerebral matter, the command-centre from which the body's countless messages are sent and received.

ceres.summary: Ceres, goddess of grain and the harvest — the nourishing mother of agriculture, at Earth and Virgo.
ceres.description: Ceres is the Roman goddess of grain, agriculture, and the fruitful earth, the counterpart of the Greek Demeter, from whose name comes the word “cereal.” Referred to Malkuth, the place of Earth, and to Virgo, the sign of the harvest, she is the nourishing maternal power that brings forth and ripens the crops. Her grief for her daughter Proserpina turns the seasons; she is the giver of bread and the sustainer of human life.

ch.summary: The aspirated guttural 'Ch' — the phonetic value Crowley sets at the path of Cheth (Cancer) in his Coptic-equivalents table.
ch.description: 'Ch' (as in Scottish 'loch' or German 'Bach') is the English approximation of the rough Hebrew Ḥet (ח) and its Coptic counterpart Ϧ/Khai, which Crowley places at path 18 — Cheth, ruling Cancer. The match is etymological as well as numerical: the path-letter Cheth, the Coptic letter Khai, and the English digraph 'Ch' all carry the same scraped-throat aspiration, the breath drawn through a barrier. In Liber 777's symbolic key this is the sound of the chariot's wall, the protective enclosure of the Sangraal — appropriate to a path whose Tarot is The Chariot and whose mystery is the bounded vessel.
tables: LI. English Equivalent of the Coptic Alphabet

chain.summary: The binding fetter of Geburah—the chain of restraint and silence, discipline that constrains and controls.
chain.description: The Chain is attributed to Geburah, the severe sphere of strength and restraint, and it is the implement of binding: the fetter that constrains, the chain that holds the limbs still and the tongue silent so that nothing is dissipated in word or movement. In the magical apparatus it is the discipline that confines and controls, the necessary severity by which force is held in check and turned inward. Where the Sword cuts and the Scourge drives, the Chain binds. Esoterically the Chain is the principle of self-restraint and the binding of the unruly powers—the disciplined silence and immobility that conserve the magician's force, the fetter laid upon the lower nature so that nothing of the gathered power leaks away before it can be used.

chalcedony.summary: The soft translucent stone of Aquarius — the gentle, humane quartz.
chalcedony.description: Chalcedony — a microcrystalline quartz of soft, milky translucence — is attributed to the path of Tzaddi and Aquarius (the path of The Star). Its mild, even, light-bearing quality suits the humane, idealistic water-bearer who pours out the waters of life for all; long worn as a stone of calm and of measured, gentle speech. Esoterically it is the gem of benevolent equanimity.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

chandra.summary: Chandra, the moon-god — the radiant lord of the lunar mansions, at Gimel.
chandra.description: Chandra is the Hindu god of the moon, the luminous deity who rides the night sky in a chariot drawn by antelopes and presides over the lunar mansions, the soma, and the tides of the mind. Referred to Gimel and the Moon, he is the silver light of feeling, memory, and the waxing and waning rhythms of life. As the cup of soma he is also the divine nectar; his cool radiance governs the watery, reflective nature.
tables: XXII. Small Selection of Hindu Deities

change.summary: Two of Disks — Change; Jupiter in Capricorn, Chokmah of Earth: the dance of flux.
change.description: Change is Crowley's title for the Two of Disks, Chokmah of the earthy suit, Jupiter in the first decan of Capricorn. The serpent-ouroboros loops the two discs into the lemniscate of infinity, the Yin-Yang turning within each: the active wisdom of Chokmah descending into matter as ceaseless transformation. It teaches that the ground of the material world is not fixity but rhythm — balance maintained only by riding the wheel of change.
tables: CXXXVI. Titles and Attributions of the Pantacle Suit

chedeqiel.summary: Chedeqiel, the angel set over Libra — the assisting intelligence of the sign on the path of Lamed.
chedeqiel.description: Chedeqiel is the angel attributed to Libra in the Golden Dawn and Crowley's 777 (Table CXLIII, the Twelve Lesser Assistant Angels of the Signs). The name carries the Hebrew theophoric ending ‑el, “of God,” marking him as a ministering intelligence rather than a ruling archangel: the lesser angel who carries the governance of the sign into act. Set over Libra (cardinal Air), he embodies the balancing justice and proportion of the scales; Crowley places him at the path of Lamed on the Tree of Life.
tables: CXLIII. Twelve Lesser Assistant Angels in the Signs (Transl).

chenen.summary: Name of the last decan of Sagittarius, the Saturnine face of aspiration overburdened.
chenen.description: Chenen is 777's name for the last decan of Sagittarius (20°–30°). Saturn rules this face and it bears the Ten of Wands—Oppression—aspiration overburdened, the fire of the quest weighed down by its own ambition. Among the thirty-six decan-faces it marks the heavy close of Sagittarius before the climb of Capricorn.
tables: CLXXII. Egyptian Names of the Cadent Decans

cherub-of-air.summary: The Kerub of Air at Aquarius—the Man-faced living creature, angelic guardian of the airy throne.
cherub-of-air.description: The Cherub of Air is attributed to Aquarius and is one of the four Kerubim, the holy living creatures of Ezekiel's vision and of Revelation that bear the throne of God and guard the quarters of creation. To Air and to Aquarius belongs the Man (or Angel), the human-faced Kerub, signifying intelligence, the rational and aspiring soul, and the airy element of mind. As a guardian-power the Kerub holds and stabilises its element, standing watch at the gate of the East. Esoterically the Cherub of Air is the angelic intelligence that governs the breath and the mind, the fixed spiritual force underlying the restless element of thought.

cherub-of-b.summary: A Kerubic guardian set at Leo—the Lion-faced living creature watching over the fiery throne.
cherub-of-b.description: This Cherub is set at Leo, the fixed-fire sign whose Kerubic emblem is the Lion, one of the four holy living creatures that bear the throne and ward the quarters of creation. As the Lion-Kerub it carries the solar majesty and devouring strength proper to Leo, the angelic power that holds and dignifies the fiery force. Like all the Kerubim it is at once guardian and sustainer—a fixed spiritual intelligence stabilising the element entrusted to it. Esoterically it figures the leonine guardian of the sacred fire, the steadfast watcher at the gate of the most ardent of signs.

cherub-of-d.summary: A Kerubic guardian set on the path of Aleph and Air—the living creature warding the airy throne.
cherub-of-d.description: This Cherub is set upon Aleph, the path of Air and the Fool, and so belongs to the airy Kerub among the four holy living creatures that bear the throne and guard the quarters. To Air the tradition gives the human-faced Kerub, the Man or Angel, sign of the rational and aspiring soul. As guardian and sustainer it holds the volatile element of breath and mind to its true nature, a fixed angelic intelligence at the gate of the East. Esoterically it figures the watcher over the element of thought, the steadfast guardian standing where the Fool steps into the boundless air.

cherub-of-e.summary: A Kerubic guardian set at Taurus—the Bull-faced living creature watching over the earthy throne.
cherub-of-e.description: This Cherub is set at Taurus, the fixed-earth sign whose Kerubic emblem is the Bull, one of the four holy living creatures of the vision that bear the throne and ward the quarters of creation. As the Bull-Kerub it carries the patient strength and stability proper to Taurus, the angelic power that holds dense matter to its order so that it may serve as foundation. Like all the Kerubim it is guardian and sustainer both, a fixed spiritual intelligence stabilising its element. Esoterically it figures the steadfast bull-guardian of the earthy throne, the watcher at the gate of form.

cherub-of-earth.summary: The Kerub of Earth—the Bull-faced living creature, steadfast guardian of the earthy throne.
cherub-of-earth.description: The Cherub of Earth is one of the four Kerubim, and to Earth belongs the Bull (Taurus), the patient, powerful beast that befits the solid, fixed element of body and form. As a holy living creature it guards the northern quarter and sustains the densest of the elements, the angelic intelligence that holds matter to its proper order so that it may be the firm foundation of the rest. Esoterically the Cherub of Earth is the guardian-power of the body and the manifest world, the steadfast bull-strength that grounds the spirit's work in the solidity of the real.

cherub-of-fire.summary: The Kerub of Fire—the Lion-faced living creature, blazing guardian of the fiery throne.
cherub-of-fire.description: The Cherub of Fire is one of the four Kerubim, and to Fire belongs the Lion, the great solar beast whose roar and radiance befit the element of heat, will and devouring energy. As a holy living creature it is at once a guardian of the southern quarter and a sustainer of the elemental force, the angelic power that holds fire to its true nature so that it warms and illumines rather than merely consumes. Esoterically the Cherub of Fire is the spiritual intelligence behind the will, the leonine guardian of the sacred flame, fixing and governing the most volatile and ardent of the elements.

cherub-of-water.summary: The Kerub of Water—the Eagle-faced living creature, soaring guardian of the watery throne.
cherub-of-water.description: The Cherub of Water is one of the four Kerubim, and to Water is given the Eagle, the high-soaring bird that, in the alchemical and Kabbalistic tradition, represents the exalted and volatile aspect of the watery element—Scorpio raised to its higher form, the eagle that mounts from the depths toward the sun. As a holy living creature it guards the western quarter and sustains the element of feeling, dream and the deep. Esoterically the Cherub of Water is the angelic intelligence governing the emotions and the astral tides, the eagle-power that lifts the heavy waters into spirit and holds them to their sacred office.

chief-among-the-mighty.summary: Part of the Emperor's title (Heh): Chief among the Mighty—the sovereign martial authority.
chief-among-the-mighty.description: ‘Chief among the Mighty’ completes the Golden Dawn title of Atu IV, the Emperor (path of Heh, Aries), whose full style is ‘The Son of the Morning, Chief among the Mighty.’ It names him as the first and foremost of the active, warlike powers—the ram-helmed ruler enthroned, the executive will that commands rather than counsels. Where the Hierophant teaches and the Empress nourishes, the Emperor governs by force of law and the sword of authority, the apex of the elemental and martial hierarchy on the Tree.

child.summary: The divine child of Tiphareth—the reborn solar god, Horus the infant crowned at the heart of the Tree.
child.description: The child is attributed to Tiphareth, the solar centre of the Tree, and it is one of that sphere's central images: the divine infant, the reborn sun, the innocent and radiant new self born at the heart of the cosmos. Here the child is Horus the babe (Harpocrates), the holy one whose finger seals the lips of silence, and the Christ-child of the winter solstice—every god who is born to redeem and renew. As the symbol of the regenerated consciousness that wakes in Tiphareth after the dark of the night, the child carries innocence, wholeness, and the promise of the future. Esoterically it is the new birth of the self upon contact with the Holy Guardian Angel, the solar child crowned in the place of beauty.

child-voiced-phoenix.summary: The magical image of Phenex — a phoenix that sings with a child's voice — Goetic Marquis of the first decan of Aries (by night).
child-voiced-phoenix.description: Phenex (Pheynix), the thirty-seventh spirit of the Goetia and a great Marquis, appears as the phoenix, singing sweet notes in the voice of a child — notes the magician must not heed, but bid him take human shape. In 777 he is the nocturnal ruler of the first decan of Aries. He is an excellent poet and obedient, and told Solomon he hoped to return to the seventh heavenly throne after twelve hundred years. The self-renewing firebird with a child's voice marks the cardinal-fire dawn of the zodiac — beginning, rebirth and the innocence of new flame.

child-with-angels-wings-rides-a-two-head.term: Child with angels wings rides a two-headed dragon
child-with-angels-wings-rides-a-two-head.displayTerm: Child with angels wings rides a two-headed dragon
child-with-angels-wings-rides-a-two-head.summary: The magical image of Volac — a winged child upon a two-headed dragon — Goetic President of the second decan of Sagittarius (by night).
child-with-angels-wings-rides-a-two-head.description: Volac (Valak, Ualac), the sixty-second spirit of the Goetia and a President, appears as a small child with the wings of an angel, riding upon a two-headed dragon. In 777 he is the nocturnal ruler of the second decan of Sagittarius. He gives true answers concerning hidden treasures, and tells where serpents may be seen, delivering them up to the magician harmless. The innocent winged child mastering the twin-headed dragon images the lofty, questing fire of the Archer — guileless wisdom riding upon primal force.

chill.summary: Chill at Mem and Water — the cold, damp incursion of the watery element.
chill.description: Chill is attributed to Mem, the path of the element Water. In humoral and astrological medicine the watery element is cold and moist, and a chill is its characteristic intrusion — the body invaded by cold damp, vitality quenched and circulation slowed. It figures the dampening, dissolving power of Water turned against the warmth of life, the shiver of the element seeking to drag heat down into its depths.

chimaeras.summary: The fire-breathing hybrid monsters, set at Mars — composite beasts of lion, goat and serpent.
chimaeras.description: Among the Legendary Orders of Being, the Chimaeras are attributed to the path of Mars. The Chimaera of Greek myth was a fire-breathing monster compounded of lion, goat and serpent, slain by Bellerophon mounted on Pegasus; from it the word 'chimerical' descends, naming any impossible, monstrous fusion. Their Martial attribution suits these violent, flame-breathing hybrids; as an order they figure the unnatural conjunction of incompatible natures into a single destructive force, the monstrous born of disorder.

chomse.summary: Chomse (Khonsu), the moon-god of Thebes — the wandering lunar traveller, at Gimel.
chomse.description: Chomse is Khonsu, the Theban god of the moon, son of Amoun and Mut, whose name means “the traveller” for the moon's journey across the night sky. Attributed to Gimel and the Moon, he is healer and reckoner of time, the youthful lunar power who drives away evil spirits and presides over the months. As the moon made divine he completes the Theban triad and governs the silver light that measures out the seasons.

christ-coming-to-judge-the-world.term: Christ coming to Judge the World
christ-coming-to-judge-the-world.displayTerm: Christ coming to Judge the World
christ-coming-to-judge-the-world.summary: Christ as Judge — the returning Christ in majesty, attributed to Geburah.
christ-coming-to-judge-the-world.description: 'Christ coming to judge the world' is set at Geburah, the fifth Sephirah, the sphere of Mars, of severity, and of divine justice. Here the gentle Saviour of Tiphareth is seen in his other aspect — the stern apocalyptic Judge wielding the sword of righteousness, separating and chastising. The attribution marks the necessary severity that balances mercy: the same God who redeems must also judge.
tables: XXXVI. Selection of Christian Gods (10); Apostles (12); Evangelists(4); and Churches of Asia (7)

christians.summary: Christians — in the Arab cosmology of the seven hells, the dwellers of Laza, set at Hod.
christians.description: In the medieval Arab scheme of the seven hells reproduced in 777, each of the seven gates of fire is allotted to a class of souls. The Christians are named as the dwellers of Laza ('the blazing flame'), set in this table at Hod. The attribution belongs to a polemical eschatology of its period, in which the adherents of each faith were ranged in the descending palaces of Jahannam; it is recorded here as a historical artefact of comparative cosmology, not as doctrine.
tables: CXXVI. Inhabitants of the Seven Hells of the Arabs

chyle.summary: The chyle, attributed to Fire, the milky fluid of digested nourishment.
chyle.description: The Chyle is attributed to Shin and Fire in this table of the Body. In the older physiology chyle is the milky fluid formed from digested food in the intestines and carried into the blood—the first refined product of nourishment, the body's nutriment made fluid. Its attribution to Fire befits this transforming office: the digestive heat that 'cooks' the food and renders it into the assimilable chyle, the warm beginning of the body's increase.

cinnamon.summary: The warm golden spice of the Sun—cinnamon, sweet and kindling, an ingredient of the holy anointing oil.
cinnamon.description: Cinnamon is attributed to the Sun (and to Gemini). Its warm, sweet, kindling fragrance is solar by nature—heat and gold made spice—and it was a chief ingredient of the holy anointing oil of the Hebrews and a treasure of the ancient spice-trade. Esoterically cinnamon is the warm solar perfume of vitality and consecration, the kindling sweetness that anoints and enlivens, fragrance of the Sun's own heat.

circle.summary: The circle — primary lineal figure attributed to Binah, the supernal Mother, in table XLIX.
circle.description: The circle is one of the most ancient and ubiquitous magical symbols — the figure without beginning or end, the bounding line of all enclosed space, the womb. In Crowley's lineal-figures table (XLIX) it is set among the yonic forms attributed to Binah, the great formative Mother on the Tree, alongside the Plane, the Diamond, and the Oval — all curves whose interior contains, receives, and gestates. As a geometric primitive it underwrites every ritual circumscription and every protective circle in Western magic, and in Liber 777's reading it is the formal sign of receptive feminine power.
tables: XLIX. Lineal Figures of the Planets, &c., and Geomany

circulatory-system.summary: The circulatory system, attributed to the Sun, the solar tide of blood through the body.
circulatory-system.description: The Circulatory System is attributed to Resh and the Sun. Centred on the solar heart, the circulation of the blood is the great rhythmic tide that carries warmth, nourishment, and life to every member and returns to be renewed—the very emblem of the Sun's life-giving radiance distributed through the body. As the Sun is the source of light and vitality in the heavens, so the circulation is the bodily current of that solar life.

civet.summary: The dark animal musk of Capricorn and Binah—civet, heavy and carnal, perfume of the deep and the goat.
civet.description: Civet is attributed to Capricorn and to Binah. A heavy, intensely animal secretion that becomes, when greatly diluted, a warm and sensual base for perfume, it carries the dark, earthy, carnal note proper to the goat-sign of Capricorn and to the deep, formative blackness of Binah, the Great Mother. Esoterically civet is the perfume of the dark generative depths—the animal heaviness that, refined, becomes the ground of desire, the scent of the fertile blackness from which form is born.

tables: CXLIX. Magical Images of the Decans (Ascendent)

clairvoyance.summary: The lunar power of clear seeing, the vision that pierces the veil of the astral light.
clairvoyance.description: Clairvoyance, attributed to Gimel and the Moon, is the faculty of seeing what the bodily eye cannot—images, presences, and patterns moving in the astral light. On the path of the High Priestess, which crosses the Abyss along the middle pillar, the moon's silver mirror reflects the hidden so that the trained seer reads it directly. In the Golden Dawn and Thelemic systems it is the first and most characteristic of the lunar powers, the opening of the inner sight by which all the other arts of vision become possible.

clangers.summary: 'The Clangers'—the qliphothic order of Gemini, communication degraded to meaningless noise.
clangers.description: In the Translation of the Orders of Qliphoth 'The Clangers' is the averse order attributed to Zayin and Gemini. As the demonic shell of the path, it is the shadow of Gemini's gift of speech and connection: living communication degraded into empty clamour, the clashing din of noise without sense, words that signify nothing. It names the corruption of the messenger's clear word into mere clattering uproar.
tables: CXXIII. Translation of the Orders of the Qliphoth

clay-of-death.summary: Tit ha-Yaven, the Miry Clay — a hell-compartment set at Geburah.
clay-of-death.description: The 'Clay of Death' (Tit ha-Yaven, the miry clay) is one of the seven compartments of Gehenna, attributed to Geburah, the Martial sphere of Severity. The name recalls the Psalmist's 'miry clay' from which he is drawn up — a region of clinging, suffocating mud in the descending underworld, the heavy, entrapping mire of the Hells answering to the rigours of the sphere of judgement.
tables: CVII. Ten Hells in Seven Palaces English

clayey.summary: 'The Clayey Ones'—the qliphothic order of Libra, harmony degraded to inert formlessness.
clayey.description: In the Translation of the Orders of Qliphoth 'The Clayey Ones' is the averse order attributed to Lamed and Libra. As the demonic shell of the path, it is the shadow of Libra's balance and justice: the poised equilibrium of the scales degraded into dead, inert clay—the heaviness that will not move, the formless mire that mimics balance only as the stillness of stagnation. It names the corruption of living harmony into lifeless mud.
tables: CXXIII. Translation of the Orders of the Qliphoth

clear-intelligence.summary: The Ninth Path, named again — the Clear Intelligence of Yesod, the limpid foundation of the images.
clear-intelligence.description: 'Clear' is a rendering of the Ninth Path's name (Sekhel Tahor, 'pure' or 'clean'), the Intelligence of Yesod, the lunar Foundation. The emphasis on clarity captures Yesod's office as the purified mirror in which the higher emanations are gathered, tested, and shown without distortion. It is the clear water of the astral foundation, the treasure-house of images kept limpid and true so that the light descending from above may pass uncorrupted into the kingdom of Malkuth.
tables: XIII. Paths of the Sefer Yetzirah

clinging-to-rules.summary: The third fetter — attachment to rites and observances (sīlabbata-parāmāsa).
clinging-to-rules.description: Clinging to Rules is sīlabbata-parāmāsa, the third of the ten fetters, attributed to Chesed. It is the misplaced belief that mere rites, rules and external observances can of themselves purify or liberate — the substitution of ritual scrupulosity for genuine insight and transformation. Severed at stream-entry, its overcoming frees the practitioner from superstition and from the bondage of the letter. Its placement at Chesed, the sphere of ordering mercy and law, fittingly marks the point where reverence for form can harden into attachment to form.

clouds.summary: Shechaqim, a heaven of Assiah at Netzach — the heaven of 'Clouds' where manna is ground.
clouds.description: Shechaqim (the 'clouds' or 'fine dusts') is one of the seven heavens of the Talmud, attributed to Netzach. It is the heaven in which stand the millstones that grind the manna for the righteous who are to come — the cloud-heaven of mysterious provision, the upper mill whose flour is the bread of the world to come.
tables: XCIV. The Heavens of Assiah English

clover.summary: The lucky leaf of Venus—clover, the trefoil of love and the four-leaf charm of fortune.
clover.description: The Clover is attributed to Venus (Daleth, the Empress). Sweet fodder and honey-flower, its trefoil leaf has long carried a charge of luck and benediction, and the rare four-leaf clover is among the most enduring charms of good fortune in love and life. Soft, fragrant, and abundant in the green meadow, it is a humble Venusian plant of sweetness and grace. Esoterically the clover is the small, lucky blessing of Venus underfoot—love and fortune offered freely in the common field.

cocaine.summary: The alkaloid of the coca leaf, set at Chokmah, Jupiter, and Geburah — force, expansion, and fierce energy.
cocaine.description: Cocaine, the powerful alkaloid extracted from the leaves of the coca shrub, is given a triple attribution among the Vegetable Drugs: to Chokmah, the dynamic Will and primal outflowing Force; to Kaph, the expansive, euphoric path of Jupiter; and to Geburah, the sphere of Mars, of fierce energy and burning power. The placement reads the drug's action with precision — the sudden surge of dynamic force (Chokmah), the inflated euphoria and grandiosity (Jupiter), the hard, martial overdrive of stimulation (Geburah). It has a brief medical history as a local anaesthetic and a long, ruinous social one. Esoterically it figures unsupported force — the lightning-flash of Chokmah's energy seized without the stabilising vessel of Binah, exhilaration that arcs straight into depletion and collapse.
cocaine.caution: DANGEROUS — historical/symbolic entry only, not advice for use. Cocaine is a highly addictive stimulant; it is cardiotoxic and overdose causes fatal heart failure, stroke, and seizure.

cocoanut.summary: The water-bearing fruit of Aquarius—the coconut, sealed vessel of sweet water carried across the sea.
cocoanut.description: The Coconut is attributed to Aquarius (Tzaddi, the Star). A sealed vessel of pure water and white flesh that floats across oceans to seed new shores, it is a fitting plant for the Water-Bearer—the fruit that carries living water within a hard shell and gives it freely. Esoterically the coconut answers the Star's emblem of the poured-out waters: nourishment and refreshment sealed within and offered to the thirsty, life borne intact across the formless sea.

coffee.summary: The caffeine stimulant, attributed to Tiphareth; the solar quickener of wakefulness.
coffee.description:
Coffee is set at Tiphareth, the sphere of the Sun, as a gentle solar stimulant — the quickener of wakefulness, clarity, and conscious focus that draws the mind up into daylight alertness. Its history is bound to the Sufi orders, who used it to sustain night-long devotions, and to the coffee-houses that became crucibles of Enlightenment thought. Esoterically it is the mild, civilising solar fire, the daily small invocation of vigilance.

Caution: caffeine is a real drug — habituating, and in large amounts capable of anxiety and cardiac effects.
coffee.caution: Caffeine is habit-forming; excess causes anxiety and cardiac effects.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

cold.summary: Cold, the passive contracting quality, root of Water and Earth.
cold.description: In the doctrine of the four primary qualities, Cold is one of the two passive principles—the contracting, condensing force that draws things together and downward. Combined with the active qualities it forms two of the four elements: Cold and Moist make Water, Cold and Dry make Earth. Attributed here to the watery and earthy paths, cold is the principle of fixity, density, and rest, the quality that gathers and settles what heat would disperse.
tables: XI. The Elements and their Planetary Rulers

collecting-intelligence.summary: The Thirtieth Path — the Collecting Intelligence of Resh, from which the astrologers read the stars.
collecting-intelligence.description: The Thirtieth Path is the Collecting or Collective Intelligence (Sekhel Kelali, the 'general' Intelligence), attributed to the letter Resh and the Sun, the path of The Sun joining Hod to Yesod. The Sepher Yetzirah says that from it astrologers, by the judgement of the stars and the celestial signs, derive and perfect their science according to the motions of the heavens. The solar path gathers and collects the scattered lights into a single luminous order — the comprehensive, synthesising radiance from which all the patterns of the sky may be read.
tables: XIII. Paths of the Sefer Yetzirah

colopatiron.summary: Liberation — the Nuctemeron genius of the ninth hour presiding over liberation, set by Crowley at Sagittarius.
colopatiron.description: Colopatiron is the Nuctemeron genius of liberation. That “Night-illumined Day”, ascribed to Apollonius of Tyana and handed down through Lévi's Transcendental Magic, sets a company of spirits over each of the twelve hours of the magical day, and Colopatiron belongs to the ninth hour. He opens prisons and looses bonds, the spirit of deliverance and release. In 777 (Table CLXXIII) Crowley redistributes these hour-genii across the zodiac, where this spirit falls at Sagittarius (Samekh).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

colophonum.summary: The dark pine-rosin of Capricorn—colophony, the burnt resin's earthy, smoky tang upon the goat's path.
colophonum.description: Colophonum (colophony, rosin) is attributed to Capricorn (Ayin, the Devil). The dark residue left when pine resin is distilled—the rosin of the violinist's bow and the pitch of old craft—it burns with a heavy, smoky, resinous tang, an earthy and slightly acrid incense fitting the saturnine goat-sign. Esoterically colophony is the dark resinous perfume of Capricorn, the smoke of the pitch-pine that clings to the material and the earthen, the heavy ground-note of the Devil's domain.
