column-left-blank-due-to-transcriber-s-c.term: Column left blank due to transcriber's complete ignorance of Arabic. May be restored at some point
column-left-blank-due-to-transcriber-s-c.displayTerm: Column left blank due to transcriber's complete ignorance of Arabic. May be restored at some point
tables: XLVII. Kings and Princes of the Jinn

compassion.summary: The Brahmavihāra of compassion (karuṇā) — the heart that trembles at the suffering of others.
compassion.description: Compassion is karuṇā, the second of the four Brahmavihāras of the Forty Meditations, attributed to Binah, the supernal Mother and sphere of sorrow understood. It is the cultivated wish that all beings be free from suffering — the heart's response that quivers in the presence of pain and moves toward its relief. As a divine abiding it is the antidote to cruelty and indifference; set at Binah, the great sea of understanding and grief, it is the dark, maternal tenderness that takes the suffering of the world into itself.

completion.summary: Four of Wands — Completion / Perfected Work; Venus in Aries, Chesed of Fire.
completion.description: The Four of Wands, called Perfected Work by the Golden Dawn and Completion by Crowley, is Chesed in the suit of Fire and the third decan of Aries, softened by Venus. The fire of will, having been asserted and established, now settles into stable order — a foursquare wheel of flame, the work brought to a harmonious resting-point. Venus lends grace and pleasure to Mars's domain, so that energy becomes festival and the labour is, for a moment, perfected.
tables: CXXXIII. Titles and Attributions of the Wand Suit

concealers.summary: Satariel — the averse Binah; hiders of the light, dwellers in the false veil.
concealers.description: The Concealers (Satariel) are the Qliphoth of Binah, the Great Mother and sphere of Understanding. Where Binah is the holy darkness that gives form, her averse shell is a darkness that hides and obscures — a false veil cast over the truth, withholding understanding rather than bestowing it. They are the concealment that imprisons rather than the silence that comprehends.
tables: CXXIII. Translation of the Orders of the Qliphoth
CL. Magical Images of the Decans (Succedent)

conduct.summary: The recollection of virtue (sīla) — the contemplation of one's own moral discipline.
conduct.description: Conduct renders sīla, the recollection of one's own virtue among the Forty Meditations, attributed to the path of Pisces. The practitioner reflects on the purity and unbrokenness of his moral discipline — the precepts kept whole — and from that reflection arises gladness, freedom from remorse, and a steadiness that supports deeper meditation. Virtue is the foundation of the whole Buddhist path, the ground on which concentration and wisdom are raised; as a meditation-subject it makes that ground itself the object of grateful and clarifying attention.

conjunctio.summary: Geomantic figure 'Conjunction' — attributed to Mercury; meeting, union, combination.
conjunctio.description: Conjunctio, 'conjunction' or 'union,' is one of the sixteen geomantic figures, attributed to Mercury and associated with Virgo. It signifies meeting, combination, and the coming-together of persons or matters — a figure of connection whose nature takes much of its quality from the figures it joins. It is favourable for partnerships, recovery of lost things, and the bringing-together of separated forces.
tables: XLIX. Lineal Figures of the Planets, &c., and Geomany

consciousness.summary: The second formless attainment — the sphere of infinite consciousness (viññāṇañcāyatana); also the fifth skandha.
consciousness.description: Consciousness names the second formless attainment (viññāṇañcāyatana), in which the meditator turns from the infinitude of space to the infinitude of the awareness that knew it — 'consciousness is infinite' — and dwells there, set in 777 at the threshold of Spirit and the Veils. The same word marks the fifth of the five skandhas, viññāṇa, the bare knowing or discernment that arises with each sense-contact and which, with form, feeling, perception and the formations, composes the apparent self. In both senses it points to awareness as process rather than possession: vast when made the object of the formless jhāna, conditioned and impermanent when seen as an aggregate.

constituting-intelligence.summary: The Fifteenth Path — the Constituting Intelligence of Heh, framing creation out of the dark.
constituting-intelligence.description: The Fifteenth Path is the Constituting Intelligence (Sekhel ha-Maamid, the 'Establishing' Intelligence), attributed to the letter Heh and the sign Aries, the path of The Emperor (or, in Crowley's revised attribution, The Star) joining Chokmah to Tiphareth. The Sepher Yetzirah says it constitutes the substance of creation in pure darkness, and that, as the mystics teach, this is the darkness spoken of in Scripture — 'thick darkness which is a swaddling band of it.' It is the establishing power that gives constituted form and standing to what is brought forth.
tables: XIII. Paths of the Sefer Yetzirah

contentment.summary: The lunar virtue of contentment, the serene acceptance of the reflected world.
contentment.description: Contentment is named here as a virtue at Gimel and the Moon, the path of the High Priestess. As the moon reflects without grasping, the virtue of contentment is the soul's serene acceptance of what is—freedom from the restless craving that drives the unquiet mind from one image to the next. It is the lunar peace of the one who has learned to rest in the present condition, neither clutching nor refusing, mirroring the light that falls upon it without disturbance.
tables: L. Transcendental Morality (10 Virtues; 7 Deadly Sins; 4 Magic Powers)

copper.summary: The Venusian metal of Netzach — love, art, and the green of living nature.
copper.description: Copper is the metal of Venus and of Netzach, the sphere of love and nature — warm, ruddy, and endlessly workable, the metal of the mirror of Aphrodite (its alchemical sign is her glass). When it weathers it blooms into verdigris, the living green that is Venus's own colour, binding the metal to the vegetable world it rules. Esoterically copper is the conductive, harmonising principle, the metal of artistry, beauty, and the attractive force that joins.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

cor-leonis.summary: Regulus, the Lion's Heart — a Royal Star marking the Leonine lunar mansion.
cor-leonis.description: Cor Leonis ('the Heart of the Lion') is Regulus, the brightest star of Leo and one of the four Royal Stars of antiquity, the watcher of the north, set in the path of Leo (Teth). Its name, 'the little king,' captures its agelong attribution: kingship, ambition, magnanimity, and the dangers of pride and downfall that shadow great power. As the very heart of the celestial Lion it is the most solar of the fixed stars.
tables: CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon

cor-scorpionis.summary: Antares, the Scorpion's Heart — a Royal Star marking the mansion al-Qalb.
cor-scorpionis.description: Cor Scorpionis is Antares, the red supergiant at the heart of Scorpio, whose very name ('rival of Mars') marks its blood-red, martial fire; it is one of the four Royal Stars, watcher of the west, set in the path of Scorpio (Nun). As the heart of the celestial Scorpion it concentrates the sign's themes of passion, danger, and transformation through death — the burning core of the autumnal mysteries.
tables: CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon

corn.summary: The grain of the harvest, attributed to Malkuth; sacrament of the earthly kingdom.
corn.description: Corn — grain, the staff of life — is placed at Malkuth, the Kingdom, the material world made fruitful. More sacrament than drug, it is the body of the slain-and-risen vegetation gods (Osiris, Demeter's daughter, John Barleycorn), the seed that must die in the earth to rise as bread. Its attribution to the tenth Sephirah is the very emblem of the divine life indwelling in matter and feeding the world: the mystery of the harvest, in which the Kingdom nourishes its inhabitants from its own substance.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

corporeal-intelligence.summary: The Twenty-ninth Path — the Corporeal Intelligence of Qoph, former of every body in every world.
corporeal-intelligence.description: The Twenty-ninth Path is the Corporeal Intelligence (Sekhel ha-Mugsham), attributed to the letter Qoph and the sign Pisces, the path of The Moon joining Netzach to Malkuth. The Sepher Yetzirah says it forms every body that is formed in all the worlds, and the reproduction of them. It is the body-making power, working through the dim, watery, dreaming light of the Moon's path — the deep biological darkness in which flesh is shaped, gestated, and brought to birth, the most material of the paths.
tables: XIII. Paths of the Sefer Yetzirah

corporeality.summary: The first skandha — form or materiality (rūpa), the bodily aggregate.
corporeality.description: Corporeality is rūpa, the first of the five skandhas or 'aggregates' that the Buddha analysed as the whole of what is mistaken for a self, attributed in 777 to the element Earth. It is materiality — the body and the physical world apprehended through the senses, built of the four great elements and their derivatives. As the grossest and most tangible of the aggregates it stands at the earthy foundation; seen rightly it is impermanent, dependent and impersonal, a flux of form arising and passing rather than a possession of any abiding 'I'.

corpse-candles.summary: The death-omen lights of Welsh lore, set at Saturn — pale flames that foretell a coming death.
corpse-candles.description: Among the Legendary Orders of Being, the Corpse Candles (Welsh canwyll corff) are attributed to Saturn. In the folklore of Wales they are spectral flames seen travelling the route a funeral will take, their size and colour foretelling who is to die — a small pale flame for a child, a larger ruddy one for an adult. Kin to the will-o'-the-wisp but specifically an omen of mortality, they belong to the Saturnian order of death-portents, the cold lights that announce the approach of the grave.

costum.summary: The warm earthy root of Taurus—costus, musky and resinous, an ancient incense-root of the patient bull.
costum.description: Costum (costus) is attributed to Taurus (Vav, the Hierophant). The aromatic root of the Himalayan Saussurea, warm, musky, and faintly animal, it was a prized incense and fixative of the ancient world, deep and earthy in character—fitting the fixed earthy sign of Taurus. Esoterically costus is the grounded, sensuous perfume of the Hierophant's sign, a root-scent that draws the fragrance downward into the warm earth, steadfast and enduring.

cowl.summary: Design detail of the Hermit (Yod): the cowl.
cowl.description: ‘Cowl’ is a fragment of Liber 777's design for Atu IX, the Hermit (path of Yod, Virgo): ‘Wrapped in a cloak and cowl…’ The cowl—the monastic hood drawn over the head—marks the Hermit as the solitary contemplative, withdrawn into the interior darkness where the lamp of wisdom shines. It is the emblem of renunciation and concealment, the covering that shuts out the world so that the seed-light of Yod may be tended in secret.
tables: CLXXXI. Correct Design of Tarot Trumps

crab.summary: The armoured creature of Cancer—the hard shell and soft heart, the sidelong-moving guardian of the Chariot.
crab.description: The crab is the proper beast of Cancer, the path of the Chariot (Cheth), and it embodies that sign's essence: a soft, vulnerable body protected by a hard shell, advancing sidelong, ready to retreat into its armour at the first threat. It is the figure of the Chariot's tortoise-like defence, the self that carries its protection with it and guards a tender interior behind a wall of horn. Bound to the tides and the moon-ruled waters, the crab belongs to the lunar, maternal, sheltering nature of Cancer. Esoterically it teaches the wisdom of the protective shell—the discipline of guarding the sensitive soul while it makes its slow, oblique advance toward the goal.

crablouse.summary: The clinging parasite of Scorpio—the basest face of the sign's sexual force, appetite that feeds on another.
crablouse.description: The crablouse is placed at Scorpio, the sign of sex, death and the deep instincts, and it represents the lowest and grossest reach of that sign's power: the parasite that fastens itself in the most intimate places and lives by feeding upon another. Where the eagle figures Scorpio raised to transcendence, the crablouse figures it sunk to its meanest expression—desire degraded into mere clinging appetite, the love-force become vermin. Esoterically it stands as a frank reminder that the same Scorpionic energy that can be exalted into spiritual transmutation can also be debased into parasitism, and that the difference lies wholly in how the force is governed.

crayfish.summary: The deep-crawler of Scorpio—the archaic creature rising from the dark water-bed of the unconscious.
crayfish.description: The crayfish is attributed to Scorpio, and like its kin the lobster it is an armoured crawler of the dark water-floor, an ancient and primitive form that lives in the silt where light scarcely reaches. It is the creature that creeps up from the deepest, oldest layers of the psyche—the half-formed thing that emerges from the unconscious waters, as in the imagery of the Moon, where such a creature crawls from the pool toward the land. Under Scorpio it belongs to the realm of death, regeneration and the buried instincts. Esoterically the crayfish figures the primordial contents that rise from the deep when the soul descends into its own waters, the archaic life stirring at the bottom of the self.

creative-world.summary: The Creative World — Briah, the world of the archangels.
creative-world.description: The Creative World is Briah, the second of the four worlds — the realm of creation, where the pure emanations of Atziluth first take on distinction as the great archangels and the throne of the divine. It is the world of the Mother (the first Heh of the Name) and, in 777's correspondences, of the element Water: the creative outpouring in which the archetypes are first given created life.

crocell.summary: The forty-ninth spirit of the Goetia, an angelic duke of Leo who teaches geometry and warms the waters.
crocell.description: Crocell (Procel) is the forty-ninth spirit of the Goetia, a great duke of the decans of Leo. He speaks of hidden and secret things, teaches geometry and the liberal sciences, makes great rushing noises like the sound of mighty waters where there are none, and warms waters and discovers baths. He appears in the form of an angel. A spirit of the fiery sign, he is the teacher of geometry and the master of the sounding and heated waters.

crocodile.summary: Sobek's beast at Saturn and the World—the primal devourer of the waters, the threshold-monster of time.
crocodile.description: The crocodile is attributed to Saturn and the path of Tav, the Universe, and it is the great primal monster of the waters—Sobek the Egyptian crocodile-god, lord of the Nile's fertile menace, and the devouring jaw that waits at the threshold. In the imagery of the Universe card a crocodile lurks beneath the dancing figure, the type of the formless power and the all-consuming nature out of which manifestation rises and into which it returns. Under Saturn, the lord of time and ending, the crocodile is the devourer that swallows all things in the end. Esoterically it figures the immense, ancient, indifferent power at the base of the world, the jaws of time and matter that the soul must pass to complete the great circle.

crook.summary: The shepherd's crook of Chesed—Osiris's emblem of merciful rule, the guidance that gathers and protects.
crook.description: The Crook is attributed to Chesed, the merciful sphere of Jupiter and benevolent kingship, and it is the shepherd's staff—the heka borne by Osiris and by every just ruler, the curved rod with which the shepherd draws back the straying and guides the flock to safety. Where the Scourge (its frequent partner) drives and corrects, the Crook gathers and protects; together they are the two emblems of true governance, mercy and severity in balance. Its place at Chesed marks it as the instrument of loving, ordering rule. Esoterically the Crook is the merciful authority of the magician—the power not to compel by force but to guide, gather and shelter the forces under his charge, the benevolent rulership of Chesed made into a tool of leading and care.

cross-of-suffering.summary: The redemptive suspension of Water—the Hanged Man's cross, salvation won through willing sacrifice.
cross-of-suffering.description: The Cross of Suffering is attributed to the watery letter Mem and the path of the Hanged Man, and it is the emblem of redemption through sacrifice: the cross or gibbet upon which the figure hangs reversed, suspended in the element of water, surrendering the lower life so that the higher may be born. It is the willing acceptance of pain and reversal—the death of the old orientation, the world seen upside-down—as the price and the means of spiritual rebirth. Its place at Mem, the still deep waters, marks it as the silent, drowning sacrifice. Esoterically the Cross of Suffering is the discipline of redemptive surrender—the magician's willing immersion in the waters of sacrifice, the inversion of the ordinary self that opens the way to a higher life through the acceptance of suffering.

crow.summary: The magical image of Raum — a crow — Goetic Earl of the first decan of Taurus (by night).
crow.description: Raum (Raim), the fortieth spirit of the Goetia and a great Earl, appears at first in the form of a crow, taking human shape at the conjuror's command. In 777 he is the nocturnal ruler of the first decan of Taurus. He steals treasures out of kings' houses, destroys cities and the dignities of men, tells things past, present and to come, and procures love between friends and foes. The dark, thieving crow set against the possessive, treasure-loving Bull aptly figures wealth seized and squandered, esteem built and cast down.

crow-with-sore-throat.summary: The magical image of Malphas — a crow with a hoarse voice — Goetic President of the third decan of Aries (by night).
crow-with-sore-throat.description: Malphas, the thirty-ninth spirit of the Goetia and a mighty President, appears first as a crow speaking with a hoarse, harsh voice, and at command puts on human shape. In 777 he is the nocturnal ruler of the third decan of Aries. He builds houses, towers and strongholds, throws down the buildings of the enemy, gives good familiars, and receives sacrifices kindly — but will deceive the operator who trusts him too far. The hoarse black crow set in cardinal fire marks the builder and breaker of the Ram's final face — sudden raising up and casting down.

crowd-of-gods.summary: Crowd of Gods — the averse plurality opposing the divine unity, at the Veils of the Negative.
crowd-of-gods.description: Among the translated names of the Qliphothic orders, 'Crowd of Gods' is set at the Veils of the Negative — the averse shadow of the unmanifest. Where the divine Veils conceal the pure unity that precedes Kether, their qliphothic reflection is a swarming multiplicity of false gods, the chaotic plurality that apes the One. It figures the first and subtlest distortion: unity scattered into a clamouring throng of idols.
tables: CXXIII. Translation of the Orders of the Qliphoth

crown.summary: The Crown—first Sephirah; pure undifferentiated unity, the root of all.
crown.description:
Kether (כתר, ‘Crown’) is the first Sephirah and the apex of the Tree of Life, the point at which the Limitless Light of the Veils first becomes a thing that can be named. It is pure being without division—unity before the One has any second to be one against. Its God-name is Eheieh, ‘I AM,’ and its associated grade is Ipsissimus (10°=1□), the consummation of the adept’s path. In the soul Kether is Yechidah, the indivisible spark of the divine self.

Because nothing precedes it within manifestation, Kether is described only by negation and by image: the Ancient of Days seen in profile, the single point, the white brilliance that contains all colour. Crowley placed here the highest mystical attainment, where subject and object collapse into a single undifferentiated awareness—the goal toward which every lower correspondence is a stepping-stone.
tables: III. Translation of the Names of the Paths
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

crown-which-is-in-yesod.summary: The completion of the foundation — Malkuth, the Kingdom crowning the work below.
crown-which-is-in-yesod.description: The 'crown which is in Yesod' is attributed to Malkuth, the tenth Sephirah, the Kingdom. The phrase marks how the highest principle is mirrored in the lowest: 'Malkuth is in Kether, and Kether is in Malkuth.' As the crown of the foundation — the consummation of the generative descent — Malkuth is the place where all the powers of the Tree come to their final realisation in the manifest world, the Kingdom that completes and reflects the Crown above.
tables: CIII. The Ten Divisions of the Body of God

crowned.summary: A recurring attribute in the magical images: crowned, the token of sovereignty.
crowned.description: ‘Crowned’ recurs across several of Liber 777's magical images, marking a figure as sovereign or exalted—seen, for example, in the throned and crowned woman of Malkuth and among the lordly figures of the Sephiroth and the decans. The crown is the universal emblem of rule, attainment, and the dignity of the higher self; wherever it appears it signals that the figure so adorned holds authority within its sphere. As an image-attribute it carries a high illustrative value for the cells in which it occurs.
tables: CXX. Magical Images of the Sephiroth

crowned-king-on-dromedary.summary: The magical image of Paimon — a crowned king upon a dromedary, amid musicians — Goetic King of the third decan of Gemini.
crowned-king-on-dromedary.description: Paimon, the ninth spirit of the Goetia and one of its greatest Kings, most obedient to Lucifer, appears as a man with a glorious crown seated upon a dromedary, with a great host of trumpeters, cymbalists and musicians sounding before him. In 777 he is set at the third decan of Gemini by day. He teaches all arts, sciences and secret things, gives dignities and good familiars, and binds men to the operator's will. The crowned king borne upon the desert-camel amid music images the sovereign mastery of knowledge proper to the airy, eloquent sign of the Twins. (For his fuller office see the entry on Paimon among the Demon Kings.)

crowned-with-stars.summary: Design detail of the Empress (Daleth): crowned with stars.
crowned-with-stars.description: ‘Crowned with stars’ opens Liber 777's design for Atu III, the Empress (path of Daleth, Venus): ‘Crowned with stars, a winged goddess stands upon the moon.’ The starry crown marks her as the celestial mother, Venus exalted to the heavens—the Woman clothed with the sun and crowned with twelve stars of the Apocalypse. The diadem of stars proclaims her dominion over the generative powers of nature, the love and beauty by which the cosmos is adorned and perpetuated.
tables: CLXXXI. Correct Design of Tarot Trumps

crucified-man.summary: The magical image of the Hanged Man (Atu XII)—the figure suspended in the waters, redemption through willing sacrifice.
crucified-man.description: This image—a man bound and suspended, hanging as if crucified—is the magical figure of the twelfth trump, the Hanged Man, attributed to the watery letter Mem. He hangs head-downward, his world reversed, surrendering his ordinary life and orientation in willing sacrifice; immersed in the element of water, he is the drowned and dying god whose self-offering redeems. The reversal is the point: by hanging inverted he sees and lives from the opposite of the natural self, dying to the lower that the higher may live. Esoterically the crucified, suspended man figures redemption through willing sacrifice and the inversion of the self—the surrender of the ordinary life and viewpoint, the drowning of the lower nature in the waters of Mem, by which the soul is turned about and reborn through the acceptance of its own sacrifice.
tables: CLXXXI. Correct Design of Tarot Trumps

cruel-ancient.summary: The magical image of Furcas — a cruel old man with long white hair on a pale horse — Goetic Knight of the second decan of Leo (by night).
cruel-ancient.description: Furcas, the fiftieth spirit of the Goetia and a Knight (the only spirit of that rank among the seventy-two), appears as a cruel old man with a long white beard and hoary hair, riding upon a pale horse and bearing a sharp weapon in his hand. In 777 he is the nocturnal ruler of the second decan of Leo. He teaches philosophy, astronomy, rhetoric, logic, chiromancy and pyromancy. The pitiless white-haired elder, armed and mounted, marks the Lion's pride matured into stern mastery — knowledge wielded like a blade.

cruelty.summary: Nine of Swords — Cruelty; Mars in Gemini, Yesod of Air: the nightmare of the mind.
cruelty.description: The Nine of Swords, Cruelty (Despair and Cruelty), is Yesod in the suit of Air and the second decan of Gemini under Mars. The nines bring the full force of the suit, and Mars ruling the foundation of the intellect breeds mental anguish: nine ragged, dripping swords, the mind devouring itself in suffering. It is the dark night of the soul, cruelty turned inward, despair, guilt, and the torments of a poisoned conscience.
tables: CXXXV. Titles and Attributions of the Sword Suit.
L. Transcendental Morality (10 Virtues; 7 Deadly Sins; 4 Magic Powers)

crysolith.summary: The golden-green 'gold-stone' of Sol — solar light caught in green fire.
crysolith.description: Crysolith (chrysolite, 'gold-stone') is set on the path of Resh and Sol — a golden-green gem (historically applied to peridot and topaz alike) whose very name proclaims the gold of the Sun. Its luminous yellow-green suits the solar path of The Sun (Resh), the regenerated light of consciousness; anciently it was held to drive away the terrors of the night and the powers of darkness. The stone of solar radiance and dispelled shadow.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

crystal.summary: The clear crystal of the lunar path — the scrying-glass of vision.
crystal.description: Crystal (clear quartz) appears on the lunar path of Gimel — the transparent stone of the scryer and the visionary, the medium in which the images of the astral light take form. Its attribution to the Moon's high path, the road of the High Priestess, marks it as the very glass of inner sight: the clear lens through which the unseen is beheld.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

crystal-gazing.summary: The watery art of scrying visions in a speculum of crystal, mirror, or dark water.
crystal-gazing.description: Crystal-gazing, attributed to Mem and Water, is the practice of fixing the sight upon a reflective speculum—crystal sphere, black mirror, bowl of ink or water—until the still surface opens into moving vision. Water, the element of reflection, memory, and the receptive astral, is its proper medium; the smooth depth becomes a doorway through which the trained seer reads images rising from the unconscious or impressed by intelligences contacted. It is among the gentlest and most widely practised of the scrying arts.

cubel-pepper.summary: The tailed pepper of Capricorn—cubeb, warm and peppery-sweet, a spice of the goat-sign's earthy fire.
cubel-pepper.description: Cubel Pepper (cubeb) is attributed to Capricorn (Ayin, the Devil). A "tailed pepper" with a warm, pungent, slightly camphorous and sweet savour, long valued in physic and old magic for vigour and protection, it carries the spicy, earthy heat fitting the saturnine goat-sign. Esoterically cubeb is the warm peppery perfume of Capricorn—the kindling spice of the Devil's path, earthy heat marshalled toward strength and ward.

cuniali.summary: Association — the Nuctemeron genius of the eighth hour presiding over association, set by Crowley at Scorpio.
cuniali.description: Cuniali is the Nuctemeron genius of association. That “Night-illumined Day”, ascribed to Apollonius of Tyana and handed down through Lévi's Transcendental Magic, sets a company of spirits over each of the twelve hours of the magical day, and Cuniali belongs to the eighth hour. He presides over fellowship and partnership, the binding of company and alliance. In 777 (Table CLXXIII) Crowley redistributes these hour-genii across the zodiac, where this spirit falls at Scorpio (Nun).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

cybele.summary: Cybele, the Great Mother of Anatolia — the throned goddess of mountains and beasts, at Binah.
cybele.description: Cybele is the Phrygian Great Mother, goddess of the wild mountains, fertility, and the whole of nature, served by ecstatic, drum-beating priests and drawn by lions. Referred to Binah, the supernal Mother, she is the archetypal magna mater, the source and womb of life, lover of the dying Attis. Her orgiastic mysteries spread throughout the Greek and Roman world; she is the primal maternal power of the earth itself.

cyclops.summary: The Cyclopes, one-eyed smiths of heaven — forgers of Zeus's thunderbolts, at Gemini.
cyclops.description: The Cyclopes are the one-eyed giants of Greek myth, the master smiths who forged the thunderbolts of Zeus, the trident of Poseidon, and the helm of Hades. Referred to Zayin and Gemini, they are the craftsmen of divine power, primordial workers in fire and metal. As the makers of the gods' weapons they embody the elemental, subterranean skill that arms the heavens.
tables: CLXIX. Egyptian Gods of the Zodiac (Succedent)

cynocephalus.summary: The Cynocephalus, the dog-headed ape — sacred companion of Thoth, at Mercury.
cynocephalus.description: The Cynocephalus, the dog-headed baboon, is the sacred animal of Thoth and an emblem of Mercury, fittingly placed at Beth, the path of the Magus. The baboon was seen greeting the rising sun with cries and uplifted paws, and so became a symbol of wisdom, writing, and the worship of light. As Thoth's companion it represents the keen, chattering intelligence of the Mercurial sphere, the animal soul of language and learning.

cypress.summary: The mourning tree of Saturn and Binah—the dark cypress, perfume of death, eternity, and the grieving Mother.
cypress.description: The Cypress is attributed to Saturn, to Binah, and to Gemini. The classic tree of mourning and of the dead, planted in graveyards from antiquity and sacred to Hades and to Saturn, its dark spire and resinous scent belong to the saturnine mysteries of death, time, and the sorrowing Mother Binah. Esoterically the cypress is the perfume of grief and eternity—the evergreen of the tomb whose shadow falls across the threshold, the scent of the great Sea of Binah into which all forms at last return.

cystitis.summary: Cystitis at Tzaddi and Aquarius — inflammation in the body's channels of elimination.
cystitis.description: Cystitis, inflammation of the bladder, is set on the path of Aquarius. The fixed-air sign of the Water-Bearer is concerned in the body with the circulation and the carrying and voiding of fluids; cystitis is read as a disorder in this Aquarian work of channeling and release, the vessel of elimination inflamed. Symbolically it marks an obstruction or fever in the very system meant to pour out and cleanse.

dalda.summary: Dalda — a letter of the Coptic alphabet (d), which Crowley attributes to the path of Daleth (Venus).
dalda.description: Dalda is a letter of the Coptic alphabet — the script in which the Egyptian language was written in the Christian era, the Greek alphabet adapted to Egyptian speech. It is from Greek delta. Crowley folds the Coptic alphabet into the great correspondence of letters and paths in 777 (Table LI), assigning Dalda to the path of Daleth (Venus) on the Tree of Life, so that the Egyptian-Christian script takes its station among the Hebrew letters and the keys of the Tarot.
tables: LI. Names of the Coptic Letters

damiana.summary: The aphrodisiac herb, attributed to Netzach; Venusian plant of desire.
damiana.description: Damiana is placed at Netzach, the sphere of Venus, as one of the classic aphrodisiac and mood-lifting herbs — a mild relaxant and reputed stimulant of desire long used in the folk medicine of Central America. Its Venusian attribution is plain: it belongs to the green realm of feeling, attraction, and the gentle quickening of the senses that is Netzach's domain. Of the milder entries in this column, it carries no severe toxicity, though as with all herbs moderation and informed care apply.
damiana.caution: Generally mild, but a pharmacologically active herb; use informed care.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

damp-earth.summary: An earth of the sevenfold scheme at Yesod — moist ground above the lowest mire.
damp-earth.description: Among the Seven Earths of Qabalistic cosmology, the 'Damp Earth' is set at Yesod, the lunar Foundation just above the material Kingdom. As Yesod is the watery, formative reservoir through which the higher influences pass into matter, its corresponding land is moist and impressionable — the damp, fertile ground in which the seeds of manifestation are kept and quickened before they descend to the dense earth below.
tables: CV. Ten Earths in Seven Palaces English

dantalion.summary: The seventy-first spirit of the Goetia, a many-faced duke of Pisces who knows all thoughts and grants visions.
dantalion.description: Dantalion is the seventy-first spirit of the Goetia, a great and mighty duke of the decans of Pisces. He teaches all arts and sciences, declares the secret counsel of anyone — for he knows the thoughts of all and can change them at will — causes love, and shows the likeness of any person, wheresoever they be, together with visions of them. He appears as a man with many faces, of men and of women, holding a book in his hand. A spirit of the watery sign, he is the reader and shaper of thoughts and the giver of visions.

dar-al-jalai.summary: Dar al-Jalal — the Abode of Glory, highest of the Arab heavens, attributed to the supernals.
dar-al-jalai.description: Dar al-Jalal, the 'Abode of Glory' or of Majesty, is named among the seven heavens or gardens of the Islamic paradise — in some traditions fashioned of red pearl. Crowley sets it at the three supernal Sephiroth, the highest of the Tree: the most exalted of the celestial abodes answering to the crown of the heavens, the dwelling of the divine glory.
tables: CXXVII. Seven Heavens of the Arabs

dar-as-salaam.summary: Dar as-Salaam — the Abode of Peace, attributed to Chesed.
dar-as-salaam.description: Dar as-Salaam, the 'Abode of Peace,' is one of the seven gardens of the Islamic paradise, a name of the highest felicity, set in 777 at Chesed, the sphere of Jupiter, mercy, and beneficence. The serene and merciful dwelling of peace fits aptly the loving-kindness of the fourth Sephirah.
tables: CXXVII. Seven Heavens of the Arabs

dark.summary: A recurring quality in the decan images: dark of complexion or aspect.
dark.description: ‘Dark’ recurs as a descriptive quality in several of Liber 777's magical images of the decans—the ‘tall, dark, restless man’ of the first decan of Aries and the ‘dark man’ of the first decan of Libra among them. In the older talismanic tradition the complexion and colouring of a decan figure were significant attributes, helping to fix its character and the planetary nature ruling its ten degrees. Darkness here connotes depth, force, and the saturnine or martial cast given to certain of these emblems.
tables: CL. Magical Images of the Decans (Succedent)
CXLIX. Magical Images of the Decans (Ascendent)

dark-blue.summary: The blue kasiṇa — a disc of dark blue used as the meditation-support for entering absorption.
dark-blue.description: Dark Blue is the blue (nīla) colour-kasiṇa of the Forty Meditations, attributed in the 777 grid to the path of Venus. The practitioner steadies attention on a field of deep blue until its after-image arises within and the discursive mind grows still. Each of the colour-kasiṇas trains the same faculty — the gathering of a scattered mind to a single point — and the blue is traditionally associated with coolness and depth, the eye drawn down into a quiet that is the threshold of the jhānas.

darkness.summary: The Plague of Darkness — the three days' night, attributed to Binah.
darkness.description: The ninth plague, the thick darkness that lay upon Egypt for three days, is set in 777 at Binah, the supernal Mother, whose colour is black and whose nature is the dark, formative womb and the great sea of night. The palpable darkness 'that might be felt' belongs fittingly to the sphere of limitation, sorrow, and the concealing dark.
tables: CXXII. The Ten Plagues of Egypt

david.summary: David — at Malkuth; the king in whom the earthly Kingdom is established.
david.description: David is attributed to Malkuth, the Kingdom. The shepherd raised to be king, the psalmist and the founder of the royal line, he embodies the realised sovereignty of the tenth Sephirah — the divine rule brought fully down into the world. As the king whose throne the Messiah will inherit, he is the very figure of the Kingdom made manifest on earth.
tables: XCI. The Saints or Adepts of the Hebrews

death.summary: Atu XIII — Nun / Scorpio; transformation, the necessary end that frees new life.
death.description: Death is trump XIII, attributed to Nun and Scorpio, the path from Tiphareth to Netzach. It is the principle of transformation through dissolution—not annihilation but the necessary ending that clears the way for renewal. Crowley’s skeletal reaper dances with his scythe, sowing bubbles of new forms even as he cuts the old; the letter Nun means ‘fish’ yet also ‘to grow.’ Scorpio’s triple emblem (scorpion, serpent, eagle) marks the stages of this change. Death teaches that all transformation requires a real ending, and that decay and generation are a single process seen from two sides.
tables: XIV. General Attribution of the Tarot
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

death-of-the-first-born.summary: The Death of the First-born — the final plague, attributed to Kether.
death-of-the-first-born.description: The tenth and culminating plague, the slaying of the first-born of Egypt at midnight, is set in 777 at Kether, the Crown — the first and highest Sephirah, the 'first-born' of emanation. The attribution is darkly apt: the stroke that falls upon every first-born is referred to the sphere of the First itself, the summit from which the whole terrible sequence descended.
tables: CXXII. The Ten Plagues of Egypt

debauch.summary: Seven of Cups — Debauch / Illusionary Success; Venus in Scorpio, Netzach of Water.
debauch.description: The Seven of Cups, Debauch (Illusionary Success), is Netzach in the suit of Water and the third decan of Scorpio under Venus. The unstable seventh sphere lets the waters putrefy: greenish, poisoned cups, the lotus rotting at the root. It is pleasure indulged past wholesomeness, the seductive corruption of feeling — drugged delight, fantasy mistaken for fulfilment, the lie that gratification can be limitless.
tables: CXXXIV. Titles and Attributions of the Chalice Suit

decarabia.summary: The sixty-ninth spirit of the Goetia, a star-formed marquis of Aquarius who knows the virtues of birds and stones.
decarabia.description: Decarabia (Carabia) is the sixty-ninth spirit of the Goetia, a great marquis of the decans of Aquarius. He knows the virtues of all birds and precious stones, and can make the likeness of all manner of birds to fly before the operator, to drink and sing as natural birds do. He appears first as a star within a pentacle, then, at command, takes human form. A spirit of the airy sign, he is the master of the secret virtues of birds and gems.

deceivers.summary: Samael — the averse Hod; liars who pervert the intellect into falsehood.
deceivers.description: The Deceivers (Samael, the 'Poison of God' or 'the Liar') are the Qliphoth of Hod, the Mercurial sphere of intellect. Against the splendour of true reason and communication they set falsehood, sophistry, and deceit — the mind's brilliance turned to lies. They are the shells of a glory become glamour, intelligence enslaved to deception.
tables: CXXIII. Translation of the Orders of the Qliphoth

defeat.summary: Five of Swords — Defeat; Venus in Aquarius, Geburah of Air: the broken intellect.
defeat.description: The Five of Swords, Defeat, is Geburah in the suit of Air and the first decan of Aquarius under Venus. The fives sunder their suit, and even gentle Venus cannot soften the severity of Geburah ruling Air: the swords are bent, broken, and crossed in disorder. It is the collapse of the mind's defences, treachery and loss in conflict, the bitter taste of failure and humiliation.
tables: CXXXV. Titles and Attributions of the Sword Suit.

dementia.summary: Dementia at Binah and Saturn — the slow Saturnine decay of understanding.
dementia.description: Dementia is placed at Binah, the sphere of Saturn and of Understanding itself. As Saturn governs age, decay, and the cold contraction of the faculties, the progressive failing of the mind is its sorrowful work upon the seat of comprehension — the great Mother's vessel of Understanding gradually darkening. Esoterically it is the eclipse of Binah in the individual, reason and memory withdrawing into the Saturnine dark.

demeter.summary: Demeter, goddess of the grain and harvest — the grieving mother of the seasons, at Binah.
demeter.description: Demeter is the Greek goddess of grain, agriculture, and the fruitful earth, whose grief at the loss of her daughter Persephone to the underworld brings winter, and whose joy at her return brings spring. Referred to Binah, the Mother, and to the place of Earth, she is the nourishing maternal power that feeds humankind. Her mysteries at Eleusis, promising blessed life beyond death, were the most revered of the ancient world.

depth.summary: One of the six directions of space in the Sefer Yetzirah — the dimension of below.
depth.description: Depth is one of the six directions, or 'depths,' of space described in the Sefer Yetzirah, the foundational text of Qabalistic cosmology. There the universe is extended in six dimensions — height and depth, east and west, north and south — each 'sealed' by a permutation of the divine Name, with the Holy Temple at the centre. Depth marks the downward extension of the created order, the dimension that reaches from the central point toward the below.
tables: CX. Elements and Quarters per the Sepher Yetzirah

desire-for-bodily-immortality.summary: The sixth fetter — craving for fine-material existence (rūpa-rāga).
desire-for-bodily-immortality.description: Desire for Bodily Immortality renders rūpa-rāga, the sixth of the ten fetters, attributed to Binah. It is the subtle craving for existence in the fine-material realms — the refined, form-based states attained in the jhānas, longed for as a kind of exalted and enduring embodiment. One of the five 'higher fetters' that bind even the advanced practitioner, it is severed only on the threshold of arahatship. Set at Binah, the supernal Mother and ground of form, it figures the most rarefied attachment to having a body at all, the wish to abide in shape and substance however sublimated.

desire-for-immaterial-immortality.summary: The seventh fetter — craving for formless existence (arūpa-rāga).
desire-for-immaterial-immortality.description: Desire for Immaterial Immortality renders arūpa-rāga, the seventh of the ten fetters, attributed to Kether. It is the most refined of all cravings for becoming: the longing to abide in the formless realms — the boundless states of space, consciousness and beyond — as a kind of disembodied, deathless existence. Among the higher fetters, it is cut only at arahatship. Its placement at the Crown marks it as the last and subtlest grasping after continued being, the will-to-exist clinging even at the very summit, where only the unconditioned remains beyond.

despair.summary: Nine of Swords — Despair and Cruelty; Mars in Gemini, Yesod of Air: anguish of mind.
despair.description: Despair is part of the Golden Dawn title 'Despair and Cruelty' for the Nine of Swords, Yesod of the airy suit, Mars in the second decan of Gemini. The full power of the intellectual suit, charged with Mars and seated in the lunar foundation, turns to mental torment: hopelessness, the wound that festers in the dark. It signifies the depths of psychic suffering, the mind's cruelty to itself.
tables: CXXXV. Titles and Attributions of the Sword Suit.

devotion.summary: The Wisdom-virtue of devotion, the soul's pure dedication to the highest.
devotion.description: Devotion is listed among the virtues at Chokmah, the supernal Father and sphere of pure Wisdom. As the moral fruit of that lofty Sephirah it is the soul's wholehearted dedication to the Divine—the fixing of the whole being upon its source in unwavering love and reverence. From the height of Chokmah, the first outflashing of the One, devotion appears as the proper response of the creature to the creative will: the giving of oneself, without reserve, to that from which one came.
tables: L. Transcendental Morality (10 Virtues; 7 Deadly Sins; 4 Magic Powers)

devotion-to-great-work.summary: The solar virtue of devotion to the Great Work, the heart consecrated to attainment.
devotion-to-great-work.description: Devotion to the Great Work is the virtue of Tiphareth, the solar heart of the Tree where the work of the adept is centred. It is the consecration of the whole life to the one aim—the perfecting of the self and its union with the divine—so that every act becomes an offering toward attainment. Fittingly seated at the sphere of the sacrificed and risen god, it is the steady flame of dedication that does not waver though the labour be long, the virtue that makes a magician of a mere seeker.
tables: L. Transcendental Morality (10 Virtues; 7 Deadly Sins; 4 Magic Powers)

dhamma.summary: The recollection of the Dhamma — the Buddha's teaching and the law of things, second Jewel.
dhamma.description: Dhamma is the second of the Three Jewels: at once the body of the Buddha's teaching and the very law or truth of reality that the teaching discloses. As a recollection among the Forty Meditations it is contemplated for its qualities — 'well-expounded, visible here and now, timeless, inviting inspection, leading onward' — so that confidence and clarity arise in the meditator. Attributed to Hod, the sphere of Mercury and of intellect and form, it fittingly figures the articulated doctrine, the ordering word by which the path is made knowable and walkable.

diamond.summary: The supreme stone of Kether—pure light, indestructibility, and unity.
diamond.description: The diamond is attributed in 777 to the highest reaches of the Tree, pre-eminently to Kether—the purest, hardest, and most brilliant of stones, a fitting emblem of the undifferentiated white light of the Crown. Crystallised carbon of perfect transparency, it refracts all colours yet is itself colourless, mirroring Kether’s containment of all things in unity. Its physical incorruptibility and supreme hardness (10 on the Mohs scale) make it the natural symbol of the eternal, the indestructible spark of the divine self. In the lapidary tradition the diamond signifies invincibility, clarity, and spiritual perfection.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

diana.summary: Diana, the moon-goddess and huntress — virgin mistress of the wild, at the Moon.
diana.description: Diana is the Roman goddess of the moon, the hunt, and the wilderness, counterpart of the Greek Artemis, chaste protectress of women and wild things. Referred to Gimel and the Moon, to Sagittarius, and to Yesod, she is the silver lunar power, the huntress roaming the night woods with her hounds. As the triple goddess of heaven, earth, and underworld she unites the maiden, the wild, and the mysteries of the moon.

diana-of-epheus.summary: Diana of Ephesus, the many-breasted mother — the great fertile goddess of Asia, at Yesod.
diana-of-epheus.description: Diana of Ephesus is the Anatolian great goddess worshipped in the famed temple at Ephesus, depicted with many breasts or egg-like ovoids, an image of boundless nourishment and fertility. Though bearing the name of the virgin Diana, she is in truth a magna mater of teeming life. Referred to Yesod, the generative Foundation, she embodies the inexhaustible nurturing and reproductive power of nature, the mother who feeds the whole world.

digestive-system.summary: The digestive system, attributed to Jupiter, the body's economy of nourishment and increase.
digestive-system.description: The Digestive System is attributed to Kaph and Jupiter. The whole apparatus by which food is received, broken down, and assimilated into the substance of the body answers to expansive, nourishing Jupiter—the planet of growth, abundance, and the increase of the flesh. As Jupiter governs all enlargement and plenty, so the digestion is the body's economy of increase, turning the food of the world into living tissue.

digitalis.summary: Foxglove, attributed to Tiphareth; the heart-medicine and heart-poison of the Sun.
digitalis.description:
Digitalis, the foxglove, is fittingly set at Tiphareth, the solar sphere of the heart — for its cardiac glycosides act directly upon the heartbeat, a true medicine of the centre that strengthens the failing heart in exact dose and stops it in excess. It is among the clearest examples in the whole pharmacopoeia of the Paracelsian truth that the dose makes the poison, and of Tiphareth's double nature as the seat of life and of sacrifice.

Caution: digitalis is a powerful cardiac poison with a very narrow therapeutic margin. Scholarly entry only.
digitalis.caution: Cardiac glycoside; narrow margin between dose and lethal poison. Scholarly entry only.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

dilatory-bandmaster.summary: The magical image of Amdusias — a unicorn, or a dilatory bandmaster of unseen music — Goetic Duke of the first decan of Aquarius (by night).
dilatory-bandmaster.description: Amdusias (Amdukias), the sixty-seventh spirit of the Goetia and a great and strong Duke, appears first as a unicorn, but when called into human shape comes as the leisurely, dilatory master of an unseen band — for at his coming trumpets and all manner of musical instruments are heard, though their players cannot be seen, until he is commanded to make them visible. In 777 he is the nocturnal ruler of the first decan of Aquarius. He can make trees bow and bend at will and gives excellent familiars. The procrastinating conductor of phantom music befits the airy, future-haunted sign of the Water-Bearer, where harmony sounds from sources unseen.

dionysis.summary: Dionysus, the twice-born god of the vine — ecstasy, death, and rebirth at the solar heart.
dionysis.description: Dionysus is the Greek god of wine, fertility, theatre, and sacred ecstasy, the twice-born deity torn apart and reborn, whose mysteries offered initiates union with the divine. Referred to Tiphareth, the centre of the dying-and-rising gods, he is the power of ecstatic dissolution and renewal — the vine cut down and bearing fruit again. His maenads, his thyrsus, and his frenzy embody the liberating, transformative madness of the god.

disappointment.summary: Five of Cups — Disappointment / Loss in Pleasure; Mars in Scorpio, Geburah of Water.
disappointment.description: The Five of Cups, Disappointment (Loss in Pleasure), is Geburah in the suit of Water and the first decan of Scorpio under Mars. The fives shatter their suit, and martial force breaking upon water troubles and empties the cups; the lotus withers, the wine is spilled. It is the sorrow that follows expected joy, pleasure soured, the bitter taste of hope unfulfilled.
tables: CXXXIV. Titles and Attributions of the Chalice Suit

dishonesty.summary: The Mercurial vice of dishonesty, the corruption of the truth-speaking mind.
dishonesty.description: Dishonesty is named among the vices at Beth and Mercury, the sphere of speech, commerce, and the cunning intellect. As the shadow of Mercury—the trickster and messenger—it is the misuse of the mind's quickness for deceit, the bending of word and dealing away from truth for advantage. The same nimble intelligence that, purified, becomes truthfulness and skill, when corrupted becomes the cheat, the forger, the liar; it is the characteristic vice of the unredeemed quicksilver nature.
tables: L. Transcendental Morality (10 Virtues; 7 Deadly Sins; 4 Magic Powers)

disk.summary: Disk — the divine 'guardian' Crowley pairs with the Face of Adam Kadmon at the supernals in table XXI.
disk.description: In Crowley's table XXI 'The Perfected Man' — his adaptation of the Adam Kadmon body-symbolism onto the Tree — each body-part is paired with a guardian name in parentheses, e.g. 'The Face (Disk)' at the supernals. 'Disk' here is the solar/lunar disc as the divine countenance — the radiant face above all faces, the gleaming circle that returns in Egyptian, Sumerian, and Vedic iconography as the visible token of the god. Its placement at the supernal triad fits the Kabbalistic principle that what is seen as 'face' at the upper Tree is the bare luminous disc of pure being, before the descent into features and form.

dispersing-ravens.summary: A'arab Zaraq — the averse Netzach; the ravens of dispersion and false love.
dispersing-ravens.description: The Dispersing Ravens (A'arab Zaraq, the 'Ravens of Dispersion') are the Qliphoth of Netzach, the sphere of Venus and victory. The unifying, harmonising love of the seventh Sephirah is here scattered into lust, decay, and the flocking carrion-birds of corrupted desire. They are the shells of a beauty gone rotten, attraction become a dispersing rather than a uniting force.
tables: CXXIII. Translation of the Orders of the Qliphoth

displays-his-art.summary: Design detail of the Magician (Beth): he displays his art.
displays-his-art.description: ‘Displays his art’ closes Liber 777's design for Atu I, the Magician (path of Beth, Mercury): ‘equipped as a Magician, displays his art.’ The phrase shows the magus in the act—not merely possessing power but exercising it, the elemental weapons in play, the work performed. The Magician's art is the Logos made operative: thought projected into manifestation, the juggler-conjuror who makes the four elements dance at the command of a focused will.
tables: CLXXXI. Correct Design of Tarot Trumps

disposing-one.summary: The Seventeenth Path — the Disposing Intelligence of Zayin, foundation of faith for the righteous.
disposing-one.description: The Seventeenth Path is the Disposing Intelligence (Sekhel ha-Hergesh, the Intelligence of Sense or Disposition), attributed to the letter Zayin and the sign Gemini, the path of The Lovers joining Binah to Tiphareth. The Sepher Yetzirah says it provides faith to the righteous and clothes them with the Holy Spirit, and calls it the Foundation of Beauty in the state of higher things. As the path of discrimination and union — the Twins, the choosing between — it disposes and orders, arranging the soul's loyalties toward the higher light.
tables: XIII. Paths of the Sefer Yetzirah

disputers.summary: Tagiriron — the averse Tiphareth; litigants who shatter harmony into strife.
disputers.description: The Disputers (Tagiriron, the 'Hagglers' or 'Litigators') are the Qliphoth of Tiphareth, the harmonising solar centre. Against the beauty and balance of the sixth Sephirah they set endless contention and ugliness — the great hideous heads that dispute and quarrel, harmony broken into faction. They are the shells of a centre that no longer holds.
tables: CXXIII. Translation of the Orders of the Qliphoth

dittany-of-crete.summary: The healing herb of Malkuth—dittany of Crete, balm of wounds and, in lore, the smoke in which spirits take shape.
dittany-of-crete.description: Dittany of Crete is attributed to Malkuth, the Kingdom and manifest earth. The famed healing herb of antiquity—wild goats wounded by arrows were said to seek it out, and it staunched the wound of Aeneas—it was also reputed, when burned, to give a smoke dense enough for spirits to clothe themselves and become visible. Both as earthly medicine and as the medium of manifestation it belongs to Malkuth, where spirit takes material form. Esoterically dittany is the perfume of incarnation and healing—the herb of the Kingdom in which the unseen is made visible and the wounded body made whole.

divination.summary: The airy art of drawing knowledge of the hidden from sign, symbol, and oracle.
divination.description: Divination is set at Aleph and Air, the path of the Fool and of pure spirit moving over the waters. As Air is the medium of intelligence and connection, divination is the magical power of reading the will of the gods and the shape of things to come through any system of signs—tarot, geomancy, the I Ching, the flight of birds. Crowley regarded it less as fortune-telling than as a disciplined method of putting a question to the unconscious or to the secret order of nature and receiving an intelligible answer through the symbolic mind.

divination-by-dreams.summary: The lunar art of receiving guidance and prophecy through the gates of sleep.
divination-by-dreams.description: Divination by Dreams, attributed to Gimel and the Moon, is the oldest and most natural of the oracular arts: the soul, loosed in sleep, wanders the astral realms and brings back images of warning, counsel, and things to come. The lunar path of the High Priestess governs the tides of the unconscious through which such dreams rise, and the magician learns to incubate, remember, and rightly read them. From the dream-temples of Asklepios to the visions of the prophets, this is the power of letting the night speak.

djin.summary: King of the Salamanders, ruler of the elemental spirits of Fire.
djin.description: Djin (Djinn) is the King of the Salamanders, sovereign of the elemental spirits of Fire in the Paracelsian scheme handed down through Eliphas Lévi and the Golden Dawn. The salamanders are the bright, darting, untamable creatures who live in and as the flame — the very life and ardour of the fiery element — and over them Djin reigns. He is invoked in the working of the Fire quarter, the hot, dry, southern element of will and transformation, and commands the salamanders who govern combustion, zeal, and the consuming, purifying power of flame. Esoterically he embodies the active, aspiring, devouring force of Fire: energy, courage, and the spiritual heat that tempers and transmutes, the elemental king whose name later folklore would bestow on the fiery spirits of Arabian legend.
tables: LXII. Kings of the Elemental Spirits

dog.summary: The faithful lunar beast—companion and guardian, the dogs that bay at the Moon on the path of Qoph.
dog.description: The Dog runs along the lunar and twilight paths of the Tree—Gimel (the High Priestess, the Moon), Samekh, and Qoph (Pisces, the Moon trump). On the 29th path especially it is the pair of dogs or jackals that bay at the rising moon in Atu XVIII, the half-tamed instinct that howls at the threshold of the unconscious. As companion, guardian, and psychopomp—Anubis the jackal who leads the dead through the dark—the Dog is loyalty and the keen scent that follows a trail where the eye fails. Esoterically it is the faithful animal soul, at once the guardian of the gate and the baying fear that must be passed on the moonlit road of return.

tables: CXLIX. Magical Images of the Decans (Ascendent)

dolphin.summary: The saving creature of Pisces—the friend of man and the gods, intelligent guide through the waters.
dolphin.description: The dolphin is attributed to Pisces, the watery sign of the fishes, and it is the most benign and luminous of sea-creatures: sacred to Apollo (who took its form) and to Poseidon, famed in myth as the rescuer of drowning poets and the carrier of souls across the sea. Where so many water-beasts of the grid are dark and devouring, the dolphin is the friendly, intelligent power of the deep, the playful saviour that guides and bears up the traveller. Under Pisces it figures the redeeming, compassionate face of the great waters. Esoterically the dolphin is the helpful intelligence within the unconscious sea, the guide that carries the soul safely through the dissolving waters of the dream-world.

tables: XLVII. Kings and Princes of the Jinn

door.summary: Daleth — 'door'; the Venusian gate of love and entrance, path of The Empress.
door.description: Daleth means 'door' — the swinging gate through which one passes from without to within. As a door it implies both threshold and welcome, opening and enclosure. In Liber 777 Daleth is the path of The Empress, attributed to Venus, joining Chokmah to Binah, uniting the supernal Father and Mother across the top of the Tree. The door is love itself: the gracious Venusian gateway between the two highest powers, the opening through which generation and beauty pour into the world.
tables: III. Translation of the Names of the Paths

dove.summary: The bird of Venus—Aphrodite's dove and the descending Spirit, emblem of love, peace and the gentle soul.
dove.description: The dove is attributed to Venus and the path of the Empress (Daleth), and it is one of the oldest emblems of love: the bird that drew Aphrodite's chariot, the messenger of peace, the soul itself depicted as a white dove rising from the body. In the Western mysteries it is also the form of the descending Holy Spirit, the gentle power of love and grace coming down upon the world. Soft, faithful, and amorous, the dove is wholly fitted to the Venusian sphere of beauty and union. Esoterically it figures the tender, peace-bringing aspect of love and the pure soul that aspires upward, the spirit of gentleness brooding upon the waters.

dragon.summary: The dragon of the Negative Veils—the coiled primal chaos before creation, the unmanifest power that rings the Tree.
dragon.description: The dragon is attributed to the Veils of the Negative, the threefold darkness (Ain, Ain Soph, Ain Soph Aur) that lies beyond and behind even Kether, and it is the supreme image of the unmanifest: the great coiled serpent-dragon of chaos that encircles the whole Tree, the Leviathan and Tiamat of the deep from whose body the worlds are made. Older than creation, the dragon is the boundless potential and the formless power that both threatens and underlies all order—the abyssal force that must be confronted, divided, and built upon for a cosmos to arise. Esoterically the dragon figures the negative existence, the dark infinite ground of being out of which the first point of light is drawn, at once the womb and the adversary of manifestation.

dragon-s-blood.summary: The red resin of Aries—dragon's blood, blazing scarlet incense of Martian power, passion, and command.
dragon-s-blood.description: Dragon's Blood is attributed to Aries (Heh, the Emperor), the fiery sign of Mars. The deep red resin of the dracaena—looking like clotted blood and burning with a heavy, sweet-resinous smoke—is the classic incense of power, passion, protection, and the bending of will, used to charge talismans and to command the elemental forces. Its scarlet, martial character is wholly of Aries. Esoterically dragon's blood is the perfume of fiery will and command—the blood-red smoke that lends force to the word and seals the magician's intent with the power of Mars.

dragon-with-3-heads-a-dog-s.term: Dragon with 3 heads a dog s
dragon-with-3-heads-a-dog-s.displayTerm: Dragon with 3 heads a dog s
dragon-with-3-heads-a-dog-s.summary: The magical image of Bune — a three-headed dragon — Goetic Duke of the second decan of Sagittarius.
dragon-with-3-heads-a-dog-s.description: Bune (Bime), the twenty-sixth spirit of the Goetia and a great and strong Duke, appears as a dragon with three heads — one like a dog, one like a gryphon, and one like a man. In 777 he is set at the second decan of Sagittarius by day. He speaks with a high and comely voice, changes the place of the dead and gathers them about their tombs, gives riches, makes men eloquent and wise, and answers truly. The winged, triple-headed dragon befits the lofty, far-ranging fire of the Archer — wisdom that commands even the company of the dead.

dragonis-blood.summary: The blood-red incense of Mars—dragon's blood at the path of the Tower, smoke of force, protection, and command.
dragonis-blood.description: Dragon's Blood (here at Pe, Mars and the Tower) is the scarlet resin of the dracaena, looking like dried blood and burning with a heavy sweet smoke—the pre-eminent incense of Martian magic. Burned for power, protection, and the breaking of obstacles, charging talismans and weapons with force, it is exactly placed upon the path of Mars and the lightning-struck Tower. Esoterically dragon's blood is the perfume of raw martial power—the red smoke that arms the will, drives off opposition, and seals an act of force.

dragons.summary: The great serpents of power, set at Teth and Leo — guardians of the hoard and the threshold.
dragons.description: The Dragons are an order of legendary beings, attributed to Teth and the sign Leo, the path of Strength (Lust). Across the world's myth they are the mighty serpent-beasts, coiled upon their hoards and guarding forbidden treasures, embodiments of primordial force that the hero must master or slay. Set at the leonine path of strength and ardent vitality, they figure the great untamed power of the life-force itself — the serpent-energy that, conquered or harnessed, yields its golden hoard to the brave.

dromedary.summary: The magical image of Uvall — a dromedary — Goetic Duke of the second decan of Cancer (by night).
dromedary.description: Uvall (Vual, Voval), the forty-seventh spirit of the Goetia and a great and mighty Duke, appears first as a dromedary and then, at command, takes human shape and speaks the Egyptian tongue, though not perfectly. In 777 he is the nocturnal ruler of the second decan of Cancer. He procures the love of women, wins friendship between friends and foes, and tells things past, present and to come. The patient desert-camel — bearer across long waterless ways — befits the tenacious, memory-laden sign of the Crab and its long-carried affections.

dropsy.summary: Dropsy at Chesed and Jupiter — the watery plethora of Jupiterian excess.
dropsy.description: Dropsy, the old name for the swelling of edema, is attributed to Chesed, the sphere of Jupiter. Jupiter is the planet of moisture, expansion, and abundance, and dropsy is his excess made pathological: the tissues bloated with retained water, the body swollen past its measure. It is the cautionary shadow of Chesed's mercy and increase — generosity become accumulation, abundance turned to waterlogged weight.

dry.summary: Dryness, the quality of separation and fixity, root of Fire and Earth.
dry.description: In the doctrine of the four primary qualities, Dry is one of the two passive principles—the quality of that which holds its own shape, resists mixture, and keeps things distinct. Combined with the active qualities it forms two of the four elements: Hot and Dry make Fire, Cold and Dry make Earth. Attributed here to the fiery, earthy, and supernal positions, dryness is the principle of definition and separation, the firm quality that bounds and fixes what moisture would dissolve.
tables: CV. Ten Earths in Seven Palaces English
XI. The Elements and their Planetary Rulers

dual-contending-forces.summary: Thaumiel — the averse Crown; two warring heads where Kether's unity should be.
dual-contending-forces.description: The Dual Contending Forces (Thaumiel, 'the Twins of God') are the Qliphoth, or shells, of Kether. Where the true Crown is the supreme and indivisible Unity, its averse reflection is a sundered duality — two giant heads forever at war, the primal One split into contending powers that deny the source from which they fell. They head the inverted Tree of the shells, the root of all division and rebellion.
tables: CXXIII. Translation of the Orders of the Qliphoth

dwelling.summary: Zebul, a heaven of Assiah at Tiphareth — the 'Dwelling' of the heavenly Temple and altar.
dwelling.description: Zebul ('lofty dwelling' or 'habitation') is one of the seven heavens of the Talmud, attributed to Tiphareth. It contains the heavenly Jerusalem, the Temple, and the altar at which the great prince Michael, the celestial High Priest, offers sacrifice — the sanctified dwelling at the harmonising solar centre of the heavenly scheme.
tables: XCIV. The Heavens of Assiah English

eagle.summary: The soaring Kerub—Jupiter's royal bird and the eagle of Scorpio's redemption, aspiration toward the Sun.
eagle.description: The Eagle is among the four Kerubic beasts, the emblem of Water in its exalted form—the redeemed Scorpio, the serpent's venom transmuted into the bird that alone can gaze unblinking into the Sun. In 777 it keeps company too with Jupiter (Kaph) and the airy heights, for it is the king of birds as Jupiter is king of gods: sovereign aspiration and far sight. Esoterically the Eagle is the soul's upward flight, the spirit that rises out of the depths of Scorpio's death to the solar light, carrying the alchemical signature of volatilisation—that which ascends, is purified, and looks at last into the source of fire.

eagle-snake-scorpion.summary: The threefold emblem of Scorpio at Water—scorpion, serpent and eagle, the three degrees of the sign's transformation.
eagle-snake-scorpion.description: The triad of eagle, snake and scorpion is attributed to the watery letter Mem and to the sign Scorpio, and together they form the classic threefold glyph of that sign's power at its three levels. The scorpion is Scorpio fallen—the creature that stings itself to death, the self-destructive lowest expression. The serpent is Scorpio in its natural force—the kundalini, the generative and transforming life-power. The eagle is Scorpio exalted—the spirit that rises from the depths and mounts toward the sun. Read together they map the whole arc of transmutation that is Scorpio's secret: from poison through power to transcendence. Esoterically this emblem is a complete teaching on the redemption of the death-and-desire force, the one energy seen in its degradation, its working, and its glory.

earned-success.summary: Six of Swords — Earned Success; Mercury in Aquarius, Tiphareth of Air: clear method.
earned-success.description: Earned Success is the Golden Dawn title of the Six of Swords, Tiphareth of the airy suit, Mercury in the second decan of Aquarius. The mind, brought to its harmonious centre, achieves clarity and balance; the swords are ordered, the rose intact. It signifies intelligence rewarded — success that is the fruit of reasoned effort and well-applied understanding.
tables: CXXXV. Titles and Attributions of the Sword Suit.

earth.summary: The element of solidity, stability, and material manifestation.
earth.description:
Earth is the element of solidity, stability, and material manifestation—cold and dry, heavy, still, the ground in which all the other elements come to rest and bear fruit. In 777 it is attributed to the path 32-bis, to the Tatwa Prithivi (a yellow square), and to the northern quarter. Its weapon is the Pentacle or Disk, its archangel Auriel (Uriel), its elemental king Ghob, its creatures the gnomes.

Earth governs the body, the senses, wealth, agriculture, and all that endures and sustains. In the elemental scheme it is the final condensation of spirit into form—the place where the abstract becomes real, and therefore the proper field of the practical, manifesting magician.
tables: CV. Ten Earths in Seven Palaces English
CX. Elements and Quarters per the Sepher Yetzirah
XCV. Contents of the Heavens of Assiah
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

earthly-power.summary: Four of Disks — Earthly Power; Sun in Capricorn, Chesed of Earth: the fortress.
earthly-power.description: Earthly Power is the Golden Dawn title of the Four of Disks, Chesed of the earthy suit, the Sun in the last decan of Capricorn. The four discs are drawn as a fortified stronghold seen from above, the firm establishment of temporal power and possession. It signifies security, governance, and the ordering of matter into a stable estate — wealth and authority that must be defended.
tables: CXXXVI. Titles and Attributions of the Pantacle Suit

east.summary: The quarter of the rising sun, in the magical scheme attributed to Air.
east.description: The East is the quarter of the dawning Light, the station from which the sun rises and toward which the temple is commonly oriented. In the elemental scheme of the Western mysteries it is attributed to Air, the element of intellect and the breath of life, and to the dawn of every work. As the place of beginning and of the rising Light, it governs the invocation that opens the magical circle.
tables: CX. Elements and Quarters per the Sepher Yetzirah

ecbolics.summary: The rye fungus, attributed to Gemini; ecbolic poison and root of psychedelic chemistry.
ecbolics.description:
Ergot — the fungus Claviceps that infects rye — is placed at the path of Zayin and Gemini, the sign of duality and the messenger, an apt home for a substance of profoundly double nature. Its alkaloids contract the womb (its use as an 'ecbolic' in childbirth) and, in poisoning, cause the gangrene and burning madness once called St Anthony's Fire; from those same alkaloids modern chemistry later derived LSD. Esoterically it is the dark twin-power, medicine and madness, the same force that delivers and that destroys.

Caution: ergot is highly toxic, historically the cause of mass poisonings. Scholarly entry only.
ecbolics.caution: Highly toxic; cause of historical mass poisonings (St Anthony's Fire). Scholarly entry only.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

ecclesia-xsti.summary: Ecclesia Christi — the Church as the Bride of Christ, attributed to Malkuth.
ecclesia-xsti.description: Ecclesia Xsti (Ecclesia Christi, 'the Church of Christ') is placed at Malkuth, the tenth Sephirah, the Kingdom and the Bride. The attribution is exact to Christian symbolism: the Church is the Bride of Christ and the body through which the divine is made manifest in the world — the Shekhinah, the indwelling presence, the Queen who is wedded to the King of Tiphareth.
tables: XXXVI. Selection of Christian Gods (10); Apostles (12); Evangelists(4); and Churches of Asia (7)

eden.summary: A content of the heavens at the lower Sephiroth — the Garden, the earthly paradise.
eden.description: Eden is reckoned among the contents of the heavens at Yesod and Malkuth — the lower, earthward terms of the cosmic order. As the garden of delight, the paradise of origins and of return, Eden is the blessed ground set at the foundation of the worlds: the locus of innocence and abundance where the human story begins and to which it longs to come home.
tables: XCV. Contents of the Heavens of Assiah

ee.summary: The long-'ee' vowel — Crowley's English equivalent at the path of Yod (Virgo) in table LI.
ee.description: The long 'ee' (as in 'feet') is set at path 20 — Yod, the small flame from which the Tetragrammaton begins and the letter ruling Virgo. Its Coptic equivalent is the letter Ⲏ (ē, derived from Greek eta), whose sound matches the Hebrew yod's vocalic value of 'i/ee'. In Crowley's correspondence-grammar the high front vowel — narrow, focused, ascending — fits the Virgoan path of the Hermit, whose lamp is the concentrated point of light. The entry records nothing more than this phonetic placement, the alphabetic atom Crowley aligns with the twentieth path.
tables: LI. English Equivalent of the Coptic Alphabet

ei.summary: Ei — a letter of the Coptic alphabet (e), which Crowley attributes to 7 Netzach.
ei.description: Ei is a letter of the Coptic alphabet — the script in which the Egyptian language was written in the Christian era, the Greek alphabet adapted to Egyptian speech. It is the short e, from Greek epsilon. Crowley folds the Coptic alphabet into the great correspondence of letters and paths in 777 (Table LI), assigning Ei to 7 Netzach on the Tree of Life, so that the Egyptian-Christian script takes its station among the Hebrew letters and the keys of the Tarot.
tables: LI. Names of the Coptic Letters

eirneus.summary: A genius of the Nuctemeron's third hour, set by Crowley at Gemini.
eirneus.description: Eirneus is listed among the genii of the third hour of the Nuctemeron, the “Day Illumined by Night” attributed to Apollonius of Tyana and transmitted by Éliphas Lévi. The older sources name him among the seven genii of the third hour but do not preserve for him a settled office, so none is here invented. Crowley ranks these hour-genii along the zodiacal paths in 777 (Table CLXXIII), where Eirneus stands at Gemini (Zayin).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

eirnils.summary: Fruits — the Nuctemeron genius of the sixth hour presiding over fruits, set by Crowley at Virgo.
eirnils.description: Among the genii of the sixth hour in the Nuctemeron of Apollonius of Tyana, Eirnils presides over fruits. His charge is the ripening fruit, the yield of orchard, vine and field. Lévi gives the roll of the hour-genii in his Transcendental Magic; Crowley tabulates them along the paths of the Tree (Table CLXXIII), assigning Eirnils to Virgo (Yod).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

eistibus.summary: Divination — the Nuctemeron genius of the fourth hour presiding over divination, set by Crowley at Cancer.
eistibus.description: Eistibus is the Nuctemeron genius of divination. That “Night-illumined Day”, ascribed to Apollonius of Tyana and handed down through Lévi's Transcendental Magic, sets a company of spirits over each of the twelve hours of the magical day, and Eistibus belongs to the fourth hour. His province is augury and the reading of omens and signs. In 777 (Table CLXXIII) Crowley redistributes these hour-genii across the zodiac, where this spirit falls at Cancer (Cheth).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

elephant.summary: The vast beast of Libra and Yesod—strength balanced by gentleness, deep memory, the patient bearer of foundations.
elephant.description: The elephant is set at Libra and at Yesod, where its enormous strength is paired with a famed gentleness and an even, deliberate tread—power in perfect equilibrium, which is the Libran ideal. It is the beast of memory and of the foundation that bears great weight without haste, fitting for Yesod, the underpinning sphere of the Tree.
