In the Eastern symbolism that 777 freely draws upon, the elephant is the vehicle of wisdom and the remover of obstacles, the steady mind that cannot be hurried or overturned. Esoterically it marks the massive, patient stability on which higher work is founded.

eligos.summary: The fifteenth spirit of the Goetia, a duke of Leo who knows the fortunes of war and wins the love of lords.
eligos.description: Eligos is the fifteenth spirit of the Goetia, a great duke of the decans of Leo. He discovers hidden things and knows the future, especially the outcome of wars and how soldiers should meet; he procures the love of lords and great persons. He appears as a goodly knight bearing a lance, an ensign or banner, and a serpent. A spirit of the lordly fire-sign, he is the captain of war-craft and the winner of noble favour.

elijah.summary: Elijah — at Tiphareth; the solar prophet taken up in the chariot of fire.
elijah.description: Elijah is attributed to Tiphareth, the radiant solar centre of the Tree. The prophet who called down fire from heaven and was carried aloft in a fiery chariot embodies the glory and the sacrificial-and-risen quality of the sixth Sephirah. Translated without death and awaited as the herald of the Messiah, he is a figure of the perfected, sun-bright self that ascends from the heart of the work.
tables: XCI. The Saints or Adepts of the Hebrews

elisha.summary: Elisha — at Malkuth; the prophet of works and wonders in the world.
elisha.description: Elisha, the disciple who received a double portion of Elijah's spirit, is attributed to Malkuth, the Kingdom. Where his master ascended in fire, Elisha remained to labour among the people, working healings and material wonders in the everyday world. His station in the tenth Sephirah fits the prophet whose power was poured out in concrete, earthly acts of providence.
tables: XCI. The Saints or Adepts of the Hebrews

elixir-vit.summary: The alchemical Elixir of Life, attributed to Kether — the draught of immortality.
elixir-vit.description: The Elixir Vitæ — the Elixir of Life — is set at Kether, the Crown, because it is less a substance than the supreme attainment itself: the liquid form of the Philosopher's Stone, the draught that confers immortality and perfect health. In the alchemical literature it is the consummation of the Great Work, the dew of the higher worlds drawn down and fixed; in the Vedic tradition it is amrita, the nectar of the gods churned from the cosmic ocean. Esoterically it names the influx of divine life that the adept who reaches the Crown is said to drink — the regeneration of the whole being by union with the Source. Its placement at Kether marks it as the goal toward which the entire pharmacopoeia of the Tree is a shadow and a ladder.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

elm.summary: The funeral tree of Saturn—the stately elm, guardian of the dead and the gate of dreams.
elm.description: The Elm is attributed to Saturn (Tav, the Universe). Tall and sombre, long used for coffins and planted in graveyards, it is a tree of mortality, dignity, and the threshold of death proper to Saturn, lord of time and endings; at the gate of Virgil's underworld it is the great elm in whose leaves the false dreams roost. Esoterically the elm is the saturnine tree of the boundary—solemn, enduring, standing watch where the living world meets the realm of the dead.

emerald.summary: The green stone of Venus and Netzach—love, nature, harmony, and growth.
emerald.description: The emerald is attributed to Netzach and the sphere of Venus, its living green the colour of love, nature, fertility, and harmony. A green variety of beryl coloured by chromium and vanadium, it has been associated since Egyptian times with the goddess of love and with the renewing power of vegetation. The fabled Emerald Tablet of Hermes makes it the very stone of esoteric wisdom (‘as above, so below’). In 777 its Venusian green marks it as the gem of the emotions, of art, and of the green force that drives all growth.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

emplacement.summary: Makhon, a heaven of Assiah at Chesed — the storehouse heaven, 'Emplacement' of the elements.
emplacement.description: Among the seven heavens of the Talmud, Makhon (here 'Emplacement', the fixed 'establishment') is attributed to Chesed. It is the storehouse heaven, the great repository in which are kept the treasures of snow and hail, the lofts of dew and rain, and the chamber of storms — the heavenly magazine of the elements, set fittingly at the Jupiterian sphere of abundance.
tables: XCIV. The Heavens of Assiah English

empresses-coins.summary: The Tens (Empresses) of the suit of Coins/Disks, attributed to the element of Earth.
empresses-coins.description: ‘Empresses – Coins’ is an entry from Liber 777's General Attribution of the Tarot linking the court and pip divisions to the element of Earth (32bis). The Tens of each suit correspond to Malkuth, the material kingdom; the suit of Coins (Disks or Pantacles) is the earthy suit of wealth, body, and manifestation. The cluster shows the element of Earth expressed across the deck—the culminating Tens and the earthy court, the powers of nature brought down into solid, fruitful form.
tables: XIV. General Attribution of the Tarot

energy.summary: Force itself as a weapon—the raw projected power of Aries and Geburah, the will discharged in action.
energy.description: Energy is reckoned among the magical weapons at Aries and at Geburah, for in the higher magic the operator's own marshalled force is itself an implement. This is the dynamic, outgoing power of Mars and the initiating fire of Aries—will not merely held but discharged, the current of vital force directed upon a target. Where the Wand directs and the Sword divides, Energy is the very thing they channel: the charge that gives the operation its power to act. Esoterically Energy as a weapon is the disciplined release of the magician's accumulated force—the trained capacity to gather power and hurl it, the severe and martial virtue of Geburah by which intention is made to strike with real and measurable effect.
tables: L. Transcendental Morality (10 Virtues; 7 Deadly Sins; 4 Magic Powers)

enneagram.summary: The nine-pointed star — attributed to the Moon; the figure of the foundation.
enneagram.description: The enneagram, the nine-pointed star, is attributed by its number to the sphere of the Moon and to Yesod, the Foundation. As the figure of nine it gathers the full strength of the lunar and foundational powers, the completion of the single digits before the return to unity in ten. It is the star of the astral foundation, the lunar seal beneath the threshold of the manifest world.
tables: XLIX. Lineal Figures of the Planets, &c., and Geomany

enoch.summary: Enoch — at Binah; the one who 'walked with God' and was taken into Understanding.
enoch.description: Enoch is attributed to Binah, the Great Mother and sphere of Understanding. He 'walked with God, and was not, for God took him' — translated alive into the supernal realm — and in the esoteric tradition became the scribe of heaven and revealer of mysteries. His placement in Binah marks the soul received into the dark womb of comprehension, passing beyond mortal form into the silence of the Mother.
tables: XCI. The Saints or Adepts of the Hebrews

enthroned-king.summary: The magical image of Chesed — the throned king, seat of merciful sovereignty.
enthroned-king.description: “A throned king” belongs to the magical image of Chesed, the fourth Sephirah, the Jupiterian sphere of mercy and rule. The throne signifies established, lawful dominion — authority at rest, secure in its order and dispensing its bounty. Together with the crown it completes the image of the mighty, crowned, and enthroned king, the very type of beneficent kingship at the heart of the merciful sphere.
tables: CXX. Magical Images of the Sephiroth

envy.summary: The Mercurial-Saturnine vice of envy, the covetous grudging of another's good.
envy.description: Envy is listed among the vices at Beth and Mercury (and at Saturn), the restless, comparing intellect turned sour. As a vice it is the grudging discontent that resents another's good fortune and covets what one lacks—the mind forever measuring itself against others to its own torment. Mercury's gift of comparison and judgment, when poisoned, becomes the envious eye; the same swift intelligence that should weigh truth instead weighs only its own deprivation.
tables: L. Transcendental Morality (10 Virtues; 7 Deadly Sins; 4 Magic Powers)

ephesus.summary: Ephesus — the first of the Seven Churches of Asia, attributed to Saturn (Tav).
ephesus.description: Ephesus is the first of the seven churches addressed in the Revelation of John, set in 777 in the path of Tav and the sphere of Saturn. The church praised for its labour yet rebuked for having 'left its first love' is fittingly given to the grave, testing, limiting nature of Saturn — the discipline that endures but must guard against coldness of heart.
tables: XXXVI. Selection of Christian Gods (10); Apostles (12); Evangelists(4); and Churches of Asia (7)

epima.summary: Name of the middle decan of Capricorn, the Martial face of skilled, constructive works.
epima.description: Epima is the name 777 keeps for the middle decan of Capricorn (10°–20°). Mars rules this face and its card is the Three of Disks—Works—skilled, constructive labour, the material foundation taking shape. Among the thirty-six Hermetic decan-faces it names the industrious heart of the Goat's sign.
tables: CLXX. Egyptian Names of the Succedent Decans

equilibrium.summary: The Libran power of perfect balance, the magic of the poised and justified soul.
equilibrium.description: Equilibrium is set at Lamed and Libra, the path of Justice (Adjustment), whose scales weigh every act and whose sword cuts true. As a magical power it is the attainment of perfect inner and outer balance—the harmonising of opposing forces so that the magician acts without excess or deficiency, the very condition the Golden Dawn held to be the first law of magic: "unbalanced force is evil." To possess equilibrium is to stand at the fulcrum of the Tree, where all powers may be safely wielded because none rules.

equipped-as-a-magician.summary: Design detail of the Magician (Beth): equipped as a Magician with the elemental weapons.
equipped-as-a-magician.description: ‘Equipped as a Magician’ is part of Liber 777's design for Atu I, the Magician (path of Beth, Mercury): the fair, winged youth stands furnished with the implements of the art. He bears the four elemental weapons—wand, cup, sword, and disk—the tools by which the magus directs fire, water, air, and earth. To be ‘equipped as a Magician’ is to hold the whole apparatus of creation in readiness, the will armed and able to shape the manifest world through the powers of Mercury.
tables: CLXXXI. Correct Design of Tarot Trumps

eregbuo.summary: Name of the first decan of Sagittarius, the Mercurial face of the loosed, swift arrow.
eregbuo.description: Eregbuo is 777's name for the first decan of Sagittarius (0°–10°), the entry into mutable fire. Mercury rules this face and it bears the Eight of Wands—Swiftness—the arrow loosed, energy flying straight toward its mark. One of the thirty-six decan-faces inherited from Egypt, it names the swift aspiration that opens the Archer's sign.
tables: CLXVIII. Egyptian Names of Asc. Decans.

ergot.summary: The rye fungus, attributed to Gemini; ecbolic poison and root of psychedelic chemistry.
ergot.description:
Ergot — the fungus Claviceps that infects rye — is placed at the path of Zayin and Gemini, the sign of duality and the messenger, an apt home for a substance of profoundly double nature. Its alkaloids contract the womb (its use as an 'ecbolic' in childbirth) and, in poisoning, cause the gangrene and burning madness once called St Anthony's Fire; from those same alkaloids modern chemistry later derived LSD. Esoterically it is the dark twin-power, medicine and madness, the same force that delivers and that destroys.

Caution: ergot is highly toxic, historically the cause of mass poisonings. Scholarly entry only.
ergot.caution: Highly toxic; cause of historical mass poisonings (St Anthony's Fire). Scholarly entry only.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

erinyes.summary: The Greek Furies of vengeance, set at Heh — the relentless avengers of blood-guilt.
erinyes.description: The Erinyes are an order of legendary beings, attributed to Heh and (with their Roman counterparts) to the Martial path of vengeance. They are the ancient Greek goddesses of retribution — Alecto, Megaera, and Tisiphone — who rise from the underworld to hound those guilty of murder, oath-breaking, and crimes against kin, pursuing the offender to madness. As an order they embody the implacable moral law of consequence, the avenging fury that no guilty soul can outrun.

eros.summary: Eros, the god of love and desire — the binding, generative power, at Gemini and Yesod.
eros.description: Eros is the Greek god of love and desire, in the oldest accounts a primordial cosmic force that draws all things together, in later myth the winged son of Aphrodite whose arrows kindle passion. Referred to Zayin and Gemini and to Yesod, the generative Foundation, he is the uniting power of attraction — at once the cosmic principle of union and the personal ardour of love. He is the force that joins, begets, and binds the worlds.

especially-fire-opal.summary: The flashing stone of Hod—opal, and especially the fire opal, alive with the iridescence of intellect.
especially-fire-opal.description: Opal—and especially the fire opal—is the gem of Hod, the eighth Sephirah, sphere of Mercury and of the intellect. Its play of colour, the shifting iridescence that seems to hold many fires at once, mirrors the quicksilver, many-faceted nature of Hod: reason, language, and the splendour of forms. A hydrated silica, the opal diffracts light through its microscopic spheres into restless rainbows; the fire opal adds to this a base of orange-red flame. Esoterically it is the stone of the glittering, mobile mind, the magician's Mercury condensed into a single shifting jewel.

established-strength.summary: Three of Wands — Virtue / Established Strength; Sun in Aries, Binah of Fire.
established-strength.description: The Three of Wands, the Golden Dawn's Lord of Established Strength and the Thoth deck's Virtue, is Binah in the suit of Fire, the second decan of Aries under the Sun. The initial blaze of will (the Two) is here received and given form by the Mother, becoming steady, confident power that looks toward a goal. It is virtue in the old Roman sense of virtus — manly strength tempered into reliable, established force.
tables: CXXXIII. Titles and Attributions of the Wand Suit
XXII. Small Selection of Hindu Deities

eternal-one.summary: The Sixteenth Path, named again — the Eternal Intelligence of Vav, enduring delight of the blessed.
eternal-one.description: 'Eternal Intelligence' is the companion rendering of the Sixteenth Path of Vav (Taurus), Sekhel Nitzchi, whose other name is Triumphal. The stress here falls on eternity: this is the everlasting paradise of pleasure prepared for the just, the deathless delight of the Hierophant's path joining Wisdom to Mercy. Fixed, faithful, and enduring like the earthy bull that carries it, the Eternal Intelligence names the abiding reward that does not pass away.
tables: XIII. Paths of the Sefer Yetzirah

euminides.summary: The 'Kindly Ones' — the Erinyes appeased, set at Heh; vengeance transmuted to blessing.
euminides.description: The Eumenides ('the Kindly Ones') are an order of legendary beings, attributed to Heh — the very same avenging Furies (Erinyes) under their propitiatory name. In Aeschylus' drama, after the acquittal of Orestes the terrible Furies are reconciled and transformed into benevolent guardians of Athens, honoured beneath the earth. As an order they figure the profound mystery by which the powers of vengeance and terror, rightly appeased, are converted into protective blessing — wrath turned to grace.

euphorbium.summary: The acrid resin of Aquarius—euphorbium, biting and caustic, a sharp and difficult incense of the Star's airy path.
euphorbium.description:
Euphorbium is attributed to Aquarius (Tzaddi, the Star). The dried caustic latex of a North African spurge, fiercely acrid and irritant, it was an incense and physic of violent power, sharp and penetrating—an unusual, electric note fitting the strange, airy, future-facing sign of the Water-Bearer. Esoterically euphorbium is the keen, almost shocking perfume of Aquarius, the sharp resin whose bite mirrors the sign's lightning-clear, disruptive, awakening current.

Caution: euphorbium is a strong irritant, caustic to skin, eyes, and lungs. This entry is symbolic and historical.
euphorbium.caution: Strong caustic irritant to skin, eyes, and airways. Symbolic/historical entry only — not advice for use.

everlasting-abode.summary: A heaven of the Arabs at the lower Sephiroth — the Everlasting Abode of the blessed.
everlasting-abode.description: In the tabulation of the seven heavens of Islam, the Everlasting Abode (recalling Dar al-Qarar, the Home of Permanence, or the eternal dwelling of the blessed) is attributed to Yesod and Malkuth. It is the enduring home of the saved, the paradise that does not pass away; in 777's comparative cosmology of the Arab heavens it takes its place at the lower, earthward Sephiroth.
tables: CXXVIII. Seven Heavens of the Arabs, English

evocation.summary: The fiery power of calling spirits to visible appearance outside the magician.
evocation.description: Evocation, set at Shin and Fire, is the art of summoning a spirit, demon, or elemental force to manifest in the triangle outside the operator—distinct from invocation, which draws a power within. Fire, the element of will, manifestation, and the consuming spirit, lends evocation its compelling heat: the magician's flame of will calls the entity up from its own plane into visible or sensible presence. It is the central operation of the grimoire tradition, demanding the strongest discipline lest the force called forth overpower its caller.

exciting-intelligence.summary: The Twenty-seventh Path — the Active or Exciting Intelligence of Pe, creator of every perceiving mind.
exciting-intelligence.description: The Twenty-seventh Path is the Active, Exciting, or Natural Intelligence (Sekhel Murgash, the 'felt' or 'sensible' Intelligence), attributed to the letter Pe and the planet Mars, the path of The Tower joining Netzach to Hod. The Sepher Yetzirah says that through it is created the intellect of every existing thing beneath the highest sphere, together with their perception. The lightning-struck Tower of Mars is the shock that excites and awakens: the violent, vivifying jolt that breaks down false structure and stirs every created thing into sensation and awareness.
tables: XIII. Paths of the Sefer Yetzirah

excreting.summary: Excreting — the eliminative function, attributed to the element Earth (32-bis).
excreting.description: Excretion — the casting-off of waste — is referred in 777 to the element Earth (the path 32-bis). As earth receives what is discarded and returns it to the cycle, the eliminative function is the earthy power of release and purgation in the body, the necessary downward and outward motion that keeps the organism clean.

excretory-organs.summary: The excretory organs, attributed to Earth, the body's return of waste to the ground.
excretory-organs.description: The Excretory Organs are attributed to Earth (32 bis). The organs that gather and expel the body's solid waste belong to the densest element, the earthy ground to which all spent matter returns. As Earth is the receiver of decay and the soil of renewal, so these organs complete the body's cycle by rendering back what cannot be used, the humble and necessary office by which the living form keeps itself clean of its own dross.

excretory-system.summary: The excretory system, attributed to Saturn, the body's casting-off of the spent and waste.
excretory-system.description: The Excretory System is attributed to Tav and Saturn. The organs by which the body voids what is used up and poisonous answer to grave, eliminating Saturn—the planet of ending, limitation, and the casting-off of the dead. As Saturn rules all that is shed, finished, and returned to the earth, so the excretory function is the body's necessary discipline of release, the clearing-away without which the living frame would be choked by its own residue.

eye.summary: Ayin — 'eye'; the seeing organ in the dark of Capricorn, path of The Devil.
eye.description: Ayin means 'eye' (and 'fountain' or 'spring') — the organ of sight, and by extension the source from which seeing wells up. In Liber 777 Ayin is the path of The Devil, attributed to Capricorn, joining Tiphareth to Hod. The eye here gazes into the dark: it is the perception of matter and instinct, the goat-eyed vision that beholds the material world in its raw, generative, and shadowed power — the eye that must learn to see the light hidden within the densest darkness.
tables: III. Translation of the Names of the Paths

eye-of-hoor.summary: The Eye of Hoor (the Eye of Horus) — the wedjat of wholeness, protection, and restored sight.
eye-of-hoor.description: The Eye of Hoor is the Eye of Horus, the wedjat, the falcon-eye torn out in his battle with Set and miraculously restored by Thoth — the supreme emblem of healing, protection, wholeness, and royal power. Referred to Malkuth and to Capricorn, it is the watchful divine sight made manifest in the world, the amulet of completeness restored from injury. Its very fractions came to denote the measures of grain, binding the symbol to order and exactness.

ezekiel.summary: 'Ezekiel' — Crowley's reference in table XLV at Hod, the vision of Ezekiel as a Mercurial magical power.
ezekiel.description: In table XLV the cell at Hod (the eighth Sephirah, Mercury) carries a reference to 'Ezekiel' — pointing to the prophet's great chariot-vision in Ezekiel 1 (the four living creatures, the wheels within wheels, the throne of sapphire), one of the foundational visions of Western mysticism and the seed of the later Merkabah tradition. The placement at Hod fits: Mercury is the Sephirah of intellectual vision and form, the sphere in which the prophet's complex symbolic image is articulated. The entry preserves Crowley's pointer.

face.summary: The face, attributed to Aries, the foremost surface of the body.
face.description: The Face is attributed to Heh and Aries in the table of the Human Body. As Aries rules the head, so it governs the face—the foremost surface where the senses are gathered and the identity is shown. In medical astrology the complexion and features fall under the Aries-ruled head, the bold frontispiece of the body that meets the world first, fittingly assigned to the cardinal fire that begins the zodiac.

fai.summary: Fai — a letter of the Coptic alphabet (f), which Crowley attributes to 8 Hod.
fai.description: Fai is one of the Coptic letters drawn not from Greek but from Demotic Egyptian, added to the borrowed Greek alphabet to record sounds Greek could not write: it is the fai, a Demotic-derived letter for the f-sound. Crowley folds the Coptic alphabet into the great correspondence of letters and paths in 777 (Table LI), assigning Fai to 8 Hod on the Tree of Life, so that the Egyptian-Christian script takes its station among the Hebrew letters and the keys of the Tarot.
tables: LI. Names of the Coptic Letters

failure.summary: Seven of Disks — Failure / Success Unfulfilled; Saturn in Taurus, Netzach of Earth.
failure.description: The Seven of Disks, Failure (Success Unfulfilled), is Netzach in the suit of Earth and the third decan of Taurus under Saturn. The unstable seventh sphere, blighted by Saturn in fertile Taurus, lets growth wither: discs lie like leaden coins on a sickly, fruitless plant. It is the labour that yields nothing, promise blighted, the discouragement of work that fails to ripen.
tables: CXXXVI. Titles and Attributions of the Pantacle Suit
CL. Magical Images of the Decans (Succedent)

fairies.summary: The folk of the otherworld, set at Lamed — the airy, capricious people of legend.
fairies.description: The Fairies are an order of legendary beings, attributed to Lamed. The 'fair folk' or 'good people' of Celtic and European lore are the inhabitants of an otherworld bordering our own — beautiful, long-lived, capricious, and perilous to deal with, bestowing gifts and curses alike. As an order they figure the elusive, enchanted intelligences of nature's hidden side, the airy and uncanny presences that dwell just beyond the edge of the ordinary world.

faithful-intelligence.summary: The Twenty-second Path — the Faithful Intelligence of Lamed, increaser of spiritual virtues.
faithful-intelligence.description: The Twenty-second Path is the Faithful Intelligence (Sekhel Neeman), attributed to the letter Lamed and the sign Libra, the path of Adjustment (Justice) joining Geburah to Tiphareth. The Sepher Yetzirah says that by it the spiritual virtues are increased, and that all the dwellers upon earth are nearly under its shadow. Libra's balance is faithfulness made law: the Ox-goad of Lamed, the path of equilibrium and justice, holds the scales steady and true, increasing virtue by holding all things to their right measure.
tables: XIII. Paths of the Sefer Yetzirah

falsehood.summary: The Mercurial vice of falsehood, the deliberate marring of the truth.
falsehood.description: Falsehood is listed among the vices at Beth and Mercury, the path of the Magus and lord of the word. As the shadow of Mercury's truthful intelligence it is the spoken or wrought lie—the deliberate distortion of reality through the very faculty meant to reveal it. Crowley held the Magus to live perpetually under the curse that his every utterance is, in the end, a falsehood, since to speak is to bind the infinite into a partial word; the vice of falsehood is the willed and selfish form of that inescapable limitation.
tables: L. Transcendental Morality (10 Virtues; 7 Deadly Sins; 4 Magic Powers)

fan.summary: The implement of Air at Aleph—the fan that stirs and moves the air, the breath of the element made a tool.
fan.description: The Fan is attributed to Aleph, the path of the Fool and the element of Air, and it serves, alongside the Dagger, as an instrument of that element: where the Dagger cuts the air, the Fan moves and stirs it, setting the element into living motion. To wield the Fan is to command the breath and the wind, to set the airy power in flow. As Aleph is the first breath, the spirit moving, the Fan is the gentle implement that makes that movement felt. Esoterically the Fan is the magician's means of rousing and directing the element of Air—the subtle stirring of the breath and the mind, the implement that quickens the airy force into motion rather than dividing it as the blade does.

fargh-the-latter.summary: al-Fargh al-Mu'akhkhar, 'the latter spout' — the lower mouth of the Urn, in Pisces.
fargh-the-latter.description: al-Fargh al-Mu'akhkhar, 'the second (lower) spout' of the Urn (closing the Square of Pegasus toward Andromeda), is the mansion set in the path of Pisces (Qoph). Pouring the last of the heavenly waters toward the Fishes, it was reckoned a fortunate station for gain, for marriage, and for the prospering of voyages.
tables: CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon

fauns.summary: The goat-legged woodland spirits, set at Capricorn — wild revellers of field and forest.
fauns.description: Among the Legendary Orders of Being, the Fauns are attributed to Capricorn, the sign of the goat. They are the goat-legged spirits of Roman myth, akin to the Greek satyrs and to the god Pan — wild, lustful, half-animal denizens of the woods and pastures, embodiments of untamed nature and rustic fertility. Their attribution to Capricorn is exact, for that sign's emblem is the goat itself; they figure the instinctual, earthy life-force in its most uninhibited and pagan form.

tables: XCVIII. Parts of the Soul English

feeling.summary: The second skandha — feeling-tone (vedanā), the pleasant, painful or neutral colouring of experience.
feeling.description: Feeling is vedanā, the second of the five skandhas, attributed to the element Fire. It is not emotion but the bare affective tone that accompanies every contact of sense and object — the immediate registering of an experience as pleasant, painful, or neither. Vedanā is the hinge on which craving turns, for it is at the point of feeling that the untrained mind reaches toward the pleasant and recoils from the painful; to watch feeling arise and pass without grasping is therefore a master-key of insight. Its fiery attribution befits the quick, kindling quality of pleasure and pain.

feet.summary: The feet, attributed to Pisces, the last sign that governs the body's base.
feet.description: The Feet are attributed to Qoph and Pisces. In medical astrology Pisces, the twelfth and final sign, rules the feet—the lowest extremity, on which the upright body stands and moves. As Pisces closes the zodiacal round and dissolves all into the universal sea, so the feet are the body's humble end, the point of contact with the earth, fittingly assigned to the watery sign of completion.

fence.summary: Cheth — 'fence' or 'enclosure'; the warded field of The Chariot.
fence.description: Cheth means 'fence,' 'wall,' or 'enclosure' — a bounded, protected field. The guttural breath of the letter suggests an enclosing hedge, a place set apart and guarded. In Liber 777 Cheth is the path of The Chariot, attributed to Cancer, joining Binah to Geburah. The image is exact: the Charioteer rides within the warded enclosure of his crab-shell armour, bearing the Grail safely across hostile ground — the fenced sanctuary that protects the holy influence as it descends.
tables: III. Translation of the Names of the Paths

fertile-land-the-king-of-the-spirits-of-.term: Fertile Land. The King of the Spirits of Earth. 20° ♌ to 20° ♍
fertile-land-the-king-of-the-spirits-of-.displayTerm: Fertile Land. The King of the Spirits of Earth. 20° ♌ to 20° ♍
fertile-land-the-king-of-the-spirits-of-.summary: Golden Dawn title and dominion of the King/Knight of Disks, ruling 20° Leo–20° Virgo.
fertile-land-the-king-of-the-spirits-of-.description: ‘Fertile Land. The King of the Spirits of Earth. 20° ♌ to 20° ♍’ is the Golden Dawn (Book T) title and celestial dominion of the King of Disks (the Knight in the Thoth deck), the active head of the earthy suit. His full style is ‘Lord of the Wide and Fertile Land, King of the Spirits of Earth,’ and his rule spans the thirty degrees from Leo into Virgo. He embodies earth made productive—the husbandman of the broad acres, the steady, generative force that turns matter to harvest.
tables:
LXIV. The Court Cards of the Tarot, with the Spheres of 
their Celestial Dominion Pantacles.

fever.summary: Fever at Fire and Geburah — the burning heat of Mars and the elemental flame.
fever.description: Fever is set both at the path of Shin (Fire) and at Geburah, the Martial sphere of Severity. It is the most elemental of fiery disorders: the body's heat raised to a consuming burn, the signature of Mars and of the fire-element raging within. Medical astrology long held fevers to be Martial and choleric crises; esoterically the fever is Geburah's severity turned inward, the purging, dangerous fire that may either burn away corruption or destroy the vessel.

fiery-serpents.summary: Fiery Serpents — the English name of the angelic choir Seraphim, the host of Assiah at Geburah.
fiery-serpents.description: In the Qabalistic angelology each Sephirah commands its own choir of angels; “Fiery Serpents” (Table CI, the Angels of Assiah given in English) renders into the vernacular the Hebrew order Seraphim, the host attributed to Geburah. These are the Fiery Serpents, the burning ones who consume in righteous severity, the martial flame of the fifth sphere. Crowley sets them at Geburah on the Tree, where the choir gives angelic form to the energy of that sphere as it acts in Assiah, the world of action.

fig.summary: The sweet fruit of Venus and Jupiter—fertility and abundance, the leaf of Eden and the fruit of plenty.
fig.description: The Fig is attributed to Venus (Daleth, the Empress) and Jupiter (Kaph), twin powers of love and increase. Among the oldest of cultivated fruits, heavy with seeds and sweetness, it is an immemorial emblem of fertility, abundance, and ripe sexuality—its leaf the first covering of Eden, its fruit a byword for plenty and ease. Esoterically the fig is the generous, fruitful sweetness of Venus crossed with the expansive bounty of Jupiter, the tree under whose shade abundance is taken for granted.

fire.summary: The active, expansive element of heat, will, and transformation.
fire.description:
Fire is the element of energy, will, and transformation—hot and dry in the classical scheme, expansive and ascending by nature. In Liber 777 it is attributed to the Hebrew letter Shin and the path 31, to the Tatwa Tejas (a red triangle), and to the southern quarter. Its magical weapon is the Wand, its archangel Michael, its elemental king Djin, and its creatures the salamanders.

Across cultures Fire is the agent of purification and divine presence—the burning bush, the Promethean spark, the sacrificial flame that carries offerings upward. Psychologically it maps to drive, courage, and the spirited part of the soul; physically, to combustion and the radiant energy that powers life. In the magician’s work it represents the directed will that initiates change.
tables: CX. Elements and Quarters per the Sepher Yetzirah
CXXII. The Ten Plagues of Egypt
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

fire-opal.summary: The flame-coloured opal of Hod and Fire — iridescence kindled to flame.
fire-opal.description: The fire opal — the opal in its flame-orange and red — is attributed to Hod and to the path of Shin, elemental Fire: the iridescent Mercurial stone kindled into living flame, uniting the play of the intellect with the ardour of fire. It is the gem of brilliant, burning thought, splendour set alight.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

firmament.summary: Raqia, the Firmament at Hod — the second heaven, in which the sun, moon, and stars are set.
firmament.description: Raqia, the Firmament, is one of the seven heavens of the Talmud, attributed to Hod. It is the heaven in which the luminaries are fixed — the sun, the moon, the stars, and the planets are all set within the Firmament, the visible vault of the sky. As the heaven of the wheeling lights it answers well to Hod, the sphere of order, number, and measured motion.
tables: XCIV. The Heavens of Assiah English

fish.summary: The creature of the deep waters—Nun, whose very name means 'fish,' and the sign Pisces; the soul in the abyss.
fish.description: The Fish belongs to the watery, hidden paths—above all to Nun, the 24th path, whose Hebrew letter literally means "fish," and to Qoph and Pisces, the sign of the Fishes. It is the life that moves unseen in the deep, the soul submerged in the waters of the unconscious and of generation. The fish is an ancient emblem of fecundity and of the saviour who descends into the flood to preserve life—the Christian ichthys, the avatar Matsya of Vishnu drawing the ark through the deluge. Esoterically the Fish is consciousness immersed in the formless waters, silent and cold-blooded, the seed of spirit hidden alike in the great Sea of Binah and in the lower deep.
tables: III. Translation of the Names of the Paths

fish-hook.summary: Tzaddi — 'fish-hook'; the angle that draws up from the deep, path of The Star (or Emperor).
fish-hook.description: Tzaddi means 'fish-hook' — the barbed angle that reaches into the water to draw forth what is hidden below. It is associated also with the righteous one (tzaddik). In Liber 777 Tzaddi is attributed to Aquarius; following the secret of Liber AL ('Tzaddi is not the Star'), Crowley reassigns the trumps so that Tzaddi corresponds to The Emperor while The Star takes Heh — but the letter's place on the path joining Netzach to Yesod, and the Aquarian water-bearer pouring out the stream, keep the fishing image alive. The hook draws the soul up out of the waters of the unconscious toward the starlight above.
tables: III. Translation of the Names of the Paths

fishy.summary: 'The Fishy Ones'—the qliphothic order of Capricorn, the cold slipperiness of the goat-fish shadow.
fishy.description: In the Translation of the Orders of Qliphoth 'The Fishy Ones' is the averse order attributed to Ayin and Capricorn—the sign whose ancient emblem is the goat-fish. As the demonic shell of the path, it is the shadow of Capricorn's disciplined ambition: the cold-blooded, slippery, bottom-dwelling aspect of the sea-goat, the clammy and evasive nature that slides away from the light. It names the corruption of patient ascent into cold, slithering self-interest.
tables: CXXIII. Translation of the Orders of the Qliphoth

flames.summary: Flames — the English name of the angelic choir Ishim, the host of Assiah at Malkuth.
flames.description: In the Qabalistic angelology each Sephirah commands its own choir of angels; “Flames” (Table CI, the Angels of Assiah given in English) renders into the vernacular the Hebrew order Ishim, the host attributed to Malkuth. These are the Flames, the Ishim or “souls of fire,” the blessed human souls perfected and burning at the foot of the Tree, the choir of the Kingdom. Crowley sets them at Malkuth on the Tree, where the choir gives angelic form to the energy of that sphere as it acts in Assiah, the world of action.

tables: CXXIII. Translation of the Orders of the Qliphoth

flaming-fire.summary: The magical image of Amy — a flaming fire — Goetic President of the first decan of Scorpio (by night).
flaming-fire.description: Amy (Avnas), the fifty-eighth spirit of the Goetia and a great President, appears first as a flaming fire and afterward puts on the shape of a man. In 777 he is the nocturnal ruler of the first decan of Scorpio. He teaches the secrets of astrology and the liberal sciences, gives good familiars, and reveals treasures that are kept and guarded by spirits. The naked flame as a first form befits the hidden, intense fire of the watery Scorpion — the consuming power that both guards and discloses what is buried.

flies.summary: The Plague of Flies — the swarms upon Egypt, attributed to Netzach.
flies.description: The fourth plague, the swarms of flies that filled the houses of Egypt, is set in 777 at Netzach, the sphere of Venus. The attribution places the buzzing multitude in the sphere of nature's teeming, sensuous fecundity turned to affliction — desire and abundance soured into a plague.
tables: CXXII. The Ten Plagues of Egypt

flora.summary: Flora, goddess of flowers and spring — the blossoming power of nature, at Virgo.
flora.description: Flora is the Roman goddess of flowers, blossoming plants, and the fertile springtime, honoured in the joyous festival of the Floralia. Referred to Yod and Virgo, the sign of growing and ripening things, she is the delicate, generative power that clothes the world in bloom. As the spirit of flowering she embodies youth, beauty, and the brief, sweet abundance of the blossoming season.

fluxes.summary: Fluxes at Aleph and Air — flowing discharges under the moving, dispersing element.
fluxes.description: Fluxes — the old term for excessive flowing discharges of the body — are attributed to Aleph, the path of the element Air. Air is the element of movement, dispersion, and ceaseless flow; the fluxes are its restless mobility made morbid, the body unable to contain or stay its own currents. As a symbol they figure the dissipating, scattering power of Air when ungoverned, substance pouring away on every wind.

focalor.summary: The forty-first spirit of the Goetia, a winged duke of Taurus with power over winds and seas.
focalor.description: Focalor is the forty-first spirit of the Goetia, a great duke of the decans of Taurus. He has power over the winds and the seas: he drowns men and overturns warships, though he will do no harm if the operator forbids it. It is said he hoped to return to the order of the Thrones after a thousand years, though in vain. He appears as a man with the wings of a griffin. A spirit of the earthy sign, he is the master of storm and shipwreck.

foras.summary: The thirty-first spirit of the Goetia, a president of Aquarius who teaches the virtues of herbs and stones and grants long life.
foras.description: Foras is the thirty-first spirit of the Goetia, a mighty president of the decans of Aquarius. He teaches logic and ethics and the virtues of herbs and precious stones; he makes men witty, eloquent, invisible and long-lived, and discovers treasures and recovers things lost. He appears as a strong man in human shape. A spirit of the airy sign, he is the giver of learning, hidden virtue and length of days.

force.summary: Force — Crowley's parenthetical gloss for Prana at Binah in table XXII, the great life-energy as 'force.'
force.description: In table XXII ('Small Selection of Hindu Deities') the cell at Binah reads in essence 'Prana (Force),' giving the English meaning of the Sanskrit term beside the name. 'Force' is therefore Crowley's parenthetical translation — the energetic, undirected primal power that, in Tantric and Yogic cosmology, animates all life and is concentrated and directed through pranayama. As a glossary entry it preserves the qualifier as it appears in the source; the principal Prana entry carries the full description.
tables: XXII. Small Selection of Hindu Deities

formative-world.summary: The Formative World — Yetzirah, the world of the angels.
formative-world.description: The Formative World is Yetzirah, the third world — the realm of formation, where the creative ideas are shaped into the patterns of the angelic hosts and the astral forms. It is the world of the Son (the Vau of the Name) and, in 777's scheme, of the element Air: the formative, designing world that mediates between creation and matter.

forneus.summary: The thirtieth spirit of the Goetia, a sea-monster marquis of Capricorn who teaches tongues and wins good repute.
forneus.description: Forneus is the thirtieth spirit of the Goetia, a great marquis of the decans of Capricorn. He teaches rhetoric and languages, gives men a good name, and makes them beloved by their friends and even their foes. He appears in the form of a great sea-monster. A spirit of the earthy sign, he is the giver of eloquence and the maker of fair reputation.

fortuna-major.summary: Geomantic figure 'Greater Fortune' — attributed to the Sun; deep, lasting good fortune.
fortuna-major.description: Fortuna Major, the 'Greater Fortune,' is one of the sixteen geomantic figures, attributed to the Sun and associated with Leo. One of the most fortunate of all the figures, it signifies great and durable success, inner strength, and the good fortune that comes through one's own power and merit. It is the geomantic emblem of solar prosperity — fortune that is solid, honourable, and self-won.
tables: XLIX. Lineal Figures of the Planets, &c., and Geomany

fortuna-minor.summary: Geomantic figure 'Lesser Fortune' — attributed to the Sun; swift, outward, fleeting luck.
fortuna-minor.description: Fortuna Minor, the 'Lesser Fortune,' is one of the sixteen geomantic figures, attributed to the Sun and associated with Leo. It signifies success that is swift but fleeting, good fortune that comes from without or through others, and matters quickly accomplished but not always lasting. Favourable for speed and for affairs soon concluded, it is the lighter, more transient face of solar luck.
tables: XLIX. Lineal Figures of the Planets, &c., and Geomany

foundation.summary: Foundation—the ninth Sephirah; the lunar sphere of the astral, dreams, and the unconscious.
foundation.description:
Yesod (יסוד, ‘Foundation’) is the ninth Sephirah, the lunar reservoir through which all the higher forces are gathered and transmitted into the material world of Malkuth. It is the sphere of the Moon, of the astral light, of dreams, imagination, sexuality, and the tides of the unconscious. Its God-name is Shaddai El Chai, its virtue independence, its vice idleness; its image a strong and beautiful naked man.

As the ‘foundation’ of the perceptible cosmos, Yesod is the realm the practical magician works in most directly—the plastic, image-making layer where intention is shaped before it crystallises into physical fact. It is the gateway between the seen and the unseen.
tables: III. Translation of the Names of the Paths
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

freya.summary: Freya, goddess of love, beauty, and war — mistress of seiðr and the fallen, at Venus and Netzach.
freya.description: Freya is the great Norse goddess of love, beauty, fertility, gold, and war, mistress of the magical art of seiðr, who rides a chariot drawn by cats and claims half the battle-slain for her hall. Referred to Daleth and Venus and to Netzach, the sphere of Venus, she is the Norse counterpart of the goddess of love — at once sensuous, sorrowing, and fierce. She embodies desire, enchantment, and the passionate power of the divine feminine.

friendliness.summary: The Brahmavihāra of loving-kindness (mettā) — boundless goodwill toward all beings.
friendliness.description: Friendliness is mettā, the first of the four Brahmavihāras or 'divine abidings' of the Forty Meditations, attributed to the merciful sphere of Chesed. It is the deliberate cultivation of unconditional goodwill — wishing the welfare and happiness of all beings without exception, beginning with oneself and radiating outward until it embraces friend, stranger and enemy alike. As the 'sublime abode' of love it dissolves ill-will and warms the whole character; placed at Jupiter's merciful Sephira it is the expansive, benevolent heart made into a meditative discipline.

frigga.summary: Frigga, queen of the Aesir — the all-knowing mother and wife of Odin, at Binah.
frigga.description: Frigga is the Norse queen of the gods, wife of Odin, goddess of marriage, motherhood, and foreknowledge, who knows all fates though she speaks them not. Referred to Binah, the supernal Mother, she is the regal, prophetic maternal power of the Aesir, mistress of Fensalir. As the sorrowing mother of Baldr and the keeper of hidden destiny, she embodies the wise and loving sovereignty of the divine wife.

frogs.summary: The Plague of Frogs — the swarming of the waters, attributed to Yesod.
frogs.description: The second plague, the swarming up of frogs from the rivers, is set in 777 at Yesod, the foundation and the watery, lunar sphere of generation. The teeming amphibian multitude rising from the waters answers to Yesod's nature as the fertile, formative astral ground from which forms swarm into being.
tables: CXXII. The Ten Plagues of Egypt

full-insanity.summary: Total madness at the path of Spirit — the mind wholly unseated by the highest fire.
full-insanity.description: 'Full insanity' is placed at the path of Spirit (31 bis), the quintessence above the four elements. Where ordinary derangements are attributed to particular planets and signs, complete madness is set at the transcendent extreme — the total overthrow of the ordered mind by a force too great for it to contain. It is the shadow-side of the highest aspiration: the spirit's fire, entering an unprepared vessel, shatters reason altogether rather than illuminating it.

furcas.summary: The fiftieth spirit of the Goetia, a knight of Leo who teaches philosophy and the divining arts.
furcas.description: Furcas is the fiftieth spirit of the Goetia, a knight of the decans of Leo. He teaches philosophy, astrology and astronomy, rhetoric, logic, chiromancy (palmistry) and pyromancy (divination by fire). He appears as a cruel old man with a long beard and hoary hair, riding upon a pale horse and bearing a sharp weapon in his hand. A spirit of the fiery sign, he is the stern teacher of philosophy and of the arts of divination.

furfur.summary: The thirty-fourth spirit of the Goetia, a stag-formed earl of Pisces who raises storms and joins man and wife.
furfur.description: Furfur is the thirty-fourth spirit of the Goetia, a great earl of the decans of Pisces. He causes love between man and wife, raises thunder, lightning, blasts and great tempests, and gives true answers of secret and divine things — but only when commanded into a triangle, for otherwise he lies. He appears as a hart with a fiery tail, then, at command, takes angelic form and speaks with a hoarse voice. A spirit of the watery sign, he is the raiser of storms and the binder of marriage.

furies.summary: The Roman avengers of crime, set at Pe and Mars — the Dirae who scourge the guilty.
furies.description: The Furies are an order of legendary beings, attributed to Pe and the planet Mars — the Roman form of the Greek Erinyes, the Dirae who punish the wicked. Armed with whips and torches and crowned with serpents, they scourge the conscience of the murderer and the oath-breaker. Set at the Martial Tower-path, they figure the violent, shattering descent of justice — the punitive fury that strikes down false structures and exacts the wage of blood-guilt.

futility.summary: Seven of Swords — Futility; Moon in Aquarius, Netzach of Air: the undermined mind.
futility.description: The Seven of Swords, Futility (Unstable Effort), is Netzach in the suit of Air and the third decan of Aquarius under the Moon. The unstable seventh sphere lets the intellect waver: six swords overpower one small central blade, effort scattered and undermined by doubt. It is vacillation, the cunning that outsmarts itself, plans that come to nothing — the mind defeated less by force than by its own unsteadiness.
tables: CXXXV. Titles and Attributions of the Sword Suit.

fylfot-cross.summary: The whirling cross of Kether—the rotating rays of creation, the wheel of force radiating from the Crown.
fylfot-cross.description: The Fylfot Cross—the whirling, bent-armed cross or swastika—is attributed to Kether, the Crown, and it figures the radiation and rotation of the first creative force: the rays streaming and turning outward from the still point at the summit of the Tree, the wheel of becoming set in motion by the original impulse. Its bent arms show force not at rest but in dynamic spin, the turning of the cosmic wheel that pours manifestation outward from the centre. Its place at Kether marks it as the very motion of the first emanation. Esoterically the Fylfot Cross is the whirling power of origination—the creative force of the Crown depicted as eternal rotation, the radiant turning by which the One sends its light spinning out into all the worlds.

gaap.summary: The thirty-third spirit of the Goetia, a prince and president of Aquarius who carries men afar and teaches philosophy.
gaap.description: Gaap is the thirty-third spirit of the Goetia, a great prince and president of the decans of Aquarius, who appears when the Sun is in the southern signs. He makes men insensible or knowing, teaches philosophy and the liberal sciences, causes love or hatred, makes men go invisibly, carries them swiftly from kingdom to kingdom, and delivers familiars from the keeping of other magicians; he guides the four great kings. A spirit of the airy sign, he is the swift conveyer of bodies and the teacher of wisdom.

gafar.summary: al-Ghafr, 'the covering' — the lunar mansion at the hem of the Virgin, toward Libra.
gafar.description: al-Ghafr, 'the cover' or 'the veil' (faint stars at the Virgin's skirts), is the Mansion of the Moon set in 777 in the path of Libra (Lamed). A gentle, concealing station, it was reckoned favourable for the hiding and safekeeping of things, for goodwill, and for journeys — its mildness consonant with the airy balance of the Scales.
tables: CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon

gaia.summary: Gaia, the primordial Earth — the deep-breasted mother of all, at the place of Earth.
gaia.description: Gaia is the primordial Greek goddess of the Earth, the deep-breasted mother who arose at the beginning and brought forth the sky, the sea, and the first divine generations. Referred to the place of Earth in Malkuth, she is the very ground of being, the living body of the world from which all life springs and to which it returns. She is the oldest mother, the foundation beneath gods and mortals alike.

gain.summary: Nine of Disks — Gain / Material Gain; Venus in Virgo, Yesod of Earth: increase.
gain.description: The Nine of Disks, Gain (Material Gain), is Yesod in the suit of Earth and the second decan of Virgo under Venus. The nines bring the full strength of their suit, and Venus enriching the foundation of matter yields abundant increase: nine discs as great coins set with precious stones, wealth multiplied. It signifies profit, inheritance, and the secure enjoyment of material good fortune.
tables: CXXXVI. Titles and Attributions of the Pantacle Suit

galangal.summary: The warming root of the Sun—galangal, fiery and aromatic, a kindler of solar heat and vigour.
galangal.description: Galangal is attributed to the Sun (Resh). A pungent, warming rhizome of the ginger family, prized in cookery and in old charm-work alike, it carries the solar virtues of heat, vitality, and vigour, and was used in spells for strength, luck, and the kindling of confidence. Esoterically the galangal is the Sun's fire condensed into a root—warming, energising, the solar power taken inwardly as heat and courage.

galbanum.summary: The airy green resin of the holy incense—galbanum, sharp and lifting, perfume of the element Air.
galbanum.description: Galbanum is attributed to Air—to Libra and Aquarius and the airy paths. A pungent, green, balsamic gum, it was one of the four sacred spices of the Hebrew incense (with stacte, onycha, and frankincense), there to bind and lift the blend. Its sharp, fresh, rising quality marks it as a perfume of the mobile, intellectual element. Esoterically galbanum is the keen green breath of Air, the bitter note that gives the holy smoke its edge and its lift.

gamigina.summary: The fourth spirit of the Goetia, a marquis of Taurus who teaches the sciences and the fate of the dead.
gamigina.description: Gamigin (Samigina) is the fourth spirit of the Goetia, a marquis ruling in the decans of Taurus. He teaches the liberal sciences and gives account of the souls of those who died in sin and remain in purgatory, calling them up to answer the operator. He appears first as a small horse or ass, then in human form, speaking with a hoarse voice. As a spirit of the earthy sign he is the patient instructor and the summoner of the restless dead.

gamma.summary: Gamma — a letter of the Coptic alphabet (g), which Crowley attributes to the path of Gimel (Luna).
gamma.description: Gamma is a letter of the Coptic alphabet — the script in which the Egyptian language was written in the Christian era, the Greek alphabet adapted to Egyptian speech. It is from Greek gamma. Crowley folds the Coptic alphabet into the great correspondence of letters and paths in 777 (Table LI), assigning Gamma to the path of Gimel (Luna) on the Tree of Life, so that the Egyptian-Christian script takes its station among the Hebrew letters and the keys of the Tarot.
tables: LI. Names of the Coptic Letters

gamori.summary: The fifty-sixth spirit of the Goetia (Gremory), a duke of Libra in the form of a beautiful woman who wins love.
gamori.description: Gremory (here Gamori) is the fifty-sixth spirit of the Goetia, a strong and mighty duke of the decans of Libra. He tells of things past, present and to come, reveals hidden treasures and where they lie, and procures the love of women, both young and old, but especially of maidens. He appears as a beautiful woman with a duchess's crown girt about the waist, riding upon a great camel. A spirit of the harmonising air-sign, this duke wears a fair feminine form and bestows love and hidden wealth.

ganesha.summary: Ganesha, the elephant-headed lord of beginnings — remover of obstacles, at Yesod.
ganesha.description: Ganesha is the beloved elephant-headed god, son of Shiva and Parvati, invoked at the start of every undertaking as the remover of obstacles and the lord of beginnings. Referred to Yesod, the Foundation, he is the genial, wise guardian of thresholds and the patron of learning and prudence. Pot-bellied and broken-tusked, riding his mouse, he is at once a cosmic power and the most approachable of deities, smoothing the way for all who honour him.
tables: XXII. Small Selection of Hindu Deities

ganymede.summary: Ganymede, the cupbearer of the gods — the youth borne to heaven, at Aquarius.
ganymede.description: Ganymede is the beautiful Trojan youth carried off by Zeus's eagle to Olympus to serve as cupbearer to the gods, pouring out the nectar of the immortals. Referred to Tzaddi and Aquarius, the Water-Bearer, he is the very figure of that sign — the lovely youth who bears and pours the heavenly draught. Set among the stars as Aquarius, he embodies the ascent of mortal beauty into the divine company.

garden-of-delights-made-of-white-diamond.term: Garden of Delights Made of White Diamond
garden-of-delights-made-of-white-diamond.displayTerm: Garden of Delights Made of White Diamond
garden-of-delights-made-of-white-diamond.summary: A heaven of the Arabs at Netzach — the Garden of Delights, fashioned of white diamond.
garden-of-delights-made-of-white-diamond.description: Among the seven heavens of Islamic cosmology as tabulated in 777, the Garden of Delights (recalling Jannat al-Na'im, the Garden of Bliss), made of white diamond, is attributed to Netzach. It is one of the ascending paradises of the blessed, its substance the flawless white adamant — the heaven of pleasure and delight in the comparative scheme of the Arab heavens, set at the Venusian sphere of joy.
tables: CXXVIII. Seven Heavens of the Arabs, English

garden-of-eden.summary: A heaven of the Arabs at the lower Sephiroth — the Garden of Eden ('Adn).
garden-of-eden.description: Among the seven heavens of Islamic cosmology as tabulated in 777, the Garden of Eden (Jannat 'Adn, the Garden of Perpetual Abode) is attributed to Yesod and Malkuth. Shared in name and image with the Eden of Genesis, it is among the most blessed of the gardens of paradise; in the comparative scheme of the Arab heavens it is set at the earthward Sephiroth, the paradise nearest to the world.
tables: CXXVIII. Seven Heavens of the Arabs, English

garden-of-eternity-made-of-yellow-coral.term: Garden of Eternity Made of Yellow Coral
garden-of-eternity-made-of-yellow-coral.displayTerm: Garden of Eternity Made of Yellow Coral
garden-of-eternity-made-of-yellow-coral.summary: A heaven of the Arabs at Tiphareth — the Garden of Eternity, fashioned of yellow coral.
garden-of-eternity-made-of-yellow-coral.description: In the tabulation of the seven heavens of Islam, the Garden of Eternity (recalling Dar al-Khuld / Jannat al-Khuld, the Abode of Eternity), made of yellow coral, is attributed to Tiphareth. One of the ascending paradises of the blessed, its golden-coral substance and its name of everlastingness suit it to the solar heart of the Tree — the enduring garden of eternal life in the comparative cosmology of the Arab heavens.
tables: CXXVIII. Seven Heavens of the Arabs, English

garden-of-mansions-made-of-yellow-copper.term: Garden of Mansions Made of Yellow Copper
garden-of-mansions-made-of-yellow-copper.displayTerm: Garden of Mansions Made of Yellow Copper
garden-of-mansions-made-of-yellow-copper.summary: A heaven of the Arabs at Geburah — the Garden of Mansions, fashioned of yellow copper.
garden-of-mansions-made-of-yellow-copper.description: Among the seven heavens of Islamic cosmology as set out in 777, the Garden of Mansions (recalling Jannat al-Ma'wa, the Garden of Abode or Refuge), made of yellow copper, is attributed to Geburah. It is one of the ascending paradises of the blessed, the heaven of dwelling-places and refuge — the mansion-garden of the comparative Arab scheme, here aligned with the Martial sphere.
tables: CXXVIII. Seven Heavens of the Arabs, English

garden-of-paradise.summary: A heaven of the Arabs at Hod — the Garden of Paradise (Firdaus).
garden-of-paradise.description: In the tabulation of the seven heavens of Islam, the Garden of Paradise (Jannat al-Firdaus, the highest garden in Islamic tradition) is attributed here to Hod. Firdaus, the very word from which 'paradise' descends, names the loftiest and most blessed of the gardens; in 777's comparative scheme it takes its place among the ascending Arab heavens, set at the Mercurial sphere of splendour.
tables: CXXVIII. Seven Heavens of the Arabs, English

gates-of-death.summary: Sha'arei Maveth, the Gates of Death — a hell-compartment set at Netzach.
gates-of-death.description: Among the seven compartments of Gehenna, the 'Gates of Death' (Sha'arei Maveth) are attributed to Netzach. The name evokes the threshold spoken of in the Psalms, the very portals through which the soul passes out of life — one of the descending halls of the underworld, the gateway-region of the dead in the Qabalistic geography of the Hells.
tables: CVII. Ten Hells in Seven Palaces English

geburah.summary: Severity—the fifth Sephirah; martial strength, justice, necessary destruction (Mars).
geburah.description:
Geburah (גבורה, ‘Strength’ or ‘Severity,’ also Pachad, ‘Fear’) is the fifth Sephirah, the martial counterweight to the mercy of Chesed. It is the power that prunes, judges, and destroys what is corrupt so that the living may continue—severity in the service of justice. Its planet is Mars, its God-name Elohim Gibor, its image a mighty warrior in his chariot, its virtues energy and courage. Its vices are cruelty and wanton destruction.

In the architecture of the Tree, Geburah’s fierce discipline is not opposed to love but its necessary partner: without severity, mercy decays into indulgence. The Golden Dawn assigned it the burning of the dross, the surgeon’s knife of the spirit.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

gemini.summary: Mutable Air, ruled by Mercury—duality, communication, and exchange.
gemini.description:
Gemini, the Twins, is mutable Air ruled by Mercury—the sign of duality, communication, curiosity, and the restless play of mind. In 777 it corresponds to the letter Zayin and the path of the Tarot trump The Lovers (path 17). It governs all that comes in pairs and all that passes between them: language, learning, kinship, and the union (and tension) of opposites.

The Twins—Castor and Pollux, the mortal and immortal brothers—embody the great theme of the two who are one, the dialogue of self and other from which consciousness is born. Gemini’s gift is versatility and connection; its shadow, inconstancy and superficiality. It is the sign of the threshold and the messenger.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

generating.summary: Generating — the function of reproduction, attributed to Spirit (31-bis).
generating.description: Generation — the power of bringing forth new life — is referred in 777 to Spirit (the path 31-bis), the quintessence above the four elements. The attribution lifts the reproductive function above mere bodily appetite to the creative principle itself: the generative power as a reflection of the all-engendering Spirit.

genital-system.summary: The genital system, attributed to Venus and Capricorn, the body's organs of generation.
genital-system.description: The Genital System is attributed to Daleth and Venus, and to Capricorn. The organs of generation belong by nature to Venus, goddess of love and the generative act, the power of attraction and union by which life is renewed; their further attribution to Capricorn binds the creative fire to the structures of the body and the lineage of generations. They are the bodily seat of the force that perpetuates life, the meeting of desire and continuance.

geomancy.summary: The earthy art of divination by figures cast in earth, sand, or marked upon paper.
geomancy.description: Geomancy is attributed to Earth (32 bis), the element to which its very name—'earth-divination'—belongs. From a series of random marks the geomancer derives sixteen figures, each built of single and double points and assigned to the planets and signs, then reads their interaction across the houses of a chart. As the earthy counterpart of the airy tarot, it is a sober, mathematical oracle, much used in the medieval and Renaissance West, in which the patterns latent in matter are made to speak.

geranium.summary: The scarlet flower of Aries—the geranium, a small flame of Martian fire upon the path of the Emperor.
geranium.description: The Geranium is attributed to Aries (Heh, the Emperor), the cardinal fire-sign ruled by Mars. Its common scarlet bloom is a little flame, the red signature of fire and of the warlike, initiating energy of the Ram. Esoterically the geranium is the bright, ardent flower of beginnings—the fiery vigour of Aries flowering into colour, modest yet unmistakably aflame.

gerodiel.summary: Angel of the third face of Aquarius, where clever effort dissipates into futility.
gerodiel.description: Gerodiel presides over the closing decan of Aquarius (20–30°), where the Moon meets the Seven of Swords, *Futility* — unstable striving, designs that slip away half-grasped. The Moon's flux undermines Aquarian resolve. Gerodiel — its ‑el naming it a servant of God amid vain effort — is the angel of the lesson that some striving cannot hold, and must be released.

ghob.summary: King of the Gnomes, ruler of the elemental spirits of Earth.
ghob.description: Ghob (Gob) is the King of the Gnomes, the sovereign of the elemental spirits of Earth in the scheme systematised by Paracelsus and transmitted through Eliphas Lévi and the Golden Dawn. Where Paracelsus peopled each of the four elements with its own order of living beings, the magician of the later tradition invokes a single ruling intelligence over each: Ghob commands the gnomes, the patient, hidden folk of caverns, mines, roots, and treasure, the very life and consciousness of solid matter. He is summoned in the working of the Earth quarter — the cold, dry, northern element of Malkuth's foundation — and governs the gnomes who guard the secret riches of the ground. Esoterically he personifies the stabilising, in-gathering force of Earth: form, endurance, and the wealth locked within the dense world that the adept learns to call forth and command.
tables: LXII. Kings of the Elemental Spirits

ghosts.summary: The lingering dead, set at the Moon — revenants of the astral light who will not depart.
ghosts.description: Among the Legendary Orders of Being, the Ghosts are attributed to the path of the Moon. Universal across human cultures, they are the spirits of the dead who linger or return — shades bound to place or unfinished purpose, glimpsed in the half-light between the worlds. Their lunar attribution suits them, for the Moon governs the astral realm of phantasms and the reflected, shadowy light in which such apparitions take form; they are the residue of personality cast upon the screen of the astral, the dead not yet wholly gone.

ghouls.summary: The grave-haunting corpse-eaters, set at Saturn — desert demons that feed upon the dead.
ghouls.description: Among the Legendary Orders of Being, the Ghouls (Arabic ghūl) are attributed to Saturn, the planet of death, decay and the grave. In the lore of the East they are demons of the wastes and burial-grounds that devour the dead and waylay the lone traveller, shape-shifting predators of the desert night. As an order they figure the most degraded clinging to the material husk — the appetite that feeds on corruption itself — fittingly placed at the Saturnian sphere of dissolution and the tomb.

gift-of-tongues.summary: The Mercurial power of speaking and understanding all languages, divine and human.
gift-of-tongues.description: The Gift of Tongues belongs to Beth and Mercury, the path of the Magus, lord of speech, writing, and communication. As a magical power it is the loosing of the word so that one may speak with the eloquence of the gods, be understood across the barriers of language, and apprehend the meaning hidden in unknown tongues—an echo of the Pentecostal flame. Mercury, swift messenger between the worlds, governs every translation of thought into intelligible sound, and this is the crown of that art.

gihon.summary: One of the four rivers of Eden — the stream that 'compasseth the land of Cush.'
gihon.description: Gihon is one of the four rivers that flowed out of Eden to water the garden (Genesis 2), 'the same that compasseth the whole land of Cush.' In the Qabalistic tradition the four rivers of Paradise are read as the four elemental streams pouring from the supernal source into the world below, each carrying one quality of the descending life. Gihon thus figures one channel of the single river of grace as it divides into the manifold elements of creation.

gima.summary: Gima — a letter of the Coptic alphabet (ch/k), which Crowley attributes to 2 Chokmah.
gima.description: Gima is one of the Coptic letters drawn not from Greek but from Demotic Egyptian, added to the borrowed Greek alphabet to record sounds Greek could not write: it is the kyima, a Demotic-derived letter for a palatal sound. Crowley folds the Coptic alphabet into the great correspondence of letters and paths in 777 (Table LI), assigning Gima to 2 Chokmah on the Tree of Life, so that the Egyptian-Christian script takes its station among the Hebrew letters and the keys of the Tarot.
tables: LI. Names of the Coptic Letters

ginseng.summary: The man-shaped root of vitality—ginseng of Yesod, restorer of the vital and generative force.
ginseng.description: Ginseng is attributed to Yesod, the lunar Foundation, sphere of the vital and generative energies. Its forked, often man-shaped root has been prized for millennia in the East as the supreme restorative—tonic of vigour, longevity, and sexual power, the very life-force in vegetable form. Set at Yesod, the storehouse of the astral and vital currents, it is exactly placed. Esoterically the ginseng is the root of the foundation-life, the concentrated vitality that underlies and replenishes the body's strength.

girdle.summary: The belt of Netzach—the cingulum that girds the robe, binding the self for readiness and chastity.
girdle.description: The Girdle is attributed to Netzach, the Venusian sphere, and it is the belt or cord with which the magician girds his robe—the cingulum that binds the loose garment close, signifying readiness for action, self-containment, and the disciplined chastity that conserves the love-force rather than spilling it. To gird oneself is to prepare for the work, to draw the scattered self together. At Netzach, the sphere of nature and desire, the girdle's binding has a special force: it is the controlled and consecrated love-power. Esoterically the Girdle is the principle of self-collection and readiness—the binding that gathers the magician's energies, especially those of feeling and desire, holding them close and dedicated so that nothing is wasted before the work begins.

tables: CL. Magical Images of the Decans (Succedent)

glasyalabolas.summary: The twenty-fifth spirit of the Goetia, a president of Sagittarius — teacher of arts, author of bloodshed, giver of invisibility.
glasyalabolas.description: Glasya-Labolas is the twenty-fifth spirit of the Goetia, a mighty president and earl of the decans of Sagittarius. He teaches all arts and sciences in an instant, is named the author of bloodshed and manslaughter, tells things past and to come, wins the minds and love of friend and foe, and makes men invisible. He appears as a dog with the wings of a griffin. A spirit of the fiery sign, he joins swift learning with violence and concealment.

glun.summary: Lightning — the Nuctemeron genius of the eleventh hour presiding over lightning, set by Crowley at Aquarius.
glun.description: In the Nuctemeron — the “Day Illumined by Night” ascribed to Apollonius of Tyana and preserved by Éliphas Lévi — Æglun is numbered among the genii of the eleventh hour, the spirit of lightning. He commands the lightning, the thunderbolt and the sudden levin-flash. Crowley arranges the twelve hours and their genii upon the paths of the Tree (777, Table CLXXIII), placing him at Aquarius (Tzaddi).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

glutton-s-luck.summary: Glutton's Luck — the English meaning of the twentieth lunar mansion (Sa'd Bula), in Capricorn.
glutton-s-luck.description: 'Glutton's Luck' (or 'the Lucky Star of the Swallower') is the English gloss of Sa'd Bula (سعد بلع), the twentieth Arabic lunar mansion, marked by ε and μ Aquarii in the region where the Water-Bearer's flask pours toward Pisces. The Arabic 'Bula' carries the sense of one who swallows up or absorbs; traditional mansion-magic links the mansion to digestion, retention, and the absorptive faculties — luck through what one can take in and hold. Crowley places it at the Ayin/Capricorn path. See also: Sa'd al-Bal'a.
tables: CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon

gnawed-by-wild-beasts-corpse.summary: The contemplation of the corpse devoured by beasts — a cemetery meditation on dissolution.
gnawed-by-wild-beasts-corpse.description: This is the 'gnawed' stage (vikkhāyitaka) of the ten foulness-contemplations of the Forty Meditations, attributed to the path of Leo: the body torn and eaten by dogs, jackals, birds and worms. The meditator holds the image steadily, watching the form that was guarded and adorned in life given over to the appetites of beasts. As with the whole cemetery series, the contemplation is a calculated shock to craving and to the conceit of self — a reminder that the body is borrowed matter, soon returned to the cycle of consumption and decay.

gnomes.summary: The elementals of Earth, set at the path of Earth — the spirits of the deep ground and its treasures.
gnomes.description: The Gnomes are the elemental spirits of Earth in the order of the legendary beings, attributed to the path of the element Earth. In the Paracelsan doctrine of the four elementals they are the inhabitants of the solid ground — patient, secretive, treasure-keeping beings who move through rock and soil as we move through air, the living intelligence of the dense element. Esoterically they govern the realm of the body and the slow, fixed, fructifying forces of matter.

goat.summary: The goat of Capricorn—Pan and Baphomet, the climbing sure-footed beast of generative force and the 'Devil.'
goat.description: The goat is the proper beast of Capricorn, the path of the Devil (Ayin), and it carries the whole rich ambiguity of that card. It is the goat that climbs sure-footed to the highest, coldest peaks—aspiration and disciplined ascent—and at the same time the goat-god Pan, the horned lord of generative nature, and Baphomet, the misunderstood emblem of the reconciled opposites that the orthodox brand 'the Devil.' Lustful, vital, and untamable, the goat is the creative-sexual force of nature seen by the fearful as diabolic. Esoterically it figures the so-called darkness that is in truth the irrepressible life-power, the horned god whom the initiate learns to recognise not as the adversary but as Pan, the All.

god.summary: The supreme Being at Kether—the One beyond all the bestiary, the godhead at the crown of the Tree.
god.description: At the head of the table of living beings stands 'God,' attributed to Kether, the Crown—for above every beast, bird and fabulous creature is the One from which they all proceed. Kether is the first emanation, the point of pure being closest to the unmanifest, and the term here names not any image but the godhead itself, the supreme unity in which all the lower forms are contained as potencies. To place 'God' at the summit of the bestiary is to remember that the whole hierarchy of creatures is a single descending ray from this source. Esoterically it marks the highest reach of the scale, the divine Being toward which the entire ladder of life ascends and from which it first came forth.

god-the-3-in-1.summary: God the Three-in-One — the Trinity in unity, attributed to Kether.
god-the-3-in-1.description: 'God the 3 in 1' — the triune Godhead considered as a single indivisible unity — is placed at Kether, the Crown, the first and simplest point from which all multiplicity proceeds. The attribution renders the mystery of the Trinity as the supreme paradox of the Qabalah: the One that is yet a plurality, the monad that holds within itself the seed of the three supernals.
tables: XXXVI. Selection of Christian Gods (10); Apostles (12); Evangelists(4); and Churches of Asia (7)

god-the-farmer-s-friend.summary: The Christian God at Chesed — the benevolent provider, friend of the husbandman.
god-the-farmer-s-friend.description: Also at Chesed, the sphere of Jupiter's bounty, Crowley glosses the Christian God as 'the Farmer's Friend' — the kindly provider who blesses the harvest and watches over flock and field. Like the companion title 'Rain-Maker,' this is part of 777's deflationary comparative scheme, in which the single God is shown taking up the homely agricultural patronage once spread among many fertility deities. It rests on a true correspondence nonetheless: Chesed is mercy, generosity, and the gracious abundance that sustains the labouring world.
tables: XXXVI. Selection of Christian Gods (10); Apostles (12); Evangelists(4); and Churches of Asia (7)

god-the-father.summary: God the Father — the first Person of the Trinity, attributed to Chokmah.
god-the-father.description: In Crowley's table of Christian correspondences, God the Father is set at Chokmah, the second Sephirah and the supernal Father (Abba), the primordial Wisdom and the fountain of generative force. The attribution makes the Christian Father not the topmost Crown but the active, begetting principle just below it — the paternal Yod of Tetragrammaton, the seed of all that the lower Tree unfolds.
tables: XXXVI. Selection of Christian Gods (10); Apostles (12); Evangelists(4); and Churches of Asia (7)

god-the-healer-of-plagues.summary: The Christian God at Hod — the Mercurial physician, healer of plagues.
god-the-healer-of-plagues.description: At Hod, the Mercurial sphere of intellect and skill, Crowley casts the Christian God as 'the Healer of Plagues' — the divine physician, the office anciently held by Mercury-Asklepios and the healing gods with their serpent-staves. In the comparative logic of Table XXXVI the one God here takes up medicine and the curing of pestilence. The correspondence is exact, for Hod-Mercury rules healing, science, and the arts of remedy, the clever, ministering intelligence that contends with disease.
tables: XXXVI. Selection of Christian Gods (10); Apostles (12); Evangelists(4); and Churches of Asia (7)

god-the-holy-ghost.summary: God the Holy Ghost — the third Person of the Trinity, attributed to Hod and Yesod.
