god-the-holy-ghost.description: God the Holy Ghost is set toward the base of the Tree at Hod and Yesod — the spheres of Mercury and of the Moon, of intellect and of the formative astral foundation. As the Spirit who descends in tongues of fire and broods upon the waters, the Paraclete is fittingly attributed to the realms of communication, inspiration, and the generative astral substance through which the divine touches the world.
tables: XXXVI. Selection of Christian Gods (10); Apostles (12); Evangelists(4); and Churches of Asia (7)

god-the-rain-maker.summary: The Christian God at Chesed — the Jupiterian rain-giver and dispenser of bounty.
god-the-rain-maker.description: At Chesed, the merciful sphere of Jupiter, Crowley's distribution casts the Christian God as 'the Rain-Maker' — the bringer of fertilising showers, the very office the ancients gave to Jupiter Pluvius and the sky-fathers. The point of Table XXXVI is comparative: the monotheist deity, having absorbed all the gods, must here play the benevolent weather-lord, pouring down abundance upon the fields. The attribution is sound, for Chesed-Jupiter is the sphere of mercy, moisture, expansion, and gracious increase.
tables: XXXVI. Selection of Christian Gods (10); Apostles (12); Evangelists(4); and Churches of Asia (7)

god-the-son.summary: God the Son — the second Person of the Trinity, attributed to Tiphareth.
god-the-son.description: God the Son is placed at Tiphareth, the solar heart of the Tree and the natural seat of every sacrificed-and-risen god. The attribution is among the most fitting in 777: the Christ who dies and rises at the centre of the cosmos answers exactly to Tiphareth's symbolism of the redeeming, mediating Sun, the child of the supernals who reconciles the higher and lower worlds.
tables: XXXVI. Selection of Christian Gods (10); Apostles (12); Evangelists(4); and Churches of Asia (7)

gods.summary: Gods — the English name of the angelic choir Elohim, the host of Assiah at Netzach.
gods.description: In the Qabalistic angelology each Sephirah commands its own choir of angels; “Gods” (Table CI, the Angels of Assiah given in English) renders into the vernacular the Hebrew order Elohim, the host attributed to Netzach. These are the “Gods,” the Elohim, the radiant victorious hosts of Venus, the many splendours of nature's creative powers. Crowley sets them at Netzach on the Tree, where the choir gives angelic form to the energy of that sphere as it acts in Assiah, the world of action.

gold.summary: The incorruptible solar metal of Tiphareth — perfection and the goal of alchemy.
gold.description: Gold is the metal of Sol and of Tiphareth, the radiant centre of the Tree — the incorruptible, untarnishing metal whose perfection made it, for the alchemists, the very symbol of the perfected soul and the end of the Great Work. Its solar yellow, its resistance to all corrosion, and its preciousness mark it as the earthly image of the immortal, regenerate self. To 'make gold' was always, esoterically, to perfect the operator: the transmutation of base metal into gold is the transmutation of the unawakened human into the illumined adept of the solar heart.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

gold-crowned-soldier-in-red-on-a-red-hor.term: Gold-crowned soldier in red on a red horse. Bad breath
gold-crowned-soldier-in-red-on-a-red-hor.displayTerm: Gold-crowned soldier in red on a red horse. Bad breath
gold-crowned-soldier-in-red-on-a-red-hor.summary: The magical image of Berith — a red-clad soldier in a golden crown upon a red horse — Goetic Duke of the first decan of Capricorn.
gold-crowned-soldier-in-red-on-a-red-hor.description: Berith, the twenty-eighth spirit of the Goetia and a great and terrible Duke, appears as a soldier clothed in red, wearing a crown of gold and mounted upon a red horse. In 777 he governs the first decan of Capricorn by day. He turns all metals into gold, gives and confirms dignities, and answers truly of things present, past and to come — but he is a notorious liar, to be trusted only within the circle, and the grimoires warn of his foul breath. His blood-red regalia images the alchemical 'reddening' and the worldly ambition proper to the sign of Saturn's heights.

gonorrhea.summary: Gonorrhea at Daleth and Venus — the venereal corruption of the generative power.
gonorrhea.description: Gonorrhea is attributed to Daleth, the path of Venus, the planet that governs the generative organs and the act of love. The venereal diseases are read in this scheme as the corruptions of Venus — the sweetness of generation soured, the gateway of love become a channel of affliction. Symbolically it is the shadow of desire, the creative Venusian current turned to disease through its own misdirection.

gorgons.summary: The snake-haired, petrifying sisters, set at Vav — the face that turns beholders to stone.
gorgons.description: The Gorgons are an order of legendary beings, attributed to Vav. Of the three monstrous, snake-haired sisters — Stheno, Euryale, and the mortal Medusa — the gaze turns any who behold them to stone. Slain by Perseus with the aid of a mirror-shield, Medusa's severed head remained a potent apotropaic charm. As an order they figure the terror that paralyses, the dreadful aspect of the feminine and the fatal danger of the unguarded direct gaze upon the forbidden.

gorse.summary: The golden furze of the Sun—gorse, ever in bloom, a blaze of solar yellow upon the heath.
gorse.description: Gorse (furze) is attributed to Tiphareth, the solar centre. Its dense, spiny growth blazes nearly year-round with coconut-scented golden flowers—"when gorse is out of bloom, kissing's out of season," runs the old saying, for it is almost never wholly out of flower. This unfailing solar gold marks it as a plant of the Sun, of fertility and enduring warmth. Esoterically the gorse is the persistent solar fire of Tiphareth flowering even upon barren heath—gold that does not fail.

gout.summary: Gout at Jupiter and Pisces — the rich man's affliction settling in the foot.
gout.description: Gout is set both at Kaph (Jupiter) and at Qoph (Pisces), and the double attribution tells its whole story. Jupiter is its cause — the disease of plenty, of rich food and wine, the inflammation born of Jupiterian excess and surfeit — while Pisces, which rules the feet, is its seat, for gout classically strikes the great toe and the foot. It is mercy and abundance overindulged, settling at last as fiery pain in the body's lowest extremity.

grave.summary: Sheol, the Grave — the supernal-rooted name of the underworld in the sevenfold Hells.
grave.description: In the Qabalistic doctrine of the Seven Hells — the seven compartments of Gehenna, the descending purgatorial underworld answering to the seven heavens — the 'Grave' (Sheol) names the deepest and oldest conception of the abode of the dead, here rooted at the supernal triad. It is the pit, the grave, the silent gathering-place to which all flesh returns: the most ancient Hebrew name for the realm beneath, mouth of the cosmic descent into death.
tables: CVII. Ten Hells in Seven Palaces English

great-extreme-of-the-yi-king.term: Great Extreme of the Yi King
great-extreme-of-the-yi-king.displayTerm: Great Extreme of the Yi King
great-extreme-of-the-yi-king.summary: The T'ai Chi, 'Great Extreme' of the Yi King — the prime polarity, at the Veils of the Negative.
great-extreme-of-the-yi-king.description: The 'Great Extreme' (T'ai Chi) of the Yi King is the supreme ultimate from which, in the I Ching's cosmogony, 'the two modes' (Yang and Yin) are born, and from them the four images and the eight trigrams. Set in 777 at the Veils of the Negative, it answers to the moment when the undifferentiated absolute first stirs toward polarity — the cosmic seed of all division, the pregnant pause before the One becomes Two.

great-lion.summary: The magical image of Marbas — a great lion — Goetic President of the second decan of Taurus.
great-lion.description: Marbas (Barbas), the fifth spirit of the Goetia and a great President, appears first as a great lion and then, at the operator's command, in human shape. In 777 he is set at the second decan of Taurus by day. He answers truly of hidden and secret things, causes and cures diseases, gives wisdom in the mechanical arts, and changes men into other shapes. The royal lion rising from the earthy Bull marks the latent power and fixed strength of Taurus brought to its fullness in the sign's middle face.

great-strength.summary: Nine of Wands — Strength / Great Strength; Moon in Sagittarius, Yesod of Fire.
great-strength.description: The Nine of Wands, Great Strength, is Yesod in the suit of Fire and the second decan of Sagittarius under the Moon. The nines bring the full and balanced power of their suit, and here that power is fire tempered by long endurance: the wands are arrows tipped with sun and moon, force now wise, wary, and immensely strong. It is strength held in reserve, recovered from change and ready for the final test.
tables: CXXXIII. Titles and Attributions of the Wand Suit

greenish-turquoise.summary: The serpent-green stone of Nun and Death—turquoise tending to green, the colour of Scorpio's transformation.
greenish-turquoise.description: The greenish turquoise is attributed to Nun, the 24th path, the sign Scorpio and the trump Death (Atu XIII). Its colour is the key: not the clear sky-blue of the perfect turquoise but a turquoise tending toward green—the green of decay and regeneration, of the serpent and the still pool, of Scorpio's threefold mystery of death, putrefaction, and rebirth. A hydrated copper-aluminium phosphate, turquoise greens as it ages and absorbs the oils of its wearer, almost a living stone. Esoterically it is the talisman of the death-and-rebirth current, the gem that holds the very colour of dissolution turning toward new life.

guebres.summary: Guebres — the Zoroastrians, dwellers of Saqar in the Arab seven hells, set at Geburah.
guebres.description: 'Guebres' (Gabr) is the old term for the Zoroastrians or fire-worshippers of Persia. In the Arab cosmology of the seven hells they are the inhabitants of Saqar, set in 777 at Geburah, the sphere of Mars and severity. As with all the entries of this table, it preserves a polemical medieval scheme that assigned each religion its palace of fire — given here as historical cosmology, not as judgment.
tables: CXXVI. Inhabitants of the Seven Hells of the Arabs

gusion.summary: The eleventh spirit of the Goetia, a duke of Cancer who answers all questions and reconciles foes.
gusion.description: Gusion is the eleventh spirit of the Goetia, a strong and great duke of the decans of Cancer. He discerns things past, present and to come, answers all questions put to him, reconciles enemies and friends, and gives honour and dignity. He is described as appearing like a xenophilus — a baboon or dog-headed ape. A spirit of the watery sign, he is the conciliator and the giver of true counsel.

haagenti.summary: The forty-eighth spirit of the Goetia, a winged-bull president of Cancer who transmutes metals and waters.
haagenti.description: Haagenti is the forty-eighth spirit of the Goetia, a great president of the decans of Cancer. He makes men wise, instructing them in many matters, transmutes all metals into gold, and changes wine into water and water into wine. He appears as a great bull with the wings of a griffin, then in human form. A spirit of the watery sign, he is the wise alchemist and the transformer of liquids and metals.

haatan.summary: The concealing of treasures — the Nuctemeron genius of the sixth hour presiding over the concealing of treasures, set by Crowley at Virgo.
haatan.description: Haatan is the Nuctemeron genius of the concealing of treasures. That “Night-illumined Day”, ascribed to Apollonius of Tyana and handed down through Lévi's Transcendental Magic, sets a company of spirits over each of the twelve hours of the magical day, and Haatan belongs to the sixth hour. His province is the hiding of treasure, the burial of wealth from the eyes of men. In 777 (Table CLXXIII) Crowley redistributes these hour-genii across the zodiac, where this spirit falls at Virgo (Yod).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

hacked-in-pieces-corpse.summary: The contemplation of the dismembered corpse — a cemetery meditation on the body's dissolution.
hacked-in-pieces-corpse.description: The Hacked-in-Pieces Corpse is the cut-apart stage (vicchiddaka) of the ten foulness-contemplations of the Forty Meditations, set at the path of Libra. The meditator contemplates the body severed and scattered into its parts, the apparent unity of the living form revealed as a heap of separable pieces. The meditation dismantles the illusion of bodily wholeness and beauty, and with it the craving that fastens upon the body; it is one of the sterner medicines in the Buddhist pharmacopoeia of dispassion.

hades.summary: Pluto—death, regeneration, and the underworld power of transformation (modern planet).
hades.description:
Pluto, discovered in 1930, entered the symbolic system as the planet of death and regeneration, the underworld power that destroys utterly in order to renew—transformation at the deepest, most irreversible level. It is associated with the supernal reaches and the Abyss, and with the alchemical nigredo, the blackening that precedes rebirth.

As Hades–Pluto, lord of the dead and of hidden wealth beneath the earth, this power governs what is buried, repressed, and capable of resurrection. Its work is the forced confrontation with mortality and the shadow, from which—if survived—comes a profounder life. Its modern reclassification as a ‘dwarf planet’ has not displaced its potent symbolic role.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

hadit.summary: Hadit, the infinitely small point — the secret flame and core of motion in Thelemic cosmology.
hadit.description: Hadit is one of the three chief deities of Thelema's Book of the Law, the complement of Nuit: where she is infinite space, he is the infinitely condensed point, the secret centre, the flame in the heart of every star. Placed among the Veils of the Negative, he is the principle of pure being and motion hidden within all things — the spark of the self that goes, the point of view that experiences the infinite. Hadit is the indivisible core of individuality, the divine ember in the breast.

hadith.summary: Hadith, the secret centre — the point-self referred to the Crown, Kether.
hadith.description: Hadith is a variant form of Hadit, the winged point at the heart of all, here referred to Kether, the Crown and first emanation. As the infinitely small complement of infinite Nuit, he is the seed of being concentrated to a single point of fire — fitly placed at the summit of the Tree, the first stirring of self out of the unmanifest. The name marks the moment when the boundless contracts to a centre and the “I” awakens.

hagith.summary: Olympic Spirit of Venus, who bestows beauty, love, and the transmutation of copper into gold.
hagith.description: Hagith is the Olympic Spirit of Venus, set by Crowley at Daleth, the path of the Empress and of Venusian love and fertility. Following the gentle, generative nature of Venus, the Arbatel grants Hagith the power to make men fair and beautiful, to adorn them with grace, to transmute copper (the metal of Venus) into gold and gold back into copper, and to provide faithful familiar spirits. He governs upon the Day of Venus (Friday). Esoterically he is the spirit of attraction and harmony in the world of forces — the magnetic sweetness of Netzach and the green door of the Mother, the love that draws disparate things into union and clothes the world in desirable form.

hahab.summary: Royal tables — the Nuctemeron genius of the twelfth hour presiding over royal tables, set by Crowley at Pisces.
hahab.description: Hahab is the Nuctemeron genius of royal tables. That “Night-illumined Day”, ascribed to Apollonius of Tyana and handed down through Lévi's Transcendental Magic, sets a company of spirits over each of the twelve hours of the magical day, and Hahab belongs to the twelfth hour. His charge is the tables of kings, the royal banquet and its service. In 777 (Table CLXXIII) Crowley redistributes these hour-genii across the zodiac, where this spirit falls at Pisces (Qoph).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

hahabi.summary: Fear — the Nuctemeron genius of the third hour presiding over fear, set by Crowley at Gemini.
hahabi.description: Among the genii of the third hour in the Nuctemeron of Apollonius of Tyana, Hahabi presides over fear. He is the spirit of dread and terror, the cold grip that unmans the heart. Lévi gives the roll of the hour-genii in his Transcendental Magic; Crowley tabulates them along the paths of the Tree (Table CLXXIII), assigning Hahabi to Gemini (Zayin).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

hail.summary: The Plague of Hail — the fire and ice from heaven, attributed to Chesed.
hail.description: The seventh plague, the storm of hail mingled with fire that smote the land, is set in 777 at Chesed, the sphere of Jupiter. The mighty tempest descending from the sky — Jupiter's thunderbolt turned to judgment — fits the vast, sovereign, weather-ruling nature of the fourth Sephirah in its severe aspect.
tables: CXXII. The Ten Plagues of Egypt

halacho.summary: Sympathies — the Nuctemeron genius of the eleventh hour presiding over sympathies, set by Crowley at Aquarius.
halacho.description: Among the genii of the eleventh hour in the Nuctemeron of Apollonius of Tyana, Halacho presides over sympathies. He presides over sympathies and antipathies, the secret affinities and aversions between things. Lévi gives the roll of the hour-genii in his Transcendental Magic; Crowley tabulates them along the paths of the Tree (Table CLXXIII), assigning Halacho to Aquarius (Tzaddi).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

halphas.summary: The thirty-eighth spirit of the Goetia, a dove-formed earl of Aries who builds towers and arms men for war.
halphas.description: Halphas (Malthus) is the thirty-eighth spirit of the Goetia, a great earl of the decans of Aries. He builds up towers and fills them with weapons and ammunition, and sends men of war to appointed places. He appears in the form of a stock-dove (a wood-pigeon) and speaks with a hoarse voice. A spirit of the martial fire-sign, he is the builder of fortresses and the marshal of armed men.

hammemit.summary: The Hammemit, the unborn spirits — the not-yet-created host of souls, among the Veils.
hammemit.description: The Hammemit are, in Egyptian thought, the host of beings not yet born — the unmanifest souls and the “sun-folk” who dwell in potential before they come into being. Referred to the Veils of the Negative and to Scorpio, they represent the reservoir of unborn life, the seeds of existence waiting beyond the threshold of manifestation. They are the multitude that is, as yet, only the promise of creation.
tables: CXVI. Egyptial Attribution of Parts of the Soul

han-ah.summary: al-Han'a, 'the brand' — the lunar mansion of the Twins, in Gemini.
han-ah.description: al-Han'a ('the brand-mark,' the camel-brand), set among the stars of Gemini, is the mansion attributed in 777 to the path of Gemini (Zayin). Traditionally a station favouring journeys, the return of the absent, and the healing of the sick, its quick mercurial character belongs to the airy world of the Twins.
tables: CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon

hand.summary: Yod — 'hand'; the smallest letter, seed-flame of creation, path of The Hermit.
hand.description: Yod means 'hand,' specifically the closed or working hand — the instrument of action and making. It is the smallest letter, a mere flame-like point, yet the seed from which all the other letters are said to be drawn, and the first letter of the Tetragrammaton, the Father. In Liber 777 Yod is the path of The Hermit, attributed to Virgo, joining Chesed to Tiphareth. The Hermit's hand bears the lantern containing the hidden light: the small, fertile point of the Father's creative will, the seed-hand from which worlds proceed.
tables: III. Translation of the Names of the Paths

hanuman.summary: Hanuman, the divine monkey-hero — boundless devotion and strength, at Mercury and Hod.
hanuman.description: Hanuman is the monkey-god of the Ramayana, the mighty, leaping son of the wind who served Rama with perfect devotion, crossing the ocean and burning Lanka. Referred to Beth and Mercury and to Hod, he embodies agile strength, eloquence, and selfless service — the swift, clever, faithful servant of the divine. His prodigious feats and humble loyalty make him a beloved emblem of devotion that knows no limit.
tables: XXII. Small Selection of Hindu Deities

happiness.summary: Nine of Cups — Happiness / Material Happiness; Jupiter in Pisces, Yesod of Water.
happiness.description: The Nine of Cups, Happiness, is Yesod in the suit of Water and the second decan of Pisces, blessed by Jupiter. The nines bring the full strength of their suit, and water made jovial overflows in nine cups arranged in perfect order, each brimming — the very picture of contentment and emotional plenty. It is the 'wish card' of the deck, the abundance of feeling that satisfies completely.
tables: CXXXIV. Titles and Attributions of the Chalice Suit
CXLIX. Magical Images of the Decans (Ascendent)

harpies.summary: The snatching wind-spirits, set at Lamed — winged hags of storm and plunder.
harpies.description: The Harpies are an order of legendary beings, attributed to Lamed. In Greek myth they are the winged, foul, woman-faced spirits of sudden storm-winds who snatch away food and people and leave their stench behind — the 'snatchers' who tormented the blind seer Phineus. As an order they figure the rapacious, defiling forces of the air, the violent gusts that seize and carry off, the predatory aspect of the wind.

harpocrates.summary: Harpocrates, Horus the Child — the god of silence and inviolate innocence.
harpocrates.description: Harpocrates is the Greek name for Hor-pa-khered, Horus the Child, depicted as an infant with finger to lips — taken by later mystics as the god of silence and secrecy. Placed among the Veils of the Negative, he is the innocent, self-sufficient babe enclosed in the lotus, the inmost spirit untouched by the world. In magic he is the Lord of Silence, the still centre and the protected child whose very speechlessness is a sign of the inexpressible mystery.

hart-with-fiery-tail.summary: The magical image of Furfur — a hart with a tail of fire — Goetic Earl of the first decan of Pisces.
hart-with-fiery-tail.description: Furfur, the thirty-fourth spirit of the Goetia and a great Earl, appears as a hart or deer with a fiery tail, and will also take the form of an angel. In 777 he is set at the first decan of Pisces by day. He speaks falsely unless compelled into the triangle, where he gives true answers of secret and divine things, raises love between man and wife, and stirs up storms, thunder and lightning. The flaming-tailed deer — a swift water-creature crowned with fire — images the volatile, dreaming sign of the Fishes touched by hidden lightning.

tables: XCV. Contents of the Heavens of Assiah

hashish.summary: The resin of cannabis, attributed to Chokmah; Crowley's chosen aid to mystic vision.
hashish.description:
Hashish — the concentrated resin of Cannabis — is placed at Chokmah, the sphere of pure outgoing force and the first flash of wisdom. Crowley devoted an entire essay, 'The Psychology of Hashish' (written as Oliver Haddo), to its use as a controlled aid to the analysis of consciousness, prized for the way it loosens the habitual structures of the mind and lets the magician observe the machinery of thought itself. In the Sufi and Indian traditions it has a long sacramental history as an aid to absorption and devotion. Esoterically it figures the volatilising of the fixed — the dissolving of ordinary perception so that the underlying flux may be seen.

It must be said plainly: cannabis is a psychoactive drug with real cognitive and, for some, psychological risks, and its possession is illegal in many jurisdictions. This entry is historical and symbolic; it is not an endorsement or instruction for use.
hashish.caution: Psychoactive; legal status varies; risk of psychological dependence and acute anxiety/psychosis in susceptible people. Historical/symbolic entry only — not advice for use.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

hathoor.summary: Hathoor (Hathor), goddess of love and joy — the heavenly cow of Venus, at Daleth.
hathoor.description: Hathoor is Hathor in the aspect most strongly attributed to Daleth and Venus, the sphere of Netzach, and the merciful Chesed: goddess of love, beauty, music, and joy. The cow-horned lady who suckles the gods and welcomes the dead, she is the very type of feminine grace and abundant pleasure. As the Egyptian Venus she presides over delight, fertility, and the arts, pouring out the sweetness of life.

hathor.summary: Hathor, the sky-cow and lady of the West — goddess of love, music, and the welcoming dead.
hathor.description: Hathor is one of the greatest Egyptian goddesses, the celestial cow whose body is the sky, mistress of love, music, dance, and drunken joy, and the gentle receiver of souls into the West. Her many attributions in Liber 777 — to the Moon, to Venus, to Water, and to the Sun — reflect her vast and shifting nature, at once heavenly mother, solar eye, and goddess of pleasure. Sistrum in hand, she is the divine power of beauty that gladdens both the living and the dead.

hati.summary: Hati — the physical, instinctive heart, attributed to Yesod.
hati.description: The Hati is the heart in its bodily, vital aspect — distinguished in the Egyptian scheme from the Ab/Aib as the physical organ and seat of instinctive life. Referred in 777 to Yesod, the foundation and the sphere of the vital, formative life, it is the animal heart beneath the moral heart, the engine of the body's vitality.
tables: CXVI. Egyptial Attribution of Parts of the Soul

hatiphas.summary: Attire — the Nuctemeron genius of the sixth hour presiding over attire, set by Crowley at Virgo.
hatiphas.description: Among the genii of the sixth hour in the Nuctemeron of Apollonius of Tyana, Hatiphas presides over attire. He presides over dress and apparel, the clothing and array of the body. Lévi gives the roll of the hour-genii in his Transcendental Magic; Crowley tabulates them along the paths of the Tree (Table CLXXIII), assigning Hatiphas to Virgo (Yod).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

hatred.summary: The fifth fetter — ill-will (paṭigha / vyāpāda), aversion and the impulse to harm.
hatred.description: Hatred is paṭigha or ill-will (vyāpāda), the fifth of the ten fetters, attributed to Geburah, the severe sphere of Mars. It is aversion in all its forms — anger, resentment, the impulse to reject and to harm — the dark counterpart of sensual craving, reaching away from rather than toward. Like kāma-rāga it is weakened by the once-returner and destroyed by the non-returner. Its placement at Geburah, the burning sphere of severity and destruction, makes it the fetter of the wrathful, sundering force when turned to its lower, unredeemed expression.

haures.summary: The sixty-fourth spirit of the Goetia (Flauros), a leopard-formed duke of Capricorn who burns enemies and guards against spirits.
haures.description: Flauros (here Haures) is the sixty-fourth spirit of the Goetia, a great duke of the decans of Capricorn. He gives true answers of things past, present and to come; if commanded into a triangle he will speak truly of the creation, of divinity and of the fall of the spirits, and he will destroy and burn the operator's enemies and defend him against other spirits. He appears as a terrible leopard, then as a man with fiery, flaming eyes. A spirit of the earthy sign, he is the burner of foes and the guardian against hostile spirits.

haven.summary: Dignity — the Nuctemeron genius of the first hour presiding over dignity, set by Crowley at Aries.
haven.description: In the Nuctemeron — the “Day Illumined by Night” ascribed to Apollonius of Tyana and preserved by Éliphas Lévi — Haven is numbered among the genii of the first hour, the spirit of dignity. He confers rank and honour, the bearing of high office and the respect that attends it. Crowley arranges the twelve hours and their genii upon the paths of the Tree (777, Table CLXXIII), placing him at Aries (Heh).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

having-two-stars-on-his-brow.term: having two stars on his brow
having-two-stars-on-his-brow.displayTerm: having two stars on his brow

hawiyah.summary: Hawiyah — the bottomless abyss, deepest of the Arab hells, attributed to the supernals.
hawiyah.description: Al-Hawiyah, 'the abyss' or 'the bottomless pit,' is the seventh and deepest of the hells of Arab cosmology — the most terrible gate, reserved in the tradition for the hypocrites. Crowley sets it, by the customary inversion of the hellish with the divine, at the three supernal Sephiroth: the lowest hell mirroring the highest heaven, the bottomless depth answering to the boundless Crown.
tables: CXXV. Seven Hells of the Arabs

hawk.summary: The solar falcon of Kether—the hawk of Ra and Horus, the highest-flying eye of the divine sun.
hawk.description: The hawk is attributed to Kether, the Crown, and it is the falcon of Ra and of Horus, the great solar bird of Egypt that flies highest and gazes unflinching into the sun. Crowned upon the heads of the sky-gods, the hawk is the far-seeing divine vision and the swift descent of celestial power, the bird whose station is the very summit of heaven. Its placement at Kether marks it as the loftiest of the winged creatures, nearest the source of light. Esoterically the hawk figures the soaring spirit that returns to its origin and the all-seeing eye of the godhead, the solar majesty looking down from the crown of the Tree upon all that has come forth from it.

hazel.summary: The tree of hidden wisdom—the hazel of the Moon, whose nuts feed the Salmon of Knowledge and whose wand divines water.
hazel.description: The Hazel is attributed to the Moon (Gimel, the High Priestess). In Celtic lore its nuts dropping into the sacred well fed the Salmon of Knowledge, and whoever ate that fish gained all wisdom; the forked hazel rod is the classic instrument of the dowser, sensitive to hidden water and unseen veins. Both lore and use mark it lunar—the tree of intuition, divination, and concealed knowing. Esoterically the hazel is the wand of the secret wisdom of Gimel, the lunar faculty that senses what lies hidden beneath the surface.

he.summary: He — a letter of the Coptic alphabet (è/u), which Crowley attributes to the path of Vav (Taurus).
he.description: He is a letter of the Coptic alphabet — the script in which the Egyptian language was written in the Christian era, the Greek alphabet adapted to Egyptian speech. It is from Greek (the upsilon-derived sign). Crowley folds the Coptic alphabet into the great correspondence of letters and paths in 777 (Table LI), assigning He to the path of Vav (Taurus) on the Tree of Life, so that the Egyptian-Christian script takes its station among the Hebrew letters and the keys of the Tarot.
tables: LI. Names of the Coptic Letters

he-covered-his-faces-with-with-two-he-co.term: he covered his faces: with with two he covered
he-covered-his-faces-with-with-two-he-co.displayTerm: he covered his faces: with with two he covered
tables: XCII. The Angelic Functions in the World of Yetzirah

head.summary: The head, attributed to Aries, the first sign that governs the summit of the body.
head.description: The Head is attributed to Heh and Aries (and to the solar Resh). In medical astrology Aries, the first sign, rules the head and face—the topmost and foremost part of the body, the seat of the senses and of the directing will. As Aries is cardinal fire, the pioneering thrust of the zodiac, so the head leads the body into the world, the crown of the physical frame answering to the beginning of the zodiacal round.
tables: III. Translation of the Names of the Paths

hearing.summary: The sense classically borne by Spirit/Akasha — the perception of sound.
hearing.description: Hearing is the sense traditionally attributed to Akasha, the element of Spirit or aether, in the Tattvic doctrine of the five senses. Because Akasha is held to be the very matrix and vehicle of sound, the ear is the organ that perceives its quality, and of the five senses hearing is reckoned the most subtle — the faculty by which the vibrating Word is received and by which the inner sound (nada) is sought in meditation.

heart.summary: The heart, solar centre of the body, attributed to Leo and the life-giving Sun.
heart.description: The Heart is attributed to Leo (and to Chesed and Geburah), the sign the whole tradition of medical astrology assigns to it. As the Sun rules Leo, so the heart is the solar organ of the body—the central fire from which the warmth of life is pumped to every member, the seat of vitality and, symbolically, of courage and love. It is the bodily analogue of Tiphareth, the harmonising heart of the Tree: the radiant centre on which the health of the whole organism depends.

heart-lesions.summary: Lesions of the heart at Tiphareth — affliction at the solar centre of the body.
heart-lesions.description: Heart lesions are placed at Tiphareth, the solar heart of the Tree, which in the body answers to the heart itself and to the life-giving Sun. Tiphareth is the centre of harmony and vitality; an injury to the heart is therefore the gravest of bodily disorders, a wound at the very seat of the integrating, radiant life-force. Esoterically it figures damage to the central self, the solar core around which the whole organism is ordered.

heavy-odours.summary: The heavy odours of Earth—dense, grounding scents that weigh upon the senses and root the soul in matter.
heavy-odours.description: "Heavy odours" are attributed to the element Earth (32 bis). Dense, lingering, and weighty—the deep musks, the thick resins, the smell of rich soil and damp stone—these are the perfumes that settle and ground, drawing the attention down into the body and the material world. Esoterically the heavy odours are the olfactory weight of Earth itself, the grounding scents that anchor consciousness in form, the gravity of matter made fragrance.

hecate.summary: Hecate, goddess of the crossroads and the dark moon — chthonic queen of witchcraft, at Binah.
hecate.description: Hecate is the chthonic goddess of the moon's dark face, of crossroads, ghosts, and sorcery, here referred to Binah and to Cancer. Torch-bearing and triple-formed, she walks the boundaries between the living and the dead and holds the keys to the underworld. As a power of the Great Mother in her terrible aspect, she presides over night, magic, and the hidden tides; witches and necromancers have ever called upon her at the dark of the moon.
tables: CLXIX. Egyptian Gods of the Zodiac (Succedent)

heels.summary: Design detail of the Magician (Beth): the winged heels of Mercury.
heels.description: ‘Heels’ is a fragment of Liber 777's design for Atu I, the Magician—‘A fair youth with winged helmet and heels.’ The winged heels (the *talaria* of Hermes-Mercury) are the classic emblem of the messenger-god's speed, the power to travel instantly between heaven, earth, and underworld. On the Magician they signify that the creative intelligence is never static: will, once focused, moves with the quickness of thought, carrying the word of power wherever it is sent.
tables: CLXXXI. Correct Design of Tarot Trumps

height.summary: One of the six directions of space in the Sefer Yetzirah — the dimension of above.
height.description: Height is one of the six directions, or 'depths,' of space set out in the Sefer Yetzirah. In that early Qabalistic cosmology the world is stretched out in six dimensions — height and depth, east and west, north and south — each sealed by a permutation of the divine Name about the central Temple. Height marks the upward extension of the created order, the dimension reaching from the central point toward the above.
tables: CX. Elements and Quarters per the Sepher Yetzirah

heiglot.summary: Snow-storms and tempests — the Nuctemeron genius of the first hour presiding over snow-storms and tempests, set by Crowley at Aries.
heiglot.description: Heiglot is the Nuctemeron genius of snow-storms and tempests. That “Night-illumined Day”, ascribed to Apollonius of Tyana and handed down through Lévi's Transcendental Magic, sets a company of spirits over each of the twelve hours of the magical day, and Heiglot belongs to the first hour. He commands the winter storm, the driving snow and the violence of cold weather. In 777 (Table CLXXIII) Crowley redistributes these hour-genii across the zodiac, where this spirit falls at Aries (Heh).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

hekar.summary: Heqet, the frog-headed goddess of the Nile flood and of birth, attributed to the watery path of Mem.
hekar.description: Hekar is a form of Heqet (Heqat, Heket), the frog-headed Egyptian goddess of the inundation, of fertility, and of the moment of birth, who in the creation myth breathed life into the bodies the potter-god Khnum shaped on his wheel. Liber 777 places her at Mem, the Mother-letter of elemental Water—fitting for a deity of the life-giving flood and of the amniotic waters of generation. The frog, swarming in multitudes with the rising Nile, made her an emblem of teeming, watery life and of resurrection, and she was numbered among the primordial powers of the deep.

hekate.summary: Hekate, triple goddess of the crossroads — torch-bearing queen of magic and the moon.
hekate.description: Hekate is the Greek goddess of crossroads, boundaries, magic, ghosts, and the moon's dark phase, often shown three-formed, bearing torches and keys. Referred to Gimel and the Moon, she is the liminal power who stands at the meeting of three ways, guardian of thresholds between the worlds and patroness of witchcraft. Invoked at night and at the crossroads, she holds the keys to the underworld and to the hidden arts.

helios.summary: Helios, the sun itself made god — the all-seeing charioteer of the day, at the Sun.
helios.description: Helios is the Greek god who is the sun in person, driving his fiery four-horse chariot across the sky from dawn to dusk and seeing all things below. Referred to Resh and the Sun, he is the unmediated solar disk, the brilliant eye of heaven before whom nothing is hidden. Distinct from Apollo's cultivated radiance, Helios is the raw celestial fire itself, the burning wheel of the day.

heliotrop.summary: The sun-turning flower—heliotrope of Sol, whose face follows the light in unbroken devotion.
heliotrop.description: The Heliotrope is attributed to the Sun (Resh)—its very name, "sun-turning," declares it, for like the sunflower it orients its bloom toward the moving light. Sweetly scented and solar by nature, it signifies devotion, faithful turning, and the warmth of the Sun made fragrant. Esoterically the heliotrope is the soul's constant facing toward its source: the small flower that, like the great luminary it loves, teaches adoration by ceaseless turning to the light.

helitomenos.summary: Presiding god of the middle decan of Taurus, the lunar heart of fixed earth where effort ripens into success.
helitomenos.description: Helitomenos is the presiding god 777 assigns to the middle decan of Taurus (10°–20°), the heart of fixed earth. The Moon rules this face and it bears the Six of Disks—Success—the equilibrium in which material effort is rewarded and the Bull's fertility ripens into visible gain. The name, with its Hellenic ring, belongs to the Greco-Egyptian roster of decan-rulers: the thirty-six faces by which the old astronomer-priests divided the sky.
tables: CLXIX. Egyptian Gods of the Zodiac (Succedent)

hell.summary: Gehinnom, Hell itself — the underworld in the sevenfold scheme, set at the lower Sephiroth.
hell.description: 'Hell' (Gehinnom) gives its very name to the doctrine of the seven Hells, attributed here to the lower Sephiroth of Yesod and Malkuth. Derived from the Valley of Hinnom outside Jerusalem, a place of ancient idolatrous sacrifice that became the type of the place of punishment, Gehinnom is the purgatorial underworld of Qabalistic and Talmudic tradition — the comprehensive name for the descending realm of the dead and its sevenfold halls.
tables: CVII. Ten Hells in Seven Palaces English
XCV. Contents of the Heavens of Assiah

hellebore.summary: The dark poison-flower of Saturn—black hellebore, ancient purge of madness, both medicine and bane.
hellebore.description:
The Hellebore is attributed to Saturn (Tav, the Universe). The black hellebore—the "Christmas rose"—and its kin were the classic ancient remedy for madness and melancholy, those saturnine afflictions, even as the plant is itself a violent poison; Saturn's signature of death, severity, and the cure that borders on the lethal is written all through it. Esoterically the hellebore is the saturnine medicine of the depths, the dark flower that purges the spirit of its madness at the very edge of death.

Caution: hellebore is a powerful poison affecting the heart. This entry is symbolic and historical and is in no way advice for use.
hellebore.caution: Powerful cardiac poison. Symbolic/historical entry only — never handle or ingest.

heptagram.summary: The seven-pointed star — attributed to Venus; the Star of Babalon.
heptagram.description: The heptagram, the seven-pointed star, is attributed by its number to the sphere of Venus. In the Thelemic tradition it is the Star of Babalon, the septagram of the Scarlet Woman, sacred to the goddess of love and the seven classical planets together. As the figure of seven it gathers the planetary powers into a single emblem of beauty and desire, the seal of the Venusian mysteries.
tables: XLIX. Lineal Figures of the Planets, &c., and Geomany

herb-mercury.summary: The herb of Mercury—Mercurialis, the plant that bears the quicksilver god's own name upon the path of Beth.
herb-mercury.description: Herb Mercury (Mercurialis) is attributed, as its name declares, to Mercury (Beth, the Magus). An ancient pot-herb and physic-plant dedicated to Hermes, it carries by name and old association the mercurial virtues of communication, cleverness, and the swift, dividing intellect. Esoterically it is the green signature of the Magus's planet—the herb of Mercury standing for the quick, articulate mind that names and divides the world.

here.summary: Heré (Hera), queen of the Olympian gods — the sovereign wife and mother, at Binah.
here.description: Heré is Hera, queen of the Greek gods, wife and sister of Zeus, goddess of marriage, women, and the sovereignty of heaven. Referred to Binah, the supernal Mother, and to the path of Taurus, she is the regal, formidable feminine power — the enthroned queen whose dignity and jealousy alike are legendary. As the goddess of wedlock and the matron of Olympus she embodies the majesty and the binding authority of the divine wife.

hermanubis.summary: Hermanubis, the union of Hermes and Anubis — the psychopomp of Yesod.
hermanubis.description: Hermanubis is the Graeco-Egyptian fusion of Hermes and Anubis, combining the Greek guide of souls with the Egyptian jackal-lord of the dead into a single psychopomp. Placed at Yesod, the lunar Foundation and gateway of the astral world, he conducts souls across the threshold between the living and the dead, between the material and the unseen. He embodies the office of the divine messenger who alone may pass freely between the worlds.

hermaphrodite.summary: The androgyne of Hod—the alchemical Rebis, child of Hermes and Aphrodite, the two sexes made one.
hermaphrodite.description: The hermaphrodite is attributed to Hod, the Mercurial sphere, and it is the figure of the reconciled sexes—Hermaphroditus, the child of Hermes and Aphrodite in whom male and female were fused into a single body. In alchemy this is the Rebis, the 'double thing,' the crowned androgyne that is the goal of the conjunction, the union of Sol and Luna, sulphur and mercury, in one perfected form. Its place at Hod, the seat of Mercury and of intellectual magic, is exact, for Mercury is the very principle that joins the opposites. Esoterically the hermaphrodite figures the wholeness beyond duality, the integrated being in whom the warring polarities are at last made one—the alchemical perfection toward which the Work tends.

hermaphroditic.summary: The hermaphrodite at the Crown—the primal androgyne in whom Sol and Luna are one.
hermaphroditic.description: In the Alchemical Tree of Life the hermaphroditic principle is set at Kether, the Crown. The Rebis, the alchemists' two-headed androgyne uniting the solar king and lunar queen, is the emblem of the original unity that precedes all division into opposites—male and female, fire and water, active and passive—still gathered in a single undifferentiated being. Placed at the summit of the Tree, it figures the primordial wholeness of the Crown, in which every pair of contraries is contained, unmanifest, before the lightning-flash splits them into the manifold worlds.

hermes.summary: Mercury—intellect, language, magic, and exchange; ruler of Hod and the path of Beth.
hermes.description:
Mercury is the planet of mind, speech, commerce, and magic—the swift messenger and trickster who crosses every boundary. In 777 it rules the eighth Sephirah Hod and the path of Beth (the Tarot trump The Magus), and is the very patron of the magician’s art of names and signs. Its metal is quicksilver, its number eight, its creatures the ibis, the ape, and the serpent.

As Hermes–Thoth–Mercurius, this power presides over writing, translation, alchemy, and the guidance of souls between worlds (Hermes Psychopompos). Quicksilver’s restless fluidity is its perfect physical emblem—the principle that flows, connects, and transmutes, never fixed, forever in motion between the poles.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

hermes-psychopompus.summary: Hermes the Psychopomp — guide of souls to the underworld, at Pisces.
hermes-psychopompus.description: Hermes Psychopompus is Hermes in his solemn office as the conductor of souls, who leads the dead with his golden wand down to the realm of Hades. Referred to Qoph and Pisces, the watery path of the descent into the unconscious depths, he is the divine guide across the final threshold. Where elsewhere he is messenger and trickster, here he is the gentle escort of the departed, the one god free to pass between the living and the dead.

hermit.summary: The ninth Trump (Yod): the Hermit, the solitary bearer of the inner light.
hermit.description: The Hermit is Atu IX, attributed in Liber 777 to the path of Yod (Virgo) joining Chesed to Tiphareth. Cloaked and cowled, he walks the dark bearing a lamp and staff—the prophet of the eternal who has withdrawn from the world to guard and carry its hidden wisdom. Yod is the seed-letter, the smallest and most fertile sign of the alphabet, and the Hermit is its image: the solitary point of light from which the creative Word will spring, the guide who illumines the path of return.
tables: XIV. General Attribution of the Tarot

heru-pa-kraath.summary: Heru-pa-kraath (Harpocrates), the Lord of Silence — Horus the inward child.
heru-pa-kraath.description: Heru-pa-kraath, Hoor-pa-kraat, is the Egyptian Horus the Child in his aspect of silence, the babe with finger to lips, here referred to Yod and Virgo and to the Veils. He is the passive, secret, indrawn pole of the dual Horus — the still inner spirit balancing the active Ra-Hoor-Khuit. As the Lord of Silence he is the protected seed of light, the inviolate centre from which the new Aeon's force is held in reserve.

heru-ra-ha.summary: Heru-Ra-Ha, the combined Horus of the Aeon — the twin god of the new age, at Kether.
heru-ra-ha.description: Heru-Ra-Ha is the composite deity of the new Aeon in Thelema, uniting the active Ra-Hoor-Khuit and the passive Hoor-pa-kraat into a single twofold Horus. Referred to Kether and to Gemini, the sign of the twins, he expresses the doubled nature of the reigning god — force and silence, the speaking and the secret, war and the inward stillness. He is the crowned and conquering child who presides over the Aeon of Horus.

heta.summary: Heta — a letter of the Coptic alphabet (ē), which Crowley attributes to 4 Chesed.
heta.description: Heta is a letter of the Coptic alphabet — the script in which the Egyptian language was written in the Christian era, the Greek alphabet adapted to Egyptian speech. It is the long e, from Greek eta. Crowley folds the Coptic alphabet into the great correspondence of letters and paths in 777 (Table LI), assigning Heta to 4 Chesed on the Tree of Life, so that the Egyptian-Christian script takes its station among the Hebrew letters and the keys of the Tarot.
tables: LI. Names of the Coptic Letters

hexagram.summary: The six-pointed star — attributed to the Sun/Tiphareth; emblem of the Macrocosm.
hexagram.description: The hexagram, the six-pointed star formed of two interlaced triangles, is attributed by its number to Tiphareth and the Sun, and is the emblem of the Macrocosm — the union of Fire and Water, the above and the below, 'as above, so below.' Where the pentagram is Man, the hexagram is the universe; in ceremonial magic it is the figure by which the forces of the planets are invoked, the solar seal of cosmic harmony.
tables: XLIX. Lineal Figures of the Planets, &c., and Geomany

hibiscus.summary: The flame-red bloom of Fire—the hibiscus, flower of passion and offering, blazing with the spirit of Shin.
hibiscus.description: The Hibiscus is attributed to the element Fire (Shin). Its great scarlet flower is among the most vivid of blooms, offered in the East to the fierce deities—the red hibiscus is sacred to Kali—and everywhere a sign of passion and ardent life. As a scarlet flower of Fire it embodies the burning, consuming energy of the element. Esoterically the hibiscus is fire flowering into open colour: the ardour and offering of Shin, passion lifted as a bright flame.

hickory.summary: The hard, resilient wood of Geburah—hickory, tough and strong, fit for the strokes of Mars.
hickory.description: Hickory is attributed to Geburah, the severe sphere of Mars and of strength. Famed for the toughness and resilience of its wood—the stuff of axe-handles, bows, and tools that must bear repeated shock—it embodies the martial virtues of hardness, endurance, and force well-applied. Esoterically the hickory is the disciplined strength of Geburah in the grain of wood: resilient, unyielding under blows, the tough fibre of the warrior.

hiddekel.summary: One of the four rivers of Eden — the biblical name of the Tigris, attributed to Air.
hiddekel.description: Hiddekel is the biblical name of the river Tigris, one of the four streams that watered the garden of Eden (Genesis 2). Among the four elemental rivers of Paradise it is commonly attributed to Air, the element of breath and intellect. As one of the channels through which the single river of Eden divides, it figures the airy current of the life that descends from the supernal source into the created world.

hidden-intelligence.summary: The Concealed Intelligence — the hidden splendour that veils itself at both Kether and Netzach.
hidden-intelligence.description: 'Hidden' or 'Concealed Intelligence' is the recurring epithet by which the Sepher Yetzirah marks those Paths whose light is too pure to be looked upon directly. It names the First Path at Kether (the Admirable, Concealed Intelligence whose essence is wholly veiled) and again the Seventh at Netzach, the Occult Intelligence that is the refulgent splendour of the intellectual virtues, beheld only by the eye of contemplation and faith. In both cases the hiddenness is not absence but excess of light: the radiance is concealed because the seer is not yet able to bear it unmediated.
tables: XIII. Paths of the Sefer Yetzirah

higher-manas.summary: Higher Manas — the higher mind, the immortal individuality, attributed to Binah.
higher-manas.description: Higher Manas, in Theosophical psychology, is the higher mind — the immortal, reincarnating individuality, the abstract reasoning soul that aspires toward Buddhi. Set in 777 at Binah, the supernal Understanding, it is the enduring intelligence of the person, distinguished from the lower, personal mind bound to a single life.

hind-lip-of-urn.summary: Hind Lip of Urn — the English meaning of a lunar mansion marker at the trailing edge of the Water-Bearer's vessel, in Pisces.
hind-lip-of-urn.description: 'Hind Lip of Urn' is one of the more descriptive star-location glosses preserved in 777's table CLXXIV, naming the lunar-mansion point at the trailing edge of the Water-Bearer's flask as the celestial pour ends and the stream enters Pisces. The mansion-tradition uses such anatomical figures for the constellations — lip, head, heart, navel, tail — to fix the manzil precisely against the night sky. The entry's symbolism is liminal: the last lip of the vessel, where the held thing finally goes free. Crowley sets it at the Qoph/Pisces path.
tables: CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon

hinderers.summary: Ghagiel — the averse Chokmah; obstructors of the creative outpouring.
hinderers.description: The Hinderers (Ghagiel) are the Qliphoth of Chokmah, the supernal Father. Against the pure, outflowing creative Wisdom of the second Sephirah they set obstruction and frustration — the shells that block, delay, and pervert the first impulse of manifestation. They are the averse Wisdom that says 'no' to the creative Word.
tables: CXXIII. Translation of the Orders of the Qliphoth

hippogriff.summary: The eagle-horse of Sagittarius—the fabulous winged steed, impossible union mounted toward the heavens.
hippogriff.description: The hippogriff is attributed to Sagittarius, and it is a fabulous hybrid—half eagle, half horse—born of the proverbially impossible crossing, a winged steed of marvellous swiftness that carries its rider through the air. As a creature of Sagittarius it figures that sign's soaring aspiration and its love of far horizons, the earthbound horse given the eagle's wings to mount toward heaven. Like all the noble hybrids of the grid it speaks of the union of opposites raised to splendour. Esoterically the hippogriff is the vehicle of high aspiration, the imagination given wings, the steed that bears the questing spirit beyond the limits of the ordinary world.

hips.summary: The hips and thighs, attributed to Sagittarius, the sign of the archer's stride.
hips.description: The Hips are attributed to Samekh and Sagittarius in this table. In medical astrology Sagittarius rules the hips and thighs—the powerful upper legs of the archer-centaur, the muscular engine of the stride. As Sagittarius is the sign of movement, travel, and far-aiming aspiration, so it governs the part of the body that carries one forward, the strong hinge from which the leg drives the body toward its goal.

his-body-elephantine-with-long-legs.term: his body elephantine with long legs
his-body-elephantine-with-long-legs.displayTerm: his body elephantine with long legs
tables: CLI. Magical Images of the Decans (Cadent)
XCII. The Angelic Functions in the World of Yetzirah

hizarbin.summary: The seas — the Nuctemeron genius of the second hour presiding over the seas, set by Crowley at Taurus.
hizarbin.description: Hizarbin is the Nuctemeron genius of the seas. That “Night-illumined Day”, ascribed to Apollonius of Tyana and handed down through Lévi's Transcendental Magic, sets a company of spirits over each of the twelve hours of the magical day, and Hizarbin belongs to the second hour. He rules the deep waters, the tides and the perils and bounty of the ocean. In 777 (Table CLXXIII) Crowley redistributes these hour-genii across the zodiac, where this spirit falls at Taurus (Vav).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

holding.summary: Holding — a vital function attributed to the element Fire (Shin).
holding.description: 'Holding' — the retentive or grasping power of the organism — is referred in 777 to Fire (the path of Shin). Among the bodily functions distributed to the elements, it marks the active, gripping force by which the living body seizes and keeps: the fiery energy of retention and hold.

tables: CL. Magical Images of the Decans (Succedent)

holy.summary: 'Holy' — the trisagion-word of the Isaiah 6 vision quoted at Malkuth in table XCII.
holy.description: Table XCII ('The Angelic Functions in the World of Yetzirah') splits the Isaiah 6:3 trisagion — 'Holy, Holy, Holy, Lord of Hosts; the whole earth is full of his glory' — across the rows of the Tree as a single descending utterance. The shard 'Holy' lands at Malkuth (the Kingdom), the third repetition of the seraphic cry that descends from the supernals into the manifest world. The entry registers the word as the trisagion fragment it is: the Hebrew qadosh, the most ancient liturgical declaration of the divine otherness, fixed by Crowley at the foot of the Tree where heaven is sung into earth.
tables: XCII. The Angelic Functions in the World of Yetzirah

holy-graal.summary: The sacred chalice of Cancer—the cup of the spirit's blood, the vessel of redemption borne in the Chariot.
holy-graal.description: The Holy Graal is attributed to Cancer, the path of the Chariot, and it is the supreme form of the Cup: the sacred vessel that holds the blood of the god and the wine of the spirit, the chalice of the mysteries sought by every questing knight. Borne within the Chariot as its secret treasure, the Graal is the heart made into a holy vessel, pure enough to receive and contain the divine influx. To win it is the goal of the whole quest, and to drink from it is communion with the source of life. Esoterically the Holy Graal is the soul transformed into a fit receptacle for the highest—the deep, consecrated capacity to receive the descending grace and to bear it, undefiled, through the world.

holy-king-under-the-starry-canopy.term: holy king under the starry canopy
holy-king-under-the-starry-canopy.displayTerm: holy king under the starry canopy
holy-king-under-the-starry-canopy.summary: Liber 777's design for the Chariot (Cheth): a holy king under the starry canopy.
holy-king-under-the-starry-canopy.description: ‘Holy king under the starry canopy’ completes Liber 777's design for Atu VII, the Chariot (path of Cheth, Cancer): ‘A young and holy king under the starry canopy.’ The canopy of stars roofs the chariot as the firmament roofs the world, marking the charioteer as a sacred sovereign bearing the heavens above him. Enthroned beneath the celestial vault, the holy king is the triumphant self—armoured, crowned, and carried forward over the great deep, the Lord of the Triumph of Light.
tables: CLXXXI. Correct Design of Tarot Trumps

holy-living-creatures.summary: Holy Living Creatures — the English name of the angelic choir Chaioth ha-Qadesh, the host of Assiah at Kether.
holy-living-creatures.description: In the Qabalistic angelology each Sephirah commands its own choir of angels; “Holy Living Creatures” (Table CI, the Angels of Assiah given in English) renders into the vernacular the Hebrew order Chaioth ha-Qadesh, the host attributed to Kether. These are the Holy Living Creatures of Ezekiel's vision, the four-faced kerubim of the Merkabah whirling at the summit of the Tree, the first stirring of created life nearest the Crown. Crowley sets them at Kether on the Tree, where the choir gives angelic form to the energy of that sphere as it acts in Assiah, the world of action.

homoth.summary: Name of the last decan of Capricorn, the solar face of established worldly power.
homoth.description: Homoth is 777's name for the last decan of Capricorn (20°–30°). The Sun rules this face and it bears the Four of Disks—Power—established worldly authority, the structure built and held. Among the thirty-six decan-faces inherited from Egypt, it marks the consolidated dominion at the summit of the Goat's sign.
tables: CLXXII. Egyptian Names of the Cadent Decans

hoor-pa-kraat-as-atu-0.summary: Hoor-pa-kraat as Atu 0 — Harpocrates identified with The Fool, at Aleph/Air.
hoor-pa-kraat-as-atu-0.description: This entry identifies Hoor-pa-kraat, the silent Horus-child, with Atu 0, The Fool, at Aleph and the element Air. The link is profound: the Fool is pure unmanifest potential, the babe of spirit before all form, and Harpocrates is precisely the inviolate inner child enclosed in silence. As the Lord of Silence made the wandering holy madman, he expresses the Aleph-mystery — the breath, the void, the innocent spirit stepping into being.

hori.summary: Hori — a letter of the Coptic alphabet (h), which Crowley attributes to the path of Heh (Aries).
hori.description: Hori is one of the Coptic letters drawn not from Greek but from Demotic Egyptian, added to the borrowed Greek alphabet to record sounds Greek could not write: it is the hori, a Demotic-derived letter for the h-sound. Crowley folds the Coptic alphabet into the great correspondence of letters and paths in 777 (Table LI), assigning Hori to the path of Heh (Aries) on the Tree of Life, so that the Egyptian-Christian script takes its station among the Hebrew letters and the keys of the Tarot.
tables: LI. Names of the Coptic Letters

hormakhu.summary: Hormakhu (Harmachis), Horus of the Horizon — the rising sun, the great Sphinx, at Cancer.
hormakhu.description: Hormakhu is Hor-em-akhet, “Horus in the Horizon,” the sun-god at the moment of his rising and setting, identified with the Great Sphinx of Giza. Placed at Cheth and Cancer, the sign of the dawning waters, he is the light breaking over the edge of the world, the falcon of the horizon who heralds each new day. As the Sphinx he is the riddle of the rising sun, the solar power emerging from the night.

horns-of-scorpio.summary: Horns of Scorpio — the English meaning of the seventeenth lunar mansion (Iklil), at the head of Scorpio.
horns-of-scorpio.description: 'Horns of Scorpio' (more literally 'crown of the head') is the English gloss of Iklil (الإكليل, 'the crown'), the seventeenth Arabic lunar mansion, marked by β, δ, and π Scorpii — the three stars forming the head or 'horns' of the scorpion. In mansion-magic Iklil governs the binding of tongues, the curbing of slander, and the strengthening of friendships against treachery — the crown-head ringed and protected. Crowley places it at the Lamed/Libra path, where the scales weigh what is said and unsaid. See also: Iklil (10°).
tables: CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon

horror.summary: Horror — a class-image in CLXXXIII Legendary Orders of Being, the affective category of the awe-and-terror-bringing beings.
horror.description: 'Horror' appears in 777's table CLXXXIII ('Legendary Orders of Being') as a class-name rather than a single creature — the family of beings whose proper effect on the witness is overwhelming dread (compare the Greek phrike, the Hebrew pachad). It collects the chthonic, abyssal, qliphothic beings under their experiential aspect: not what they are but what they are like to encounter. The entry registers it as one of Crowley's category-headers in CLXXXIII rather than as an isolated specimen.

horse.summary: The bearer and the rider's power—war-horse of Mars and the galloping half of the Sagittarian centaur.
horse.description: The Horse carries the paths of motion and force—Pe (Mars, the war-horse charging), Samekh (Sagittarius, whose centaur is half horse, the arrow in flight), and Lamed (Libra). It is harnessed power: swiftness and strength given direction by a rider, the noblest servant of human will in war, labour, and the hunt. Esoterically the Horse is the vital energy that bears the spirit forward—the steed of the soul that must be both spurred and reined—and in the centaur of Sagittarius it is the animal nature fused with the aiming, aspiring intellect that looses the arrow toward heaven.

horse-avatar.summary: Kalki, the horse avatar of Vishnu — the rider of the age's end, at Sagittarius.
horse-avatar.description: The Horse-Avatar is Kalki, the prophesied final avatar of Vishnu, who is to appear at the end of the dark age (Kali Yuga) riding a white horse and bearing a blazing sword to destroy evil and inaugurate a new golden age. Referred to Samekh and Sagittarius — the archer, the arrow aimed at the future — he is the apocalyptic restorer of righteousness. He embodies the divine intervention that ends one cosmic cycle and begins the next.
tables: XXII. Small Selection of Hindu Deities

horus.summary: Egyptian falcon god of the sun, kingship, and the New Aeon.
horus.description: Horus (Egyptian Heru) is the falcon-headed god of the sky, the sun, and kingship—the avenging son of Isis and Osiris who defeats Set and inherits the throne, and whose two eyes are the sun and moon. In Thelema he is the central deity of the present age: Crowley proclaimed the Aeon of Horus, the crowned-and-conquering child Ra-Hoor-Khuit, succeeding the dying-god Aeon of Osiris. As both the warrior-king and the divine child, Horus embodies active, self-determined force and the new order of consciousness that the New Aeon announces. In 777 his various forms thread through the solar and martial attributions of the Tree.
tables: CLXXI. Egyptian Gods of the Zodiac (Cadent)
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

hot.summary: Heat, the active expansive quality, root of Fire and Air.
hot.description: In the doctrine of the four primary qualities inherited from Aristotle and the medieval philosophers, Hot is one of the two active principles. It is the expansive, separating force that drives things apart and upward, and, combined with the two passive qualities, it generates two of the four elements: Hot and Dry make Fire, Hot and Moist make Air. Attributed here to the airy and fiery paths, heat is the energising, vivifying principle of the elemental scheme, the quality of activity and life.
tables: XI. The Elements and their Planetary Rulers

house.summary: Beth — 'house'; the Mercurial dwelling of the Magus, path of The Magician.
house.description: Beth means 'house' — a dwelling, a contained space. As the second letter of the Hebrew alphabet and the first letter of Genesis (Bereshith), it opens the Torah, and tradition makes much of the fact that creation begins with a 'house,' a sheltering enclosure for the divine indwelling. In Liber 777 Beth is the path of The Magus, attributed to Mercury, joining Kether to Binah: the Word that builds a habitation for spirit, the house of the will in which the magician's power is gathered and wielded.
tables: III. Translation of the Names of the Paths

house-of-glory-made-of-pearls.term: House of Glory Made of Pearls
house-of-glory-made-of-pearls.displayTerm: House of Glory Made of Pearls
house-of-glory-made-of-pearls.summary: The highest heaven of the Arabs — the House of Glory, fashioned of pearls.
house-of-glory-made-of-pearls.description: In Crowley's tabulation of the seven heavens of Islamic cosmology, mapped onto the Sephiroth, the supreme heaven is described as the House of Glory, made of pearls, attributed to the supernal triad. The seven heavens of the Arabs are conceived as ascending paradises of ever more precious substance; this pearl-built House of Glory crowns the series, the most exalted of the gardens of the blessed. (Presented here as comparative religious cosmology, not as doctrine.)
tables: CXXVIII. Seven Heavens of the Arabs, English

house-of-rest.summary: A heaven of the Arabs at Chesed — the House of Rest, abode of peace.
house-of-rest.description: Among the seven heavens of Islamic cosmology as tabulated in 777, the House of Rest (recalling Dar al-Salam, the Abode of Peace) is attributed to Chesed. It is one of the ascending paradises of the blessed, the heaven of peace and repose — fittingly aligned with the merciful Jupiterian sphere of grace and rest in the comparative scheme of the Arab heavens.
tables: CXXVIII. Seven Heavens of the Arabs, English

hrumachis.summary: Hrumachis (Harmachis), the dawning sun and herald of the equinox of the gods — at Tiphareth.
hrumachis.description: Hrumachis is another rendering of Harmachis, Horus of the two horizons, here referred to Tiphareth, the solar centre. In Thelemic cosmology Hrumachis is the “double-wanded one” who arises to take his throne at the equinox of the gods, the herald of the changing Aeon. As the sun upon the horizon he marks the turning-point of cosmic ages, the dawning glory at the heart of the Tree.

human-faced-bull.summary: The magical image of Marax — a great bull with a man's face — Goetic Earl and President of the third decan of Libra.
human-faced-bull.description: Marax (Morax, Foraii), the twenty-first spirit of the Goetia, both Earl and President, appears as a great bull with a man's face. In 777 he is set at the third decan of Libra by day. He teaches astronomy and all the liberal sciences, gives good and wise familiars, and imparts the knowledge of herbs and precious stones. The man-faced bull — strength governed by reason — is a fit emblem of the balanced sign of the Scales, where instinct is brought under the rule of intelligence.

hurtful-angel.summary: The magical image of Astaroth — a hurtful angel astride an infernal dragon, a viper in hand — Goetic Duke of the second decan of Capricorn.
hurtful-angel.description: Astaroth, the twenty-ninth spirit of the Goetia and a mighty, strong Duke, appears as a hurtful (foul) angel riding upon an infernal dragon or beast and holding a viper in his right hand. In 777 he rules the second decan of Capricorn by day. He gives true answers of things past, present and to come, discovers all secrets, and will discourse willingly of the fall of the spirits — yet his breath is so noxious that the magician must guard his face with the magical ring. The corrupted angel enthroned upon the dragon images the ambition of the Goat's heights turned to ruin: the high intelligence fallen and made venomous.

hutamah.summary: Hutamah — the crushing fire, third of the Arab hells, attributed to Netzach.
hutamah.description: Al-Hutamah, 'the crushing' or 'the breaker,' is the third of the seven hells, set in 777 at Netzach — a devouring fire that 'leaps up over the hearts,' as the Qur'an says. In the sevenfold cosmology it is one of the deeper gates, allotted to a class of the damned.
tables: CXXV. Seven Hells of the Arabs

hybrid-deities.summary: 'hybrid Deities' — Crowley's category-note at Gemini in table XXII for the twin/composite Hindu gods of the Geminian path.
hybrid-deities.description: Crowley's table XXII marks the Geminian cell with 'hybrid Deities' — recognising that the gods most naturally placed at path 17 (Zayin/Gemini, the path of the Lovers, of Twins, of dual-natured beings) are those whose iconography itself is twinned or composite: the Ashvins (the divine twin horsemen), Mitra-Varuna (the Vedic divine pair), Hari-Hara (the composite Vishnu-Shiva), the ardhanarishvara form of Shiva-Parvati. The class-note is itself the entry: a Crowleyean editorial header collecting the Geminian compounds.
tables: XXII. Small Selection of Hindu Deities

hybrids.summary: Creatures of mixed nature attributed to Mercury and Gemini—the offspring of crossing, emblem of synthesis and dual descent.
hybrids.description: Hybrids—beasts woven of two natures—are placed at Mercury and at Gemini, the twin-sign and the planet of crossing and combination. They are the living figure of the Mercurial principle that joins what is sundered, the alchemical conjunction made flesh: griffin, sphinx, centaur and chimera are all children of this idea. Under Gemini, the sign of the Twins, the hybrid speaks of the doubled and reconciled nature, two essences bound in one body. Esoterically the hybrid is the symbol of the magician's own work, which is the marriage of opposites; it is also a reminder that the products of such union are powerful and ambiguous, neither wholly one thing nor the other.

hymen.summary: Hymen, god of marriage — the bringer of the wedding song, at Taurus and Gemini.
hymen.description: Hymen is the Roman and Greek god of marriage and the wedding feast, invoked in the bridal song that bears his name. Referred to Vav and Taurus and to Zayin and Gemini — signs of love, union, and the joining of two — he presides over the rites that bind man and woman. As the youthful god of the marriage torch he is the divine sanction and joy of wedlock.

hypocrisy.summary: The Jupiterian vice of hypocrisy, the false show of virtue masking corruption.
hypocrisy.description: Hypocrisy is named among the vices at Kaph and Jupiter, the path of the Wheel of Fortune. As the shadow of Jupiter—the expansive, benevolent, religious planet—it is the counterfeit of goodness: the outward show of piety, generosity, or righteousness that conceals a self-serving heart. Where Jupiter's virtue is true magnanimity, its vice is the politician's and the false priest's display of it, the bloated pretence of a charity that does not exist within.
tables: L. Transcendental Morality (10 Virtues; 7 Deadly Sins; 4 Magic Powers)

hypocrites.summary: Hypocrites — cast into al-Hawiyah, the lowest abyss of the Arab hells, set at the supernals.
hypocrites.description: In the Arab cosmology of the seven hells the hypocrites — the munafiqun, who feign belief while denying it in their hearts — are consigned to al-Hawiyah, 'the abyss,' the deepest and most terrible of the seven. Crowley sets them, by the customary inversion of the hellish with the divine, at the three supernal Sephiroth (Kether, Chokmah, Binah): the lowest hell answering to the highest heaven, the bottomless pit mirroring the boundless crown. The entry is preserved as historical cosmology.
tables: CXXVI. Inhabitants of the Seven Hells of the Arabs

hyssop.summary: The purifying herb of Jupiter—the bunch that cleanses and absolves: 'purge me with hyssop, and I shall be clean.'
hyssop.description: Hyssop is attributed to Jupiter (Kaph, the Wheel). The aromatic herb of ritual cleansing throughout the Bible—"purge me with hyssop, and I shall be clean"—it was bound into the aspergillum that sprinkled lustral water and struck the blood upon the doorposts at the Passover. Its office of purification and absolution suits beneficent, priestly Jupiter. Esoterically the hyssop is the herb of cleansing grace, the Jovial mercy that washes the soul and makes it fit to approach the holy.

i-e-unwedded.summary: 'i.e. unwedded' — Crowley's parenthetical gloss at Malkuth in table XIX, qualifying a paired deity in their pre-marital aspect.
i-e-unwedded.description: In table XIX ('Selection of Egyptian Gods') the cell at Malkuth in one column reads (in essence) 'Seb. Lower (i.e. unwedded) Isis and Nephthys' — referring to the two sister-goddesses in their pre-conjugal aspect, before Isis is wedded to Osiris and Nephthys to Set. The shard 'i.e. unwedded' is therefore Crowley's clarifying gloss, fixing the aspect under which the goddesses appear at the Kingdom-Sephirah. The entry preserves the qualifier as it stands in the source.

iao-inri.summary: The solar gnostic formula: Isis, Apophis, Osiris—and the cross of Light at the heart of the Sun.
iao-inri.description: IAO at Resh and the Sun is the supreme Gnostic name of the solar god, its three letters read by Crowley as the great cycle of Isis (nature, the mother), Apophis (the destroyer, the necessary death), and Osiris (the redeemed and risen lord). It is the formula of every initiation that passes through dissolution to rebirth. INRI, the inscription of the cross, the Golden Dawn unfolds as the keys of the elements and of L.V.X.—Yod the virgin Isis, Nun the slain Apophis, Resh the risen Osiris—so that the very title of the crucified becomes the formula for drawing down the Light. At the solar path they together crown the mystery of the dying and conquering Sun.

ibis.summary: The sacred bird of Mercury—the ibis of Thoth, emblem of wisdom, writing and the measuring mind.
ibis.description: The ibis is attributed to Mercury, and it is the sacred bird of Thoth, the Egyptian god of wisdom, writing, magic and measure, who is most often depicted ibis-headed. Wading the margins of the Nile with its long curved bill, the ibis was held to embody the discriminating, ordering intelligence of the god—the power of speech, number and the written word. Its place at Mercury is therefore perfect, for Thoth is the very Hermes of Egypt. Esoterically the ibis figures the wisdom that records and measures, the divine scribe's mind that gives form to thought through language, the patient intelligence that walks the boundary between the waters and the land.

iceland-spar.summary: The doubly-refracting calcite of Gemini — one image split in two.
iceland-spar.description: Iceland spar — clear calcite — is attributed to the path of Zayin and Gemini for the most elegant of reasons: it splits a single ray of light into two (double refraction), so that one sees any object viewed through it doubled. The very stone makes one into two, the visible signature of the Twins. (It may also be the 'sunstone' by which the Norse navigators are thought to have located the hidden sun.) Esoterically it is the gem of the doubling of vision, the one that reveals itself as two.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

idlness.summary: The lunar vice of idleness, the listless inertia of the unstirred soul.
idlness.description: Idleness is named among the vices at Gimel and the Moon, the path of the High Priestess. As the shadow of the lunar nature—passive, reflective, given to dream—it is sloth: the drifting inertia that lets the tides carry it and never rouses to the work. Where the moon's virtue is serene receptivity, its vice is the torpor that mistakes passivity for peace, the soul becalmed in its own reflections and unwilling to take up the labour of attainment.
tables: L. Transcendental Morality (10 Virtues; 7 Deadly Sins; 4 Magic Powers)

idolators.summary: Idolators — dwellers of al-Jahim in the Arab seven hells, set at Chesed.
idolators.description: The idolaters — worshippers of images and of the 'many gods' — are, in the Arab scheme of the seven hells, the inhabitants of al-Jahim, set in 777 at Chesed. The entry belongs to the medieval comparative eschatology that ranked the religions in the descending hells; it is recorded as a historical artefact of that cosmology rather than as doctrine.
tables: CXXVI. Inhabitants of the Seven Hells of the Arabs

ignorance.summary: The tenth fetter — ignorance (avijjā), the root unknowing that underlies all the rest.
ignorance.description: Ignorance is avijjā, the tenth and most fundamental of the ten fetters, attributed to Malkuth, the kingdom of manifest experience. It is not mere lack of information but a deep not-knowing of things as they are — of suffering and its cause, of impermanence and not-self — the primordial darkness from which all the other fetters and the whole round of becoming proceed. Last to be severed, its destruction is the final liberation, arahatship itself. Set at Malkuth, the world of appearances, it figures the veiling of reality by the very density of the manifest.
