ihvh.summary: The Tetragrammaton, the four-lettered Name unfolded as the whole machinery of the worlds.
ihvh.description: IHVH—the Tetragrammaton, Yod-Heh-Vav-Heh—is the ineffable four-lettered Name of God, attributed in the formulae table to Chesed, the sphere of mercy, majesty, and the loving Father. Read elementally and dynamically it is the master-formula of the Qabalah: Yod the Father and the fire of the primal will, the first Heh the Mother and the receptive water, Vav the Son and the airy six-fold heart, the final Heh the Daughter and the bride who falls into Malkuth and must be raised again to the throne of the Mother. The whole drama of manifestation, fall, and redemption is folded into these four letters, which the magician learns to pronounce not with the lips but with the life.

ikarus.summary: Icarus, who flew too near the sun — the emblem of aspiration and its fall, at the solar heights.
ikarus.description: Icarus is the youth who, escaping Crete on wings of wax and feathers made by his father Daedalus, flew too near the sun, melted his wings, and fell into the sea. Referred to Kether, Tiphareth, and the place of Spirit, he is a striking emblem of aspiration toward the divine light — the soul's soaring ascent and the peril of overreaching. His fall warns that the flight to the sun demands measure as well as daring.

illuminating-intelligence.summary: The Illuminating Intelligence — the Second and Fourteenth Paths, the splendour of Chokmah and the radiance of Daleth.
illuminating-intelligence.description: The Sepher Yetzirah names the Second Path the Illuminating Intelligence (Sekhel Mazhir), the Crown of Creation and the splendour of Unity, exalting itself above every head — the dazzling outflow of Chokmah, the first stir of force from the unmanifest. The same luminous title returns at the Fourteenth Path of Daleth (the Luminous or Illuminating Intelligence, Sekhel Meir), the establisher of the holy arcana, where the brilliance of the supernal Wisdom is mediated through Venusian beauty and form. In each, 'illumination' marks the active shining-forth of light into a vessel prepared to receive it.
tables: XIII. Paths of the Sefer Yetzirah

illusionary-success.summary: Seven of Cups — Illusionary Success; Venus in Scorpio, Netzach of Water: hollow delight.
illusionary-success.description: Illusionary Success is the Golden Dawn title of the Seven of Cups, Netzach of the watery suit, Venus in the last decan of Scorpio. Beauty (Venus) sunk into Scorpio's depths breeds glamour and self-deception: cups that seem to brim with delight but hold only vapour. The card warns of pleasures and successes that dissolve on contact, the wishful dream that flatters and then fails.
tables: CXXXIV. Titles and Attributions of the Chalice Suit

imaginative-intelligence.summary: The Twenty-fourth Path — the Imaginative Intelligence of Nun, fashioner of likenesses.
imaginative-intelligence.description: The Twenty-fourth Path is the Imaginative Intelligence (Sekhel ha-Dimyoni), attributed to the letter Nun and the sign Scorpio, the path of Death joining Tiphareth to Netzach. The Sepher Yetzirah says it furnishes a likeness to all the similitudes which are created in like manner to its harmonious elegancies. It is the image-making power of transformation: through the Scorpionic mystery of death and regeneration, forms are dissolved and re-imagined, one likeness passing into another in the endless figurative work of nature.
tables: XIII. Paths of the Sefer Yetzirah

impotence.summary: Impotence at Yesod — the failure of the lunar Foundation of generation.
impotence.description: Impotence is attributed to Yesod, the Foundation, the lunar sphere that in the microcosm governs the generative organs and the reproductive power. As the treasure-house through which the vital force is gathered and transmitted, Yesod is the seat of potency; its failure is impotence — the foundation unable to channel the creative current. Symbolically it is a blockage at the base of the Tree, the generative power dammed at its source.

in-the-sign-of-osiris-risen.term: in the Sign of Osiris Risen
in-the-sign-of-osiris-risen.displayTerm: in the Sign of Osiris Risen
in-the-sign-of-osiris-risen.summary: Design detail of the Lovers (Zayin): in the Sign of Osiris Risen.
in-the-sign-of-osiris-risen.description: ‘In the Sign of Osiris Risen’ completes Liber 777's design for Atu VI, the Lovers (path of Zayin, Gemini): ‘A prophet, young, and in the Sign of Osiris Risen.’ The Sign of Osiris Risen is a Golden Dawn ritual posture—arms crossed upon the breast in the attitude of the resurrected god, signifying life triumphant over death. Set upon the prophet of the Lovers, it sanctifies the union and the choice with the promise of regeneration: the marriage of opposites consummated under the sign of the risen one.
tables: CLXXXI. Correct Design of Tarot Trumps

including-most-of-minor.summary: A fragment of a court card's celestial dominion: the region of the sky including most of Leo Minor.
including-most-of-minor.description: ‘Including most of ♌ Minor’ (Leo Minor) is a fragment of the celestial-dominion description in Liber 777's tables of the Court Cards (after the Golden Dawn's Book T). Each court card rules a region of the actual heavens, named by the constellations it contains. This fragment assigns most of Leo Minor—the small lion that crouches beside the greater Leo—to one such dominion, locating the card's rule among the real northern stars as well as upon the zodiacal band.
tables: LXXI. Court Cards of the Tarot, with the Spheres of their Celestial Dominion - Wands

including-most-of-pegasus.summary: A fragment of a court card's celestial dominion: the region of the sky including most of Pegasus.
including-most-of-pegasus.description: ‘Including most of Pegasus’ is a fragment of the celestial-dominion description in Liber 777's tables of the Court Cards (after the Golden Dawn's Book T). Each court card is assigned not only a band of the zodiac but a swathe of the actual starry heavens—the constellations lying within its rule. This fragment names the great winged horse Pegasus as falling chiefly within one such dominion, locating the card's authority among the real stars of the night sky as well as upon the zodiacal wheel.
tables: LXII. The Court Cards of the Tarot, with the Spheres of their Celestial Dominion Cups

including-part-of-andromeda.summary: A fragment of a court card's celestial dominion: the region of the sky including part of Andromeda.
including-part-of-andromeda.description: ‘Including part of Andromeda’ is a fragment of the celestial-dominion description in Liber 777's tables of the Court Cards (after the Golden Dawn's Book T). Each court card rules a defined region of the actual heavens, named by the constellations it contains. This fragment assigns part of the constellation Andromeda—the chained princess of Greek myth—to one such dominion, anchoring the card's rule among the fixed stars as well as in the moving zodiac.
tables: LXXI. Court Cards of the Tarot, with the Spheres of their Celestial Dominion - Wands

including-part-of-hercules.summary: A fragment of a court card's celestial dominion: the region of the sky including part of Hercules.
including-part-of-hercules.description: ‘Including part of Hercules’ is a fragment of the celestial-dominion description in Liber 777's tables of the Court Cards (after the Golden Dawn's Book T). The court cards are each given a tract of the real starry sky, identified by its constellations. This fragment places part of the constellation Hercules—the kneeling hero of antiquity—within one such dominion, tying the card's authority to a particular quarter of the heavens among the fixed stars.
tables: LXXI. Court Cards of the Tarot, with the Spheres of their Celestial Dominion - Wands

incubi.summary: The male night-demons of lust, set at Jupiter — spirits that lie upon sleepers in the dark.
incubi.description: Among the Legendary Orders of Being, the Incubi are attributed to the path of Jupiter. In medieval demonology the incubus is the male night-spirit that descends upon a sleeper to couple with her, the counterpart of the female succubus — a demon of nocturnal lust born of the dreaming mind and its repressed desires. As an order they figure the invasion of the soul by ungoverned sexual force in sleep, the dark underside of generation; theology and folklore alike made them the demonic fathers of monstrous or fated offspring.

independence.summary: The lunar virtue of independence, the self-reliance of the foundation.
independence.description: Independence is named as the virtue of Yesod, the ninth Sephirah, the astral foundation and sphere of the Moon. Though Yesod is the seat of the reactive, image-haunted lunar nature, its redeeming virtue is independence—the standing-firm of the soul upon its own foundation, free of the pull of every passing tide and the suggestion of every reflected image. It is the strength to be self-determined amid the changeable astral currents, the foundation that holds steady so that the whole structure above may rest secure.
tables: L. Transcendental Morality (10 Virtues; 7 Deadly Sins; 4 Magic Powers)

indian-hemp.summary: The Indian cannabis variety, attributed to Netzach and Hod; visionary and sensory.
indian-hemp.description:
Cannabis Indica appears at Netzach and Hod — the Venusian sphere of feeling and the Mercurial sphere of mind — reflecting the two faces of its action: the heightening of the senses and emotions on the one hand, and the loosening and acceleration of thought on the other. The same plant whose resin (hashish) Crowley set at Chokmah is here placed in the lower personality, where its effects are felt in ordinary consciousness. In the Indian tradition (bhang, ganja) it carries an ancient sacramental and Shaivite association.

Caution: this is a psychoactive drug with genuine risks and variable legality. The entry is scholarly and symbolic, not an encouragement to use.
indian-hemp.caution: Psychoactive; legality varies; dependence and acute anxiety/psychosis risk. Symbolic/historical entry only.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

indifference.summary: The Brahmavihāra of equanimity (upekkhā) — the even, unshaken mind beyond preference.
indifference.description: Indifference here renders upekkhā, the fourth and crowning Brahmavihāra of the Forty Meditations, attributed to Kether. It is not coldness but equanimity — the serene, impartial balance that meets gain and loss, praise and blame, pleasure and pain with the same unshaken composure. As the highest of the divine abidings it completes and steadies the other three, love and compassion and joy held in perfect poise; set at the Crown it figures the still, all-embracing evenness of a mind that rests at the summit, untouched by the swing of opposites.

indigestion.summary: Indigestion at Vav and Taurus — disorder of appetite under the earthy Bull.
indigestion.description: Indigestion is set on the path of Taurus, the fixed earth sign of appetite, the throat, and the body's intake, ruled by Venus. Taurus governs nourishment and the pleasures of the table; indigestion is the disorder of its own province — the earthy, sensual appetite overindulged or its processes obstructed, the body unable to assimilate what it has taken in. It is the shadow of Taurean abundance, satisfaction turned to discomfort.

indigo.summary: The dark blue smoke of Saturn—indigo, deep and sombre, perfume of the saturnine night.
indigo.description: Indigo is attributed to Saturn (Tav, the Universe)—the deepest of the cold dark colours, the blue that verges upon black, and so the chromatic and aromatic signature of Saturn's night. Listed among the saturnine perfumes, its sombre, heavy character belongs to the sphere of time, limitation, and the dark. Esoterically indigo is the perfume of saturnine depth—the dark blue note of the midnight sphere, the colour of the abyss turned to scent and smoke.

indolence.summary: Eight of Cups — Indolence / Abandoned Success; Saturn in Pisces, Hod of Water.
indolence.description: The Eight of Cups, Indolence (Abandoned Success), is Hod in the suit of Water and the first decan of Pisces under Saturn. Saturn's blight upon the watery suit drains the cups and leaves a leaden, stagnant pool: pleasure abandoned not through satiety but through listlessness and decay. It is the turning-away from a joy that has gone flat, the weary withdrawal that leaves success unclaimed.
tables: CXXXIV. Titles and Attributions of the Chalice Suit

indra.summary: Indra, king of the gods and lord of storm — the thunder-wielding sovereign, at Jupiter.
indra.description: Indra is the Vedic king of the gods, wielder of the thunderbolt (vajra) and slayer of the drought-serpent Vritra, whose victory releases the waters and the dawn. Referred to Kaph and Jupiter and to Chesed, he is the sovereign, benevolent, storm-bringing power of the heavens — the warrior-king of the devas. As the rain-giver and conqueror of chaos he embodies the expansive, ruling majesty of the sky.
tables: XXII. Small Selection of Hindu Deities

infernal-dragon.summary: Infernal Dragon — a recurring image-class in the magical-image and qliphothic tables, the great serpent of the depths.
infernal-dragon.description: 'Infernal Dragon' appears in Liber 777's image-columns as a class-image rather than a named being — the figure of the great serpent-monster of the abyss that returns across the world's mythologies as Tiamat, Leviathan, Apophis, Python, Jörmungandr, and the dragon under the foot of St Michael. In Hermetic-Qabalistic symbolism the infernal dragon is the chthonic, devouring counterpart to the celestial serpent — the kundalini turned negative, the qliphothic flow of force without a vessel. The entry registers it as a recurring iconographic motif in 777's image-tables, not as a single named demon.

inflammation.summary: Inflammation at Pe and Mars — the heat, redness, and swelling of the war-planet.
inflammation.description: Inflammation is attributed to Pe, the path of Mars. The cardinal signs of inflammation — heat, redness, pain, and swelling — are the very signature of Mars, the planet of fire, blood, and aggression; the inflamed tissue is the body waging war upon itself or upon an invader. Esoterically it is Martial energy localised and intensified, the fiery, defensive force that protects when measured but destroys when it rages unchecked.

initiation.summary: The Virgoan power of guiding the soul through the gates of the Mysteries.
initiation.description: Initiation is attributed to Yod and Virgo, the path of the Hermit who, having attained, turns to light the way for others. As a magical power it is the capacity to bring another across a threshold of consciousness—to open, by ritual and contact, a door that cannot be opened from within alone. The Hermit's hidden lamp is precisely this: the transmitted spark by which the descending light of the Supernals is passed from initiate to candidate, generation to generation.

inner-guard.summary: The guardian within the door, here at Yesod — keeper of the threshold.
inner-guard.description: The Inner Guard keeps the inside of the door of the lodge, admitting those who are duly qualified and reporting alarms. Attributed to Yesod, the Foundation and the threshold between the worlds, the office guards the passage by which the candidate enters — the watcher at the gate of the astral foundation.
tables: CXV. Officers in a Masonic Lodge

insanity.summary: Insanity at Chokmah — reason overthrown by an uncontainable supernal force.
insanity.description: Insanity is placed at Chokmah, the supernal sphere of pure, undifferentiated Force. Chokmah is the dynamic outflowing power at the head of the Tree, force without the limiting form that Binah supplies; madness is read here as that overwhelming force breaking into a mind unable to give it bound or shape. It is the peril of contact with the highest energies — wisdom's lightning striking a vessel too weak to hold it, and shattering instead of enlightening.

intelligence-of-all-the-activities-of-th.term: Intelligence of all the Activities of the Spiritual Being
intelligence-of-all-the-activities-of-th.displayTerm: Intelligence of all the Activities of the Spiritual Being
intelligence-of-all-the-activities-of-th.summary: The Nineteenth Path — the Intelligence of all the Activities of the Spiritual Beings, of Teth.
intelligence-of-all-the-activities-of-th.description: The Nineteenth Path is the Intelligence of all the Activities of the Spiritual Beings (Sekhel Sod ha-Peuloth ha-Ruchaniyim), attributed to the letter Teth and the sign Leo, the path of Strength (Lust, in the Thoth deck) joining Chesed to Geburah. The Sepher Yetzirah says it is so named because of the influx diffused into it from the most high and exalted glory above. It governs the deeds and operations of the angelic and spiritual orders — the leonine, joyous strength by which the powers of the higher Tree act in the world.
tables: XIII. Paths of the Sefer Yetzirah

intelligence-of-conciliation.summary: The Twenty-first Path — the Intelligence of Conciliation and Reward of Kaph, receiver of the divine influx.
intelligence-of-conciliation.description: The Twenty-first Path is the Intelligence of Conciliation, also called the Intelligence of Desire and Reward (Sekhel ha-Chafetz ve-ha-Mevukash), attributed to the letter Kaph and the planet Jupiter, the path of Fortune (The Wheel) joining Chesed to Netzach. The Sepher Yetzirah says it receives the divine influence flowing into it from its benediction upon all and each existence. Jupiter's turning wheel of fortune conciliates and rewards: it is the gracious, expansive power that mediates between the merciful sphere and the sphere of victory, distributing blessing and recompense.
tables: XIII. Paths of the Sefer Yetzirah

intelligence-of-probation.summary: The Twenty-fifth Path — the Intelligence of Probation of Samekh, the trial of the righteous.
intelligence-of-probation.description: The Twenty-fifth Path is the Intelligence of Probation, or the Tentative Intelligence (Sekhel Nisyoni), attributed to the letter Samekh and the sign Sagittarius, the path of Temperance (Art) joining Tiphareth to Yesod. The Sepher Yetzirah says it is the primary temptation by which the Creator tries all the righteous. As the great central arrow-path aimed from the heart toward the foundation, it is the testing way — the probation through which the aspirant's tempering and proving is accomplished, the trial that refines.
tables: XIII. Paths of the Sefer Yetzirah

intelligence-of-the-house-of-influence.term: Intelligence of the House of Influence
intelligence-of-the-house-of-influence.displayTerm: Intelligence of the House of Influence
intelligence-of-the-house-of-influence.summary: The Eighteenth Path — the Intelligence of the House of Influence of Cheth, by which good things abound.
intelligence-of-the-house-of-influence.description: The Eighteenth Path is the Intelligence of the House of Influence (Sekhel Beth ha-Shefa), attributed to the letter Cheth and the sign Cancer, the path of The Chariot joining Binah to Geburah. The Sepher Yetzirah says that by the greatness of its abundance the influx of good things is increased, and that from within itself it draws forth the arcana and hidden meanings that dwell in its shadow. It is the 'house' or vessel through which the higher flux pours into the world — the warded, shell-armoured Chariot that bears the holy influence safely down.
tables: XIII. Paths of the Sefer Yetzirah

intelligence-of-the-mediating-influence.summary: The Sixth Path — the Mediating Intelligence of Tiphareth, where all the influxes are multiplied and shared.
intelligence-of-the-mediating-influence.description: The Sixth Path is the Mediating Intelligence (Sekhel ha-Memshet, the Intelligence of the Mediating Influence), assigned to Tiphareth, the radiant solar centre of the Tree. The Sepher Yetzirah says that in it the influences of the emanations are multiplied, and that it causes that abundance to flow into all the reservoirs of blessing with which they are united. Tiphareth is the great mediator and harmoniser, the heart that stands at the meeting of higher and lower, gathering the streams of the supernals and distributing them in balance to the spheres below — the seat, in the Thelemic reading, of the Holy Guardian Angel.
tables: XIII. Paths of the Sefer Yetzirah

intelligence-of-transparency.summary: The Twelfth Path — the Transparent Intelligence of Beth, source of vision and prophecy.
intelligence-of-transparency.description: The Twelfth Path is the Intelligence of Transparency, or the Bright/Transparent Intelligence (Sekhel Bahir), attributed to the letter Beth and the planet Mercury, the path of The Magus from Kether to Binah. The Sepher Yetzirah names it the source of vision in those who behold apparitions, the medium through which prophecy is seen. Transparency is its key: Beth, the Mercurial channel of the Word, is the clear glass through which the higher light passes to become image, vision, and intelligible speech.
tables: XIII. Paths of the Sefer Yetzirah

intelligence-of-will.summary: The Twentieth Path — the Intelligence of Will of Yod, by which primordial Wisdom is known.
intelligence-of-will.description: The Twentieth Path is the Intelligence of Will (Sekhel ha-Ratzon), attributed to the letter Yod and the sign Virgo, the path of The Hermit joining Chesed to Tiphareth. The Sepher Yetzirah says it is the means by which the existence of the primordial Wisdom becomes known, the preparation of all and each created being. As the path of the Hermit's solitary, indrawn light, it joins the merciful sphere to the heart of the Tree by an act of pure intention — the Will that prepares and consecrates the way of return.
tables: XIII. Paths of the Sefer Yetzirah

interference.summary: Eight of Swords — Interference / Shortened Force; Jupiter in Gemini, Hod of Air.
interference.description: The Eight of Swords, Interference (Shortened Force), is Hod in the suit of Air and the first decan of Gemini under Jupiter. In Hod, the sphere of intellect, the airy suit grows over-busy: many short swords cross and block two long blades, the mind tangled in its own complications. It is meddling, restriction, and the frustration of clear action by a clutter of petty obstacles.
tables: CXXXV. Titles and Attributions of the Sword Suit.

intestines.summary: The intestines, attributed to Scorpio, the dark passage of dissolution and absorption.
intestines.description: The Intestines are attributed to Nun and Scorpio. In medical astrology Scorpio governs the lower digestive tract and the organs of elimination—the dark, hidden passages where the last nourishment is drawn from food and the residue prepared for expulsion. As Scorpio rules the mysteries of dissolution, putrefaction, and the cleansing that precedes renewal, so it governs this final and secret labour of the body's interior.

invisibility.summary: The Virgoan power of going unseen, the magic of withdrawing the self from notice.
invisibility.description: Invisibility is attributed to Yod and Virgo (and to Spirit), the path of the Hermit, whose lamp is hidden and whose nature is secret and self-contained. As a magical power it is less the literal vanishing of the body than the art of so withdrawing and veiling the magnetic presence that one is not perceived—the attention of others simply passing over. Crowley described practical work toward it as the controlled suppression of the astral and magical 'shew' by which we are normally registered, a discipline natural to the solitary, inward sign of the Virgin.

ipos.summary: The twenty-second spirit of the Goetia, an earl and prince of Scorpio who makes men witty and bold.
ipos.description: Ipos is the twenty-second spirit of the Goetia, an earl and mighty prince of the decans of Scorpio. He knows things past and to come, and makes men witty and bold. He appears in a strange composite shape — the body of an angel with a lion's head, the feet of a goose and the tail of a hare. A spirit of the penetrating water-sign, he sharpens the wit and emboldens the heart.

ipsissimus.summary: 10°=1, the grade of Kether — the 'very self'; the supreme attainment beyond the Abyss.
ipsissimus.description: Ipsissimus, 'one's very own self,' is the highest grade of the A∴A∴, attributed to Kether, the Crown. It marks the final stage of the magical ascent, the master who has wholly realised the truth of his own being and stands in perfect identity with the All. So utterly does the Ipsissimus dwell in the unmanifest that, by Crowley's account, the grade can scarcely be spoken of at all — its nature is to be free of every distinction, including that of attainment itself.

iris.summary: Iris, goddess of the rainbow — the swift messenger between heaven and earth, at Sagittarius.
iris.description: Iris is the Roman and Greek goddess of the rainbow, the winged messenger of the gods who descends along the bow to carry their words to mortals. Referred to Samekh and Sagittarius, the path of the arrow and the bridge between worlds, she is the shining arc that joins heaven and earth. As messenger and rainbow she embodies the link, the bridge, and the bright passage of the divine into the human realm.

iron.summary: The martial metal of Geburah — strength, the sword, blood, and discipline.
iron.description: Iron is the metal of Mars and of Geburah, the sphere of severity and strength — the metal of the sword and the plough, of weapons and tools, hard, strong, and answering to the magnet as the will answers to command. It runs in the blood as the iron of haemoglobin, binding the martial planet to the very fluid of life and vigour, and in medicine it builds the depleted blood. Esoterically it is disciplined force made solid — the principle of strength that both defends and destroys, and that, magnetised, gives the lodestone its directing power.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

isis.summary: Egyptian great goddess of magic, motherhood, and resurrection.
isis.description: Isis (Egyptian Aset) is the great goddess of magic, motherhood, healing, and resurrection—the devoted wife who reassembles the murdered Osiris and conceives the avenger Horus, and the supreme mistress of the words of power. As the throne (her hieroglyph) she is the seat of kingship; as the mourning and life-restoring mother she became the most widely worshipped deity of the late ancient world, her mysteries spreading across the Roman Empire. In the esoteric scheme she embodies the feminine, formative, and magical power of nature—the veiled goddess ‘whose veil no mortal has lifted,’ and the type of the Great Mother in her nurturing and initiatory aspects.
tables: CLXVII. Egyptian Gods of the Zodiac (Asc. Decans)
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

israfel-blowing-the-last-trumpet.summary: Liber 777's design for Judgement/The Aeon (Shin): Israfel blowing the Last Trumpet.
israfel-blowing-the-last-trumpet.description: ‘Israfel blowing the Last Trumpet’ is part of Liber 777's design for Atu XX, Judgement—the Aeon—on the path of Shin (Fire): ‘Israfel blowing the Last Trumpet; the dead arising from their tombs.’ Israfel is the Islamic archangel of the resurrection, whose trumpet-blast ends the old world and summons the dead to rise. As the Spirit of the Primal Fire, the trump is the great awakening: the searing call of Shin that consumes the former order and resurrects all things into the new aeon.
tables: CLXXXI. Correct Design of Tarot Trumps

ivy.summary: The clinging evergreen of Binah and earth—Dionysian, faithful, binding life fast to the dark.
ivy.description: Ivy is given to Binah and to Malkuth and Earth, the evergreen that clings and endures through winter. Paired with the vine in the rites of Dionysus, it is the dark, female, persistent counterpart to the vine's intoxication—the wreath of Bacchus and of poets. Its habit of binding itself to wall and tree makes it an emblem of faithfulness and of the constricting, form-giving power of Binah, the Mother who binds spirit into matter. Esoterically the ivy is tenacity and the quiet, shadowed life that holds fast where brighter growth has died back.

jacinth.summary: The fiery orange zircon of Sagittarius — the questing flame made stone.
jacinth.description: Jacinth (hyacinth) — an orange-to-red zircon — is set on the path of Samekh and Sagittarius, the mutable-fire sign of the aspiring archer. Its warm fiery colour suits the questing flame of Sagittarius, and in the lapidary and biblical tradition it was a stone of protection on journeys and a guard for the traveller. Esoterically it is the gem of aspiration, the fire of the soul's arrow shot toward the higher truth.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

jacinths.summary: A heaven of the Arabs at Chesed — a paradise fashioned of jacinth (hyacinth) stone.
jacinths.description: Among the seven heavens of Islamic cosmology as tabulated in 777, jacinths — the orange-red hyacinth gemstone — are named as the substance of a heaven attributed to Chesed. The ascending paradises of the blessed are each built of a precious material; the jacinth-stone characterises the splendour of this level of the Arab heavens, here aligned with the merciful sphere.
tables: CXXVIII. Seven Heavens of the Arabs, English

jackal.summary: Anubis's beast at Pisces and Hod—the guide of the dead, opener of ways through the lunar underworld.
jackal.description: The jackal is placed at Pisces (the path of Qoph, the Moon) and at Hod, and it is forever the animal of Anubis, the jackal-headed opener of the ways who conducts the dead through the underworld and presides over the weighing of the heart. As a scavenger of the desert's edge and the burial-ground, the jackal lives at the threshold between the living and the dead, exactly the liminal territory of Qoph's dark lunar path. Under Hod, the sphere of Mercury and Hermes-the-psychopomp, this guiding office is doubled. Esoterically the jackal is the trusted guide through the night of the soul, the intelligence that knows the road through the land of the dead and does not lose its way.

jacob.summary: Jacob — here at Geburah; the wrestler who strove with the angel and prevailed.
jacob.description: Jacob is attributed here to Geburah, the sphere of Severity and strength. The patriarch who wrestled through the night with the angel and would not let go until he was blessed — and was renamed Israel, 'he who strives with God' — embodies the strenuous, transformative struggle proper to the fifth Sephirah. His is the strength won through ordeal, the severity that purifies and renames.
tables: XCI. The Saints or Adepts of the Hebrews

jahim.summary: Jahim — the fierce fire, sixth of the Arab hells, attributed to Chesed.
jahim.description: Al-Jahim, 'the fierce blazing fire,' is the sixth of the seven hells of Arab cosmology, set in 777 at Chesed. One of the deeper gates of the descending Jahannam, it is allotted in the tradition to the idolaters — a vast and terrible furnace far below the milder upper hells.
tables: CXXV. Seven Hells of the Arabs

janja.summary: Janja — a letter of the Coptic alphabet (j/g), which Crowley attributes to 9 Yesod.
janja.description: Janja is one of the Coptic letters drawn not from Greek but from Demotic Egyptian, added to the borrowed Greek alphabet to record sounds Greek could not write: it is the janja, a Demotic-derived letter for the soft palatal. Crowley folds the Coptic alphabet into the great correspondence of letters and paths in 777 (Table LI), assigning Janja to 9 Yesod on the Tree of Life, so that the Egyptian-Christian script takes its station among the Hebrew letters and the keys of the Tarot.
tables: LI. Names of the Coptic Letters

jannat-al-and.summary: Jannat al-'Adn — the Garden of Eden, attributed to Yesod.
jannat-al-and.description: Jannat al-'Adn, the 'Garden of Eden' or of perpetual abode, is one of the seven gardens of the Islamic paradise — the everlasting dwelling promised to the righteous — set in 777 at Yesod, the foundation of the Tree. The primal garden of Eden, the rooted home of bliss, is fittingly referred to the foundational ninth Sephirah.
tables: CXXVII. Seven Heavens of the Arabs

jannat-al-firdaus.summary: Jannat al-Firdaus — the Garden of Paradise, attributed to Hod.
jannat-al-firdaus.description: Jannat al-Firdaus, 'the Garden of Paradise' (Firdaus, cognate with the Persian 'paradise' and the Garden of Eden), is in the tradition the loftiest and most excellent of the gardens, from beneath which the rivers of paradise are said to flow; in 777's distribution it is set at Hod. The supreme garden, the goal of the faithful, is here referred to the mercurial sphere of the ordered heavens.
tables: CXXVII. Seven Heavens of the Arabs

jannat-al-karar.summary: Jannat al-Karar (Dar al-Qarar) — the Abode of Permanent Settlement, attributed to Malkuth.
jannat-al-karar.description: Jannat al-Karar (Dar al-Qarar), the 'Abode of Settlement' or of permanent rest, is one of the seven gardens of the Islamic paradise — the final, abiding dwelling — set in 777 at Malkuth, the Kingdom and the foot of the Tree. The garden of lasting repose, the journey's end, is referred to the lowest Sephirah, where the descent comes home to rest.
tables: CXXVII. Seven Heavens of the Arabs

jannat-al-khuld.summary: Jannat al-Khuld — the Garden of Eternity, attributed to Tiphareth.
jannat-al-khuld.description: Jannat al-Khuld, the 'Garden of Eternity' or of immortality, is one of the seven gardens of the Islamic paradise, set in 777 at Tiphareth, the radiant solar heart of the Tree. The everlasting garden — the abode of unfading life — answers to the centre of beauty and harmony where the dying god is reborn into eternity.
tables: CXXVII. Seven Heavens of the Arabs

jannat-al-maawa.summary: Jannat al-Ma'wa — the Garden of Refuge, attributed to Geburah.
jannat-al-maawa.description: Jannat al-Ma'wa, the 'Garden of Refuge' or shelter, is one of the seven gardens of the Islamic paradise, the place of harbour for the blessed, set in 777 at Geburah. The garden of refuge — sanctuary won and held — is referred to the sphere of Mars and strength, the stronghold of the fifth Sephirah.
tables: CXXVII. Seven Heavens of the Arabs

jannat-al-naim.summary: Jannat al-Na'im — the Garden of Delight, attributed to Netzach.
jannat-al-naim.description: Jannat al-Na'im, the 'Garden of Bliss' or Delight, is among the most celebrated of the seven gardens of the Islamic paradise, set in 777 at Netzach, the sphere of Venus. The garden of sensuous delight and joy is the perfect heaven for the Venusian sphere of love, beauty, and pleasure.
tables: CXXVII. Seven Heavens of the Arabs

janus.summary: Janus, the two-faced god of doorways and beginnings — who looks both ways, at Chokmah and Gemini.
janus.description: Janus is the Roman god of doorways, gates, beginnings, and transitions, depicted with two faces gazing in opposite directions, toward the past and the future. Referred to Chokmah, the first force, and to Zayin and Gemini, the sign of duality, he is the threshold-god who opens every undertaking — the first month, January, bears his name. As the keeper of beginnings and the lord of the two-fold gaze, he presides over all passage and inception.

jasmine.summary: The night-blooming flower of Yesod—jasmine, sensual and lunar, 'queen of the night,' perfume of the astral Foundation.
jasmine.description: Jasmine is attributed to Yesod, the lunar Foundation of the astral and generative life. Opening and pouring out its heady sweetness by night, the "queen of the night" is a deeply sensual, dreamy, moon-loving flower, an aphrodisiac of fragrance fitting the sphere of the Moon, of dream, and of sexual vitality. Esoterically jasmine is the perfume of the astral and generative current of Yesod—the night-scent that opens the dream-gates and stirs the secret life, lunar sweetness charged with desire.

jazar.summary: The compelling of love — the Nuctemeron genius of the seventh hour presiding over the compelling of love, set by Crowley at Libra.
jazar.description: Jazar is the Nuctemeron genius of the compelling of love. That “Night-illumined Day”, ascribed to Apollonius of Tyana and handed down through Lévi's Transcendental Magic, sets a company of spirits over each of the twelve hours of the magical day, and Jazar belongs to the seventh hour. He compels affection, the forcing and binding of love by spell. In 777 (Table CLXXIII) Crowley redistributes these hour-genii across the zodiac, where this spirit falls at Libra (Lamed).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

jehannam.summary: Jahannam — the uppermost of the seven Arab hells, attributed to Malkuth and Yesod.
jehannam.description: Jahannam is the first and least terrible of the seven hells of Arab cosmology — the topmost gate, set in 777 at Malkuth and Yesod, to which sinful believers are assigned and from which, in the tradition, they may in time be released. Its name became the general word for hell, but in the sevenfold scheme it is the mildest degree, nearest the world above.
tables: CXXV. Seven Hells of the Arabs

jesus-as-hanged-man.summary: Jesus as the Hanged Man — the crucified god, attributed to the element of Water (Mem).
jesus-as-hanged-man.description: Jesus 'as Hanged Man' is referred to the path of Mem and the element of Water, the path of the Hanged Man of the Tarot — the figure suspended, reversed, and self-offered. The attribution reads the Crucifixion as the supreme mystery of redemptive sacrifice and reversal: the god who, by hanging upon the tree, turns the world's values upside down and brings life out of death, even as the still waters of Mem give way to bring forth life.
tables: XXXVI. Selection of Christian Gods (10); Apostles (12); Evangelists(4); and Churches of Asia (7)

jews.summary: Jews — dwellers of al-Hutamah in the Arab seven hells, set at Netzach.
jews.description: In the medieval Arab cosmology of the seven hells, the Jews are named as the inhabitants of al-Hutamah ('the crushing fire'), set in this table at Netzach. The attribution is part of a polemical eschatology of its era that distributed the several faiths among the descending gates of Jahannam; it is preserved here strictly as a historical artefact of comparative religion, carrying no endorsement.
tables: CXXVI. Inhabitants of the Seven Hells of the Arabs

jhanas.summary: The jhānas — the deep meditative absorptions, set at Malkuth as the ground of attainment.
jhanas.description: Jhanas are the meditative absorptions of the Buddhist (and broader Indian) contemplative path, here listed among the Hindu/Buddhist Results and attributed to Malkuth. They are the successive states of deepening concentration — the four form-jhānas marked by the fading of distraction and the arising of rapture, bliss and one-pointed equanimity, leading on to the formless attainments. Their placement at Malkuth, the kingdom and starting-point of the work, marks them as the foundational fruits of concentration on which the whole edifice of insight and liberation is built.
tables: XXIV. Certain of the Hindu/Buddhist Results

jinseng.summary: The vital root-scent of Yesod—ginseng, the man-shaped restorative whose fragrance breathes the Foundation's life-force.
jinseng.description: Jinseng (ginseng) appears among the fragrant roots of Yesod, the lunar Foundation of the vital and generative energies. The forked, often man-shaped root prized in the East as the supreme restorative of vigour and longevity, it stands here as the very type of the odoriferous root—the hidden, earth-deep source of vitality—drawn up into the sphere of the foundation-life. Esoterically ginseng is the root-perfume of Yesod's vitality, the concentrated life-force that underlies and replenishes the body's strength.

john.summary: John — the Evangelist of the Eagle, attributed to the element of Water (Mem).
john.description: John, figured as the soaring Eagle (Scorpio/Water) for the heights of his contemplative, mystical Gospel, is set in 777 in the path of Mem, the element of Water. He is the kerub of the Eagle's face among the four living creatures — the visionary who looks unblinking into the divine Sun.
tables: XXXVI. Selection of Christian Gods (10); Apostles (12); Evangelists(4); and Churches of Asia (7)

joseph.summary: Joseph — at Yesod; the dreamer and interpreter, faithful foundation of his people.
joseph.description: Joseph is attributed to Yesod, the Foundation. The dreamer of dreams and reader of their meaning, whose visions belong to Yesod's dominion over the astral and the night-world, he becomes the faithful foundation that preserves his family through famine. His chastity, his prophetic dreaming, and his role as the sustaining base of Israel all befit the ninth Sephirah, the treasure-house of images on which the Kingdom rests.
tables: XCI. The Saints or Adepts of the Hebrews

joy.summary: The Brahmavihāra of sympathetic joy (muditā) — gladness at the happiness of others.
joy.description: Joy is muditā, the third of the four Brahmavihāras of the Forty Meditations, attributed to Chokmah, the sphere of pure outflowing force. It is sympathetic or altruistic joy — the cultivated delight in the good fortune and happiness of others, the gladness that rejoices without a trace of envy. As a divine abiding it is the remedy for jealousy and discontent; in the dynamic, generative position of Chokmah it figures the spontaneous, overflowing rejoicing of a heart that has ceased to measure another's joy against its own.

junior-deacon.summary: Bearer of messages from Senior to Junior Warden, here at Hod.
junior-deacon.description: The Junior Deacon attends the Senior Warden and conveys his orders to the Junior Warden, guarding the inner approaches of the lodge. Attributed to Hod, the Mercurial sphere of intellect and communication, the office fittingly embodies the carrying of word and instruction through the lodge's order.
tables: CXV. Officers in a Masonic Lodge

junior-warden.summary: The Third of the Lodge, at Tiphareth — the noonday Sun in the South.
junior-warden.description: The Junior Warden is the third principal officer, seated in the South, who marks the sun at meridian and presides over the brethren at refreshment. Attributed to Tiphareth, the harmonising solar centre of the Tree, his station is that of beauty and balance — the high point of the day, mediating between the rising and the setting lights.
tables: CXV. Officers in a Masonic Lodge

juno.summary: Juno, queen of the gods — sovereign protectress of women and marriage, at Binah.
juno.description: Juno is the Roman queen of the gods, wife of Jupiter, goddess of marriage, women, and the sovereignty of the state, counterpart of the Greek Hera. Referred to Binah, the supernal Mother, and to the airy paths, she is the regal, matronly power of heaven, guardian of wives and protectress of Rome. As the great queen she embodies the dignity, authority, and watchful care of the divine consort.

jupiter.summary: Jupiter—expansion, sovereignty, fortune, and mercy; ruler of Chesed and the path of Kaph.
jupiter.description:
Jupiter is the planet of expansion, abundance, sovereignty, and benevolent order—the great fortune that enlarges and blesses. In 777 it rules the fourth Sephirah Chesed and the path of Kaph (the Tarot trump Fortune / the Wheel), governing kingship, law, generosity, and growth. Its metal is tin, its number four, its emblems the sceptre, the eagle, and royal blue and purple.

As Zeus–Jupiter–Marduk, the sky-father and king of the gods, this power presides over the just rule of the cosmos and the turning wheel of fortune. Its danger is excess—the expansion that becomes bloat or tyranny—but balanced by Martian severity it supplies the magnanimity and right rule that hold a world together.
tables: CXXXIX. Planets Exalted in the Signs of the Zodiac
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

justice.summary: Atu VIII — Lamed / Libra; cosmic balance, karma, and exact equilibrium.
justice.description: Adjustment (the older Justice) is trump VIII, attributed to Lamed and Libra, the path from Geburah to Tiphareth. It is the principle of cosmic balance and karmic exactitude—every action weighed, every force answered by its equal. Crowley renamed Justice ‘Adjustment’ to strip away moralism: this is not human judgement but the impersonal law by which the universe keeps its equilibrium. The masked, dancing figure poised on her toes balances the sword and the scales. Adjustment teaches that truth is equilibrium, and that all things are continually corrected toward the mean.
tables: XIV. General Attribution of the Tarot
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

ka.summary: Ka — the Egyptian 'double,' the vital life-force, attributed to Chokmah.
ka.description: The Ka, in the Egyptian division of the soul, is the 'double' — the vital essence or life-force born with each person and sustained after death by offerings, the spectral twin that dwells in the tomb-statue. Set in 777 at Chokmah, the fount of generative force, it answers to the energetic, life-giving principle of the being — the breath of vitality distinguished from the personal soul.
tables: CXVI. Egyptial Attribution of Parts of the Soul

kabeshunt.summary: Qebehsenuef, the hawk-headed Son of Horus and guardian of the canopic jars, attributed to elemental Fire.
kabeshunt.description: Kabeshunt is a form of Qebehsenuef (Kebehsenuf), the hawk- or falcon-headed member of the Four Sons of Horus, to whom the intestines were entrusted under the protection of the scorpion-goddess Serqet; his name carries the sense of “he who refreshes his brethren.” Though his classical guardianship is of the West, Liber 777 sets him at Shin—the path of elemental Fire and the Aeon/Judgement trump, the letter of the descending Spirit-fire. With his brothers Ameshet, Hapi, and Duamutef he completes the fourfold guard that preserves the body of the dead for resurrection.

kadamidi.summary: Angel of the first face of Taurus, where earthbound effort meets the anxiety of scarcity.
kadamidi.description: Kadamidi governs the opening decan of Taurus (0–10°), where the Golden Dawn places Mercury and the Five of Disks, *Worry* — the strain of material insecurity at the threshold of the zodiac's most earthy sign. Mercury's restlessness disturbs Taurean stability, producing the gnawing care of one who labours yet fears want. Kadamidi is the angel of this testing ground, presiding over the first hard lesson of matter: that security must be built, never assumed.

kalab.summary: Sacred vessels — the Nuctemeron genius of the twelfth hour presiding over sacred vessels, set by Crowley at Pisces.
kalab.description: In the Nuctemeron — the “Day Illumined by Night” ascribed to Apollonius of Tyana and preserved by Éliphas Lévi — Kalab is numbered among the genii of the twelfth hour, the spirit of sacred vessels. He presides over the holy vessels, the consecrated instruments of worship. Crowley arranges the twelve hours and their genii upon the paths of the Tree (777, Table CLXXIII), placing him at Pisces (Qoph).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

kalb.summary: al-Qalb, 'the heart' — Antares, the burning heart of the Scorpion, the lunar mansion in Scorpio.
kalb.description: al-Qalb, 'the heart of the Scorpion,' is the great red star Antares, one of the four Royal Stars and watcher of the west, the Mansion of the Moon set in the path of Scorpio (Nun). Its smouldering crimson fire gave it a fierce, martial, and fated character — a star of intensity, courage, obsession, and violent ends — burning at the very core of the sign of death and regeneration.
tables: CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon

kama.summary: Kāma — sensual desire; the fourth fetter and the Hindu principle of craving.
kama.description: Kāma is craving or sensual desire, appearing both as the fourth of the Buddhist fetters (kāma-rāga) and in the Hindu analysis of the soul, attributed in 777 to Netzach and Yesod. It is the force of attraction toward the objects of the senses — the appetitive, desiring nature that fuels becoming. In Indian thought kāma is one of the legitimate aims of life when rightly ordered, yet from the contemplative's standpoint it is precisely the bond to be loosened, the heat of wanting that must cool before peace can arise. Set in the lower Sephiroth of feeling and foundation, it is desire as the engine of the manifest world.

kamotz.summary: Angel of the first face of Scorpio, where feeling sours into loss and disappointment.
kamotz.description: Kamotz rules the opening decan of Scorpio (0–10°), where Mars, the sign's traditional ruler, meets the Five of Cups, *Disappointment* — soured pleasure, the bitter dregs in the cup. Mars wounds the watery feeling at the threshold of the deepest sign. Kamotz is the angel of the grief of expectation betrayed, the first descent into Scorpio's testing depths.

kan.summary: Kan (K'an), the trigram of Water and the abyss — attributed to the Moon, Mars, and the elemental paths.
kan.description: Kan (K'an, an unbroken line between two broken) is the trigram of Water, the abyss, danger, and 'the pit' — the deep, the moon, the flowing peril through which one must pass. In 777 it gathers several attributions (the Moon, Mars, and the elemental paths of Fire and Earth), marking the dangerous, fluid, plunging principle among the eight trigrams.

kappa.summary: Kappa — a letter of the Coptic alphabet (k), which Crowley attributes to the path of Kaph (Jupiter).
kappa.description: Kappa is a letter of the Coptic alphabet — the script in which the Egyptian language was written in the Christian era, the Greek alphabet adapted to Egyptian speech. It is from Greek kappa. Crowley folds the Coptic alphabet into the great correspondence of letters and paths in 777 (Table LI), assigning Kappa to the path of Kaph (Jupiter) on the Tree of Life, so that the Egyptian-Christian script takes its station among the Hebrew letters and the keys of the Tarot.
tables: LI. Names of the Coptic Letters

kataris.summary: Dogs — the Nuctemeron genius of the tenth hour presiding over dogs, set by Crowley at Capricorn.
kataris.description: Among the genii of the tenth hour in the Nuctemeron of Apollonius of Tyana, Kataris presides over dogs. He governs the dogs and, in the older lists, those given over to the profane and the abandoned. Lévi gives the roll of the hour-genii in his Transcendental Magic; Crowley tabulates them along the paths of the Tree (Table CLXXIII), assigning Kataris to Capricorn (Ayin).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

kha.summary: Kha — a higher principle of the Egyptian soul, attributed to Kether.
kha.description: Kha appears in 777's table of the Egyptian parts of the soul among the highest principles, set at Kether. In the Egyptian scheme the loftier members — the shining Akh and the divine spark — gather at the crown of the being; Kha is given here as one such supernal principle, the soul considered at its most exalted and least embodied. (The transliterations of the Egyptian soul-parts vary between authorities.)
tables: CXVI. Egyptial Attribution of Parts of the Soul

khai.summary: The Khu (Akh) — the luminous, glorified spirit, set at Chokmah, the shining immortal self.
khai.description: Khai corresponds to the Egyptian Khu or Akh, the 'shining' or 'glorified' spirit, attributed here to Chokmah. Among the parts of the Egyptian soul the Khu was the luminous, imperishable spirit-body, the radiant intelligence that survived death and dwelt among the imperishable stars — the soul rendered effective and glorious. Set at Chokmah, the supernal sphere of pure radiant force and the first light below the Crown, it stands for the highest, shining principle of the self, the immortal star within.
tables: CXVI. Egyptial Attribution of Parts of the Soul

khan.summary: Khan — a trigram of the Yi King in Crowley's Taoist table, set at Malkuth and Saturn.
khan.description: Khan appears in 777's table of Taoism among the trigrams of the Yi King, referred to Malkuth and to Saturn (Tav) — the spheres of the manifest Kingdom and of form and limitation. (Crowley follows Legge's older transliteration of the eight kua, in which the trigram names differ from those of the modern Pinyin system.) Its placement at the foot of the Tree marks a grave, earth-ward, settling principle.

khat.summary: Khat — the physical body, the corruptible flesh, attributed to Malkuth.
khat.description: The Khat is the physical body, the corruptible flesh that decays and which mummification sought to preserve as a seat for the other parts of the soul. Set fittingly in 777 at Malkuth, the material Kingdom, it is the densest vehicle of the Egyptian being — the earthly house from which the Ka, the Ba, and the spirit depart.
tables: CXVI. Egyptial Attribution of Parts of the Soul

khei.summary: Khei — a letter of the Coptic alphabet (kh), which Crowley attributes to the path of Cheth (Cancer).
khei.description: Khei is one of the Coptic letters drawn not from Greek but from Demotic Egyptian, added to the borrowed Greek alphabet to record sounds Greek could not write: it is the khai, a Demotic-derived letter for the guttural kh. Crowley folds the Coptic alphabet into the great correspondence of letters and paths in 777 (Table LI), assigning Khei to the path of Cheth (Cancer) on the Tree of Life, so that the Egyptian-Christian script takes its station among the Hebrew letters and the keys of the Tarot.
tables: LI. Names of the Coptic Letters

kheibt.summary: Kheibt — the shadow, the Egyptian shade of the soul, attributed to Malkuth.
kheibt.description: The Kheibt (Khaibit) is the Shadow, one of the parts of the Egyptian soul — the shade that accompanies the person and was held to partake of their substance, able to move independently after death. Set in 777 at Malkuth, it belongs to the lower, earth-bound complex of the being: the dark double cast by the living form.
tables: CXVI. Egyptial Attribution of Parts of the Soul

khem.summary: Khem (Min), the ithyphallic god of generative power — lord of fertility, at Capricorn.
khem.description: Khem is Min, the ancient ithyphallic god of male generative force, fertility, and the harvest, here referred to Ayin and Capricorn — the sign of the goat, of potency and the steep ascent. With upraised arm and erect phallus he embodies the raw creative power of nature, the seed and the increase of the fields. Crowley adopted “Khem” as a name for Egypt itself and for this generative magical current.

khenti-khas.summary: Khenti-Khas — the divine guardian Crowley pairs with the Nostril of Adam Kadmon in table XXI.
khenti-khas.description: Khenti-Khas appears as the parenthetical guardian of the Nostril in Crowley's table XXI, at paths 14 (Daleth/Venus) and 27 (Pe/Mars). The name is plausibly a transliteration of the Egyptian Khenty-Khas (or Khenti-Kheti), a Lower-Egyptian falcon-and-crocodile god of the nome of Athribis whose functions included perception and warding. In the perfected-body schema the nostril is the organ through which life-breath enters, and its guardian is fittingly a god of perception and threshold. The entry preserves the name and its placement; the etymological grounding is offered as a plausible reading rather than a certain identification.

khephra.summary: Khephra (Khepri), the scarab of the midnight sun — god of becoming and self-renewal.
khephra.description: Khephra is Khepri, the scarab-headed god of the rising and the midnight sun, whose name means “he who comes into being.” Attributed to the dark, watery paths of Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces, he is the sun in its hidden, nocturnal journey through the underworld, rolling the solar disk toward a new dawn as the beetle rolls its ball of dung. He is the very principle of self-generation and transformation, being perpetually reborn from itself.

khi.summary: Khi — a letter of the Coptic alphabet (kh), which Crowley attributes to the path of Qoph (Pisces).
khi.description: Khi is a letter of the Coptic alphabet — the script in which the Egyptian language was written in the Christian era, the Greek alphabet adapted to Egyptian speech. It is from Greek chi. Crowley folds the Coptic alphabet into the great correspondence of letters and paths in 777 (Table LI), assigning Khi to the path of Qoph (Pisces) on the Tree of Life, so that the Egyptian-Christian script takes its station among the Hebrew letters and the keys of the Tarot.
tables: LI. Names of the Coptic Letters

khien.summary: Khien (Qian), the trigram of Heaven — the pure Yang, attributed to Chokmah and the Sun.
khien.description: Khien (Ch'ien, three unbroken lines), the first trigram of the Yi King — the pure and creative Yang — signifies Heaven, the father, the dragon, the unceasing initiating power. In 777 it is referred to Chokmah and to the Sun (Resh): the active, generative, celestial principle, the begetting force at the head of the eight trigrams.

khwan.summary: Khwan (Kun), the trigram of Earth — the pure Yin, attributed to Binah and the Moon.
khwan.description: Khwan (K'un, three broken lines), the pure and receptive Yin, is the trigram of Earth — the mother, the yielding, the nourishing field that receives and brings to form. In 777 it is set at Binah and the Moon (Gimel): the great receptive principle answering to Khien's creative force, the womb of manifestation among the trigrams.

kidney-disorders.summary: Kidney disorders at Lamed and Libra — affliction of the organs of balance.
kidney-disorders.description: Disorders of the kidneys are attributed to the path of Libra, the cardinal air sign that classically rules the kidneys, the loins, and the lower back. Libra is the sign of balance and equilibrium, and the kidneys are the body's great balancers — filtering, regulating, holding the inner fluids in just proportion. Their disorder is therefore the failure of Libran equilibrium in the flesh, the scales of the body's chemistry thrown out of true.

kidneys.summary: The kidneys, attributed to Aquarius, the filtering and balancing of the body's waters.
kidneys.description: The Kidneys are attributed to Tzaddi and Aquarius in this table. The paired kidneys filter the blood and regulate the body's waters and salts, casting off what is spent while conserving what is needed—a work of fine and constant balance. Their attribution to Aquarius, the fixed airy sign of circulation and the water-bearer who pours and measures the stream, befits this regulating office among the body's inner fluids.

kimaris.summary: The sixty-sixth spirit of the Goetia (Cimeies), a warrior-marquis of Capricorn who rules Africa and finds the lost.
kimaris.description: Cimeies (here Kimaris) is the sixty-sixth spirit of the Goetia, a great marquis of the decans of Capricorn, ruling over the spirits of the land of Africa. He teaches grammar, logic and rhetoric, discovers things lost or hidden and buried treasures, and makes a man into a good and valiant soldier. He appears as a valiant warrior riding upon a strong black horse. A spirit of the earthy sign, he is the captain of soldiers and the finder of what is lost.

kingdom.summary: Kingdom—the tenth Sephirah; the material world, the Shekhinah indwelling in matter.
kingdom.description:
Malkuth (מלכות, ‘Kingdom’) is the tenth and final Sephirah, the physical world in which the entire descent of the Tree comes to rest. It is the realm of the four elements, of the body and the senses, the ‘Inferior Mother’ and the Bride (Kallah) who is the Shekhinah, the divine presence dwelling within matter itself. Its God-name is Adonai ha-Aretz, its virtue discrimination, its vice avarice and inertia; its image a young woman, crowned and throned.

Far from being merely ‘the lowest,’ Malkuth is sacramental: ‘Kether is in Malkuth, and Malkuth is in Kether, but after another manner.’ The whole magical enterprise begins here, in the kingdom of the ordinary, because it is in the material world that the divine seeks to be redeemed and made manifest.
tables: III. Translation of the Names of the Paths
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

kings.summary: Kings — the English name of the angelic choir Malachim, the host of Assiah at Tiphareth.
kings.description: In the Qabalistic angelology each Sephirah commands its own choir of angels; “Kings” (Table CI, the Angels of Assiah given in English) renders into the vernacular the Hebrew order Malachim, the host attributed to Tiphareth. These are the Kings or Messengers, the royal angels of the Sun-centre, mediators who bear the king's word through the worlds. Crowley sets them at Tiphareth on the Tree, where the choir gives angelic form to the energy of that sphere as it acts in Assiah, the world of action.

kirtabus.summary: Languages — the Nuctemeron genius of the ninth hour presiding over languages, set by Crowley at Sagittarius.
kirtabus.description: Among the genii of the ninth hour in the Nuctemeron of Apollonius of Tyana, Kirtabus presides over languages. His province is tongues and speech, the gift and mastery of languages. Lévi gives the roll of the hour-genii in his Transcendental Magic; Crowley tabulates them along the paths of the Tree (Table CLXXIII), assigning Kirtabus to Sagittarius (Samekh).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

knights.summary: The charging fiery fathers of the Tarot court—the active masculine force of the suits, attributed to Chokmah and Fire.
knights.description: The Knights are the court cards attributed to Chokmah, the supernal Father, and to the fiery letter (the Yod of the divine Name), the swift mounted figures who embody the active, initiating, masculine force of their suits. In Crowley's Thoth Tarot these are the Knights who come charging on horseback—the fierce, outgoing, fatherly power that begins and impels, the first impulse of each elemental kingdom set in violent motion. As the highest of the court figures they correspond to the creative outrush of Chokmah and the fire of pure will. Esoterically the Knights figure the active, originating force in each of the four worlds—the swift, ardent, fatherly impulse that initiates and drives, the charging fiery power by which each suit's energy is first set going.
tables: XIV. General Attribution of the Tarot

knowledge-of-sciences.summary: The Mercurial power of mastering the arts and sciences, the encyclopaedic intellect.
knowledge-of-sciences.description: Knowledge of Sciences is attributed to Beth and Mercury, the path of the Magus, the patron of all learning and skill. As a magical power it is the swift, comprehensive grasp of the structures of knowledge—mathematics, medicine, the mechanical and liberal arts—granted to the mind that has aligned itself with Mercury's quicksilver intelligence. It expresses the ancient belief that the god of writing and number is also the giver of every science, and that adepthood includes the disciplined cultivation of the understanding.

krishna.summary: Krishna, the divine cowherd and charioteer — the eighth avatar of Vishnu, teacher of the Gita.
krishna.description: Krishna is the eighth and most beloved avatar of Vishnu, at once the playful cowherd of Vrindavan, the divine lover of the gopis, and the supreme teacher who delivers the Bhagavad Gita upon the field of battle. Referred to Cheth and Cancer and to the path of Mars, he is the descent of the godhead in fully personal form — love, wisdom, and dharma incarnate. His flute calls the soul to union; his teaching reconciles action with liberation.
tables: XXII. Small Selection of Hindu Deities

kronos.summary: Saturn—time, limitation, structure, and death; ruler of Binah and the path of Tav.
kronos.description:
Saturn is the planet of time, limitation, structure, and death—the great teacher whose discipline gives form to all things and whose scythe ends them. In 777 it rules the third Sephirah Binah, the formative Mother, and the path of Tav (the Tarot trump The Universe), the last letter and the completion of the work. Its metal is lead, its number three, its emblems the scythe, the hourglass, and the colour black.

As Kronos–Saturn, the old king of the golden age who devours his children, this power is simultaneously the boundary-maker and the destroyer, the principle that everything in form must end. The alchemists made lead the prima materia, the heavy base matter that, rightly worked, becomes gold—so Saturn’s leaden weight is also the necessary ground of transmutation.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

ksi.summary: Ksi — a letter of the Coptic alphabet (x), which Crowley attributes to the path of Samekh (Sagittarius).
ksi.description: Ksi is a letter of the Coptic alphabet — the script in which the Egyptian language was written in the Christian era, the Greek alphabet adapted to Egyptian speech. It is from Greek xi. Crowley folds the Coptic alphabet into the great correspondence of letters and paths in 777 (Table LI), assigning Ksi to the path of Samekh (Sagittarius) on the Tree of Life, so that the Egyptian-Christian script takes its station among the Hebrew letters and the keys of the Tarot.
tables: LI. Names of the Coptic Letters

kundalini.summary: Kundalini, the serpent-power coiled at the base — the latent divine energy of ascent.
kundalini.description: Kundalini is the coiled serpent-energy that lies dormant at the base of the spine, the latent divine power that, awakened, rises through the chakras to union with the crown. Referred to Malkuth and to Nun and Scorpio — the depths and the sign of regeneration — she is the goddess Shakti as raw, transformative force within the body. Her ascent is the very engine of yogic attainment, the kindling of the lowest into the highest.
tables: XXII. Small Selection of Hindu Deities

kurm-avatar.summary: Kurma, the tortoise avatar of Vishnu — the cosmic support, at Yesod.
kurm-avatar.description: Kurma is the second avatar of Vishnu, the tortoise who descended to the bottom of the sea of milk and bore upon his back the churning-mountain Mandara, so that the gods might churn the ocean for the nectar of immortality. Referred to Yesod, the Foundation, he is the divine support beneath the great work of creation, the steadfast base upon which the cosmos is stirred to yield its treasures. He embodies patient, foundational strength.
tables: XXII. Small Selection of Hindu Deities

kwan-se-on.summary: Kwan-yin (Kwan-se-on) — the Bodhisattva of compassion, attributed to Binah.
kwan-se-on.description: Kwan-se-on (Guanshiyin, Kwan-yin), 'she who hears the cries of the world,' the Bodhisattva of boundless compassion, is set at Binah, the supernal Mother and sphere of understanding and sorrowful mercy. Though Buddhist in origin, she is wholly at home among the Taoist correspondences as the great compassionate Mother — the merciful feminine who answers every suffering, exactly the maternal aspect of Binah.

laberzerin.summary: Success — the Nuctemeron genius of the second hour presiding over success, set by Crowley at Taurus.
laberzerin.description: Laberzerin is the Nuctemeron genius of success. That “Night-illumined Day”, ascribed to Apollonius of Tyana and handed down through Lévi's Transcendental Magic, sets a company of spirits over each of the twelve hours of the magical day, and Laberzerin belongs to the second hour. He grants prosperity in undertakings and the fortunate outcome of effort. In 777 (Table CLXXIII) Crowley redistributes these hour-genii across the zodiac, where this spirit falls at Taurus (Vav).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

labus.summary: Inquisition — the Nuctemeron genius of the twelfth hour presiding over inquisition, set by Crowley at Pisces.
labus.description: Among the genii of the twelfth hour in the Nuctemeron of Apollonius of Tyana, Labus presides over inquisition. His province is inquisition, the relentless searching-out and interrogation of the accused. Lévi gives the roll of the hour-genii in his Transcendental Magic; Crowley tabulates them along the paths of the Tree (Table CLXXIII), assigning Labus to Pisces (Qoph).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

laetitia.summary: Geomantic figure 'Joy' — attributed to Jupiter; joy, health, upward movement.
laetitia.description: Laetitia, 'joy,' is one of the sixteen geomantic figures, attributed to Jupiter and associated with Pisces. Its upward-rising form signifies gladness, health, hope, and the lifting of the spirits — a figure of well-being and favourable outcome. Among the most beneficent of the figures, it bodes well for happiness, recovery, and the cheerful prospering of an affair.
tables: XLIX. Lineal Figures of the Planets, &c., and Geomany

lakshmi.summary: Lakshmi, goddess of fortune and abundance — the lotus-throned consort of Vishnu, at Malkuth.
lakshmi.description: Lakshmi is the Hindu goddess of wealth, beauty, fortune, and prosperity, consort of Vishnu, who rose radiant from the churning of the cosmic ocean. Referred to Malkuth, the Kingdom and the realised, material world, she is the giver of all worldly and spiritual abundance, seated upon the lotus with gold flowing from her hand. She is grace made bountiful, the auspicious power that blesses the home and the harvest.
tables: XXII. Small Selection of Hindu Deities

lalita.summary: Lalita (Tripura Sundari), the beautiful goddess of the three worlds — the supreme Shakti, at Venus.
lalita.description: Lalita, “She Who Plays,” is the supreme goddess Tripura Sundari, the most beautiful in the three worlds, central deity of the Shri Vidya tradition. Referred to Daleth and Venus, she is the radiant erotic and creative power of the divine feminine, enthroned upon the Shri Yantra, sovereign of love and bliss. As the playful, beautiful Shakti she is the joyous, all-attracting energy at the heart of tantric devotion.
tables: XXII. Small Selection of Hindu Deities

lamiae.summary: The child-devouring night-demons, set at Nun — serpent-women of Scorpionic dread.
lamiae.description: The Lamiae are an order of legendary beings, attributed to Nun and the sign Scorpio. In Greek lore the Lamia was a queen cursed to devour children, becoming a serpent-bodied demoness who preyed on the young and seduced and drained young men by night — a figure later merged with the vampire and the succubus. As an order they figure the devouring, predatory shadow of the feminine, the deathly Scorpionic underside of desire and generation.

lamp.summary: The flame of guidance—the light of the spirit kept burning through Capricorn's dark and Fire's blaze.
lamp.description: The Lamp appears again among the weapons at Capricorn and at the fiery letter Shin, and in both it signifies the kept flame: the light of the spirit maintained through the cold dark of Capricorn's depths and identified, at Shin, with the sacred fire itself. As an implement it is the disciplined, tended illumination that the magician keeps alive within—the inner flame that must be fed and guarded if it is to give light. To bear the Lamp is to be responsible for a fire that can warm and reveal or, neglected, gutter out. Esoterically the Lamp is the consciousness of the divine spark kept consciously burning, the small faithful fire that mirrors the great Fire and lights the working from within.

laodicea.summary: Laodicea — the 'lukewarm' church, attributed to the Moon (Gimel).
laodicea.description: Laodicea, the church rebuked as 'neither cold nor hot' and so 'spewed out,' is set in 777 in the path of Gimel and the sphere of the Moon. The lunar attribution catches its wavering, reflected, tepid faith — neither the fire of zeal nor the cold of open refusal, but the changeable half-light of the Moon, called to buy 'gold tried in the fire.'
tables: XXXVI. Selection of Christian Gods (10); Apostles (12); Evangelists(4); and Churches of Asia (7)

lapis-lazuli.summary: The starry blue stone of the heavens—sovereignty, the night sky, and sacred wisdom.
lapis-lazuli.description: Lapis lazuli, the deep blue stone flecked with golden pyrite ‘stars,’ is associated with the heavens, with sovereignty, and with sacred wisdom—its night-sky appearance making it a natural emblem of the celestial vault. Prized in ancient Egypt and Mesopotamia above almost all other stones, ground into the sacred pigment ultramarine, it adorned the regalia of gods and kings and the eyes of funerary masks. In the esoteric scheme its starry blue aligns it with the higher, ordering powers and the mystery of the heavens made visible in stone.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

lares.summary: The Lares, guardian spirits of the household — protectors of home and family, at Cancer.
lares.description: The Lares are the Roman tutelary spirits of the household and the hearth, the protective ancestral powers honoured at the family shrine. Referred to Cheth and Cancer, the sign of home, family, and the protective shell, they are the indwelling guardians of domestic life. Each home kept its Lar, fed and garlanded at the table; they embody the sanctity and continuity of the household.

tables: CL. Magical Images of the Decans (Succedent)

larvae.summary: The malignant dead of Roman belief, set at Saturn — restless, hostile shades that torment the living.
larvae.description: Among the Legendary Orders of Being, the Larvae are attributed to Saturn. In Roman religion the larvae were the malevolent spirits of the dead — those who, denied proper rites or wicked in life, returned as hostile, frightening shades to haunt and torment the living, the dark counterpart of the kindly ancestral Lares. Set at Saturn, the sphere of death and the heavy, binding past, they figure the unquiet dead in their most threatening aspect, the spectral residue of unredeemed lives.

larynx.summary: The Larynx — bodily seat of the throat centre, attributed to Binah.
larynx.description: The larynx, the organ of voice, is given as the bodily seat of the throat chakra (Vishuddha), set in 777 at Binah. It is the physical instrument of the creative Word — the place where breath is shaped into speech, the inner made outer, fittingly drawn to the formative supernal Mother.

laslara.summary: Diurnal angelic Lord of Virgo within the Earthy Triplicity.
laslara.description: Laslara is the day-governor of Virgo among the angelic Lords of the Triplicities. As the mutable, discriminating member of the Earth trine, Virgo by day is the careful daytime ordering of the harvest, the sifting and refining of matter; Laslara presides over this exact, methodical labour of the light.

last-judgement.summary: 'Last Judgement' — Crowley's bracketed gloss for Yama at the path of Sol in table XXII.
last-judgement.description: In table XXII the cell at path 30 (Resh/Sol) reads in essence 'Yama [Last Judgement],' giving the Tarot-Hermetic correspondence beside the Hindu name. Yama is the Vedic god of death and the judge of the dead; Crowley pairs him with the Tarot trump XX (Judgement / The Aeon), whose subject is exactly the great weighing and sorting at the end of the cycle. The slug 'Last Judgement' preserves the bracketed qualifier as it appears in the source; the principal Yama entry holds the description.
tables: XXII. Small Selection of Hindu Deities

last-judgement-wands-kings.summary: The cluster attributed to Shin/Fire: the Last Judgement, the suit of Wands, and the Kings.
last-judgement-wands-kings.description: This entry from Liber 777's General Attribution of the Tarot gathers under the path of Shin (Fire) the trump of the Last Judgement (the Aeon), the suit of Wands, and the court rank of the Kings (Knights). Shin is the three-tongued letter of fire and spirit, the Wands are the fiery suit of will and energy, and the Kings are the fiery, active heads of the court. The cluster shows the current of Fire running through the deck—the resurrecting flame of Judgement, the burning will of the Wands, and the dynamic sovereignty of the Kings.
tables: XIV. General Attribution of the Tarot

lastal-m-m.summary: The formula of LA and AL—Naught and All—the two thirty-ones balanced at the Veils.
lastal-m-m.description: LASTAL belongs to the Veils of the Negative, the unmanifest beyond Kether, and it encodes Crowley's deepest doctrine of the two words whose value is 31: LA, meaning "not" or "naught," and AL, meaning "God" or "the All." Read forward and back, LA-AL becomes LASTAL, the formula in which absolute Nothing and absolute All are revealed as the same point seen from either side of the Abyss—"the Naught and the All are one." It is the supreme cipher of the Thelemic cosmos, the equilibrium at the root of being where existence and non-existence cancel into the silent zero from which the universe is perpetually born.

lauda.summary: Lauda — a letter of the Coptic alphabet (l), which Crowley attributes to the path of Lamed (Libra).
lauda.description: Lauda is a letter of the Coptic alphabet — the script in which the Egyptian language was written in the Christian era, the Greek alphabet adapted to Egyptian speech. It is from Greek lambda. Crowley folds the Coptic alphabet into the great correspondence of letters and paths in 777 (Table LI), assigning Lauda to the path of Lamed (Libra) on the Tree of Life, so that the Egyptian-Christian script takes its station among the Hebrew letters and the keys of the Tarot.
tables: LI. Names of the Coptic Letters

laural.summary: The sun's laurel—Apollo's victorious bay crowning the solar sphere of Resh.
laural.description: Laural (laurel, the bay) is attributed here to the Sun (Resh)—the solar tree of Apollo, evergreen crown of victory, poetry, and prophecy. Sacred to the god of the Sun, its leaves wreathed the brows of conquerors and the inspired, and gave the Pythia her oracular trance. Esoterically the solar laurel is the wreath of the illumined and triumphant will, the green emblem of victory worn in the light of the Sun.

laurel.summary: Apollo's victorious tree—the laurel crown of the poet and conqueror, solar glory of Tiphareth.
laurel.description: The Laurel (bay) is attributed to Tiphareth and Netzach, and it is above all the tree of Apollo—into whose leaves the fleeing nymph Daphne was transformed, and whose foliage thereafter crowned the god, his poets, his victors, and his prophetess. As the solar wreath of triumph and of inspired song it belongs to the radiant centre of the Tree and to the sphere of Venus and the arts. Esoterically the laurel is the green crown of the achieved work—victory, fame, and poetic afflatus made visible upon the brow.

tables: CXLIX. Magical Images of the Decans (Ascendent)

laza.summary: Laza — the blazing flame, second of the Arab hells, attributed to Hod.
laza.description: Laza, 'the blazing flame,' is the second of the seven hells of Arab cosmology, set in 777 at Hod. A fiercer fire than the Jahannam above it, it is in the traditional scheme the gate allotted to one of the classes of unbelievers, one degree deeper in the descending palaces.
tables: CXXV. Seven Hells of the Arabs

lead.summary: The saturnine metal of Binah — heaviness, time, the prima materia of the Work.
lead.description:
Lead is the metal of Saturn and of Binah, the formative Mother and the lord of time and limitation — heavy, dull, and base, the very type of dense, inert matter.
