For the alchemists it was the prima materia, the leaden base substance which, precisely because it is the lowest, holds the secret promise of the highest: the Work begins with lead and ends with gold. Esoterically it is the weight of mortality and form, the saturnine ground that must be confronted and transmuted.

Caution: lead is a cumulative poison; even small chronic exposures damage the nervous system. The alchemical symbolism must never be mistaken for a sanction to handle or ingest it.
lead.caution: Cumulative neurotoxic poison. Symbolic/alchemical entry only — do not handle or ingest.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

tables: CLI. Magical Images of the Decans (Cadent)

lebarmin.summary: Nocturnal angelic Lord of Sagittarius within the Fiery Triplicity.
lebarmin.description: Lebarmin is the night-governor of Sagittarius among the angelic Lords of the Triplicities. As the mutable member of the Fire trine by night, Sagittarius' flame turns to the fire of vision and dream, the arrow loosed in darkness toward distant and inward aims; Lebarmin presides over this nocturnal, prophetic fire.

left-arm.summary: The left arm of Adam Kadmon — Geburah, the smiting hand of severity.
left-arm.description: In the body of Adam Kadmon the left arm is attributed to Geburah, the fifth Sephirah, the sphere of Severity and strength. As the left arm is the arm that smites and restrains, it embodies the disciplinary, judging, force-wielding power of Geburah. Balancing the merciful right arm of Chesed, it is the hand by which the macrocosmic Man imposes limit, justice, and correction.
tables: CIII. The Ten Divisions of the Body of God

left-brain.summary: The left side of the head of Adam Kadmon — Binah, the supernal Mother.
left-brain.description: In the body of Adam Kadmon the left side of the head — the left brain — is attributed to Binah, the third Sephirah and the supernal Mother. As Binah is the receptive Understanding that gives form to the creative impulse of Chokmah, it is placed at the left hand of the head, the side of receiving and of form. Together the two sides of the brain figure the supernal Father and Mother whose union conceives the created world.
tables: CIII. The Ten Divisions of the Body of God

left-leg.summary: The left leg of Adam Kadmon — Hod, the pillar of form below.
left-leg.description: In the body of Adam Kadmon the left leg is attributed to Hod, the eighth Sephirah, the Mercurial sphere of splendour and intellect. As one of the two supports of the body, the left leg embodies the formative, ordering power of Hod in the lower world. Balancing the right leg of Netzach, it completes the pair upon which the macrocosmic Man stands.
tables: CIII. The Ten Divisions of the Body of God

left-lower-point.summary: The left-lower point of the pentagram, attributed to Earth.
left-lower-point.description: In the Attribution of the Pentagram the Left Lower Point is given to Earth (32 bis). As one of the four elemental points beneath the crowning apex of Spirit, it marks the station of the earthy element—dense, stable, the ground of manifestation. The lower points of the star are the heavy elements settled at its base; in ritual the strokes to and from this point invoke or banish Earth, the foundation on which the figure stands.

left-upper-point.summary: The left-upper point of the pentagram, attributed to Air.
left-upper-point.description: In the Attribution of the Pentagram the Left Upper Point is given to Aleph and Air. As one of the four elemental points beneath the crowning apex of Spirit, it marks the station of the airy element—mobile, intellectual, the breath that mediates between fire and water. In the drawing and tracing of the figure in elemental ritual, this point is the gate of Air, invoked or banished by the proper stroke from or toward it.

legs.summary: The two legs of the Perfected Man, the pillars on which the body stands and moves.
legs.description: The Legs are attributed to Pisces, Netzach, and Hod in the body of Adam Kadmon. As the legs bear the whole weight of the organism and carry it through the world, they correspond to the lower limbs of the Tree, the supports descending from the hips of Netzach and Hod toward the ground. In the symbolic body they are the means of the soul's movement and standing in Malkuth—the firm yet mobile foundation through which the upright human meets the earth.

lemures.summary: The wandering dead of Rome, set at the Moon — restless nocturnal shades appeased by the Lemuria.
lemures.description: Among the Legendary Orders of Being, the Lemures are attributed to the path of the Moon. In Roman belief they were the restless, formless spirits of the dead who wandered abroad by night, neither wholly malign like the larvae nor benign like the household Lares; the festival of the Lemuria was kept each May to placate them and drive them from the home. Their lunar attribution befits these creatures of the night and the shadow-world, the drifting, half-shaped dead who haunt the dark hours.

lencher.summary: Name of the second decan of Aries, where the Ram's headlong fire steadies into solar, established strength.
lencher.description: Lencher is Liber 777's name for the second decan of Aries (10°–20°), where the headlong fire of the Ram steadies into sustained force. The Sun rules this face, and its card is the Three of Wands—Virtue, or Established Strength—the moment the initiating spark of the sign proves it can hold and direct its own flame. Among the thirty-six Hermetic decan-faces inherited from the Egyptian star-clocks, this is the station of confident, solar will already at work.
tables: CLXX. Egyptian Names of the Succedent Decans

leo.summary: Fixed Fire, ruled by the Sun—sovereignty, creative power, and the radiant heart.
leo.description:
Leo, the Lion, is fixed Fire ruled by the Sun—the sign of sovereignty, creative self-expression, courage, and the radiant heart. In 777 it answers to the letter Teth and the path of the Tarot trump Lust / Strength (path 19), where a woman rides and masters the lion, the spiritual force tamed by love. It is the solar power made personal: dignity, generosity, and the will to shine.

The Lion has been the king of beasts and emblem of solar kingship across every culture—from the lion-gods of Egypt to the lion of Judah. Leo’s strength is wholehearted vitality and noble leadership; its shadow, pride and the hunger for adulation. It is the courageous, creative centre of the fiery triplicity.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

leopard.summary: The spotted beast of beauty and savagery, ranged across Libra, Capricorn and the Sun in the decan images—Dionysian splendour with claws.
leopard.description: The leopard appears among the magical images of the decans and in the bestiary of the grid at Libra, Capricorn and the Sun, a creature whose dappled coat makes it a thing of fierce beauty. Sacred to Dionysus, who rode upon panthers, the leopard unites grace and lethal power, the velvet and the claw—an apt emblem for the seductive, intoxicating face of force. In its solar attribution it carries the radiance and pride of the lion's kin; under Libra it is beauty poised over violence, and under Capricorn the patient ambush of the heights. The leopard teaches that splendour and danger are often a single skin.

leopard-s-head.summary: The magical image of Sitri — a leopard's head and gryphon's wings — Goetic Prince of the third decan of Cancer.
leopard-s-head.description: Sitri, the twelfth spirit of the Goetia and a great Prince, appears first with the head of a leopard and the wings of a gryphon, and at the operator's command puts on a very beautiful human form. In 777 he is set at the third decan of Cancer by day. He enflames men with women's love and women with men's, and will cause them to show themselves naked. The spotted predatory head joined to the gryphon's wings — soon exchanged for ravishing beauty — images the dangerous allure that stirs beneath the tender, watery sign of the Crab.

lerakhka.summary: The fourteenth spirit of the Goetia (Leraje), a marquis of Leo who stirs battles and festers wounds.
lerakhka.description: Leraje (here Lerakhka) is the fourteenth spirit of the Goetia, a great marquis of the decans of Leo. He causes great battles and contests, and makes the wounds of those struck by arrows to putrefy and grow gangrenous. He appears as a gallant archer clad in green, bearing a bow and quiver. A spirit of the martial fire-sign, he embodies strife, the loosed arrow and the festering hurt of war.

li.summary: Li, the trigram of Fire and clinging brightness — attributed to Tiphareth and the Sun.
li.description: Li (a broken line between two unbroken) is the trigram of Fire, light, and 'the clinging' — the sun, the lightning, the brightness that depends upon what it feeds on. In 777 it is referred to Tiphareth, Jupiter (Kaph), and the Sun (Resh): the radiant, illuminating principle, fittingly drawn to the solar heart of the Tree.

liber.summary: Liber, the Italic god of wine and fertility — the free one of vine and seed, at Spirit.
liber.description: Liber, “the free one,” is the ancient Italic god of wine, fertility, and male generative power, early identified with Bacchus-Dionysus. Referred to the place of Spirit (31bis), he is the liberating, intoxicating divine force that loosens bounds and quickens life. His festival, the Liberalia, celebrated the vine and the coming of age; he embodies the joyous freedom and fertile abundance of the god of wine.

liberality.summary: The recollection of generosity (cāga) — the contemplation of one's own openhandedness.
liberality.description: Liberality renders cāga, the recollection of generosity among the Forty Meditations, attributed to the bountiful path of Jupiter. The meditator calls to mind his own acts of giving and relinquishment, and in that recollection the heart grows glad, free of the meanness and grasping that bind it. Generosity is the first of the perfections and the natural overflow of a loosened heart; set at Jupiter, the planet of abundance and benevolence, it is openhandedness itself made a source of meditative joy.

libitina.summary: Libitina, goddess of funerals and the dead — patroness of the rites of passing, at Chesed.
libitina.description: Libitina is the Roman goddess presiding over funerals, corpses, and the business of burial, in whose grove the registers of the dead were kept and the undertakers had their seat. Referred here to Chesed, the merciful sphere, she governs the solemn, ordered rites that attend death. As the goddess of obsequies she embodies the dignified care and ceremony owed to the departed.

libra.summary: Cardinal Air, ruled by Venus—justice, balance, harmony, and relationship.
libra.description:
Libra, the Balance, is cardinal Air ruled by Venus—the sign of justice, equilibrium, harmony, and relationship, the only zodiacal emblem that is an object rather than a creature. In 777 it answers to the letter Lamed and the path of the Tarot trump Adjustment / Justice (path 22), where the scales weigh every act. It governs partnership, law, art, and the search for the fair mean.

Lamed means ‘ox-goad’ and is linked to teaching and direction; balanced against Aleph (the ox) it suggests the disciplined guidance of force toward right measure. Libra’s genius is diplomacy and proportion; its shadow, indecision and the avoidance of necessary conflict. It is the fulcrum of the zodiac, where karma is weighed.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

librabis.summary: Hidden gold — the Nuctemeron genius of the seventh hour presiding over hidden gold, set by Crowley at Libra.
librabis.description: In the Nuctemeron — the “Day Illumined by Night” ascribed to Apollonius of Tyana and preserved by Éliphas Lévi — Librabis is numbered among the genii of the seventh hour, the spirit of hidden gold. His province is gold concealed, the buried and secret hoard of riches. Crowley arranges the twelve hours and their genii upon the paths of the Tree (777, Table CLXXIII), placing him at Libra (Lamed).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

lice.summary: The Plague of Lice — the dust turned to vermin, attributed to Hod.
lice.description: The third plague, the turning of the dust of the earth into lice (or gnats), is referred in 777 to Hod, the sphere of Mercury. The minute, multiplying, irritating swarm — bred from the very dust — is given to the mercurial sphere of the small, the many, and the restless.
tables: CXXII. The Ten Plagues of Egypt

light.summary: The light kasiṇa (āloka) — radiance itself taken as the object of absorption.
light.description: Light is the luminosity-kasiṇa (āloka-kasiṇa) of the Forty Meditations, attributed to the path of the Sun. Here the support is not a coloured disc but radiance itself — a patch of light, or the brightness seen through an aperture — held in attention until an inner luminosity arises and steadies the mind. Of all the kasiṇas the light-disc is most naturally allied to clarity and to the dispelling of dullness; in the solar position it figures the illuminated consciousness, the mind made bright and one-pointed.

lign-aloes.summary: The precious aromatic wood of Sagittarius—lign-aloes (agarwood), rare and lifting smoke of aspiration.
lign-aloes.description: Lign-aloes (agarwood, the "wood of aloes," or oud) is attributed to Sagittarius (Samekh, Art). The dark resinous heartwood, born when the aquilaria is wounded and infected, yields one of the rarest and most prized of all incenses—deep, sweet, and lifting—named among the fragrant woods of scripture. Its precious, far-sought, elevating character suits the aspiring, questing sign of the Archer. Esoterically lign-aloes is the rare perfume of aspiration: the wounded wood whose smoke rises like the arrow toward the far and holy mark.

like-a-guide-to-be-kings.term: Like a guide. To be kings
like-a-guide-to-be-kings.displayTerm: Like a guide. To be kings

like-a-xenopilus.summary: The magical image of Gusion — given cryptically as 'like a Xenopilus' — Goetic Duke of the second decan of Cancer.
like-a-xenopilus.description: Gusion, the eleventh spirit of the Goetia and a great and strong Duke, is described in the grimoires (and so in 777) by the obscure phrase that he appears 'like a Xenopilus' — a word of uncertain meaning, often taken for a cynocephalus or dog-headed ape. In 777 he is set at the second decan of Cancer by day. He discerns all things past, present and to come, answers questions truly, reconciles friends, and bestows honour and dignity. The very vagueness of his image suits the veiled, shape-shifting sign of the Moon, where the form that is seen is never quite fixed.

like-agares.summary: The magical image of Vassago — given as 'like Agares' — Goetic Prince of the third decan of Aries.
like-agares.description: Vassago, the third spirit of the Goetia and a mighty Prince of good nature, is given in 777 (following the grimoires) the image simply of 'like Agares' — that is, after the manner of the fair old man riding a crocodile. In 777 he is set at the third decan of Aries by day. Of much the same office as Agares but bent to good, he declares things past and to come and discovers what is lost or hidden, and so was much used by scryers. That his very form is borrowed from another marks him as the gentler reflection of his fiery neighbour in the sign of the Ram.

lily.summary: The flower of purity—the Virgin's lily of Virgo, white emblem of chastity and the Supernal Mother.
lily.description: The Lily belongs to Virgo (Yod, the Hermit), to Binah, and to Malkuth—the white flower of purity and of the Virgin. In Christian symbolism it is the Annunciation lily, the bloom of immaculate conception held out by Gabriel; in the older mind it is the chaste counterpart to the rose's passion. Attributed to the virginal earth-sign and to the Supernal Mother alike, it signifies a purity that is not barren but fertile in its very chastity. Esoterically the lily is the cleansed and dedicated vessel, the soul made white and ready to receive.

lime.summary: The sweet-scented tree of Mercury—the lime (linden), airy and mellifluous, humming with the bees of Beth.
lime.description: The Lime (the linden, Tilia) is attributed to Mercury (Beth, the Magus). Its heart-shaped leaves and clouds of honey-scented blossom, loud with bees, give a light, airy, communicative character fitting Mercury; the flowers yield a gentle calming tea. Esoterically the lime is the mellifluous, sociable tree of the Magus—sweetness and gentle speech, the mercurial grace that soothes and connects.

limited-aperture.summary: The aperture kasiṇa — a bounded opening of light or space used to fix the absorbed mind.
limited-aperture.description: Limited Aperture is the space-by-aperture kasiṇa (paricchinnākāsa) of the Forty Meditations, set on the path of Sagittarius. The meditator gazes through a small hole or window — a bounded opening onto light or empty space — taking that delimited gap as the object until its counterpart-sign arises within. It is the practice that bridges the colour- and light-discs and the formless contemplations of space, the eye narrowing to a single defined aperture so that the mind may pass cleanly into absorption.

limitless-lvx.summary: Ain Soph Aur — 'Limitless Light' (LVX); the third Veil, the boundless radiance before Kether.
limitless-lvx.description: Ain Soph Aur (אין סוף אור), 'Limitless Light' — rendered here as Limitless LVX, using the Rosicrucian sigil of Light — is the third and last of the Veils of the Negative above Kether. It is the boundless infinite (Ain Soph) now conceived as radiance: the first stirring of the Negative toward manifestation, the endless ocean of light that concentrates itself, in the Lurianic image, by withdrawing (the Tzimtzum) to leave a space in which the point of Kether may shine forth. LVX is the formula of that Light — the boundless brilliance poised on the very threshold of being, the last veil before the Crown of the Tree.
tables: III. Translation of the Names of the Paths

linden.summary: Mercury's honeyed tree—the linden, whose fragrant, bee-loud blossom breathes the gentle air of Beth.
linden.description: The Linden (the lime-tree, Tilia) is attributed to Mercury (Beth, the Magus). Beloved across Europe as the tree of the village green and of lovers' meetings, its sweet blossom scents the summer air and its tea calms the nerves—an airy, mercurial, sociable tree. Esoterically the linden carries the same signature as the lime to which it is kin: the gentle, connective, mellifluous virtue of Mercury, sweetness shared upon the moving air.

linga-sharira.summary: Linga Sharira — the astral or etheric double, attributed to Yesod.
linga-sharira.description: Linga Sharira, the 'sign-body' or astral double, is in Theosophical doctrine the subtle, formative model upon which the physical body is built — the etheric template that holds vitality and sensation. Set in 777 at Yesod, the foundation and the astral sphere of the Tree, it is the ghostly mould of the flesh, the link between the dense body and the higher principles.

lingam.summary: The phallic emblem of the creative force—the Wand of Chokmah, the divine Yod, generative power at its source.
lingam.description: The lingam is the upright emblem of the male generative power, attributed in the grid to Chokmah, the supernal Father, and to the fiery, initiating positions of Aries and the foundational Yesod. As the phallus of the god—Shiva's lingam, the raised wand—it is the very image of the creative impulse going forth, the first outpouring of force from the unmanifest, the divine Yod from which all else is begotten. Its placement at Chokmah, the Wisdom that is the primal masculine, marks it as the cosmic seed-power itself. Esoterically the lingam is not crude sexuality but the sacred principle of creative projection, the will to bring forth—the same force whether it engenders a child, a world, or a Work, ever to be reverenced as the channel of the life that flows from the highest.
tables: XXII. Small Selection of Hindu Deities

lion.summary: The Lion-Kerub of Fire and Leo—solar courage, the royal beast of Tiphareth and the Sun.
lion.description:
The Lion is the Kerub of Fire and the beast of Leo, the Sun's own sign—royal, courageous, the fierce vitality of the heart. At Tiphareth and the Sun (Resh) he is the solar king, the radiant power of the harmonised centre, the golden beast crowned at the middle of the Tree.

On the path of Strength or Lust (Teth, Leo) the Lion is the wild force mastered by the woman who rides him—passion not killed but governed and made joyous by love. Esoterically the Lion is the noble fire of the will, courage made flesh, the daylight counterpart to the serpent: the energy of life raised to its kingly, solar height.

lion-faced-man-riding-a-bear.summary: The magical image of Purson — a lion-faced man riding a bear, a viper in hand — Goetic King of the second decan of Libra.
lion-faced-man-riding-a-bear.description: Purson, the twentieth spirit of the Goetia and a great King, comes with a lion's face, carrying a cruel viper in his hand and riding upon a bear, while trumpets sound before him. In 777 he is set at the second decan of Libra by day. He knows hidden things, discovers treasure, tells past, present and to come, and gives good familiars. The royal man crowned with a lion's face yet borne by the lumbering bear images sovereign judgement riding upon brute strength — fit for the Balance weighing force against right.

lion-on-black-horse-carrying-viper.term: Lion on black horse carrying viper
lion-on-black-horse-carrying-viper.displayTerm: Lion on black horse carrying viper
lion-on-black-horse-carrying-viper.summary: The magical image of Vine — a lion upon a black horse, bearing a viper — Goetic King and Earl of the third decan of Gemini (by night).
lion-on-black-horse-carrying-viper.description: Vine (Vinea), the forty-fifth spirit of the Goetia, both King and Earl, appears as a lion (or lion-headed man) riding upon a black horse and carrying a viper in his hand. In 777 he is the nocturnal ruler of the third decan of Gemini. He discovers hidden things, reveals witches and wizards, tells things past, present and to come, builds towers, throws down walls, and makes the waters stormy. The lion upon the black steed gripping the serpent befits the dual, knowledge-seeking sign of the Twins — sovereign insight that uncovers every concealment. (For his fuller office see the entry on Vine.)

lion-on-horse.summary: The magical image of Orias — a lion upon a horse, with a serpent's tail and two hissing serpents in hand — Goetic Marquis of the second decan of Scorpio (by night).
lion-on-horse.description: Orias (Oriax), the fifty-ninth spirit of the Goetia and a great Marquis, appears as a lion (or lion-faced man) riding upon a strong horse, his own tail that of a serpent, holding in his right hand two great hissing serpents. In 777 he is the nocturnal ruler of the second decan of Scorpio. He teaches the virtues of the stars and the mansions of the planets, transforms men, gives dignities and prelacies, and wins the favour of friends and foes. The serpent-handed lion befits the venomous, star-wise depths of the Scorpion — power over the heavens held in coils of snakes.

lion-s-eye.summary: Lion's Eye — the English meaning of the eighth lunar mansion (Tarf), at the eye of Leo.
lion-s-eye.description: 'Lion's Eye' is the English gloss of Tarf (الطرف, 'the eye [or glance]'), the eighth Arabic lunar mansion, marking the bright stars at the head of Leo — principally κ Cancri and λ Leonis, the leonine eye. In the lunar-mansion tradition Tarf is associated with the piercing gaze that startles and turns back — magically with the breaking of enmity and the disordering of enemies. Crowley places it on the Cheth/Cancer path. See also: Tarf.
tables: CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon

lion-s-forehead.summary: Lion's Forehead — the English meaning of the ninth lunar mansion (Jabhah), at the forehead of Leo.
lion-s-forehead.description: 'Lion's Forehead' is the English gloss of Jabhah (الجبهة, 'the brow'), the ninth Arabic lunar mansion, marking the bright stars at the forehead of Leo — ζ, γ, η, and α Leonis (Regulus). Of all the manzils Jabhah carries one of the strongest royal-solar valences, anchored as it is on Regulus, the 'Little King.' Traditional mansion-magic links it to the strengthening of authority, the favour of kings, and the success of public undertakings. Crowley fixes it on the Cheth/Cancer path. See also: Jabhah (30°).
tables: CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon

lion-s-mane.summary: Lion's Mane — the English meaning of the tenth lunar mansion (Zubrah), at the mane of Leo.
lion-s-mane.description: 'Lion's Mane' is the English gloss of Zubrah (الزبرة, 'the mane'), the tenth Arabic lunar mansion, marked by δ and θ Leonis at the great curl of the lion's neck. In the traditional mansion-tables the Moon passing through Zubrah is favourable for the consolidation of strength, the conducting of armies, and the building of one's reputation — the mane being the visible sign of leonine power. Crowley sets it at the Teth/Leo path. See also: Zubrah.
tables: CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon

lion-s-nose.summary: Lion's Nose — the English meaning of one of the leonine lunar mansions, at the muzzle of Leo.
lion-s-nose.description: 'Lion's Nose' is one of the English glosses given in the lunar-mansion tradition for the leonine sector of the zodiac, naming the mansion marked at the lion's muzzle. The 'Eye,' 'Forehead,' 'Nose,' and 'Mane' mansions cluster across Cancer and Leo in different orderings depending on which Arabic source one follows; Crowley's table CLXXIV preserves the Lion's Nose as a distinct cell in the Cancer column. The entry records the English etymology — the named feature of the celestial Lion at this point — without forcing it onto a single Arabic name where the source-tradition itself varies.
tables: CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon

lion-with-ass-s-head.summary: The magical image of Valefor — a lion with an ass's head, bellowing — Goetic Duke of the third decan of Taurus.
lion-with-ass-s-head.description: Valefor, the sixth spirit of the Goetia and a mighty Duke, appears in the shape of a lion with the head of an ass, bellowing. In 777 he rules the third decan of Taurus by day. He is a good familiar to those he is bound to, yet tempts those who keep his company to steal, and so is called a thief and a tempter. The royal lion saddled with the braying ass's head images the strength of the Bull yoked to stubborn appetite — nobility and base craving in one bellowing form.

lion-with-gryphon-s-wings.summary: The magical image of Vapula — a lion with the wings of a gryphon — Goetic Duke of the third decan of Scorpio (by night).
lion-with-gryphon-s-wings.description: Vapula (Naphula), the sixtieth spirit of the Goetia and a great, strong Duke, appears as a lion with the wings of a gryphon. In 777 he is the nocturnal ruler of the third decan of Scorpio. He makes men knowing in all handicrafts and professions, and in philosophy and the sciences. The winged lion — earthbound strength given flight — befits the penetrating, transforming sign of the Scorpion, where mastery is raised from instinct to art.

little-horse.summary: The magical image of Gamigin — a little horse or ass — Goetic Marquis of the first decan of Taurus.
little-horse.description: Under this form the spirit Gamigin (Samigina), the fourth spirit of the Goetia and a great Marquis, first shows himself when evoked: a little horse or an ass, before changing into human shape and speaking with a hoarse voice. In 777 he is the diurnal ruler of the first decan of Taurus. A teacher of the liberal sciences who gives account of the souls of those who have died in sin, his lowly equine image marks the patient, burden-bearing earthiness of the Bull's first face — the humble beast that carries the living and the dead alike.

liver.summary: The liver, attributed to Libra, the great balancer and filter of the body's chemistry.
liver.description: The Liver is attributed to Lamed and Libra in this table of the Human Body. The largest internal organ, the liver is the body's great chemical laboratory—filtering the blood, balancing its constituents, and transforming nutriment into usable form. Its attribution to Libra, the sign of balance and adjustment, befits this office of equilibrium: the organ that holds the body's inner chemistry in just proportion, weighing and refining what the system takes in.

loathsomeness-of-good.summary: The contemplation of the loathsomeness of food (āhāre paṭikūlasaññā) — perceiving the repugnance in eating.
loathsomeness-of-good.description: Loathsomeness of Good is the perception of the repulsiveness of food, āhāre paṭikūlasaññā — one of the Forty Meditations, here attributed to the path of the Moon ('Good' standing for 'Food' in the source). The practitioner reflects on the unlovely truth of nourishment: the seeking and preparing, the chewing and swallowing, the body's processing of food into waste, until the craving and heedlessness around eating are loosened. It is a sober, particular discipline aimed squarely at gluttony and at the subtle attachments of the appetite, turning the daily necessity of food into an occasion for dispassion.

lobster.summary: The armoured deep-dweller of Scorpio—the ancient crawler of the dark sea-floor, primal life beneath the waters.
lobster.description: The lobster is attributed to Scorpio, and like the crayfish it is an armoured, archaic crawler of the dark sea-bed, a creature of the cold depths encased in horn and armed with crushing claws. It belongs to the oldest, most primitive layers of life, dwelling where the light fails, and so it serves as an emblem of the deep unconscious and of the ancient instinctual powers that move beneath the surface of the mind. Under Scorpio it shares in the sign's themes of the hidden, the buried, and the slow renewal that comes of shedding the old shell. Esoterically the lobster figures the primordial life of the depths, the armoured archaic self that must, in its season, cast off its hard casing to grow.

locusts.summary: The Plague of Locusts — the devouring host, attributed to Chokmah.
locusts.description: The eighth plague, the locusts that devoured every green thing, is referred in 777 to Chokmah, the supernal Father and the sphere of the dynamic, all-pervading force. The vast, irresistible, sweeping host answers to Chokmah's character as the boundless outpouring of power — here become a consuming multitude.
tables: CXXII. The Ten Plagues of Egypt

loki.summary: Loki, the trickster of the Aesir — the shape-shifting bringer of cunning and chaos, at Hod.
loki.description: Loki is the ambiguous Norse trickster, blood-brother of Odin, a shape-shifter whose cunning both aids and imperils the gods, and who is fated to lead the forces of chaos at Ragnarok. Referred to Hod, the Mercurial sphere of intellect and craft, he embodies the quick, slippery, double-edged power of the mind unbound by scruple. At once helper and saboteur, he is the necessary disruptive cleverness within the divine order.

long-o.summary: The long 'O' (omega) sound — Crowley's English equivalent at Tiphareth in table LI.
long-o.description: The long 'O' is the English transcription of the Coptic Ⲱ (omega, the great 'O'), placed by Crowley at the sixth Sephirah — Tiphareth, the radiant solar centre. Where short 'o' opens narrowly, omega is the full open round vowel, the breath that fills the chest and resonates — fittingly the sound of awe, of the heart's exclamation, set at the heart of the Tree. In Greek theology omega is the closing letter, the Last; in Tiphareth's solar mystery the long 'O' is the sound of the perfected centre to which all paths return.
tables: LI. English Equivalent of the Coptic Alphabet
CL. Magical Images of the Decans (Succedent)

lord-of-hosts.summary: Lord of Hosts — the divine title Tzabaoth, the commander of the armies of heaven, borne at Netzach and Hod.
lord-of-hosts.description: “Lord of Hosts” translates the Hebrew divine title Tzabaoth (צבאות, “armies” or “hosts”), the name of God as marshal of the heavenly armies — the angelic legions and the hosts of the stars. In the Qabalah it is divided between the two lower pillars: YHVH Tzabaoth, “Lord of Hosts,” at Netzach, and Elohim Tzabaoth, “God of Hosts,” at Hod, the twin spheres through which the divine marshals the manifold forces of nature. The title also rings through the angelic liturgy of Yetzirah, in the Seraphic cry of Isaiah's vision — “Holy, holy, holy, the Lord of Hosts; the whole earth is full of his glory” — from which Crowley's Yetziratic table is drawn.
tables: XCII. The Angelic Functions in the World of Yetzirah
XXXVI. Selection of Christian Gods (10); Apostles (12); Evangelists(4); and Churches of Asia (7)

lords-of-kereba.summary: Lords of Kereba — Crowley's name for the divine guardians of the Reins (kidneys) in his Adam Kadmon body-table XXI.
lords-of-kereba.description: In table XXI 'The Perfected Man,' Crowley pairs 'The Reins' — the older anatomical term for the kidneys and the lower back, traditionally the seat of judgement and desire in Hebrew scripture ('Yahweh trieth the heart and reins') — with the parenthetical guardians 'Lords of Kereba.' The title 'Kereba' is not a standard Egyptological or Sanskrit name; it appears most plausibly to be a Hellenistic-Hebrew transliteration whose exact source-text Crowley did not annotate. The entry preserves the Lords of Kereba as Crowley fixed them: guardians of the lower trunk in the perfected body, placed at Netzach, Hod, and Aquarius — the Sephirothic seats of desire, intellect, and the airy fixed sign.

lorelai.summary: The siren of the Rhine, set at Aquarius — the maiden whose song lures boatmen to the rocks.
lorelai.description: Among the Legendary Orders of Being, the Lorelei is attributed to the path of Aquarius. She is the famed siren of the Rhine, a golden-haired maiden seated upon the great rock above the river who combs her hair and sings, luring distracted boatmen onto the reefs to their doom. A relatively late figure of German Romantic legend, she nonetheless belongs to the ancient order of water-sirens — the enchanting, fatal voice of the waters personified, beauty and destruction joined in a single song.

losanahar.summary: Angel of the first face of Leo, where the lion's fire meets contention and struggle.
losanahar.description: Losanahar rules the opening decan of Leo (0–10°), where Saturn meets the Five of Wands, *Strife* — fire under restraint, competitive struggle. Saturn's resistance to Leo's flame strikes sparks of conflict; the lion must contend before it can reign. Losanahar is the angel of the contest through which strength is tested and proven.

loss-in-pleasure.summary: Five of Cups — Loss in Pleasure; Mars in Scorpio, Geburah of Water: joy gone sour.
loss-in-pleasure.description: Loss in Pleasure is the Golden Dawn name for the Five of Cups, Geburah of the watery suit, Mars in the first decan of Scorpio. The severity of the fifth Sephirah, charged with Mars's force, disturbs the still waters of feeling: cups stand drained, the flowers droop. The card speaks of disillusion within delight — the discovery that what was sought brings less than it promised.
tables: CXXXIV. Titles and Attributions of the Chalice Suit

lotus.summary: The sacred flower of the waters—Binah's lotus, creation unfolding upon the abyss, the East's supreme emblem of the soul.
lotus.description:
The Lotus is attributed to Binah and to the element Water, and beyond even these to the Veils of the Negative—for it is the supreme flower of the whole system, the bloom that opens upon the dark waters of the deep. Rooted in mud, rising through water, opening to the air and sun, it is the perfect image of the soul's unfolding through the worlds. In Egypt the lotus bore the new-born sun; in India it is the padma on which Brahma is enthroned and the chakra-flower of the awakening body; for the Qabalist it is the cup of Binah, the Great Sea, in which form first stirs.

As an emblem of purity arising untouched from corruption, the lotus teaches that the highest beauty is born of the dark and formless. To meditate upon it is to contemplate the very act of creation: the still black water, and upon it the flower of light.

lotus-wand.summary: The banded wand of Virgo—the adept's zodiacal rod crowned with the lotus, the flower of unfolding wisdom.
lotus-wand.description: The Lotus Wand is attributed to Virgo, and it is the implement of the adept in the Golden Dawn tradition: a wand banded in the twelve colours of the zodiac, white and black at its ends, and surmounted by a many-petalled lotus blossom. By gripping it at the appropriate coloured band the magician attunes the wand to a given sign or force. The lotus at its head is the flower of the spirit unfolding from the waters, the emblem of growth into illumination. Its place at Virgo, the sign of careful, perfecting work, suits its precise and many-keyed nature. Esoterically the Lotus Wand is the refined instrument of the trained adept—the will made supple and exact enough to tune itself to every force, crowned with the unfolding flower of the awakening soul.

love-philtres.summary: The Venusian art of kindling love and desire by sympathetic magic.
love-philtres.description: Love-philtres are set at Daleth and Venus, the path of the Empress, sphere of love, beauty, and generative desire. As a magical power it is the working of attraction—through potion, talisman, image, or invocation—to awaken or bind affection between persons. Venus rules all the sympathetic bonds of liking and longing, and so the art of the philtre falls naturally under her dominion, though the tradition counsels that love compelled against the will is a violation that returns upon its worker.

lower-manas.summary: Lower Manas — the personal mind, attributed to the central Sephiroth.
lower-manas.description: Lower Manas is the lower, personal mind — the reasoning and desiring intellect bound to a single incarnation, the meeting-point of the immortal individuality and the animal nature. Referred in 777 to the central Sephiroth (Chesed, Geburah, Tiphareth), it is the everyday self of thought and will, which may turn upward toward the higher mind or downward toward the passions.

luck-of-lucks.summary: Luck of Lucks — the English meaning of the twenty-fourth lunar mansion (Sa'd al-Sa'ud), at the heart of Aquarius.
luck-of-lucks.description: 'Luck of Lucks' (also 'Luckiest of the Lucky') is the English gloss of Sa'd al-Sa'ud (سعد السعود), the twenty-fourth Arabic lunar mansion — and the most fortunate of the four 'sa'd' (luck) mansions of the great winter sector. Its principal stars are β Aquarii and ξ Aquarii in the body of the Water-Bearer. In the mansion-magic of al-Bīrūnī, the Picatrix, and Agrippa, Sa'd al-Sa'ud carries the strongest beneficent influence — favourable for marriage, for the freeing of captives, for prosperity and abundance. Crowley places it at the Ayin/Capricorn path. See also: Sa'd al-Sa'ud (30°).
tables: CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon

luck-of-tents.summary: Luck of Tents — the English meaning of the twenty-fifth lunar mansion (Sa'd al-Akhbiya), in Aquarius.
luck-of-tents.description: 'Luck of Tents' (or 'Luck of the Hidden Things') is the English gloss of Sa'd al-Akhbiya (سعد الأخبية, 'the luck of the tents/hiding-places'), the twenty-fifth Arabic lunar mansion, marked by γ, ζ, η, and π Aquarii — a tent-like quadrilateral in the Water-Bearer's body. In traditional mansion-magic it governs hidden things, secrets, and the revealing of what is concealed; its 'luck' is the discovery of what was sheltered out of sight. Crowley fixes it at the Tzaddi/Aquarius path. See also: ad al-Akhbiyah.
tables: CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon

luke.summary: Luke — the Evangelist of the Ox, attributed to the element of Earth (32-bis).
luke.description: Luke, figured as the winged Ox (Taurus/Earth) for the sacrificial, priestly theme of his Gospel, is set in 777 at the element of Earth (the path 32-bis). He is the kerub of the Ox's face among the four living creatures, the patient, sacrificial, earthward voice of the four.
tables: XXXVI. Selection of Christian Gods (10); Apostles (12); Evangelists(4); and Churches of Asia (7)

luna.summary: The Moon—reflection, tides, the unconscious; ruler of Yesod and the path of Gimel.
luna.description:
Luna, the Moon, governs reflection, cycle, and the tidal life of the unconscious. In 777 she rules the ninth Sephirah Yesod and the high path of Gimel that crosses the Abyss to Kether (the Tarot trump The High Priestess), making her both the lowest astral foundation and the secret road to the highest. Her metal is silver, her number nine, her creatures the dog, the hare, and the owl.

The Moon’s borrowed light and monthly phases make her the natural emblem of change, fertility, menstruation, dream, and the receptive feminine mysteries. As Diana–Hecate–Selene she rules the thresholds of birth and death and the magic of the night. Astronomically her gravitation drives the ocean tides—an apt literalisation of her dominion over all that ebbs and flows.
tables: CXXXIX. Planets Exalted in the Signs of the Zodiac
XCV. Contents of the Heavens of Assiah
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

lungs.summary: The lungs, attributed to Gemini, the airy sign of breath and exchange.
lungs.description: The Lungs are attributed to Zayin and Gemini. In medical astrology Gemini, the airy, dual sign, rules the lungs, the breath, and the bronchial passages—the paired bellows by which the body takes in the vital air and renders back its spent breath. As Gemini governs all that is twofold and all exchange and communication, so it governs the rhythmic give-and-take of respiration, the body's constant traffic with the surrounding air.

lust.summary: Atu XI — Teth / Leo; the ecstatic mastery of the life-force, woman riding the Beast.
lust.description: Lust (the older Strength) is trump XI, attributed to Teth and Leo, the path from Chesed to Geburah. Crowley renamed it ‘Lust’ to emphasise the joyous, ecstatic mastery of the life-force rather than mere restraint: the Scarlet Woman rides the seven-headed Beast, holding the Grail aloft, not subduing the lion but riding it in rapture. It is courage as wholehearted vitality, the spiritual will united with and exalting the animal power rather than suppressing it. The card teaches the sacred use of energy and desire—strength as the embrace, not the conquest, of the Beast.
tables: L. Transcendental Morality (10 Virtues; 7 Deadly Sins; 4 Magic Powers)
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

luxury.summary: Four of Cups — Luxury / Blended Pleasure; Moon in Cancer, Chesed of Water.
luxury.description: The Four of Cups, called Blended Pleasure by the Golden Dawn and Luxury by Crowley, is Chesed in the suit of Water and the third decan of Cancer, the Moon doubly at home. Pleasure here is stable and abundant, but the still waters begin to grow stagnant; comfort shades toward surfeit. It is happiness that has settled and risks becoming inert — the first faint weariness within ease.
tables: CXXXIV. Titles and Attributions of the Chalice Suit

lymph.summary: The lymph, attributed to Fire in this table, the clear fluid bathing the tissues.
lymph.description: The Lymph is attributed to Shin and Fire in this table of the Body. The clear fluid that bathes and cleanses the tissues and carries the body's defences is here set among the vital substances under the fiery element—perhaps for the quickening, defending heat it bears to the body's farthest reaches. With blood, breath, and the other humours it makes up the living fluids through which the elemental forces are distributed in the frame.

lymphatic-system.summary: The lymphatic system, attributed to the Moon, the body's tide of clear inner waters.
lymphatic-system.description: The Lymphatic System is attributed to Gimel and the Moon. The slow, tidal circulation of the lymph—the clear fluid that bathes the tissues, drains and cleanses them, and carries the body's defences—belongs to the watery, tidal Moon, ruler of all the body's fluids and rhythms. As the Moon governs the tides and the moist, receptive nature, so it governs this quieter inner sea, the lymph that ebbs and flows beneath the brighter tide of blood.

lynx.summary: The sharp-eyed wild cat of Netzach—the beast of piercing sight that perceives what is hidden.
lynx.description: The lynx is attributed to Netzach, the Venusian sphere of nature, and it is famed above all for its sight: to be 'lynx-eyed' is to see what others cannot, to pierce concealment and perceive the hidden truth. A solitary wild cat of the wood and mountain, tufted-eared and elusive, the lynx unites the feline self-possession of its kin with an almost supernatural keenness of vision. Esoterically the lynx figures the faculty of clear, penetrating perception within the realm of nature and feeling—the power to see through appearances to the reality beneath, the watchful sight that misses nothing in the green and shadowed world of Netzach.

ma.summary: Ma (Maat), the goddess of truth — the feather against which the heart is weighed, at Libra.
ma.description: Ma is a form of Maat, the goddess of truth, justice, and the right order of the cosmos, attributed to Lamed and Libra, the sign of the balance. Her emblem is the ostrich feather against which the heart of the dead is weighed in the hall of judgement. As Ma she is truth itself, the principle of cosmic equilibrium by which gods and mortals alike must be measured.

maat.summary: Maat, goddess of truth, justice, and cosmic order — the measure of all things, at Libra.
maat.description: Maat is the Egyptian goddess and principle of truth, justice, balance, and the divine order that holds the universe together. Referred to Lamed and Libra, she is the feather of truth on the scales of judgement, against which the heart of every soul is weighed. Pharaohs ruled by upholding Maat; the cosmos itself endures only so long as her order is maintained against the encroaching chaos. She is righteousness made a goddess.

mace.summary: The lacy spice of Mercury—mace, warm and aromatic, the nutmeg's bright veil upon the path of Beth.
mace.description: Mace is attributed to Mercury (Beth, the Magus). The lacy scarlet aril that sheathes the nutmeg, milder and brighter than the seed it covers, it is a warm, fragrant, subtle spice fitting Mercury's airy, refined, communicative nature. Esoterically mace is a delicate mercurial perfume—the bright, aromatic veil of the Magus's planet, warmth and sweetness made fine and articulate.

made-of-red-gold.summary: A heaven of the Arabs at Hod — a paradise fashioned of red gold.
made-of-red-gold.description: In the tabulation of the seven heavens of Islam, one of the ascending paradises is described as made of red gold, attributed to Hod. The heavens of the Arab scheme are each formed of an ever more precious substance; the red-gold material marks the splendour of this level of the blessed gardens, set in 777's comparative cosmology at the Mercurial sphere.
tables: CXXVIII. Seven Heavens of the Arabs, English

made-of-red-pearls.summary: A heaven of the Arabs at the lower Sephiroth — a paradise fashioned of red pearls.
made-of-red-pearls.description: Among the seven heavens of Islamic cosmology as set out in 777, one of the ascending paradises is described as made of red pearls, attributed to Yesod and Malkuth. Each heaven of the Arab scheme is formed of a precious substance; the red-pearl material characterises this level of the blessed gardens in the comparative cosmology, here aligned with the lower, earthward Sephiroth.
tables: CXXVIII. Seven Heavens of the Arabs, English

mag-sulph.summary: Epsom salt, attributed to Malkuth; the earthy purge and reliever.
mag-sulph.description: Magnesium sulphate — Epsom salt — is placed at Malkuth, the material Kingdom, an apt home for a common mineral salt of the body and the bath, used to purge, to ease aching limbs, and in medicine to calm convulsions and the dangerous seizures of pregnancy. Its earthy, bodily, thoroughly material character belongs to the tenth Sephirah and the world of the flesh. A relatively benign substance in ordinary use, though not without effect in excess.
mag-sulph.caution: Generally mild; excessive oral use causes purging and electrolyte disturbance.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

magic-mirror.summary: The scrying glass of Pisces—the dark speculum that reflects the astral, the still surface of vision.
magic-mirror.description: The Magic Mirror is attributed to Pisces (the path of Qoph, the Moon), and it is the instrument of scrying: the polished or blackened speculum into whose depths the seer gazes until the surface clouds and the visions of the astral light arise. Its place at the dreaming, lunar, watery path of Qoph is exact, for the mirror is a pool of still water made portable, a threshold onto the reflective world of dream and image. What appears in it is drawn up from the deep, and the seer must learn to tell true vision from the mind's own projection. Esoterically the Magic Mirror is the disciplined faculty of inner vision—the trained, passive, reflecting consciousness that receives the images of the unseen, the still dark surface upon which the astral light writes its forms.

magick.summary: Magick — the creative will itself, attributed to Spirit (31-bis).
magick.description: 'Magick' — in the table of functions, the highest power of the being — is given to Spirit (the path 31-bis), the fifth element that crowns and unifies fire, water, air, and earth. As Crowley defines Magick as 'the Science and Art of causing Change to occur in conformity with Will,' its placement at Spirit marks it as the quintessential function: the operation of the whole integrated being upon the world.

magister-templi.summary: 8°=3, the grade of Binah — Master of the Temple; the adept who has crossed the Abyss.
magister-templi.description: The Magister Templi, Master of the Temple, is the grade attributed to Binah, the Great Mother, attained by crossing the Abyss and pouring out the whole of one's blood in the Cup of Babalon. Having annihilated the ego in the gulf of Daath, the Master tends the 'garden' of disciples and comprehends the sorrow of existence with perfect understanding. It is the first of the truly supernal grades, in which the self has become 'none and two' — dissolved, yet able to administer the powers above the Abyss.

magpie.summary: The black-and-white chatterer of Gemini—thief of bright things, the dual gossiping bird of the Twins.
magpie.description: The magpie is attributed to Gemini, the airy sign of the Twins ruled by Mercury, and it suits that sign perfectly: a clever, restless, talkative bird, pied black-and-white in token of Gemini's twin nature, and a famous collector and thief of glittering trifles. The magpie's endless chatter and its magpie hoarding figure the Geminian mind in its lighter aspect—curious, acquisitive, quick, drawn to every shining novelty. Esoterically it marks both the gift and the danger of the restless intellect: the bright, gathering, communicative mind that flits from thing to thing, capable of wit and mimicry but apt, ungoverned, to mistake the glittering for the gold.

magus.summary: 9°=2, the grade of Chokmah — the Magus who utters the Word that creates a world.
magus.description: The Magus is the grade of the A∴A∴ attributed to Chokmah, the sphere of the creative Word and pure Wisdom. The Magus does not merely perform magic but becomes the living Logos, uttering the Word of an aeon and thereby fashioning reality itself, as Crowley held himself to have proclaimed the Word of Thelema. The grade is solitary and tragic, for the Magus, being the source of duality, is condemned to be misunderstood — truth, in his mouth, becomes the falsehood of all who hear it.

maker-of-fine-weather.summary: The Christian God at Tiphareth — the genial solar deity, maker of fair weather.
maker-of-fine-weather.description: At Tiphareth, the radiant solar centre of the Tree, Crowley's table presents the Christian God as the 'Maker of fine Weather' — the bright, genial, sun-bringing deity whose favour is warmth and clear skies. The gloss carries 777's gentle mockery of monotheism reduced to a meteorological convenience, yet it answers truly to the sphere: Tiphareth is the Sun, the harmonising heart, the source of light and life, and a god seated there is fittingly the lord of sunshine and benign weather.
tables: XXXVI. Selection of Christian Gods (10); Apostles (12); Evangelists(4); and Churches of Asia (7)

making-of-pantacles.summary: The earthy art of consecrating the talismanic disk, the magic of form and matter.
making-of-pantacles.description: The Making of Pantacles is attributed to Earth (32 bis), the element of body, manifestation, and the magician's own physical instrument. The pantacle is the disk of the elements, the consecrated symbol upon which the operator inscribes the forces to be condensed into matter; its making is the magical power of bringing spirit fully to earth, fixing an idea in a material form that radiates its virtue. As Earth is the last and densest of the elements, this is the art of completion—giving the work a body.

mako.summary: Mako — an Egyptian theophoric name Crowley lists at path 32 (Tav/Saturn) in table XIX.
mako.description: Mako appears in table XIX at path 32 (Tav/Saturn), among the Egyptian gods Crowley placed at the saturnine path. The name has no firm attestation in mainstream Egyptology under that exact spelling; like several of Crowley's more obscure XIX entries it likely derives from a late-magical or Coptic source (Mathers's papyri, or possibly a Greek-magical transliteration of an Egyptian theophoric ending in -ko, of which there are several). The entry holds the name as a placement-fact: an Egyptian title fixed at the path of Tav in 777, whose deeper source-text Crowley did not annotate.

malignant-woman.summary: The Malignant Woman — a qliphothic shell of the path of Qoph (Pisces), the deceiving feminine.
malignant-woman.description: 'The Malignant Woman' is among the translated names of the Qliphothic orders, set at the path of Qoph and the sign of Pisces — the path of the Moon's deceptive light, of glamour, nightmare, and illusion. The shell personifies the devouring, deceiving feminine of that watery, deluding station: the false enchantress of the astral twilight, the seductive phantom that lures the unwary into the world of shells.
tables: CXXIII. Translation of the Orders of the Qliphoth

mallow.summary: The soothing earth-herb of Taurus—mallow, soft and emollient, a gentle plant of the patient bull.
mallow.description: The Mallow is attributed to Taurus (Vav, the Hierophant). A soft-leaved, mucilaginous herb whose soothing emollient virtue eases and calms, it suits the fixed earthy sign of comfort, nourishment, and patient growth; its kin the marsh-mallow gave its name to the sweet. Esoterically the mallow is the gentle, fertile earthiness of Taurus—the homely plant of soothing and sustenance, the bull's quiet kindliness in leaf.

malphas.summary: The thirty-ninth spirit of the Goetia, a crow-formed president of Aries who builds, destroys enemies, and deceives.
malphas.description: Malphas is the thirty-ninth spirit of the Goetia, a mighty president of the decans of Aries. He builds houses and high towers, brings the artificers and possessions of enemies, gives good familiars, and reveals the thoughts and designs of foes. He receives sacrifices kindly but will deceive the one who offers them. He appears as a crow, then in human form, speaking with a hoarse voice. A spirit of the fiery sign, he is at once the builder, the spy upon enemies and the deceiver of his suppliants.

man.summary: The microcosm and the Man-Kerub of Aquarius—humanity as the image and measure of the whole.
man.description:
Man appears across the grid as both the Kerub of Air—the fixed sign Aquarius, whose emblem among the four holy living creatures (the Man, the Bull, the Lion, the Eagle) is the human face—and as the recurring "Image" of several paths. As Kerub he is the airy, rational power among the four elements, the knower who stands upright between earth and heaven.

In Qabalah Man is the microcosm: Adam, made in the divine image and so containing the whole Tree within himself, the creature in whom the axiom "as above, so below" is written in the very form. To meditate on Man in 777 is to meditate on the human being as the meeting-point of all the correspondences—the one being in whom the entire system becomes self-aware.

man-holding-a-great-serpent.summary: The magical image of Andromalius — a man holding a great serpent — Goetic Earl of the third decan of Pisces (by night).
man-holding-a-great-serpent.description: Andromalius, the seventy-second and last spirit of the Goetia and a mighty Earl, appears as a man holding a great serpent in his hand. In 777 he is the nocturnal ruler of the third decan of Pisces, closing the round of the seventy-two. He brings back the thief and the stolen goods, discovers all wickedness and underhand dealing, punishes thieves and the wicked, and finds out hidden treasures. The man gripping the great serpent — mastery laid upon the deceiver — befits the final face of the Fishes, the end of the zodiac, where what is hidden is brought to light and set right.

man-with-3-heads-a-serpent-s.term: Man with 3 heads a serpent s
man-with-3-heads-a-serpent-s.displayTerm: Man with 3 heads a serpent s
man-with-3-heads-a-serpent-s.summary: The magical image of Aim — a man with three heads, riding a viper and bearing a firebrand — Goetic Duke of the second decan of Scorpio.
man-with-3-heads-a-serpent-s.description: Aim (Aym, Haborym), the twenty-third spirit of the Goetia and a great Duke, appears as a man with three heads — the first like a serpent, the second like a man with two stars upon his brow, the third like a calf — riding upon a viper and carrying a lighted firebrand with which he sets cities, castles and great places ablaze. In 777 he rules the second decan of Scorpio by day. He makes men witty in all ways and gives true answers of private matters. The triple-headed incendiary upon his serpent fitly embodies the destroying, transforming fire that smoulders in the depths of the Scorpion.

man-with-gryphons-wings.summary: The magical image of Focalor — a man with the wings of a gryphon — Goetic Duke of the second decan of Taurus (by night).
man-with-gryphons-wings.description: Focalor (Forcalor, Furcalor), the forty-first spirit of the Goetia and a mighty Duke, appears as a man with a gryphon's wings. In 777 he is the nocturnal ruler of the second decan of Taurus. He has power over the winds and the sea: he drowns men and sinks ships of war, though he will harm none if commanded to forbear, and he confessed the hope of returning to the heavenly throne after a thousand years. The winged man ruling wind and wave marks the earthy Bull lifted toward the upper air — fixed strength given dominion over the moving elements.

man-with-many-countenances.summary: The magical image of Dantalion — a man wearing many faces, a book in his right hand — Goetic Duke of the second decan of Pisces (by night).
man-with-many-countenances.description: Dantalion, the seventy-first spirit of the Goetia and a great and mighty Duke, appears as a man with many countenances — the faces of all men and all women — holding a book in his right hand. In 777 he is the nocturnal ruler of the second decan of Pisces. He teaches all arts and sciences, declares the secret counsel of any, knows and can change the thoughts of all men and women to his will, and causes love. The man wearing every human face at once befits the dissolving, all-encompassing sign of the Fishes — the spirit who reads and remakes every mind because he wears them all.

man-with-sharp-sword-seemeth-to-answer-i.term: Man with sharp sword seemeth to answer in burning ashes
man-with-sharp-sword-seemeth-to-answer-i.displayTerm: Man with sharp sword seemeth to answer in burning ashes

mandrake.summary: The man-shaped root of magic—mandrake of Yesod, fertility-charm and sleep-bringer that screams when torn from the earth.
mandrake.description:
The Mandrake is attributed to Yesod, the lunar Foundation of the astral and generative life—a perfect seat for the most magical of roots. Its forked root resembling a human body, the mandrake was reputed to shriek fatally when uprooted, to confer fertility (the "love-apples" of Rachel and Leah), to bring sleep, and to serve a hundred charms; it is a true plant of the foundation-world where vitality, sex, and dream are rooted. Esoterically the mandrake is the man-shaped life-force of Yesod, the root in which the generative and dream-bearing powers take half-human form.

Caution: the mandrake is a poisonous nightshade with powerful narcotic and deliriant effects. This entry is symbolic and historical and is in no way advice for use.
mandrake.caution: Poisonous narcotic nightshade; deliriant and dangerous. Symbolic/historical entry only — not advice for use.

mangrove.summary: The tidal threshold-tree of Pisces—the mangrove, rooted between sea and land in the dim waters of Qoph.
mangrove.description: The Mangrove is attributed to Pisces (Qoph, the Moon). Standing upon its arched roots in the brackish tide-zone, neither wholly of the land nor of the sea, it thrives exactly in the dim, in-between waters that Qoph and Pisces signify—the murky borderland of the unconscious and of dreaming sleep. Esoterically the mangrove is the plant of the watery threshold, living where solid ground dissolves into the deep, an image of consciousness rooted in the formless tide.

mania.summary: The Roman goddess-spirit of the dead, set at Aries — mother of the ghosts and the underworld shades.
mania.description: Among the Legendary Orders of Being, Mania is attributed to the path of Aries. In Roman religion she was an underworld goddess reckoned the mother or grandmother of the Manes, the spirits of the dead, and of the Lares — a dread power presiding over the ghostly hosts, sometimes invoked with the chthonic god Mania/Manius. As an order-name she stands for the company of the dead under their queen; her attribution to the fierce, initiating sign of Aries marks the primal, fearsome face of the underworld's maternal power.

manipura.summary: Manipura — the solar-plexus chakra of fire, attributed to Netzach.
manipura.description: Manipura, the 'city of jewels' at the navel and solar plexus, is the third wheel, seat of the element Fire and of will, power, and digestion. Referred in 777 to Netzach, it is the furnace of personal force and vital heat — the radiant centre from which the energy of the self is exerted upon the world.

mano.summary: Māna — the eighth fetter, conceit; the subtle measuring of self against others.
mano.description: Mano renders māna, the eighth of the ten fetters, conceit, attributed to Netzach. It is not coarse pride alone but the whole subtle activity of self-measurement — the comparing of oneself as superior, inferior or equal to others, the persistent residue of 'I am' that lingers even when gross self-view is gone. One of the higher fetters, it is uprooted only at arahatship. Set at Netzach, the sphere of Venus and of feeling and desire, it figures the tender, tenacious self-regard that colours even refined states of mind.

marax.summary: The twenty-first spirit of the Goetia (Morax), an earl and president of Libra who teaches astronomy.
marax.description: Marax (Morax) is the twenty-first spirit of the Goetia, a great earl and president of the decans of Libra. He teaches astronomy and the liberal sciences, gives good and wise familiars, and imparts knowledge of the virtues of herbs and precious stones. He appears as a great bull with the face of a man. A spirit of the airy Venusian sign, he is the patient instructor in the stars and the secret natures of things.

marbas.summary: The fifth spirit of the Goetia, a president of Taurus who heals, sickens, and reveals hidden things.
marbas.description: Marbas is the fifth spirit of the Goetia, a great president of the decans of Taurus. His office is to answer truly of things hidden and secret, to cause and to cure diseases, to give wisdom in the mechanical arts, and to change men into other shapes. He appears at first as a great lion, then in human form at the operator's command. A spirit of the fixed earthy sign, he embodies craft, the mastery of disease, and the power of transformation.

marchosias.summary: The thirty-fifth spirit of the Goetia, a fierce marquis of Pisces who is a strong fighter and true answerer.
marchosias.description: Marchosias is the thirty-fifth spirit of the Goetia, a great and mighty marquis of the decans of Pisces. He is a strong and valiant fighter and gives true answers to all questions. He appears as a wolf with the wings of a griffin and a serpent's tail, vomiting fire from his mouth, then takes human shape at the operator's command; it is said he hoped to return after a time to the order of the Thrones. A spirit of the watery sign, he embodies martial strength joined to a longing for redemption.

mark.summary: Mark — the Evangelist of the Lion, attributed to the element of Fire (Shin).
mark.description: Mark, traditionally figured as the winged Lion (Leo/Fire) for the desert voice and royal power with which his Gospel opens, is set in 777 in the path of Shin, the element of Fire. He is the kerub of the Lion's face among the four living creatures, the fiery herald of the kingdom.
tables: XXXVI. Selection of Christian Gods (10); Apostles (12); Evangelists(4); and Churches of Asia (7)

marnes.summary: The discernment of spirits — the Nuctemeron genius of the twelfth hour presiding over the discernment of spirits, set by Crowley at Pisces.
marnes.description: Among the genii of the twelfth hour in the Nuctemeron of Apollonius of Tyana, Marnes presides over the discernment of spirits. His province is the discerning of spirits, the telling of the true from the false and the holy from the unclean. Lévi gives the roll of the hour-genii in his Transcendental Magic; Crowley tabulates them along the paths of the Tree (Table CLXXIII), assigning Marnes to Pisces (Qoph).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

marrow.summary: The marrow, attributed to Spirit, the inmost generative core of the bones.
marrow.description: The Marrow is attributed to Spirit (31 bis), the quintessence above the elements. Hidden in the innermost hollow of the bones, the marrow is the deep wellspring of the blood and was anciently held the most concentrated essence of the body's life. Its attribution to Spirit befits this inwardness: the marrow is the secret, generative core of the frame, the most rarefied and vital substance, seated at the very centre of the earthy skeleton yet answering to the highest principle.

mars.summary: Mars—energy, conflict, courage, and severity; ruler of Geburah and the path of Pe.
mars.description:
Mars is the planet of energy, war, courage, and necessary destruction—the cutting, driving force that clears the field for new growth. In 777 it rules the fifth Sephirah Geburah and the path of Pe (the Tarot trump The Tower), and embodies the principle of severity and decisive action. Its metal is iron, its number five, its emblems the sword, the spear, and the colour scarlet.

As Ares–Nergal–Horus the avenger, Mars is the warrior god whose aggression, rightly directed, becomes protection and justice; wrongly directed, it becomes cruelty and ruin. The magician learns from Mars the disciplined release of force—the surgeon’s knife rather than the berserker’s rage.
tables: CXXXIX. Planets Exalted in the Signs of the Zodiac
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

mascarun.summary: Death — the Nuctemeron genius of the third hour presiding over death, set by Crowley at Gemini.
mascarun.description: Mascarun is the Nuctemeron genius of death. That “Night-illumined Day”, ascribed to Apollonius of Tyana and handed down through Lévi's Transcendental Magic, sets a company of spirits over each of the twelve hours of the magical day, and Mascarun belongs to the third hour. His province is death itself, the severance of the living soul from the world of the living. In 777 (Table CLXXIII) Crowley redistributes these hour-genii across the zodiac, where this spirit falls at Gemini (Zayin).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

mastho.summary: Delusive appearances — the Nuctemeron genius of the tenth hour presiding over delusive appearances, set by Crowley at Capricorn.
mastho.description: Among the genii of the tenth hour in the Nuctemeron of Apollonius of Tyana, Mastho presides over delusive appearances. His province is illusion and false seeming, the deceiving show that misleads the eye. Lévi gives the roll of the hour-genii in his Transcendental Magic; Crowley tabulates them along the paths of the Tree (Table CLXXIII), assigning Mastho to Capricorn (Ayin).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

mastic.summary: The clear bright resin of Mercury—mastic, clean and pine-sweet, a clarifying incense of the Magus's path.
mastic.description: Mastic is attributed here to Mercury (Beth, the Magus). The pale tears of the Chios lentisk, chewed to cleanse the breath and burned as a clean, bright, faintly pine-sweet incense, carry the clarifying, communicative virtue proper to Mercury. Esoterically mastic is the bright perfume of the Magus—the clear resin of Mercury that sweetens speech and clarifies the air, the clean note of the quick and ordering mind.

mastick.summary: The clear chewing-resin of Mercury's signs—mastic of Gemini and Virgo, clean and bright incense of the airy mind.
mastick.description: Mastick (mastic) is attributed to Gemini and Virgo, the two mansions of Mercury. The pale, brittle tears of the Chios lentisk, chewed to sweeten the breath and burned as a clean, bright incense, it has a light, clarifying, slightly pine-sweet character fitting the mercurial signs of discrimination and speech. Esoterically mastic is the clear perfume of the discerning mind—the bright, cleansing resin of Mercury's airy and earthy houses, clarity made fragrant.

material-gain.summary: Nine of Disks — Material Gain; Venus in Virgo, Yesod of Earth: wealth multiplied.
material-gain.description: Material Gain is the Golden Dawn title of the Nine of Disks, Yesod of the earthy suit, Venus in the second decan of Virgo. Nine richly ornamented discs signify increase and the fruition of material effort: gain, profit, and the comfortable assurance of wealth well founded.
tables: CXXXVI. Titles and Attributions of the Pantacle Suit

material-happiness.summary: Nine of Cups — Material Happiness; Jupiter in Pisces, Yesod of Water: fullness of feeling.
material-happiness.description: Material Happiness is the Golden Dawn title of the Nine of Cups, Yesod of the watery suit, Jupiter in the second decan of Pisces. Jupiter's bounty pouring into the foundation of the waters yields complete and stable joy: nine full cups, well-being settled and assured. The card promises pleasure, plenty, and the satisfaction of the heart's desires.
tables: CXXXIV. Titles and Attributions of the Chalice Suit

material-success.summary: Six of Disks — Material Success; Moon in Taurus, Tiphareth of Earth: prosperity in balance.
material-success.description: Material Success is the Golden Dawn title of the Six of Disks, Tiphareth of the earthy suit, the Moon in the second decan of Taurus. Six discs bearing planetary marks circle a central rose-cross, the harmonious distribution of abundance. The card signifies prosperity attained and shared, gain that rests on balance and right proportion.
tables: CXXXVI. Titles and Attributions of the Pantacle Suit

material-trouble.summary: Five of Disks — Material Trouble; Mercury in Taurus, Geburah of Earth: strain and want.
material-trouble.description: Material Trouble is the Golden Dawn name for the Five of Disks, Geburah of the earthy suit, Mercury in the first decan of Taurus. The discs clash as ill-meshing gears, signifying the disruption of material order: hardship, financial strain, and the insecurity that follows when the foundations of the world are shaken.
tables: CXXXVI. Titles and Attributions of the Pantacle Suit

material-works.summary: Three of Disks — Material Works; Mars in Capricorn, Binah of Earth: foundations laid.
material-works.description: Material Works is the Golden Dawn name for the Three of Disks, Binah of the earthy suit, Mars in the second decan of Capricorn. Three discs form the apex of a pyramid against a dark ground, signifying constructive energy applied to matter — the disciplined beginning of building, business, and the practical realisation of a design.
tables: CXXXVI. Titles and Attributions of the Pantacle Suit

material-world.summary: The Material World — Assiah, the world of action and matter.
material-world.description: The Material World is Assiah, the lowest of the four worlds — the realm of action and of dense matter, the world we inhabit, where the divine pattern is at last made manifest (and where the shells, the Qliphoth, also cling). It is the world of the Daughter (the final Heh of the Name) and of the element Earth: the completed descent of the Light into form.

mathravash.summary: Angel of the first face of Cancer, where feeling first flows out to meet another in love.
mathravash.description: Mathravash rules the opening decan of Cancer (0–10°), where Venus meets the Two of Cups, *Love*. At the source of the watery trine, Venus in nurturing Cancer is tenderness itself — the harmonious meeting of two hearts. Mathravash is the angel of reciprocal affection at its birth, the first outflowing of the feeling-nature toward another.

matsya-avatar.summary: Matsya, the fish avatar of Vishnu — saviour of the flood, at Pisces.
matsya-avatar.description: Matsya is the first avatar of Vishnu, the great fish who warned Manu of the coming deluge and drew his ark to safety, preserving the seeds of life and the Vedas. Fittingly referred to Qoph and Pisces, the sign of the fishes and the deep waters, he is the divine saviour amid the cosmic flood. As the first descent of the preserver he sets the pattern of god intervening to rescue creation from dissolution.
tables: XXII. Small Selection of Hindu Deities

matter.summary: Matter — the material substrate, attributed to the element Earth (32-bis).
matter.description: 'Matter' is given in 777 to the element Earth (the path 32-bis) — the densest of the elements and the very principle of substance. Among the bodily functions and grounds, it marks the solid material basis of the organism, the earthy stuff in which all the other functions are clothed.

matthew.summary: Matthew — the Evangelist of the Man, attributed to the element of Air (Aleph).
matthew.description: The four Evangelists were anciently identified with the four 'living creatures' of Ezekiel and Revelation, the kerubim of the elements. Matthew, whose Gospel opens with the human genealogy of Christ, is the Man (Aquarius/Air) and is set in 777 in the path of Aleph, the element of Air — the kerub of the human face among the four fixed signs.
tables: XXXVI. Selection of Christian Gods (10); Apostles (12); Evangelists(4); and Churches of Asia (7)

mau.summary: Mau, the solar cat — the sacred feline who slays the serpent of darkness, at Leo.
mau.description: Mau is the divine cat of Egypt, the form taken by Ra to slay the serpent Apep beneath the sacred sycamore. Attributed to Teth and Leo and to the element of Fire, the cat embodies the solar power in its fierce, watchful, predatory aspect — the eye that sees in the dark and the claw that destroys the chaos-serpent. Sacred to Bast and to the sun alike, Mau is the guardian flame against the night.

maut.summary: Maut (Mut), the great vulture-mother — the divine consort of Amoun, at Binah.
maut.description: Maut is Mut, the great mother-goddess of Thebes, vulture-crowned consort of Amoun and mother of Khonsu. Referred to Binah, the supernal Mother, she is the archetypal maternal power, the womb of the gods. As the vulture she shelters and nourishes; as queen of the Theban triad she is the formative feminine principle through whom the hidden god's power takes shape.

me.summary: Me — a letter of the Coptic alphabet (m), which Crowley attributes to the path of Mem (Water).
me.description: Me is a letter of the Coptic alphabet — the script in which the Egyptian language was written in the Christian era, the Greek alphabet adapted to Egyptian speech. It is from Greek mu. Crowley folds the Coptic alphabet into the great correspondence of letters and paths in 777 (Table LI), assigning Me to the path of Mem (Water) on the Tree of Life, so that the Egyptian-Christian script takes its station among the Hebrew letters and the keys of the Tarot.
tables: LI. Names of the Coptic Letters

measuring-cohesive.summary: The Fourth Path — the Measuring, Cohesive Intelligence of Chesed, holding the holy powers in array.
measuring-cohesive.description: The Fourth Path is the Measuring, Cohesive, or Receptacular Intelligence (Sekhel Kavua), assigned to Chesed, the sphere of Mercy and Jupiter. The Sepher Yetzirah says it contains all the holy powers, and that from it emanate all the spiritual virtues with their most subtle essences. As the first Sephirah below the Abyss, Chesed measures and holds together what the supernals pour down — the merciful, organising love that gives stable receptacle and ordered cohesion to the emanations, the architect's gentleness that frames a cosmos.
tables: XIII. Paths of the Sefer Yetzirah

medicina-metallorum.summary: The Medicine of the Metals at Malkuth—the alchemical Elixir that heals the base metals and perfects matter.
medicina-metallorum.description: Medicina Metallorum—the 'Medicine of the Metals'—is attributed to Malkuth, the manifest kingdom, and it is an alchemical name for the great Elixir or Stone in its power to heal and perfect: the medicine that cures the 'sickness' of the base metals, transmuting their imperfection into the gold that is their health and completion. Just as the Elixir heals the body, so the Medicine of the Metals restores fallen matter to its perfected state. Its place at Malkuth, the sphere of the material world, marks it as the redemption of matter itself. Esoterically Medicina Metallorum figures the perfecting power of the Great Work upon the densest plane—the medicine that heals and exalts gross matter, the alchemical grace by which the fallen kingdom of Malkuth is cured of its imperfection and raised toward the gold of its true nature.

men-thu.summary: Men-Thu (Montu), the falcon war-god — the fierce solar warrior, at Aries.
men-thu.description: Men-Thu is Montu, the Theban falcon-headed god of war and the burning, victorious sun, here referred to Heh and Aries, the cardinal fire of the warrior. He embodies martial valour and the conquering heat of the desert sun; pharaohs invoked him for triumph in battle. As the bellicose aspect of the solar power he is the divine champion, swift and pitiless against the foe.
