menstrual-blood.summary: The lunar life-fluid—the menstruum of the Moon's path, charged in old and Tantric lore with the force of the feminine current.
menstrual-blood.description: Menstrual blood is listed among Crowley's lunar correspondences at Gimel (the High Priestess, the Moon)—a "perfume" not in any ordinary sense but as one of the magically charged bodily substances assigned to the lunar, feminine current. Bound by its very rhythm to the cycle of the Moon, it has been treated across many traditions—at once as taboo and as sacred—as carrying a peculiar generative and magical potency; in certain Tantric and Western sexual-magical systems it is held a sacrament of the lunar power. Esoterically it figures the raw feminine life-force tied to the lunar tides, the fluid in which the cyclic, generative mystery of the Moon is made flesh. This is a symbolic and historical correspondence within Crowley's system, recorded here for completeness.

menstrual-disorders.summary: Menstrual disorders at Gimel and the Moon — irregularity of the lunar tide.
menstrual-disorders.description: Menstrual disorders are set on the path of Gimel, ruled by the Moon. The Moon governs the tides, the waters, and the monthly rhythms of the female body; the menstrual cycle is her work made flesh, and its disorders are disturbances of the lunar tide within. Symbolically they figure a disruption in the great rhythmic ebb and flow of generation, the silver cycle of the Priestess fallen out of its measure.

menstrual-fluid.summary: The fluid of the deep—the menstruum assigned to Pisces, generative water of the dim lunar tide of Qoph.
menstrual-fluid.description: Menstrual fluid appears among Crowley's correspondences at Qoph (Pisces, the trump of the Moon)—a bodily, watery substance set in the dim, generative sign of the deep. Like the lunar attribution at Gimel, it belongs to the magically charged "perfumes" of the body that Crowley assigned to the watery and lunar currents, where the rhythms of generation and the tides of the unconscious meet. Esoterically it figures the generative water of the Piscean depths, the bodily tide bound to the Moon and the sea—the fluid of the formless, fertile deep. This is a symbolic and historical correspondence within Crowley's system, recorded here for completeness.

mental-formation.summary: The fourth skandha — the formations or volitions (saṅkhāra), the shaping and karmic activities of mind.
mental-formation.description: Mental-formation is saṅkhāra, the fourth of the five skandhas, attributed to the element Air. It is the most complex of the aggregates: the volitional and constructing activities of the mind — intentions, dispositions, habits and all the karmically charged movements that shape experience and forge the chain of becoming. Where feeling registers and perception recognises, the formations respond and intend, and it is here that karma is made. Its airy attribution suits the mobile, fabricating restlessness of the will, the wind that drives the wheel of conditioned existence.

mentu.summary: Mentu (Montu), god of war — the martial falcon referred to Mars.
mentu.description: Mentu is Montu, the Theban war-god, here referred to Pe and Mars, the planet of war and sudden force. Falcon-headed and sun-crowned, he is the divine warrior whose strength brings victory in arms. The Martial attribution fixes him as the embodiment of aggressive, conquering power, the fierce energy of battle made a god.

mercophta.summary: Presiding god of the third decan of Cancer, the lunar face where feeling settles into luxury.
mercophta.description: Mercophta is the presiding god 777 attributes to the third decan of Cancer (20°–30°). The Moon—Cancer's own ruler—governs this face, and it carries the Four of Cups, Luxury or Blended Pleasure: feeling grown comfortable, even sated, as the cardinal tide settles. The name belongs to the Greco-Egyptian list of thirty-six decan-rulers that underlies the Western system of faces.
tables: CLXXI. Egyptian Gods of the Zodiac (Cadent)

mercurius-hermaphroditus.summary: The hermaphroditic Mercury, the Rebis — union of Sol and Luna, at Kether.
mercurius-hermaphroditus.description: Mercurius Hermaphroditus, the hermaphroditic Mercury, is the philosophical Mercury in its perfected, two-sexed form — the Rebis, the 'double thing' in which Sol and Luna, male and female, sulphur and salt, are reconciled in a single body. Attributed to Kether, the Crown, it figures the consummation of the Great Work: the coincidence of all opposites in the original Unity, the alchemical androgyne crowning the Tree as the symbol of completed transmutation.

mercurius-philosophorum.summary: The Mercury of the Philosophers — the living secret agent of the Work, at Malkuth.
mercurius-philosophorum.description: Mercurius Philosophorum, the Mercury of the Philosophers, is not common quicksilver but the secret, living spirit that the alchemists held to pervade and animate all matter — at once the prima materia from which the Work begins and the hidden agent by which it is accomplished. Attributed to Malkuth, the Kingdom, it marks the divine spark concealed within the lowest and most material of the spheres: the gold that lies buried in the dross, awaiting the philosopher who knows how to release it.

mercury.summary: Mercury—intellect, language, magic, and exchange; ruler of Hod and the path of Beth.
mercury.description:
Mercury is the planet of mind, speech, commerce, and magic—the swift messenger and trickster who crosses every boundary. In 777 it rules the eighth Sephirah Hod and the path of Beth (the Tarot trump The Magus), and is the very patron of the magician’s art of names and signs. Its metal is quicksilver, its number eight, its creatures the ibis, the ape, and the serpent.

As Hermes–Thoth–Mercurius, this power presides over writing, translation, alchemy, and the guidance of souls between worlds (Hermes Psychopompos). Quicksilver’s restless fluidity is its perfect physical emblem—the principle that flows, connects, and transmutes, never fixed, forever in motion between the poles.
tables: CXXXIX. Planets Exalted in the Signs of the Zodiac
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

mercury-atop-venus.summary: The alchemical conjunction at Netzach—the sign of Mercury raised upon Venus, spirit wedded to love and copper.
mercury-atop-venus.description: This figure—the glyph of Mercury set above the glyph of Venus—is attributed to Netzach, the Venusian sphere, and it represents an alchemical conjunction: the volatile, spiritualising power of Mercury (quicksilver) joined to and lifting the receptive, loving nature of Venus (copper). In the language of the metals it marks the union of the mercurial spirit with the cuprous, generative body, the quickening of love and nature by the transforming agent. Its station at Netzach roots it in the sphere of desire and natural force, here exalted by the mercurial principle. Esoterically Mercury atop Venus figures the spiritualising of love and nature—the volatile transforming power crowning and raising the Venusian force, the conjunction in which desire is lifted and quickened toward a higher and more refined expression.

mercury-atop-venus-inverted.summary: The reversed conjunction at Hod—Mercury and Venus turned about, the mercurial sphere's mirrored sign.
mercury-atop-venus-inverted.description: This figure—the conjunction of Mercury and Venus shown inverted—is attributed to Hod, the Mercurial sphere that mirrors the Venusian Netzach across the Tree. Where at Netzach the sign expresses the spiritualising of love and nature, here in its inverted form at Hod it belongs to the realm of intellect and form, the reflected counterpart of the Netzach figure. Hod and Netzach are the paired pillars of the lower triad—mind and desire, the abstract and the concrete—and the reversed glyph signals the same forces read in the opposite register, mercury's own sphere claiming and turning the sign. Esoterically the inverted Mercury-atop-Venus figures the same conjunction of spirit and love seen from the side of intellect rather than of nature—the mirrored, formal expression in Hod of what Netzach expresses in living desire, the two spheres reflecting one truth in opposite ways.

mercy.summary: Mercy—the fourth Sephirah; benevolent order, the merciful king (Jupiter).
mercy.description:
Chesed (חסד, ‘Mercy’ or ‘Loving-kindness,’ also Gedulah, ‘Majesty’) is the fourth Sephirah and the first below the Abyss—the highest point the ordinary mind can readily reach. It is the merciful, organising, all-embracing love that follows the supernal formation: the benevolent king, the lawgiver, the architect who builds a cosmos that can endure. Its planet is Jupiter, its God-name El, its grade Exempt Adept.

Chesed is expansion held in trust. Its virtue is obedience and its vice is bigotry or tyranny—the danger of a mercy so settled it becomes complacent rule. Balanced against the severity of Geburah, it supplies the generous, stabilising pole of the cosmic order.
tables: III. Translation of the Names of the Paths
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

mermaid.summary: The magical image of Vepar — a mermaid — Goetic Duke of the third decan of Taurus (by night).
mermaid.description: Vepar (Separ, Vephar), the forty-second spirit of the Goetia and a great Duke, appears in the form of a mermaid. In 777 she is the nocturnal ruler of the third decan of Taurus. She guides the waters and steers ships laden with arms, and at the magician's word makes the sea rough and stormy and causes it to appear full of ships; she can also bring about death by wounds that putrefy and breed worms. The sea-maiden set in earthy Taurus marks the fertile, alluring deep — beauty above the waist and the cold tide below, that guides and that destroys.

mermaids.summary: The siren-women of the waters, set at Virgo and Aquarius — half-human dwellers of the sea between worlds.
mermaids.description: Among the Legendary Orders of Being, the Mermaids are attributed to the paths of Virgo and Aquarius. Across the folklore of every seafaring people they are the half-woman, half-fish dwellers of the deep, by turns alluring and perilous, luring sailors with their beauty and song toward love or drowning. As an order they figure the seductive, ambiguous power of the unconscious waters — the lower kingdom of feeling that draws the soul down into its enchantment, beautiful and dangerous in equal measure.

merota.summary: Presiding god of the middle decan of Scorpio, the solar face of deep regenerating pleasure.
merota.description: Merota is the presiding god 777 attributes to the middle decan of Scorpio (10°–20°). The Sun rules this face and it bears the Six of Cups—Pleasure—the welling-up of deep, regenerating delight at the heart of fixed water. The name comes from the Greco-Egyptian list of decan-rulers, the thirty-six faces by which the priests divided the year's nights.
tables: CLXIX. Egyptian Gods of the Zodiac (Succedent)

merti.summary: The Merti, the twin goddesses Isis and Nephthys, attributed to Gemini, the sign of the Twins.
merti.description: Merti—the “Two,” the double-goddess—names the paired deities Isis and Nephthys, the sisters who together mourn, protect, and reconstitute Osiris and who appear as twin uraei or as the “two eyes” flanking the throne. Liber 777 attributes them to Zayin/Gemini, the sign of the Twins—an exact correspondence, for the Merti are duality made divine: sister and sister, the bright and the dark, the two halves whose union restores the slain god. As the mourners at either end of the bier, they frame the mystery of death and resurrection in the symmetry of the pair.

merti-goddesses.summary: The two Merti — the divine sisters of the sanctuaries, commonly Isis and Nephthys.
merti-goddesses.description: The Merti are the two goddesses of the twin sanctuaries of Upper and Lower Egypt, the divine sisters who together guard the dual kingdom and the body of the dead. They are most often identified with Isis and Nephthys, the mourning sisters who stand at the head and foot of the bier and call the slain Osiris back to life. As a doubled feminine power they figure the two complementary aspects of the Mother, the binding-together of the divided land and the divided soul.

messiah.summary: Messiah — the Anointed deliverer, attributed to Netzach.
messiah.description: The Messiah, 'the anointed one,' is placed at Netzach, the sphere of Venus, of victory, and of the enduring love that conquers. The attribution casts the promised deliverer less as a martial king than as the triumph of desire and devotion — the victory (netzach means both 'victory' and 'eternity') of love over the world, the radiant hope that draws the faithful onward.
tables: XXXVI. Selection of Christian Gods (10); Apostles (12); Evangelists(4); and Churches of Asia (7)

messias-filius-david.summary: Messiah, Son of David — at Kether; the anointed one crowning the Tree.
messias-filius-david.description: Messias Filius David, the Messiah, Son of David, is set at Kether, the Crown and summit of the Tree. As the awaited anointed one in whom the line of David is fulfilled and the divine purpose crowned, he figures the supreme and unitive principle — the redeemer-king who stands at the very head of manifestation, the first and highest emanation made personal.
tables: XCI. The Saints or Adepts of the Hebrews

metallic-radix.summary: The root of the metals at Kether—the primal metallic first-matter, the seed from which all metals spring.
metallic-radix.description: The Metallic Radix—the 'metallic root'—is attributed to Kether, the Crown, and it is the alchemical name for the original first-matter of the metals: the single undifferentiated metallic seed or principle from which, by the working of nature and art, all the particular metals are held to grow and differentiate. Its place at Kether, the first emanation and the root of all things, is exact, for the radix is to the metals what the Crown is to the Tree—the undivided source before any distinction. From this one root spring lead and gold and all between. Esoterically the Metallic Radix figures the primal unity behind material multiplicity—the single metallic principle at the crown of the mineral world, the undifferentiated seed from which the whole hierarchy of metals descends, mirroring in matter the way all things descend from the One.

mexican.summary: Mexican — one of the pantheon columns Crowley reserved in 777 for future expansion, left unfilled.
mexican.description: Among the deity-tables of Liber 777 (XXV-XXXII) Crowley reserved columns for several pantheons whose attributions he had not personally worked out — Mexican, Mongolian, Syrian, Tibetan, West African, South Sea, and Zend among them. The 'Mexican' column was intended to receive the Mesoamerican gods of the Aztec and Maya traditions (Quetzalcoatl, Tezcatlipoca, Huitzilopochtli, Tlaloc, Xochiquetzal, the Hero Twins of the Popol Vuh) attributed across the Tree according to their elemental, planetary, and zodiacal natures. In 777 itself the column stands blank, an honest editorial placeholder — Crowley's marker that the Hermetic synthesis is unfinished and that whole world-traditions remain to be folded in.

mighty-terrible-one.summary: Mighty Terrible One — the divine guardian Crowley pairs with the Breast of Adam Kadmon at the heart of the Tree.
mighty-terrible-one.description: In Crowley's adaptation of Adam Kadmon (table XXI), the Breast — the seat of the heart, the centre of the body — is paired with the guardian title 'Mighty Terrible One.' The epithet itself is biblical-sounding (compare the gibbor nora of the Hebrew liturgy, 'the mighty and the terrible'), and its placement at the heart-Sephirah Tiphareth (with secondary placements at Aleph/Air and Teth/Leo, the airy and solar paths) fits the Qabalistic principle that the divine heart, when contemplated directly, is awesome — the still centre is also the seat of the most overwhelming power. The exact textual source of the title in 777 is not annotated; the entry preserves Crowley's placement as the meaning.

mikhael-offering-souls-of-the-just.term: Mikhael offering souls of the just
mikhael-offering-souls-of-the-just.displayTerm: Mikhael offering souls of the just
mikhael-offering-souls-of-the-just.summary: A content of the heaven Zebul at Tiphareth — Michael's offering at the heavenly altar.
mikhael-offering-souls-of-the-just.description: Among the contents of the heavens, the great prince Michael offering the souls of the just is set in Zebul, attributed to Tiphareth. The Talmud places in Zebul the heavenly Temple and altar where Michael, the celestial High Priest, makes offering — here the offering of the souls of the righteous, presented before the divine at the harmonising solar heaven.
tables: XCV. Contents of the Heavens of Assiah

millstones-where-manna-is-just-ground-fo.term: Millstones where manna is just ground for future times
millstones-where-manna-is-just-ground-fo.displayTerm: Millstones where manna is just ground for future times
millstones-where-manna-is-just-ground-fo.summary: A content of the heaven Shechaqim at Netzach — the mills that grind manna for the righteous.
millstones-where-manna-is-just-ground-fo.description: Among the contents of the heavens, the millstones that grind manna are placed in Shechaqim, the cloud-heaven attributed to Netzach. The Talmud (Hagigah 12b) says that in Shechaqim stand the mills that grind manna for the righteous of the world to come — a content kept in store against future times, the heavenly provision of the bread of the blessed.
tables: XCV. Contents of the Heavens of Assiah

minacharai.summary: Angel of the second face of Taurus, where steady labour ripens into material success.
minacharai.description: Minacharai rules the middle decan of Taurus (10–20°), attributed to the Moon and the Six of Disks, *Success*. Lunar nourishment within fertile Taurus brings the harvest in; the worry of the first face gives way to equilibrium and fair reward. Minacharai is the angel of prosperity rightly distributed — the season in which patient cultivation visibly pays.

minerva.summary: Minerva, goddess of wisdom and craft — the armed maiden of skill and war, at Aries.
minerva.description: Minerva is the Roman goddess of wisdom, crafts, and strategic war, counterpart of the Greek Athena, sprung from the head of Jupiter. Referred to Heh and Aries, the sign of pioneering force, she joins keen intelligence to martial readiness — the spear and aegis wedded to the arts and skills. Patroness of artisans, scholars, and warriors alike, she embodies disciplined wisdom and the mastery of craft.

minos.summary: Minos, king and judge of the dead — the lawgiver of the underworld, at Libra.
minos.description: Minos is the legendary king of Crete who, after death, became one of the three judges of the underworld, the chief arbiter who pronounces final sentence on the souls of the dead. Referred to Lamed and Libra, the sign of justice, he embodies sovereign judgement and the rule of law extended beyond the grave. In life the master of the labyrinth, in death he is the supreme magistrate of the shades.

minotaurs.summary: The bull-headed men of the labyrinth, set at Taurus — monstrous hybrids of human and bull.
minotaurs.description: Among the Legendary Orders of Being, the Minotaurs are attributed to Taurus, the sign of the Bull. The Minotaur of Crete — the bull-headed man begotten upon Pasiphaë and penned within the labyrinth, fed on youths and slain by Theseus — is the type of the order: the human form crowned with the brute head, reason imprisoned within and ruled by the animal. The Taurean attribution is exact, the bull made monstrous; esoterically the Minotaur figures the lower nature unmastered, the beast at the centre of the maze of the self that the hero must confront and kill.

miracles-of-healing.summary: The Mercurial power of restoring health by word, herb, and the laying-on of will.
miracles-of-healing.description: Miracles of Healing belong to Beth and Mercury, whose serpent-twined caduceus remains the emblem of the healing arts. As a magical power it is the restoration of the sick by other than ordinary means—the directed flow of vital force, the spoken charm, the sympathetic remedy—through the magician who has become a clear channel for the balancing intelligence of Mercury. The same swift god who governs the nerves and the breath governs their mending.

mishpar.summary: Angel of the third face of Virgo, where labour culminates in settled, inherited wealth.
mishpar.description: Mishpar presides over the closing decan of Virgo (20–30°), where Mercury, ruler of the sign, meets the Ten of Disks, *Wealth* — completed material achievement, fortune consolidated and passed on. Mercury perfects the methodical work into a finished, administered estate. Mishpar is the angel of the fullness of earthly riches and their right governance.

mishrath.summary: Angel of the first face of Sagittarius, where fire is loosed swift as the arrow.
mishrath.description: Mishrath rules the opening decan of Sagittarius (0–10°), where Mercury meets the Eight of Wands, *Swiftness* — the arrow in flight, rapid energy released toward its mark. Mercury speeds Sagittarius's flame into pure directed motion. Mishrath is the angel of the swift, aimed impulse, of force that travels straight and fast.

misnim.summary: Angel of the first face of Capricorn, where matter sets in motion the dance of change.
misnim.description: Misnim rules the opening decan of Capricorn (0–10°), where Jupiter meets the Two of Disks, *Change* — the flux of fortune, the perpetual juggling of gain and loss. Jupiter sets earthy Capricorn turning at the year's pivot. Misnim is the angel of the ceaseless balancing of material affairs, the harmonised motion that keeps the world's accounts in play.

misran.summary: Persecution — the Nuctemeron genius of the twelfth hour presiding over persecution, set by Crowley at Pisces.
misran.description: Misran is the Nuctemeron genius of persecution. That “Night-illumined Day”, ascribed to Apollonius of Tyana and handed down through Lévi's Transcendental Magic, sets a company of spirits over each of the twelve hours of the magical day, and Misran belongs to the twelfth hour. He is the spirit of persecution, the hounding and oppression of the hunted. In 777 (Table CLXXIII) Crowley redistributes these hour-genii across the zodiac, where this spirit falls at Pisces (Qoph).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

mistletoe.summary: The Golden Bough—the Druids' sacred mistletoe, growing between heaven and earth, Balder's bane and the key to the underworld.
mistletoe.description: The Mistletoe is given to Chokmah and to Virgo (Yod). Rootless in the earth and ever-green upon the bare winter oak, it grows in a place that is neither heaven nor earth, and so the ancients held it most holy: the Druids cut it from the oak with a golden sickle, and in the North it was the one thing that could slay the shining Balder. As Frazer's Golden Bough it is the talisman that opens the gate of the underworld. Esoterically the mistletoe is the spark of life suspended between the worlds—the wisdom (Chokmah) that is not rooted in matter yet lives upon the great tree, potent, paradoxical, and sacred.

mizgitari.summary: Eagles — the Nuctemeron genius of the seventh hour presiding over eagles, set by Crowley at Libra.
mizgitari.description: Mizgitari is the Nuctemeron genius of eagles. That “Night-illumined Day”, ascribed to Apollonius of Tyana and handed down through Lévi's Transcendental Magic, sets a company of spirits over each of the twelve hours of the magical day, and Mizgitari belongs to the seventh hour. He governs the eagles, the high birds of prey that hold dominion of the upper air. In 777 (Table CLXXIII) Crowley redistributes these hour-genii across the zodiac, where this spirit falls at Libra (Lamed).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

mizkun.summary: Amulets — the Nuctemeron genius of the first hour presiding over amulets, set by Crowley at Aries.
mizkun.description: Among the genii of the first hour in the Nuctemeron of Apollonius of Tyana, Mizkun presides over amulets. He presides over talismans and amulets, the charged objects that ward and protect their bearer. Lévi gives the roll of the hour-genii in his Transcendental Magic; Crowley tabulates them along the paths of the Tree (Table CLXXIII), assigning Mizkun to Aries (Heh).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

moist.summary: Moisture, the quality of fluidity and combination, root of Air and Water.
moist.description: In the doctrine of the four primary qualities, Moist (or Wet) is one of the two passive principles—the quality of that which flows, yields, and readily takes the shape of another. Combined with the active qualities it forms two of the four elements: Hot and Moist make Air, Cold and Moist make Water. Attributed here to the airy and watery paths, moisture is the principle of combination and adaptability, the binding wetness that joins and blends where dryness would separate.
tables: XI. The Elements and their Planetary Rulers

moly.summary: Hermes' magical herb—moly, the black-rooted white flower that warded Odysseus against the spells of Circe.
moly.description: Moly is attributed to Hod, the sphere of Mercury—and it is the very herb that Hermes gave to Odysseus to protect him from the enchantments of Circe, "black at the root, with a flower like milk." The gods' own antidote to sorcery, hard for mortals to pluck, it is the type of the protective magical plant; its place at mercurial Hod is exact, for it is Hermes' gift and a thing of cunning safeguard. Esoterically moly is the saving knowledge that breaks enchantment—the herb of the magician's protection, given from above against the powers that would turn the soul into a beast.

mongolian.summary: Mongolian — a pantheon column Crowley reserved in 777 for future expansion, left unfilled.
mongolian.description: In tables XXV-XXXII Crowley left a 'Mongolian' column among the pantheon-correspondences — intended to hold the gods of the Mongol-Turkic shamanic and Buddhist syncretic tradition (Erlik, Ülgen, Tengri the sky-god, the great mountain spirits) — and never filled it. The blank column is a candid editorial fact, not a meaning: Crowley acknowledged that 777's synthesis was Western- and Indo-centric and that the great Inner Asian traditions deserved their place. The entry preserves the column as Crowley left it: an open invitation rather than an attribution.

monoceros-de-astris.summary: The Unicorn of the Stars at Hod—the celestial unicorn, purity raised into the Mercurial heavens.
monoceros-de-astris.description: Monoceros de Astris—the 'Unicorn of the Stars,' the constellation Monoceros—is attributed to Hod, the Mercurial sphere, and it lifts the familiar emblem of the unicorn into the firmament. As the heavenly counterpart of the earthly unicorn it joins that beast's meaning of purity and concentrated single-pointed power to the intellectual, ordering nature of Hod and Mercury: a star-set figure of the chaste and unified mind. The phrase itself, in its Latin, carries the flavour of the old star-maps and the magical correspondences between the constellations and the spheres. Esoterically the Unicorn of the Stars figures the higher, celestial purity of the intellect, the single horn of focused thought raised among the lights of heaven.

monster.summary: Monster — a generic image-class in the magical-image tradition, the inchoate or hybrid form.
monster.description: 'Monster' (and the variant 'A Monster') is one of the catch-all image-descriptors that recur across Liber 777's magical-image and Goetia-image columns when the source iconography prescribes a hybrid, inchoate, or formless being whose features cannot be pinned to a single creature. Functionally it stands for the limit-form of the magical image — the moment at which the imagination passes from compound creatures (lion-headed snakes, serpent-tailed bulls) into pure protean shape-shifting. The entry registers the image-class as such rather than tying it to a single attribution.

monuphtha.summary: Presiding god of the third decan of Capricorn, the same solar face of consolidated authority.
monuphtha.description: Monuphtha is the presiding god 777 attributes to the third decan of Capricorn (20°–30°), the solar face the names-column calls Homoth. Bearing the Four of Disks—Power—it names the consolidated earthly authority at the close of the Goat's sign. The name comes from the Greco-Egyptian list of thirty-six decan-rulers.
tables: CLXXI. Egyptian Gods of the Zodiac (Cadent)

moonstone.summary: The shimmering feldspar of the lunar path — captured moonlight.
moonstone.description: The moonstone is attributed to the lunar path of Gimel — a feldspar whose soft blue-white sheen (adularescence) seems to hold moonlight within the stone, making it the very gem of Luna. It has everywhere been a stone of the Moon's mysteries, of intuition, dream, and the feminine tides; esoterically it is captured moonlight, the talisman of the High Priestess's path across the Abyss.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

moonwort.summary: The lock-opening fern of the Moon—moonwort, the lunar herb reputed to spring locks and loosen iron.
moonwort.description: Moonwort is attributed to the Moon (Gimel, the High Priestess)—a small crescent-leaved fern long wrapped in lunar magic, fabled to open locks and draw the nails from horseshoes, to gather silver and work silent wonders by night. Both its name and its lore are wholly of the Moon. Esoterically the moonwort is the secret, unlocking power of the lunar current—the quiet herb of Gimel that opens what is shut and loosens what is bound, working by night and indirection.

more-places-at-one-time.summary: 'Being in more places at one time' — one of the Western magical powers Crowley attributes to the path of Zayin (Gemini).
more-places-at-one-time.description: In table XLV ('Magical Powers — Western Mysticism') the cell at path 17 (Zayin/Gemini) names the power of 'being in more places at one time' — bilocation, the saintly and adept charism of appearing simultaneously in two or more locations. The placement is fitting: Zayin is the path of the Lovers, of twinning, of the doubled self. Western hagiography records the power for Padre Pio, Anthony of Padua, Maria of Agreda, and others; in Hermetic practice it is one of the marks of the adept who has stabilised the higher self across more than one localised vehicle.

mors.summary: Mors, death personified — the Roman embodiment of mortality, at Scorpio.
mors.description: Mors is the Roman personification of death itself, counterpart of the Greek Thanatos, the inexorable end that comes to all. Referred to Nun and Scorpio, the sign of death and transformation, he (or she) is mortality as a cosmic fact rather than a judging power. As the figure of death Mors marks the universal law of dissolution that no living thing escapes.

mosheh.summary: Moses — at Chokmah; the lawgiver and prophet who beheld the Wisdom of God.
mosheh.description: Mosheh, Moses, is attributed to Chokmah, the sphere of Wisdom and the creative Word. The lawgiver who spoke with God 'face to face' and brought down the Torah is fittingly placed in the supernal Father, the fountain of wisdom and revelation. As the prophet through whom the divine will was uttered to a people, he embodies the channel of pure Wisdom flowing into form.
tables: XCI. The Saints or Adepts of the Hebrews

moslems.summary: Moslems — sinful believers in the uppermost hell Jahannam, set at Malkuth and Yesod.
moslems.description: In the Arab scheme of the seven hells the (sinning) Muslims occupy Jahannam itself, the uppermost and least terrible of the seven — set in 777 at Malkuth and Yesod, the base of the Tree. In the tradition these are the believers who, purged of their sins, may in time be released; their place at the foot of the descending hells marks the mildest of its degrees. Recorded here as historical cosmology.
tables: CXXVI. Inhabitants of the Seven Hells of the Arabs

mout.summary: Mout (Mut), the mother-goddess as the breath of air — referred to Aleph.
mout.description: Mout is a form of Mut, the Theban mother-goddess, here referred to Aleph and the element of Air. In this attribution her maternal, all-embracing nature is figured as the encompassing breath — the air that surrounds and sustains all life, the mother as atmosphere. The placement links the great mother to the first and subtlest of the elements, the spirit-wind in which creation is cradled.

mouth.summary: Pe — 'mouth'; the organ of utterance and the lightning-shattered Tower.
mouth.description: Pe means 'mouth' — the organ of speech, breath, and devouring. It is the letter of the spoken word and of the breach through which sound (and ruin) erupts. In Liber 777 Pe is the path of The Tower (The House of God), attributed to Mars, joining Netzach to Hod. The mouth becomes the opened breach: the violent utterance of the war-god, the shattering speech that breaks down false structures, the lightning-mouth from which the destroying and liberating Word is hurled.
tables: III. Translation of the Names of the Paths

moving.summary: Moving — the function of locomotion, attributed to the path of Tav (Saturn).
moving.description: Movement — the body's power of locomotion — is given in 777 to the path of Tav and Saturn, the sphere of form and of the dense world. As the dancing figure of the World card (Tav) turns within its bounds, so the moving function is the measured motion of the body through the material world.

mud.summary: The lowest of the Seven Earths, set at Malkuth — the densest, miry ground of our world.
mud.description: In the Qabalistic doctrine of the Seven Earths (drawn from the Zohar), the cosmos is conceived as a descending series of seven lands, of which our own is the lowest and grossest. 'Mud' names this nethermost earth, attributed to Malkuth, the Kingdom — the heavy, miry, material ground of ordinary existence, the most clouded and inert of the inhabited worlds. It is the bottom of the cosmic descent, where spirit is most deeply buried in matter.
tables: CV. Ten Earths in Seven Palaces English

mugwort.summary: The dreaming herb of the Moon—mugwort, opener of visions and guardian of the night-traveller.
mugwort.description: Mugwort is attributed to the Moon (Gimel, the High Priestess). An Artemisia sacred to the moon-goddess, it is the classic herb of vivid dreams, scrying, and divination—placed beneath the pillow or drunk before sleep to open the lunar gates of vision—and a protective charm for travellers. Esoterically the mugwort is the herb of the lunar threshold, loosening the inner sight and guarding the soul as it passes into the country of dream that Gimel rules.

muladhara.summary: Muladhara — the root chakra at the base of the spine, attributed to Yesod.
muladhara.description: Muladhara, the 'root-support' chakra at the base of the spine, is the first of the seven wheels of the subtle body, seat of the coiled Kundalini and of the element Earth. In 777 it is referred to Yesod, the foundation of the Tree. It governs survival, rootedness, and the latent serpent-power that, awakened, begins its ascent through the centres toward the crown.

murmur.summary: The fifty-fourth spirit of the Goetia, a duke and earl of Virgo who teaches philosophy and calls up the dead.
murmur.description: Murmur (Murmus) is the fifty-fourth spirit of the Goetia, a great duke and earl of the decans of Virgo. He teaches philosophy perfectly and constrains the souls of the dead to appear before the operator and answer his questions. He appears as a warrior riding upon a griffin or vulture, with a ducal crown upon his head, preceded by his ministers with trumpets. A spirit of the earthy sign, he is the philosopher and the summoner of the dead.

murrain.summary: The Plague of Murrain — the death of the cattle, attributed to Tiphareth.
murrain.description: The fifth plague, the murrain that destroyed the livestock of Egypt, is set in 777 at Tiphareth, the solar centre. As Tiphareth is the sphere of the sacrificed beast and of the dying god, the slaughter of the herds finds a fitting, if sombre, place at the heart of the Tree.
tables: CXXII. The Ten Plagues of Egypt

muscular-system.summary: The muscular system, attributed to Mars, the body's engine of force and motion.
muscular-system.description: The Muscular System is attributed to Pe and Mars. The muscles, by whose contraction the body moves and exerts its strength, answer to forceful, martial Mars—the planet of energy, action, and physical power. As Mars is the warrior and the principle of dynamic force, so the muscles are the body's seat of strength and motion, the engine of every deed and effort, fittingly given to the red planet of vigour.

musk.summary: The primal animal perfume—musk of Chokmah and Capricorn, the deep warm base of vitality and generative force.
musk.description: Musk is attributed to Chokmah and to Capricorn. The classic animal perfume—warm, penetrating, profoundly sensual, the strongest and most lasting of the old fixatives—it carries the note of raw vitality and generative power proper to Chokmah, the supernal Father and primal active force, and to the carnal earthiness of Capricorn. Esoterically musk is the perfume of primal life itself, the deep warm signature of the generative current, vitality reduced to a single irresistible scent.

myrrh.summary: The bitter resin of sorrow—myrrh of Binah and Water, perfume of grief, embalming, and the mourning Mother.
myrrh.description: Myrrh is attributed to Binah and to the element Water. A bitter, dark, balsamic gum, it was the great embalming resin of Egypt, an incense of mourning and of the temple, and the Magi's gift that foretold the saviour's death—its very name a byword for bitterness and grief. Its sorrowful, watery, maternal character belongs to Binah, the Great Sea and the Mother of sorrows. Esoterically myrrh is the perfume of holy grief and of death accepted—the bitter smoke of Binah, in which mourning is made sacred and the body prepared for the tomb.

myrtle.summary: The bridal leaf of Venus—fragrant myrtle, sacred to Aphrodite, perfume of love and marriage.
myrtle.description: The Myrtle is attributed to Venus (and here also to Aries). Evergreen and sweetly aromatic, it was the tree most sacred to Aphrodite, woven into bridal wreaths and the garlands of lovers, an emblem of love, beauty, and married happiness. Esoterically the myrtle is the green and fragrant token of Venus—the perfume of love made constant, the evergreen of desire crowned and blessed.

naaim.summary: al-Na'a'im, 'the ostriches' — the lunar mansion in the Archer's stars, Sagittarius.
naaim.description: al-Na'a'im, 'the ostriches' (stars of Sagittarius read as ostriches drinking at the Milky Way), is the Mansion of the Moon set in the path of Sagittarius (Samekh). The old astrologers held it favourable for the taming of beasts and the building of trust, for hunting and for safe travel — its fleet, half-wild character belonging to the centaur-archer.
tables: CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon

naberius.summary: The twenty-fourth spirit of the Goetia, a marquis of Scorpio who restores lost honours and teaches eloquence.
naberius.description: Naberius is the twenty-fourth spirit of the Goetia, a valiant marquis of the decans of Scorpio. He makes men cunning in all arts and sciences, but especially in rhetoric, and restores lost dignities and honours. He appears as a black crane or crow, fluttering about the circle and speaking with a hoarse, raucous voice. A spirit of the watery sign, he gives back what was lost and teaches the persuasive tongue.

nail.summary: Vav — 'nail' or 'hook'; the joining-pin of heaven and earth, path of The Hierophant.
nail.description: Vav means 'nail,' 'hook,' or 'peg' — the fastener that joins things together, and in grammar the conjunction 'and' that links word to word. It is the letter that binds the upper Heh to the lower in the Tetragrammaton, the Son who unites Father and Bride. In Liber 777 Vav is the path of The Hierophant, attributed to Taurus, joining Chokmah to Chesed: the nail that fixes the divine to the human, the great connector and teacher through whom heaven is pinned to earth.
tables: III. Translation of the Names of the Paths

nantur.summary: Writing — the Nuctemeron genius of the eighth hour presiding over writing, set by Crowley at Scorpio.
nantur.description: Among the genii of the eighth hour in the Nuctemeron of Apollonius of Tyana, Nantur presides over writing. He presides over the written word, the letter, the pen and the secret of script. Lévi gives the roll of the hour-genii in his Transcendental Magic; Crowley tabulates them along the paths of the Tree (Table CLXXIII), assigning Nantur to Scorpio (Nun).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

napula.summary: The sixtieth spirit of the Goetia (Vapula), a winged-lion duke of Scorpio who teaches all crafts and sciences.
napula.description: Vapula (here Napula) is the sixtieth spirit of the Goetia, a great and strong duke of the decans of Scorpio. He makes men knowing and skilful in all handicrafts and professions, and in philosophy and the sciences. He appears as a lion with the wings of a griffin. A spirit of the watery sign, he is the bestower of skill in every craft and learning.

nara-singh-avatar.summary: Narasimha, the man-lion avatar of Vishnu — destroyer of the tyrant, at Leo.
nara-singh-avatar.description: Narasimha is the fourth avatar of Vishnu, the fierce man-lion who burst from a pillar to slay the demon-king Hiranyakashipu and protect his devotee Prahlada, neither man nor beast, killing at neither day nor night. Referred to Teth and Leo, the sign of the lion, he is the terrible protective fury of the divine, the wrath of god unleashed against tyranny. He embodies the ferocity that guards the faithful and shatters the proud oppressor.
tables: XXII. Small Selection of Hindu Deities

narcissus.summary: The self-mirroring flower—narcissus of Virgo, bloom of reflection, sleep, and the gaze that drowns in itself.
narcissus.description: The Narcissus is attributed to Virgo (Yod, the Hermit). Named for the youth who pined away gazing at his own reflection, its heavy, narcotic sweetness (the Greek narke, "numbness," lies hidden in its name) belongs to spring and to the flowers Persephone was gathering before her descent. Its self-regarding, dreamy, slightly stupefying character has an inward, solitary quality fitting the Hermit's sign. Esoterically the narcissus is the flower of reflection and self-absorbed reverie—beauty turned inward to the point of trance, the perfume of the soul gazing into its own still water.

nasrah.summary: al-Nathra, 'the gap' — Praesepe, the Beehive cluster, the lunar mansion in Cancer.
nasrah.description: al-Nathra, 'the gap' or 'the crib,' is the soft nebulous glow of Praesepe (the Beehive cluster) between the two Aselli in Cancer, set by 777 in the path of Cancer (Cheth). Its hazy, swarming light — a 'little cloud' to the ancients — gave it a reputation for things hidden, nurtured, and brought to birth, fitting the maternal, sheltering nature of the Crab.
tables: CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon

nathdorinel.summary: Nocturnal angelic Lord of Pisces within the Watery Triplicity.
nathdorinel.description: Nathdorinel — whose name closes on the divine ‑el — is the night-governor of Pisces among the angelic Lords of the Triplicities, and the last of the set. As the mutable member of the Water trine by night, Pisces is the dreaming ocean, the dark water of the unconscious in which the wheel of the signs dissolves and is renewed; Nathdorinel presides over this nocturnal, boundless sea that closes the round.

natural-intelligence.summary: The Twenty-eighth Path — the Natural Intelligence of Tzaddi, perfecting all beneath the Sun.
natural-intelligence.description: The Twenty-eighth Path is the Natural Intelligence (Sekhel Mutba, the 'inborn' Intelligence), attributed to the letter Tzaddi and the sign Aquarius, the path of The Star joining Netzach to Yesod (in Crowley's revised attribution following Liber AL). The Sepher Yetzirah says that by it is completed and perfected the nature of every existing thing beneath the orb of the Sun. It is the indwelling intelligence of nature itself — the starlight poured upon the waters, the natural order by which all sublunary things attain their proper form.
tables: XIII. Paths of the Sefer Yetzirah

navel.summary: The Navel — bodily seat of a subtle centre, attributed to Hod.
navel.description: The navel is given in 777 as the bodily location of a subtle centre, set at Hod. As the scar of the severed cord that once bound child to mother, it is a natural symbol of the centre of the body and of the formative life received before birth — here referred to the mercurial sphere of Hod.

navel-of-fish-s-belly.summary: Navel of Fish's Belly — the English meaning of the twenty-eighth (final) lunar mansion (Batn al-Hut), in Pisces.
navel-of-fish-s-belly.description: 'Navel of Fish's Belly' is the English gloss of Batn al-Hut (بطن الحوت, 'belly of the fish'), the twenty-eighth and final Arabic lunar mansion, marked by β Andromedae (Mirach) at the centre of the constellation of the Northern Fish. In the mansion-tradition it is the closing manzil — the last station of the lunar year — and is associated with the safe return of travellers, the binding of trade, and the consolidation of what has been long in process. Crowley fixes it at the Qoph/Pisces path, the final watery descent of the Tree.
tables: CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon

nd-order.summary: The Second Order — the adept grades about Tiphareth, from Tiphareth to Geburah and Chesed.
nd-order.description: The Second Order — the R.R. et A.C. of the Golden Dawn, the 'Order of the Rose of Ruby and Cross of Gold' — comprises the grades of the adept gathered about the solar centre: Adeptus Minor (Tiphareth), Adeptus Major (Geburah), and Adeptus Exemptus (Chesed). Its work is the great labour of Tiphareth, the Knowledge and Conversation of the Holy Guardian Angel, and the mastery that lies between the first attainment and the dread crossing of the Abyss.

nd-plane-left-pillar.summary: Second plane, Left Pillar — the geometric position of Binah, the supernal Mother.
nd-plane-left-pillar.description: The second plane on the Left Pillar (the Pillar of Severity) is Binah — Understanding, the supernal Mother, ruled by Saturn and the receiving womb of all form. In Crowley's geometric reading of the Tree (table XII) every Sephirah and every path has a definable position; Binah's place — opposite Chokmah and below Kether — is the topmost station on the dark, restraining pillar, the source of limit and shape.
tables: XII. Position on the Glyph of the Tree of Life

nd-plane-right-pillar.summary: Second plane, Right Pillar — the geometric position of Chokmah, supernal Wisdom.
nd-plane-right-pillar.description: The second plane on the Right Pillar (the Pillar of Mercy) is Chokmah — Wisdom, the supernal Father, the lightning-flash of pure masculine force that issues from Kether and meets Binah across the abyss. Crowley's 'Position on the Glyph' table places Chokmah at this exact intersection: the topmost station on the bright, expansive pillar — origin of expression, energy, and the Yod of Tetragrammaton.
tables: XII. Position on the Glyph of the Tree of Life

necromancy.summary: The Scorpionic art of commerce with the dead, the magic of the dark waters of death.
necromancy.description: Necromancy is attributed to Nun and Scorpio, the path of Death, where the mysteries of putrefaction, the grave, and the spirits of the departed hold sway. As a magical power it is the dangerous art of summoning and questioning the dead, or of working with the residual forces left behind by the dying. Crowley and the Western tradition treat it with caution: Scorpio's path can lead to the lowest sorcery or to the highest transmutation, and the same descent into death that breeds the necromancer's commerce with shades is also the gate of regeneration.

neith.summary: Neith, the ancient weaver-goddess — mistress of war and wisdom, at Chesed and Geburah.
neith.description: Neith is among the oldest Egyptian deities, the self-begotten weaver of the world, goddess of war, hunting, and wisdom, and the mysterious mother “whose veil no mortal has lifted.” Referred to Chesed and Geburah, the spheres of mercy and severity, she unites the kindly and the martial — the bow and arrows of the huntress with the loom of creation. She is the primordial creatrix whose veil is the great emblem of hidden truth.

neither-p-nor-p.summary: The fourth formless attainment — the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.
neither-p-nor-p.description: This is the fourth and subtlest of the formless attainments, nevasaññānāsaññāyatana — 'neither perception nor non-perception' — attributed to the Veils of the Negative. Here perception is so refined that it can neither be said to be present nor wholly absent; the mind hovers at the very rim of the conditioned, a stillness so attenuated that thought has all but ceased. In the Buddha's own account it is the highest of the mundane absorptions, the last station before the cessation of perception-and-feeling, and in the 777 ladder it stands among the negative veils that border the Unmanifest.

nemesis.summary: Nemesis, goddess of retribution — the balancer of fortune who humbles the proud, at Libra.
nemesis.description: Nemesis is the goddess of divine retribution and the just apportioning of fortune, who punishes hubris and restores the balance disturbed by excess. Referred to Lamed and Libra, the sign of the scales, she is the cosmic corrective that brings the over-fortunate low and avenges the wronged. As the personification of righteous indignation she embodies the inescapable redress of the moral order.

neophyte.summary: 0°=0 / Malkuth — the Newly Planted; the initiate's first admission to the Light.
neophyte.description: The Neophyte is the first grade of initiation, the 'newly planted,' admitted across the threshold of the Temple into the Outer Order. Standing at Malkuth, the Kingdom, the candidate is brought from darkness into the first contact with the Light and given the foundational instruction of the Work. It is the seed-grade from which all subsequent ascent of the Tree of Life proceeds.

nephthy.summary: Nephthy (Nephthys), the mourning sister — lady of the hidden and the threshold, at Binah.
nephthy.description: Nephthy is a form of Nephthys, sister of Isis and consort of Set, the goddess of the unseen, of mourning, and of the protective margins of life. Referred to Binah, the dark supernal Mother, she is the shadow-sister of Isis, lamenting the slain Osiris and guarding the dead. She is the silent, veiled feminine — the hidden side of the maternal mystery, present at every threshold of death and birth.

nephthys.summary: Nephthys, lady of the house and of the dead — Isis's sister, mistress of the hidden margins.
nephthys.description: Nephthys is the Egyptian goddess of the household, of mourning, and of the concealed edges of existence, sister to Isis and Osiris and wife to Set. Spread across Binah, Geburah, Sagittarius, and the place of Earth in Liber 777, she is the protective mourner who, with Isis, gathers and laments the dead and watches over the embalmed body. She is the dark complement to Isis's light, the keeper of what is hidden and the friend of the deceased.

neptune.summary: Neptune—mysticism, dissolution, dream, and the oceanic (modern planet).
neptune.description:
Neptune, discovered in 1846, was taken into the esoteric system as the planet of mysticism, imagination, dissolution, and the oceanic unconscious—the dissolver of boundaries between self and cosmos. It is associated with the highest reaches of the Tree (sometimes Kether or the element Water in its spiritual octave) and with visionary, devotional, and transcendent states.

Where Uranus shatters by sudden insight, Neptune dissolves by gentle merging; its shadow is illusion, glamour, and self-deception, its glory the genuine mystical union in which the separate ego is washed away. As lord of the sea it rules all that is fluid, formless, and infinite.
tables: CXXXIX. Planets Exalted in the Signs of the Zodiac
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

nereids.summary: The sea-nymphs, daughters of Nereus, set at Mem — gentle spirits of the salt deep.
nereids.description: The Nereids are an order of legendary beings, the fifty sea-nymph daughters of the old sea-god Nereus, attributed to Mem and the element of Water. Gentle and beautiful, they attend the Mediterranean's waves and aid sailors in distress; among them are Thetis, mother of Achilles, and Amphitrite, queen of the sea. As an order they personify the kindly, lovely face of the deep — the watery feminine spirits of the calm and bountiful ocean.

nerodha-samapatti.summary: Nirodha-samāpatti — the attainment of cessation, in which perception and feeling are stilled.
nerodha-samapatti.description: Nerodha-samapatti renders nirodha-samāpatti, the 'attainment of cessation' among the Hindu/Buddhist Results, attributed to the Veils of the Negative. It is the supreme attainment of the Buddhist adept: a temporary, complete suspension of perception and feeling — and indeed of mental activity altogether — accessible only to non-returners and arahats who have mastered all eight absorptions. A foretaste of Nibbāna while yet living, it is set among the negative veils as the deepest of the cessations, where consciousness itself is stilled.
tables: XXIV. Certain of the Hindu/Buddhist Results

nerve-troubles.summary: Nervous troubles at Hod and Mercury — disorder of the body's Mercurial network.
nerve-troubles.description: Nerve troubles are attributed to Hod, the sphere of Mercury. Mercury rules the nervous system, the communicating network of impulse and message that ties the whole organism together; nervous disorders are the static and disarray of that Mercurial web. As Hod is the sphere of intellect, language, and the rapid traffic of signals, its afflictions are precisely the frayed nerves, the agitation and miscommunication of the body's swift messenger-system.

nervous-system.summary: The nervous system, attributed to Mercury, the body's network of swift communication.
nervous-system.description: The Nervous System is attributed to Beth and Mercury. The web of nerves that carries sensation and command throughout the body is the very image of Mercury's domain—swift, branching, connective, the messenger-network by which every part is kept in instant communication with the whole. As Mercury is the god of roads, messages, and the quick exchange of intelligence, so the nervous system is the body's quicksilver web of transmission.

neththe.summary: Presiding god of the last decan of Leo, the Martial face of courage defending its won ground.
neththe.description: Neththe is the presiding god 777 sets over the last decan of Leo (20°–30°). Mars rules this face and its card is the Seven of Wands—Valour—courage that must fight to hold the ground its sovereignty has won. The name comes from the Greco-Egyptian roster of decan-rulers, the thirty-six faces of the old sky-religion.
tables: CLXXI. Egyptian Gods of the Zodiac (Cadent)

nettle.summary: The stinging nettle, attributed to Geburah; martial plant of the sting and the tonic.
nettle.description: The stinging nettle is placed at Geburah, the martial sphere — for it is the plant that wounds, its formic sting a small Mars in botanical form, and it was even used in 'urtication,' the deliberate flogging with nettles to rouse the blood. Yet the same plant is a valued food and blood-building tonic once cooked, a clear image of Geburah's fierce strength turned to nourishment. A mild herb in practice, requiring only ordinary care.
nettle.caution: Mild; stings raw but is a safe food once cooked.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

nightmares.summary: The oppressors of sleep, set at Jupiter — the night-mare that sits crushing upon the dreamer's breast.
nightmares.description: Among the Legendary Orders of Being, the Nightmares are attributed to the path of Jupiter. The nightmare of old belief is no mere bad dream but a malign spirit — the 'mare' that rides or sits upon the sleeper's chest, bringing suffocating dread and the paralysis of sleep. Kin to the incubus, this order personifies the terrors that rise from the unconscious in the helplessness of slumber, the dark visitations that oppress the soul when the guard of waking will is down.

nightshade.summary: The deadly flower of Saturn—nightshade, the witches' poison of death, darkness, and the saturnine threshold.
nightshade.description:
Nightshade is attributed to Saturn (Tav, the Universe). The deadly nightshade (belladonna) and its kin are the very type of the saturnine poison-plant: dark-berried, lethal, bound up with witchcraft, the flying-ointment, and death itself—the shadowed virtues of Saturn, lord of endings and of the underworld. Esoterically the nightshade is the saturnine plant of the death-threshold, beautiful and fatal, the darkness of Binah's lower reflection condensed into berry and leaf.

Caution: deadly nightshade is among the most poisonous of plants, fatal in small amounts. This entry is symbolic and historical and is in no way advice for use.
nightshade.caution: DEADLY POISON — fatal in small amounts (belladonna). Symbolic/historical entry only — never handle or ingest.

nike.summary: Nike, the goddess of victory — the winged bringer of triumph, at Netzach.
nike.description: Nike is the Greek goddess of victory, the swift winged figure who crowns the triumphant in war and in games. Referred to Netzach, the seventh Sephirah whose very name means “Victory,” she is the perfect emblem of that sphere — the soaring spirit of conquest and success. Often shown alighting with wreath and palm, she is triumph itself made a goddess, attendant upon Zeus and Athena.

niksa.summary: King of the Undines, ruler of the elemental spirits of Water.
niksa.description: Niksa (Nichsa, Necksa) is the King of the Undines, sovereign of the elemental spirits of Water in the system of Paracelsus as transmitted through Lévi and the Golden Dawn. The undines are the inhabitants of seas, rivers, springs, and rain — fluid, beautiful, mutable beings, the very life and feeling of the liquid element — and over them Niksa reigns. He is invoked in the working of the Water quarter, the cold, moist, western element of dissolution, reflection, and love, and commands the undines who govern the tides of emotion and the generative deep. Esoterically he personifies the receptive, dissolving, in-flowing force of Water: feeling, intuition, and the formless current that takes the shape of whatever contains it, the elemental counterpart of the soul's depths.
tables: LXII. Kings of the Elemental Spirits

nirvikalpa-samadhi.summary: Nirvikalpa-samādhi — the seedless, formless absorption beyond all distinction, set at the Veils.
nirvikalpa-samadhi.description: Nirvikalpa-samadhi is the 'samādhi without distinction or seed' among the Hindu/Buddhist Results, attributed to the Veils of the Negative. It is the highest absorption of the yogic path, in which all mental modifications (vṛtti) cease and the duality of knower and known dissolves — a state with no object, no thought, no division, the pure unconditioned consciousness resting in itself. Set beyond Kether at the negative veils, it figures the consummation of contemplative attainment, the threshold where the self is wholly absorbed in the absolute.
tables: XXIV. Certain of the Hindu/Buddhist Results

nitibus.summary: The stars — the Nuctemeron genius of the second hour presiding over the stars, set by Crowley at Taurus.
nitibus.description: In the Nuctemeron — the “Day Illumined by Night” ascribed to Apollonius of Tyana and preserved by Éliphas Lévi — Nitibus is numbered among the genii of the second hour, the spirit of the stars. His dominion is the fixed lights of heaven, the constellations and the influences they shed. Crowley arranges the twelve hours and their genii upon the paths of the Tree (777, Table CLXXIII), placing him at Taurus (Vav).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

nitika.summary: Precious stones — the Nuctemeron genius of the sixth hour presiding over precious stones, set by Crowley at Virgo.
nitika.description: In the Nuctemeron — the “Day Illumined by Night” ascribed to Apollonius of Tyana and preserved by Éliphas Lévi — Nitika is numbered among the genii of the sixth hour, the spirit of precious stones. He rules over gems and the secret virtues locked within stones. Crowley arranges the twelve hours and their genii upon the paths of the Tree (777, Table CLXXIII), placing him at Virgo (Yod).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

nitrates.summary: The nitrate and nitrite mineral drugs, set at Fire — the explosive, oxidising, igniting principle.
nitrates.description: Among the Mineral Drugs, "nitrates" are assigned to Shin, the path of the Aeon (Judgement) and the element of Fire — the explosive, oxidising principle, for nitre (saltpetre, potassium nitrate) is the very heart of gunpowder and the chemistry of combustion. The medical members of the class are chiefly the vasodilators — amyl nitrite and the nitrites that dilate the blood-vessels and were used against angina, with their flushing rush of heat. The fiery attribution is exact: these are the igniting, dilating, heat-flushing agents of the mineral kingdom. Esoterically they figure the Shin-fire applied to the body — sudden expansion, ignition, and the volatile rush of the flaming letter.
nitrates.caution: Historical/symbolic entry only — not medical advice. Nitrites/nitrates can cause dangerous blood-pressure collapse and methaemoglobinaemia; misuse can be fatal.

no-attribution-possible.summary: The unassignable—the positions of Spirit and the Negative Veils where no weapon of the elements can reach.
no-attribution-possible.description: This entry marks the places in the table of Magical Weapons where the system itself declares that no attribution is possible: the quintessence (31bis, Spirit) and the Veils of the Negative beyond Kether. The four elemental weapons—Wand, Cup, Sword, Pantacle—belong to the four elements, but Spirit, which is their root and reconciler, and the unmanifest Veils, which lie before all manifestation, cannot be grasped by any single implement, for they are that out of which all implements come. To write 'no attribution possible' is therefore not a failure but a precise act of reverence. Esoterically it teaches the limit of the magical apparatus: there are heights and depths that no tool can seize, where the operator must lay every weapon down and meet the formless with empty hands.

no-constellation.summary: 'no constellation' — a positional marker in table CLXXIV for a lunar mansion not anchored on a named constellation.
no-constellation.description: In table CLXXIV (Mansions of the Moon) some mansions sit at points of the zodiac where the underlying constellation provides no named figure — Crowley records this honestly with the marker 'no constellation' rather than fabricating an attribution. The slug preserves the editorial note as it appears at the Samekh/Sagittarius placement: the mansion is at this location, but the stellar background here is not the body of a major asterism.
tables: CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon

no-limit.summary: Ain Soph — 'No Limit'; the second Veil, the boundless infinite.
no-limit.description: Ain Soph (אין סוף), 'No Limit' or 'the Limitless,' is the second of the three Veils of the Negative above Kether. If Ain is the absolute Nothing, Ain Soph is that Nothing conceived as boundless extension — the infinite without end or edge, the unlimited from which all limitation will be drawn. It is the second stage of the Qabalistic descent from the unknowable toward the knowable: the No-Thing now apprehended as endless, the infinite reservoir behind the first point of the Crown.
tables: III. Translation of the Names of the Paths

noisy-peacock.summary: The magical image of Andrealphus — a noisy peacock — Goetic Marquis of the second decan of Capricorn (by night).
noisy-peacock.description: Andrealphus, the sixty-fifth spirit of the Goetia and a mighty Marquis, appears first as a peacock with great noise, and afterward in human shape. In 777 he is the nocturnal ruler of the second decan of Capricorn. He teaches geometry and all things pertaining to measurement, and astronomy, makes men subtle and cunning therein, and can turn a man into the likeness of a bird. The clamorous, many-eyed peacock befits ambitious, eminence-seeking Capricorn — display and exact measure, vanity and precision joined.

north.summary: The quarter of greatest darkness, attributed to the element Earth.
north.description: The North is the quarter of midnight and of the deepest darkness, the place the sun never reaches in its course. In the elemental scheme of the Western mysteries it is attributed to Earth, the densest and most material element, and to the foundation upon which the temple stands. As the station of greatest density and rest, it anchors the circle in the solid ground of manifestation.
tables: CX. Elements and Quarters per the Sepher Yetzirah

noscere.summary: 'To Know'—the airy power of the Sphinx, the virtue of knowledge.
noscere.description: Noscere, 'to know,' is set at Aleph and Air, the first of the Four Powers of the Sphinx that the Western tradition assigns to the elements: to Know, to Will, to Dare, and to Keep Silent. As the airy power it is the virtue of knowledge and discrimination—the clear, mobile intelligence that must precede all magical action. The Sphinx, compounded of the four kerubic beasts, guards the threshold with these four words; Noscere is the human-faced power of the mind, without which the will is blind.
tables: L. Transcendental Morality (10 Virtues; 7 Deadly Sins; 4 Magic Powers)

nothing.summary: Ain — 'Nothing'; the first Veil of the Negative, the absolute void before being.
nothing.description: Ain (אין), 'Nothing' or 'Not,' is the first of the three Veils of the Negative that lie above Kether and beyond the Tree of Life. It is not emptiness in any ordinary sense but the absolute, the No-Thing that precedes and exceeds all existence — the divine darkness that cannot be predicated, conceived, or named, of which even 'being' is too gross a description. From this unfathomable Nothing the whole Tree is said to crystallise: the via negativa's first and deepest term, the ground that is no ground.
tables: III. Translation of the Names of the Paths

nr.summary: Nr — a letter of the Coptic alphabet (n), which Crowley attributes to the path of Nun (Scorpio).
nr.description: Nr is a letter of the Coptic alphabet — the script in which the Egyptian language was written in the Christian era, the Greek alphabet adapted to Egyptian speech. It is from Greek nu. Crowley folds the Coptic alphabet into the great correspondence of letters and paths in 777 (Table LI), assigning Nr to the path of Nun (Scorpio) on the Tree of Life, so that the Egyptian-Christian script takes its station among the Hebrew letters and the keys of the Tarot.
tables: LI. Names of the Coptic Letters

nu.summary: Nu (Nun), the primordial waters — the boundless abyss from which creation arose; also Nuit, the sky.
nu.description: Nu is the primeval ocean of Egyptian cosmology, the dark, formless waters of the abyss out of which the first land and the creator-god emerged. Referred to Aleph and to the Veils of the Negative, Nu is the unmanifest infinity preceding all things; the name also evokes Nuit, the star-goddess of infinite space in Thelema. As the boundless waters or the boundless sky, Nu is the limitless ground of being before and behind all creation.

nuit.summary: Egyptian sky goddess; in Thelema, infinite space and the star-strewn heavens.
nuit.description: Nuit (Egyptian Nut) is the goddess of the sky, depicted as the star-covered woman arched over the earth, her body the very vault of heaven from which the sun is born each morning. In Thelema she is exalted into a supreme cosmic principle: infinite space, the totality of possibility, the star-goddess who declares in the Book of the Law ‘Every man and every woman is a star.’ As the infinitely extended, all-containing feminine, Nuit is the macrocosmic counterpart to the point-self Hadit; their union generates all experience. She represents the boundless, loving matrix of the cosmos.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

nuith.summary: Egyptian sky goddess; in Thelema, infinite space and the star-strewn heavens.
nuith.description: Nuit (Egyptian Nut) is the goddess of the sky, depicted as the star-covered woman arched over the earth, her body the very vault of heaven from which the sun is born each morning. In Thelema she is exalted into a supreme cosmic principle: infinite space, the totality of possibility, the star-goddess who declares in the Book of the Law ‘Every man and every woman is a star.’ As the infinitely extended, all-containing feminine, Nuit is the macrocosmic counterpart to the point-self Hadit; their union generates all experience. She represents the boundless, loving matrix of the cosmos.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

nundohar.summary: Angel of the second face of Scorpio, where feeling revives as wholesome pleasure.
nundohar.description: Nundohar governs the middle decan of Scorpio (10–20°), attributed to the Sun and the Six of Cups, *Pleasure* — renewed delight, the well-spring restored. The Sun warms Scorpio's depths into joy and memory. Nundohar is the angel of the pleasure that heals, the return of warmth after the disappointment of the first face.

nut.summary: Egyptian sky goddess; in Thelema, infinite space and the star-strewn heavens.
nut.description: Nuit (Egyptian Nut) is the goddess of the sky, depicted as the star-covered woman arched over the earth, her body the very vault of heaven from which the sun is born each morning. In Thelema she is exalted into a supreme cosmic principle: infinite space, the totality of possibility, the star-goddess who declares in the Book of the Law ‘Every man and every woman is a star.’ As the infinitely extended, all-containing feminine, Nuit is the macrocosmic counterpart to the point-self Hadit; their union generates all experience. She represents the boundless, loving matrix of the cosmos.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

nutmeg.summary: The warm sweet seed of Mercury—nutmeg, fragrant and kindly in the kitchen, dreamily potent in excess.
nutmeg.description:
Nutmeg is attributed to Mercury (Beth, the Magus). Its warm, sweet, aromatic fragrance—comforting in food and drink, and long carried as a charm for luck and clear wits—suits Mercury's genial, communicative nature. Esoterically nutmeg is a warm mercurial perfume of good cheer and quick fortune, the kindly spice of the Magus's hearth.

Caution: in large quantities nutmeg is toxic and powerfully deliriant. The kindly character described here applies only to ordinary culinary use, and the entry is in no way advice for any other.
nutmeg.caution: Toxic and deliriant in large doses. Ordinary culinary use only; not advice for any other use.

nutrition.summary: Nutrition — the vital function of the element Fire, attributed to the path of Shin.
nutrition.description: Nutrition — the transmuting of food into living substance — is given in 777 to Fire (the path of Shin). As fire transforms what it consumes, so the nourishing function is the body's inner flame, the digestive heat (the 'gastric fire' of the yogins) by which matter is turned to vitality.

nux-vomica.summary: The strychnine-bearing seed, attributed to Geburah; martial stimulant and poison.
nux-vomica.description:
Nux Vomica, the seed of Strychnos nux-vomica, is placed at Geburah, the sphere of Mars and severity — the source of strychnine, a violent stimulant of the nervous system used in minute doses as a tonic and, in larger amounts, as a deadly poison that throws the body into convulsions. Its martial attribution is exact: it is sheer, undiluted excitation, the goad turned weapon, life-force intensified to the point of destruction.

Caution: strychnine is a lethal convulsant poison. This entry is scholarly only and is in no sense advice for use.
nux-vomica.caution: Source of strychnine — a lethal convulsant poison. Scholarly entry only.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

nymphs.summary: Nature-spirits of grove, spring, and mountain, set at Mem — the feminine genii of the wild.
nymphs.description: The Nymphs are among the Legendary Orders of Being, here attributed to Mem and the element of Water. In Greek myth they are the beautiful feminine spirits of the natural world — of springs (naiads), trees (dryads), mountains (oreads), and the sea (nereids) — the indwelling life and divinity of place. As an order of beings they figure the animate soul of nature herself, the watery, fertile, alluring presences that haunt the wild places of the world.

oak.summary: The king of trees—Jupiter's thunder-oak of Dodona, sovereign strength rooted in the earth.
oak.description: The Oak is the tree of Jupiter (Kaph) and of the strong spheres Geburah and Tiphareth, the very type of the king-tree—massive, long-lived, and lightning-struck. Sacred to Zeus at Dodona, where his oracle spoke in the rustling of its leaves, and to the Druids who took their name and their mistletoe from it, the oak is sovereignty, endurance, and the thunder-god's power made wood. Esoterically it is the firm, magnanimous strength of Jupiter rooted in the earth (32 bis), the trunk that bears the storm and stands—an emblem of the just king and the enduring will.

obediance.summary: The merciful virtue of obedience, the submission of the will to the higher law.
obediance.description: Obedience is the virtue of Chesed, the fourth Sephirah, the sphere of Jupiter, mercy, and lawful rule. As the moral fruit of the kingly, ordering Sephirah, it is the willing submission of the lesser will to the greater—the discipline by which the soul aligns itself with the divine order rather than asserting its own. Crowley noted that the virtue of the master is precisely his obedience, for only one who has learned to obey the higher law is fit to command, and Chesed's benevolent authority rests upon it.
tables: L. Transcendental Morality (10 Virtues; 7 Deadly Sins; 4 Magic Powers)

obscene-ones.summary: Gamaliel — the averse Yesod; the lustful shells of the corrupted foundation.
obscene-ones.description: The Obscene Ones (Gamaliel) are the Qliphoth of Yesod, the lunar Foundation. The pure generative and imaginative power of the ninth Sephirah is here perverted into obscenity and sterile lust — the dark side of the moon, the realm of nightmares and the misuse of the creative-sexual force. They are the shells of the foundation defiled, ruled in tradition by Lilith.
tables: CXXIII. Translation of the Orders of the Qliphoth

occult.summary: The Seventh Path — the Occult Intelligence of Netzach, the hidden splendour of the virtues.
occult.description: The Seventh Path is the Occult or Hidden Intelligence (Sekhel Nistar), attributed to Netzach, the sphere of Venus and Victory. The Sepher Yetzirah names it the refulgent splendour of all the intellectual virtues which are beheld by the eyes of intellect and the contemplation of faith. 'Occult' here carries its true sense of hidden — the radiance is veiled not because it is dark but because it shines behind the veil of the emotions and instincts, the place where the higher virtues are felt and intuited rather than reasoned, the secret glory of love and desire.
tables: XIII. Paths of the Sefer Yetzirah

och.summary: Olympic Spirit of the Sun, giver of gold, perfect health, and the secret of the philosophers.
och.description: Och is the Olympic Spirit of the Sun in the Arbatel, placed by Crowley at Resh, the solar path of the great luminary. As the Sun is the heart and king of the planets, so the tradition makes Och the most splendid of givers: he confers six hundred years of perfect health, renders the operator a flawless physician, transmutes base substance into the purest gold and precious stones, prepares the Medicine of metals (the philosophers' stone), and grants the most excellent of spirits as familiars. He reigns upon the Day of the Sun (Sunday). Esoterically he is the radiant centre — the Tiphareth-force reflected into the world of works, the gold that is both metal and enlightenment, health, harmony, and the kingly self made manifest.

octagram.summary: The eight-pointed star — attributed to Mercury; the star of order and the eightfold Word.
octagram.description: The octagram, the eight-pointed star, is attributed by its number to the sphere of Mercury. As the figure of eight it expresses the Mercurial powers of order, structure, and intelligence — the eightfold division and the perfected regularity of thought. It is the star of the Magus and of the disciplined mind that orders the cosmos into intelligible form.
tables: XLIX. Lineal Figures of the Planets, &c., and Geomany

odin.summary: Odin, the all-father — god of wisdom, war, and the runes, won by self-sacrifice, at Chokmah.
odin.description: Odin is the chief god of the Norse pantheon, the one-eyed all-father of wisdom, war, poetry, and magic, who hung nine nights upon the world-tree Yggdrasil to win the runes and gave his eye for a draught from the well of wisdom. Referred to Chokmah, the supernal Father, and to Hod, the sphere of magic and intellect, he is the seeker-god whose authority is bought with sacrifice. Wandering cloaked and far-seeing, he embodies the hard-won wisdom that rules through knowledge.

of-adonai.summary: 'of Adonai' — Crowley's trailing reference in table XLV at Malkuth, the mystical knowledge of the Lord.
of-adonai.description: In table XLV the cell at Malkuth closes with a reference to '[the Knowledge] of Adonai' — Adonai being the Hebrew title 'Lord,' here used in its Qabalistic sense as the Holy Guardian Angel and the manifest face of the divine in the world. The placement at Malkuth is significant: it is in the Kingdom — in incarnated experience — that the practitioner first knows Adonai concretely, before the higher attainments of Tiphareth. The entry preserves Crowley's pointer as it appears in the source.

of-prophecy.summary: 'of Prophecy' — Crowley's trailing reference in table XLV at Zayin, the power of prophetic foresight.
of-prophecy.description: In table XLV the cell at path 17 (Zayin/Gemini) closes with a reference to '[the gift] of Prophecy' — the Western magical-mystical power of foreseeing what is to come, the charism of the Hebrew nevi'im, the Pythia at Delphi, and the apostolic 'prophecy' of 1 Corinthians 12. The placement at Zayin is consistent with the path's doubled vision — past and future as twin faces of the eternal present. The entry preserves Crowley's pointer as it appears in the source.
