ogameron.summary: Nocturnal angelic Lord of Gemini within the Airy Triplicity.
ogameron.description: Ogameron is the night-governor of Gemini among the angelic Lords of the Triplicities, complement to the day-Lord Sarash. As the mutable member of the Air trine by night, Gemini's bright traffic becomes the whispering night wind, thought turned inward and dreaming; Ogameron presides over this nocturnal, interior commerce of the mind.

ohooohatan.summary: Ohooohatan — Crowley's transliteration in table LVIII at path 32 (Tav/Saturn), one of the Supreme Elemental Kings.
ohooohatan.description: Ohooohatan appears in 777's table LVIII at path 32 (Tav/Saturn). The four 'Supreme Elemental Kings' of Dee/Kelly's Enochian system properly govern the four elements; Crowley's extension to a saturnine fifth — placing a King at Tav — is one of 777's structural elaborations of the original Watchtower scheme. The name's repeated 'o's and final 'tan' are characteristic of Enochian's vocalic, drawn-out incantatory style. The entry records the name as Crowley fixed it at Tav, beside the other three Kings at Air, Fire, and Earth.

old-man.summary: The magical image of Agares — an old man riding a crocodile, a goshawk on his fist — Goetic Duke of the second decan of Aries.
old-man.description: Agares, the second spirit of the Goetia and a great Duke of the eastern part, comes in the likeness of a fair old man riding upon a crocodile and carrying a goshawk upon his fist. In 777 he rules the second decan of Aries by day. He teaches all languages, brings back runaways and stops those that flee, causes earthquakes, and overthrows dignities. The venerable rider mastering the crocodile images authority over swift and primal forces — the seasoned will reining in the raw onrush of the Ram.

olibanum.summary: Frankincense—the solar incense of Tiphareth and the Sun, smoke of adoration rising from the heart of the Tree.
olibanum.description: Olibanum (frankincense) is attributed to the Sun, to Leo, to Fire, and to Tiphareth—the supreme solar incense. The golden resin of the Boswellia, burned in every temple of the ancient world, its clean and lifting smoke is the very breath of worship and of the radiant solar centre; it was one of the gifts of the Magi laid before the newborn sun-king. Esoterically olibanum is the perfume of the harmonised heart, the fragrant adoration that rises from Tiphareth toward the source of light.

olive.summary: The tree of peace and mercy—Athena's gift, Chesed's anointing oil and the dove's green branch.
olive.description: The Olive is attributed chiefly to Chesed, the merciful sphere of Jupiter, and to the airy reaches of Aries and Aquarius. It is the ancient emblem of peace, reconciliation, and divine favour—Athena's gift to her city, the branch the dove brought back over the receding flood, the oil with which kings and priests were anointed and the lamps of the temple kept burning. Esoterically the olive is the gentle, civilising mercy of Chesed, the fruit whose pressed oil is light and consecration, the sign that the wrath of the waters has passed and grace returned.

olus.summary: Aeolus, keeper of the winds — the lord who binds and looses the gales, at Air.
olus.description: Aeolus is the Greek and Roman ruler of the winds, who keeps the gales bound in his cave or bag and looses them at the will of the gods. Referred to Aleph and Air and to Aquarius, he is the master of the moving atmosphere, the divine warden of the storm-winds. As keeper of the winds he embodies command over the airy element, the power to raise or still the tempest.

ominous-appearances.summary: Ominous Appearances — a class-image in CLXXXIII Legendary Orders of Being, the family of presaging, sign-bearing visions.
ominous-appearances.description: 'Ominous Appearances' is one of the class-categories Crowley names in table CLXXXIII ('Legendary Orders of Being') — collecting the visionary beings whose function is to presage, warn, or announce: the banshees, the death-omens, the herald-shades, the spirit-fetches seen before a great event. The class is defined less by morphology than by office: the appearance itself is the message. The entry registers it as a Crowleyean category-header in CLXXXIII.

omphta.summary: Presiding god of the second decan of Libra, the same Saturnine face of severance and sorrow.
omphta.description: Omphta is the presiding god 777 sets over the second decan of Libra (10°–20°), the Saturnine face the names-column calls Aterechinis. Bearing the Three of Swords—Sorrow—it names the severance and grief at the centre of the scales. It belongs to the Greco-Egyptian roster of decan-rulers, the thirty-six faces of the old astronomy.
tables: CLXIX. Egyptian Gods of the Zodiac (Succedent)

on.summary: On (Heliopolis), the City of the Sun — the sacred seat of the solar cult.
on.description: On is the biblical name for Heliopolis (Egyptian Annu), the ancient city sacred to the sun-god Ra and home of the great priesthood of the solar theology. Referred to Tiphareth and the solar paths, it stands by metonymy for the cult of the sun itself — the centre of light, the seat of the Ennead and of the doctrines of solar creation. To name On is to invoke the radiant heart of Egyptian religion.

tables: XCII. The Angelic Functions in the World of Yetzirah

onycha.summary: The sea-born incense of Cancer—onycha, the shell's fragrant operculum, one of the four holy spices of the waters.
onycha.description: Onycha is attributed to Cancer and to Water. One of the four sacred spices of the Hebrew incense, it was prepared (by tradition) from the operculum—the little "nail" or lid—of a sea-snail, a perfume literally drawn from the waters and fitting the watery, lunar sign of Cancer. Esoterically onycha is the holy perfume of the sea, the fragrance won from the shell of a creature of the deep—the watery element offered up as sacred smoke.

onyx.summary: The black banded stone of Saturn — gravity, grounding, and the boundary.
onyx.description: Onyx — black (often white-banded) chalcedony — is attributed to the path of Tav and Saturn, the last letter and the sphere of time, limitation, and form. Its sober blackness suits the saturnine principle of gravity and boundary; long worn as a stone of grounding, of self-mastery, and in mourning, and carved for the cameo and the seal. Esoterically it is the gem of the threshold and of disciplined, earthing weight — the seal set on the completed work.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

oo.summary: The long 'oo' (Coptic Ⲟⲩ) vowel-value — also placed at Tiphareth in Crowley's English-equivalents column.
oo.description: 'Oo' (as in 'moon') is Crowley's English rendering of the Coptic digraph Ⲟⲩ (omicron-upsilon), the long high back vowel, which his table LI sets — like long 'O' — at Tiphareth. Two distinct Coptic letters/letter-pairs converge here at the solar sphere, both rounded and resonant, both vibrating outward from a still centre. The entry is a phonetic marker only: the slot in Crowley's grid where the long round vowel of the Coptic alphabet aligns with the sixth Sephirah on the Middle Pillar.
tables: LI. English Equivalent of the Coptic Alphabet

opal.summary: The iridescent stone of Hod and Mercury — shifting play of all colours.
opal.description: The opal is set at Hod and the path of Mercury — a stone of shifting, iridescent fire that plays through all the colours at once, perfectly suiting Mercurial Hod, the sphere of multiplicity, intellect, and the many-coloured splendour of the analytic mind. Its restless interplay of hues is the very image of Mercury's quicksilver versatility; esoterically it is the gem of the shimmering, shape-shifting intelligence.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

ophiel.summary: Olympic Spirit of Mercury, master of the quicksilver arts, familiars, and every science.
ophiel.description: Ophiel is the Olympic Spirit of Mercury in the Arbatel, placed by Crowley at Beth, the path of the Magus and of Mercurial intellect. As Mercury is the swift messenger and lord of all crossings, the tradition makes Ophiel the teacher of every art and science, the giver of familiar spirits, and — most famously — the master who confers the secret of fixing quicksilver, turning the volatile mercury of the philosophers into the stable Stone. He reigns upon the Day of Mercury (Wednesday). Esoterically he is the spirit of mind and communication poured into the world of action — the nimble, double-natured power of Hod, learning, magic, commerce, and the cunning that binds the higher and lower together.

ophionius.summary: Ophion, the primordial world-serpent — the first ruler of Olympus, at Libra.
ophionius.description: Ophionius is Ophion, the great serpent of Orphic and Pelasgian myth who, with Eurynome, ruled the cosmos before Kronos and Rhea, coiled about the world-egg from which creation hatched. Referred to Lamed and Libra, he is the encircling serpent of primal order, the first power to hold dominion over the heights. As the world-encircling snake he is a Greek cousin of the cosmic serpents found across the ancient mythologies.
tables: CLXXI. Egyptian Gods of the Zodiac (Cadent)

opium.summary: The dried poppy latex, attributed to Chesed; dream, expansion, and oblivion.
opium.description:
Opium, the dried latex of the poppy, is placed at Chesed, the merciful, expansive sphere of Jupiter — for it brings a vast, dreamy enlargement of inner space, the painless majesty and oceanic ease that is Jupiter's gift turned narcotic. It has been medicine, sacrament, and scourge across millennia, the wellspring of the dream-literature of De Quincey and Coleridge and of Crowley's own 'Diary of a Drug Fiend.' Esoterically it figures the seductive descent into the lotus-world of the unconscious, the mercy that, ungoverned, becomes dissolution.

Caution: opium and its derivatives are among the most physically addictive and lethal substances known; overdose is fatal. This entry is historical and symbolic, in no way an encouragement of use.
opium.caution: Highly addictive opioid; overdose is lethal. Historical/symbolic entry only — emphatically not advice for use.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

opium-poppy.summary: The flower of sleep and death—the poppy of Binah and Chesed, dream-bringer and gate of oblivion.
opium-poppy.description:
The Opium Poppy is set between Binah and Chesed—the dark Mother of form and sleep, and the merciful, dreamy expansiveness of Jupiter. Its scarlet bloom and milky latex have signified sleep, dream, forgetfulness, and gentle death since antiquity: the flower of Hypnos and Morpheus, strewn upon tombs, the painless oblivion that is at once mercy and dissolution. Esoterically it figures the descent into the dream-world of Binah's deep waters, the sweet sleep that borders upon death.

Caution: the latex of this plant is the source of opium and its derivatives, among the most addictive and lethal substances known. This entry is symbolic and historical and is in no way advice for use.
opium-poppy.caution: Source of opium; the latex yields highly addictive, potentially lethal narcotics. Symbolic/historical entry only — not advice for use.

opoponax.summary: Sweet myrrh of Scorpio—opoponax, warm and balsamic, the dark resin's gentler, deeper voice.
opoponax.description: Opoponax ("sweet myrrh") is attributed to Scorpio (Nun, Death). A warm, sweet, balsamic gum-resin, richer and softer than true myrrh, it carries a deep, slightly animal sweetness fitting the intense, secretive, transformative water-sign. Esoterically opoponax is the warm dark perfume of Scorpio's depths—the sweetness hidden within the resin of death, the balsam of the place where dissolution turns toward new life.

oppression.summary: Ten of Wands — Oppression; Saturn in Sagittarius, Malkuth of Fire: force turned cruel.
oppression.description: The Ten of Wands, Oppression, is Malkuth in the suit of Fire and the third decan of Sagittarius, crushed by Saturn. When fire descends wholly into matter and is ruled by the lord of limitation, will becomes tyranny: force divorced from its higher purpose, burning blindly and to no end. It is the fire that oppresses rather than illumines — energy gone stale, heavy, and consuming.
tables: CXXXIII. Titles and Attributions of the Wand Suit

ops.summary: Ops, goddess of plenty and the harvest — consort of Saturn, the power of abundance, at the Sun.
ops.description: Ops is the Roman goddess of plenty, fertility, and the riches of the harvest, wife of Saturn and associated with the bounty of the sown earth. Referred to Resh and the Sun, she is the generative wealth that the sun's warmth ripens into abundance. Her name survives in words of wealth and opulence; she embodies the overflowing plenty of a fruitful world.

orchid-root.summary: The aphrodisiac tuber, attributed to Yesod and Capricorn; root of generative power.
orchid-root.description: Orchid root — the orchis or 'satyrion' of the old herbals — is attributed to Yesod, the lunar foundation, and to Capricorn, the generative goat: the plant's very name derives from the Greek for the testicles its paired tubers resemble, and it carried an ancient reputation as an aphrodisiac and restorer of virility. Its placement at the sexual-foundational sphere of Yesod is exact; it is the root of generative life, the earthy ground of desire and fertility through which the higher forces descend into form.
orchid-root.caution: Folk aphrodisiac; many orchid species are protected — wild harvest is harmful.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

orchids.summary: The flower of the Lovers—orchids of Gemini, whose very name means 'testicle,' blooms of refined and twinned eros.
orchids.description: Orchids are attributed to Gemini (Zayin, the Lovers). The Greek orchis, "testicle," named them for their paired root-tubers, and the whole family carries an air of refined, sometimes uncanny eroticism—mimicking insects, mates, and forms to lure their pollinators—a fitting flora for the airy sign of duality, attraction, and the joining of opposites. Esoterically the orchid is the subtle, intelligent eros of Gemini: desire grown exquisite and strange, the union of two made flower.

orchis.summary: The aphrodisiac tuber, attributed to Yesod and Capricorn; root of generative power.
orchis.description: Orchid root — the orchis or 'satyrion' of the old herbals — is attributed to Yesod, the lunar foundation, and to Capricorn, the generative goat: the plant's very name derives from the Greek for the testicles its paired tubers resemble, and it carried an ancient reputation as an aphrodisiac and restorer of virility. Its placement at the sexual-foundational sphere of Yesod is exact; it is the root of generative life, the earthy ground of desire and fertility through which the higher forces descend into form.
orchis.caution: Folk aphrodisiac; many orchid species are protected — wild harvest is harmful.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

orchis-root.summary: The aphrodisiac root of the Devil—orchis ('satyrion'), tuber of lust upon the goat-path of Capricorn.
orchis-root.description: Orchis Root is attributed to Capricorn (Ayin, the Devil). The paired tubers of the orchis—the ancient "satyrion," named for the lustful satyrs—were the classic aphrodisiac of the old herbals, and so belong fittingly to the Devil's goat-path of Capricorn, lord of carnal force and earthy desire. Esoterically the orchis root is the concentrated generative lust of Ayin, the dark fertile power of the goat that the path of the Devil both embodies and sets as an ordeal.

organs-of-circulation.summary: The organs of circulation, attributed to Fire, the heat that drives the body's tides.
organs-of-circulation.description: The Organs of Circulation are attributed to Shin and Fire. The heart and vessels that drive the warm blood through the body answer to the fiery element—the heat and active energy without which the circulation would still and the body cool to death. As Fire is the principle of vital warmth and motion, so the circulatory organs are its bodily instrument, the burning engine that keeps the life-tide moving through every member.

organs-of-intelligence.summary: The organs of intelligence, attributed to Spirit, the body's instruments of mind.
organs-of-intelligence.description: The Organs of Intelligence are attributed to Spirit (31 bis), the quintessence above the four elements. The brain and the finest nervous structures through which thought and awareness arise answer to the spiritual quintessence—that which is more than any single element, the subtle ground of consciousness itself. Their attribution to Spirit marks the mind's instruments as the highest and most refined apparatus of the body, the place where the elemental organism opens toward the divine spark.

organs-of-nutrition.summary: The organs of nutrition, attributed to Water, the body's assimilation of nourishment.
organs-of-nutrition.description: The Organs of Nutrition are attributed to Mem and Water. The organs by which food is dissolved, taken up, and assimilated into the body's substance answer to the watery element—the solvent and receptive principle that breaks down and blends. As Water is the medium of mixture and nourishment, so these organs are its bodily seat, the moist interior labour by which the food of the world is made into living flesh.

oriax.summary: The fifty-ninth spirit of the Goetia (Orias), a serpent-bearing marquis of Scorpio who teaches the virtues of the stars.
oriax.description: Orias (here Oriax) is the fifty-ninth spirit of the Goetia, a great marquis of the decans of Scorpio. He teaches the virtues of the stars and the mansions of the planets, transforms men, and gives dignities, prelacies and the favour of friends and foes. He appears as a lion with a serpent's tail, riding upon a strong horse and holding in his right hand two great hissing serpents. A spirit of the watery sign, he is the master of astral virtue and transformation.

oriens.summary: One of the four cardinal demon-kings — Oriens, 'the East,' ruling the element of Air.
oriens.description: Oriens, whose name means 'the East,' is one of the four demon-kings of the quarters in the Goetic and Abramelin systems. Set here to the element of Air, he is the king of the eastern region from which the sun rises, commanding a host of subordinate spirits. With Paimon, Ariton, and Amaimon he forms the fourfold infernal sovereignty of the directions invoked in the operations of the old grimoires.

oroasoer.summary: Name of the first decan of Aquarius, the same Venusian face of chilly reversal.
oroasoer.description: Oroasoer is the name 777 records for the first decan of Aquarius (0°–10°), the Venusian face the gods-column calls Brondeus. Bearing the Five of Swords—Defeat—it marks the chilly reversal at the opening of fixed air. Like all thirty-six decan-names it descends from the Egyptian division of the sky into ten-degree faces.
tables: CLXVIII. Egyptian Names of Asc. Decans.

orobas.summary: The fifty-fifth spirit of the Goetia, a horse-formed prince of Libra — faithful, who tells of the divine and creation.
orobas.description: Orobas is the fifty-fifth spirit of the Goetia, a great and mighty prince of the decans of Libra. He tells truly of things past, present and to come, and of the divinity and the creation of the world; he gives dignities and prelacies and the favour of friends and foes. He is notably faithful, and will not suffer the conjurer to be tempted or deceived by any spirit. He appears first as a horse, then takes human form. A spirit of the airy Venusian sign, he is the trustworthy revealer of sacred mysteries.

osiris.summary: Egyptian god of death, resurrection, and the underworld; the slain-and-risen king.
osiris.description: Osiris (Egyptian Asar) is the slain-and-risen god—king of the dead, lord of resurrection, and judge of souls in the hall of the underworld. Murdered and dismembered by his brother Set, reassembled by Isis, and reborn to rule the realm of the dead, he is the archetypal dying god whose story promises life beyond death. In 777 he is attributed to the solar centre Tiphareth, the place of the sacrificed-and-reborn god, and Crowley made the ‘Formula of Osiris’ (the slain god) the keynote of the superseded Aeon, now yielding to the Aeon of the child Horus. Osiris embodies the mystery of regeneration through death.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

oso.summary: The fifty-seventh spirit of the Goetia (Ose), a leopard-formed president of Libra who confers wisdom and shape-shifting madness.
oso.description: Ose (here Oso) is the fifty-seventh spirit of the Goetia, a great president of the decans of Libra. He makes men wise in all the liberal sciences and gives true answers of divine and secret things; he can also transform a man into any shape so completely that the man believes himself to be that very thing, falling into a kind of madness or delusion. He appears as a leopard, then takes human form. A spirit of the airy sign, he is the giver of wisdom and the weaver of delusion.

other-ascendency.summary: 'other Ascendency' — Crowley's trailing reference in table XLV at Jupiter (path of Kaph).
other-ascendency.description: In table XLV the cell at path 21 (Kaph/Jupiter) closes with 'other Ascendency' — the Jupiterian magical power of rising in status, gaining authority, and prevailing in matters of public office and good fortune. The placement is consistent with Jupiter's classical rulership of expansion, honour, and the merciful order. The entry preserves Crowley's pointer as it appears in the source.

other-yoni-symbols.summary: Catch-all entry in table XLIX — Crowley's marker that Binah's lineal forms include all 'other yoni symbols.'
other-yoni-symbols.description: After enumerating the Plane, Diamond, Oval, and Circle at Binah in table XLIX, Crowley closes the cell with 'and other Yoni Symbols' — an explicit catch-all making clear that the named forms are representative rather than exhaustive. The yoni (Sanskrit 'womb,' 'source') is the receptive aperture, the feminine generative organ raised to a metaphysical principle in Tantric and Saktic tradition; in 777's Western-Eastern synthesis any closed, receptive geometric form falls under it. The entry preserves Crowley's editorial signal that Binah's geometric vocabulary cannot be enumerated in a finite list — the receptive principle is too wide for that.
tables: XLIX. Lineal Figures of the Planets, &c., and Geomany

oval.summary: The oval or vesica — a yoni-symbol of Binah, the supernal Mother.
oval.description: The oval, like the vesica and the lozenge, is one of the ancient yoni-symbols attributed to Binah, the supernal Mother and giver of form. As the shape of the egg, the womb, and the encircling vulva, it figures the receptive, containing, generative power of the third Sephirah — the dark sea of Understanding within which the creative seed of Chokmah is conceived and given form. It is the feminine vessel of manifestation, complement to the masculine line and point.
tables: XLIX. Lineal Figures of the Planets, &c., and Geomany

ow.summary: Ow — a letter of the Coptic alphabet (o), which Crowley attributes to the path of Ayin (Capricorn).
ow.description: Ow is a letter of the Coptic alphabet — the script in which the Egyptian language was written in the Christian era, the Greek alphabet adapted to Egyptian speech. It is from Greek omicron/omega. Crowley folds the Coptic alphabet into the great correspondence of letters and paths in 777 (Table LI), assigning Ow to the path of Ayin (Capricorn) on the Tree of Life, so that the Egyptian-Christian script takes its station among the Hebrew letters and the keys of the Tarot.
tables: LI. Names of the Coptic Letters

owl.summary: The night-bird of hidden wisdom—Athena's owl and the prophet of darkness, sight where others are blind.
owl.description: The owl is the great bird of the night, and the grid sets it among the fiery, initiating powers of Aries. Sacred to Athena as the emblem of wisdom, and to the dark goddesses as the bird of omen and the night, the owl sees where others are blind, hunting in the dark with silent wing and unerring eye. It carries the double meaning of all night-creatures: the bearer of secret wisdom and clear sight in obscurity, and at the same time the herald of dread and the unknown. Esoterically the owl figures the wisdom that comes only in darkness, the inner vision that opens when the daylight of the ordinary mind is put out, the prophet-bird that perceives what is hidden from the waking eye.

ox.summary: The beast of the path Aleph—the patient primal life of Air, the Fool's faithful ox of pure being.
ox.description: The ox belongs to Aleph, the path of the Fool and the element of Air, and as with Gimel the attribution is built into the alphabet: the letter Aleph means 'ox.' It is the first beast, the type of patient, plodding, generative life—the broad strength that breaks the ground and draws the plough, primal and uncomplaining. As the emblem of Air and of Aleph's zero it carries the sense of breath and of the undifferentiated life-force that precedes all form. Esoterically the ox is the silent labour of being itself, the great gentle power beneath the Fool's careless dance.
tables: III. Translation of the Names of the Paths

ox-goad.summary: Lamed — 'ox-goad'; the prod of discipline and law, path of Adjustment.
ox-goad.description: Lamed means 'ox-goad' — the pointed staff used to drive and direct the ploughing ox — and from it derive the Hebrew words for teaching and learning (lamad, 'to learn'; melamed, 'teacher'). The tallest of the letters, it rises above the line like a tower of instruction. In Liber 777 Lamed is the path of Adjustment (Justice), attributed to Libra, joining Geburah to Tiphareth. The goad is the discipline of the Law: the corrective prod that keeps the soul to the straight furrow, the teaching authority that balances and directs.
tables: III. Translation of the Names of the Paths

oyster.summary: The pearl-bearer of Capricorn—the rough closed shell that breeds a hidden jewel from its own wound.
oyster.description: The oyster is attributed to Capricorn, the earthy sign of patient labour and hidden depth, and it is the maker of the pearl: a homely, hard-shelled creature that, from the irritation of a single grain of grit, builds over long years a flawless jewel within its own body. It is therefore a perfect emblem of secret, slow transformation—of the treasure that is formed precisely out of suffering and concealment, sealed within a rough and unpromising casing. Under Capricorn this speaks of the patient work that turns hardship into something precious. Esoterically the oyster figures the soul that, in darkness and under pressure, grows the pearl of great price from the very wound it cannot escape.

pagans.summary: Pagans — heathen worshippers among the inhabitants of the Arab hells, set at Chesed.
pagans.description: The pagans or heathen — those outside the 'peoples of the Book' — appear among the inhabitants of the seven hells of Arab cosmology, set in 777 at Chesed alongside the idolaters. The attribution reflects the medieval scheme of assigning each class of unbelievers its palace of fire, preserved here as historical cosmology and carrying no endorsement.
tables: CXXVI. Inhabitants of the Seven Hells of the Arabs

paimon.summary: One of the great kings of the Goetia, set at Gemini and Saturn — a crowned spirit of arts, secrets and dominion.
paimon.description: Paimon is the ninth spirit of the Goetia and one of its greatest kings, ruling many legions and most obedient to Lucifer; in 777 he stands at the decans of Gemini and at the path of Saturn among the Demon Kings. He teaches all arts, sciences and secret things, reveals the mysteries of earth, wind and water, gives dignities and good familiars, and binds men to the operator's will. He appears as a figure with a glorious, almost effeminate face, crowned and riding a dromedary, preceded by a host of trumpeters and musicians. As both a Goetic spirit and one of the cardinal Demon Kings, he embodies sovereign command over knowledge and men.

pakiel.summary: Pakiel, the angel set over Cancer — the assisting intelligence of the sign on the path of Cheth.
pakiel.description: Pakiel is the angel attributed to Cancer in the Golden Dawn and Crowley's 777 (Table CXLIII, the Twelve Lesser Assistant Angels of the Signs). The name carries the Hebrew theophoric ending ‑el, “of God,” marking him as a ministering intelligence rather than a ruling archangel: the lesser angel who carries the governance of the sign into act. Set over Cancer (cardinal Water), he embodies the sheltering, tidal feeling of the crab; Crowley places him at the path of Cheth on the Tree of Life.
tables: CXLIII. Twelve Lesser Assistant Angels in the Signs (Transl).

palace-of-benevolence.summary: The Palace of Will and Benevolence — the hall of Briah set at Tiphareth.
palace-of-benevolence.description: The Palace of Benevolence (associated with Hekhal Ratzon, the Palace of Will or Good Pleasure) is one of the Seven Palaces of Briah, attributed to Tiphareth, the harmonising solar centre. It is the radiant hall of divine good will and gracious favour at the heart of the heavenly ascent — the central sanctuary where the soul comes into accord with the beneficent will of the divine.

palace-of-crystalline-whiteness.summary: Hekhal Livnath ha-Sappir, the Palace of Sapphire Whiteness — the first hall of Briah.
palace-of-crystalline-whiteness.description: The Palace of Crystalline Whiteness (Hekhal Livnath ha-Sappir, the 'whiteness of the sapphire') is the lowest of the Seven Palaces of Briah, attributed to Yesod and Malkuth — the threshold hall at which the ascent through the palaces begins. Its name is drawn from the 'paved work of a sapphire stone' beneath the feet of God in Exodus: the translucent, gleaming-white pavement that forms the first sanctuary, gateway to the heavenly halls above.

palace-of-love.summary: Hekhal Ahavah, the Palace of Love — the hall of Briah set at Chesed.
palace-of-love.description: Among the Seven Palaces of Briah, the Palace of Love (Hekhal Ahavah) is attributed to Chesed, the sphere of Mercy. It is the heavenly hall of divine love and lovingkindness, the sanctuary in which the soul, ascending the palaces, is met by the merciful, embracing aspect of God — fittingly seated at the great Sephirah of grace and benevolence.

palace-of-merit.summary: Hekhal Zekhuth, the Palace of Merit — the hall of Briah set at Geburah.
palace-of-merit.description: The Palace of Merit (Hekhal Zekhuth) is one of the Seven Palaces of Briah, attributed to Geburah, the sphere of Severity and judgement. It is the hall in which merit and desert are weighed — the sanctuary of righteous deserving answering to the disciplining, judging power of the Martial Sephirah, where the worth of the ascending soul is assessed.

palace-of-serenity.summary: The Palace of Serenity (Nogah) — the bright, tranquil hall of Briah set at Hod.
palace-of-serenity.description: The Palace of Serenity, associated with Hekhal Nogah ('brightness' or 'glow'), is one of the Seven Palaces of Briah, attributed to Hod. It is the hall of luminous calm and tranquil radiance in the heavenly ascent — the serene, glowing sanctuary answering to the Mercurial sphere of ordered splendour, a place of clear and peaceful light along the soul's upward way.

palace-of-the-holy-of-holies.term: Palace of the Holy of Holies
palace-of-the-holy-of-holies.displayTerm: Palace of the Holy of Holies
palace-of-the-holy-of-holies.summary: The supreme Palace of Briah — the Holy of Holies, innermost sanctuary of the creative world.
palace-of-the-holy-of-holies.description: In the doctrine of the Seven Palaces (Hekhalot) of the world of Briah, the heavenly halls are conceived as a series of sanctuaries through which the soul ascends toward the divine. The Palace of the Holy of Holies (Hekhal Qodesh ha-Qodashim) is the highest, attributed to the supernal triad — the innermost shrine answering to the earthly Temple's Holy of Holies, where the Presence dwells. It is the goal of the ascent through the palaces, the sanctum at the summit of the created world.

palace-of-the-substance-of-heaven.term: Palace of the Substance of Heaven
palace-of-the-substance-of-heaven.displayTerm: Palace of the Substance of Heaven
palace-of-the-substance-of-heaven.summary: Hekhal Etzem ha-Shamayim, the Palace of Heaven's Substance — the hall of Briah at Netzach.
palace-of-the-substance-of-heaven.description: The Palace of the Substance of Heaven (Hekhal Etzem ha-Shamayim, the very 'body' or essence of the sky, compared to sapphire) is one of the Seven Palaces of Briah, here attributed to Netzach. It is the lucent hall whose floor is as the clear blue substance of the heavens themselves — the sapphire sanctuary of the heavenly ascent, named from the pavement 'like the body of heaven in its clearness' seen by the elders of Israel.

palm.summary: The upright tree of triumph—the palm of victory and peace, of Mercury's grace and Jupiter's bounty.
palm.description: The Palm is attributed to Mercury (Beth) and Jupiter (Kaph). Tall, straight, and ever-green, fruitful even in the desert, it has always signified victory, uprightness, and triumphant life—the palm-branch of the conqueror and the martyr, strewn before kings, and a sign of resurrection, for the date-palm renews itself and shares its very name with the self-renewing phoenix. Esoterically the palm is the upright spine of the aspirant flourishing in barren places, the graceful, fruitful triumph of spirit over the wilderness.
tables: III. Translation of the Names of the Paths

pan.summary: Pan, the goat-god of the wild — the all-pervading life of nature, at Capricorn and the Veils.
pan.description: Pan is the goat-horned and goat-legged god of the wild, of shepherds, flocks, and the lonely mountain places, whose sudden cry sows “panic” terror. Referred to Ayin and Capricorn and to the Veils of the Negative, he is read esoterically as “the All” (pan), the total, all-pervading life-force of nature itself. At once rustic piper and cosmic principle, he is the divine vitality of the whole, the god behind the Devil card and the green heart of the world.

panic-demons.summary: The spirits of sudden dread, set at Capricorn — the panic of Pan that seizes the lonely and the lost.
panic-demons.description: Among the Legendary Orders of Being, the Panic-demons are attributed to Capricorn, the sign of the goat-god. They are the spirits of 'panic' in its original sense — the sudden, causeless terror that the Greeks ascribed to Pan, falling upon travellers in wild and lonely places, upon herds and even upon armies. Their Capricornian attribution is precise, for panikos means 'of Pan'; they figure the irrational dread that the wilderness and the great god of nature inspire, fear arising not from a visible threat but from the uncanny presence in solitude.

panotragus.summary: Panotragus, Pan the He-Goat — the goat-god of the wild, at Capricorn's neighbour signs.
panotragus.description: Panotragus, “Pan the goat,” is the goat-footed god of the wild places, of flocks, fertility, and panic terror, here referred to Virgo and Scorpio. He is the all-pervading life-force of untamed nature, half-beast and half-divine, whose pipes sound through the lonely hills. As the goat-god he is kin to the Capricornian and Devil imagery of the Tree, the generative and uncanny power of the wilderness.
tables: CLXXI. Egyptian Gods of the Zodiac (Cadent)

papus.summary: Medicine — the Nuctemeron genius of the first hour presiding over medicine, set by Crowley at Aries.
papus.description: In the Nuctemeron — the “Day Illumined by Night” ascribed to Apollonius of Tyana and preserved by Éliphas Lévi — Papus is numbered among the genii of the first hour, the spirit of medicine. As the spirit set over the healer's art he answers to the restoration of the body's harmony and the curing of disease. Crowley arranges the twelve hours and their genii upon the paths of the Tree (777, Table CLXXIII), placing him at Aries (Heh).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

parabrahm.summary: Parabrahman, the supreme absolute — the unconditioned reality beyond all gods, at Kether.
parabrahm.description: Parabrahman is the supreme, unconditioned Absolute of Vedanta, the formless reality beyond all attributes, names, and even the creator-gods. Referred to Kether, the Crown and the first emanation, it is as near as the Tree can come to the ineffable source — pure being-consciousness-bliss without a second. Parabrahman is not a deity to be worshipped but the ultimate ground in which all deities and worlds arise and dissolve.
tables: XXII. Small Selection of Hindu Deities

paralda.summary: King of the Sylphs, ruler of the elemental spirits of Air.
paralda.description: Paralda is the King of the Sylphs, sovereign of the elemental spirits of Air, set at Aleph — the path of the Fool and of the airy letter, the breath that begins all things. In the Paracelsian order of elemental beings carried into the Golden Dawn, the sylphs are the inhabitants of the winds, quick and light, the life and intelligence of the breathable element; over them Paralda reigns. He is invoked in the working of the Air quarter — the warm, moist, eastern element — and commands the sylphs who govern thought, motion, and the subtle currents that bear sound, scent, and spirit. Esoterically he embodies the volatile, vivifying force of Air: intellect, freedom, and the rushing, ungraspable mobility that mediates between fire and water in the elemental cross.
tables: LXII. Kings of the Elemental Spirits

paralysis.summary: Paralysis at Yod and Virgo — the arrest of motion under exacting Mercury.
paralysis.description: Paralysis is placed on the path of Virgo, the mutable earth sign ruled by Mercury. Virgo governs the nervous detail-work and fine control of the body; paralysis is the extreme failure of that governance — motion arrested, the Mercurial command to the limbs broken off entirely. Where ataxia is movement disordered, paralysis is movement stopped, the earthy body fallen still and unresponsive to the will.

parasa-rama.summary: Parashurama, the axe-wielding avatar of Vishnu — the warrior-sage, at Mercury.
parasa-rama.description: Parashurama, “Rama with the Axe,” is the sixth avatar of Vishnu, the brahmin-warrior who took up arms to cleanse the earth of corrupt and arrogant kshatriyas. Referred to Beth and Mercury, he unites the sage and the warrior — knowledge wedded to decisive, even terrible, action. As the immortal master of weapons and teacher of heroes, he embodies the righteous wrath that restores the balance of the world.
tables: XXII. Small Selection of Hindu Deities

parrot.summary: The bright mimic of Gemini—the talking bird of speech and imitation, plumage of the airy Twins.
parrot.description: The parrot is attributed to Gemini, the airy Mercurial sign of speech and exchange, and it is the great mimic of the bird world: brilliant of plumage, endlessly chattering, able to echo the human voice without always grasping its sense. It figures the Geminian gift of language and the faculty of imitation—the quick, communicative, repeating mind. Like the ape among beasts, the parrot carries a gentle warning within its gift: the power to reproduce words is not the same as the power to understand them. Esoterically the parrot is the talkative surface of the intellect, the bright and clever tongue that can either carry true speech or merely repeat what it has heard, according to the wit behind it.

parthenogenesis.summary: The Virgoan mystery of generation without union, the self-born and immaculate.
parthenogenesis.description: Parthenogenesis—'virgin birth'—is set at Yod and Virgo, the sign of the Virgin and the path of the Hermit, whose nature is sealed, solitary, and self-sufficient. As a magical power it figures the highest mystery of creation from within: the soul, like the goddesses who conceive without a partner, bringing forth the redeemer or the work of attainment out of its own intact substance. It is the spiritual counterpart of the Hermit's enclosed lamp, the light that lights itself.

pasht.summary: Pasht (Bast), the cat-goddess — guardian of joy, home, and the fierce solar eye, at Leo.
pasht.description: Pasht is Bast, the cat-headed goddess of the home, of music and festivity, and of the protective, fiery solar power, here referred to Teth and Leo. Gentle as the household cat yet fierce as the lioness, she guards against evil spirits and embodies the joyful, vital warmth of the sun. Her cult at Bubastis was famed for its ecstatic festivals; she is the playful and the protective feline made divine.

past-master.summary: One who has ruled the Lodge, here among the Supernals — bearer of the transmitted light.
past-master.description: A Past Master is one who has served as Worshipful Master and retains the dignity and experience of that office. Attributed here to the Supernal Triad, the rank signifies the elder authority that has passed beyond active rule into the transmission of wisdom — the seasoned light handed down to guide those who govern now.
tables: CXV. Officers in a Masonic Lodge

pasture.summary: An earth of the sevenfold scheme at Tiphareth — the fair, fruitful land of the solar centre.
pasture.description: The 'Pasture' is the earth assigned to Tiphareth, the radiant, harmonising heart of the Tree, in the Qabalistic scheme of the Seven Earths. As the solar sphere of beauty and balanced life, its corresponding land is the green and fruitful pasture — the temperate, nourishing ground bathed in the central light, the fairest of the inhabited worlds below the supernals.
tables: CV. Ten Earths in Seven Palaces English

patigha.summary: Paṭigha — the Pali name for the fifth fetter, aversion or ill-will.
patigha.description: Patigha (paṭigha) is the Pali for the fifth of the ten fetters, the aversive 'striking-against' of the mind — anger, repugnance and ill-will, set at Geburah. With sensual craving it forms the pair of reactions, grasping and pushing-away, that drive the round of suffering; it is uprooted at the stage of the non-returner. (Its English face appears under 'Hatred'.)

peace.summary: Two of Swords — Peace; Moon in Libra, Chokmah of Air: the mind in balance.
peace.description: Peace is Crowley's title for the Two of Swords, Chokmah of the airy suit, the Moon in the first decan of Libra. The keen energy of the intellect, just risen into duality, is here held in poised equilibrium — two swords crossed without striking, conflict suspended in a fragile harmony. Libra's balance and the Moon's calm grant a respite of the mind, peace restored but not yet secured.
tables: CXXXV. Titles and Attributions of the Sword Suit.

peace-made-of-rubies.summary: A heaven of the Arabs at Chesed — the Abode of Peace, fashioned of rubies.
peace-made-of-rubies.description: In the tabulation of the seven heavens of Islam, the Abode of Peace, made of rubies, is described at Chesed. Among the ascending paradises of the blessed, this is the ruby-built heaven of peace (Dar al-Salam) — its precious red substance and its name of tranquillity assigned to the merciful sphere in the comparative cosmology of the Arab heavens.
tables: CXXVIII. Seven Heavens of the Arabs, English

peach.summary: The sweet, soft fruit of Venus—the peach of sensual delight and, in the East, of immortal life.
peach.description: The Peach is attributed to Venus (Daleth, the Empress). Soft, fragrant, and downy, the very byword for sweetness and sensual ripeness, it is a thoroughly Venusian fruit; in China the peach is moreover the fruit of immortality, grown in the garden of the Queen Mother of the West and ripening but once in many millennia. Esoterically the peach is the tender, sensual sweetness of Venus—the soft fruit of love that, in its Eastern guise, opens upon deathless life.

peacock.summary: The eyed splendour of Aquarius—Juno's bird and the alchemical cauda pavonis, the all-coloured display before perfection.
peacock.description: The peacock is attributed to Aquarius, the sign of the Star, and it is the bird of dazzling display, its great fan spangled with a hundred shining 'eyes'—an apt emblem for the starry, light-bearing nature of that sign. Sacred to Juno and, in the East, the vehicle of high gods, the peacock figures both glorious splendour and the vanity that splendour breeds. In alchemy the cauda pavonis, the 'peacock's tail,' names the stage at which the matter of the Work breaks into iridescent rainbow colours, the shimmering threshold just before the whitening—a sign that the transformation is succeeding. Esoterically the peacock is the radiant, many-eyed display of the soul's powers, the iridescent glory that heralds, but is not yet, the final perfection.

pearl.summary: The lunar stone of Yesod—the Moon, purity, the hidden treasure of the deep.
pearl.description: The pearl is attributed to the lunar sphere of Yesod, its soft luminous sheen the very image of the Moon and of the astral light. Unique among gems as a living product of the sea—formed when an oyster transmutes an irritant into a lustrous sphere—it is a natural symbol of purity, of the feminine mysteries, and of treasure won from the deep unconscious. In many traditions the pearl is the soul itself, or the hidden wisdom that must be sought beneath the waters.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

pelican.summary: The self-wounding bird of Tiphareth—the mother that feeds her young with her own blood, supreme emblem of sacrifice and rebirth.
pelican.description: The pelican is attributed to Tiphareth, the solar sphere of the sacrificed-and-risen god, and it is among the most beloved of the Christian and Rosicrucian symbols. By ancient legend the mother pelican, when no other food remained, pierced her own breast to feed her starving young with her blood, and so became the very image of redemptive self-sacrifice—the one who dies that others may live. This makes it perfectly fitted to Tiphareth, the place of the dying god whose blood renews the world. The Rosy Cross of the higher grades bears the pelican vulning her brood. Esoterically the pelican figures the love that gives its own life-blood for the sake of new life, the sacrifice at the heart of the solar mystery of death and resurrection.

penates.summary: The Penates, gods of the storeroom — guardians of the household's provision, at Cancer.
penates.description: The Penates are the Roman household gods of the larder and the inner store, who with the Lares protected the family's welfare and sustenance. Referred to Cheth and Cancer, the sign of home and nourishment, they are the indwelling guardians of the family's food and prosperity. Honoured at the hearth, they embody the security and continuity of the domestic order.

penguin.summary: The two-realmed bird of Gemini—the wing exchanged for the fin, formal black-and-white of the dual sign.
penguin.description: The penguin is attributed to Gemini, the dual air-sign of the Twins, and though a comical inclusion among the grid's nobler beasts it carries a fitting symbolism: a bird that has given up the air for the water, swimming where its kind fly, and clothed in the formal black-and-white that marks so many of Gemini's creatures. It lives between two elements, belonging fully to neither, an emblem of the doubled and divided nature that is the keynote of the Twins. Esoterically the penguin figures the paradox of the sign—the being of two worlds, the wing turned to a fin, the light and dark worn together—and a reminder that the dual nature can adapt itself to realms its kindred never enter.

pennyroyal.summary: The emmenagogue mint, attributed to the path of Luna; herb of the womb.
pennyroyal.description:
Pennyroyal is set on the lunar path of Gimel among the emmenagogues — herbs that promote menstruation — a fitting placement for a plant governed by the Moon's dominion over the tides of the female body. It has an ancient reputation in folk gynaecology and as an insect-repellent strewing herb. Esoterically it belongs to the lunar mysteries of cycle and generation.

Caution: pennyroyal oil is acutely toxic to the liver and has caused deaths, especially when used as an abortifacient. Historical/symbolic entry only.
pennyroyal.caution: Pennyroyal oil is acutely hepatotoxic; has caused deaths. Historical/symbolic entry only — do not ingest.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

pentagram.summary: The five-pointed star — attributed to Mars/Geburah; emblem of Man and the elements crowned by Spirit.
pentagram.description: The pentagram, the five-pointed star, is attributed by its number to Geburah and the planet Mars, and is the great emblem of the Microcosm — Man — the four elements crowned and governed by the fifth, Spirit. Drawn point upward it signifies Spirit ruling matter and the will exalted; reversed, the spirit subjected to the elements. As the figure of the human form with limbs outstretched, it is the central glyph of the magician's power over the elemental world.
tables: XLIX. Lineal Figures of the Planets, &c., and Geomany

pepper.summary: The fiery grain of Mars—pepper, hot and biting, the martial spice that stings the blood to action.
pepper.description: Pepper is attributed to Mars (Pe, the Tower). The sharp, biting heat of the peppercorn is the very type of a hot, pungent, martial savour—rousing, aggressive, quickening—fitting the planet of war and severity. Esoterically pepper is the kindling fire of Mars taken as scent and taste, the sharp heat that breaks inertia, sharpens the senses, and spurs the will to its stroke.

peppermint.summary: The carminative mint, attributed to Air; cooling, clarifying herb of the breath.
peppermint.description: Peppermint is set on the path of Aleph, the element Air — a cooling, clarifying carminative whose volatile oil opens the breath and settles the stomach, its very airiness and pungent freshness fitting the elemental attribution. A benign and ancient household medicine, it represents the gentle airy virtue of clearing and quickening.
peppermint.caution: Generally very safe in culinary amounts; the concentrated oil is potent.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

perception.summary: The third skandha — perception (saññā), the faculty that recognises and labels experience.
perception.description: Perception is saññā, the third of the five skandhas, attributed to the path of Saturn. It is the recognising, marking and naming faculty — that which seizes on the distinguishing signs of an object and identifies it: 'blue', 'a man', 'a sound'. Saññā makes experience legible, but it also overlays the bare given with concept and memory, and so can distort as readily as it clarifies. Set at Saturn, the sphere of form, definition and limit, it figures the mind's structuring power, the imposition of name and category upon the flux of the senses.

perdition.summary: Abaddon, Perdition — a hell-compartment set at Chesed.
perdition.description: 'Perdition' (Abaddon, 'destruction') is a compartment of Gehenna in the sevenfold scheme of the Hells, here attributed to Chesed. Personified elsewhere as the angel of the bottomless pit, Abaddon names the region of utter loss and undoing in the descending underworld — the place of perdition that, paradoxically set at the merciful sphere, marks the highest of the named Hells in the Qabalistic cosmology.
tables: CVII. Ten Hells in Seven Palaces English

perfect-intelligence.summary: The Eighth Path, named again — the Perfect Intelligence of Hod, the finished splendour of mind.
perfect-intelligence.description: 'Perfect Intelligence' (Sekhel Shalem) is the companion title of the Eighth Path of Hod, the Mercurial sphere of intellect and form. Where 'Absolute' stresses its self-sufficiency, 'Perfect' stresses its completeness: Hod is the place where the powers of mind, language, and number are brought to finished, flawless order. The Sepher Yetzirah roots its perfection in the hidden depths of Gedulah above, so that the splendour of Hod is the merciful abundance of Chesed made exact, articulate, and whole.
tables: XIII. Paths of the Sefer Yetzirah

perfected-success.summary: Ten of Cups — Perfected Success; Mars in Pisces, Malkuth of Water: fulfilment complete.
perfected-success.description: Perfected Success is the Golden Dawn name for the Ten of Cups, Malkuth of the watery suit, Mars in the last decan of Pisces. The cups arrange themselves in the figure of the Tree of Life, the waters of feeling realised entirely in the world below. It signifies lasting contentment and the consummation of emotional good fortune — though, being a ten, it already contains the seed of its own dissolution.
tables: CXXXIV. Titles and Attributions of the Chalice Suit

perfected-work.summary: Four of Wands — Perfected Work; Venus in Aries, Chesed of Fire: harmonious settling.
perfected-work.description: Perfected Work is the Golden Dawn title of the Four of Wands, Chesed of the fiery suit, Venus in the last decan of Aries. The active will of Fire is here brought to its first stable completion: a square of wands, order and rule established under the merciful, ordering influence of Jupiter's sphere with Venus's grace. It marks the satisfying close of a phase of effort — sound, but only a way-station before strife returns.
tables: CXXXIII. Titles and Attributions of the Wand Suit

pergamos.summary: Pergamos — the church 'where Satan's seat is,' attributed to Mars (Pe).
pergamos.description: Pergamos, dwelling 'where Satan's seat is' and called to war against false doctrine, is set in 777 in the path of Pe and the sphere of Mars. The martial attribution suits a church defined by spiritual conflict — holding fast the Name amid the strongholds of the adversary.
tables: XXXVI. Selection of Christian Gods (10); Apostles (12); Evangelists(4); and Churches of Asia (7)

peridot.summary: The green stone of Virgo — the pure green of the harvest and the Hermit's earth.
peridot.description: Peridot — gem olivine — is set at the path of Yod and Virgo, the mutable-earth sign of the harvest and the Hermit. Its clear olive-green is the colour of growing things and of the fertile field that Virgo rules; mined since antiquity (the Egyptians drew it from the 'serpent isle' of the Red Sea), it was prized as a stone of light and clarity. Esoterically it is the green of the earthly harvest perfected by Mercurial discernment.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

perpetual-intelligence.summary: The Thirty-first Path — the Perpetual Intelligence of Shin, regulating the courses of Sun and Moon.
perpetual-intelligence.description: The Thirty-first Path is the Perpetual or Continuous Intelligence (Sekhel Tadiri), attributed to the letter Shin and the element Fire (and, in the extended scheme, Spirit), the path of The Aeon (Judgement) joining Hod to Malkuth. The Sepher Yetzirah says it regulates the motions of the Sun and Moon, each in its proper order and orbit. The threefold flame of Shin is the perpetual fire of the last judgement and the new aeon — the ceaseless, self-renewing combustion by which the lights are kept in their everlasting rounds.
tables: XIII. Paths of the Sefer Yetzirah

persephone.summary: Persephone, queen of the underworld — the maiden of spring carried into the dark, at Malkuth.
persephone.description: Persephone is the daughter of Demeter, carried off by Hades to be queen of the dead, who returns to the upper world each spring and descends again each autumn. Referred to Malkuth, the Kingdom at the foot of the Tree, she is the maiden who bridges the living and the dead, the seed that must go down into the earth to rise again. Her annual cycle is the very rhythm of death and rebirth in the natural world.

perseus.summary: Perseus, slayer of Medusa — the hero of the reflected gaze, at Leo.
perseus.description: Perseus is the Greek hero who beheaded the Gorgon Medusa, using his polished shield to look upon her safely, and freed Andromeda from the sea-monster. Referred to Teth and Leo, the sign of heroic strength, he represents valour guided by cunning — the courage that conquers the petrifying terror by indirection. His tale of the mirror-gaze became a favourite emblem of the soul's confrontation with what cannot be faced directly.
tables: CLXIX. Egyptian Gods of the Zodiac (Succedent)

peur.summary: Geomantic figure 'Boy' (Puer) — attributed to Mars; energy, rashness, the masculine.
peur.description: Puer, 'the boy,' is one of the sixteen geomantic figures, attributed to Mars and associated with Aries. A figure of raw masculine energy, courage, and impulsiveness, it signifies action, conflict, and headstrong drive — well-omened for war, contest, and bold undertakings, but rash and quarrelsome in matters of peace or love. It is the martial counterpart to the Venusian Puella.
tables: XLIX. Lineal Figures of the Planets, &c., and Geomany

ph.summary: The aspirated 'Ph' (φ) sound — Crowley's English-equivalent at the fifth Sephirah, Geburah.
ph.description: 'Ph' is the Latin transcription of the Coptic Ⲫ (Phi, derived from Greek φ), placed by Crowley at Geburah, the fifth Sephirah of severity and martial force. The plosive, breathy 'Ph' is the sound of expelled energy — the breath driven out under pressure — and its placement at the sphere of Mars and the burning sword is consistent with Crowley's lifelong interest in sound as a magical force. The entry preserves only this fact: that in 777's Coptic-equivalence column, the labio-dental aspirate sits with the warrior Sephirah.
tables: LI. English Equivalent of the Coptic Alphabet

ph-nix.summary: The fire-reborn bird of Tiphareth—the phoenix that burns to ash and rises again, the solar resurrection itself.
ph-nix.description: The phoenix is attributed to Tiphareth, the solar centre of death and rebirth, and it is the supreme bird of resurrection: the creature that, at the end of its long life, builds a pyre of fragrant wood, is consumed in flame, and rises new-born from its own ashes. No symbol fits Tiphareth better, for that sphere is the seat of the god who dies and is reborn at the heart of the cosmos, and the phoenix enacts that mystery in solar fire. In the magical weapons the Phoenix Wand carries this power of regeneration. Esoterically the phoenix figures the self that willingly undergoes its own death by fire and rises transfigured—the immortal solar spirit that is renewed precisely by being consumed, the perfect emblem of the great transformation.

phaldor.summary: Oracles — the Nuctemeron genius of the eleventh hour presiding over oracles, set by Crowley at Aquarius.
phaldor.description: In the Nuctemeron — the “Day Illumined by Night” ascribed to Apollonius of Tyana and preserved by Éliphas Lévi — Phaldor is numbered among the genii of the eleventh hour, the spirit of oracles. His province is the oracles, the prophetic voices and the answers they return. Crowley arranges the twelve hours and their genii upon the paths of the Tree (777, Table CLXXIII), placing him at Aquarius (Tzaddi).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

phaleg.summary: Olympic Spirit of Mars, the War-Lord who raises men to honour through conflict and command.
phaleg.description: Phaleg is the Olympic Spirit of Mars, named in the Arbatel "the War-Lord," set by Crowley at Pe, the path of the Tower and of martial force. To the fierce, sundering nature of Mars and Geburah the tradition ascribes Phaleg's power to raise men to great honour and renown in all warlike affairs, to govern strife, courage, iron, and the severing edge. He reigns upon the Day of Mars (Tuesday). Esoterically he is the spirit of necessary destruction and disciplined violence — the lightning that throws down what is unsound, the surgeon's stroke of Geburah carried into the field of action, ambition and valour personified.

phalgus.summary: Judgment — the Nuctemeron genius of the fourth hour presiding over judgment, set by Crowley at Cancer.
phalgus.description: Among the genii of the fourth hour in the Nuctemeron of Apollonius of Tyana, Phalgus presides over judgment. He presides over discernment and the passing of sentence upon what is weighed. Lévi gives the roll of the hour-genii in his Transcendental Magic; Crowley tabulates them along the paths of the Tree (Table CLXXIII), assigning Phalgus to Cancer (Cheth).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

phallophorus.summary: Phallophorus, the phallus-bearer — the ithyphallic principle of generation, at Pisces.
phallophorus.description: Phallophorus, “bearer of the phallus,” is an epithet of the ithyphallic gods and a title for those who carried the sacred phallus in fertility processions, here referred to Qoph and Pisces. The image expresses the generative power celebrated in the rites of Osiris, Dionysus, and Min — the divine seed of life borne in solemn procession. It marks the creative, regenerative current flowing even through the watery, dissolving sign of the Fishes.
tables: CLXXI. Egyptian Gods of the Zodiac (Cadent)

phantoms.summary: The insubstantial apparitions, set at Pisces — fleeting images cast upon the astral waters.
phantoms.description: Among the Legendary Orders of Being, the Phantoms are attributed to the path of Pisces. They are the apparitions and unreal appearances — shapes seen and vanishing, images without solid substance, the very stuff of illusion. Their attribution to Pisces, the dreamy, dissolving water-sign of glamour and the blurred boundary of things, is fitting: phantoms are the deceptive forms that arise upon the astral and psychic waters, half-real, half-imagined, the order of beings nearest to mere illusion.

pharzuph.summary: Fornication — the Nuctemeron genius of the fourth hour presiding over fornication, set by Crowley at Cancer.
pharzuph.description: Among the genii of the fourth hour in the Nuctemeron of Apollonius of Tyana, Pharzuph presides over fornication. He is the spirit of lust and illicit union, the genius of the bed unsanctioned. Lévi gives the roll of the hour-genii in his Transcendental Magic; Crowley tabulates them along the paths of the Tree (Table CLXXIII), assigning Pharzuph to Cancer (Cheth).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

phenex.summary: The thirty-seventh spirit of the Goetia, a phoenix-formed marquis of Aries — a marvellous poet who hopes for redemption.
phenex.description: Phenex (Pheynix) is the thirty-seventh spirit of the Goetia, a great marquis of the decans of Aries. He is a marvellous poet, obedient to the operator, and will discourse willingly of the sciences. He appears as a phoenix, singing sweet notes in the voice of a child — a song the magician is warned not to heed until it takes human form. It is said he hopes after many centuries to return to the order of the Thrones. A spirit of the fiery sign, he is the singer and poet who yearns for heaven.

phi.summary: Phi — a letter of the Coptic alphabet (ph), which Crowley attributes to 5 Geburah.
phi.description: Phi is a letter of the Coptic alphabet — the script in which the Egyptian language was written in the Christian era, the Greek alphabet adapted to Egyptian speech. It is from Greek phi. Crowley folds the Coptic alphabet into the great correspondence of letters and paths in 777 (Table LI), assigning Phi to 5 Geburah on the Tree of Life, so that the Egyptian-Christian script takes its station among the Hebrew letters and the keys of the Tarot.
tables: LI. Names of the Coptic Letters

philadelphia.summary: Philadelphia — the church of the open door, attributed to Jupiter (Kaph).
philadelphia.description: Philadelphia ('brotherly love'), the faithful church before whom an 'open door' is set, is referred in 777 to the path of Kaph and the sphere of Jupiter. The Jovial attribution of expansion, beneficence, and opportunity suits the one church wholly praised: the door of grace flung wide, the kingly favour of Jupiter.
tables: XXXVI. Selection of Christian Gods (10); Apostles (12); Evangelists(4); and Churches of Asia (7)

philosophus.summary: 4°=7, the grade of Netzach — the Philosopher; mastery of the element of Fire.
philosophus.description: Philosophus is the grade of the Golden Dawn and A∴A∴ attributed to Netzach, the sphere of Venus and victory. The fourth of the outer grades, it completes the elemental work with the mastery of Fire and the cultivation of devotion, love, and the imaginative faculty. The Philosophus has learned to feel the unity behind nature's diversity, ascending the Tree by the path of the senses refined into spiritual ardour.

phlogabitus.summary: Adornment — the Nuctemeron genius of the third hour presiding over adornment, set by Crowley at Gemini.
phlogabitus.description: In the Nuctemeron — the “Day Illumined by Night” ascribed to Apollonius of Tyana and preserved by Éliphas Lévi — Phlogabitus is numbered among the genii of the third hour, the spirit of adornment. He presides over ornament and finery, the beautifying and decking of the person. Crowley arranges the twelve hours and their genii upon the paths of the Tree (777, Table CLXXIII), placing him at Gemini (Zayin).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

phoenix-wand.summary: The wand of regeneration at Leo—the rod surmounted by the phoenix, the implement of the rising, reborn spirit.
phoenix-wand.description: The Phoenix Wand is attributed to Leo, and it is the implement crowned with the phoenix, the bird that is reborn from its own ashes—a wand of resurrection and of the solar fire of regeneration. In the Golden Dawn mysteries it is borne by the officer who enacts the role of the reviving power, the one who raises the candidate as the phoenix rises from the flame. Its station at Leo, the fixed-fire sign of the Sun, marks it as the rod of the regenerating solar energy. Esoterically the Phoenix Wand is the magician's instrument of renewal and rebirth—the will directed toward transformation through the fire, the rod that calls forth new life from the ashes of the old, the power of the undying spirit to rise again.

phosphorus.summary: The light-bearer, attributed to Chokmah; the element of cold fire and the spark of force.
phosphorus.description:
Phosphorus — its name means 'light-bearer,' the Greek of Lucifer and the morning star — is placed at Chokmah, the sphere of the first outgoing force and the wisdom of beginning. It glows in the dark with a cold spontaneous fire and bursts into flame at a touch, a fitting image of the primal, kindling energy of the supernal Father. It is also essential to the chemistry of life and of thought (in the nerves and the genetic code). Esoterically it is the spark — the light-bearing impulse that initiates.

Caution: white phosphorus is acutely toxic and dangerously flammable. Scholarly entry only.
phosphorus.caution: White phosphorus is acutely toxic and spontaneously flammable. Scholarly entry only.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

phrath.summary: One of the four rivers of Eden — the Euphrates, attributed to Earth.
phrath.description: Phrath (Perath) is the biblical name of the river Euphrates, the fourth of the streams that watered the garden of Eden (Genesis 2). Among the four elemental rivers of Paradise it is commonly attributed to Earth, the densest of the elements. As the great river of Mesopotamia and the boundary of the Promised Land, it figures the earthy current of the descending life, the channel by which the river of Eden reaches the solid ground of the world.

phthysis.summary: Phthisis (consumption) at Zayin and Gemini — the wasting disease of the Gemini lungs.
phthysis.description: Phthisis — the old name for pulmonary consumption, or tuberculosis — is attributed to the path of Gemini, the airy sign that rules the lungs and the organs of breath. Consumption is the classic disease of the lungs, the body wasting as the breath fails; set under Gemini it is the corruption of the very seat of air and respiration. Symbolically it is the slow failing of the breath of life in its own elemental house.

phul.summary: Olympic Spirit of the Moon, supreme over his fellows; lord of silver, the waters, and long life.
phul.description: Phul is the Olympic Spirit of the Moon in the Arbatel, named "the Lord of the Powers of the Moon" and reckoned the supreme regent of the seven, set by Crowley at Gimel, the lunar path of the High Priestess that crosses the Abyss. Following the Moon's watery, reflective nature, the tradition grants Phul the power to change all metals into silver, to heal the dropsy, to command the spirits of the waters (the undines, who serve and appear in human form), and to prolong life to three hundred years. He reigns upon the Day of the Moon (Monday). Esoterically he is the spirit of reflection, flux, and the tides of the unconscious carried into the world of forces — the silver mirror of Yesod and the veiling priestess of the Middle Pillar, governing dream, generation, and the rhythmic ebb and flow of all living things.

phuonidie.summary: Name of the third decan of Leo, the same Martial face of embattled valour.
phuonidie.description: Phuonidie is the name 777 preserves for the third decan of Leo (20°–30°), the Martial face the gods-column calls Neththe. Bearing the Seven of Wands—Valour—it names the embattled courage at the close of the Lion's reign. It belongs to the Egyptian decan-names, the ten-degree divisions that once served as star-clocks of the night.
tables: CLXXII. Egyptian Names of the Cadent Decans

pi.summary: Pi — a letter of the Coptic alphabet (p), which Crowley attributes to the path of Pe (Mars).
pi.description: Pi is a letter of the Coptic alphabet — the script in which the Egyptian language was written in the Christian era, the Greek alphabet adapted to Egyptian speech. It is from Greek pi. Crowley folds the Coptic alphabet into the great correspondence of letters and paths in 777 (Table LI), assigning Pi to the path of Pe (Mars) on the Tree of Life, so that the Egyptian-Christian script takes its station among the Hebrew letters and the keys of the Tarot.
tables: LI. Names of the Coptic Letters

pi-osiris.summary: Pi-Osiris, “the Osiris” — the slain and risen god in his Virgoan aspect.
pi-osiris.description: Pi-Osiris means simply “the Osiris,” the great god of death, resurrection, and the fertile Nile, here referred to Yod and Virgo. Osiris, murdered by Set and restored by Isis, is the archetype of the dying-and-rising god and the judge of the dead; in the Virgoan attribution he is linked to the seed buried in the earth that springs again as grain. Every blessed dead Egyptian became “an Osiris,” sharing in his triumph over death.
tables: CLXIX. Egyptian Gods of the Zodiac (Succedent)

pineal-gland.summary: The Pineal Gland — physical correlate of the brow centre, attributed to Chokmah.
pineal-gland.description: The pineal gland, the small endocrine body deep in the brain long held to be the seat of inner vision (Descartes' 'seat of the soul'), is given in 777 as a bodily correlate of the higher centre at Chokmah — near the station of the Ajna 'third eye.' It marks the meeting of physiology and mysticism: the gland of light-sensitive rhythm read as the organ of spiritual sight.

pipal-tree.summary: The sacred pipal of Wisdom—the Indian fig (Ficus religiosa) of awakening, set at Chokmah.
pipal-tree.description: The Pipal Tree (Ficus religiosa, the same sacred fig as the Bo and the Ashvattha) is attributed to Chokmah, the sphere of supernal Wisdom. Holiest of Indian trees, its restless heart-shaped leaves trembling upon long stalks, it is the tree under which sages meditate and the Buddha awoke—the very tree of enlightenment. Esoterically the pipal at Chokmah is the tree of pure Wisdom, the canopy of awakening under which the conditioned mind opens into the unbounded.

pisces.summary: Mutable Water, ruled by Jupiter/Neptune—dissolution, compassion, and mystical union.
pisces.description:
Pisces, the Fishes, is mutable Water ruled traditionally by Jupiter (and in the modern scheme by Neptune)—the final sign, of dissolution, compassion, imagination, and mystical union. In 777 it corresponds to the letter Qoph and the path of the Tarot trump The Moon (path 29), the dark journey through illusion and the deep before dawn. It governs the boundless, the sacrificial, and the return of all things to their source.

The two fishes bound and swimming in opposite directions figure the tension of soul and body, spirit and matter, ever pulling apart yet joined—the last lesson of the wheel before it begins again. Pisces’ gift is empathy, devotion, and visionary art; its shadow, escapism and self-loss. As the closing sign it dissolves the year’s forms back into the ocean of potential.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

pison.summary: One of the four rivers of Eden — Pishon, that 'compasseth the land of Havilah.'
pison.description: Pison (Pishon) is the first-named of the four rivers of Eden, 'that compasseth the whole land of Havilah, where there is gold' (Genesis 2). In the Qabalistic reading of the garden, the four rivers are the elemental streams into which the one river of Paradise divides as it flows down into manifestation. Pison thus represents one of the four channels by which the undivided life of Eden is distributed to the world.

pit-of-destruction.summary: Beer Shachath, the Pit of Destruction — a hell-compartment set at Tiphareth.
pit-of-destruction.description: The 'Pit of Destruction' (Beer Shachath) is a compartment of Gehenna in the sevenfold scheme of the Hells, here set at Tiphareth. Named in the Psalms as the pit from which the soul prays to be delivered, it is the deep well of ruin and corruption in the underworld's descent — one of the named halls through which, in the Qabalistic cosmology, the unredeemed soul must pass.
tables: CVII. Ten Hells in Seven Palaces English

plain.summary: Araboth, the highest heaven — rendered 'Plain', the supernal-rooted summit of the seven skies.
plain.description: In the Talmudic doctrine of the seven heavens (Hagigah 12b), Araboth is the seventh and highest heaven, here rendered 'Plain' and rooted at the supernal triad. It is the dwelling of righteousness and judgement, holding the treasuries of life, peace, and blessing, the souls of the righteous and the spirits yet to be born, and the dew with which God will revive the dead. As the topmost heaven it is the very floor of the divine throne-world.
tables: XCIV. The Heavens of Assiah English

planets.summary: A content of the Firmament at Hod — the wandering planets set among the lights.
planets.description: The planets are reckoned among the contents of the Firmament (Raqia), attributed to Hod in the table of the heavens. With the sun, moon, and stars they are set within the second heaven, the wandering lights whose measured courses move across the vault — appropriately gathered to Hod, the Mercurial sphere of the ordered motions of number and time.
tables: XCV. Contents of the Heavens of Assiah

pleasure.summary: Six of Cups — Pleasure; Sun in Scorpio, Tiphareth of Water: joy in full flower.
pleasure.description: The Six of Cups, Pleasure, is Tiphareth in the suit of Water and the second decan of Scorpio, warmed by the Sun. The harmonising solar centre restores the troubled waters to their fullest, most radiant flowering — six cups arranged like a blossoming lotus-garden, feeling perfected and freely enjoyed. It is well-being, the innocent fruition of desire, joy without (as yet) the worm of excess.
tables: CXXXIV. Titles and Attributions of the Chalice Suit

pluto.summary: Pluto—death, regeneration, and the underworld power of transformation (modern planet).
pluto.description:
Pluto, discovered in 1930, entered the symbolic system as the planet of death and regeneration, the underworld power that destroys utterly in order to renew—transformation at the deepest, most irreversible level. It is associated with the supernal reaches and the Abyss, and with the alchemical nigredo, the blackening that precedes rebirth.

As Hades–Pluto, lord of the dead and of hidden wealth beneath the earth, this power governs what is buried, repressed, and capable of resurrection. Its work is the forced confrontation with mortality and the shadow, from which—if survived—comes a profounder life. Its modern reclassification as a ‘dwarf planet’ has not displaced its potent symbolic role.
tables: CXXXIX. Planets Exalted in the Signs of the Zodiac
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

pneumonia.summary: Pneumonia at Zayin and Gemini — inflammation of the airy organs of breath.
pneumonia.description: Pneumonia is likewise set on the path of Gemini, the sign governing the lungs. Where phthisis is the slow wasting of those organs, pneumonia is their acute inflammation and congestion — the air-passages flooded, the breath labouring. As an affliction of the Gemini province it figures the choking of the body's airy commerce, the lungs, those twin bellows of life, overwhelmed.

polayan.summary: Nocturnal angelic Lord of Aquarius within the Airy Triplicity.
polayan.description: Polayan is the night-governor of Aquarius among the angelic Lords of the Triplicities. As the fixed member of the Air trine by night, Aquarius' clear reason becomes the night air of solitary vision, ideas germinating in the dark before they are spoken; Polayan presides over this nocturnal, visionary intellect.

pollux.summary: Pollux, the immortal twin of the Dioscuri — the boxer who shared his deathlessness, at Gemini.
pollux.description: Pollux is the immortal son of Zeus and Leda, twin to mortal Castor, renowned as a boxer and protector of sailors. Referred to Zayin and Gemini, he embodies the divine half of the celebrated pair; when Castor died, Pollux begged Zeus to let them share immortality, and so the two were set among the stars as Gemini. He is the emblem of devotion that overcomes even the division of death.

tables: CXLIX. Magical Images of the Decans (Ascendent)

pomegranate.summary: Persephone's fruit of the underworld—the many-seeded pomegranate of Malkuth, hung upon the High Priestess's veil.
pomegranate.description: The Pomegranate is given to Malkuth and to the Moon (Gimel, the High Priestess)—and upon the veil of the High Priestess, between the pillars, the pomegranates are figured. It is the fruit Persephone ate in Hades, binding her to the underworld for half the year, and so the very emblem of the descent into the kingdom of the dead and the cycle of return. Its rind packed with crimson seeds makes it a sign of teeming fertility and of the hidden, manifold life of Malkuth. Esoterically the pomegranate is the gate of the mysteries, the fruit whose tasting binds the soul to the lower world and to the wheel of generation.

poplar.summary: The hero's tree of Jupiter—the white poplar of Heracles, crown of the victor and of the upper world.
poplar.description: The Poplar is attributed to Jupiter (Kaph, the Wheel).
