The white poplar was sacred to Heracles, who wore its leaves crowning his brow on his return from the underworld—their two-toned leaves, dark above and silver below, said to mark the realms of the dead and the living. As a tall, swift-growing, kingly tree it suits expansive, sovereign Jupiter. Esoterically the poplar is the Jovial tree of the hero's triumph, the silver-backed leaf that remembers both worlds and crowns the one who has passed between them.

populus.summary: Geomantic figure 'People' — attributed to the Moon; the crowd, multitude, the neutral tide.
populus.description: Populus, 'people' or 'crowd,' is one of the sixteen geomantic figures, attributed to the Moon and associated with Cancer. Composed of all eight points doubled, it represents the multitude, the assembly, and the shifting tide of public feeling. Of itself it is neutral, a gathering whose meaning depends on its company — the lunar emblem of the many, receptive and ever-changing.
tables: XLIX. Lineal Figures of the Planets, &c., and Geomany

poseidon.summary: Neptune—mysticism, dissolution, dream, and the oceanic (modern planet).
poseidon.description:
Neptune, discovered in 1846, was taken into the esoteric system as the planet of mysticism, imagination, dissolution, and the oceanic unconscious—the dissolver of boundaries between self and cosmos. It is associated with the highest reaches of the Tree (sometimes Kether or the element Water in its spiritual octave) and with visionary, devotional, and transcendent states.

Where Uranus shatters by sudden insight, Neptune dissolves by gentle merging; its shadow is illusion, glamour, and self-deception, its glory the genuine mystical union in which the separate ego is washed away. As lord of the sea it rules all that is fluid, formless, and infinite.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

power.summary: Four of Disks — Power / Earthly Power; Sun in Capricorn, Chesed of Earth.
power.description: The Four of Disks, Power (Earthly Power), is Chesed in the suit of Earth and the third decan of Capricorn under the Sun. The fours bring stable order, and matter ruled by merciful Jupiter's sphere and the Sun becomes a fortress: four discs as the towers and walls of a citadel, law and dominion established on earth. It is worldly authority, security, and the consolidation of material strength — solid, but rigid and on guard.
tables: CXXXVI. Titles and Attributions of the Pantacle Suit

power-of-acquiring-political.summary: The Jupiterian power of rising to political ascendancy and command over others.
power-of-acquiring-political.description: The Power of Acquiring Political Ascendency is attributed to Kaph and Jupiter, the path of the Wheel of Fortune, the planet of expansion, rulership, and worldly fortune. As a magical power it is the operation for honour, office, and dominion—the drawing-down of Jupiter's largesse to lift the magician into authority and the favour of the great. The benevolent king-planet governs all increase of station, and works for power and patronage turn upon his turning wheel.

power-of-acquiring-wealth.summary: The solar power of gathering riches, the magnetism of gold drawn to gold.
power-of-acquiring-wealth.description: The Power of Acquiring Wealth is set at Resh and the Sun, the sphere of gold, abundance, and radiant generosity. As a magical power it is the drawing of riches and prosperity—the operation by which the magician aligns himself with the solar current of increase so that wealth flows toward him. The Sun, giver of all growth and ripeness, is the natural lord of plenty, and works for wealth fall under its golden dominion, tempered by the warning that gold sought for itself alone tarnishes the soul.

power-of-being-in-two.summary: The Geminian power of bilocation, of being present in two or more places at one time.
power-of-being-in-two.description: The Power of Being in Two or More Places at One Time is set at Zayin and Gemini, the path of the Lovers, the sign of the twins and of division and doubling. As a magical power it is bilocation—the projection of a perceptible double so that the operator appears, or acts, in more than one place at once. Gemini's dual, mercurial nature makes it the proper seat of this faculty, an exteriorising of the body of light reported in the lives of many saints and magi.

power-of-casting-enchantments.summary: The Cancerian power of casting enchantments, the binding magic of the watery moon.
power-of-casting-enchantments.description: The Power of Casting Enchantments belongs to Cheth and Cancer, the path of the Chariot, the cardinal water sign ruled by the Moon. As a magical power it is the weaving of spells that bind, charm, or compel—the throwing of an enchantment over person or place. Cancer's tenacious, sheltering, tidal nature lends this work its grip; the same lunar water that nourishes and protects can, turned to enchantment, enclose another in a current not their own.

power-of-consecrating-things.summary: The Aries power of consecration, the kindling of things with magical virtue.
power-of-consecrating-things.description: The Power of Consecrating Things is set at Heh and Aries, the cardinal fire of beginnings and forceful initiation. As a magical power it is the act of making sacred—charging an object, place, or instrument with divine force so that it becomes a fit vessel of the work. The pioneering, igniting energy of Aries is well suited to consecration, which is precisely the first kindling of the holy fire within the profane.

power-of-training-wild-beasts.summary: The Leonine power of mastering wild beasts, the magic of dominion over the animal world.
power-of-training-wild-beasts.description: The Power of Training Wild Beasts is attributed to Teth and Leo, the path of Strength (Lust), whose image is the woman who masters the lion with a gentle hand. As a magical power it is the command of the animal kingdom—the calming and governing of savage creatures—through the radiant, courageous force of the heart that Leo embodies. It is dominion not by violence but by the higher will that beasts instinctively obey, the taming of the lion that is also the taming of one's own animal nature.

powerful-lion.summary: Design detail of Strength/Lust (Teth): the fierce and powerful lion.
powerful-lion.description: ‘Powerful lion’ completes Liber 777's design for Atu VIII/XI, Strength/Lust (path of Teth, Leo): ‘A smiling woman holds the open jaws of a fierce and powerful lion.’ The lion is Leo itself—the solar beast, the concentrated vital and sexual force of nature at its most potent. In the trump it is neither slain nor caged but joyously mastered, its open jaws held by the smiling woman. The powerful lion is the energy that, rightly governed, becomes the strength of the adept.
tables: CLXXXI. Correct Design of Tarot Trumps

practicus.summary: 3°=8, the grade of Hod — the Practitioner; mastery of the element of Water.
practicus.description: Practicus is the grade attributed to Hod, the sphere of Mercury and intellect. Here the aspirant masters the element of Water and undertakes the study of the formative mysteries — Qabalah, astrology, and the disciplines of the mind. The grade trains the reason and the receptive, reflective faculties, building the mental vessel that later work will require.

prana.summary: Prana, the vital breath — the life-force pervading body and cosmos, at Binah and Hod.
prana.description: Prana is the vital breath or life-energy of Hindu and yogic thought, the subtle force that animates the body and pervades the whole universe. Referred to Binah and to Hod, it is the formative, sustaining current drawn in with the breath and circulated through the subtle channels. To master prana through breath-control (pranayama) is to govern the very energy of life; it is the bridge between body, mind, and the cosmic vitality.
tables: XXII. Small Selection of Hindu Deities

prana-yama.summary: Prāṇāyāma — the control of the breath and vital force, set at Spirit.
prana-yama.description: Prana-yama is the yogic regulation of the breath among the Hindu/Buddhist Results, attributed to Spirit. The fourth limb of Patañjali's yoga, it is the disciplined control and extension of prāṇa, the vital force carried on the breath — the measured inhalation, retention and exhalation by which the energies of the body are gathered and the mind made still. Set at Spirit, the quintessence, it figures the mastery of the life-current itself, the bridge by which the gross body is linked to the subtle and the will laid upon the very rhythm of living.
tables: XXIV. Certain of the Hindu/Buddhist Results

praying-mantis.summary: The prophet-insect of Jupiter—the 'seer' at prayer, devourer of its mate, ambiguous oracle of fortune.
praying-mantis.description: The praying mantis is attributed to Jupiter, and its very name preserves its esoteric character: the Greek mantis means 'prophet' or 'diviner,' so that the insect, reared up in its attitude of prayer, was held to be a small soothsayer, a bringer of omen and counsel. This prophetic, oracular aspect suits the Jupiterian sphere of providence and the wheel of fortune. Yet the mantis is also the cool predator that devours its mate in the act of love, a creature of devout posture and merciless appetite. Esoterically the praying mantis figures the prophetic power that comes wrapped in ambiguity—wisdom and ravening joined—the seer whose oracle, like fortune itself, may bring blessing or doom according to how it is met.

tables: CLI. Magical Images of the Decans (Cadent)

preliminary.summary: The preparatory discipline at Leo—the preliminary labour of self-mastery that conditions the Work.
preliminary.description: Listed among the weapons at Leo, beside 'the Discipline,' the Preliminary signifies the preparatory work that must precede any true operation—the initial labour of purification, self-control and conditioning by which the operator makes himself fit for the force he intends to wield. Under Leo, the fiery sign of the strong, ardent will, this preliminary is the disciplining of that very strength, the breaking-in of the lion before it can be ridden. No weapon avails in untrained hands; the Preliminary is the unglamorous first work that all the rest presupposes. Esoterically the Preliminary is the necessary groundwork of the magician—the preparatory ordeal and discipline that tempers the raw power of the self, the indispensable first labour without which the higher Work cannot safely begin.

priapus.summary: The ithyphallic god of Capricorn—the erect generative power, lord of gardens and the irrepressible force of life.
priapus.description: Priapus is attributed to Capricorn (the path of Ayin, the Devil), and he is the rustic ithyphallic god—the guardian of gardens and vineyards depicted with an enormous erect phallus, the embodiment of raw generative power and exuberant fertility. His place at the Devil card is exact, for he is the same horned, lustful, life-engendering force that the fearful brand obscene and the wise revere as the engine of nature's increase. Comic and shameless, Priapus is fecundity that cannot be repressed, the creative organ raised in frank potency. Esoterically Priapus figures the generative force of nature in its most direct and unabashed form—the erect creative power of Capricorn and the Devil, the irrepressible engine of life that the initiate learns to honour rather than to fear, the phallic god of the teeming earth.
tables: CLXXXI. Correct Design of Tarot Trumps

pride.summary: The solar vice of pride, the self-exaltation of the unredeemed heart.
pride.description: Pride is named among the vices at Resh and the Sun (and at Netzach), the radiant centre whose shadow is self-glorification. As the dark side of the solar virtues of confidence and dignity, it is the swelling of the ego that mistakes the reflected light for its own source—the magician who, beholding the powers passing through him, claims them as his own. It is held the most insidious of the vices precisely because it grows at the place of attainment, turning the light of the heart into the glare of vanity.
tables: L. Transcendental Morality (10 Virtues; 7 Deadly Sins; 4 Magic Powers)

princes.summary: The court rank attributed to Tiphareth: the Princes, airy sons of the Tarot court.
princes.description: The Princes are the court rank attributed in Liber 777 to Tiphareth, the solar centre of the Tree. In the Thoth/Golden Dawn scheme the Princes are the sons—the airy, intellectual figures who ride in chariots, the active mediators between the fiery Knights (Kings) and the watery Queens. Their seat at Tiphareth, the place of the harmonised heart and the reborn god, marks them as the questing, princely self at the centre of the personal universe, bearing the powers of their suits into manifestation.
tables: XIV. General Attribution of the Tarot

princesses.summary: The court rank attributed to Malkuth: the Princesses, earthy daughters of the Tarot court.
princesses.description: The Princesses are the court rank attributed in Liber 777 to Malkuth, the Kingdom, the tenth Sephirah and the throne of the manifest world. In the Thoth/Golden Dawn scheme the Princesses are the daughters—the earthy, culminating figures in whom the energy of each suit comes to rest and fruition. Seated at Malkuth, they are the powers of the elements crystallised into matter, the thrones of the Aces and the brides of the Princes, in whom the whole cycle of the court is completed and made real.
tables: XIV. General Attribution of the Tarot

prithiva-bhawana.summary: Pṛthivī-bhāvanā — the meditation upon the earth-element, set at Earth.
prithiva-bhawana.description: Prithiva-Bhawana is the 'cultivation of the earth-element' among the Hindu/Buddhist Results, attributed to the element Earth. It is the concentrative meditation upon earth — its solidity and extension taken inwardly as the object until the mind, steadied upon the element, gains the powers and absorptions proper to it. One of the series of elemental bhāvanās, it answers to the earth-kasiṇa of the Buddhist scheme; set at Earth, it figures the meditator's union with the principle of stability and form.
tables: XXIV. Certain of the Hindu/Buddhist Results

prithivi.summary: The element of solidity, stability, and material manifestation.
prithivi.description:
Earth is the element of solidity, stability, and material manifestation—cold and dry, heavy, still, the ground in which all the other elements come to rest and bear fruit. In 777 it is attributed to the path 32-bis, to the Tatwa Prithivi (a yellow square), and to the northern quarter. Its weapon is the Pentacle or Disk, its archangel Auriel (Uriel), its elemental king Ghob, its creatures the gnomes.

Earth governs the body, the senses, wealth, agriculture, and all that endures and sustains. In the elemental scheme it is the final condensation of spirit into form—the place where the abstract becomes real, and therefore the proper field of the practical, manifesting magician.
tables: XXII. Small Selection of Hindu Deities
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

prop.summary: Samekh — 'prop' or 'support'; the upholding pillar, path of Temperance and Art.
prop.description: Samekh means 'prop,' 'support,' or 'pillar' — that which holds up and sustains, the only fully closed circular letter, a ring of unbroken support. In Liber 777 Samekh is the path of Temperance (Art), attributed to Sagittarius, the great central path joining Tiphareth to Yesod. It is the prop of the aspirant on the Path: the sustaining discipline of the Knowledge and Conversation, the supporting structure that upholds the soul as it ascends the arrow's flight from the foundation to the heart of the Tree.
tables: III. Translation of the Names of the Paths

proteus.summary: Proteus, the shape-shifting old man of the sea — the prophetic, ever-changing water-god, at Aquarius.
proteus.description: Proteus is the Greek sea-god, herdsman of the seals, who could foretell the future but would change his shape endlessly to escape questioning. Referred to Tzaddi and Aquarius, he embodies the fluid, protean nature of the waters and of prophecy — truth that must be seized and held fast through all its transformations. He is the very image of mutable form concealing a hidden certainty.
tables: CLXXI. Egyptian Gods of the Zodiac (Cadent)

prudence.summary: Eight of Disks — Prudence; Sun in Virgo, Hod of Earth: patient cultivation.
prudence.description: The Eight of Disks, Prudence, is Hod in the suit of Earth and the first decan of Virgo under the Sun. Hod's careful intellect applied to matter yields skill and husbandry: eight discs grow as the blossoms of a fruitful tree, the gardener's patient art. It signifies prudence, craftsmanship, attention to detail, and the steady accumulation that comes of disciplined, methodical work.
tables: CXXXVI. Titles and Attributions of the Pantacle Suit

ps.summary: The 'Ps' (psi) sound-value — placed at the path of Tzaddi (Aquarius) in Crowley's table.
ps.description: 'Ps' is the English transcription of the Coptic Ⲯ (Psi, from Greek ψ), which Crowley assigns to path 28 — Tzaddi, ruling Aquarius and the Tarot Star (later, in Liber AL, the Emperor). The hissing-plus-plosive of 'ps' shares acoustic territory with the Hebrew Tzaddi (צ, 'ts'), and Crowley's correspondence relies on this phonetic kinship: the Coptic ψ and the Hebrew צ both crystallise into a sharp, fricative point — apt to Tzaddi's image of the meditative angler casting his line into the deep. The entry is the alphabetic atom alone, placed.
tables: LI. English Equivalent of the Coptic Alphabet

psi.summary: Psi — a letter of the Coptic alphabet (ps), which Crowley attributes to the path of Tzaddi (Aquarius).
psi.description: Psi is a letter of the Coptic alphabet — the script in which the Egyptian language was written in the Christian era, the Greek alphabet adapted to Egyptian speech. It is from Greek psi. Crowley folds the Coptic alphabet into the great correspondence of letters and paths in 777 (Table LI), assigning Psi to the path of Tzaddi (Aquarius) on the Tree of Life, so that the Egyptian-Christian script takes its station among the Hebrew letters and the keys of the Tarot.
tables: LI. Names of the Coptic Letters

psyche.summary: Psyche, the soul made goddess — the mortal bride of Eros, at Malkuth.
psyche.description: Psyche is the mortal maiden whose name means “soul,” beloved of Eros, who through trials and the wrath of Aphrodite at last won immortality and union with love. Referred to Malkuth, the Kingdom, she is the human soul embodied in the world, undergoing suffering and purification to be wedded to the divine. Her tale is a great allegory of the soul's journey through ordeal to its sacred marriage.

ptah.summary: Ptah, the creator-craftsman of Memphis — who made the world by the word, at Kether.
ptah.description: Ptah is the great creator-god of Memphis, the divine artificer who brought the world into being by conceiving it in his heart and speaking it with his tongue. Referred to Kether and to the element of Water, he is the demiurge of the highest, the maker who shapes all forms — patron of craftsmen, architects, and artists. His creation by thought and word makes him a profound emblem of the Logos, the divine intelligence that fashions the cosmos.

puella.summary: Geomantic figure 'Girl' — attributed to Venus; beauty, harmony, the feminine.
puella.description: Puella, 'the girl,' is one of the sixteen geomantic figures, attributed to Venus and associated with Libra. A figure of beauty, harmony, pleasure, and the gentle feminine power, it signifies attraction, peace, and favour in matters of love and friendship. Generally fortunate, it can carry a hint of fickleness or surface-charm, but its essential nature is graceful and benign.
tables: XLIX. Lineal Figures of the Planets, &c., and Geomany

pure.summary: The Ninth Path — the Pure Intelligence of Yesod, purifier and prover of the emanations.
pure.description: The Ninth Path is the Pure Intelligence (Sekhel Tahor), attributed to Yesod, the lunar Foundation. The Sepher Yetzirah says it purifies the emanations, proves and corrects the design of their representations, and establishes their unity that they may remain without diminution or division. As the treasure-house of images and the channel through which all the higher powers are gathered and transmitted to Malkuth, Yesod is the great filter and purifier, refining the flux of force before it crystallises into the material world.
tables: XIII. Paths of the Sefer Yetzirah

pure-musk.summary: A heaven of the Arabs at the lower Sephiroth — a paradise of the fragrance of pure musk.
pure-musk.description: In the tabulation of the seven heavens of Islam, pure musk names the fragrant substance of one of the ascending paradises, attributed to Yesod and Malkuth. Islamic descriptions of Jannah dwell on its perfumes, its soil said to be of musk; in 777's comparative scheme this musk-scented heaven takes its place among the blessed gardens, set at the lower Sephiroth.
tables: CXXVIII. Seven Heavens of the Arabs, English

purple-corpse.summary: The contemplation of the discoloured (livid) corpse — a cemetery meditation on decay.
purple-corpse.description: The Purple Corpse renders the discoloured or livid stage of decomposition (vinīlaka) among the ten foulness-contemplations of the Forty Meditations, attributed to the path of Aquarius. Here the meditator steadies attention on the body gone blotched and purple-black in death. As with all the asubha meditations, the object is deliberately repugnant: by holding the mind unflinching upon the body's corruption, attachment to the flesh — one's own and another's — is undermined, and the contemplative is freed toward dispassion.

purson.summary: The twentieth spirit of the Goetia, a king of Libra who reveals treasure and the secrets of creation.
purson.description: Purson is the twentieth spirit of the Goetia, a great king of the decans of Libra. He tells of things hidden, discovers treasure, declares things past, present and to come, and answers truly of all secret things and of the creation of the world; he can take an aerial or a human body. He appears as a man with the face of a lion, carrying a fierce viper and riding a bear, preceded by a blast of trumpets. A spirit of the balancing air-sign, he is the kingly revealer of hidden wealth and cosmic origins.

putrid-corpse.summary: The contemplation of the festering corpse — a cemetery meditation on the body's decay.
putrid-corpse.description: The Putrid Corpse corresponds to the festering or suppurating stage (vipubbaka) of the ten foulness-contemplations of the Forty Meditations, set at the path of Capricorn. The meditator contemplates the body broken open and oozing in decay. These are among the most austere of Buddhist meditations, prescribed especially as an antidote to lust: by confronting the body's destiny of rot and dissolution, the practitioner cuts through sensual fascination and the deep-seated belief that the body is a fit object of clinging.

pyche.summary: Psyché, the soul — the principle of the living spirit, at Binah.
pyche.description: Pyché is a spelling of Psyche, the soul personified, here referred to Binah, the supernal Mother and the source of form and understanding. Where the maiden Psyche belongs to the Kingdom, this attribution lifts the idea of soul to the heights — the formative, understanding principle from which the individual spirit derives. It marks the soul not merely as the suffering bride but as a power rooted in the great Mother of the Tree.

pyramid-of.summary: The Pyramid of Fire at Shin—the upward triangle of flame, the form of the ascending fiery force.
pyramid-of.description: The Pyramid of Fire is attributed to the letter Shin and the element of Fire, and it is the implement and figure of that element: the pyramid or upward-pointing triangle that is the very glyph of fire, the form of the rising flame and of force ascending to a single point. As a magical figure the fiery pyramid concentrates and lifts the elemental power, gathering the broad base of energy up to one apex. Its station at Shin, the holy fire of spirit, marks it as the form of the spiritual flame. Esoterically the Pyramid of Fire is the ascending, concentrating fiery force in the magician's working—the disciplined gathering of energy from a wide base into a single rising point, the geometry of aspiration burning upward toward the apex of spirit.

pyromancy.summary: The fiery art of divination by flame, ember, and the behaviour of fire.
pyromancy.description: Pyromancy, attributed to Shin and Fire, is divination by the reading of flame—its colour, its leaping, the shapes in glowing coals, the cracking of objects cast into the blaze. Fire, the element of spirit and will, is held to answer the questioner directly through its restless motion, and the seer who has attuned to its nature reads the future in its dance. It is among the most ancient of oracular practices, kin to the gazing arts but using the living, devouring element rather than the still mirror of water.

pyrrho-zoroastrianusm.summary: The crowning paradox at Kether: total doubt and total faith held as one.
pyrrho-zoroastrianusm.description: Pyrrho-Zoroastrianism, set at Kether, the Crown, is Crowley's compound name for the highest 'moral' attitude—the union of Pyrrhic scepticism (the suspension of all judgment, the doubt of everything) with Zoroastrian devotion (the wholehearted worship of the light). At the summit of the Tree the two apparent opposites are reconciled: the adept doubts every formulation utterly, yet adores the ineffable with his whole being. It is the supreme equilibrium of mind, in which absolute scepticism and absolute faith, far from cancelling, complete one another in the silence of the Crown.
tables: L. Transcendental Morality (10 Virtues; 7 Deadly Sins; 4 Magic Powers)

quartz.summary: The clear crystal of Yesod — the lens and reservoir of the astral light.
quartz.description: Quartz is attributed to Yesod, the lunar foundation and the astral reservoir — the clear, abundant crystal that has served immemorially as the scryer's sphere and the focus of vision. Its transparency and its real power to store and transmit electrical vibration (piezoelectricity) make it an apt emblem of Yesod's office as the medium that gathers and transmits the higher forces into the world. It is the crystal of the astral light, the lens of the unseen.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

quiescence.summary: The recollection of peace (upasamānussati) — contemplation of the stilling that is Nibbāna.
quiescence.description: Quiescence renders upasamānussati, the recollection of peace among the Forty Meditations, attributed to the path of Saturn. The meditator turns the mind toward the qualities of the stilling of all formations — the cessation of craving, the unbinding that is Nibbāna — and in contemplating that supreme tranquillity the mind inclines toward it. Set at Saturn, the planet of limit, rest and the great silence, it is the contemplation of the final repose, the peace that lies beyond all becoming.

tables: CLI. Magical Images of the Decans (Cadent)

ra.summary: Egyptian supreme sun god, creator and sovereign of the heavens.
ra.description: Ra (Re) is the supreme sun god of Egypt—creator, sovereign of the heavens, and the daily voyager who sails his solar barque across the sky and through the perils of the underworld to be reborn each dawn. The other gods were understood as his aspects or offspring, and pharaohs ruled as ‘sons of Ra.’ In the esoteric scheme he is the solar power in its fullest majesty, attributed to the Sun and the heart of the Tree. His nightly passage through the duat and triumphant re-emergence is among the oldest and grandest of all resurrection myths, the cosmic drama of light renewed.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

ra-hoor-khuit.summary: Egyptian falcon god of the sun, kingship, and the New Aeon.
ra-hoor-khuit.description: Horus (Egyptian Heru) is the falcon-headed god of the sky, the sun, and kingship—the avenging son of Isis and Osiris who defeats Set and inherits the throne, and whose two eyes are the sun and moon. In Thelema he is the central deity of the present age: Crowley proclaimed the Aeon of Horus, the crowned-and-conquering child Ra-Hoor-Khuit, succeeding the dying-god Aeon of Osiris. As both the warrior-king and the divine child, Horus embodies active, self-determined force and the new order of consciousness that the New Aeon announces. In 777 his various forms thread through the solar and martial attributions of the Tree.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

raadar.summary: Diurnal angelic Lord of Cancer within the Watery Triplicity.
raadar.description: Raadar is the day-governor of Cancer among the angelic Lords of the Triplicities. As the cardinal source of the Water trine, Cancer by day is the tide that rises in the light, feeling that reaches outward to nourish; Raadar presides over this daylight flow of the waters, the protective, outgoing care of the sign.

radical-intelligence.summary: The Fifth Path — the Radical Intelligence of Geburah, rooted in the depths of Wisdom.
radical-intelligence.description: The Fifth Path is the Radical or Rooted Intelligence (Sekhel Nishrash), attributed to Geburah, the sphere of Severity and Mars. The Sepher Yetzirah says it most resembles Unity, uniting itself to Binah, Understanding, which itself springs from the primordial depths of Chokmah. 'Radical' is meant in its literal sense — of the root: Geburah is the deep taproot of strength and judgement, the disciplining power that draws its severity directly from the foundations of Wisdom and Understanding, pruning all that is not essential.
tables: XIII. Paths of the Sefer Yetzirah

rahadetz.summary: Angel of the second face of Cancer, where shared feeling overflows into joyful abundance.
rahadetz.description: Rahadetz governs the middle decan of Cancer (10–20°), attributed to Mercury and the Three of Cups, *Abundance* — the cup running over, conviviality and plenty. Mercury quickens the Cancerian waters into celebration. Rahadetz is the angel of emotional fullness freely shared, the festival of feeling at its most generous.

rain.summary: A content of the heaven Makhon at Chesed — the lofts of rain and dew.
rain.description: 'Rain' is reckoned among the contents of the storehouse-heaven Makhon, attributed to Chesed in the table of the heavens. The Talmud names in this heaven the upper chambers of rain and the lofts of dew; the rain is one of the elemental treasures of the heavenly storehouse, fittingly held at the Jupiterian sphere of moisture and gracious increase.
tables: XCV. Contents of the Heavens of Assiah

ram.summary: The headlong beast of Aries—initiating fire, the horned god Amoun, the spring's first charge of will.
ram.description: The ram is the proper beast of Aries, the cardinal fire that begins the zodiacal year, and so it figures in the magical images at Aries and across the fiery decans. It is the animal of Amoun (Amun-Ra), the hidden creative power crowned with curling horns, and of every horned god of generative force. To charge head-down is the ram's nature: raw, initiating, unreflecting will, the first surge of the Word into manifestation. Esoterically it marks the springtime of any Work—the moment of pure outgoing energy, courageous and impatient, that must later be tempered by the slower signs.

ram-s-belly.summary: Ram's Belly — the English meaning of the second lunar mansion (Butain), at the belly of Aries.
ram-s-belly.description: 'Ram's Belly' is the English gloss of Butain (البطين, 'the little belly'), the second Arabic lunar mansion, marked by ε, δ, and ρ Arietis at the body of the constellation. The Moon's transit through this manzil follows immediately on Sharatan; in the traditional mansion-magic of al-Bīrūnī and the Picatrix, Butain is associated with the recovery of lost things, the healing of breaches, and the nourishment of what has been newly begun — fitting symbolism for the belly that takes in and digests what the head has reached for. The mansion sits at the Heh/Aries path on Crowley's Tree.
tables: CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon

ram-s-head.summary: Ram's Head — the English meaning of the first lunar mansion (Sharatan), at the head of Aries.
ram-s-head.description: 'Ram's Head' is the English gloss of Sharatan (الشرطين, 'the two signs'), the first Arabic lunar mansion (manzil), occupying the head of Aries. Its principal stars are β and γ Arietis, marking the head of the constellation; in the lunar-mansion system the Moon's transit of this point opens the lunar zodiac as Aries opens the solar one. The mansion's symbolism is initiatory: the Ram's Head is the spring point, the leap into the new year, and traditional Arabic mansion-magic assigns to it virtues of beginning, courage, and the breaking of resistances. See also: Sharatan.
tables: CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon

ramara.summary: Diurnal angelic Lord of Pisces within the Watery Triplicity.
ramara.description: Ramara is the day-governor of Pisces among the angelic Lords of the Triplicities. As the mutable, dissolving member of the Water trine, Pisces by day is the daytime sea that mirrors the sky, feeling diffused into sympathy and dream; Ramara presides over this luminous, boundless water of the light.

ranunculus.summary: The water-loving flower of the Moon—ranunculus, the 'little frog' blooming at the lunar margin of Gimel.
ranunculus.description: The Ranunculus is attributed to the Moon (Gimel, the High Priestess). Its name, "little frog," marks its love of wet and watery ground, and its glossy petals catch and throw back the light as the moon catches the sun's—a small, reflective, water-haunting flower fit for the lunar path. Esoterically the ranunculus is a humble bloom of the lunar margin, dwelling where water gathers, mirroring borrowed light in the manner of the Moon it serves.

rasphuia.summary: Necromancy — the Nuctemeron genius of the first hour presiding over necromancy, set by Crowley at Aries.
rasphuia.description: Among the genii of the first hour in the Nuctemeron of Apollonius of Tyana, Rasphuia presides over necromancy. His province is the calling-up of the dead and the divinations practised upon them. Lévi gives the roll of the hour-genii in his Transcendental Magic; Crowley tabulates them along the paths of the Tree (Table CLXXIII), assigning Rasphuia to Aries (Heh).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

raum.summary: The fortieth spirit of the Goetia, a crow-formed earl of Taurus who steals treasure and overthrows cities.
raum.description: Raum is the fortieth spirit of the Goetia, a great earl of the decans of Taurus. He steals treasures out of the houses of kings and carries them where he is bidden, destroys cities and the dignities of men, tells things past, present and to come, and causes love between friends and foes. He appears at first as a crow, then takes human form at the operator's command. A spirit of the earthy sign, he is the thief, the destroyer of greatness and the maker of love.

raven.summary: The black bird of Pisces and Netzach—herald of the alchemical nigredo, carrion-prophet of dissolution and renewal.
raven.description: The raven is attributed to Pisces and to Netzach, and it is the bird of the nigredo, the blackening that opens the alchemical Work—the colour of putrefaction out of which the gold is later won. A carrion bird and a famed prophet, the raven keeps company with death yet is counted among the wisest and most cunning of birds, sacred to gods of fate and oracle. Under the watery, dreaming sign of Pisces it figures the descent into the dark dissolving waters; its blackness is not evil but the necessary night before the dawn. Esoterically the raven is the messenger who speaks from the edge of the grave and the first sign that the transformation has begun.

raydyah.summary: Angel of the second face of Virgo, where disciplined work yields material gain.
raydyah.description: Raydyah governs the middle decan of Virgo (10–20°), attributed to Venus and the Nine of Disks, *Gain* — the reward of careful husbandry, increase well-earned. Venus graces Virgo's harvest with refinement and pleasure in the well-kept estate. Raydyah is the angel of accumulated, well-managed plenty.

rayel.summary: Diurnal angelic Lord of Taurus within the Earthy Triplicity.
rayel.description: Rayel — whose name carries the divine ‑el — is the day-governor of Taurus among the angelic Lords of the Triplicities. As the fixed ground of the Earth trine, Taurus by day is the fertile soil worked under the sun; Rayel presides over this productive, daylight husbandry, the patient turning of earth into harvest.

razanil.summary: The onyx — the Nuctemeron genius of the tenth hour presiding over the onyx, set by Crowley at Capricorn.
razanil.description: In the Nuctemeron — the “Day Illumined by Night” ascribed to Apollonius of Tyana and preserved by Éliphas Lévi — Razanil is numbered among the genii of the tenth hour, the spirit of the onyx. His charge is the onyx, the dark and banded stone. Crowley arranges the twelve hours and their genii upon the paths of the Tree (777, Table CLXXIII), placing him at Capricorn (Ayin).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

rd-order.summary: The Third Order — the supernal grades beyond the Abyss, in Binah, Chokmah, and Kether.
rd-order.description: The Third Order is the secret, supernal degree of the magical hierarchy, attained only across the Abyss: Magister Templi (Binah), Magus (Chokmah), and Ipsissimus (Kether). These are the grades of the Masters — the 'Silver Star' itself — beyond the reach of the ordinary aspirant, where the self is annihilated and rebuilt in the supernal light. In the A.'.A.'. they are held to be the province of those who have wholly transcended the individual.

rd-plane-left-pillar.summary: Third plane, Left Pillar — the geometric position of Geburah, severity and martial force.
rd-plane-left-pillar.description: The third plane of the Left (Severity) Pillar is Geburah — the fifth Sephirah, ruled by Mars, the sphere of judgement, the burning sword, and the necessary destruction of the unworthy. Geometrically it sits beneath Binah and across from Chesed, balancing mercy with rigour at the ethical level of the Tree. In Crowley's table this position is what defines Geburah's role: the cutting, ordering counterpart to Chesed's expansion, set on the dark pillar at the ethical plane.
tables: XII. Position on the Glyph of the Tree of Life

rd-plane-right-pillar.summary: Third plane, Right Pillar — the geometric position of Chesed, mercy and Jupiterian expansion.
rd-plane-right-pillar.description: The third plane of the Right (Mercy) Pillar is Chesed — the fourth Sephirah, ruled by Jupiter, the sphere of grace, abundance, and lawful expansion. Geometrically it sits beneath Chokmah and across from Geburah, the bright counterweight to its severing twin at the ethical plane of the Tree. Crowley's geometric table records this placement as a structural fact: Chesed is the highest station on the expansive pillar after the supernals, and it is from this point that the merciful current is dispensed downward.
tables: XII. Position on the Glyph of the Tree of Life

receptacular-intelligence.summary: The Fourth Path, named again — the Receptacular Intelligence of Chesed, vessel of the emanated virtues.
receptacular-intelligence.description: 'Receptacular' is the third of the names the Sepher Yetzirah gives the Fourth Path of Chesed (alongside Measuring and Cohesive), Sekhel Kavua, the 'fixed' or 'established' Intelligence. The emphasis here falls on Chesed as receptacle: the merciful sphere is the great vessel that catches and holds the descending spiritual virtues, containing all the holy powers so that nothing of the supernal abundance is lost. It is the cup of Jupiter's grace, fixed and abiding, into which the higher waters are gathered and from which they are dispensed.
tables: XIII. Paths of the Sefer Yetzirah
CXLIX. Magical Images of the Decans (Ascendent)

red-earth.summary: An earth of the sevenfold scheme at Chesed — the rich red land of Jupiterian abundance.
red-earth.description: The 'Red Earth' is the land set at Chesed, the merciful sphere of Jupiter, in the Qabalistic doctrine of the Seven Earths. Its redness suggests the rich, fertile soil of plenty (and recalls Adamah, the red earth from which Adam was formed) — the generous, life-bearing ground proper to the sphere of mercy, growth, and gracious increase, highest of the inhabited earths below the Abyss.
tables: CV. Ten Earths in Seven Palaces English

red-poppy.summary: The blood-red poppy of Fire—the scarlet field-poppy of Shin: flame, blood, and remembrance.
red-poppy.description: The Red Poppy is attributed to the element Fire (Shin, the Aeon). The scarlet field-poppy—distinct from the pale opium poppy—is the flower of blood and of fire, springing up red over turned and broken ground, and so become the very emblem of sacrifice and remembrance. Its burning colour marks it as a scarlet flower of the fiery element. Esoterically the red poppy is fire and shed blood flowering together: the ardent, sacrificial bloom of Shin rising from the disturbed earth.

red-sandal.summary: The warm red sandalwood of Netzach—a sweet, sensual wood-perfume of Venusian love and devotion.
red-sandal.description: Red Sandal (red sandalwood) is attributed to Netzach, the Venusian sphere. Warm, sweet, and softly woody, valued for love-work, devotion, and the consecration of Venusian rites, it has the tender, sensual character of the sphere of love and the arts. Esoterically red sandalwood is a perfume of Netzach's gentle fire—the warm wood-scent of love and worship, devotion made fragrant.

red-triangle.summary: The Tattvic symbol of Tejas — the red upward triangle of Fire.
red-triangle.description: The Red Triangle is the Tattvic symbol of Tejas, the element of Fire. In Tattvic meditation each element is given a coloured geometric form, and the upward-pointing red triangle expresses the rising, consuming, illuminating nature of Fire — heat, light, and the energy of transformation. It serves as the meditative gateway into the fiery region of the subtle world.

reflux.summary: Part of the Moon's title (Qoph): 'Reflux'—the returning ebb of the lunar tide.
reflux.description: ‘Reflux’ is a fragment of the Golden Dawn title of Atu XVIII, the Moon (path of Qoph, Pisces): ‘The Ruler of Flux and Reflux; The Child of the Sons of the Mighty.’ Flux and reflux are the flowing and the ebbing of the tide; the word ‘reflux’ names the returning movement—the withdrawal of the waters, the backward pull of dream and dissolution that complements their advance. Together they express the Moon's dominion over every rhythmic alternation, the great breathing of the deep through which the soul passes on its nocturnal journey.

rekht.summary: Rekht — an Egyptian theophoric name Crowley assigns to path 17 (Zayin/Gemini) in table XIX.
rekht.description: Rekht is the form Crowley gives at path 17 (Zayin/Gemini) in table XIX. In standard Egyptology rekhyt (rḫyt) is the plover-glyph denoting the 'common people' or 'subjects,' and in funerary literature also a class of glorified spirits — but Crowley's single-name placement here suggests a divine or angelic intermediary rather than the collective noun. The entry preserves the spelling as it appears in 777 — fixed at the Geminian path of the Lovers — without forcing a single Egyptological identification onto it.

renovating-intelligence.summary: The Twenty-sixth Path — the Renovating Intelligence of Ayin, by which God renews creation.
renovating-intelligence.description: The Twenty-sixth Path is the Renovating or Renewing Intelligence (Sekhel ha-Mechudash), attributed to the letter Ayin and the sign Capricorn, the path of The Devil joining Tiphareth to Hod. The Sepher Yetzirah says the Holy God renews by it all the changing things which are renewed by the creation of the world. Beneath the goat-horned, earthy darkness of Capricorn — the Eye (Ayin) that sees in the dark — works the perpetual renovation of matter: the relentless self-renewing fertility of the natural and instinctual world.
tables: XIII. Paths of the Sefer Yetzirah

rephan.summary: Rephan (Remphan), the star-god of Saturn — the astral idol of the Book of Acts, at Pisces.
rephan.description: Rephan, or Remphan, is the name in the Book of Acts (and in the Septuagint of Amos) for an astral deity associated with the planet Saturn, identified with the Mesopotamian Kaiwan. Referred to Qoph and Pisces, he is the star-idol of the heavens, an object of forbidden worship in the biblical account. As the deity of Saturn he embodies the heavy, fateful power of the outermost planet, the god of time and limitation under a foreign name.
tables: CLXVII. Egyptian Gods of the Zodiac (Asc. Decans)

repletion.summary: Repletion at Resh and the Sun — the disorder of solar over-fullness.
repletion.description: Repletion — morbid over-fullness, a body gorged and congested — is attributed to Resh, the path of the Sun. The Sun is the source of vital abundance and warmth; repletion is that abundance overflowing its measure, the system glutted and plethoric. It is the shadow of solar generosity, the life-giving radiance turned to surfeit, fullness become a burden rather than a blessing.

repressing-fire-of-vulcan.summary: The Repressing Fire of Vulcan — the controlled, contained smithy-flame, at Leo.
repressing-fire-of-vulcan.description: “The Repressing Fire of Vulcan” names fire in its restrained, governed aspect — the smith's flame held and directed rather than let run wild — here referred to Teth and Leo, the fixed fire of the sign. Where raw fire devours, Vulcan's repressing fire is contained heat put to work, the disciplined blaze of the forge that tempers and shapes. The phrase marks the mastery of the fiery element, energy bound to purpose.

residence.summary: Ma'on, a heaven of Assiah at Geburah — the 'Residence' where the angels sing by night.
residence.description: Ma'on ('dwelling' or 'residence') is one of the seven heavens of the Talmud, attributed to Geburah. It is the heaven in which the companies of ministering angels stand and sing the praises of God through the night, falling silent by day so that Israel's praise may be heard — the resounding angelic residence of the heavenly ascent.
tables: XCIV. The Heavens of Assiah English

respiratory-organs.summary: The respiratory organs, attributed to Air, the body's gateway to the vital breath.
respiratory-organs.description: The Respiratory Organs are attributed to Aleph and Air. The lungs and airways through which the body draws and renders the breath belong, fittingly, to the airy element itself—the medium of the vital air that the organism cannot live without for more than moments. As Air is the element of life and exchange, so the respiratory organs are the gate through which that element enters and animates the body, the place where the outer air becomes the inner breath.

resplendent-intelligence.summary: The Tenth Path — the Resplendent Intelligence of Malkuth, enthroned splendour of the Kingdom.
resplendent-intelligence.description: The Tenth Path is the Resplendent or Glittering Intelligence (Sekhel Mithnotzetz), assigned to Malkuth, the Kingdom. The Sepher Yetzirah says it is exalted above every head and sits upon the throne of Binah; it illuminates the splendour of all the lights and causes an influence to flow from the Prince of Countenances, the Angel of Kether. Though Malkuth is the lowest Sephirah, its Intelligence is resplendent because the whole light of the Tree finally shines forth and is reflected in it — the daughter who, restored to the throne of the supernal Mother, makes the material world a lamp of the divine.
tables: XIII. Paths of the Sefer Yetzirah

rest-from-strife.summary: Four of Swords — Rest from Strife; Jupiter in Libra, Chesed of Air: a guarded peace.
rest-from-strife.description: Rest from Strife is the Golden Dawn name for the Four of Swords, Chesed of the airy suit, Jupiter in the last decan of Libra. Jupiter's order and mercy impose calm upon the restless sword-suit: an armistice, the mind retiring to gather strength. The card counsels recuperation and the strategic suspension of conflict rather than its true resolution.
tables: CXXXV. Titles and Attributions of the Sword Suit.
CXLIX. Magical Images of the Decans (Ascendent)

restlessness.summary: The ninth fetter — agitation (uddhacca), the unsettled wavering of the mind.
restlessness.description: Restlessness is uddhacca, the ninth of the ten fetters, attributed to Tiphareth. It is mental agitation and disquiet — the scattered, unsettled wavering that cannot come fully to rest, the last residue of inner turbulence that persists even in the advanced practitioner. Among the higher fetters, it is destroyed only at full awakening. Its placement at Tiphareth, the harmonising solar centre, marks restlessness as precisely the disturbance of that central equilibrium, the final ripple before perfect stillness.

rhadamanthus.summary: Rhadamanthus, the wise judge of the dead — the incorruptible lawgiver, at Libra.
rhadamanthus.description: Rhadamanthus is the wise and just son of Zeus and Europa who, for his righteousness, became a judge of the dead, ruler over the souls of Asia in the underworld. Referred to Lamed and Libra, the sign of the scales, he embodies stern and incorruptible justice. With Minos and Aeacus he completes the tribunal of the afterlife, famed above all for the severity and fairness of his judgements.

rhea.summary: Rhea, the Titan mother of the Olympians — the flowing mother who saved Zeus, at Binah.
rhea.description: Rhea is the Titaness, daughter of Earth and Sky, who bore the great Olympians to Kronos and saved the infant Zeus from his devouring father by guile. Referred to Binah, the supernal Mother, and to the path of Water, she is the maternal source of the ruling gods, the flowing, generative feminine of the elder generation. As the mother who preserved the future king of heaven she embodies the protective, life-bearing power of the great mother.

rheumatism.summary: Rheumatism at Cheth and Cancer — the cold, damp affliction of the watery Moon.
rheumatism.description: Rheumatism is set on the path of Cancer, the cardinal water sign ruled by the Moon. Cold and damp are its humoral causes, and Cancer-Moon is the very seat of the cold, moist, watery temperament; rheumatic pain in the joints and muscles is read as the watery element settling and stagnating in the body. Symbolically it is the Moon's dampness lodged in the flesh, the tides of the body grown cold and heavy.

rhinoceros.summary: The armoured solitary of Virgo—the single-horned beast, thick-hided and alone, the Hermit's heavy strength.
rhinoceros.description: The rhinoceros is attributed to Virgo, the sign of the Hermit, and it suits that solitary path: a massive, thick-hided, single-horned beast that lives apart, dim of sight but immovable in its course, asking nothing of the herd. Its single horn led the medieval bestiaries to link it with the unicorn, the emblem of unity and concentrated power, and its armoured solitude makes it a fitting image of the Hermit's withdrawn and self-sufficient strength. Esoterically the rhinoceros figures the patient, heavily defended self that walks its own road alone, slow to be moved and slower to be turned, carrying its single point of focused force through a world it does not need.

rhombus.summary: The rhombus — one of the lineal figures Crowley attributes to Jupiter (path of Kaph) in table XLIX.
rhombus.description: The rhombus — a four-sided figure with equal sides but unequal angles, the leaning square — is among the lineal figures Crowley places at path 21 (Kaph/Jupiter). The four-sidedness is fitting: four is Jupiter's number on the Tree (Chesed, the fourth Sephirah, is Jupiter's), and the rhombus is the four-square stretched into a generous, opening lozenge — a figure of magnanimity and inclusive ordering. Its inclusion among Jupiter's geometric attributes carries Crowley's broader principle that every Tree position has its proper lineal form.
tables: XLIX. Lineal Figures of the Planets, &c., and Geomany

rhubarb.summary: The bitter purging root of Aquarius—rhubarb, cleansing and astringent, a strange earthy note of the Star's path.
rhubarb.description: Rhubarb is attributed to Aquarius (Tzaddi, the Star). Its root, a famous bitter purgative and tonic of the old pharmacopoeia, has a sharp, earthy, cleansing character—an unexpected, somewhat eccentric note fitting the singular, reforming, airy sign of the Water-Bearer. Esoterically rhubarb is the cleansing bitterness of Aquarius, the purging root that clears and renews, the astringent note of the sign that empties the old to make room for the new.

rider-on-pale-horse.summary: The magical image of Beleth — a king riding a pale horse amid trumpets — Goetic King of the first decan of Leo.
rider-on-pale-horse.description: Beleth, the thirteenth spirit and a great and terrible King of the Goetia, comes riding upon a pale horse, preceded by a blaring host of trumpeters and musicians, his countenance fierce at the first to affright the conjuror. In 777 he is set at the first decan of Leo by day, and the kingly solar pomp of his image — the royal rider and his fanfare — befits the Lion's opening face. He kindles the love of man for woman until the magician's will is accomplished, and must be received with courtesy and the protective ring.

right-arm.summary: The right arm of Adam Kadmon — Chesed, the merciful, giving hand.
right-arm.description: In the body of Adam Kadmon the right arm is attributed to Chesed, the fourth Sephirah, the sphere of Mercy. As the right arm is the arm of giving and of blessing, it fittingly embodies the open-handed, benevolent, building power of Chesed. With the left arm (Geburah) it forms the pair of forces by which the macrocosmic Man extends mercy and severity into the world.
tables: CIII. The Ten Divisions of the Body of God

right-aspiration.summary: The second limb of the Eightfold Path — Right Intention (sammā-saṅkappa).
right-aspiration.description: Right Aspiration is sammā-saṅkappa, the second limb of the Noble Eightfold Path, attributed to the path of the Moon. It is right intention or resolve — the turning of the will toward renunciation, goodwill and harmlessness, away from craving, ill-will and cruelty. Together with Right View it forms the wisdom (paññā) division of the path, thought rightly directed following sight rightly gained. Its lunar attribution suits the reflective, reorienting movement of the mind as it inclines itself toward the good.

right-brain.summary: The right side of the head of Adam Kadmon — Chokmah, the supernal Father.
right-brain.description: In the body of Adam Kadmon the right side of the head — the right brain — is attributed to Chokmah, the second Sephirah and the supernal Father. As Chokmah is the active, outpouring Wisdom that initiates the work of creation, it is placed at the right hand of the head, the side of force and giving. With the left brain (Binah) it forms the supernal pair of faculties crowning the macrocosmic Man.
tables: CIII. The Ten Divisions of the Body of God

right-conduct.summary: The fourth limb of the Eightfold Path — Right Action (sammā-kammanta).
right-conduct.description: Right Conduct is sammā-kammanta, the fourth limb of the Noble Eightfold Path, attributed to the path of Venus. It is right bodily action — refraining from killing, from taking what is not given, and from sexual misconduct — the wholesome ordering of one's deeds toward harmlessness and integrity. Part of the moral division of the path, it is set at Venus, the sphere of love and right relation, where conduct toward other beings is governed by care rather than craving.

right-discipline.summary: The fifth limb of the Eightfold Path — Right Livelihood (sammā-ājīva).
right-discipline.description: Right Discipline renders sammā-ājīva, the fifth limb of the Noble Eightfold Path, attributed to the path of Jupiter. It is right livelihood — earning one's living by means that bring no harm, avoiding trades in weapons, living beings, flesh, intoxicants and poison, so that the very ground of one's daily sustenance is ethical. Completing the moral division of the path, it is set at Jupiter, the sphere of lawful increase and benevolent order, where the discipline of right living is sustained.

right-energy.summary: The sixth limb of the Eightfold Path — Right Effort (sammā-vāyāma).
right-energy.description: Right Energy is sammā-vāyāma, the sixth limb of the Noble Eightfold Path, attributed to the path of Mars. It is right effort — the fourfold endeavour to prevent and abandon unwholesome states and to arouse and maintain wholesome ones, the sustained exertion that drives the practice forward. The first of the three limbs of the concentration (samādhi) division, it is fittingly set at Mars, the sphere of energy and will, where ardour is harnessed to the work of purification.

right-leg.summary: The right leg of Adam Kadmon — Netzach, the pillar of force below.
right-leg.description: In the body of Adam Kadmon the right leg is attributed to Netzach, the seventh Sephirah, the sphere of Venus and victory. As the legs uphold and carry the body, the right leg embodies the active, enduring force of Netzach in the lower world. With the left leg (Hod) it forms the pair of supports by which the macrocosmic Man stands and moves upon the earth.
tables: CIII. The Ten Divisions of the Body of God

right-lower-point.summary: The right-lower point of the pentagram, attributed to the saturnine earth.
right-lower-point.description: In the Attribution of the Pentagram the Right Lower Point is given to Tav and Saturn—the path of the Universe, the earthy and saturnine base of the figure. As one of the lower elemental points settled beneath the apex of Spirit, it answers to the densest, most fixed and binding pole of the star, where the heaviness of earth meets the gravity of Saturn. In elemental tracing it is one of the grounding stations from or toward which the lines of the figure are drawn.

right-rapture.summary: The eighth limb of the Eightfold Path — Right Concentration (sammā-samādhi).
right-rapture.description: Right Rapture is sammā-samādhi, the eighth and culminating limb of the Noble Eightfold Path, attributed to the path of the Sun. It is right concentration — the gathering of the mind into the deep, unified absorption of the jhānas, the one-pointed stillness in which insight ripens. Crowning the concentration division of the path, it is set at the Sun, the centre of harmony and radiance, where the fully integrated mind rests in luminous, collected peace.

right-recollection.summary: The seventh limb of the Eightfold Path — Right Mindfulness (sammā-sati).
right-recollection.description: Right Recollection is sammā-sati, the seventh limb of the Noble Eightfold Path, attributed to the path of Tav and Saturn. It is right mindfulness — the clear, sustained awareness established upon body, feelings, mind and mental objects (the four foundations of mindfulness), the watchful presence that underlies all insight. Part of the concentration division of the path, its placement at the grounding, structuring sphere figures the steady, recollected attention that holds experience in the light of awareness.

right-speech.summary: The third limb of the Eightfold Path — Right Speech (sammā-vācā).
right-speech.description: Right Speech is sammā-vācā, the third limb of the Noble Eightfold Path, attributed to the path of Mercury. It is abstaining from falsehood, slander, harsh words and idle chatter — and, positively, speaking what is true, kindly, helpful and timely. The first of the three limbs that compose the moral (sīla) division of the path, it is fittingly set at Mercury, the planet of language and communication, where the ethical discipline of the tongue finds its natural home.

right-upper-point.summary: The right-upper point of the pentagram, attributed to Fire.
right-upper-point.description: In the Attribution of the Pentagram the Right Upper Point is given to Shin and Fire. As one of the four elemental points below the apex of Spirit, it marks the station of the fiery element—the active, ascending power of will and transformation. In elemental ritual the lines drawn to or from this point invoke or banish Fire, the most volatile and energetic of the four that the star sets in their proper order beneath the spirit.

right-viewpoint.summary: The first limb of the Eightfold Path — Right View (sammā-diṭṭhi), seeing things as they are.
right-viewpoint.description: Right Viewpoint is sammā-diṭṭhi, the first limb of the Noble Eightfold Path, attributed to the path of Tav. It is right understanding — the clear seeing of the Four Noble Truths, of cause and effect, of impermanence, suffering and not-self — the wisdom that both opens the path and is perfected at its end. As the foundation of the whole eightfold way it gives direction to all the rest; placed at Tav, the comprehensive final letter, it figures the encompassing vision that orders the entire course of practice.

riruphta.summary: Presiding god of the second decan of Capricorn, the same Martial face of constructive labour.
riruphta.description: Riruphta is the presiding god 777 sets over the second decan of Capricorn (10°–20°), the Martial face the names-column calls Epima. Bearing the Three of Disks—Works—it names the constructive labour at the centre of the Goat's climb. It belongs to the Greco-Egyptian roster of decan-rulers, the thirty-six faces of the night sky.
tables: CLXIX. Egyptian Gods of the Zodiac (Succedent)

rishaa.summary: al-Risha, 'the well-rope' — the belly of the Fish, the twenty-eighth and final lunar mansion, in Pisces.
rishaa.description: al-Risha, 'the well-rope' (also Batn al-Hut, 'the belly of the Fish'), is the last of the twenty-eight Mansions of the Moon, a faint ring of stars in Andromeda, set in 777 in the path of Pisces (Qoph). As the rope that draws up water and the cord binding the two Fishes, it closes the lunar cycle on a note of gathering and return — held favourable for the safety of travellers, the binding of love, and the homecoming of the absent.
tables: CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon

risnuch.summary: Agriculture — the Nuctemeron genius of the ninth hour presiding over agriculture, set by Crowley at Sagittarius.
risnuch.description: In the Nuctemeron — the “Day Illumined by Night” ascribed to Apollonius of Tyana and preserved by Éliphas Lévi — Risnuch is numbered among the genii of the ninth hour, the spirit of agriculture. He governs the tilling of the soil and the whole labour of the farm. Crowley arranges the twelve hours and their genii upon the paths of the Tree (777, Table CLXXIII), placing him at Sagittarius (Samekh).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

ritual.summary: Attachment to ritual — a facet of the third fetter (sīlabbata-parāmāsa).
ritual.description: Ritual, in the list of the ten fetters, names the binding aspect of sīlabbata-parāmāsa: the mind's tendency to mistake the performance of observances for the work of liberation, set at Chesed. The Buddha did not condemn discipline or ceremony as such, but the clinging to them — the belief that rite alone sanctifies — which leaves the heart unchanged. As a fetter it is severed at stream-entry, freeing the practitioner from the husk of mere form toward the kernel of realisation.

ro.summary: Ro — a letter of the Coptic alphabet (r), which Crowley attributes to the path of Resh (Sol).
ro.description: Ro is a letter of the Coptic alphabet — the script in which the Egyptian language was written in the Christian era, the Greek alphabet adapted to Egyptian speech. It is from Greek rho. Crowley folds the Coptic alphabet into the great correspondence of letters and paths in 777 (Table LI), assigning Ro to the path of Resh (Sol) on the Tree of Life, so that the Egyptian-Christian script takes its station among the Hebrew letters and the keys of the Tarot.
tables: LI. Names of the Coptic Letters

rock-crystal.summary: Pure clear quartz of Malkuth — the heavenly water frozen into the earthly kingdom.
rock-crystal.description: Rock crystal — the purest clear quartz — is set at Malkuth, the material Kingdom. The ancients believed it to be water so perfectly frozen it could never melt (its very name, krystallos, means ice), an image of the heavenly waters made solid and brought wholly down into matter. As the transparent stone of the lowest Sephirah it figures the divine clarity hidden within, and redeemable from, the physical world.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

ronove.summary: The twenty-seventh spirit of the Goetia, a marquis and earl of Sagittarius who teaches rhetoric and tongues.
ronove.description: Ronove is the twenty-seventh spirit of the Goetia, a marquis and great earl of the decans of Sagittarius. He teaches the art of rhetoric and the knowledge of tongues, gives good and faithful servants, and procures the favour of friends and foes. He is described as appearing in the form of a monster. A spirit of the fiery sign, he is the master of language and the winner of goodwill.

root-of.summary: 'Root of' a given element — Crowley's structural label in table XI for the supernal pre-elemental principle.
root-of.description: In table XI ('The Elements and their Planetary Rulers') Crowley assigns to each supernal Sephirah a 'Root of' formula — e.g. 'Root of Air,' 'Root of Fire,' 'Root of Water' — signalling that the supernals (Kether, Chokmah, Binah) are not the elements themselves but the primal, undifferentiated source from which the four elements descend. The phrase 'Root of' is therefore a structural label, not a thing: it marks each supernal Sephirah as the metaphysical wellspring of an elemental quality before that quality has crystallised into matter. The entry collects the multiple appearances of this formula across the supernal triad.
tables: XI. The Elements and their Planetary Rulers

rosabis.summary: Metals — the Nuctemeron genius of the eleventh hour presiding over metals, set by Crowley at Aquarius.
rosabis.description: Among the genii of the eleventh hour in the Nuctemeron of Apollonius of Tyana, Rosabis presides over metals. His charge is the metals, the ores of the earth and the working of them. Lévi gives the roll of the hour-genii in his Transcendental Magic; Crowley tabulates them along the paths of the Tree (Table CLXXIII), assigning Rosabis to Aquarius (Tzaddi).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

rose.summary: The flower of love and of the heart's secret—the rose of Venus and Netzach, queen of perfumes and emblem of the soul.
rose.description:
The Rose is attributed to Venus and Netzach, and beyond them to the Veils of the Negative—for it is the supreme flower of love, the queen of scents, and one of the great symbols of the whole Western tradition. Its perfume is the very signature of Venusian beauty and desire; its form, unfolding petal within petal around a hidden centre, makes it the emblem of the heart, of the soul, and of the mysteries spoken only sub rosa, "under the rose."

Joined to the cross it becomes the Rosicrucian rose, the blossoming of spirit upon the matter of the cross; in the East the same office falls to the lotus. Esoterically the rose is love made fragrant and the heart unfolding toward the light—the flower in which beauty, secrecy, and sacrifice are bound into a single scent.

rosy-cross.summary: The Rose upon the Cross at Tiphareth—union of soul and sacrifice, the badge of the adept and the heart's flowering.
rosy-cross.description: The Rosy Cross is attributed to Tiphareth, and it is the central glyph of the adept: a rose of many petals blossoming at the heart of a cross. The cross figures the four elements, the body, and the sacrifice—the extension of spirit into matter and the willing death of the lower self—while the rose is the unfolding soul, the flower of consciousness, the beauty and love that bloom precisely at the point of sacrifice. Their union at the centre is the mystery of Tiphareth, the place where the dying god is also the flowering of new life. Worn as the Lamen of the higher grades, it declares the attainment of the harmonised heart. Esoterically the Rosy Cross is the perfected self—the soul that has flowered upon the cross of its own sacrifice, beauty born from surrender.

rubeus.summary: Geomantic figure 'Red' — attributed to Mars; passion, violence, danger.
rubeus.description: Rubeus, 'red,' is one of the sixteen geomantic figures, attributed to Mars and associated with Scorpio. A figure of passion, violence, and turbulence, it is reckoned among the most unfortunate, signifying anger, deceit, ruin, and dangerous appetites. Traditional geomancers counted it so ill that a chart bearing it in certain places was best abandoned — the martial-watery emblem of destructive force.
tables: XLIX. Lineal Figures of the Planets, &c., and Geomany

ruby.summary: The blood-red stone of Geburah—Mars, vital fire, courage, and power.
ruby.description: The ruby is attributed to Geburah and the sphere of Mars—its deep blood-red the perfect emblem of martial fire, vital energy, courage, and power. A red variety of corundum coloured by chromium, the ruby has been prized since antiquity as the ‘king of gems,’ a stone of warriors and rulers believed to kindle passion, protect in battle, and concentrate the life-force. In the Qabalistic scheme its severity and heat align it with the disciplined strength of the fifth Sephirah, the fire that both destroys and defends.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

rue.summary: The bitter herb of grace—rue of Mars, ward against evil and emblem of repentance, sharp and pungent.
rue.description:
Rue is attributed to Mars (Pe, the Tower). The "herb of grace," bitter and strong-smelling, it was the classic plant of protection—hung against witchcraft and plague, sprinkled in exorcism—and a token of repentance and regret (to "rue"). Its pungent, defensive, slightly dangerous virtue suits martial Pe. Esoterically the rue is the bitter, protective fire of Mars in herb-form, the sharp grace that drives off evil and stings the conscience awake.

Caution: rue is toxic in quantity, a known abortifacient and photosensitiser. This entry is symbolic and historical and is in no way advice for use.
rue.caution: Toxic in quantity; abortifacient and skin-sensitiser. Symbolic/historical entry only — not advice for use.

ruin.summary: Ten of Swords — Ruin; Sun in Gemini, Malkuth of Air: the intellect collapsed.
ruin.description: The Ten of Swords, Ruin, is Malkuth in the suit of Air and the third decan of Gemini under the Sun. When the intellect descends wholly into matter, reason overreaches and destroys itself: ten swords arranged on the Tree, the central blade shattered, the heart pierced through. It is the logical extreme of the airy suit — the mind's bankruptcy, the collapse and undoing that follow when thought is severed from all higher light.
tables: CXXXV. Titles and Attributions of the Sword Suit.

rupa.summary: Rūpa — the Pali name for form or materiality, the first of the five skandhas.
rupa.description: Rūpa is the Pali term for the first skandha, materiality or form, set at the element Earth. It denotes all that is material in experience: the body composed of the four great elements, and the sense-objects through which the physical world is known. In the Buddhist analysis rūpa is the most evident of the five aggregates and the easiest to mistake for a solid self; its contemplation as impermanent and not-self begins the dismantling of that error. (Its English face appears under 'Corporeality'.)

rupraga.summary: Rūpa-rāga — the Pali name for the sixth fetter, craving for fine-material existence.
rupraga.description: Rupraga (rūpa-rāga) is the Pali for the sixth of the ten fetters, the craving for existence in the realms of subtle form — the longing for the refined embodiment of the form-jhānas, set at Binah. One of the higher fetters destroyed only at full awakening, it is the persistence of the will-to-be in its most exalted material guise. (Its English face appears under 'Desire for bodily immortality'.)

rush.summary: The arrow-reed of Sagittarius—the rush, straight shaft of the archer's aim upon the path of Samekh.
rush.description: The Rush is attributed to Sagittarius (Samekh, Art / Temperance). Straight, slender, and swift-growing at the water's edge, rushes and reeds furnished the shafts of arrows—the very weapon of the Archer—and the rushlight that gave a humble flame; their upright simplicity suits the aiming, aspiring sign. Esoterically the rush is the straight shaft of Sagittarian aspiration, the simple reed made arrow, the aim that flies toward the far mark.

tables: CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon

sa-ad-al-bal-a.summary: Sa'd Bula', 'the luck of the swallower' — the second of the Fortunes, at Capricorn.
sa-ad-al-bal-a.description: Sa'd Bula', 'the good fortune of the swallower' or 'of the glutton,' is the second of the lucky mansions, set in 777 in the path of Capricorn (Ayin). The Arab astrologers read it as a station of healing and of release — favourable for divorce and the breaking of enchantments, and for the recovery of the afflicted.
tables: CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon

sa-ad-al-zabih.summary: Sa'd al-Dhabih, 'the luck of the slaughterer' — the first of the four Fortunes, in Capricorn.
sa-ad-al-zabih.description: Sa'd al-Dhabih, 'the luck of the slaughterer,' is the first of the four auspicious 'sa'd' mansions, set in 777 in the path of Capricorn (Ayin). Despite its grim sacrificial name it was counted fortunate — a station for the cutting of bonds, the healing of the sick, and the favourable conclusion of difficult matters, fitting the disciplined, saturnine resolve of the Goat.
tables: CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon

sa-ir.summary: Sa'ir — the blaze, fourth of the Arab hells, attributed to Tiphareth.
sa-ir.description: Sa'ir, 'the blaze' or 'the flaming fire,' is the fourth of the seven hells of Arab cosmology, set in 777 at Tiphareth. Standing at the centre of the sevenfold descent, it is one of the burning gates assigned in the tradition to a class of unbelievers.
tables: CXXV. Seven Hells of the Arabs

sabians.summary: Sabians — dwellers of Sa'ir in the Arab seven hells, set at Tiphareth.
sabians.description: The Sabians — a 'people of the Book' variously identified with the star-worshippers of Harran or with the Mandaeans — are, in the Arab cosmology of the seven hells, the inhabitants of Sa'ir ('the blaze'), set in 777 at Tiphareth. The entry preserves the medieval comparative eschatology of the seven gates, given as a historical artefact.
tables: CXXVI. Inhabitants of the Seven Hells of the Arabs

sabnock.summary: The forty-third spirit of the Goetia, a lion-headed marquis of Gemini who builds fortresses and afflicts with sores.
sabnock.description: Sabnock (Savnok) is the forty-third spirit of the Goetia, a mighty marquis of the decans of Gemini. He builds high towers, castles and cities and furnishes them with armour; he afflicts men for many days with wounds and sores that rot and breed worms, and he gives good familiars. He appears as an armed soldier with the head of a lion, riding upon a pale horse. A spirit of the airy sign, he is the builder of strongholds and the sender of festering plagues.

sabrus.summary: Sustenance — the Nuctemeron genius of the seventh hour presiding over sustenance, set by Crowley at Libra.
sabrus.description: Among the genii of the seventh hour in the Nuctemeron of Apollonius of Tyana, Sabrus presides over sustenance. He sustains and nourishes, upholding life with food and renewed strength. Lévi gives the roll of the hour-genii in his Transcendental Magic; Crowley tabulates them along the paths of the Tree (Table CLXXIII), assigning Sabrus to Libra (Lamed).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

sachluph.summary: Plants — the Nuctemeron genius of the second hour presiding over plants, set by Crowley at Taurus.
sachluph.description: Among the genii of the second hour in the Nuctemeron of Apollonius of Tyana, Sachluph presides over plants. He governs the green world, the secret virtues of herbs and the life of growing things. Lévi gives the roll of the hour-genii in his Transcendental Magic; Crowley tabulates them along the paths of the Tree (Table CLXXIII), assigning Sachluph to Taurus (Vav).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

sacred-bull.summary: The Sacred Bull — the divine bull of strength and fertility, at Taurus.
sacred-bull.description: The Sacred Bull, referred to Vav and Taurus, is the universal emblem of generative strength, fertility, and the steadfast power of the earth, honoured from the Apis of Egypt to Nandi, the mount of Shiva. As the bull of the zodiac he embodies the fixed, fruitful, enduring nature of the sign — the patient potency of the soil and the loins. Across the ancient world the bull was the supreme animal of divine vigour and increase.
tables: XXII. Small Selection of Hindu Deities

saffron.summary: The golden costly spice of Jupiter—saffron, royal and radiant, the most precious of perfumes and dyes.
saffron.description: Saffron is attributed to Jupiter (Kaph, the Wheel). The dried stigmas of the crocus—the costliest of spices, golden in colour and warmly aromatic, prized for dye, medicine, and the robes of kings and gods—carry the regal, expansive, beneficent splendour of Jupiter. Esoterically saffron is the perfume of Jovial majesty and good fortune, the golden, precious scent of abundance and royalty, riches made fragrant.

sagarash.summary: Angel of the first face of Gemini, where the restless mind is hemmed in by its own complications.
sagarash.description: Sagarash rules the opening decan of Gemini (0–10°), attributed to Jupiter and the Eight of Swords, *Interference* — well-meaning thought tangled in detail and indecision. Jupiter's expansiveness in airy Gemini overproduces options until the intellect is fenced in by them. Sagarash is the angel of the cluttered mind that must learn to cut a single clean line through its abundance.

sagen.summary: Name of the middle decan of Sagittarius, the lunar face of tempered, steadying strength.
sagen.description: Sagen is the name 777 records for the middle decan of Sagittarius (10°–20°). The Moon rules this face and its card is the Nine of Wands—Strength—the gathered, well-tempered power that steadies the Archer's aim. Among the Hermetic decan-faces of Egyptian descent, it names the disciplined force at the heart of mutable fire.
tables: CLXX. Egyptian Names of the Succedent Decans

sagittarius.summary: Mutable Fire, ruled by Jupiter—aspiration, the arrow toward higher truth.
sagittarius.description:
Sagittarius, the Archer, is mutable Fire ruled by Jupiter—the sign of aspiration, philosophy, travel, and the arrow of the soul shot toward higher truth. In 777 it answers to the letter Samekh and the path of the Tarot trump Art / Temperance (path 25), where opposites are alchemically combined and aimed at a transcendent target.
