It governs the questing intellect and the expansive search for meaning.

The centaur-archer joins beast and sage, instinct and vision, his arrow rising from the animal body toward the stars—an apt emblem of the Great Work of directing the lower nature to a higher end. Sagittarius’ gift is optimism, breadth, and faith; its shadow, dogmatism and restlessness. It is the pilgrim of the zodiac.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

sahaqanab.summary: Nocturnal angelic Lord of Scorpio within the Watery Triplicity.
sahaqanab.description: Sahaqanab is the night-governor of Scorpio among the angelic Lords of the Triplicities. As the fixed deep of the Water trine by night, Scorpio becomes the abyssal water in darkness, the depth where death and transformation do their work unseen; Sahaqanab presides over this nocturnal, regenerating deep.

saharnatz.summary: Angel of the second face of Libra, where balance is broken and the heart knows sorrow.
saharnatz.description: Saharnatz governs the middle decan of Libra (10–20°), attributed to Saturn and the Three of Swords, *Sorrow* — separation, grief, the cutting of the cord. Saturn's chill enters the airy scales and the equilibrium is severed. Saharnatz is the angel of the necessary sorrow through which the mind is cleansed and clarified.

sahasrara.summary: Sahasrara — the thousand-petalled crown chakra, attributed to Kether.
sahasrara.description: Sahasrara, the 'thousand-petalled lotus' at the crown of the head, is the seventh and highest wheel, the seat of pure consciousness and the goal of the risen Kundalini, where Shakti is reunited with Shiva. Referred in 777 to Kether, the Crown itself, it is the centre of union with the divine — the blossoming of the whole subtle body into illumination.

sahiber.summary: Angel of the third face of Leo, where victory must be defended with sheer valour.
sahiber.description: Sahiber presides over the closing decan of Leo (20–30°), where Mars meets the Seven of Wands, *Valour* — courage holding its ground against odds. Mars in Leo is the brave heart standing alone after the crowd disperses. Sahiber is the angel of the valour that defends what it has won, the resolve that keeps the high ground under pressure.

sahu.summary: Sahu — the incorruptible spiritual body, attributed to Malkuth.
sahu.description: The Sahu is the 'spiritual body,' the glorified and incorruptible form into which the justified dead are raised — the perfected vehicle that arises when the funerary rites and the judgment are accomplished. Given in 777 at Malkuth (the sphere of the body, here in its redeemed aspect), it is the imperishable counterpart of the mortal Khat, the resurrection-body of Egyptian belief.
tables: CXVI. Egyptial Attribution of Parts of the Soul
XCII. The Angelic Functions in the World of Yetzirah

sair.summary: The stibium of the sages — the Nuctemeron genius of the fifth hour presiding over the stibium of the sages, set by Crowley at Leo.
sair.description: In the Nuctemeron — the “Day Illumined by Night” ascribed to Apollonius of Tyana and preserved by Éliphas Lévi — Sair is numbered among the genii of the fifth hour, the spirit of the stibium of the sages. His charge is the alchemists' antimony, the stibnite by which the sages cleansed and ruled the metals. Crowley arranges the twelve hours and their genii upon the paths of the Tree (777, Table CLXXIII), placing him at Leo (Teth).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

saitziel.summary: Saitziel, the angel set over Scorpio — the assisting intelligence of the sign on the path of Nun.
saitziel.description: Saitziel is the angel attributed to Scorpio in the Golden Dawn and Crowley's 777 (Table CXLIII, the Twelve Lesser Assistant Angels of the Signs). The name carries the Hebrew theophoric ending ‑el, “of God,” marking him as a ministering intelligence rather than a ruling archangel: the lesser angel who carries the governance of the sign into act. Set over Scorpio (fixed Water), he embodies the deep, transforming intensity of the scorpion; Crowley places him at the path of Nun on the Tree of Life.
tables: CXLIII. Twelve Lesser Assistant Angels in the Signs (Transl).

sakar.summary: Saqar — the scorching fire, fifth of the Arab hells, attributed to Geburah.
sakar.description: Saqar, 'the scorching heat' that 'spares nothing and leaves nothing,' is the fifth of the seven hells, set in 777 at Geburah, the sphere of Mars and severity. A fierce and consuming gate, it is allotted in the traditional scheme to one of the classes of the damned, its martial harshness suiting the fifth Sephirah.
tables: CXXV. Seven Hells of the Arabs

sakkya-ditti.summary: Sakkāya-diṭṭhi — the Pali name for the first fetter, the belief in a personal self.
sakkya-ditti.description: Sakkya-ditti (sakkāya-diṭṭhi) is the Pali for the first of the ten fetters, the 'personality-view' — the mistaken identification of a self with, or in relation to, the five aggregates. It is the primordial error from which the whole edifice of egoism is built, and the first fetter broken by one who attains the path. Set at Hod, it is the conceptual self exposed and undone. (Its English face appears under 'Belief in a personality'.)

salamanders.summary: The elementals of Fire, set at Shin — fiery spirits living in and as the flame.
salamanders.description: Among the Legendary Orders of Being, the Salamanders are the elemental spirits of Fire, attributed to Shin, the path of the fiery letter. In the scheme of Paracelsus the four elements are each peopled by their own order of living beings, and the Salamanders are the inhabitants of flame — bright, darting, untamable creatures that are to fire what fish are to water, the very life and consciousness of the element. Esoterically they are the active, ardent forces of the magician's fiery operations.

salilus.summary: The opening of doors — the Nuctemeron genius of the seventh hour presiding over the opening of doors, set by Crowley at Libra.
salilus.description: In the Nuctemeron — the “Day Illumined by Night” ascribed to Apollonius of Tyana and preserved by Éliphas Lévi — Salilus is numbered among the genii of the seventh hour, the spirit of the opening of doors. His charge is the opening of doors and the loosing of whatever is barred and shut. Crowley arranges the twelve hours and their genii upon the paths of the Tree (777, Table CLXXIII), placing him at Libra (Lamed).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

sallos.summary: The nineteenth spirit of the Goetia, a peaceable duke of Libra who causes love between man and woman.
sallos.description: Sallos is the nineteenth spirit of the Goetia, a great duke of the decans of Libra, of a peaceable and quiet nature. His office is to cause the love of men toward women and of women toward men. He appears as a gallant soldier riding upon a crocodile, with a ducal crown upon his head. A spirit of the harmonising air-sign of Venus, he is the gentle bringer of mutual love.

salt.summary: The mineral of Earth (32-bis) — the alchemical Body, fixed and incorruptible.
salt.description: Salt is attributed to the 32-bis path of Earth, and like sulphur it is far more than a mineral: in alchemy it is the third philosophical principle, the fixed, crystalline Body that remains when spirit and soul (Mercury and Sulphur) have done their work — the stable ground of manifestation. Preservative, purifying, and immemorially sacred (the 'salt of the earth,' the salt of covenant and of the protective circle), it is the very emblem of incorruptible matter. Esoterically it is the body of the Work, the fixed Earth in which spirit is made stable and real.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

samaditthi.summary: Sammā-diṭṭhi — the Pali name for the first limb of the Path, Right View.
samaditthi.description: Samaditthi (sammā-diṭṭhi) is the Pali for Right View, the first limb of the Noble Eightfold Path, set at Tav. It is the clear understanding of the Four Noble Truths and of the conditioned nature of things — the vision that both begins and completes the path. (Its English face appears under 'Right Viewpoint'.)

samma-ajivo.summary: Sammā-ājīva — the Pali name for the fifth limb of the Path, Right Livelihood.
samma-ajivo.description: Samma Ajivo (sammā-ājīva) is the Pali for Right Livelihood, the fifth limb of the Noble Eightfold Path, set at Jupiter. It is earning one's living by harmless means, completing the moral division of the path. (Its English face appears under 'Right Discipline'.)

samma-kammanto.summary: Sammā-kammanta — the Pali name for the fourth limb of the Path, Right Action.
samma-kammanto.description: Samma Kammanto (sammā-kammanta) is the Pali for Right Action, the fourth limb of the Noble Eightfold Path, set at Venus. It is the right ordering of bodily conduct — refraining from killing, stealing and sexual misconduct. (Its English face appears under 'Right Conduct'.)

samma-samadhi.summary: Sammā-samādhi — the Pali name for the eighth limb of the Path, Right Concentration.
samma-samadhi.description: Samma Samadhi (sammā-samādhi) is the Pali for Right Concentration, the eighth and crowning limb of the Noble Eightfold Path, set at the Sun. It is the unified absorption of the jhānas in which the collected mind ripens toward liberation. (Its English face appears under 'Right Rapture'.)

samma-sankappo.summary: Sammā-saṅkappa — the Pali name for the second limb of the Path, Right Intention.
samma-sankappo.description: Samma Sankappo (sammā-saṅkappa) is the Pali for Right Intention, the second limb of the Noble Eightfold Path, set at the Moon. It is the will turned toward renunciation, goodwill and harmlessness, completing with Right View the wisdom division of the path. (Its English face appears under 'Right Aspiration'.)

samma-sati.summary: Sammā-sati — the Pali name for the seventh limb of the Path, Right Mindfulness.
samma-sati.description: Samma Sati (sammā-sati) is the Pali for Right Mindfulness, the seventh limb of the Noble Eightfold Path, set at Tav and Saturn. It is the establishment of clear awareness upon body, feeling, mind and mental objects, the ground of insight. (Its English face appears under 'Right Recollection'.)

samma-vaca.summary: Sammā-vācā — the Pali name for the third limb of the Path, Right Speech.
samma-vaca.description: Samma Vaca (sammā-vācā) is the Pali for Right Speech, the third limb of the Noble Eightfold Path, set at Mercury. It is the discipline of truthful, kindly, useful and timely speech, first of the moral limbs. (Its English face appears under 'Right Speech'.)

samma-vayamo.summary: Sammā-vāyāma — the Pali name for the sixth limb of the Path, Right Effort.
samma-vayamo.description: Samma Vayamo (sammā-vāyāma) is the Pali for Right Effort, the sixth limb of the Noble Eightfold Path, set at Mars. It is the fourfold exertion to abandon the unwholesome and cultivate the wholesome, first of the concentration limbs. (Its English face appears under 'Right Energy'.)

samqiel.summary: Samqiel, the angel set over Capricorn — the assisting intelligence of the sign on the path of Ayin.
samqiel.description: Samqiel is the angel attributed to Capricorn in the Golden Dawn and Crowley's 777 (Table CXLIII, the Twelve Lesser Assistant Angels of the Signs). The name carries the Hebrew theophoric ending ‑el, “of God,” marking him as a ministering intelligence rather than a ruling archangel: the lesser angel who carries the governance of the sign into act. Set over Capricorn (cardinal Earth), he embodies the climbing, structuring ambition of the goat; Crowley places him at the path of Ayin on the Tree of Life.
tables: CXLIII. Twelve Lesser Assistant Angels in the Signs (Transl).

sanahem.summary: Diurnal angelic Lord of Leo within the Fiery Triplicity.
sanahem.description: Sanahem is the day-governor of Leo among the angelic Lords of the Triplicities. As the fixed heart of the Fire trine, Leo by day is the steady solar blaze sustained at full strength; Sanahem presides over this constant, radiant flame, the dignity of fire that holds the centre while the sun rides high.

sanctifying-intelligence.summary: The Third Path — the Sanctifying Intelligence of Binah, the foundation of primordial faith.
sanctifying-intelligence.description: The Third Path of Wisdom is the Sanctifying Intelligence (Sekhel Mekudash), attributed to Binah, the Mother and Understanding. The Sepher Yetzirah calls it the foundation of primordial wisdom, the parent of faith — for from this dark sea of Understanding the powers of belief themselves emanate, rooted in the Amen. As the great Sephirah of form and sorrowful comprehension, Binah sanctifies: it sets apart and consecrates, giving holy shape to the formless flood of Chokmah's force.
tables: XIII. Paths of the Sefer Yetzirah

sandali.summary: Diurnal angelic Lord of Capricorn within the Earthy Triplicity.
sandali.description: Sandali is the day-governor of Capricorn among the angelic Lords of the Triplicities. As the cardinal, structuring member of the Earth trine, Capricorn by day is the daylight labour of building and ascent, the architecture of ambition; Sandali presides over this disciplined raising of enduring form.

sandals.summary: The footwear of the magician at Yesod—the winged readiness to travel the astral, protection where spirit touches earth.
sandals.description: The Sandals are attributed to Yesod, the foundational and astral sphere, and they are the footwear of the magician—paired in the table with the Perfumes—signifying readiness to travel and the protection of the feet where they meet the ground of the work. As the winged sandals of Hermes carry the messenger between the worlds, so the magician's sandals figure his freedom to move upon the astral plane that Yesod governs, and his foundation set firmly upon it. They guard the point of contact between the operator and the subtle earth he treads. Esoterically the Sandals are the established readiness of the magician to walk the inner worlds—the firm yet swift foundation beneath him, the consecrated footing that lets him travel the astral of Yesod surely and return unharmed.

sandalwood.summary: The fragrant heartwood of Venus—sandalwood, sweet and serene, perfume of love, devotion, and meditative peace.
sandalwood.description: Sandalwood is attributed to Venus (Daleth, the Empress). Its sweet, creamy, enduring fragrance—one of the great incenses of the East, burned in temples and worn upon the body—unites sensual warmth with a serene, meditative calm, the very signature of Venusian beauty and love refined toward worship. Esoterically sandalwood is the perfume of the Empress: love made serene and devotional, the sweet heartwood whose smoke quiets the mind even as it warms the senses.

sandy-earth.summary: An earth of the sevenfold scheme at Netzach — dry, shifting ground of the Venusian land.
sandy-earth.description: In the doctrine of the Seven Earths, the 'Sandy Earth' is attributed to Netzach, the sphere of Venus and of the natural instincts. It is a dry and shifting land, granular and many-grained — an image, in the cosmic geography of the worlds, of the diffuse, sensuous, ever-moving ground proper to the Venusian sphere of nature's profusion.
tables: CV. Ten Earths in Seven Palaces English

sangha.summary: The recollection of the Sangha — the community of the awakened, second of the Three Jewels.
sangha.description: Sangha is the assembly of noble disciples — the community of those who have entered the path to awakening — and the third of the Three Jewels (Buddha, Dhamma, Sangha) in which the Buddhist takes refuge. As one of the recollections among the Forty Meditations it is contemplated for its virtue: the practitioner calls to mind the integrity and attainment of the noble Sangha, gladdening and steadying the mind. In the 777 grid it is set at the lower Sephiroth of the foundation, the living vessel through which the teaching is carried and embodied in the world.

sankhara.summary: Saṅkhāra — the Pali name for the volitional formations, the fourth of the five skandhas.
sankhara.description: Saṅkhāra is the Pali term for the fourth skandha, the formations: the constructing, intending, karma-forming activities of mind, set at the element Air. The word also names, more broadly, all conditioned and compounded things; as an aggregate it is the seat of volition and habit, the workshop in which deeds and dispositions are forged. To see the formations as impermanent and not-self is to loosen the grip of the will-to-become. (Its English face appears under 'Mental-formation'.)

sanna.summary: Saññā — the Pali name for perception, the third of the five skandhas.
sanna.description: Saññā is the Pali term for the third skandha, the perceiving faculty that recognises and labels the objects of experience, set at the path of Saturn. By grasping the marks of things it allows the world to be named and remembered, yet the same activity layers concept over the bare event and can breed distortion and 'perversion of perception'. Its clear seeing as an impersonal, conditioned process is part of the insight that undoes the illusion of self. (Its English face appears under 'Perception'.)

santal-alb.summary: The white sandalwood of Pisces—santal album, cool and serene, a meditative incense of the watery deep of Qoph.
santal-alb.description: Santal Alb (santal album, white sandalwood) is attributed to Pisces (Qoph, the Moon). The true white sandal, sweet and cool and quieting, is among the supreme meditative incenses of the East, drawing the mind inward and down—fitting the dim, dreamy, watery sign of the Fishes. Esoterically white sandalwood is the perfume of the Piscean depths, the cool serene smoke that stills the surface mind and opens the still waters of the unconscious.

santal-flav.summary: The yellow sandalwood of Virgo—santal flav, fine and pure, a clean meditative wood-scent of the Hermit's sign.
santal-flav.description: Santal Flav (yellow sandalwood) is attributed to Virgo (Yod, the Hermit). The fine, pale-golden heartwood, sweet but restrained and clean, has a pure and refined character fitting the discriminating, virginal earth-sign of the Hermit. Esoterically yellow sandalwood is a perfume of Virgo's purity—the fine, clean wood-scent of inward retreat and quiet discrimination, sweetness made spare and exact.

sapatavi.summary: Nocturnal angelic Lord of Aries within the Fiery Triplicity.
sapatavi.description: Sapatavi is the night-governor of Aries among the angelic Lords of the Triplicities, complement to the day-Lord Sateraton. As the cardinal igniter of the Fire trine seen by night, Aries' flame is banked and inward, the smouldering heat of the Ram that keeps its charge through the dark; Sapatavi presides over this hidden, persisting fire.

sapphire.summary: The blue stone of Chesed—Jupiter, devotion, sovereignty, and heavenly order.
sapphire.description: The sapphire is attributed to Chesed and the sphere of Jupiter, its deep celestial blue evoking the heavens, devotion, truth, and benevolent sovereignty. A blue variety of corundum (the same mineral as the ruby, coloured instead by iron and titanium), it has long been the stone of kings, priests, and the vault of heaven. Its serene blue aligns it with the merciful, ordering majesty of the fourth Sephirah—the wisdom of just rule and the loyalty that binds a cosmos in harmony.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

sarash.summary: Diurnal angelic Lord of Gemini within the Airy Triplicity.
sarash.description: Sarash is the day-governor of Gemini among the angelic Lords of the Triplicities. As the mutable member of the Air trine, Gemini by day is the bright, communicative wind — thought in open exchange; Sarash presides over this quick daylight commerce of ideas, the speech and traffic of the lit mind.

sarayel.summary: Sarayel, the angel set over Gemini — the assisting intelligence of the sign on the path of Zayin.
sarayel.description: Sarayel is the angel attributed to Gemini in the Golden Dawn and Crowley's 777 (Table CXLIII, the Twelve Lesser Assistant Angels of the Signs). The name carries the Hebrew theophoric ending ‑el, “of God,” marking him as a ministering intelligence rather than a ruling archangel: the lesser angel who carries the governance of the sign into act. Set over Gemini (mutable Air), he embodies the doubled, quick-witted breath of the twins; Crowley places him at the path of Zayin on the Tree of Life.
tables: CXLIII. Twelve Lesser Assistant Angels in the Signs (Transl).

sardis.summary: Sardis — the church with 'a name to live' yet dead, attributed to Mercury (Beth).
sardis.description: Sardis, which has 'a name that thou livest, and art dead,' summoned to watchfulness, is set in 777 in the path of Beth and the sphere of Mercury. The mercurial attribution is pointed: the church of mere reputation and outward word without inner life is given to the planet of speech and appearance, and called to make its name a reality.
tables: XXXVI. Selection of Christian Gods (10); Apostles (12); Evangelists(4); and Churches of Asia (7)

saritiel.summary: Saritiel, the angel set over Sagittarius — the assisting intelligence of the sign on the path of Samekh.
saritiel.description: Saritiel is the angel attributed to Sagittarius in the Golden Dawn and Crowley's 777 (Table CXLIII, the Twelve Lesser Assistant Angels of the Signs). The name carries the Hebrew theophoric ending ‑el, “of God,” marking him as a ministering intelligence rather than a ruling archangel: the lesser angel who carries the governance of the sign into act. Set over Sagittarius (mutable Fire), he embodies the far-flying aspiration of the archer; Crowley places him at the path of Samekh on the Tree of Life.
tables: CXLIII. Twelve Lesser Assistant Angels in the Signs (Transl).

sasia.summary: Nocturnal angelic Lord of Virgo within the Earthy Triplicity.
sasia.description: Sasia is the night-governor of Virgo among the angelic Lords of the Triplicities. As the mutable member of the Earth trine by night, Virgo's labour turns inward — the quiet ordering and sifting of matter while the world sleeps; Sasia presides over this hidden, discriminating work of the dark.

saspam.summary: Angel of the first face of Aquarius, where the mind's overreach ends in defeat.
saspam.description: Saspam rules the opening decan of Aquarius (0–10°), where Venus meets the Five of Swords, *Defeat* — failure born of discord, the hollow conquest turned to loss. Venus unsettled in airy Aquarius cannot hold its ground. Saspam is the angel of the defeat that exposes the limits of mere cleverness, the cost of winning by division.

satem.summary: Satem — an Egyptian name Crowley lists at the Earthy quadrant in table XIX, beside Ahapshi.
satem.description: Satem appears at position 32bis (Earth) in Crowley's table XIX, paired with Ahapshi at the Earthy supernal quarter. The name is plausibly Crowley's transliteration of Setem / Sem — the Egyptian sem-priest, the funerary officiant who wore the leopard skin and performed the Opening of the Mouth — or, less certainly, a variant of Sutekh/Set. As with the other obscure XIX entries the precise Egyptian referent is not unambiguously fixed in the source-text; the entry preserves the spelling and the placement at the Earthy quarter without overcommitting to a single identification.

sateraton.summary: Diurnal angelic Lord of Aries within the Fiery Triplicity.
sateraton.description: Sateraton is one of the angelic Lords of the Triplicities tabulated in 777, governing Aries by day. The triplicity doctrine groups the zodiac into four elemental trines, each with a governor for the daylight and another for the night; Sateraton holds the diurnal office over Aries, cardinal igniter of the Fire trine — the outward, kindling face of flame that belongs to the hours of light.

satiety.summary: Ten of Cups — Satiety / Perfected Success; Mars in Pisces, Malkuth of Water.
satiety.description: The Ten of Cups, Satiety (Perfected Success), is Malkuth in the suit of Water and the third decan of Pisces under Mars. When feeling descends fully into matter, perfect fulfilment teeters on the edge of excess: ten cups arranged as the Tree itself, brimming, yet Mars's intrusion threatens to spill and disorder them. It is joy at its fullest and most precarious — bliss so complete it begins to cloy.
tables: CXXXIV. Titles and Attributions of the Chalice Suit

satonder.summary: Angel of the third face of Aries, where the first labour of fire reaches perfected completion.
satonder.description: Satonder presides over the closing decan of Aries (20–30°), attributed to Venus and the Four of Wands, *Completion* or Perfected Work. Here the headlong fire of the Ram arrives at its first settled rest: what was begun in dominion and steadied in virtue is now perfected and enjoyed. Venus brings harmony and reward to the martial sign, and Satonder is the angel of that consummation — the finished foundation on which the building zodiac proceeds.

satrip.summary: Angel of the third face of Pisces, where the waters close the zodiac in perfected satiety.
satrip.description: Satrip presides over the final decan of Pisces (20–30°), where Mars meets the Ten of Cups, *Satiety* — feeling at its very fullest, the whole emotional cycle brimming and complete. Mars stirs the last Piscean waters as the wheel closes upon itself. Satrip is the angel of the consummation and exhaustion of feeling at the zodiac's end, where all that the cups have gathered returns at last to the source.

saturn.summary: Saturn—time, limitation, structure, and death; ruler of Binah and the path of Tav.
saturn.description:
Saturn is the planet of time, limitation, structure, and death—the great teacher whose discipline gives form to all things and whose scythe ends them. In 777 it rules the third Sephirah Binah, the formative Mother, and the path of Tav (the Tarot trump The Universe), the last letter and the completion of the work. Its metal is lead, its number three, its emblems the scythe, the hourglass, and the colour black.

As Kronos–Saturn, the old king of the golden age who devours his children, this power is simultaneously the boundary-maker and the destroyer, the principle that everything in form must end. The alchemists made lead the prima materia, the heavy base matter that, rightly worked, becomes gold—so Saturn’s leaden weight is also the necessary ground of transmutation.
tables: CXXXIX. Planets Exalted in the Signs of the Zodiac
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

satyrion.summary: The aphrodisiac tuber, attributed to Yesod and Capricorn; root of generative power.
satyrion.description: Orchid root — the orchis or 'satyrion' of the old herbals — is attributed to Yesod, the lunar foundation, and to Capricorn, the generative goat: the plant's very name derives from the Greek for the testicles its paired tubers resemble, and it carried an ancient reputation as an aphrodisiac and restorer of virility. Its placement at the sexual-foundational sphere of Yesod is exact; it is the root of generative life, the earthy ground of desire and fertility through which the higher forces descend into form.
satyrion.caution: Folk aphrodisiac; many orchid species are protected — wild harvest is harmful.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

satyrs.summary: The goat-legged spirits of wild fertility, set at Ayin — Pan's lustful, dancing retinue.
satyrs.description: The Satyrs are an order of legendary beings, attributed to Ayin and the sign Capricorn, the goat. Half-man and half-goat, they are the riotous companions of Dionysus and Pan — spirits of unbridled lust, drunkenness, music, and the fertile wildness of nature. As an order they embody the goatish, instinctual, generative force of the Capricornian-Devil path: the raw vitality of the natural world that civilisation both fears and depends upon.

scammony.summary: The drastic purging resin of Saturn—scammony, bitter and cathartic, a harsh saturnine medicine and incense.
scammony.description:
Scammony is attributed to Saturn (Tav, the Universe). The resin of a bindweed, a violent purgative of the old pharmacopoeia, bitter and drastic in action, it carries the harsh, scouring, saturnine character of the sphere of severity and limitation. Esoterically scammony is a perfume of saturnine catharsis—the bitter resin that purges and empties, the hard cleansing of Saturn that strips away the superfluous.

Caution: scammony is a powerful and potentially dangerous purgative. This entry is symbolic and historical and is in no way advice for use.
scammony.caution: Drastic, potentially dangerous purgative. Symbolic/historical entry only — not advice for use.

scattered-corpse.summary: The contemplation of the scattered corpse — a cemetery meditation on the body's dispersal.
scattered-corpse.description: The Scattered Corpse is the dispersed stage (vikkhittaka) of the ten foulness-contemplations of the Forty Meditations, attributed to the path of Taurus: the bones and remnants strewn and scattered about, no longer recognisable as a single body. Holding this image, the meditator sees the final undoing of the form's coherence and the futility of clinging to it. Like the rest of the asubha series it is an antidote to lust and to the deep conviction of permanence, turning the mind toward the sober freedom of dispassion.

scepticism.summary: The earthy vice of scepticism, the corrosive doubt that denies all attainment.
scepticism.description: Scepticism is named among the vices at Malkuth, the Kingdom, the sphere of the material world. As the shadow of Malkuth's solidity and common sense, it is the flat materialism that admits nothing beyond the senses—the corrosive doubt that, refusing all that cannot be weighed and measured, denies the very possibility of the spiritual. A measure of healthy doubt is the magician's safeguard against credulity, but raised into a creed it becomes the prison of the merely earthbound mind, the vice of the kingdom that has forgotten its crown.
tables: L. Transcendental Morality (10 Virtues; 7 Deadly Sins; 4 Magic Powers)

sceptre.summary: The rod of kingship at Chesed—the staff of benevolent rule, authority wielded in mercy and order.
sceptre.description: The Sceptre is attributed to Chesed, the merciful sphere of Jupiter and of just kingship, and it is the rod of sovereign authority—the staff borne by the rightful ruler, emblem of lawful dominion and ordered power. Where the Wand is force and aspiration, the Sceptre is settled, legitimate rule, the authority that governs rather than merely strikes. Its place at Chesed marks it as power exercised in mercy and magnanimity, the benevolent command of the king who orders his realm for its good. Esoterically the Sceptre is the magician's established authority over the forces he governs—dominion held not by violence but by right and by the merciful, ordering wisdom of Chesed, the rod by which a kingdom is ruled in justice and peace.

schachlil.summary: The rays of the sun — the Nuctemeron genius of the ninth hour presiding over the rays of the sun, set by Crowley at Sagittarius.
schachlil.description: In the Nuctemeron — the “Day Illumined by Night” ascribed to Apollonius of Tyana and preserved by Éliphas Lévi — Schachlil is numbered among the genii of the ninth hour, the spirit of the rays of the sun. He presides over the sunbeams, the radiance and quickening heat of the solar light. Crowley arranges the twelve hours and their genii upon the paths of the Tree (777, Table CLXXIII), placing him at Sagittarius (Samekh).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

schiekron.summary: The love of beasts — the Nuctemeron genius of the fourth hour presiding over the love of beasts, set by Crowley at Cancer.
schiekron.description: Schiekron is the Nuctemeron genius of the love of beasts. That “Night-illumined Day”, ascribed to Apollonius of Tyana and handed down through Lévi's Transcendental Magic, sets a company of spirits over each of the twelve hours of the magical day, and Schiekron belongs to the fourth hour. His province in the old lists is bestial lust, the unnatural desire that crosses the bound of kind. In 777 (Table CLXXIII) Crowley redistributes these hour-genii across the zodiac, where this spirit falls at Cancer (Cheth).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

science.summary: Six of Swords — Science / Earned Success; Mercury in Aquarius, Tiphareth of Air.
science.description: The Six of Swords, Science (Earned Success), is Tiphareth in the suit of Air and the second decan of Aquarius under Mercury. The solar harmony of the sixth sphere restores order to the intellect, the six swords meeting cleanly at a golden rose-cross: thought clarified, balanced, and made effective. Mercury in Aquarius gives the card its character of disciplined intelligence — knowledge organised into method and success won by skill.
tables: CXXXV. Titles and Attributions of the Sword Suit.

scintillating-intelligence.summary: The Eleventh Path — the Scintillating Intelligence of Aleph, the curtain before the Cause of Causes.
scintillating-intelligence.description: The Eleventh Path is the Scintillating or Fiery Intelligence (Sekhel Metzuchtzach), the first of the twenty-two paths joining the Sephiroth, attributed to the letter Aleph and the element Air, the path of The Fool from Kether to Chokmah. The Sepher Yetzirah calls it the essence of that curtain (Pargod) which is set close before the order of the arrangement, a special dignity granted that it may stand before the Face of the Cause of Causes. It scintillates with the first sparkling of differentiation, the shimmering veil where the One first stirs toward the Two.
tables: XIII. Paths of the Sefer Yetzirah

scorpio.summary: Fixed Water, ruled by Mars/Pluto—death, sex, regeneration, and hidden depth.
scorpio.description:
Scorpio is fixed Water ruled traditionally by Mars (and in the modern scheme by Pluto)—the sign of death and regeneration, sexuality, and the penetrating descent into hidden depths. In 777 it corresponds to the letter Nun (‘fish,’ but also ‘to sprout/grow’) and the path of the Tarot trump Death (path 24). It governs transformation through dissolution, the mysteries of generation and decay.

Scorpio carries a famous triple symbolism—the scorpion that stings, the serpent that sheds its skin, and the eagle that soars—marking three stages from base reaction through transformation to transcendence. Its power is intensity, depth, and the courage to face what others avoid; its shadow, vengeance and obsession. It is the alchemical crucible of the zodiac.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

scourge.summary: The flail of Geburah—the whip of severity that drives and chastens, the discipline that corrects by pain.
scourge.description: The Scourge is attributed to Geburah, the severe sphere of strength and judgement, and it is the flail—the nekhakha borne by Osiris opposite the Crook—the whip of correction that drives the will onward and chastens what strays. Where the Crook gently gathers, the Scourge sternly drives; the two together are the balanced emblems of rule, mercy and severity, the shepherd's guidance and the master's correction. As a magical implement it figures the discipline applied to the self and to the forces under command, the necessary harshness that goads the sluggish nature into motion. Esoterically the Scourge is the severe self-discipline of the magician—the chastening force, applied without cruelty but without indulgence, that drives the lower nature toward the goal and purges it of sloth and excess.

scratchers.summary: 'The Scratchers'—the qliphothic order of Virgo, fine discrimination degraded to petty clawing.
scratchers.description: In the Translation of the Orders of Qliphoth 'The Scratchers' is the averse order attributed to Yod and Virgo. As the demonic shell of the path, it is the shadow of Virgo's analytic precision and service: the discriminating hand degraded into one that pettily picks, scratches, and frets—criticism soured into carping, care turned to clawing fault-finding. It names the corruption of discerning purity into mean and scraping spite.
tables: CXXIII. Translation of the Orders of the Qliphoth

sea-monster.summary: The magical image of Forneus — a great sea-monster — Goetic Marquis of the third decan of Capricorn.
sea-monster.description: Forneus, the thirtieth spirit of the Goetia and a great Marquis, appears in the likeness of a great monster of the sea. In 777 he is set at the third decan of Capricorn by day. He teaches rhetoric and all the arts and languages, gives men a good name and the renown of their tongue, and makes them beloved even by their enemies. The leviathan of the deep marks the watery, oceanic root of the sign of the Goat-Fish — eloquence that rises, like the sea-beast, out of hidden depths.

seb-lower.summary: Seb (Geb), the earth-god — the ground of the world, lord of the lower realm, at Malkuth.
seb-lower.description: Seb is Geb, the Egyptian god of the earth, husband of the sky-goddess Nut and father of Osiris, Isis, Set, and Nephthys. Referred to Malkuth, the Kingdom and the lowest, most material Sephirah, he is the very body of the world — the fertile ground from which plants spring and upon which all life rests. His laughter was said to be earthquakes; he is the solid earth made divine, the foundation beneath the feet.

sebek.summary: Sebek (Sobek), the crocodile-god — the dark power of the waters, at Saturn.
sebek.description: Sebek is Sobek, the crocodile-headed god of the Nile's waters, of fertility and of fearsome strength, here referred to Tav and Saturn. At once a giver of the river's bounty and a terrifying predator of its depths, he embodies the ambivalent power of the waters — life-giving and devouring. The Saturnine attribution marks his heavy, primordial, and dangerous aspect, the old god of the dark flood.

seere.summary: The seventieth spirit of the Goetia, a winged-horse prince of Pisces — good-natured and swift as thought.
seere.description: Seere (Sear or Seir) is the seventieth spirit of the Goetia, a mighty prince of the decans of Pisces, of a good and benign nature. He goes and comes in the twinkling of an eye, brings abundance of all things, discovers hidden treasures and things, and can accomplish anything the operator desires in an instant. He appears as a beautiful man riding upon a strong winged horse. A spirit of the watery sign, he is the swift and willing bringer of plenty and hidden wealth.

sekhet.summary: Sekhet (Sekhmet), the lioness of war and pestilence — the burning eye of Ra, at Leo.
sekhet.description: Sekhet is Sekhmet, the lion-headed goddess of war, plague, and the scorching power of the sun, here referred to Leo, Water, and Scorpio. The “Powerful One,” she is the burning Eye of Ra unleashed against his enemies, whose breath is the desert wind and whose fury could destroy mankind. Yet she is also a great healer, mistress of the arts of medicine; her dual nature joins destruction and cure in the fierce solar feminine.

sellen.summary: The favour of the great — the Nuctemeron genius of the twelfth hour presiding over the favour of the great, set by Crowley at Pisces.
sellen.description: In the Nuctemeron — the “Day Illumined by Night” ascribed to Apollonius of Tyana and preserved by Éliphas Lévi — Sellen is numbered among the genii of the twelfth hour, the spirit of the favour of the great. He wins the favour of the great, the goodwill and patronage of the powerful. Crowley arranges the twelve hours and their genii upon the paths of the Tree (777, Table CLXXIII), placing him at Pisces (Qoph).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

semen.summary: The semen, attributed to Spirit, the body's concentrated seed of generation.
semen.description: The Semen is attributed to Spirit (31 bis), the quintessence. The generative seed, in which the power of producing new life is concentrated, is held throughout the magical tradition to be among the most potent of the body's substances—the bodily vehicle of the creative force itself. Its attribution to Spirit marks it as the highest distillation of vital essence, the seed in which the spark of life is gathered and from which, in the symbolism of the alchemists and yogis alike, both bodily offspring and inner regeneration may proceed.

semma.summary: Semma — a letter of the Coptic alphabet (s), which Crowley attributes to 10 Malkuth.
semma.description: Semma is a letter of the Coptic alphabet — the script in which the Egyptian language was written in the Christian era, the Greek alphabet adapted to Egyptian speech. It is from Greek sigma. Crowley folds the Coptic alphabet into the great correspondence of letters and paths in 777 (Table LI), assigning Semma to 10 Malkuth on the Tree of Life, so that the Egyptian-Christian script takes its station among the Hebrew letters and the keys of the Tarot.
tables: LI. Names of the Coptic Letters

senciner.summary: Name of the last decan of Scorpio, the Venusian face where desire decays into excess.
senciner.description: Senciner is 777's name for the last decan of Scorpio (20°–30°). Venus rules this face and its card is the Seven of Cups—Debauch—desire turned to excess, the seductive illusion in which fixed water can drown. Among the thirty-six Hermetic decan-faces it marks the perilous close of Scorpio, where pleasure decays toward dissolution.
tables: CLXXII. Egyptian Names of the Cadent Decans

senior-deacon.summary: Bearer of messages from Master to Senior Warden, here at Netzach.
senior-deacon.description: The Senior Deacon carries the commands of the Worshipful Master to the Senior Warden and attends upon the candidate, an officer of communication and conduct within the lodge. Attributed here to Netzach, the sphere of Venus, the office expresses the active, outgoing transmission of the Master's will through the body of the work.
tables: CXV. Officers in a Masonic Lodge

senior-warden.summary: The Second of the Lodge, at Geburah — strength and the closing of the day in the West.
senior-warden.description: The Senior Warden is the second principal officer of a Masonic lodge, seated in the West, who marks the setting sun and pays the craft their wages. Attributed to Geburah, the sphere of Severity and strength, he represents the disciplined power that sustains and completes the work begun by the Master, the firm hand of justice balancing the Master's mercy.
tables: CXV. Officers in a Masonic Lodge

sentacer.summary: Name of the first decan of Scorpio, the Martial face of loss that opens the sign of death.
sentacer.description: Sentacer is 777's name for the first decan of Scorpio (0°–10°), the entry into fixed water. Mars—Scorpio's ancient ruler—governs this face, and its card is the Five of Cups—Disappointment—the loss and emotional emptying that open the sign of death and regeneration. One of the thirty-six decan-faces of the Egyptian sky, it names the grief that begins Scorpio's descent.
tables: CLXVIII. Egyptian Names of Asc. Decans.

serapis.summary: Serapis, the syncretic god of Ptolemaic Egypt — Osiris-Apis crowned with plenty, at Taurus.
serapis.description: Serapis is the composite god created in Ptolemaic Alexandria to unite Greek and Egyptian worship, fusing Osiris with the Apis bull and bearing aspects of Zeus, Hades, and Asklepios. Referred to Vav and Taurus, he is a god of fertility, the afterlife, and healing, crowned with the corn-measure of abundance. His great temple, the Serapeum, was a centre of late antique devotion; he embodies the meeting of two cultures in a single benevolent deity.
tables: CLXVII. Egyptian Gods of the Zodiac (Asc. Decans)

serpent.summary: The serpent of Teth/Leo and of the path-name—kundalini fire, wisdom and temptation, the coiled power of life.
serpent.description: The serpent is attributed to Teth (the path of Lust/Strength, joined to Leo) and is named in the translation of the paths, for the letter Teth itself is figured as a serpent. It is among the most charged of all symbols: the coiled kundalini sleeping at the base of the spine, the healing serpent of Aesculapius, the wise tempter of Eden, and the Ouroboros that devours its own tail in token of eternity. Under Teth and Leo it is the serpent-power roused and ridden, the controlled fire of generation that, raised through the centres, becomes illumination. Esoterically the serpent unites the lowest and the highest—poison and medicine, fall and wisdom—according to how its force is governed.
tables: III. Translation of the Names of the Paths

serpentine.summary: The serpent-stone of Scorpio — the coiled power of death and renewal.
serpentine.description: The snakestone is attributed to the path of Nun and Scorpio — the fixed-water sign of death, sex, and regeneration whose own emblem is the serpent that sheds its skin. The name has been given to coiled ammonite fossils (taken in folklore for petrified snakes), to serpentine, and to stones reputed to cure snakebite; all carry the Scorpionic charge of the serpent-power, the venom that is also medicine, the death that is also rebirth. The stone of the coiled, transforming force.
tables: CXXIII. Translation of the Orders of the Qliphoth
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

serucuth.summary: Name of the first decan of Libra, the lunar face of suspended, weighed peace.
serucuth.description: Serucuth is 777's name for the first decan of Libra (0°–10°), the cardinal initiation of airy balance. The Moon rules this face and it bears the Two of Swords—Peace—the poised equilibrium of opposed forces held in suspension. One of the thirty-six decan-faces of the Egyptian sky, it names the first act of weighing by which the scales are set.
tables: CLXVIII. Egyptian Names of Asc. Decans.

set.summary: Set, god of storm, desert, and chaos — the murderer of Osiris, at Capricorn.
set.description: Set is the turbulent Egyptian god of the desert, storms, violence, and disorder, slayer of his brother Osiris and eternal adversary of Horus. Referred to Ayin and Capricorn, he is the wild, sterile power of the wastelands and the strength that both threatens and, defending the sun-barque against Apep, defends the cosmic order. Ambivalent and feared, Set is the necessary force of conflict and separation within the divine drama.

sexual-aspect-of-sakti.summary: 'sexual aspect of Sakti' — Crowley's parenthetical gloss for Lalita in table XXII at Venus.
sexual-aspect-of-sakti.description: In table XXII the cell at path 14 (Daleth/Venus) reads (in essence) 'Lalita (sexual aspect of Sakti),' qualifying the goddess in her erotic, voluptuous, and play-creative aspect rather than her wrathful (Kali) or compassionate (Tara) forms. 'Sakti' is the great feminine cosmic energy of Tantra; Lalita is its sexual face — fitting the Venusian path. The entry preserves Crowley's parenthetical qualifier; the principal Lalita entry holds the description.
tables: XXII. Small Selection of Hindu Deities

sezarbil.summary: A genius of the Nuctemeron's tenth hour, set by Crowley at Capricorn.
sezarbil.description: Sezarbil is listed among the genii of the tenth hour of the Nuctemeron, the “Day Illumined by Night” attributed to Apollonius of Tyana and transmitted by Éliphas Lévi. He stands among the genii of the tenth hour, reckoned in the older lore a baleful or adverse spirit; no certain office survives for him, and none is here fabricated. Crowley ranks these hour-genii along the zodiacal paths in 777 (Table CLXXIII), where Sezarbil stands at Capricorn (Ayin).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

shachdar.summary: Angel of the third face of Libra, where the warring mind lays down its arms in truce.
shachdar.description: Shachdar presides over the closing decan of Libra (20–30°), where Jupiter meets the Four of Swords, *Truce* — rest after strife, the convalescence of thought. Jupiter brings respite and recovery to Libra's intellect. Shachdar is the angel of the armistice that allows the wounded mind to heal before it must think again.

shadow-of-death.summary: Tzalmaveth, the Shadow of Death — a hell-compartment set at Hod.
shadow-of-death.description: The 'Shadow of Death' (Tzalmaveth) is one of the seven compartments of Gehenna, attributed to Hod. The phrase, familiar from the Psalms' 'valley of the shadow of death,' names a region of deep gloom and dread in the descending underworld — the shadowed hall where the light of life is all but extinguished, a stage in the Qabalistic anatomy of the Hells.
tables: CVII. Ten Hells in Seven Palaces English

shai.summary: Shai — a letter of the Coptic alphabet (sh), which Crowley attributes to the path of Shin (Fire).
shai.description: Shai is one of the Coptic letters drawn not from Greek but from Demotic Egyptian, added to the borrowed Greek alphabet to record sounds Greek could not write: it is the shai, a Demotic-derived sign for a sound Greek lacked. Crowley folds the Coptic alphabet into the great correspondence of letters and paths in 777 (Table LI), assigning Shai to the path of Shin (Fire) on the Tree of Life, so that the Egyptian-Christian script takes its station among the Hebrew letters and the keys of the Tarot.
tables: LI. Names of the Coptic Letters

shamrock.summary: The trefoil of mercy—the shamrock of Chesed, Saint Patrick's emblem of the Three-in-One.
shamrock.description: The Shamrock is attributed to Chesed, the merciful sphere of Jupiter. The little trefoil by which (in legend) Saint Patrick taught the Trinity—three leaves upon one stem—it is a plant of benediction, faith, and good fortune well suited to beneficent, magnanimous Jupiter. Esoterically the shamrock is the green token of grace and the threefold blessing, the humble leaf in which the many-in-one is shown, fittingly set in the sphere of mercy.

shang-ti.summary: Shang Ti — the Supreme Lord of Heaven, attributed to Kether.
shang-ti.description: Shang Ti, the 'Lord on High' of archaic Chinese religion, the supreme sovereign deity of Heaven, is set at Kether, the Crown and highest Sephirah. The attribution gives the celestial emperor of the Chinese pantheon his rightful place as the One above all — the august ruling principle from which the ordered cosmos descends.

sharatan.summary: al-Sharatan, 'the two signs' — the first lunar mansion, the horns of the Ram opening the zodiacal year.
sharatan.description: The first of the twenty-eight Manazil al-Qamar (Mansions of the Moon), al-Sharatan ('the two signs,' or the two horns) is marked by the bright stars of the Ram's head and in Liber 777 falls in the path of Aries (Heh). As the station where the Moon's monthly course was anciently reckoned to begin, it carries the symbolism of inception and martial onset — the first spark of the cardinal-fire year. The Arab astrologers held it a mansion of beginnings, journeys, and the breaking of bonds.
tables: CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon

sharatiel.summary: Sharatiel, the angel set over Leo — the assisting intelligence of the sign on the path of Teth.
sharatiel.description: Sharatiel is the angel attributed to Leo in the Golden Dawn and Crowley's 777 (Table CXLIII, the Twelve Lesser Assistant Angels of the Signs). The name carries the Hebrew theophoric ending ‑el, “of God,” marking him as a ministering intelligence rather than a ruling archangel: the lesser angel who carries the governance of the sign into act. Set over Leo (fixed Fire), he embodies the steady royal flame and courage of the lion; Crowley places him at the path of Teth on the Tree of Life.
tables: CXLIII. Twelve Lesser Assistant Angels in the Signs (Transl).

sharhiel.summary: Sharhiel, the angel set over Aries — the assisting intelligence of the sign on the path of Heh.
sharhiel.description: Sharhiel is the angel attributed to Aries in the Golden Dawn and Crowley's 777 (Table CXLIII, the Twelve Lesser Assistant Angels of the Signs). The name carries the Hebrew theophoric ending ‑el, “of God,” marking him as a ministering intelligence rather than a ruling archangel: the lesser angel who carries the governance of the sign into act. Set over Aries (cardinal Fire), he embodies the ram's first leap of spring, raw initiating force; Crowley places him at the path of Heh on the Tree of Life.
tables: CXLIII. Twelve Lesser Assistant Angels in the Signs (Transl).

shark.summary: The perfect predator of Scorpio—the devouring death of the deep waters, hunger that never rests.
shark.description: The shark is attributed to Scorpio, the fixed-water sign of death and the deep instincts, and it is the consummate predator of the sea: ancient, tireless, drawn unerringly to blood, an engine of appetite that must keep moving to live. It embodies the killing aspect of the great waters, the death that waits in the depths, the relentless devouring hunger that is one true face of Scorpio. Where the dolphin is the saving intelligence of the sea, the shark is its merciless one. Esoterically the shark figures the ruthless instinctual drive at the bottom of the psyche—the deep, cold hunger that cannot be reasoned with and that the soul descending into its own waters must learn to recognise and reckon with.

shax.summary: The forty-fourth spirit of the Goetia, a dove-formed marquis of Gemini who steals the senses and the goods of others.
shax.description: Shax (Shass) is the forty-fourth spirit of the Goetia, a great marquis of the decans of Gemini. He takes away the sight, hearing and understanding of any person at the operator's command, steals money out of kings' houses and carries it back, and brings horses and other things; he is deceitful unless commanded into a triangle, where he speaks truly and gives good familiars. He appears as a stock-dove with a hoarse voice. A spirit of the airy sign, he is the thief of the senses and of treasure.

shehadani.summary: Angel of the second face of Gemini, where the mind turns its blades upon itself in anguish.
shehadani.description: Shehadani governs the middle decan of Gemini (10–20°), where Mars meets the Nine of Swords, *Cruelty* — mental suffering, nightmare, the sword-edge of relentless thought. Mars sharpens the airy mind into a weapon against its own peace. Shehadani is the angel of this dark night of the intellect, the anguish that the over-active mind inflicts on itself.

shelathiel.summary: Shelathiel, the angel set over Virgo — the assisting intelligence of the sign on the path of Yod.
shelathiel.description: Shelathiel is the angel attributed to Virgo in the Golden Dawn and Crowley's 777 (Table CXLIII, the Twelve Lesser Assistant Angels of the Signs). The name carries the Hebrew theophoric ending ‑el, “of God,” marking him as a ministering intelligence rather than a ruling archangel: the lesser angel who carries the governance of the sign into act. Set over Virgo (mutable Earth), he embodies the discerning, harvesting precision of the virgin; Crowley places him at the path of Yod on the Tree of Life.
tables: CXLIII. Twelve Lesser Assistant Angels in the Signs (Transl).
CLI. Magical Images of the Decans (Cadent)

shiva.summary: Shiva, the destroyer and transformer — the great ascetic and lord of the dance, at the supernals.
shiva.description: Shiva is the third power of the Hindu trinity, the destroyer who dissolves the universe so that it may be renewed, and the supreme yogi seated in eternal meditation on Mount Kailash. Referred to Kether, Chokmah, and the fiery paths of Aries and Taurus, he unites opposites — ascetic and erotic, terrible and benign, the still meditator and the cosmic dancer whose Tandava destroys and recreates the worlds. His third eye burns illusion to ash; his is the power of transformation through destruction.
tables: XXII. Small Selection of Hindu Deities

shiva-darshana.summary: The Vision of Shiva (śiva-darśana) — the realisation of dissolution and the destroyer-god, set at the Veils.
shiva-darshana.description: Shiva-darshana is the 'vision of Shiva' among the Hindu/Buddhist Results, attributed to the Veils of the Negative. Shiva is the great dissolver, the god in whom all forms are gathered back into the formless; his vision is the experience of universal dissolution — the annihilation of the manifest in the dance of destruction that is also liberation. Set beyond Kether at the negative veils, it figures the supreme samādhi of unmaking, where the seer and the seen alike are consumed and only the unconditioned remains.
tables: XXIV. Certain of the Hindu/Buddhist Results

shortened-force.summary: Eight of Swords — Shortened Force; Jupiter in Gemini, Hod of Air: action hemmed in.
shortened-force.description: Shortened Force is the Golden Dawn title of the Eight of Swords, Hod of the airy suit, Jupiter in the first decan of Gemini. The crossed and crowded blades show power curtailed, energy hemmed in by detail and circumstance. The card speaks of good intentions hampered, decisive force fragmented into ineffectual small efforts.
tables: CXXXV. Titles and Attributions of the Sword Suit.

should-contain-a-demonstration-of-the-qu.term: Should contain a demonstration of the quadrature of the circle
should-contain-a-demonstration-of-the-qu.displayTerm: Should contain a demonstration of the quadrature of the circle
should-contain-a-demonstration-of-the-qu.summary: Liber 777's design note for the Universe (Tav): it should contain a demonstration of the squaring of the circle.
should-contain-a-demonstration-of-the-qu.description: ‘Should contain a demonstration of the quadrature of the circle’ is Liber 777's design note for Atu XXI, the Universe (path of Tav, Saturn). The squaring of the circle—reconciling the round (spirit, heaven, the infinite) with the square (matter, earth, the fourfold world)—is the perennial emblem of the Great Work accomplished. As the final trump, the Universe shows that union completed: the dancing figure within the cosmic mandala, the marriage of the circle and the square, spirit perfectly wedded to form. The ‘demonstration’ is the visible proof of the whole system brought to completion.
tables: CLXXXI. Correct Design of Tarot Trumps

shoulders.summary: The shoulders, attributed to Taurus, the bearers of the body's burdens.
shoulders.description: The Shoulders are attributed to Vav and Taurus in this table of the Human Body. In medical astrology Taurus, the fixed earthy sign of the bull, rules the neck and shoulders—the strong, patient bearers of weight, the yoke upon which loads are carried. As the ox endures its burden, so the shoulders are the body's seat of steady, rooted strength, fittingly given to the enduring sign of Taurus.

shu.summary: Shu, god of air and light — who lifts the sky from the earth, at Yesod.
shu.description: Shu is the Egyptian god of air, light, and the empty space between, who stands upon the earth-god Geb and lifts the sky-goddess Nut above him, holding the heavens apart from the ground. Referred to Yesod, the Foundation, he is the supporting atmosphere, the breath of life and the medium of light. As the divine separator he makes the cosmos habitable, sustaining the vault of heaven by his strength.

tables: CLI. Magical Images of the Decans (Cadent)

sialul.summary: Prosperity — the Nuctemeron genius of the seventh hour presiding over prosperity, set by Crowley at Libra.
sialul.description: Sialul is the Nuctemeron genius of prosperity. That “Night-illumined Day”, ascribed to Apollonius of Tyana and handed down through Lévi's Transcendental Magic, sets a company of spirits over each of the twelve hours of the magical day, and Sialul belongs to the seventh hour. He grants flourishing and abundance, the steady increase of fortune. In 777 (Table CLXXIII) Crowley redistributes these hour-genii across the zodiac, where this spirit falls at Libra (Lamed).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

siamese-benzoin.summary: The warm balsam of Scorpio—Siamese benzoin, sweet and resinous, an incense of the deep transforming water-sign.
siamese-benzoin.description: Siamese Benzoin is attributed to Scorpio (Nun, Death). The fine vanilla-balsamic resin of the Siam styrax, warm and sweet and richly enveloping, lends a deep, comforting smoke here drawn into the intense, secretive, transformative sign of Scorpio. Esoterically Siamese benzoin is the warm sweet perfume of Scorpio's depths—the balsam that soothes even within the death-and-rebirth current, sweetness found in the very place of dissolution.

sight.summary: The sense classically borne by Fire/Tejas — the perception of form and light.
sight.description: Sight is the sense traditionally attributed to Tejas, the element of Fire, in the Tattvic doctrine of the senses. Because the eye perceives by light, and light is the radiance of the fiery element, vision is the faculty proper to Fire — the apprehension of form, colour, and luminous appearance. It is the sense most associated with knowledge and the 'inner light' of vision.

sign-of-the-holy-covenant.summary: The generative member of Adam Kadmon — Yesod, the Foundation.
sign-of-the-holy-covenant.description: The 'sign of the holy covenant' — the membrum and the place of circumcision — is attributed to Yesod, the ninth Sephirah, the Foundation. As Yesod is the channel through which the powers of the whole Tree are gathered and transmitted into Malkuth, so the generative organ is the seat of the creative force in the body of Adam Kadmon. The covenant marked upon it signifies the consecration of that generative power to its divine purpose.
tables: CIII. The Ten Divisions of the Body of God

silabata-paramesa.summary: Sīlabbata-parāmāsa — the Pali name for the third fetter, attachment to rites and rules.
silabata-paramesa.description: Silabata-paramesa (sīlabbata-parāmāsa) is the Pali for the third of the ten fetters, the clinging to rules and observances as ends in themselves, set at Chesed. Broken at the first stage of awakening, it marks the release from ritualism into the substance of the path. (Its English face appears under 'Clinging to rules'.)

silence.summary: The divine Silence of the supernals — the stillness before the Word, figured in Harpocrates.
silence.description: Silence is the attribute of the highest, the stillness of the unmanifest that precedes and surrounds every utterance of the creative Word. Set among the supernals, between the Crown and the Mother, it is the holy quiet from which Wisdom speaks and into which all returns. In the magical tradition it is personified as Harpocrates (Hoor-pa-kraat), the babe enthroned upon the lotus with finger to lips — the secret self at the still centre, whose silence is itself the most potent of magical 'words.'
tables: L. Transcendental Morality (10 Virtues; 7 Deadly Sins; 4 Magic Powers)

silver.summary: The lunar metal of Yesod and the Moon — reflection, purity, the astral light.
silver.description: Silver is the metal of Luna, attributed to the lunar foundation of Yesod — white, reflective, and cool, the perfect counterpart of solar gold. As the metal that mirrors light rather than generating it, silver embodies the Moon's office of reflection and reception, the astral looking-glass in which the higher light is shown to the lower world. It is the metal of the mirror and the chalice, of purity and the receptive feminine current, and (in its salts) of the very chemistry of the photographic image — light captured and held.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

silver-crescent.summary: The Tattvic symbol of Apas — the silver crescent of Water.
silver-crescent.description: The Silver Crescent is the Tattvic symbol of Apas, the element of Water. In the Tattvic system the elements are visualised as coloured forms, and the silvery lunar crescent expresses the cool, receptive, flowing nature of Water — feeling, reflection, and the medium of taste. It is the meditative gateway into the watery quarter of the subtle world.

simak.summary: al-Simak al-A'zal, 'the unarmed' — Spica, the wheat-ear of the Virgin, the lunar mansion in Virgo.
simak.description: al-Simak al-A'zal ('the unarmed lofty one'), marked by the brilliant white star Spica, is the Mansion of the Moon set in the path of Virgo (Yod). Spica is the ear of wheat in the Virgin's hand — the perennial emblem of harvest and of the grain-goddess — and the mansion was accordingly held among the most fortunate, presiding over love, fertility, and abundance.
tables: CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon
CXXIII. Translation of the Orders of the Qliphoth

sinbuck.summary: Judges — the Nuctemeron genius of the first hour presiding over judges, set by Crowley at Aries.
sinbuck.description: Sinbuck is the Nuctemeron genius of judges. That “Night-illumined Day”, ascribed to Apollonius of Tyana and handed down through Lévi's Transcendental Magic, sets a company of spirits over each of the twelve hours of the magical day, and Sinbuck belongs to the first hour. He governs the seat of judgment, the weighing of causes and the rendering of verdicts. In 777 (Table CLXXIII) Crowley redistributes these hour-genii across the zodiac, where this spirit falls at Aries (Heh).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours
CL. Magical Images of the Decans (Succedent)

sirens.summary: The singing enchantresses of the deep, set at Tzaddi — luring voices upon the waters.
sirens.description: The Sirens are an order of legendary beings, attributed to Tzaddi. In Greek myth they are the bird-and-woman (later fish-and-woman) enchantresses whose irresistible song lures sailors to wreck upon their rocks — the voices that Odysseus bound himself to the mast to hear and survive. As an order they figure the perilous allure of beauty and longing, the seductive call from across the water that promises bliss and delivers destruction to the unwary.

sisera.summary: Desire — the Nuctemeron genius of the second hour presiding over desire, set by Crowley at Taurus.
sisera.description: Sisera is the Nuctemeron genius of desire. That “Night-illumined Day”, ascribed to Apollonius of Tyana and handed down through Lévi's Transcendental Magic, sets a company of spirits over each of the twelve hours of the magical day, and Sisera belongs to the second hour. He is the spirit of concupiscence and longing, the heat of wanting that drives the appetites. In 777 (Table CLXXIII) Crowley redistributes these hour-genii across the zodiac, where this spirit falls at Taurus (Vav).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

sislau.summary: Poisons — the Nuctemeron genius of the fourth hour presiding over poisons, set by Crowley at Cancer.
sislau.description: In the Nuctemeron — the “Day Illumined by Night” ascribed to Apollonius of Tyana and preserved by Éliphas Lévi — Sislau is numbered among the genii of the fourth hour, the spirit of poisons. He governs venoms and the poisoner's art, the baneful draught and the tainted cup. Crowley arranges the twelve hours and their genii upon the paths of the Tree (777, Table CLXXIII), placing him at Cancer (Cheth).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

sitlacer.summary: Name of the middle decan of Leo, the Jovial zenith of the Lion crowned in victory.
sitlacer.description: Sitlacer governs the middle decan of Leo (10°–20°), the radiant heart of fixed fire. Jupiter rules this face and it bears the Six of Wands—Victory—the triumphant, well-earned glory proper to the Lion at his zenith. One of the thirty-six faces inherited from the Egyptian decans, it marks the station of crowned, confident power.
tables: CLXX. Egyptian Names of the Succedent Decans

sitri.summary: The twelfth spirit of the Goetia, a prince of Cancer who inflames desire and unveils the body.
sitri.description: Sitri is the twelfth spirit of the Goetia, a great prince of the decans of Cancer. He inflames men with the love of women and women with the love of men, and causes them to show themselves naked if it be desired. He appears first with the head of a leopard and the wings of a griffin, then as a very beautiful man. A spirit of the tender water-sign, he embodies the kindling and unveiling power of erotic desire.

tables: XCII. The Angelic Functions in the World of Yetzirah

skeleton.summary: The skeleton, attributed to Earth, the enduring framework of the body.
skeleton.description: The Skeleton is attributed to Earth (32 bis). The bony frame upon which all the softer tissues are built and hung answers to the densest, most stable and enduring of the elements—the structural ground of the organism. Long after the flesh decays the bones remain, the earthy architecture of the body; their attribution to Earth marks them as the fixed and lasting scaffold that gives the living form its standing shape.

skeleton-corpse.summary: The contemplation of the skeleton — last of the cemetery meditations on the body's decay.
skeleton-corpse.description: The Skeleton (aṭṭhika) is the final stage of the ten foulness-contemplations of the Forty Meditations, attributed to the path of Scorpio. When flesh and sinew are gone, the meditator contemplates the bare bones — the enduring framework that is the body's last image before it too whitens and crumbles to dust. As the culmination of the cemetery series it offers the clearest mirror of mortality, and in the Scorpionic position of death and regeneration it figures the stripping-away of all that is perishable until only the stark, impersonal truth of dissolution remains.

skeptical-doubt.summary: The second fetter — sceptical doubt (vicikicchā), wavering uncertainty that paralyses the path.
skeptical-doubt.description: Skeptical Doubt is vicikicchā, the second of the ten fetters, attributed to Chokmah. It is not honest inquiry but the corrosive, unresolved wavering that cannot commit — doubt about the teacher, the teaching, the path and one's own capacity, which leaves the mind divided and the practice stalled. Severed at stream-entry along with personality-view, its overcoming is the steadying of confidence that allows the path to be walked. Its placement at Chokmah, the sphere of pure directed force, marks doubt as the failure of that single-pointed certainty.

skin-troubles.summary: Skin troubles at Netzach and Venus — disorders of the body's Venusian surface.
skin-troubles.description: Troubles of the skin are attributed to Netzach, the sphere of Venus. Venus governs beauty, the complexion, and the fair outer surface of the body; afflictions of the skin are therefore the marring of her province — the smooth Venusian envelope blemished, eruptive, or inflamed. As Netzach is the sphere of the senses and of natural attraction, its disorders surface, fittingly, upon the very skin through which we are seen and touched.

skull.summary: The cranium of Adam Kadmon — Kether, the Crown seated at the head.
skull.description: In the figure of Adam Kadmon, the primordial Man whose body is the Tree of Life, the skull or crown of the head is attributed to Kether, the first Sephirah. As the Crown rests upon the head of the king, so Kether sits at the very summit of the macrocosmic body, the seat of the highest and least manifest principle. The cranium that houses the brain and is encircled by the crown is the natural emblem of the supreme point from which all descends.
tables: CIII. The Ten Divisions of the Body of God
CLI. Magical Images of the Decans (Cadent)

sluggishness.summary: Sluggishness at the path of Earth — the heavy torpor of the densest element.
sluggishness.description: Sluggishness is placed at the path of Earth (32 bis), the heaviest and most inert of the elements. Earth is cold, dry, and slow, and sluggishness is its temperament made symptom — the body and spirit weighed down, dull, and immobile, mired in elemental density. It figures the perennial danger of matter: the tendency of the earthy nature toward stagnation, inertia, and torpid heaviness when not quickened by the higher elements.

smell.summary: The sense classically borne by Earth/Prithivi — the perception of odour.
smell.description: Smell is the sense traditionally attributed to Prithivi, the element of Earth, in the Tattvic doctrine of the senses. Because odour arises from the solid, particulate quality of things, smell is the faculty proper to the earthy element — the densest and most material of the senses, rooted in the body and the ground. It is closely bound to memory and instinct.

smyrna.summary: Smyrna — the suffering church, attributed to the Sun (Resh).
smyrna.description: Smyrna, the persecuted church promised the crown of life, is set in 777 in the path of Resh and the sphere of the Sun. The attribution links its faithfulness through tribulation to the solar mystery of death and rebirth — the church that, like the Sun, passes through darkness to rise crowned.
tables: XXXVI. Selection of Christian Gods (10); Apostles (12); Evangelists(4); and Churches of Asia (7)

snakestone.summary: The serpent-stone of Scorpio — the coiled power of death and renewal.
snakestone.description: The snakestone is attributed to the path of Nun and Scorpio — the fixed-water sign of death, sex, and regeneration whose own emblem is the serpent that sheds its skin. The name has been given to coiled ammonite fossils (taken in folklore for petrified snakes), to serpentine, and to stones reputed to cure snakebite; all carry the Scorpionic charge of the serpent-power, the venom that is also medicine, the death that is also rebirth. The stone of the coiled, transforming force.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

snow.summary: A content of the heaven Makhon at Chesed — the stored treasuries of snow.
snow.description: In the contents of the heavens, 'Snow' is among the elemental treasures kept in the storehouse-heaven Makhon, attributed to Chesed. The Talmud places in this heaven the chambers of snow and hail; the snow is one of the meteorological treasures held in the heavenly magazine, released in its season upon the earth.
tables: XCV. Contents of the Heavens of Assiah

snowdrop.summary: The virgin flower of Virgo—the snowdrop, first pure bloom to pierce the winter snow, emblem of hope and chastity.
snowdrop.description: The Snowdrop is attributed to Virgo (Yod, the Hermit). The earliest flower of the year, lifting its small white head through the last of the snow, it is an immemorial emblem of purity, hope, and consolation—the bloom of Candlemas and of the Virgin, chaste and unsullied. Its place in the virginal earth-sign is exact. Esoterically the snowdrop is the pure, solitary light of Virgo breaking the winter—the chaste first sign of returning life, modest and undefiled.

socratic-genius.summary: The daimonion of Socrates, set at Spirit — the inner divine voice that warns and guides.
socratic-genius.description: Among the Legendary Orders of Being, the Socratic Genius is attributed to Spirit (the path of the quintessence). It is the famous daimonion of Socrates — the inner divine sign or voice which, as he told his judges, came to him from childhood and never urged him on but only ever held him back from error. As the type of the personal guiding spirit it prefigures the Holy Guardian Angel of later magick: the indwelling genius that counsels the soul from within. Set at Spirit, it is the highest and most rarefied of these orders, the divine daemon as inner guide.

soda.summary: Presiding god of the first decan of Capricorn, the Jovial face where the Goat begins its climb amid change.
soda.description: Soda is the presiding god 777 assigns to the first decan of Capricorn (0°–10°), the cardinal initiation of the earth-triplicity. Jupiter rules this face and it bears the Two of Disks—Change—the dynamic balancing of forces by which the Goat begins its ambitious ascent. The name belongs to the Greco-Egyptian list of thirty-six decan-rulers, the faces of the old sky-religion.
tables: CLXVII. Egyptian Gods of the Zodiac (Asc. Decans)

sol.summary: The Sun—centre, self, sovereignty; ruler of Tiphareth and the path of Resh.
sol.description:
Sol, the Sun, is the luminary of the centre—source of light, life, and sovereignty. In 777 it rules the sixth Sephirah Tiphareth and the path of the letter Resh (the Tarot trump The Sun), and stands as the very type of the harmonised Self. Its metal is gold, its day Sunday, its number six, its principal correspondences the lion, the rose, the heliotrope, and the figure of the dying-and-rising god.

Astronomically the Sun is the gravitational heart around which the system turns; symbolically it is the heart of the human being, the seat of the conscious, integrating self and of the Holy Guardian Angel in Thelemic doctrine. Solar gods—Ra, Helios, Apollo, Mithras, the risen Christ—everywhere embody illumination, kingship, and the triumph of light over the darkness of death.
tables: CXXXIX. Planets Exalted in the Signs of the Zodiac
XCV. Contents of the Heavens of Assiah
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

solar-plexus.summary: The Solar Plexus — bodily seat of the fire centre, attributed to Netzach.
solar-plexus.description: The solar plexus, the great network of nerves behind the stomach, is the bodily seat of the navel chakra (Manipura), set in 777 at Netzach. Long felt as the centre of 'gut' emotion, vital heat, and instinctive power, it is the somatic correlate of the fiery wheel of will.

soldier-with-red-leonine-face.summary: The magical image of Alloces — a soldier with a red lion's face and flaming eyes on a great horse — Goetic Duke of the first decan of Virgo (by night).
soldier-with-red-leonine-face.description: Alloces (Alocer), the fifty-second spirit of the Goetia and a strong and mighty Duke, appears as a soldier riding upon a great horse, his face that of a lion, red and ruddy, with flaming eyes, speaking with a hoarse and great voice. In 777 he is the nocturnal ruler of the first decan of Virgo. He teaches astronomy and the liberal arts and gives good and faithful familiars. The fiery leonine warrior set in earthy Virgo marks a martial, illuminating intelligence — burning sight bent to study and to instruction.

solid-structures.summary: The solid structures of the body, attributed to Earth, its dense and lasting parts.
solid-structures.description: The Solid Structures are attributed to Earth (32 bis). All that is firm, dense, and enduring in the body—the bones, the framework, the fixed tissues—answers to the earthy element, the principle of solidity and permanence. As Earth is the most material of the four, so the solid structures are the body's earthly portion, the durable architecture that gives the fluid life of the organism a stable and lasting form to dwell in.

solider-with-ducal-crown-riding-a-crocod.term: Solider with ducal crown riding a crocodile
solider-with-ducal-crown-riding-a-crocod.displayTerm: Solider with ducal crown riding a crocodile
solider-with-ducal-crown-riding-a-crocod.summary: The magical image of Sallos — a gallant soldier crowned as a duke, riding a crocodile — Goetic Duke of the first decan of Libra.
solider-with-ducal-crown-riding-a-crocod.description: Sallos (Saleos), the nineteenth spirit of the Goetia and a great Duke, shows himself as a gallant soldier wearing a ducal crown and riding upon a crocodile. In 777 he rules the first decan of Libra by day.
