Peaceable in nature, he causes the love of men toward women and of women toward men, binding them in mutual affection — a fitting office for the sign of the Balance and of Venus, his amorous work carried, incongruously, on the back of the river's cold reptile.

solider-with-lion-s-head-rides-a-pale-ho.term: Solider with Lion's head rides a pale horse
solider-with-lion-s-head-rides-a-pale-ho.displayTerm: Solider with Lion's head rides a pale horse
solider-with-lion-s-head-rides-a-pale-ho.summary: The magical image of Sabnock — an armed soldier with a lion's head upon a pale horse — Goetic Marquis of the first decan of Gemini (by night).
solider-with-lion-s-head-rides-a-pale-ho.description: Sabnock (Savnok), the forty-third spirit of the Goetia and a mighty, great Marquis, appears as an armed soldier with the head of a lion, riding upon a pale horse. In 777 he is the nocturnal ruler of the first decan of Gemini. He builds high towers, castles and cities and furnishes them with arms, and afflicts men for many days with wounds and sores that rot and breed worms. The lion-headed man-at-arms upon his pale mount marks martial power loosed in the airy sign of the Twins — the builder and the wounder in one.

soma.summary: The Vedic entheogen and god of the sacred draught, attributed to Binah.
soma.description: Soma is the visionary sacrament of the Rig Veda — at once a plant, a pressed and offered draught, and a deity, the very ambrosia by which the gods became immortal and the seers (rishis) touched the eternal. Crowley places it at Binah, the supernal Mother and the sphere of the bitter sea, fitting for a drink that opens the gate of understanding through ecstatic dissolution of the ordinary self. Its botanical identity has been debated for centuries (Amanita muscaria, ephedra, and others proposed), but its esoteric meaning is unambiguous: Soma is the archetype of the entheogen, the sacred intoxicant that lifts consciousness into communion with the divine. It embodies the principle that the body itself may become the chalice of revelation.
tables: XXII. Small Selection of Hindu Deities
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

sons-of-god.summary: Sons of God — the English name of the angelic choir Beni Elohim, the host of Assiah at Hod.
sons-of-god.description: In the Qabalistic angelology each Sephirah commands its own choir of angels; “Sons of God” (Table CI, the Angels of Assiah given in English) renders into the vernacular the Hebrew order Beni Elohim, the host attributed to Hod. These are the Sons of God, the angelic intelligences of Mercury, the reasoning and communicating hosts of the eighth sphere. Crowley sets them at Hod on the Tree, where the choir gives angelic form to the energy of that sphere as it acts in Assiah, the world of action.

sorrow.summary: Three of Swords — Sorrow; Saturn in Libra, Binah of Air: the heart pierced.
sorrow.description: The Three of Swords, Sorrow, is Binah in the suit of Air and the second decan of Libra under Saturn. The dark Mother of Form, armed with Saturn's grief, drives the intellect into mourning: three swords pierce and sunder the heart, the central blade cleaving the rose of feeling. It is melancholy, separation, and the deep sorrow that belongs to Binah, the sea of understanding that is also the sea of tears.
tables: CXXXV. Titles and Attributions of the Sword Suit.

sorrow-can-be-remedied.summary: The Third Noble Truth — the cessation of suffering (nirodha).
sorrow-can-be-remedied.description: Sorrow can be Remedied states the Third Noble Truth, the truth of cessation (nirodha), attributed to the element Fire. Because suffering arises from craving, the fading-away and ending of that craving is the ending of suffering — Nibbāna, the unbinding, the great extinguishing. It is the truth of hope at the heart of the teaching: liberation is genuinely possible. Its fiery attribution befits the image of a flame gone out, the cooling of the fever of thirst into perfect peace.

sorrow-has-a-remedy-in-the-eightfold-pat.term: Sorrow has a remedy in the Eightfold Path
sorrow-has-a-remedy-in-the-eightfold-pat.displayTerm: Sorrow has a remedy in the Eightfold Path
sorrow-has-a-remedy-in-the-eightfold-pat.summary: The Fourth Noble Truth — the path leading to the cessation of suffering (magga).
sorrow-has-a-remedy-in-the-eightfold-pat.description: Sorrow has a Remedy in the Eightfold Path states the Fourth Noble Truth, the truth of the way (magga), attributed to the path of Tav. The remedy is the Noble Eightfold Path — right view, intention, speech, action, livelihood, effort, mindfulness and concentration — the Middle Way between indulgence and austerity that leads to the ending of craving. The practical conclusion of the whole teaching, it is fittingly set at Tav, the all-comprehending final letter: the prescription that gathers the diagnosis into a complete and walkable course of cure.

sorrow-is-a-condition-of-existence.term: Sorrow is a condition of existence
sorrow-is-a-condition-of-existence.displayTerm: Sorrow is a condition of existence
sorrow-is-a-condition-of-existence.summary: The First Noble Truth — the truth of suffering (dukkha).
sorrow-is-a-condition-of-existence.description: Sorrow is a Condition of Existence states the First Noble Truth, the truth of dukkha, attributed to the element of Earth. The Buddha's diagnosis begins here: birth, ageing, sickness and death, union with the disliked and parting from the loved, the not-getting of what is wished — all conditioned existence is shot through with unsatisfactoriness, an inherent dis-ease that no arrangement of circumstances can finally cure. Set at the densest element, earth, it grounds the whole teaching in the unflinching recognition of suffering as the very texture of becoming.

sorrow-is-caused-by-attachment.summary: The Second Noble Truth — the origin of suffering in craving (samudaya).
sorrow-is-caused-by-attachment.description: Sorrow is Caused by Attachment states the Second Noble Truth, the truth of the origin (samudaya), attributed to the element Air. Suffering is not random or imposed from without but arises from craving — the thirst for sensual pleasure, for existence and for non-existence — and the clinging that follows it. By tracing dukkha to its cause, the Buddha makes it something that can in principle be undone; its airy attribution suits the restless, reaching movement of desire that fabricates the whole round of becoming.

sothis.summary: Sothis (Sopdet), the star Sirius deified — herald of the inundation, at Cancer.
sothis.description: Sothis is the Greek name for Sopdet, the goddess of the star Sirius, whose heliacal rising heralded the annual flooding of the Nile and the start of the Egyptian year. Referred to Cheth and Cancer, the watery sign of the rising tide, she is the brilliant star-goddess whose appearance promised renewal and abundance. As the celestial herald of the inundation she joins the rhythms of the heavens to the life-giving river.
tables: CLXVIII. Egyptian Names of Asc. Decans.

sou.summary: Sou — a letter of the Coptic alphabet (s/numeral), which Crowley attributes to 1 Kether.
sou.description: Sou is a letter of the Coptic alphabet — the script in which the Egyptian language was written in the Christian era, the Greek alphabet adapted to Egyptian speech. It is the soou, the old digamma-derived sign kept chiefly as a numeral. Crowley folds the Coptic alphabet into the great correspondence of letters and paths in 777 (Table LI), assigning Sou to 1 Kether on the Tree of Life, so that the Egyptian-Christian script takes its station among the Hebrew letters and the keys of the Tarot.
tables: LI. Names of the Coptic Letters

soul.summary: 'soul' — Crowley's trailing element in CXIX at Hod, naming one of the Buddhist Fetters.
soul.description: In table CXIX ('The Ten Fetters' in English) the cell at Hod reads (in essence) 'Belief in a personality, soul' — naming the first samyojana of the Buddhist tradition, sakkaya-ditthi, the false view of an enduring 'self.' The shard 'soul' is the trailing half of the compound, qualifying 'personality' with the English-philosophical equivalent. The entry preserves it as it appears: the second clause of the Fetter, the substantialist version of the self-view that the Buddhist path is set to unbind. The principal entry (belief-in-a-personality) carries the full description.

sourut.summary: Presiding god of the middle decan of Pisces, the Jovial face of brimming emotional happiness.
sourut.description: Sourut is the presiding god 777 attributes to the middle decan of Pisces (10°–20°). Jupiter—Pisces' ancient ruler—governs this face, and it bears the Nine of Cups—Happiness—the full, contented welling of feeling, emotion at its most generous. The name belongs to the Greco-Egyptian roster of thirty-six decan-rulers of the night sky.
tables: CLXIX. Egyptian Gods of the Zodiac (Succedent)

south.summary: The quarter of the noonday heat, attributed to the element Fire.
south.description: The South is the quarter of the sun at its zenith, of greatest heat and brightness. In the elemental scheme of the Western mysteries it is attributed to Fire, the element of will, energy, and transformation. As the station of the noonday blaze, it carries the active, consuming, and illuminating power within the magical circle.
tables: CX. Elements and Quarters per the Sepher Yetzirah

south-sea.summary: South Sea — a pantheon column Crowley reserved in 777 for the Pacific Islander gods, left unfilled.
south-sea.description: The 'South Sea' column among the pantheon tables (XXV-XXXII) was Crowley's placeholder for the Polynesian, Melanesian, and Micronesian deities of the Pacific — Pele, Kane, Lono, Maui, the great voyaging and creator gods of Hawaiʻi, Aotearoa, Tahiti, and beyond. Like the other reserved columns it stands blank in 777, an open frame waiting for the cross-cultural attribution Crowley signalled but did not complete. The entry registers the placeholder.

sow.summary: The teeming mother-pig of Venus—Demeter's beast of abundant fertility, the great fruitful womb of nature.
sow.description: The sow is attributed to Venus and the path of the Empress, and she is the emblem of teeming fertility: the great mother-pig with her litter, sacred to Demeter and the chthonic goddesses of the harvest, whose flesh and increase were offered in the mysteries of the grain. Fecund, earthy, and abundantly nourishing, the sow figures the lush, prodigal generation of nature that is the Empress's own gift—life multiplying without stint. There is no daintiness here but a frank, fruitful animal abundance. Esoterically the sow is the fertile maternal ground of Venus-Netzach, the womb of nature that brings forth life in profusion, the rich and unrefined generosity of the green world.

space.summary: The first formless attainment — the sphere of infinite space (ākāsānañcāyatana).
space.description: Space is the first of the four formless attainments (arūpa-jhānas) of the Buddhist scheme, attributed in 777 to the Veils of the Negative. Having mastered the form-jhānas, the meditator drops the last residue of the material object and dwells in the perception of boundless space — 'space is infinite' — an expanse with neither edge nor content. Set at the Veils, beyond even Kether, it figures the dissolution of all form into limitless extension, the first of the ascending negations by which consciousness approaches the unconditioned.

sparrow.summary: The amorous little bird of Venus—Aphrodite's lustful sparrow, small emblem of desire and love.
sparrow.description: The sparrow is attributed to Venus and the path of the Empress, and it was anciently the most amorous of birds, sacred to Aphrodite and drawing her chariot in the verses of Sappho—a byword for ardent and unwearied love-making. Small, common, and irrepressibly lively, the sparrow figures the everyday, earthly face of desire, the warm sensual life that belongs to the Venusian sphere. It is love not as lofty ideal but as the quick, natural appetite of living things. Esoterically the sparrow marks the humble, ubiquitous presence of the love-force in nature—desire as the small, persistent flame that animates the whole green and breeding world.

sparrowhawk.summary: The small solar falcon of the Sun—the swift keen raptor of Resh, the hawk of day in lesser form.
sparrowhawk.description: The sparrowhawk is attributed to the Sun and the path of Resh, and it is a smaller kin of the great solar falcon of Kether: a swift, keen-eyed raptor of the open day, all sharpness and speed. Where the hawk crowns the summit of the Tree as the falcon of Ra, the sparrowhawk carries that same solar fire down to the sphere of Resh, the radiant, life-giving Sun of the manifest world. It is the bright bird of clear daylight and unerring strike, vision and decisiveness joined. Esoterically the sparrowhawk figures the solar consciousness in action—the keen, swift, illuminated will that sees its mark plainly and descends upon it without hesitation under the full light of the Sun.

speaking.summary: Speaking — the bodily function of the element Air, attributed to the path of Aleph.
speaking.description: In 777's table of the bodily functions referred to the elements, speech is given to Air (the path of Aleph) — the breath shaped into the spoken word. As Air is the medium of vibration and exchange, so speaking is its proper function in the microcosm: the airy power by which the inner is communicated outward.

spear.summary: The piercing lance of Geburah—the martial thrust of directed force, the spear that wounds and opens.
spear.description: The Spear is attributed to Geburah, the martial sphere of Mars, and it is the lance—the piercing weapon of the warrior, the spear of Longinus that opened the side of the dying god and so released the redeeming blood. As a magical implement it is force concentrated to a single point and thrust home: penetrating, decisive, and martial, the directed power that pierces whatever resists it. Its place at Geburah marks it as the severe, wounding strength that, like the holy lance, can both destroy and, paradoxically, open the way to grace. Esoterically the Spear is the magician's penetrating, single-pointed force—the concentrated thrust of will that pierces through obstruction to its mark, the martial power of Geburah focused to a wounding, opening point.

sphere-of-jupiter.summary: The Sphere of Jupiter — Tzedek, attributed to Chesed.
sphere-of-jupiter.description: The Sphere of Jupiter (Tzedek, 'righteousness') is set in 777 at Chesed, the fourth Sephirah. Jupiter — the great benefic, the sphere of mercy, expansion, sovereignty, and beneficence — is the proper planet of Chesed, the loving-kindness and majestic largesse of the Tree.
tables: VII. Translation of Heavens of Assiah

sphere-of-luna.summary: The Sphere of the Moon — Levanah, attributed to Yesod.
sphere-of-luna.description: The Sphere of the Moon (Levanah) is set in 777 at Yesod, the ninth Sephirah. The Moon — ruler of tides, dreams, generation, and the astral light — is the proper planet of Yesod, the foundation and the formative astral sphere upon which the material world rests.
tables: VII. Translation of Heavens of Assiah

sphere-of-mars.summary: The Sphere of Mars — Madim, attributed to Geburah.
sphere-of-mars.description: The Sphere of Mars (Madim) is set in 777 at Geburah, the fifth Sephirah. Mars — the planet of war, severity, force, and the cutting sword — is the natural ruler of Geburah, the sphere of strength and judgment that balances the mercy of Chesed.
tables: VII. Translation of Heavens of Assiah

sphere-of-mercury.summary: The Sphere of Mercury — Kokab, attributed to Hod.
sphere-of-mercury.description: The Sphere of Mercury (Kokab) is set in 777 at Hod, the eighth Sephirah. Mercury — the planet of intellect, speech, magic, and commerce — is the natural ruler of Hod, the sphere of reason, language, and the marshalled forms of thought.
tables: VII. Translation of Heavens of Assiah

sphere-of-saturn.summary: The Sphere of Saturn — Shabbathai, attributed to Binah.
sphere-of-saturn.description: The Sphere of Saturn (Shabbathai) is set in 777 at Binah, the supernal Mother. Saturn, the slowest and outermost of the classical planets, lord of time, form, and limitation, is the natural planet of Binah — the sphere of the great constraining Mother who gives boundary and form to all that the higher light pours forth.
tables: VII. Translation of Heavens of Assiah

sphere-of-sol.summary: The Sphere of the Sun — Shemesh, attributed to Tiphareth.
sphere-of-sol.description: The Sphere of the Sun (Shemesh) is set in 777 at Tiphareth, the sixth Sephirah and the radiant heart of the Tree. The Sun — source of light, life, and harmony, and the planet of every solar redeemer-god — is the perfect ruler of Tiphareth, the sphere of beauty, balance, and the reborn god at the centre.
tables: VII. Translation of Heavens of Assiah

sphere-of-the-elements.summary: The Sphere of the Elements — the sublunary world, attributed to Malkuth.
sphere-of-the-elements.description: The Sphere of the Elements (Olam Yesodoth, 'the world of the foundations') is the sublunary realm of the four elements, set in 777 at Malkuth, the tenth Sephirah. Below the spheres of the planets lies the world of earth, water, air, and fire — the material Kingdom in which the whole descending order of the heavens comes finally to rest.
tables: VII. Translation of Heavens of Assiah

sphere-of-the-primum-mobile.summary: The Sphere of the Primum Mobile — the First Swirlings, attributed to Kether.
sphere-of-the-primum-mobile.description: The Sphere of the Primum Mobile ('the first moved,' the Rashith ha-Gilgalim, 'beginning of the whirlings') is the outermost heaven of the old cosmology, the first motion imparted to the cosmos, set in 777 at Kether. It is the sphere nearest the Crown — the primal stirring from which all the lower spheres take their turning, the first whirl of manifestation.
tables: VII. Translation of Heavens of Assiah

sphere-of-the-zodiac.summary: The Sphere of the Zodiac — the heaven of the fixed stars, attributed to Chokmah.
sphere-of-the-zodiac.description: The Sphere of the Zodiac (the Mazloth, the heaven of the fixed stars) is set in 777 at Chokmah, the supernal Father. As Chokmah is the sphere of the all-begetting stellar force, the band of the zodiac — the wheel of the twelve signs encircling the cosmos — is its fitting heaven, the starry field of the second Sephirah.
tables: VII. Translation of Heavens of Assiah

sphere-of-venus.summary: The Sphere of Venus — Nogah, attributed to Netzach.
sphere-of-venus.description: The Sphere of Venus (Nogah, 'brightness') is set in 777 at Netzach, the seventh Sephirah. Venus — the planet of love, desire, art, and natural fecundity — is the proper ruler of Netzach, the sphere of victory through love and of the teeming beauty of nature.
tables: VII. Translation of Heavens of Assiah

spheres.summary: A content of the Firmament at Hod — the celestial spheres carrying the lights.
spheres.description: Among the contents of the heavens, the spheres are placed at the Firmament, attributed to Hod. In the older cosmology the lights are borne upon nested celestial spheres; these revolving shells, carrying sun, moon, stars, and planets in their courses, are reckoned a content of the second heaven, the great machinery of the sky assigned to the sphere of measured order.
tables: XCV. Contents of the Heavens of Assiah

sphinx.summary: The fourfold guardian and riddle—the compounded kerubic beast that holds the four magical powers, throned upon the Wheel.
sphinx.description: The Sphinx appears across Malkuth, Cancer, Jupiter and the quintessence of Spirit, and it is the great composite creature—bull's body, lion's strength, eagle's wings, and human head—uniting the four Kerubic beasts and so the four elements in a single form. It is at once the guardian who sets the riddle at the threshold and the answer to it, the figure of the adept who has mastered and balanced the elemental powers within himself. Seated upon the Wheel of Fortune (Jupiter), the Sphinx is the still, knowing centre that the turning cannot move. To it belong the four magical powers of the Sphinx: to Know, to Will, to Dare, and to Keep Silent. Esoterically the Sphinx is the perfected master of the elements—the balanced and silent intelligence, compounded of all the powers, that holds the riddle of nature and abides unshaken at the centre of the turning world.
tables: CLXXXI. Correct Design of Tarot Trumps

sphinx-as-synthesis-of-elements.summary: The Sphinx, synthesis of the four elements — the kerubic guardian, at Malkuth.
sphinx-as-synthesis-of-elements.description: The Sphinx, with the head of a human, body of a bull or lion, paws of a lion, and wings of an eagle, is understood esoterically as the synthesis of the four elements and the four kerubic signs of the zodiac (Aquarius, Taurus, Leo, Scorpio). Referred to Malkuth, the realised Kingdom, it represents the four powers of the elements united and mastered in a single form. The Sphinx is the guardian of the mysteries, embodying the magician's command of earth, air, fire, and water made one.

spica-virginis.summary: Spica, the Virgin's wheat-ear — the bright star of the mansion al-Simak.
spica-virginis.description: Spica Virginis, the alpha star of Virgo, is the luminous wheat-ear held by the celestial Virgin and the heart of the lunar mansion al-Simak; 777 sets it in the path of Virgo (Yod). Its rising once announced the season of harvest across the ancient world, binding it forever to the grain-goddesses — Demeter, Ceres, Isis — and to the symbolism of ripening, plenty, and the gathered fruit of labour.
tables: CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon

spider.summary: The weaver of Libra and Tiphareth—spinner of the web of fate, balance held at the centre of the net.
spider.description: The spider is placed at Libra and at Tiphareth, and it is the great weaver, sitting motionless at the exact centre of a web whose every thread it feels—an image of equilibrium and of the conscious centre that governs a whole field of forces. Its web is the figure of Maya, the woven veil of appearances, and of the net of cause and consequence in which all things are caught. At Libra the spider is the perfect balance of the suspended net; at Tiphareth it is the harmonising self seated at the heart of its own creation. Esoterically the spider is both the artist who spins reality from its own substance and the fate that binds—creation and entanglement issuing from one source.

spinal-weakness.summary: Weakness of the spine at Yod and Virgo — failure of the body's central support.
spinal-weakness.description: Spinal weakness is attributed to the path of Virgo, the mutable earth sign of the Mercurial body and its fine structure. The spine is the central column that upholds the frame and carries the cord of the nerves; its weakness is a failure at the very axis of the body's support and Mercurial transmission. Symbolically it is the giving-way of the inner pillar, the upright structure of the self losing its strength.

spirit.summary: The fifth element; the quintessence that unifies and transcends the other four.
spirit.description:
Spirit (Akasha, the Aether or quintessence) is the fifth element, the unifying source from which the four material elements proceed and to which they return. It is not one force among others but their living root and their reconciliation—the silent centre of the pentagram, the still point of the wheel. In 777 it is associated with the path 31-bis and the letter Shin in its higher, all-elemental sense.

Spirit is the principle of integration: where Fire, Water, Air, and Earth are partial and complementary, Spirit is whole. The aspirant who masters the four elements and then ascends to their quintessence achieves the elemental equilibrium that is the foundation of all higher magical attainment.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

spirit-of-life.summary: A content of the heavens at Chesed — the breath of life held in the merciful sphere.
spirit-of-life.description: Among the contents of the heavens of Assiah, the 'Spirit of Life' is reckoned at Chesed, the sphere of Jupiter and mercy. It is the vivifying breath, the living spirit dispensed from the heavenly storehouse — the animating principle that, flowing from the merciful sphere, quickens the worlds below with life.
tables: XCV. Contents of the Heavens of Assiah

splendour.summary: Splendour—the eighth Sephirah; the sphere of Mercury, intellect, language, and magic.
splendour.description:
Hod (הוד, ‘Splendour’ or ‘Glory’) is the eighth Sephirah, the sphere of Mercury and the seat of the rational, analytic, and linguistic mind. Where Netzach feels, Hod thinks: it governs abstraction, classification, writing, and the formal apparatus of ceremonial magic itself. Its God-name is Elohim Tzabaoth, its virtue truthfulness, its vice falsehood and dishonesty; its image a hermaphrodite.

Hod is the splendour of the well-ordered intellect—the magician’s workshop of names, sigils, and correspondences (777 is itself a Hod-like labour). Yet its glory is reflective rather than self-originating, and it requires the living impulse of Netzach lest its brilliance become mere cleverness.
tables: III. Translation of the Names of the Paths
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

spout-of-the-urn.summary: Spout of the Urn — the English meaning of one of the aquarian lunar mansions, at the Water-Bearer's pouring.
spout-of-the-urn.description: 'Spout of the Urn' is the English gloss of the lunar mansion marked at the mouth of the Water-Bearer's pouring vessel — most often associated with stars in the lower body of Aquarius where the celestial water descends toward Pisces (often identified with Sa'd al-Mulk or its neighbour). The image is the pouring spout — that point at which the stored water becomes the flowing river — and the mansion's traditional magic concerns the release of held things and the directing of currents (whether literal water, or fortune, or desire). Crowley fixes it on the Tzaddi/Aquarius path.
tables: CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon

square.summary: The four-sided figure — attributed to Jupiter/Chesed; order, law, and stable rule.
square.description: The square, the four-sided figure, is attributed by its number to Chesed and the planet Jupiter. As the emblem of four it signifies order, law, measure, and the stable foundation of rule — the foursquare establishment of the world and the just governance of the merciful king. It is the figure of solidity and equilibrium, the ground-plan of the temple and the throne.
tables: XLIX. Lineal Figures of the Planets, &c., and Geomany

st.summary: The 'St' digraph — set by Crowley at the first Sephirah, Kether, in the Coptic-equivalents column.
st.description: 'St' is one of the lighter, more ambiguous entries in table LI, placed at Kether — the Crown, the first Sephirah, the unmanifest point from which the Tree descends. The placement most likely renders the Coptic Ⲥⲧ cluster or the Greek στ found in the most sacred Coptic loanwords (Stauros, the Cross; Stoicheia, the Elements). Whatever the precise glyph, the entry is what Crowley made it: a phonetic mark — a hissed/stopped sibilant pair — fixed at the supernal apex. As with all of LI it is a piece of his attempt to give the Hebrew Tree a complete polyglot phonology.
tables: LI. English Equivalent of the Coptic Alphabet

st-order.summary: The First Order — the Golden Dawn elemental grades, from Malkuth to Hod and Yesod.
st-order.description: In the threefold scheme of the magical grades (after the Golden Dawn and the A.'.A.'.), the First Order comprises the elemental grades climbing the lower Tree — Zelator, Theoricus, Practicus, and Philosophus, attributed to Malkuth, Yesod, Hod, and Netzach beneath the veil of Tiphareth. It is the Order of the beginner: the purification and balancing of the four elements in the aspirant, the necessary foundation laid before the heart-centre can be reached.

st-plane-middle-pillar.summary: First plane, Middle Pillar — the supernal apex of the Tree, the geometric position of Kether.
st-plane-middle-pillar.description: In Crowley's table XII, 'Position on the Glyph,' the Tree of Life is divided horizontally into four 'planes' (Supernal, Ethical, Astral, Material) and vertically into three pillars (Severity/Left, Mercy/Right, Mildness/Middle). The first plane on the Middle Pillar is Kether — the Crown, the single point at the head of the Tree from which Chokmah and Binah are emanated. As a geometric statement the entry is austere: there is one place above all others, and it is here.
tables: XII. Position on the Glyph of the Tree of Life

stable-intelligence.summary: The Twenty-third Path — the Stable Intelligence of Mem, the constancy among the emanations.
stable-intelligence.description: The Twenty-third Path is the Stable Intelligence (Sekhel Kayam, the 'enduring' Intelligence), attributed to the letter Mem and the element Water, the path of The Hanged Man joining Geburah to Hod. The Sepher Yetzirah says it has the property of constancy amidst all the numerations, preserving their stability. The still, deep water of Mem is paradoxically the most stable of the elemental paths: in the surrender and suspension of the Hanged Man, in the motionless depth beneath the surface, the changing flux finds a fixed and abiding ground.
tables: XIII. Paths of the Sefer Yetzirah

staff.summary: Design detail of the Hermit (Yod): the staff.
staff.description: ‘Staff’ is a fragment of Liber 777's design for Atu IX, the Hermit (path of Yod, Virgo): ‘…bearing a lamp and staff.’ The staff is the Hermit's support and his rod of power—the wand of the wayfarer that steadies his solitary climb and, esoterically, the channel of the generative force of Yod. With lamp in one hand and staff in the other, the ancient unites illumination and will, light and the means to walk by it.
tables: CLXXXI. Correct Design of Tarot Trumps

star-ruby.summary: The asterism ruby of Chokmah — the living star of primal force.
star-ruby.description: The star ruby — red corundum bearing the six-rayed asterism — is set at Chokmah, the sphere of pure outgoing force and the Sphere of the Zodiac. Its blazing red star, alive with movement, fittingly images the dynamic, masculine fire of the second Sephirah, the seed-point of force set among the stars. (Crowley also gave the name to one of his published rituals.)
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

star-sapphire.summary: The asterism sapphire of the Veils and Binah — the hidden star in the dark.
star-sapphire.description: The star sapphire — a sapphire whose included needles scatter light into a moving six-rayed star (asterism) — is attributed to the Veils of the Negative and to Binah, the supernal Mother. Its symbolism is exact and beautiful: a star hidden within the dark blue depth, revealed only when light falls rightly, an emblem of the secret light concealed in the womb of darkness and in the Great Sea of Understanding. It is the gem of the star found in the night.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

stars.summary: A content of the Firmament at Hod — the fixed stars set in the second heaven.
stars.description: Among the contents of the heavens, the stars are placed in the Firmament (Raqia), attributed to Hod. The Talmud says the sun, moon, stars, and planets are all set in the Firmament; the stars are thus reckoned a content of the second heaven, the spangled lights fixed in the vault, fittingly assigned to the sphere of order and number.
tables: XCV. Contents of the Heavens of Assiah

CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon
CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon

sterility.summary: Sterility at Malkuth — barrenness of the Kingdom, the earth that will not bear.
sterility.description: Sterility is set at Malkuth, the Kingdom, the final Sephirah of manifest matter and the body of the world. Malkuth is the bride and the fruitful earth in which all the higher influences come at last to harvest; sterility is that ground rendered barren — the Kingdom unable to bring forth, the generative current that descends the whole Tree finding no issue in the world of fact. It figures fruitlessness at the very point where spirit should become flesh.

sthula-sharira.summary: Sthula Sharira — the gross physical body, attributed to Malkuth.
sthula-sharira.description: Sthula Sharira, the 'gross body,' is the dense physical vehicle — the lowest of the human principles, the temporary house of the incarnate soul. Referred fittingly in 777 to Malkuth, the material Kingdom, it is the perishable form through which the higher principles act and learn in the world of matter.

stock-dove-with-sore-throat.summary: The magical image of a stock-dove with a hoarse voice — shared by Halphas and Shax, Goetic spirits of the second decans of Aries and Gemini (by night).
stock-dove-with-sore-throat.description: This image — a stock-dove (wood-pigeon) that speaks with a hoarse, sore-throated voice — is borne in 777 by two Goetic spirits at once: Halphas (Malthus), the thirty-eighth spirit and a great Earl, nocturnal ruler of the second decan of Aries; and Shax (Chax, Scox), the forty-fourth spirit and a great Marquis, nocturnal ruler of the second decan of Gemini. Halphas builds towers and fills them with weapons and munitions and sends men of war to appointed places. Shax takes away the sight, hearing and understanding of any man or woman, steals money and brings it again, and discovers hidden things — though he is a deceiver unless bound within the triangle. The soft, mournful pigeon, broken of voice, fitly clothes spirits of war and of cunning theft.

stolas.summary: The thirty-sixth spirit of the Goetia, a raven-formed prince of Pisces who teaches astronomy and the virtues of herbs and stones.
stolas.description: Stolas is the thirty-sixth spirit of the Goetia, a great and powerful prince of the decans of Pisces. He teaches astronomy and the virtues of herbs and precious stones. He appears first as a (crowned) night-raven or owl, then in human shape. A spirit of the watery sign, he is the instructor in the stars and the hidden potencies of the natural world.

stomach.summary: The stomach, attributed to Cancer, the nurturing vessel of digestion.
stomach.description: The Stomach is attributed to Cheth and Cancer. In medical astrology Cancer, the watery, sheltering sign ruled by the Moon, governs the stomach and the digestion—the receptive vessel that receives nourishment and begins to break it down. As Cancer is the great symbol of the nurturing and the inward, so the stomach is the organ of bodily nurture, the moon-ruled cauldron where food is gathered and the body fed.

storax.summary: The sweet balsam resin of Mercury and Hod—storax, warm and honeyed smoke of the intellect's splendour.
storax.description: Storax (styrax) is attributed to Mercury, to Hod, to Taurus and to Earth. A warm, sweet, balsamic resin long burned as incense and used to carry other scents, it has the grounding, honeyed quality that suits Hod's mercurial splendour brought down toward the earthy and the formed. Esoterically storax is the sweet smoke of the Mercurial sphere, the fragrant fixative that binds and warms—reason and beauty of form made into a mellow incense.

stork.summary: The pious bird of the Moon—bringer of birth and of return, the migratory herald of the lunar path.
stork.description: The stork is attributed to the Moon and the path of Gimel, the High Priestess, and it carries a wealth of fitting lore: it is the bird that brings the newborn child, the herald of birth and renewal, and its Hebrew name, chasidah, means 'the pious' or 'loving one,' for its faithful return and its care for its parents. As a great migrant that departs and unfailingly comes back with the season, it belongs to the cyclic, tidal nature of the Moon. Esoterically the stork figures the bringing-forth of new life out of the lunar deep and the faithful rhythm of departure and return—the soul's recurring descent into and emergence from the waters ruled by the Priestess.

straight-application-of-force.summary: The directness of the Arrow at Sagittarius—force sent undeviating to its mark, the shortest path to the goal.
straight-application-of-force.description: The 'straight application of force' is named among the weapons at Sagittarius, describing the quality of the Arrow that is that sign's emblem: force sent in a perfectly straight line to its target, without deviation, hesitation, or waste. It is the principle that the shortest distance between the will and its goal is the undeviating line, and that aspiration accomplishes most when it is single, direct, and unbending. Under Sagittarius this is the archer's virtue—the clean, aimed release that neither swerves nor scatters. Esoterically the straight application of force is the magician's economy of will: the discipline of aiming the whole power at one point and loosing it along the most direct path, so that nothing is dissipated and the force arrives whole at its mark.

stramonium.summary: Datura / thornapple, attributed to Tiphareth and to Spirit; potent deliriant.
stramonium.description:
Stramonium — datura, the thornapple — appears both at Tiphareth and at the 31-bis path of Spirit, marking it as a plant of intense, sometimes shattering visionary force. It has a worldwide history in oracular and shamanic practice (the Delphic and many other traditions are associated with daturas) precisely because its tropane alkaloids dissolve the boundary between waking and hallucination so completely that the visions are mistaken for reality. Esoterically it is the double-edged solar/spiritual fire — illumination that can scorch the one who grasps it unprepared.

Caution: datura is an extremely dangerous deliriant; the gap between an active and a lethal dose is small, and poisonings are frequently fatal. This is a historical and symbolic entry only.
stramonium.caution: EXTREMELY DANGEROUS deliriant; narrow margin to a lethal dose; frequent fatalities. Historical/symbolic only — never ingest.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

strength.summary: Atu XI — Teth / Leo; the ecstatic mastery of the life-force, woman riding the Beast.
strength.description: Lust (the older Strength) is trump XI, attributed to Teth and Leo, the path from Chesed to Geburah. Crowley renamed it ‘Lust’ to emphasise the joyous, ecstatic mastery of the life-force rather than mere restraint: the Scarlet Woman rides the seven-headed Beast, holding the Grail aloft, not subduing the lion but riding it in rapture. It is courage as wholehearted vitality, the spiritual will united with and exalting the animal power rather than suppressing it. The card teaches the sacred use of energy and desire—strength as the embrace, not the conquest, of the Beast.
tables: CXXXIII. Titles and Attributions of the Wand Suit
III. Translation of the Names of the Paths
XIV. General Attribution of the Tarot
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

strife.summary: Five of Wands — Strife; Saturn in Leo, Geburah of Fire: fire broken by struggle.
strife.description: The Five of Wands, Strife, is Geburah in the suit of Fire and the first decan of Leo under heavy Saturn. The harmonious square of the Four is shattered by the fives, which everywhere bring the disruption of pure number by the entry of struggle. Saturn's weight crossing Leo's flame produces quarrel, contest, and the friction of opposed wills — yet it is the wholesome strife of the games, energy tested against energy rather than mere malice.
tables: CXXXIII. Titles and Attributions of the Wand Suit

stryges.summary: The owl-vampires of Roman lore, set at Scorpio — night-witches that feed on blood and flesh.
stryges.description: Among the Legendary Orders of Being, the Stryges (Latin striga, strix) are attributed to Scorpio. In Roman and later European belief they were screech-owl demons or night-witches that flew in the dark to feed upon the blood and entrails of the living, especially of infants — ancestors of the later vampire and witch traditions. Their Scorpionic attribution suits these creatures of nocturnal blood and death; they figure the predatory, devouring power of the dark turned against new life.

success.summary: Six of Disks — Success / Material Success; Moon in Taurus, Tiphareth of Earth.
success.description: The Six of Disks, Success (Material Success), is Tiphareth in the suit of Earth and the second decan of Taurus under the Moon. The solar harmony of the sixth sphere restores matter to its balanced fruition: six discs arranged about a rose-cross as the planets in their courses, prosperity flowing in measured order. It is well-earned material success, generosity, and the equitable circulation of wealth.
tables: CXXXVI. Titles and Attributions of the Pantacle Suit

success-in-bhaktioga.summary: Success in Bhakti-yoga — attainment by the path of devotion, set at Venus.
success-in-bhaktioga.description: Success in Bhaktioga names, among the Hindu/Buddhist Results, the fruit of Bhakti-yoga — the path of loving devotion — attributed to Venus. Where jñāna attains by knowledge and rāja by concentration, bhakti reaches the divine through love: the heart's surrender to and union with the beloved deity, until lover, beloved and loving are one. Set at Venus, the sphere of love and of the longing heart, it figures the perfection of the devotional way, the soul melted into God by the heat of adoration.
tables: XXIV. Certain of the Hindu/Buddhist Results

success-in-hathayoga.summary: Success in Haṭha-yoga — mastery of the body and breath, set at the path of Taurus.
success-in-hathayoga.description: Success in Hathayoga names, among the Hindu/Buddhist Results, the fruit of Haṭha-yoga — the discipline of posture, breath and bodily purification — attributed to the path of Taurus. Through āsana, prāṇāyāma and the awakening of the subtle channels, the practitioner brings the body and its energies under control, making the physical vehicle a fit instrument for higher attainment. Its earthy, Taurean attribution suits this most embodied of yogas, the patient labour upon the flesh and breath that lays the ground for the rousing of the serpent power.
tables: XXIV. Certain of the Hindu/Buddhist Results

success-unfulfilled.summary: Seven of Disks — Success Unfulfilled; Saturn in Taurus, Netzach of Earth: blighted growth.
success-unfulfilled.description: Success Unfulfilled is the Golden Dawn name for the Seven of Disks, Netzach of the earthy suit, Saturn in the last decan of Taurus. Saturn's blight upon Venus-ruled Taurus shows fertile ground gone barren, effort that does not come to fruit. The card speaks of stalled enterprises, anxiety over delayed return, and toil that profits little.
tables: CXXXVI. Titles and Attributions of the Pantacle Suit

succubi.summary: The female night-demons of lust, set at Venus — seducing spirits that visit sleepers.
succubi.description: Among the Legendary Orders of Being, the Succubi are attributed to Venus, the sphere of love and desire. The succubus of medieval lore is the female night-demon who comes to a sleeping man in the guise of a beautiful woman to draw off his seed and his vitality — the counterpart of the incubus and a personification of nocturnal lust and its dreaming temptations. Their Venusian attribution is apt, for they are the shadow-form of love's power turned predatory, beauty become a snare for the unwary soul.

suclagus.summary: Fire — the Nuctemeron genius of the ninth hour presiding over fire, set by Crowley at Sagittarius.
suclagus.description: Suclagus is the Nuctemeron genius of fire. That “Night-illumined Day”, ascribed to Apollonius of Tyana and handed down through Lévi's Transcendental Magic, sets a company of spirits over each of the twelve hours of the magical day, and Suclagus belongs to the ninth hour. He rules over fire, the flame in all its uses and all its dangers. In 777 (Table CLXXIII) Crowley redistributes these hour-genii across the zodiac, where this spirit falls at Sagittarius (Samekh).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

sugar.summary: Refined sweetness, attributed to Taurus; the earthy Venusian principle of pleasure.
sugar.description:
Sugar is placed at the path of Vav and Taurus — fixed earth ruled by Venus — as the very principle of sweetness and bodily pleasure, the Taurean delight of the senses crystallised. Its history is also a dark one, bound to empire and the sugar plantations, a reminder that the earthiest pleasures carry the heaviest material entanglements. Esoterically it is the seduction of the sensual earth.

Caution: refined sugar in excess is a genuine driver of metabolic disease.
sugar.caution: Excess refined sugar drives metabolic disease.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

sulfur.summary: The alchemical fiery principle, attributed to Geburah; the soul of metals.
sulfur.description:
Sulphur — brimstone — is placed at Geburah, the martial sphere of fire and severity, and it is far more than a mineral drug: in alchemy it is one of the three philosophical principles, the fiery, active, masculine Soul of the metals (with Mercury the spirit and Salt the body). Yellow, combustible, and acrid, it is the very element of fire made solid, the 'fire and brimstone' of scripture. Esoterically it is the burning principle of will and transformation, the fixed fire within all things.

Caution: medicinal sulphur is relatively mild, but its compounds and fumes (sulphur dioxide) are hazardous.
sulfur.caution: Elemental sulphur is mild medicinally; fumes and compounds are hazardous.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

sulphates.summary: The sulphate mineral salts, set at Water — the flushing, dissolving, purging element.
sulphates.description: Among the Mineral Drugs, "sulphates" are placed at Mem, the path of the Hanged Man and the element of Water, the dissolving and flushing principle. The attribution suits their chief medicinal use: many sulphate salts are purgatives and emetics that draw water through the body — magnesium sulphate (Epsom salt) and sodium sulphate (Glauber's salt) as saline cathartics, copper and zinc sulphate as emetics. The watery placement reads them as the mineral agents of flushing and release. Esoterically they figure the cleansing, downward-flowing power of Water in the kingdom of salts — dissolution and purgation crystallised into mineral form.
sulphates.caution: Historical/symbolic entry only — not medical advice. Several sulphate salts (e.g. copper sulphate) are toxic if ingested and can cause serious poisoning.

sulphur.summary: The alchemical fiery principle, attributed to Geburah; the soul of metals.
sulphur.description:
Sulphur — brimstone — is placed at Geburah, the martial sphere of fire and severity, and it is far more than a mineral drug: in alchemy it is one of the three philosophical principles, the fiery, active, masculine Soul of the metals (with Mercury the spirit and Salt the body). Yellow, combustible, and acrid, it is the very element of fire made solid, the 'fire and brimstone' of scripture. Esoterically it is the burning principle of will and transformation, the fixed fire within all things.

Caution: medicinal sulphur is relatively mild, but its compounds and fumes (sulphur dioxide) are hazardous.
sulphur.caution: Elemental sulphur is mild medicinally; fumes and compounds are hazardous.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

sun.summary: The Sun—centre, self, sovereignty; ruler of Tiphareth and the path of Resh.
sun.description:
Sol, the Sun, is the luminary of the centre—source of light, life, and sovereignty. In 777 it rules the sixth Sephirah Tiphareth and the path of the letter Resh (the Tarot trump The Sun), and stands as the very type of the harmonised Self. Its metal is gold, its day Sunday, its number six, its principal correspondences the lion, the rose, the heliotrope, and the figure of the dying-and-rising god.

Astronomically the Sun is the gravitational heart around which the system turns; symbolically it is the heart of the human being, the seat of the conscious, integrating self and of the Holy Guardian Angel in Thelemic doctrine. Solar gods—Ra, Helios, Apollo, Mithras, the risen Christ—everywhere embody illumination, kingship, and the triumph of light over the darkness of death.
tables: XXII. Small Selection of Hindu Deities
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

sunflower.summary: The solar flower that follows the sun—heliotrope of Leo and Sol, devotion turned wholly to the light.
sunflower.description: The Sunflower is attributed to Leo (Teth) and the Sun (Resh), and its very form and habit declare its lord: a golden disc ringed with flame-like petals that turns through the day to face the sun. It is the perfect emblem of devotion and of the soul's heliotropism—the will that orients itself wholly to its source. Esoterically the sunflower is the aspirant's adoration of the solar Self of Tiphareth, the creature that becomes an image of its god by ceaseless turning toward the light.

suphlatus.summary: Dust — the Nuctemeron genius of the fifth hour presiding over dust, set by Crowley at Leo.
suphlatus.description: Among the genii of the fifth hour in the Nuctemeron of Apollonius of Tyana, Suphlatus presides over dust. He presides over dust and the dry powder of the earth, the fine matter the wind carries. Lévi gives the roll of the hour-genii in his Transcendental Magic; Crowley tabulates them along the paths of the Tree (Table CLXXIII), assigning Suphlatus to Leo (Teth).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

surya.summary: Surya, the sun-god — the blazing eye of heaven, referred to Fire.
surya.description: Surya is the Hindu sun-god, the radiant deity who rides his chariot drawn by seven horses across the sky, the visible source of light, life, and truth. Referred to Shin and the element of Fire, he is the burning solar power, the eye of the heavens before whom darkness flees. Ancient and ever-worshipped, he is health, illumination, and the divine order made manifest in the daily course of the sun.
tables: XXII. Small Selection of Hindu Deities

susabo.summary: Voyages — the Nuctemeron genius of the sixth hour presiding over voyages, set by Crowley at Virgo.
susabo.description: Susabo is the Nuctemeron genius of voyages. That “Night-illumined Day”, ascribed to Apollonius of Tyana and handed down through Lévi's Transcendental Magic, sets a company of spirits over each of the twelve hours of the magical day, and Susabo belongs to the sixth hour. He governs journeys and the fortunes and hazards of travel. In 777 (Table CLXXIII) Crowley redistributes these hour-genii across the zodiac, where this spirit falls at Virgo (Yod).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

svadistthana.summary: Svadhisthana — the sacral chakra of the waters, attributed to Hod.
svadistthana.description: Svadhisthana, the 'own-abode' chakra at the sacrum, is the second wheel, seat of the element Water and of generation, desire, and the unconscious. Set in 777 at Hod, it governs the flowing, fluid life of sensation and procreation — the tidal, watery substratum just above the root.

swallow.summary: The swift messenger of Mercury—herald of spring and the returning soul, sacred to Isis.
swallow.description: The swallow is attributed to Mercury and the path of the Magus, and it is the swift, darting, far-travelling bird that heralds the spring and returns unfailingly to its old nest—an apt emblem of Mercurial speed, movement and message. In Egypt it was sacred to Isis, who took the swallow's form as she circled the pillar that held the body of Osiris, and so it became a bird of the searching, faithful, mourning-and-restoring soul. Quick on the wing and bound to the turning of the seasons, the swallow figures the soul as messenger and traveller. Esoterically it is the swift spirit that carries word between the worlds and the harbinger of renewal, the herald that announces the return of the light.

swan.summary: The bird of Kether and Venus—Hamsa of the sacred breath AUM, white emblem of purity, beauty and the Word.
swan.description: The swan is attributed to Kether and to Venus, the crown and the sphere of love, and it is among the loftiest of bird-symbols. In the Eastern lore that 777 weaves through its tables the swan is the Hamsa, whose call is the sacred syllable AUM and which is the vehicle of Brahma the creator—hence its place at the very crown of the Tree as an emblem of the first utterance and the breath of being. Under Venus it is pure white beauty, grace upon the water, and the bird of poets. Esoterically the swan unites the highest unity with the loveliness of form: the Word made beautiful, the soul that glides serene upon the waters of manifestation.

swastika.summary: The whirling solar wheel of Kether—the four-armed cross in rotation, the radiating motion of the creative force.
swastika.description: The Swastika is attributed to Kether, the Crown, and it is the ancient four-armed whirling cross—a universal solar and creative emblem found across the world's traditions long before its later misuse, signifying the turning wheel of becoming and the radiation of force from a central point. Its bent arms depict force in dynamic rotation, the original creative impulse of Kether spinning outward into manifestation along the four directions. As the highest of symbols it marks the very motion of the first emanation. Esoterically the Swastika is the whirling creative power of the Crown—the four-fold radiation of the primal force set in eternal motion, the wheel by which the still point at the summit pours its light spinning out into all the worlds.

swift.summary: The swiftness of the Arrow at Sagittarius—the quality of speed in aspiration, the will loosed without delay.
swift.description: 'Swift' is named among the weapons at Sagittarius as a quality of the Arrow that is the sign's emblem—the speed with which the well-aimed dart flies to its mark once loosed. Swiftness in the magical sense is not haste but the absence of delay between intention and act: the will, once resolved and aimed, released at once and travelling without hesitation to its goal. Under Sagittarius, the sign of soaring aspiration, this swiftness is the eager, unwavering rush of the spirit toward the divine. Esoterically swiftness is the virtue of an aspiration that does not falter or linger—the immediate, undelayed flight of the rightly-directed will, the quickness that carries the arrow of the soul straight and fast to the heaven it seeks.

swiftness.summary: Eight of Wands — Swiftness; Mercury in Sagittarius, Hod of Fire: the arrow loosed.
swiftness.description: The Eight of Wands, Swiftness, is Hod in the suit of Fire and the first decan of Sagittarius, ruled by Mercury. Here the fire of will is electrified and made luminous, flying like lightning or the loosed arrow toward its mark — energy at last become communication, message, and speed. Mercury in the Archer's sign gives the card its sense of rapid, even instantaneous, transmission of force.
tables: CXXXIII. Titles and Attributions of the Wand Suit

sword.summary: Zayin — 'sword' or 'weapon'; the blade of discrimination, path of The Lovers.
sword.description: Zayin means 'sword,' 'weapon,' or 'armament.' Its very shape suggests a hilted blade, and esoterically it is the instrument of cutting and division — the analytic edge that separates one thing from another. In Liber 777 Zayin is the path of The Lovers, attributed to Gemini, joining Binah to Tiphareth. Here the sword is the discrimination at the heart of every choice and union: the keen blade that divides the contraries so that they may be consciously rejoined, the weapon of the intellect drawn in the service of love.
tables: III. Translation of the Names of the Paths

sylphs.summary: The elementals of Air, set at Aleph — the airy spirits of wind and breath.
sylphs.description: The Sylphs are the elemental spirits of Air in the order of the legendary beings, attributed to Aleph, the path of the airy letter. In the Paracelsan doctrine of the four elementals they are the inhabitants of the air — swift, light, and volatile beings, the living intelligence of wind and breath, as natural to their element as birds are to the sky. Esoterically they answer to the realm of thought and the subtle currents the magician stirs in the element of Air.

symbol-of-mercury-with-downward-pointing.term: Symbol of Mercury with downward-pointing arrow under cross
symbol-of-mercury-with-downward-pointing.displayTerm: Symbol of Mercury with downward-pointing arrow under cross

syncope.summary: Syncope (fainting) at Teth and Leo — the momentary failing of the solar heart.
syncope.description: Syncope — fainting, the sudden loss of consciousness — is attributed to the path of Leo, the fixed fire sign that rules the heart and is governed by the Sun. The faint is a brief failure of the heart's solar power to sustain the brain, the life-light guttering for an instant; set under leonine Leo it is the lapse of the body's central, heart-borne vitality. Symbolically it is the momentary eclipse of the inner sun.

syphilis.summary: Syphilis at Daleth and Venus — the deep venereal corruption of the love-planet.
syphilis.description: Syphilis is attributed to Daleth, the path of Venus, the planet of the generative organs and of love. Like the other venereal afflictions it is read as a corruption of Venus — and as the gravest of them, a deep and systemic poisoning that follows upon the misdirection of the love-current. Esoterically it is the most cautionary of the Venusian shadows: the sweetness of generation turned to a pervasive and disfiguring disease.

syrian.summary: Syrian — a pantheon column Crowley reserved in 777 for future expansion, left unfilled.
syrian.description: Crowley's 'Syrian' column in the pantheon tables (XXV-XXXII) would have received the gods of the ancient Levant — Baal, El, Anat, Astarte, Hadad, the Phoenician and Ugaritic pantheons whose roots lie in the same Semitic soil as Hebrew Qabalah. The fit with the Tree would have been close (Baal/Hadad to Mars or Jupiter, Astarte to Venus, El to Kether, Anat to Geburah), but Crowley left the column blank — a marker of work he saw as needed but did not undertake. The entry preserves the placeholder.

syth.summary: Syth (Set), the adversary — the dark brother in his Cancerian attribution.
syth.description: Syth is a variant of Set, the god of chaos, storm, and the desert, here referred to Cheth and Cancer. The spelling preserves the older Greek “Seth,” by which he was sometimes identified with the monstrous Typhon. As the dark and turbulent brother who slays Osiris and contends with Horus, he is the principle of disruption and division — the shadow without which the drama of death and resurrection could not unfold.
tables: CLXX. Egyptian Names of the Succedent Decans

sz.summary: The 'Sz' sound-value — placed at Chokmah (the second Sephirah) in Crowley's English-equivalents column.
sz.description: 'Sz' (an unusual Latinisation, the sound also written 'sh' in English or sz/cs in some Slavic systems) is set at Chokmah, the supernal Sephirah of Wisdom and the explosive primal masculine force. In late Coptic the letter Ϣ (Shai) carried the 'sh' sound — a hissing breath that, in Hermetic-Qabalistic phonosymbolism, suits the lightning-bolt eruption of Chokmah from Kether. The entry records only the placement: Crowley fixes this letter's English transcription opposite the second Sephirah, completing the Coptic column at that rank.
tables: LI. English Equivalent of the Coptic Alphabet

taautus.summary: Taautus, the Phoenician Thoth — inventor of letters, at Gemini.
taautus.description: Taautus is the name given by the Phoenician historian Sanchuniathon to the god of writing, identified with the Egyptian Thoth and the Greek Hermes, here referred to Zayin and Gemini. As the inventor of the alphabet and of the arts of record, he is the divine scribe and culture-bringer. The Gemini attribution, sign of communication and the written word, fits this archetypal patron of letters and learning.
tables: CLXVII. Egyptian Gods of the Zodiac (Asc. Decans)

tablibik.summary: Fascination — the Nuctemeron genius of the fifth hour presiding over fascination, set by Crowley at Leo.
tablibik.description: In the Nuctemeron — the “Day Illumined by Night” ascribed to Apollonius of Tyana and preserved by Éliphas Lévi — Tablibik is numbered among the genii of the fifth hour, the spirit of fascination. He governs enchantment and the binding of the gaze, the spell that captivates and holds. Crowley arranges the twelve hours and their genii upon the paths of the Tree (777, Table CLXXIII), placing him at Leo (Teth).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

tabris.summary: Free will — the Nuctemeron genius of the sixth hour presiding over free will, set by Crowley at Virgo.
tabris.description: In the Nuctemeron — the “Day Illumined by Night” ascribed to Apollonius of Tyana and preserved by Éliphas Lévi — Tabris is numbered among the genii of the sixth hour, the spirit of free will. He presides over choice and the liberty of the will, the power to elect one's path. Crowley arranges the twelve hours and their genii upon the paths of the Tree (777, Table CLXXIII), placing him at Virgo (Yod).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

tacere.summary: 'To Keep Silent'—the earthy power of the Sphinx, the virtue of silence.
tacere.description: Tacere, 'to keep silent,' is attributed to Earth (32 bis), the earthy and culminating member of the Four Powers of the Sphinx—to Know, to Will, to Dare, and to Keep Silent. As the power of Earth it is the virtue of silence, the sealing of the work so that its force is not dissipated in speech. The bull-faced strength of the Sphinx, it is the discretion that contains and matures what has been known, willed, and dared; the magician who cannot keep silence loses all, for power spoken is power spilled.
tables: L. Transcendental Morality (10 Virtues; 7 Deadly Sins; 4 Magic Powers)

tacritau.summary: Goetic magic — the Nuctemeron genius of the fifth hour presiding over goetic magic, set by Crowley at Leo.
tacritau.description: Tacritau is the Nuctemeron genius of goetic magic. That “Night-illumined Day”, ascribed to Apollonius of Tyana and handed down through Lévi's Transcendental Magic, sets a company of spirits over each of the twelve hours of the magical day, and Tacritau belongs to the fifth hour. His province is goëtia, the sorcery that constrains the lower and earth-bound spirits. In 777 (Table CLXXIII) Crowley redistributes these hour-genii across the zodiac, where this spirit falls at Leo (Teth).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

tahoeloj.summary: Tahoeloj — Crowley's transliteration in table LVIII of the Supreme Elemental King of Air.
tahoeloj.description: Tahoeloj appears in Liber 777's table LVIII as the Supreme Elemental King attributed to path 11 (Aleph/Air). The spelling is one of several Enochian transliterations in use: Dee and Kelly's manuscripts give the King of Air variously as Bataivah or Bataiva, drawn from the Tablet of Union and the Great Table; Crowley's idiosyncratic rendering here (closer in shape to 'ta-hoe-loj') reflects either an alternate phonetic reading of the same name or, more likely, a transcription of a different Enochian title associated with the Airy quadrant. The entry preserves it as Crowley wrote it: a name of one of the great elemental rulers of the Watchtowers, invoked at the Airy path of the Tree.

tail-of-scorpio.summary: Tail of Scorpio — the English meaning of the eighteenth lunar mansion (Shaulah), at the sting of Scorpio.
tail-of-scorpio.description: 'Tail of Scorpio' is the English gloss of Shaulah (الشولة, 'the raised tail'), the eighteenth Arabic lunar mansion, marked by λ and υ Scorpii — the two bright stars at the very sting of the constellation. In traditional mansion-magic Shaulah carries one of the strongest malefic charges of the lunar zodiac, suited to the besieging of cities, the overthrowing of enemies, and curses; it is the mansion of the venomous strike. Crowley fixes it at the Samekh/Sagittarius path, where the bowman's arrow takes over from the scorpion's sting. See also: Shaulah (20°).
tables: CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon

talismans.summary: The watery art of charging an object to hold and radiate magical force.
talismans.description: Talismans, set at Mem and Water, are objects—metal, parchment, stone—charged by ritual to attract or store a desired influence. Water, the receptive and shaping element, governs the giving-of-form to fluid force, and so the consecration and 'wetting' of the talisman with charged life falls to it. Distinguished from the pantacle (a symbol of the whole) the talisman is made for a single purpose, a reservoir of directed power carried or placed where its work is needed.

tables: CL. Magical Images of the Decans (Succedent)

tarab.summary: Extortion — the Nuctemeron genius of the twelfth hour presiding over extortion, set by Crowley at Pisces.
tarab.description: Tarab is the Nuctemeron genius of extortion. That “Night-illumined Day”, ascribed to Apollonius of Tyana and handed down through Lévi's Transcendental Magic, sets a company of spirits over each of the twelve hours of the magical day, and Tarab belongs to the twelfth hour. He is the spirit of extortion and pillage, the wringing of gain by force and threat. In 777 (Table CLXXIII) Crowley redistributes these hour-genii across the zodiac, where this spirit falls at Pisces (Qoph).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

tarasni.summary: Angel of the first face of Libra, where opposing forces are balanced into peace.
tarasni.description: Tarasni rules the opening decan of Libra (0–10°), where the Moon meets the Two of Swords, *Peace* (Peace Restored) — tension held in living equilibrium. The Moon steadies airy Libra's scales so that contraries are reconciled rather than crushed. Tarasni is the angel of the truce in which balance is achieved without victory of one side over the other.

tarf.summary: al-Tarf, 'the glance' — the eye of the Lion, the lunar mansion in Cancer.
tarf.description: al-Tarf, 'the glance' or 'the eye of the Lion,' is the Mansion of the Moon set in the path of Cancer (Cheth). Read by the old astrologers as a station of siege and hindrance, of the casting down of enemies, its watchful, predatory gaze sits at the threshold where the watery Crab gives way to the solar Lion.
tables: CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon

tarpesheth.summary: Tarpesheth — an Egyptian name Crowley assigns to path 31 (Shin/Fire) in table XIX.
tarpesheth.description: Tarpesheth appears in 777's table XIX at path 31 (Shin/Fire). The name is not a standard Egyptological form; it may be Crowley's Hellenistic-Coptic transliteration of a fiery or solar theophoric, or a name drawn from the magical papyri whose precise source he did not cite. The entry preserves the spelling at the fiery path, where the more familiar fire-gods (Horus, the solar lions, the sekhem-flame) sit in the same column — the placement itself encodes the identification Crowley intended, even without an annotated etymology.

taste.summary: The sense classically borne by Water/Apas — the perception of savour.
taste.description: Taste is the sense traditionally attributed to Apas, the element of Water, in the Tattvic doctrine of the senses. Because savour is perceived only through moisture upon the tongue, taste is the faculty proper to the watery element — the receptive, dissolving sense that draws the quality of a thing into the body. It belongs to the realm of feeling and assimilation.

tau.summary: Tav — 'cross' or 'mark'; the Saturnine seal that completes the alphabet, path of The Universe.
tau.description: Tau (Tav) means 'mark,' 'sign,' or 'cross' — the last letter of the Hebrew alphabet, anciently written as a cross or an X, the seal set upon a thing to mark it as finished or chosen (as in Ezekiel's mark upon the foreheads of the faithful). In Liber 777 Tav is the path of The Universe (The World), attributed to Saturn (and Earth), joining Yesod to Malkuth. As the final letter and the cross of matter, it is the seal of completion: the mark that closes the alphabet, the Saturnine cross on which the manifest universe is fixed and made whole.
tables: III. Translation of the Names of the Paths

taurus.summary: Fixed Earth, ruled by Venus—stability, fertility, the steady force of growth.
taurus.description:
Taurus, the Bull, is fixed Earth ruled by Venus—the sign of stability, fertility, endurance, and the patient sensual enjoyment of the material world. In 777 it answers to the letter Vav and the path of the Tarot trump The Hierophant (path 16). It is the settled, productive force that consolidates what Aries begins, rooting energy in solid form.

The Bull is among the oldest of sacred animals—the Apis of Egypt, the bull of Mithras, the golden calf—everywhere an emblem of generative power and earthly abundance. Its virtues are steadfastness and loyalty; its shadow, stubbornness and possessiveness. Taurus teaches the magician the strength of the immovable and the sanctity of the body.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

taw.summary: Taw — a letter of the Coptic alphabet (t), which Crowley attributes to the path of Tav (Saturn).
taw.description: Taw is a letter of the Coptic alphabet — the script in which the Egyptian language was written in the Christian era, the Greek alphabet adapted to Egyptian speech. It is from Greek tau. Crowley folds the Coptic alphabet into the great correspondence of letters and paths in 777 (Table LI), assigning Taw to the path of Tav (Saturn) on the Tree of Life, so that the Egyptian-Christian script takes its station among the Hebrew letters and the keys of the Tarot.
tables: LI. Names of the Coptic Letters

tejas.summary: The active, expansive element of heat, will, and transformation.
tejas.description:
Fire is the element of energy, will, and transformation—hot and dry in the classical scheme, expansive and ascending by nature. In Liber 777 it is attributed to the Hebrew letter Shin and the path 31, to the Tatwa Tejas (a red triangle), and to the southern quarter. Its magical weapon is the Wand, its archangel Michael, its elemental king Djin, and its creatures the salamanders.

Across cultures Fire is the agent of purification and divine presence—the burning bush, the Promethean spark, the sacrificial flame that carries offerings upward. Psychologically it maps to drive, courage, and the spirited part of the soul; physically, to combustion and the radiant energy that powers life. In the magician’s work it represents the directed will that initiates change.
tables: XXII. Small Selection of Hindu Deities
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

temperence.summary: The fourteenth Trump (Samekh): Temperance, the tempering art of combination.
temperence.description: Temperance (here spelled ‘Temperence,’ Crowley's Art) is Atu XIV, attributed in Liber 777 to the path of Samekh (Sagittarius) joining Tiphareth to Yesod. The figure mingles and pours the streams of opposing natures—fire and water, the volatile and the fixed—reconciling contraries in a single vessel. As the Daughter of the Reconcilers and the Bringer Forth of Life, the trump is the great alchemical work of tempering: the arrow of aspiration loosed from earth toward heaven, the elixir distilled from the marriage of opposites.
tables: XIV. General Attribution of the Tarot

tendency.summary: The shaping tendencies — a rendering of saṅkhāra, the dispositional formations of the fourth skandha.
tendency.description: Tendency renders the dispositional aspect of saṅkhāra, the fourth skandha, attributed to the element Air. It names the accumulated bent of the mind — the habits, inclinations and latent drives that, formed by past intention, slant present experience and condition future action. As a facet of the formations-aggregate it underscores that what we call character is itself a compounded, impermanent process: a momentum of habit rather than a fixed self, alterable by the very practice that observes it.

tentative-one.summary: The Twenty-fifth Path, named again — the Tentative Intelligence of Samekh, the testing arrow of Art.
tentative-one.description: 'Tentative Intelligence' (Sekhel Nisyoni) is the companion rendering of the Twenty-fifth Path of Samekh (Sagittarius), whose other name is the Intelligence of Probation. The word names the trial directly: this is the testing, proving, tempting Intelligence by which the righteous are assayed. On the path of Temperance and Art — the alchemical mingling that aims the arrow of aspiration from Tiphareth to Yesod — every advance is a probation, a tentative reaching that must be confirmed by ordeal.
tables: XIII. Paths of the Sefer Yetzirah

tepisatras.summary: Name of the last decan of Aquarius, the lunar face of futile, vacillating effort.
tepisatras.description: Tepisatras is 777's name for the last decan of Aquarius (20°–30°). The Moon rules this face and it bears the Seven of Swords—Futility—effort undone by vacillation, the over-clever plan that comes to nothing. Among the thirty-six decan-faces it marks the unstable close of the Water-Bearer's sign before the dissolution of Pisces.
tables: CLXXII. Egyptian Names of the Cadent Decans

tepiseuth.summary: Name of the second decan of Scorpio, the same solar face of regenerative joy.
tepiseuth.description: Tepiseuth is the name 777 keeps for the second decan of Scorpio (10°–20°), the solar face the gods-column calls Merota. Bearing the Six of Cups—Pleasure—it names the deep regenerative joy at the centre of the Scorpion's sign. Like its fellows it descends from the Egyptian decans, the ten-degree watches of the night sky.
tables: CLXX. Egyptian Names of the Succedent Decans

tepistosoa.summary: Name of the final decan of Gemini, where over-extended intellect reaches ruin.
tepistosoa.description: Tepistosoa governs the final decan of Gemini (20°–30°), where mutable air reaches its breaking-point. The Sun rules this face and its card is the Ten of Swords—Ruin—the total collapse of an over-extended intellect, the end of a cycle of thought. Among the Hermetic decan-faces it stands at the close of the Twins, before the wheel descends into the waters of Cancer.
tables: CLXXII. Egyptian Names of the Cadent Decans

terminus.summary: Terminus, god of boundaries — the divine landmark that fixes every border, at the Foundation.
terminus.description: Terminus is the Roman god of boundary-markers, the sacred stones that fixed the limits of fields and territories, so holy that not even Jupiter could displace him. Referred to Gimel, Yesod, and Tav — the foundations and the bound of Saturn — he embodies the principle of limit, demarcation, and the inviolability of established bounds. As the god of the boundary-stone he is the very spirit of definition and the respect for limits.

tables: CXVI. Egyptial Attribution of Parts of the Soul
XLVII. Kings and Princes of the Jinn

th.summary: The 'Th' (theta) sound-value — Crowley's English equivalent at the path of Teth (Leo).
th.description: 'Th' is the Latin transcription of the Coptic Ⲑ (theta, θ), which Crowley fixes at path 19 — Teth, the serpent-letter ruling Leo and the Tarot Lust/Strength. The match is exact at the level of sound: Hebrew Teth (ט), Greek theta (θ), and English 'th' share the soft fricative-stop family. Phonosymbolically the sound is the breath of the serpent — the slow, sustained, hissed sibilant Crowley associated with the snake-power of kundalini in Yoga and the leonine ecstasy of Liber Tisharb. The entry preserves only the placement.
tables: LI. English Equivalent of the Coptic Alphabet

th-plane-left-pillar.summary: Fourth plane, Left Pillar — the geometric position of Hod, the sphere of intellect and Mercury.
th-plane-left-pillar.description: The fourth plane on the Left (Severity) Pillar is Hod — the eighth Sephirah, ruled by Mercury, the sphere of intellect, language, magick, and clear form. Geometrically it sits beneath Geburah and across from Netzach, balancing the heart's instinct with the mind's analysis at the astral plane of the Tree. In Crowley's 'Position on the Glyph' this slot anchors the lower mind on the structural pillar, where thought, name, and ordered ritual take their place.
tables: XII. Position on the Glyph of the Tree of Life

th-plane-middle-pillar.summary: Fourth plane, Middle Pillar — the central column's lower stations: Tiphareth, Yesod, and Malkuth.
th-plane-middle-pillar.description: On the Middle Pillar — the central column of equilibrium — three Sephiroth descend below Kether: Tiphareth (the heart-sun at the ethical/astral hinge), Yesod (the lunar foundation at the astral), and Malkuth (the earthly kingdom at the material). Crowley's table XII groups these middle-pillar stations as the Tree's spine, the axis along which mediation, balance, and incarnation occur. The slug here collapses multiple plane-rows of the table because Crowley's column repeats the descriptor at each middle-pillar Sephirah; the entry holds for them all as a structural definition of the Tree's central axis.
tables: XII. Position on the Glyph of the Tree of Life

th-plane-right-pillar.summary: Fourth plane, Right Pillar — the geometric position of Netzach, Venusian victory and feeling.
th-plane-right-pillar.description: The fourth plane on the Right (Mercy) Pillar is Netzach — the seventh Sephirah, ruled by Venus, the sphere of feeling, desire, art, and natural sympathy. Geometrically it sits beneath Chesed and across from Hod, balancing reason with passion at the astral plane of the Tree. In Crowley's geometric table this position fixes Netzach as the affective counterpart to Hod's intellect, the bright pulse of love and instinct under the merciful pillar.
tables: XII. Position on the Glyph of the Tree of Life

thagrinus.summary: Confusion — the Nuctemeron genius of the fourth hour presiding over confusion, set by Crowley at Cancer.
thagrinus.description: In the Nuctemeron — the “Day Illumined by Night” ascribed to Apollonius of Tyana and preserved by Éliphas Lévi — Thagrinus is numbered among the genii of the fourth hour, the spirit of confusion. He sows bewilderment and disorder, the muddling and clouding of the mind. Crowley arranges the twelve hours and their genii upon the paths of the Tree (777, Table CLXXIII), placing him at Cancer (Cheth).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

thahaaothahe.summary: Thahaaothahe — Crowley's transliteration in table LVIII of the Supreme Elemental King of Earth.
thahaaothahe.description: Thahaaothahe is the form Crowley sets at position 32bis (Earth) in table LVIII, the Supreme Elemental King of the Earthy quadrant. The Dee/Kelly tradition typically gives the Earthy King as Iczhhcal or Iczhihal; Crowley's longer, more vowel-laden 'Thahaaothahe' is an alternative rendering whose precise source manuscript is debated.
