The entry preserves Crowley's spelling as a glossary fact: this is the angelic king he names at the Earthy crown of the Watchtower system in 777's mapping.

thahebyobeaatan.summary: Thahebyobeaatan — Crowley's transliteration in table LVIII of the Supreme Elemental King of Fire.
thahebyobeaatan.description: Thahebyobeaatan is the form Crowley gives in table LVIII for the Supreme Elemental King attributed to path 31 (Shin/Fire). As with the other Enochian Kings, the standard Dee/Kelly form (commonly Edlprnaa for Fire) differs from Crowley's rendering — 777 is famously eclectic in its transliterations, drawing variously on the Cipher Manuscripts, Mathers's Golden Dawn material, and Crowley's own ear. Whatever the source, the entry records the name as it stands in 777: an angelic king of the fiery quadrant of the Watchtowers, called at the path of Shin.

thanatos.summary: Thanatos, the personification of death — the gentle and inexorable end, at Scorpio.
thanatos.description: Thanatos is the Greek personification of death itself, the winged daemon who comes to carry mortals to the underworld, twin brother of Hypnos (Sleep). Referred to Nun and Scorpio, the sign of death and transformation, he is death not as judge or king but as the simple, inevitable fact — the quiet closing of every life. He embodies mortality as a natural law, neither cruel nor merciful, but certain.

the-4-aces.summary: The four Aces, attributed to Kether—the roots of the powers of the elements.
the-4-aces.description: The four Aces are attributed in Liber 777 to Kether, the Crown, the first and highest Sephirah. As Kether is the seed of the whole Tree, so each Ace is the root and origin of its suit—the Root of the Powers of Fire, Water, Air, and Earth. They are the elements in their first, undifferentiated purity, the spark of the divine from which all the numbered cards unfold. The Aces are the gifts of the Crown distributed into the four worlds.
tables: XIV. General Attribution of the Tarot

the-4-eights.summary: The four Eights, attributed to Hod—the rationalised, ordered force of each suit.
the-4-eights.description: The four Eights are attributed in Liber 777 to Hod, Splendour, the eighth Sephirah and the sphere of Mercury. Hod is the principle of intellect, language, and analytical order, the counterpoise to Venusian Netzach. The Eights express the ordering and rationalising of each element's force—swiftness, prudence, interference, and abandoned success. They are the energies of nature brought under the measuring, classifying mind, for good or ill, the splendour and the limitation of pure reason.
tables: XIV. General Attribution of the Tarot

the-4-fives.summary: The four Fives, attributed to Geburah—the strife and severity of each suit.
the-4-fives.description: The four Fives are attributed in Liber 777 to Geburah, Severity, the fifth Sephirah and the sphere of Mars. Geburah is the principle of strength, judgement, and necessary destruction, the breaking of the settled order of Chesed. The Fives express this disruption in each suit—strife, loss, defeat, and worry—the shock by which complacency is broken and energy renewed. They are the cosmic surgery of severity, painful but purgative, that clears the way for new equilibrium.
tables: XIV. General Attribution of the Tarot

the-4-fours.summary: The four Fours, attributed to Chesed—the established order of each suit.
the-4-fours.description: The four Fours are attributed in Liber 777 to Chesed, Mercy, the fourth Sephirah and the sphere of Jupiter. Chesed is the principle of stable, benevolent order, the first Sephirah below the Abyss where the formative ideas take settled shape. The Fours express this consolidation in each suit—rule, foundation, and lawful abundance. They are the calm, established condition that follows the formation of the Threes, the merciful order in which each element is given a secure throne.
tables: XIV. General Attribution of the Tarot

the-4-nines.summary: The four Nines, attributed to Yesod—the consolidated foundation of each suit.
the-4-nines.description: The four Nines are attributed in Liber 777 to Yesod, the Foundation, the ninth Sephirah and the sphere of the Moon. Yesod is the treasure-house of images, the astral foundation upon which the material world rests, where all the higher energies gather before their final descent. The Nines express this consolidation and fullness in each suit—strength, happiness, cruelty, and gain—the powers of each element brought to their most concentrated and stable expression just above manifestation.
tables: XIV. General Attribution of the Tarot

the-4-sevens.summary: The four Sevens, attributed to Netzach—the unstable striving of each suit.
the-4-sevens.description: The four Sevens are attributed in Liber 777 to Netzach, Victory, the seventh Sephirah and the sphere of Venus. Netzach is the principle of desire, feeling, and instinctual force, the first Sephirah of the lower, personal triad. The Sevens express the unstable, often troubled striving of each element away from the balance of Tiphareth—valour, debauch, futility, and unstable effort. They are the energies of nature in their restless, emotional, only partly mastered condition.
tables: XIV. General Attribution of the Tarot

the-4-sixes-emperor.summary: The four Sixes (and the solar trump), attributed to Tiphareth—the harmonised heart of each suit.
the-4-sixes-emperor.description: ‘The 4 Sixes – Emperor’ are attributed in Liber 777 to Tiphareth, Beauty, the sixth Sephirah and the radiant solar centre of the Tree. The Sixes express harmony, success, and balanced beauty in each suit—the reconciliation of the strife of the Fives in a centre of equilibrium. Tiphareth is the place of the sacrificed-and-risen god and of the Princes of the court; the Sixes are its gift of harmonised power, the heart in which the energies of each element find their poised and beautiful midpoint.
tables: XIV. General Attribution of the Tarot

the-4-tens-empresses.summary: The four Tens (and Princesses), attributed to Malkuth—the manifest fruition of each suit.
the-4-tens-empresses.description: ‘The 4 Tens – Empresses’ are attributed in Liber 777 to Malkuth, the Kingdom, the tenth Sephirah and the throne of the material world. The Tens express the full and final manifestation of each element in matter—oppression, satiety, ruin, and wealth—the energy of the suit come at last to earth, for better or worse. The Princesses (here ‘Empresses’) are likewise seated at Malkuth as the earthy daughters of the court. Together they mark the completion of the descent, the powers of the elements made solid and real.
tables: XIV. General Attribution of the Tarot

the-4-threes-queens.summary: The four Threes (and Queens), attributed to Binah—the formative mother of each suit.
the-4-threes-queens.description: ‘The 4 Threes – Queens’ are attributed in Liber 777 to Binah, Understanding, the third Sephirah and the great formative Mother. The Threes give form and stability to the raw force of the Twos, the first crystallisation of each element into pattern. The Queens are seated here as the receptive, nurturing thrones of the court. Together they embody Binah's principle of formation and womb-like containment, shaping the will of Chokmah into the enduring structures of each suit.
tables: XIV. General Attribution of the Tarot

the-4-twos-kings.summary: The four Twos (and Kings), attributed to Chokmah—the first active force of each suit.
the-4-twos-kings.description: ‘The 4 Twos – Kings’ are attributed in Liber 777 to Chokmah, Wisdom, the second Sephirah and the first outflowing of force. The Twos express the pure, dynamic will of each element before it has met resistance—Chokmah's masculine, initiating energy. The Kings (the Knights of the Thoth deck) are likewise seated here as the fiery, active heads of the court. Together they embody the principle of dynamic beginning, the creative thrust of Wisdom radiating into each of the four suits.
tables: XIV. General Attribution of the Tarot

the-aeon.summary: Atu XX — Shin / Fire & Spirit; rebirth, the new age, and the call to higher life.
the-aeon.description: The Aeon (the older Judgement) is trump XX, attributed to Shin and the element Fire (with Spirit), the path from Hod to Malkuth. Crowley renamed and remade it to proclaim the New Aeon of Horus: in place of a Christian Last Judgement, the card shows Nuit, Hadit, and the crowned-and-conquering child Heru-Ra-Ha presiding over a cosmic rebirth. It is the trump of awakening to a new order of consciousness, the fiery call that resurrects the self into a higher life. The Aeon teaches that an age has turned, and that the individual is summoned to live by a new and self-determined law.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

the-altar.summary: The altar at Yesod—the foundation on which the work is laid, the base of the temple's mysteries.
the-altar.description: The Altar appears again among the weapons at Yesod, the foundational sphere of the Tree, and the attribution deepens its meaning: Yesod is the very principle of foundation, and the altar is the foundation made into a sacred object. It is the steady base upon which every implement is placed and every offering made, the still support beneath the moving work. As Yesod underpins the manifest Malkuth, so the altar underpins the rite. Esoterically the Altar at Yesod is the established ground of the operation, the firm psychic and astral foundation the magician builds before any higher working can be raised upon it—the base that must be sure before the spirit is invoked.

the-angel.summary: An old title of Judgement (Shin): the Angel, sounding the trumpet of resurrection.
the-angel.description: ‘The Angel’ is an older title of Atu XX, Judgement—Crowley's Aeon—attributed in Liber 777 to the path of Shin (Fire). The angel is Israfel (or Gabriel) blowing the last trumpet, at whose blast the dead rise from their tombs. As the Spirit of the Primal Fire, the trump is the great awakening and resurrection: the searing call of Shin that ends the old aeon and summons all things into new and higher life.
tables: XIV. General Attribution of the Tarot

the-animal-soul.summary: The Animal Soul — the instinctive nature, Nephesch, attributed to Malkuth.
the-animal-soul.description: 'The Animal Soul' renders the Nephesch, the lowest part of the soul — the seat of instinct, appetite, and the unconscious vital functions, set at Malkuth. It is the bodily, animal nature shared with all living things, the foundation upon which the higher faculties rest and which they must govern and refine.
tables: XCVIII. Parts of the Soul English

the-arms.summary: The two arms of the Perfected Man—Mercy and Severity, the right and left hands of the Tree.
the-arms.description: The Arms are attributed to Chesed and Geburah, the fourth and fifth Sephiroth that form the shoulders of the Tree's two outer pillars. The right arm is Chesed, the open hand of mercy and giving; the left is Geburah, the clenched fist of severity and restraint. In the body of Adam Kadmon they are the limbs of action through which the divine reaches into the world—the one to bestow and the other to withhold, their balance the very rhythm of creation and judgment.

the-arrow.summary: The Arrow of Sagittarius—aspiration shot toward the divine, the straight path of the upward will.
the-arrow.description: The Arrow is the weapon of Sagittarius (the path of Samekh), whose very glyph is the arrow drawn and aimed at heaven, and it is the perfect emblem of that sign's soaring aspiration. Samekh is the path of Temperance, the tempering and direction of force, and the arrow is force given a single straight aim—'the straight line is the shortest distance between two points,' the undeviating flight of the will toward its goal. To loose the arrow is to commit wholly to the upward path. Esoterically the Arrow of Sagittarius is the disciplined aspiration that pierces upward through the middle pillar, the concentrated and rightly-aimed will that flies true toward the divine target without wavering or turning aside.

the-back.summary: The back, attributed to Leo, the spine that bears and dignifies the upright body.
the-back.description: The Back is attributed to Teth and Leo in this table. In medical astrology Leo rules the back and the spine—the central column of the skeleton, the proud upright axis that bears the body and carries the great nerve-trunk. As Leo is the royal, solar sign of dignity and the heart, so the back is the noble pillar of the frame, the strong support whose health underlies the bearing and vigour of the whole.

the-belly.summary: The belly of the Perfected Man, the watery depths of digestion and inward transformation.
the-belly.description: The Belly is attributed to Mem and Nun, Water and Scorpio, in the body of Adam Kadmon. As the abdomen is the dark interior where food is dissolved and transformed, it answers to the watery, Scorpionic mysteries of putrefaction and regeneration—the alchemical vessel within the body where gross matter is broken down and made over. It is the seat of the deep, instinctual processes that sustain life from below the threshold of awareness.

the-body.summary: Mindfulness of the body (kāyagatāsati) — contemplation of the body's parts as impersonal and impermanent.
the-body.description: The Body renders kāyagatāsati, mindfulness directed to the body among the Forty Meditations, attributed to the lower Sephiroth of the foundation. The practitioner reviews the body part by part and constituent by constituent — hair, nails, teeth, skin, flesh, bone, the inner organs and fluids — seeing it as a compound of impersonal, perishable elements rather than a lovely or enduring 'self'. The meditation steadies attention, cools sensual craving, and grounds awareness in the immediate fact of embodiment; it is the somatic counterpart to the cemetery contemplations, working not on the corpse but on the living frame.

the-bones.summary: The bones of the Perfected Man, the earthy skeleton that frames and upholds the body.
the-bones.description: The Bones are attributed to Earth (32 bis) in the body of Adam Kadmon. As the skeleton is the firm, enduring framework upon which all the softer tissues are hung, it answers to the densest and most stable element—the structural ground of the whole organism. In the symbolic body the bones are the fixed architecture of the Tree made flesh, the rigid scaffold of Earth that gives the descending divine influence a lasting form to inhabit.

the-bread.summary: The sustenance of the Hermit at Virgo—the consecrated bread of the harvest, the food borne on the solitary path.
the-bread.description: The Bread is named among the weapons at Virgo, the sign of the Hermit and of the wheat-bearing Virgin, and it is the consecrated food of the work—the simple sustaining substance carried by the solitary seeker and offered as a sacrament of the harvest. Virgo is the sign of the ripened grain and of patient service, and the bread is its fruit: the nourishment won by labour and made holy. As the Hermit walks his lonely road he bears this plain bread, the food that sustains the body so that the spirit may continue. Esoterically the Bread at Virgo is the humble, hard-won nourishment of the solitary path—the consecrated sustenance of the harvest that feeds the worker, the everyday food of life raised into a sacrament of patient, purified service.

the-breast.summary: The breast of the Perfected Man, the solar heart-region of the Tree.
the-breast.description: The Breast is attributed to the airy, leonine, and solar centre—Aleph, Leo, and Tiphareth—the heart of the body of Adam Kadmon. As the chest houses the heart and lungs, so this region of the Perfected Man corresponds to Tiphareth, the harmonising sixth Sephirah and the seat of the indwelling solar self. It is the place of breath and of feeling, where the radiant central fire of the organism, the beauty of the reconciled god, beats at the very middle of the Tree.

the-breezes-the-king-of-the-spirits-of-a.term: the Breezes. The King of the Spirits of Air. 20° ♉ to 20° ♊
the-breezes-the-king-of-the-spirits-of-a.displayTerm: the Breezes. The King of the Spirits of Air. 20° ♉ to 20° ♊
the-breezes-the-king-of-the-spirits-of-a.summary: Golden Dawn title and dominion of the King/Knight of Swords, ruling 20° Taurus–20° Gemini.
the-breezes-the-king-of-the-spirits-of-a.description: ‘the Breezes. The King of the Spirits of Air. 20° ♉ to 20° ♊’ is the Golden Dawn (Book T) title and celestial dominion of the King of Swords (the Knight in the Thoth deck), the active, fiery head of the airy suit. His full style is ‘Lord of the Winds and the Breezes, King of the Spirits of Air,’ and his rule spans the thirty degrees from Taurus into Gemini. He embodies air in violent motion—the storm-wind of intellect and force, the warrior whose thought cuts and sweeps like the gale.
tables: LXIII. The Court Cards of the Tarot, with the Spheres of their Celestial Dominion Swords.

the-bringer-forth-of-life.summary: Part of Temperance/Art's title (Samekh): the Bringer Forth of Life—the fruitful union of opposites.
the-bringer-forth-of-life.description: ‘The Bringer Forth of Life’ completes the Golden Dawn title of Atu XIV, Temperance/Art (path of Samekh, Sagittarius): ‘The Daughter of the Reconcilers; The Bringer Forth of Life.’ The figure pours and mingles the streams of opposing natures, and from their reconciliation new life is generated—the elixir, the arrow loosed toward the sun. The title celebrates the creative fertility of right combination: it is by the marriage of contraries, tempered in the one cauldron, that the living spirit is brought forth.

the-burin.summary: The engraver's graver at Aries—the tool that inscribes the names and figures, will cut into matter.
the-burin.description: The Burin is attributed to Aries (the path of Heh, the Emperor), and it is the engraving tool—the sharp graver with which the magician cuts the divine names, sigils and figures into the substance of his implements, fixing the invisible will into visible, enduring form. Its place at the initiating fire of Aries is fitting, for engraving is an act of forceful, decisive impression, the imposing of design upon resistant matter. To wield the burin is to make one's intention permanent and manifest. Esoterically the Burin is the instrument by which the magician inscribes his will upon the world—the decisive, ruling power of the Emperor that cuts thought into form, fixing the fluid idea into a lasting and operative sign.

the-buttocks.summary: The buttocks of the Perfected Man, the earthy base of the seated body.
the-buttocks.description: The Buttocks are attributed to Malkuth and Capricorn in the body of Adam Kadmon—the lowest, most material region of the trunk. As the seat on which the body rests, they correspond to the earthy, saturnine foundation of physical stability, the dense base where the descending influence of the Tree comes finally to rest upon the ground. They mark the meeting of the structured body with the solidity of the Kingdom.

the-censer.summary: The thurible of Aquarius—the vessel of incense, purification and prayer rising as fragrant smoke.
the-censer.description: The Censer is attributed to Aquarius, and it is the swinging vessel in which incense is burned—the implement of purification by fire and fragrant smoke, paired with the Aspergillus that purifies by water. As the coals consume the incense, the rising smoke cleanses the temple, carries the operator's prayer aloft, and conditions the atmosphere of the working with the appropriate suffumigation. Its place at the airy, humane sign of Aquarius befits the upward-streaming, aspiring nature of the smoke. Esoterically the Censer is the instrument of purification and aspiration by fire—the means by which the magician hallows the field of the Work and sends his intention rising heavenward, the fragrant smoke that bears the prayer of the heart up toward the powers invoked.

the-chariot.summary: Atu VII — Cheth / Cancer; the Grail-bearing victor, will held in armoured control.
the-chariot.description: The Chariot is trump VII, attributed to Cheth and Cancer, the path from Binah to Geburah. It is the figure of triumphant, disciplined will—the armoured charioteer who masters opposing forces (the black and white sphinxes) and bears the Holy Grail through the world. Cancer’s protective shell becomes the warrior’s armour; the soft, lunar interior guards a sacred charge. The Chariot teaches victory through self-command and the carrying of the inmost light safely across hostile terrain. In the Thoth deck the charioteer cradles the Grail like a sacrament.
tables: XIV. General Attribution of the Tarot
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

the-child-of-the-forces-of-time.term: The Child of the Forces of Time
the-child-of-the-forces-of-time.displayTerm: The Child of the Forces of Time
the-child-of-the-forces-of-time.summary: Part of the Devil's title (Ayin): the Child of the Forces of Time—generation bound in matter.
the-child-of-the-forces-of-time.description: ‘The Child of the Forces of Time’ completes the Golden Dawn title of Atu XV, the Devil (path of Ayin, Capricorn): ‘The Lord of the Gates of Matter; The Child of the Forces of Time.’ Capricorn is ruled by Saturn, lord of time and limitation, and the trump is the offspring of those temporal, material forces—desire and generation imprisoned within the conditions of the manifest world. Far from mere evil, the figure represents the creative, mirthful, goat-footed power of Nature laughing in her chains, the eye (Ayin) that sees and the lust that drives the wheel of incarnate life.

the-child-of-the-great-transformers.term: The Child of the Great Transformers
the-child-of-the-great-transformers.displayTerm: The Child of the Great Transformers
the-child-of-the-great-transformers.summary: Part of Death's title (Nun): the Child of the Great Transformers—offspring of the powers of change.
the-child-of-the-great-transformers.description: ‘The Child of the Great Transformers’ is part of the Golden Dawn title of Atu XIII, Death, on the path of Nun (Scorpio) joining Tiphareth to Netzach; the full style is ‘The Child of the Great Transformers; The Lord of the Gate of Death.’ Scorpio is the sign of death and regeneration, and the trump is transformation itself—the skeleton-reaper whose scythe-handle is a Tau, mowing only that life may spring anew. As *child of the great transformers* it is the issue of the higher powers of metamorphosis, the necessary agent by which all forms are dissolved and recombined.

the-child-of-the-powers-of-the-waters-th.term: The Child of the Powers of the Waters: The Lord of the Triumph of Light
the-child-of-the-powers-of-the-waters-th.displayTerm: The Child of the Powers of the Waters: The Lord of the Triumph of Light
the-child-of-the-powers-of-the-waters-th.summary: The esoteric title of the Chariot (Cheth): Child of the Powers of the Waters, Lord of the Triumph of Light.
the-child-of-the-powers-of-the-waters-th.description: ‘The Child of the Powers of the Waters: The Lord of the Triumph of Light’ is the Golden Dawn title of Atu VII, the Chariot, on the path of Cheth (Cancer) joining Binah to Geburah. Cancer is a water sign, and the charioteer—armoured, enthroned beneath a starry canopy—is the soul borne upon the great deep yet triumphant over it, bearing the Holy Grail. The title fuses opposites: he is *child of the waters* (the receptive, lunar element) and yet *lord of the triumph of light*, the disciplined will that carries the secret fire safely through the flood. The Chariot is the vehicle of the conquering self.

the-child-of-the-sons-of-the-mighty.term: The Child of the Sons of the Mighty
the-child-of-the-sons-of-the-mighty.displayTerm: The Child of the Sons of the Mighty
the-child-of-the-sons-of-the-mighty.summary: Part of the Moon's title (Qoph): the Child of the Sons of the Mighty—offspring of the deep powers.
the-child-of-the-sons-of-the-mighty.description: ‘The Child of the Sons of the Mighty’ completes the Golden Dawn title of Atu XVIII, the Moon (path of Qoph, Pisces): ‘The Ruler of Flux and Reflux; The Child of the Sons of the Mighty.’ The phrase places the lunar trump in a lineage of power—the descendant of high and ancient forces, inheriting their authority over the tidal realm of the unconscious. Qoph governs the back of the head and the most primitive strata of mind; the Moon is the dim, atavistic light by which the soul threads the path between the towers and the howling dogs toward the dawn.

the-children-of-the-voice-the-oracle-of-.term: The Children of the Voice: The Oracle of the Mighty Gods
the-children-of-the-voice-the-oracle-of-.displayTerm: The Children of the Voice: The Oracle of the Mighty Gods
the-children-of-the-voice-the-oracle-of-.summary: The esoteric title of the Lovers (Zayin): the Children of the Voice, the Oracle of the Mighty Gods.
the-children-of-the-voice-the-oracle-of-.description: ‘The Children of the Voice: The Oracle of the Mighty Gods’ is the Golden Dawn title of Atu VI, the Lovers, on the path of Zayin (Gemini) joining Binah to Tiphareth. Gemini is the sign of the twins, of duality and discrimination, and the trump turns on choice, analysis, and the union of opposites under inspiration. The title frames the card as an *oracle*: the place where the divided self, hearing the Voice, must discern and decide, and where the marriage of contraries (king and queen, fire and water) is consummated under the eye of the gods. It is the sword of intellect that both cleaves and weds.

the-circle.summary: The circle of the Veils — the symbol of the unmanifest infinite, the zero before all.
the-circle.description: The Circle is attributed to the Veils of the Negative — Ain, Ain Soph, Ain Soph Aur — that lie above Kether. As the figure that has no beginning and no end, no angle and no side, returning forever into itself, the circle is the natural emblem of the infinite and the unmanifest: the zero from which the point of Kether emerges, the boundless 'nothing' that contains all things in potential. It is the serpent that swallows its own tail, eternity before extension.
tables: XLIX. Lineal Figures of the Planets, &c., and Geomany

the-cross-of-equilibrium.summary: The equal-armed cross of Libra—the balance of the elements in perfect equipoise, the geometry of justice.
the-cross-of-equilibrium.description: The Cross of Equilibrium is attributed to Libra (the path of Lamed, Adjustment), and it is the equal-armed cross—the four arms of identical length signifying the four elements held in perfect balance, none preponderating, the still point where all forces are reconciled. Where the Cross of Suffering is the gibbet of sacrifice, this cross is the figure of poise and justice, the equilibrium that is Libra's whole concern. As the balanced cross it is the emblem of the harmonised self and the just measure that gives each force its due. Esoterically the Cross of Equilibrium is the principle of balance made into a working figure—the perfect equipoise of the elements within the magician, the achieved justice and centredness from which alone right action can proceed, the still cross at the heart of the scales.

the-crown.summary: The diadem of the Scorpion — the meaning of the lunar mansion al-Iklil.
the-crown.description: 'The Crown' renders al-Iklil, the seventeenth Mansion of the Moon, the bright circlet of stars upon the brow of Scorpio, set in 777 in the path of Libra (Lamed). As a crown it signifies sovereignty conferred and oaths bound; the Arab astrologers counted it strong for the establishing of love, of dominion, and of works that must endure.
tables: CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon

the-cup.summary: The magical weapon of Water—the vessel of receptivity and understanding, the Graal of Binah.
the-cup.description: The Cup is the elemental weapon of Water, attributed to the watery letter Mem, to Cancer, and to Binah the supernal Mother, and it is the implement of receptivity, love and understanding. Where the Wand projects, the Cup receives; it is the held vessel into which the influence of the higher is gathered and in which it is treasured, the chalice of the heart and of the Great Sea of Binah. As the Holy Graal it is the cup of the spirit's blood, the vessel of redemption. In the magician's hand the Cup is the trained capacity to contain and to feel without spilling, the disciplined emotional nature. Esoterically it is the supernal Understanding made an implement—the soul shaped into a vessel pure and deep enough to hold the descending light.

the-dagger.summary: The elemental weapon of Air at Aleph—the swift blade of the intellect that cuts and divides the airy realm.
the-dagger.description: The Dagger is the elemental weapon of Air, attributed to Aleph, the path of the Fool and the breath of spirit, and it is the smaller, swifter kin of the Sword: the air-dagger that cuts, divides and analyses, the keen edge of the intellect in its quickness. Where the Sword belongs to the severity of Geburah, the dagger is the nimble blade of thought itself, the implement of discrimination and of the banishing that clears the air. Its place at Aleph marks it as the cutting power born of the first breath. Esoterically the Dagger is the magician's swift discriminating mind—the keen, mobile intellect that divides the true from the false and clears the working-space of all that clouds it, the bright edge of thought wielded in the element of air.

the-daughter-of-the-firmament.summary: Part of the Star's title (Tzaddi): the Daughter of the Firmament—the starry hope of the heavens.
the-daughter-of-the-firmament.description: ‘The Daughter of the Firmament’ is part of the Golden Dawn title of Atu XVII, the Star, on the path of Tzaddi (Aquarius) joining Netzach to Yesod; the full style is ‘The Daughter of the Firmament; The Dweller Between the Waters.’ Aquarius is the water-bearer, and the trump shows the naked goddess pouring the waters of life beneath a great star. As *daughter of the firmament* she is born of the starry heavens themselves—the principle of hope, meditation, and pure aspiration, the light of the inmost star reflected in the still pool of the soul.

the-daughter-of-the-flaming-sword.term: The Daughter of the Flaming Sword
the-daughter-of-the-flaming-sword.displayTerm: The Daughter of the Flaming Sword
the-daughter-of-the-flaming-sword.summary: The esoteric title of Strength/Lust (Teth): the Daughter of the Flaming Sword—the woman who masters the lion.
the-daughter-of-the-flaming-sword.description: ‘The Daughter of the Flaming Sword’ is the Golden Dawn title of Atu VIII (XI in some orders), Strength—Crowley's Lust—on the path of Teth (Leo) joining Chesed to Geburah. The Flaming Sword is the lightning-path of creation that descends the Tree; its ‘daughter’ is the courageous, ecstatic force that tames raw power not by suppression but by joyous mastery. The smiling woman who holds open the jaws of the lion embodies the strength that flows from union with vital fire: serpent-power channelled, the beast ridden rather than slain.

the-daughter-of-the-lords-of-truth.term: The Daughter of the Lords of Truth
the-daughter-of-the-lords-of-truth.displayTerm: The Daughter of the Lords of Truth
the-daughter-of-the-lords-of-truth.summary: Part of Justice/Adjustment's title (Lamed): the Daughter of the Lords of Truth—cosmic equilibrium.
the-daughter-of-the-lords-of-truth.description: ‘The Daughter of the Lords of Truth’ is part of the Golden Dawn title of Atu VIII/XI, Justice (Crowley's Adjustment), on the path of Lamed (Libra) joining Geburah to Tiphareth; the full style is ‘The Daughter of the Lords of Truth; The Ruler of Balance.’ Libra is the scales, and the trump is the principle of exact equilibrium—karma, the precise weighing of every act against its consequence. As *daughter of the lords of truth* she is born of those higher powers whose nature is rightness itself, the living embodiment of the law that holds the universe in poise.

the-daughter-of-the-mighty-ones.term: The Daughter of the Mighty Ones
the-daughter-of-the-mighty-ones.displayTerm: The Daughter of the Mighty Ones
the-daughter-of-the-mighty-ones.summary: The esoteric title of the Empress (Daleth): Daughter of the Mighty Ones, Venus as universal mother.
the-daughter-of-the-mighty-ones.description: ‘The Daughter of the Mighty Ones’ is the Golden Dawn title of Atu III, the Empress, on the path of Daleth (Venus) joining Chokmah to Binah across the top of the Tree. She is the generative love that flows between the Supernal Father and Mother and so the fruit of their union—daughter of the mighty, yet herself the fertile gate through which all forms are born. Venus here is no mere romance but the cosmic principle of attraction and beauty by which the universe coheres and propagates; the Empress is Nature crowned and throned, the green womb of the world.

the-daughter-of-the-reconcilers.summary: Part of Temperance/Art's title (Samekh): the Daughter of the Reconcilers—the alchemical mingling.
the-daughter-of-the-reconcilers.description: ‘The Daughter of the Reconcilers’ is part of the Golden Dawn title of Atu XIV, Temperance—Crowley's Art—on the path of Samekh (Sagittarius) joining Tiphareth to Yesod; the full style is ‘The Daughter of the Reconcilers; The Bringer Forth of Life.’ Sagittarius is the arrow aimed from earth to heaven, and the trump is the great work of combination: fire and water, gold and silver, mingled in one vessel. As *daughter of the reconcilers* she is born of the powers that harmonise opposites, the tempering art that fuses contraries into a living third thing.

the-dead-arising-from-their-tombs.term: the dead arising from their tombs
the-dead-arising-from-their-tombs.displayTerm: the dead arising from their tombs
the-dead-arising-from-their-tombs.summary: Design detail of Judgement/The Aeon (Shin): the dead arising from their tombs.
the-dead-arising-from-their-tombs.description: ‘The dead arising from their tombs’ completes Liber 777's design for Atu XX, Judgement/Aeon (path of Shin, Fire): ‘Israfel blowing the Last Trumpet; the dead arising from their tombs.’ At the trumpet's call the dead break their graves and rise—the image of resurrection, the summons to a higher life. Under the fiery letter Shin the trump marks the end of one cycle and the awakening into another; what was buried in the old aeon is raised, purified, and reborn in the primal fire.
tables: CLXXXI. Correct Design of Tarot Trumps

the-devil.summary: Atu XV — Ayin / Capricorn; generative matter, joyous embodiment, and creative force.
the-devil.description: The Devil is trump XV, attributed to Ayin and Capricorn, the path from Tiphareth to Hod. Far from a figure of evil, in the Thoth system it is the joyous, generative force of matter and embodiment—the goat of Mendes, Pan, the creative phallic energy that delights in incarnate existence. The letter Ayin means ‘eye,’ the all-seeing and laughing god of life. What looks like bondage to the unawakened is, rightly understood, the ecstatic play of spirit in flesh. The Devil teaches the sanctity of the body, of desire, and of the manifest world—the divine hidden in the ‘base’ and the material.
tables: XIV. General Attribution of the Tarot
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

the-disciples.summary: The Disciples — the company of the Apostles, attributed to Aries (Heh).
the-disciples.description: 'The Disciples,' the gathered followers of Christ, are set in 777 in the path of Heh and the sign of Aries — the cardinal fire of beginnings and of zeal. The attribution casts the apostolic band as the springtime kindling of the new dispensation, the first flame of the Word carried outward into the world.
tables: XXXVI. Selection of Christian Gods (10); Apostles (12); Evangelists(4); and Churches of Asia (7)

the-discipline.summary: The self-mastery of Leo—the whip that tames the lion, the disciplined control of the strong will.
the-discipline.description: The Discipline is attributed to Leo (the path of Teth, Lust or Strength), and it is the instrument of self-mastery—often a literal scourge or whip—by which the strong, ardent will of that fiery sign is tamed and governed. Leo's power is the lion's: magnificent, passionate, and dangerous if unbridled, and the Discipline is what breaks it to the rider's hand. It is the willing acceptance of a hard regimen, the chastening of one's own strength so that strength may serve rather than rule. Esoterically the Discipline is the magician's mastery over his own most powerful energies—the rigorous self-training that subdues the lion of the passions and the will, turning raw force into governed, ridden power fit for the Work.

the-dog.summary: The Dog — the English meaning of the lunar mansion Kalb, at the heart of Scorpio (Antares).
the-dog.description: 'The Dog' is the English gloss of Kalb (قلب, more accurately 'heart' — but the consonants overlap closely with kalb 'dog,' and some 777 transmissions confuse the two), the sixteenth Arabic lunar mansion. The mansion's principal star is Antares (α Scorpii), the red 'rival of Mars' at the heart of Scorpio — and the proper Arabic is Qalb al-'Aqrab, 'Heart of the Scorpion.' The English 'Dog' in 777 likely reflects an early transmission slip; the entry preserves it as Crowley printed it, while pointing to the canonical mansion. See also: Kalb.
tables: CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon

the-dweller-between-the-waters.summary: Part of the Star's title (Tzaddi): the Dweller Between the Waters—poised between heaven and earth.
the-dweller-between-the-waters.description: ‘The Dweller Between the Waters’ completes the Golden Dawn title of Atu XVII, the Star (path of Tzaddi, Aquarius): ‘The Daughter of the Firmament; The Dweller Between the Waters.’ The goddess kneels with two vessels, pouring one upon the land and one upon the sea—she dwells at the meeting of the upper and lower waters, mediating heaven's gift to earth. The title names her station: the serene intermediary between the celestial and terrestrial deeps, the channel through which the waters of life and inspiration descend.

the-dweller-of-the-threshold.summary: The guardian-phantom at the gate of initiation, set at Earth — the accumulated dross of the self made fearsome.
the-dweller-of-the-threshold.description: Among the Legendary Orders of Being, the Dweller of the Threshold is attributed to the path of Earth (Tav). Given its classic name by Bulwer-Lytton in 'Zanoni' and taken up by the Theosophists and the Golden Dawn, it is the terrifying apparition that confronts the aspirant at the threshold of true initiation — the embodied sum of one's own past faults, fears and unredeemed nature, risen up as a guardian-monster that must be faced and overcome before the higher worlds may be entered. As an order of being it figures the psychic residue of the lower self made objective; set at the gate of Earth, it is the dark guardian one meets at the very entrance to the Path.

the-emperor.summary: Atu IV — Heh / Aries; sovereignty, order, the structuring paternal will.
the-emperor.description: The Emperor is trump IV, attributed (in Crowley’s revised scheme) to the letter Heh and the sign Aries, the path from Chokmah to Tiphareth. He is the principle of sovereignty, law, and structure—the paternal will that orders the world it has fathered, ruling by reason and decisive force. Enthroned with the ram and the orb, he is fiery initiative crystallised into government. The Emperor’s strength is stable authority and protective order; his shadow, rigidity and tyranny. Crowley’s exchange of the zodiacal attributions of The Emperor and The Star is one of the signature reforms of the Thoth system.
tables: XIV. General Attribution of the Tarot
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

the-empress.summary: Atu III — Daleth / Venus; the Great Mother, love, fertility, and creative nature.
the-empress.description: The Empress is trump III, attributed to Daleth and Venus, the path joining Chokmah to Binah. She is the Great Mother and the principle of love, beauty, and generative nature—the womb of forms in which the seed of the Magus comes to fruition. Crowned with stars and surrounded by abundance, she unites the supernal Father and Mother in fertile harmony. The Empress governs growth, pleasure, art, and the nurturing power that brings all things to flower; she is Venus in her most exalted, world-creating aspect.
tables: XIV. General Attribution of the Tarot
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

the-evil-eye.summary: The Capricornian power of blighting by a glance, the oldest and darkest of folk sorceries.
the-evil-eye.description: The Evil Eye is set at Ayin and Capricorn, the path of the Devil, the sign of material constriction and the goatish, earthbound passions. As a magical power it is the ancient, near-universal faculty of harming by a look charged with envy or malice—withering crops, sickening children, souring milk. Capricorn's saturnine, binding nature makes it the proper seat of this blight. The same folk-tradition that fears it is rich in amulets against it, and the Western magus is warned that to cast it is to invite its return.

the-evil-woman.summary: Nehemoth / Lilith — the averse Malkuth; the Qlipha of the fallen Kingdom.
the-evil-woman.description: The Evil Woman (Nehemoth, associated with Lilith, 'Queen of the Night') is the Qlipha of Malkuth, the Kingdom. Where the true Bride is the Shekhinah indwelling in the world, her averse reflection is the seductress of matter, the harlot of the shells who lures the soul to mistake the husk for the fruit. She is the lowest of the Qliphoth, the temptation of the material world divorced from its divine source.
tables: CXXIII. Translation of the Orders of the Qliphoth

the-face.summary: The countenance of the Perfected Man, set in the three Supernals—the Long Face of the Most Holy.
the-face.description: In the table of the Perfected Man the Face is attributed to the three Supernals, Kether, Chokmah, and Binah—the highest triad of the Tree. This is the Qabalistic doctrine of the body of Adam Kadmon, the primordial human whose limbs and features are the Sephiroth: the countenance belongs to the crown of the head, the Long Face (Arikh Anpin) of the Idrot of the Zohar, the august visage of the Most Holy Ancient One whose every feature is a mystery of the divine. To behold the Face is to gaze upon the Supernal world itself.

the-figure-of-a-hanged.summary: Liber 777's design for the Hanged Man (Mem): the figure of a hanged or crucified man.
the-figure-of-a-hanged.description: ‘The figure of a hanged’ is Liber 777's design for Atu XII, the Hanged Man (path of Mem, Water): ‘The figure of a hanged or crucified man.’ Suspended head-downward, often by one foot in the form of a cross and triangle, he is the image of willing sacrifice and reversal—the lower self surrendered, the ordinary view of the world inverted. As the Spirit of the Mighty Waters he hangs drowned in the element of Mem, the slain god whose immersion fertilises the world and whose death is the gateway to a higher life.
tables: CLXXXI. Correct Design of Tarot Trumps

the-figure-of-a-water-nymph-disporting-h.term: The figure of a water nymph disporting herself
the-figure-of-a-water-nymph-disporting-h.displayTerm: The figure of a water nymph disporting herself
the-figure-of-a-water-nymph-disporting-h.summary: Liber 777's design for the Star (Tzaddi): a water nymph disporting herself.
the-figure-of-a-water-nymph-disporting-h.description: ‘The figure of a water nymph disporting herself’ is Liber 777's design for Atu XVII, the Star (path of Tzaddi, Aquarius). The naked nymph plays among the waters she pours from her vessels—the goddess Nuit or the daughter of the firmament, freely bestowing the waters of life beneath the great star. Her unguarded play is the image of hope, purity, and inspired aspiration: the soul bathing in the celestial dew, the dweller between the waters joyfully mediating heaven's gift to earth.
tables: CLXXXI. Correct Design of Tarot Trumps

the-figure-of-diana-huntress.summary: Liber 777's design for Temperance/Art (Samekh): the figure of Diana the huntress.
the-figure-of-diana-huntress.description: ‘The figure of Diana huntress’ is Liber 777's design for Atu XIV, Temperance—Crowley's Art—on the path of Samekh (Sagittarius). Diana, the archer-goddess of the chase, embodies Sagittarius, the centaur's arrow loosed from earth toward heaven. As the trump of tempering and combination she aims and directs the volatile and the fixed toward a single mark; the huntress's bent bow is the disciplined aspiration that reconciles opposites and brings forth the living elixir.
tables: CLXXXI. Correct Design of Tarot Trumps

the-figure-of-pan.summary: Liber 777's design for the Devil (Ayin): the figure of Pan (or Priapus).
the-figure-of-pan.description: ‘The figure of Pan’ is Liber 777's design for Atu XV, the Devil (path of Ayin, Capricorn): ‘The figure of Pan or Priapus.’ Pan—the goat-footed All-God of wild nature, with Priapus his phallic, generative aspect—is the true meaning behind the medieval ‘devil.’ Capricorn is the goat that climbs from the deepest valley to the highest peak, and the trump is the creative, mirthful, earthy force of incarnate life: spirit entering matter through the gate of generation, the god of nature laughing in his apparent chains.
tables: CLXXXI. Correct Design of Tarot Trumps

the-flock.summary: 'The Flock'—the qliphothic order of Aries, the herd-mind that is the shadow of the pioneer.
the-flock.description: In the Translation of the Orders of Qliphoth 'The Flock' is the averse order attributed to Heh and Aries. The Qliphoth are the unbalanced, demonic shells of the Tree, each the shadow of a path's virtue; here the bold, self-originating fire of Aries is degraded into its opposite—the mindless herd that stampedes without thought, the flock that follows blindly where the true ram would lead. It names the corruption of pioneering will into mere mob-instinct.
tables: CXXIII. Translation of the Orders of the Qliphoth

the-fool.summary: Atu 0 — Aleph / Air; pure potential, the divine madman stepping into the void.
the-fool.description: The Fool is the first and numberless trump (0), attributed to the letter Aleph and the element Air, the path joining Kether to Chokmah. He is pure unconditioned potential—the divine child or holy madman who steps off the cliff in perfect trust, carrying nothing yet containing everything. As zero he is the egg of spirit before all manifestation; in Crowley’s Thoth deck he is the green god of spring, ecstatic and self-renewing. The Fool teaches that the highest wisdom can look like folly to the world, and that every journey begins with a leap into the unknown.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

the-fool-swords-emperors-of-princes.term: The Fool - Swords - Emperors of Princes
the-fool-swords-emperors-of-princes.displayTerm: The Fool - Swords - Emperors of Princes
the-fool-swords-emperors-of-princes.summary: The cluster attributed to Aleph/Air: the Fool, the suit of Swords, and the Emperors (Princes).
the-fool-swords-emperors-of-princes.description: This entry from Liber 777's General Attribution of the Tarot gathers under the path of Aleph (Air) the trump of the Fool, the suit of Swords, and the court rank of the Emperors or Princes. Air is the element of Aleph and of the airy suit of Swords (intellect and conflict), and the cluster shows how a single elemental principle threads through the three divisions of the deck—trump, pip-suit, and court. The Fool as the Spirit of Aether stands at the head of this airy current that the Swords and their Princes carry into the world.
tables: XIV. General Attribution of the Tarot

the-furnace.summary: The athanor of Cancer—the enclosed vessel of transforming heat, the womb of slow gestation.
the-furnace.description: The Furnace is attributed to Cancer (the path of Cheth, the Chariot), and it is the athanor of the alchemists—the enclosed furnace whose steady, contained heat digests and transforms the matter sealed within it. Its place at the watery, maternal, sheltering sign of Cancer reveals its deeper sense: the furnace is a womb, an incubating vessel in which transformation proceeds slowly and in secret, protected from the outer world. The Chariot's enclosing shell becomes here the closed crucible of change. Esoterically the Furnace is the magician's sealed vessel of transformation—the protected, sustained inner heat in which the raw material of the self is digested and changed, the womb-like crucible where, hidden and undisturbed, the great alteration is brought to maturity.

the-girdle.summary: The cestus of Venus—the magic belt of Aphrodite, the encircling band of love's binding allure.
the-girdle.description: The Girdle appears among the weapons at Venus (the path of the Empress), where it takes on the character of the famous cestus of Aphrodite—the enchanted belt that lent its wearer irresistible charm and bound the heart of any who beheld it. Here the girdle's encircling and binding nature is turned to the work of love and attraction: it is the magic of allure, the power to draw and to hold by beauty and desire. As the Empress's implement it belongs to the fertile, magnetic forces of nature. Esoterically the Girdle of Venus is the binding power of love and beauty in the magician's hand—the magnetic, encircling attraction that draws together what it would unite, the cestus by which the heart is bound and the will of love accomplished.

the-gods.summary: The recollection of the deities (devatānussati) — contemplating the qualities that lift beings to the heavens.
the-gods.description: The Gods renders devatānussati, the recollection of the deities among the Forty Meditations, attributed to Tiphareth, the solar centre of the Tree. The practitioner does not worship the gods but reflects that the qualities which raised beings to the heavenly states — faith, virtue, learning, generosity and wisdom — are present in himself, and in that reflection confidence and gladness arise. Set at the harmonising sphere of the Sun, it figures the contemplation of the luminous, exalted possibilities of the being, the divine measure held up as mirror and aspiration.

the-great-one-of-the-night-of-time.term: The Great One of the Night of Time
the-great-one-of-the-night-of-time.displayTerm: The Great One of the Night of Time
the-great-one-of-the-night-of-time.summary: The esoteric title of the Universe/World (Tav): the Great One of the Night of Time—the completed cosmos.
the-great-one-of-the-night-of-time.description: ‘The Great One of the Night of Time’ is the Golden Dawn title of Atu XXI, the Universe (the World), on the path of Tav (Saturn) joining Yesod to Malkuth—the final path, the completion of the Tree. Saturn is the lord of time and of the dark, fertile night out of which all things emerge and to which they return. The trump is the dancing maiden within the cosmic mandala, the marriage of matter and spirit, the Great Work accomplished. As *great one of the night of time* it is the totality of manifestation crowned and sealed—the universe beheld whole, the end that is also the threshold of a new beginning.

the-great-work.summary: The supreme aim of all magic, the union of the soul with its source.
the-great-work.description: The Great Work—here attributed to Mem and Water, the path of the Hanged Man and its mystery of redemptive surrender—is the name the Hermetic tradition gives to the whole purpose of the art: the perfecting of the human being through union with the divine, the accomplishment of the alchemical Stone within. The watery path of self-sacrifice and inversion is well chosen for it, for the Work is achieved not by grasping but by giving up, the drowning of the lesser self in the greater. Every other magical power is but a step toward this one end.

the-hair.summary: The hair of the Perfected Man, streaming from the unmanifest beyond the Crown.
the-hair.description: The Hair is attributed to the Veils of the Negative, the boundless nothingness beyond Kether. In the Idra Rabba of the Zohar the hairs of the Ancient of Days flow from the white skull of Macroprosopus in countless filaments, each a channel of influence from the unmanifest. So in the body of Adam Kadmon the hair represents the finest, most rarefied emanations descending from that which is before all manifestation—the streaming locks of the Vast Countenance, rooted in the Naught from which the Tree depends.

the-hanged-man.summary: Atu XII — Mem / Water; sacrifice, surrender, and redemption through reversal.
the-hanged-man.description: The Hanged Man is trump XII, attributed to Mem and the element Water, the path from Geburah to Hod. It is the mystery of sacrifice and surrender—the willing reversal of the ordinary self, suspended between worlds, by which a higher redemption is won. Hung by one foot in the posture of the drowned or the dying god, he sees the world inverted and so truly. As elemental Water it is the dissolution of the ego and the baptism that precedes rebirth. The card teaches that the way up is the way down, and that real attainment requires a letting-go that looks like loss.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

the-hanged-man-cups-queens.summary: The cluster attributed to Mem/Water: the Hanged Man, the suit of Cups, and the Queens.
the-hanged-man-cups-queens.description: This entry from Liber 777's General Attribution of the Tarot gathers under the path of Mem (Water) the trump of the Hanged Man, the suit of Cups, and the court rank of the Queens. Mem is the elemental letter of water, the Cups are the watery suit of love and emotion, and the Queens are the watery, receptive thrones of the court. The cluster reveals the single current of Water flowing through trump, suit, and court—sacrifice and immersion (the Hanged Man), feeling (the Cups), and the nurturing sovereignty of the Queens.
tables: XIV. General Attribution of the Tarot

the-hermit.summary: Atu IX — Yod / Virgo; the solitary lamp-bearer and the fertile seed of light.
the-hermit.description: The Hermit is trump IX, attributed to Yod and Virgo, the path from Chesed to Tiphareth. He is the solitary sage who withdraws from the world to seek and to share the inner light, lifting his lamp in the darkness for those who follow. As Yod—the seed-letter and spermatozoon of the Tetragrammaton—he carries a hidden fertility: his solitude is generative, the secret germ of wisdom. Crowley’s Hermit is accompanied by the cosmic egg and the serpent, marking the path as one of fruitful concealment. The card teaches the necessity of withdrawal, patience, and the self-illumined search.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

the-hierophant.summary: Atu V — Vav / Taurus; the teacher of mysteries, tradition, and the inner voice.
the-hierophant.description: The Hierophant is trump V, attributed to Vav and Taurus, the path from Chesed to Chokmah. He is the revealer of sacred mysteries—the bridge (pontifex) between the divine and the human, the teacher, initiator, and keeper of tradition. Enthroned before the temple, he transmits the eternal law to those prepared to receive it. As the letter Vav (‘nail,’ the conjunction ‘and’) he is the link that binds; in the New Aeon Crowley reinterprets him as the herald of the child Horus. The Hierophant teaches through form, ritual, and the voice of the inner master.
tables: XIV. General Attribution of the Tarot
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

the-high-priestess.summary: Atu II — Gimel / Luna; the veiled mysteries, intuition, the secret road to the Crown.
the-high-priestess.description: The High Priestess is trump II, attributed to Gimel and the Moon, the long path that crosses the Abyss from Tiphareth to Kether. She is the guardian of the hidden mysteries—the veiled feminine wisdom that is felt rather than spoken, intuition and the inner light. Seated between the pillars with the scroll of secret law, she is the purest, most spiritual lunar power, the silver thread that leads directly to the Crown. She teaches receptivity, the wisdom of silence, and the knowledge that comes only through inner stillness.
tables: XIV. General Attribution of the Tarot
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

the-hips.summary: The two hips of the Perfected Man, the lower pair of side-Sephiroth bearing the trunk.
the-hips.description: The Hips are attributed to Netzach and Hod, the seventh and eighth Sephiroth that stand as the lower pair of the side-pillars. As the hips carry the weight of the body and join the trunk to the legs, so Netzach and Hod—the spheres of feeling and intellect—bear the structure of the personality above and transmit it to the foundation below. In the body of Adam Kadmon they are the balanced supports on the right and left through which the Tree is upheld.

the-holy-ghost.summary: The Holy Ghost — the indwelling Spirit, attributed to the element of Spirit (31-bis).
the-holy-ghost.description: Beyond its lower attribution to Hod and Yesod, the Holy Ghost is also referred to Spirit itself — the quintessence above the four elements (the path 31-bis). Here the Paraclete is the fifth, all-pervading element, the breath (pneuma, ruach) that informs and unifies fire, water, air, and earth: the divine Spirit as the secret root and crown of the elemental world.
tables: XXXVI. Selection of Christian Gods (10); Apostles (12); Evangelists(4); and Churches of Asia (7)

the-horns.summary: The horns of Aries—the ram's crown of force, the emblem of generative power and divine authority.
the-horns.description: The Horns are attributed to Aries (the path of Heh, the Emperor), and they are the curling horns of the ram, the sign's own beast—the crown of the horned god, the emblem of initiating force, virile power, and divine authority. Horns have ever signified might and rank: the rays of light depicted as horns upon the heads of gods and prophets, the strength of the charging ram, the generative power of the horned lord of nature. Their place at Aries, the cardinal fire, marks them as the very crown of the outgoing, initiating will. Esoterically the Horns are the magician's emblem of empowered authority and generative force—the crown of strength worn by the one who initiates and rules, the rayed power of the horned god lifted upon the brow.

the-house-of-god.summary: An old title of the Tower (Pe): the House of God, struck by lightning.
the-house-of-god.description: ‘The House of God’ (La Maison Dieu) is the old title of Atu XVI, the Tower, attributed in Liber 777 to the path of Pe (Mars). The phrase is ironic and profound: the proud tower built in ignorance is struck by the lightning of divine wrath, its false structure shattered and its occupants cast down. As the Lord of the Hosts of the Mighty, the trump is sudden, martial, liberating catastrophe—the breaking-open of the prison of error so that the light of truth may enter.
tables: XIV. General Attribution of the Tarot
XXII. Small Selection of Hindu Deities

the-inner-robe-of-glory.summary: The luminous inner garment of Chokmah—the body of light hidden beneath, the secret splendour of the adept.
the-inner-robe-of-glory.description: The Inner Robe of Glory is attributed to Chokmah, the supernal Father and the sphere of Wisdom, and it is the bright, luminous garment worn beneath the outer robe—the hidden body of light that signifies the adept's inner attainment and the splendour of the higher self. Where the Outer Robe of Concealment is dark and veils the glory from the profane, the Inner Robe is radiant, the secret brilliance reserved for the work and revealed only in the heights. Its place at Chokmah, nearest the crown, marks it as the glory of the highest wisdom. Esoterically the Inner Robe of Glory is the magician's realised body of light—the luminous spiritual nature, kept hidden beneath the outer concealment, that shines forth as the splendour of attainment when the soul ascends toward its source.

the-intellect.summary: The Intellect — the reasoning soul, Ruach, attributed to the central Sephiroth.
the-intellect.description: 'The Intellect' answers to the Ruach, the reasoning mind, set across the central Sephiroth from Chesed to Yesod. It is the everyday self of thought, feeling, and will — the mediating soul that gathers the powers of the middle Tree, capable of rising toward the higher understanding or sinking toward the animal nature below.
tables: XCVIII. Parts of the Soul English

the-intuition.summary: The Intuition — the higher understanding, Neschamah, attributed to Binah.
the-intuition.description: 'The Intuition' renders the Neschamah, the higher soul or intuitive understanding, set at Binah. It is the silent inner knowing that apprehends directly, without reasoning — the supernal Mother's gift of comprehension, the part of the soul that listens to the divine and understands.
tables: XCVIII. Parts of the Soul English

the-juggler.summary: An old title of the Magician (Beth): the Juggler, the conjuror of the elements.
the-juggler.description: ‘The Juggler’ is the older French and English title (Le Bateleur) of Atu I, the Magician, attributed in Liber 777 to the path of Beth (Mercury). The juggler is the mountebank at his table of tricks—but esoterically his ‘conjuring’ is the true magic of the Logos: the Mercurial mind that keeps the four elements in play and makes the manifest world appear from the unmanifest. The humble showman's name conceals the highest art, the focused will displaying its power over the elemental forces.
tables: XIV. General Attribution of the Tarot

the-labour-of-preparation.summary: The patient groundwork of Taurus—the diligent preparatory toil that readies the materials of the Work.
the-labour-of-preparation.description: The Labour of Preparation is attributed to Taurus (the path of Vau, the Hierophant), and it names the patient, earthy work that must precede every operation: the gathering and readying of materials, the building of the temple, the slow diligent toil by which the ground is made fit for the rite. Taurus is the fixed-earth sign of steady, unhurried industry, and this labour is its virtue applied to the magical work—the unglamorous foundation-building on which all higher results depend. Nothing skips this stage and prospers. Esoterically the Labour of Preparation is the disciplined, methodical groundwork of the magician—the patient, faithful toil that prepares the vessel, the materials and the self, the necessary earthy industry without which no consecration or invocation can succeed.

the-lamen.summary: The breastplate of office at Tiphareth—the worn badge declaring the magician's authority and true name.
the-lamen.description: The Lamen is attributed to the Sun and to Tiphareth, and it is the emblem worn upon the breast—a plate or pendant, often the Rosy Cross—that proclaims the magician's authority, grade and identity in the work. Worn over the heart, the seat of Tiphareth, it is the outward sign of the inner attainment, the badge by which the operator declares himself before the forces he summons and the seal that focuses his solar power. Where the weapons in the hands act, the Lamen on the breast simply is, a statement of being. Esoterically the Lamen is the realised self displayed as a sign of office—the harmonised solar nature of Tiphareth made visible, the heart's truth worn openly as the authority by which one stands in the temple.

the-lamp.summary: The light borne in darkness—the Hermit's lamp and the secret wisdom, the supernal light of Kether carried below.
the-lamp.description: The Lamp is attributed to Kether, to Virgo (the Hermit) and to Netzach, and it is the implement of the inner light: the lantern the Hermit lifts to illumine the dark path, the secret wisdom carried concealed and revealed only to those who walk near. At Kether it is the supreme light at the crown of the Tree; in the Hermit's hand it is that light borne down into the world's night so that others may find the way. The Lamp must be tended, shielded from the wind, and never allowed to go out. Esoterically the Lamp is the spark of divine illumination that the adept guards and bears through the darkness—the light of the higher self made portable, a single steady flame against the surrounding dark.

the-left-ear.summary: The left ear of the Perfected Man, attributed to expansive Jupiter.
the-left-ear.description: The Left Ear is attributed to Kaph and Jupiter in the body of Adam Kadmon. The faculty of hearing—the receptive sense that takes in the word and the harmony of the spheres—is here divided between the planets, and the left ear is given to the benevolent, expansive Jupiter. In the symbolic body it is an organ of receptive understanding, attuned to the wide and generous resonances of the Jovian sphere.

the-left-eye.summary: The left eye of the Perfected Man, the lunar eye that mirrors the Moon.
the-left-eye.description: The Left Eye is attributed to Gimel and the Moon in the body of Adam Kadmon. The ancient doctrine of the two great lights places the Sun in the right eye and the Moon in the left, and so it is here: the left eye is lunar, the receptive, reflecting organ that perceives by borrowed and changeable light, mirror of the tides of the inner world. It is the eye of vision and dream, the silver counterpart to the golden eye of day.

the-left-nostril.summary: The left nostril of the Perfected Man, the breath of Venus.
the-left-nostril.description: The Left Nostril is attributed to Daleth and Venus in the body of Adam Kadmon. The twin gates of the breath are divided between the planets, and the left nostril is given to gentle, attractive Venus—the channel of the softer, sweeter inspiration. In the symbolic body and in the breath-disciplines that read the flow of the nostrils as currents of subtle force, it is the Venusian conduit of the vital air, the inhalation of love and harmony.

the-life.summary: The Life — the vital spirit, Chiah, attributed to Chokmah.
the-life.description: 'The Life' answers to the Chiah, the life-force or vital spirit of the soul, set at Chokmah. It is the dynamic, outpouring energy of the being — the divine will-to-live that proceeds from the Self, the surge of pure vitality at the root of the individual existence.
tables: XCVIII. Parts of the Soul English

the-lightning-the-king-of-the-spirits-of.term: the Lightning. The King of the Spirits of Fire. Rules 20° ♏ to 20° ♐
the-lightning-the-king-of-the-spirits-of.displayTerm: the Lightning. The King of the Spirits of Fire. Rules 20° ♏ to 20° ♐
the-lightning-the-king-of-the-spirits-of.summary: Golden Dawn title and dominion of the King/Knight of Wands, ruling 20° Scorpio–20° Sagittarius.
the-lightning-the-king-of-the-spirits-of.description: ‘The Lightning. The King of the Spirits of Fire. Rules 20° ♏ to 20° ♐’ is the Golden Dawn (Book T) title and celestial dominion of the King of Wands (the Knight in the Thoth deck), the swiftest and most fiery figure of the court. His full style is ‘Lord of the Flame and the Lightning, King of the Spirits of Fire,’ and his rule spans the thirty degrees from the heart of Scorpio into Sagittarius. He embodies fire at its most sudden and overwhelming—the lightning-stroke of pure will, energy that acts before it can be resisted.
tables: LXXI. Court Cards of the Tarot, with the Spheres of their Celestial Dominion - Wands

the-line.summary: The one-dimensional line — Chokmah; the first extension, force in pure direction.
the-line.description: The Line is attributed to Chokmah, the second Sephirah. When the point moves, it generates the line — the first dimension, extension in a single direction, the image of pure force flowing out from the source. As Chokmah is the outpouring creative Wisdom, dynamic and directional, the line is its fitting geometrical emblem: being no longer a mere point, but not yet a world.
tables: XLIX. Lineal Figures of the Planets, &c., and Geomany

the-lips.summary: The lips of the Perfected Man, the Mercurial gate of speech.
the-lips.description: The Lips are attributed to Beth and Mercury in the body of Adam Kadmon. As the lips shape the breath into the word, they belong to Mercury, lord of speech, writing, and all communication—the swift god whose path is the Magus. In the symbolic body they are the instrument by which the inner wisdom is uttered, the gate through which silent thought passes into living language, the very organ of the magical word.

the-lord-of-dominion.summary: Two of Wands — Dominion; Mars in Aries, Chokmah of Fire: pure will established.
the-lord-of-dominion.description: The Two of Wands, titled the Lord of Dominion, is Chokmah in the suit of Fire and the first decan of Aries, ruled by Mars. Here the undivided fire of the Ace first takes on duality and direction: two crossed dorjes or thunderbolts, force willed and aimed. It is the energy of the warrior-king, dominion established by the sheer assertion of will before any obstacle has arisen — swift, proud, and a little ruthless.
tables: CXXXIII. Titles and Attributions of the Wand Suit

the-lord-of-harmonious-change.summary: Two of Disks — Change; Jupiter in Capricorn, Chokmah of Earth: matter in flux.
the-lord-of-harmonious-change.description: The Two of Disks, the Lord of Harmonious Change, is Chokmah in the suit of Earth and the first decan of Capricorn under Jupiter. A great serpent crowned, forming the figure-eight of infinity, binds two discs marked with the Tao: matter first set in motion, the eternal dance of flux and reflux. It is the principle of change itself, the necessity of constant rebalancing, stability found only in perpetual movement.
tables: CXXXVI. Titles and Attributions of the Pantacle Suit

the-lord-of-love.summary: Two of Cups — Love; Venus in Cancer, Chokmah of Water: the cup of union.
the-lord-of-love.description: The Two of Cups, the Lord of Love, is Chokmah in the suit of Water and the first decan of Cancer, where Venus pours into the Moon's own house. Two cups overflow from a single lotus, fed by dolphins of Mercury and Venus: it is love as the harmonising of two natures into one, the first reflection of the watery Ace. Pure, mutual affection and the joy of perfect reciprocity belong to this card.
tables: CXXXIV. Titles and Attributions of the Chalice Suit

the-lord-of-peace-restored.summary: Two of Swords — Peace; Moon in Libra, Chokmah of Air: harmony of opposed minds.
the-lord-of-peace-restored.description: The Two of Swords, the Lord of Peace Restored, is Chokmah in the suit of Air and the first decan of Libra under the Moon. Two crossed swords meet at a blue rose, the warring intellect briefly reconciled: thought divided into duality yet held in delicate balance. It is peace after conflict, the truce of reason — stable only so long as the equilibrium of forces is maintained.
tables: CXXXV. Titles and Attributions of the Sword Suit.

the-lord-of-the-fire-of-the-world.term: The Lord of the Fire of the World
the-lord-of-the-fire-of-the-world.displayTerm: The Lord of the Fire of the World
the-lord-of-the-fire-of-the-world.summary: The esoteric title of the Sun (Resh): the Lord of the Fire of the World—the radiant solar lord.
the-lord-of-the-fire-of-the-world.description: ‘The Lord of the Fire of the World’ is the Golden Dawn title of Atu XIX, the Sun, on the path of Resh (the Sun) joining Hod to Yesod. The Sun is the visible glory of the cosmos, the source of light, life, and warmth, and the trump is joy, clarity, regeneration, and the innocent freedom of the redeemed. As *lord of the fire of the world* the solar power is the kindling principle of all manifest vitality—the dancing children, the blossoming garden, the great luminary under which the world is made new. It is consciousness fully awake and rejoicing.

the-lord-of-the-flame.summary: Part of the title of the King/Knight of Wands: the Lord of the Flame and the Lightning.
the-lord-of-the-flame.description: ‘The Lord of the Flame’ opens the Golden Dawn (Book T) title of the King of Wands (the Knight in the Thoth deck): ‘The Lord of the Flame and the Lightning, the King of the Spirits of Fire.’ He is the most active and fiery of the court—the rushing, kindling force of his element, ruling from 20° Scorpio to 20° Sagittarius. The flame and the lightning express his swift, consuming, irresistible energy: pure fiery will in its most dynamic and untrammelled form.
tables: LXXI. Court Cards of the Tarot, with the Spheres of their Celestial Dominion - Wands

the-lord-of-the-forces-of-life.term: The Lord of the Forces of Life
the-lord-of-the-forces-of-life.displayTerm: The Lord of the Forces of Life
the-lord-of-the-forces-of-life.summary: The esoteric title of the Wheel of Fortune (Kaph): the Lord of the Forces of Life—the turning of fate.
the-lord-of-the-forces-of-life.description: ‘The Lord of the Forces of Life’ is the Golden Dawn title of Atu X, the Wheel of Fortune, on the path of Kaph (Jupiter) joining Chesed to Netzach. Jupiter is the great benefic, the principle of expansion, fortune, and rhythmic increase, and the ever-turning wheel is the engine of becoming—the rise and fall of all conditioned things. To name it ‘the forces of life’ is to see destiny not as dead mechanism but as the living circulation of energy through fortune and misfortune alike, the whirling of the triad of Hermanubis, the Sphinx, and Typhon about an unmoving centre.

the-lord-of-the-gate-of-death.term: The Lord of the Gate of Death
the-lord-of-the-gate-of-death.displayTerm: The Lord of the Gate of Death
the-lord-of-the-gate-of-death.summary: Part of Death's title (Nun): the Lord of the Gate of Death—warden of the passage of transformation.
the-lord-of-the-gate-of-death.description: ‘The Lord of the Gate of Death’ completes the Golden Dawn title of Atu XIII, Death (path of Nun, Scorpio): ‘The Child of the Great Transformers; The Lord of the Gate of Death.’ Death is not an end but a threshold, and this trump is its keeper—the dark gate through which all must pass on the way to renewal. Scorpio's triple emblem of scorpion, serpent, and eagle marks the stages of putrefaction, regeneration, and transcendence; the Lord of the Gate presides over them all, the necessary doorway between one mode of being and the next.

the-lord-of-the-gates-of-matter.term: The Lord of the Gates of Matter
the-lord-of-the-gates-of-matter.displayTerm: The Lord of the Gates of Matter
the-lord-of-the-gates-of-matter.summary: Part of the Devil's title (Ayin): the Lord of the Gates of Matter—the descent into dense form.
the-lord-of-the-gates-of-matter.description: ‘The Lord of the Gates of Matter’ is part of the Golden Dawn title of Atu XV, the Devil, on the path of Ayin (Capricorn) joining Tiphareth to Hod; the full style is ‘The Lord of the Gates of Matter; The Child of the Forces of Time.’ Capricorn is the goat that climbs the highest peak from the lowest valley, and the trump is the mystery of incarnation—spirit entering matter, the creative force at its most concentrated and earthy. As *lord of the gates of matter* the figure (Pan, Priapus, the goat of Mendes) presides over the threshold where the unmanifest takes on flesh, generative power bound into form.

the-lord-of-the-hosts-of-the-mighty.term: The Lord of the Hosts of the Mighty
the-lord-of-the-hosts-of-the-mighty.displayTerm: The Lord of the Hosts of the Mighty
the-lord-of-the-hosts-of-the-mighty.summary: The esoteric title of the Tower (Pe): the Lord of the Hosts of the Mighty—the lightning that shatters.
the-lord-of-the-hosts-of-the-mighty.description: ‘The Lord of the Hosts of the Mighty’ is the Golden Dawn title of Atu XVI, the Tower (the House of God), on the path of Pe (Mars) joining Netzach to Hod. Mars is the war-god, and the trump is sudden, violent liberation—the tower of false structure struck by the lightning of divine wrath, its occupants cast down. The title evokes the marshalled armies of heaven, the overwhelming martial force that breaks every proud edifice built in ignorance of the truth. What looks like catastrophe is the breaking-open of the prison so that the light may enter.

the-lord-of-the-waves.summary: Part of the title of the King/Knight of Cups: the Lord of the Waves and the Waters.
the-lord-of-the-waves.description: ‘The Lord of the Waves’ opens the Golden Dawn (Book T) title of the King of Cups (the Knight in the Thoth deck): ‘The Lord of the Waves and the Waters, the King of the Hosts of the Sea.’ He is the active, fiery aspect of the watery suit—the rider who masters the moving sea, ruling from 20° Aquarius to 20° Pisces. The waves and waters express his command over the fluid element: passion and feeling stirred into dynamic, surging motion.
tables: LXII. The Court Cards of the Tarot, with the Spheres of their Celestial Dominion Cups

the-lord-of-the-wide.summary: Part of the title of the King/Knight of Disks: the Lord of the Wide and Fertile Land.
the-lord-of-the-wide.description: ‘The Lord of the Wide’ opens the Golden Dawn (Book T) title of the King of Disks (the Knight in the Thoth deck): ‘The Lord of the Wide and Fertile Land, the King of the Spirits of Earth.’ He is the active aspect of the earthy suit—the labourer and husbandman who masters the broad, productive land, ruling from 20° Leo to 20° Virgo. The wide and fertile land expresses his domain over the element of earth: matter made fruitful, the patient, generative power of cultivated nature.
tables:
LXIV. The Court Cards of the Tarot, with the Spheres of 
their Celestial Dominion Pantacles.

the-lord-of-the-winds.summary: Part of the title of the King/Knight of Swords: the Lord of the Winds and the Breezes.
the-lord-of-the-winds.description: ‘The Lord of the Winds’ opens the Golden Dawn (Book T) title of the King of Swords (the Knight in the Thoth deck): ‘The Lord of the Winds and the Breezes, the King of the Spirits of Air.’ He is the active, fiery aspect of the airy suit—the swift rider of the storm, ruling from 20° Taurus to 20° Gemini. The winds and breezes express his command over the element of air: thought and intellect set in violent, decisive motion, the sweeping force of the mind in action.
tables: LXIII. The Court Cards of the Tarot, with the Spheres of their Celestial Dominion Swords.

the-lord-of-yoga.summary: The Lord of Yoga (Yogeshvara) — Shiva as the supreme master of union, at Virgo.
the-lord-of-yoga.description: “The Lord of Yoga” is a title of Shiva as Yogeshvara, the supreme ascetic and master of the discipline of union, here referred to Yod and Virgo — the sign of the solitary, the analytical, the perfected method. As the great yogi seated in unmoving meditation, he is the archetype of the practitioner who, through self-mastery, attains identity with the absolute. The title fixes the divine as the model and goal of all spiritual discipline.
tables: XXII. Small Selection of Hindu Deities

the-lovers.summary: Atu VI — Zayin / Gemini; union of opposites, choice, and the alchemical marriage.
the-lovers.description: The Lovers is trump VI, attributed to Zayin and Gemini, the path from Binah to Tiphareth.
