It is the mystery of union and discrimination—the bringing together of opposites (king and queen, sulphur and salt, conscious and unconscious) under the blessing of a higher power, and the choice that such union demands. Crowley’s card stages an alchemical marriage presided over by the Hermit-Mercury. The Lovers teaches that true union is achieved through the reconciliation of difference, and that love is at root an act of analysis and synthesis—the Twins made one.
tables: XIV. General Attribution of the Tarot
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

the-magical-circle.summary: The circle of art at Malkuth—the bounded field of working, the magician's defence and image of the cosmos.
the-magical-circle.description: The Magical Circle is attributed to Malkuth, the manifest kingdom, and it is the consecrated boundary within which the whole operation takes place—the line of defence that shuts out hostile forces and the sacred field in which the magician stands as the still centre of his own universe. Inscribed with divine names, the circle is at once a fortress and a map of the cosmos, the operator placing himself at its heart as the microcosm reflecting the macrocosm. To step outside it during the work is to abandon protection. Esoterically the Magical Circle is the disciplined sphere of consciousness the adept establishes and holds inviolate—the bounded, ordered world he creates around himself, within which alone the dangerous powers may safely be called and commanded.

the-magus.summary: Atu I — Beth / Mercury; the will and word that translate spirit into act.
the-magus.description: The Magus (The Magician) is trump I, attributed to Beth and Mercury, the path from Kether to Binah. He is the principle of Will and Word—the juggler of the elements who, standing between above and below, channels divine power into creative act. The four elemental weapons lie on his table; the lemniscate of infinity crowns him. As Mercury–Hermes–Thoth he is the magician proper, master of communication, skill, and the magical link between intention and manifestation. His danger is the trickster’s deceit; his glory, the true Word that creates.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

the-magus-of-power.summary: The esoteric title of the Magician (Beth): the Magus of Power, Mercury made the mover of all things.
the-magus-of-power.description: ‘The Magus of Power’ is the Golden Dawn title of Atu I, the Magician, on the path of Beth (Mercury) descending from Kether to Binah. He is the Word that creates—Logos, Thoth, Hermes—the will focused to a single point through which the formless light of the Crown is first articulated into act. The title insists not on cleverness but on *power*: the magician is the channel by which the One becomes the many, the swift god who stands with the four elemental weapons at his command and directs the currents of force. In him intelligence becomes efficacious; thought becomes deed.

the-magus-of-the-eternal.summary: The esoteric title of the Hierophant (Vav): the Magus of the Eternal—the hierarch of the inner teaching.
the-magus-of-the-eternal.description: ‘The Magus of the Eternal’ (sometimes ‘Magus of the Eternal Gods’) is the Golden Dawn title of Atu V, the Hierophant, on the path of Vav (Taurus) joining Chesed to Chokmah. He is the bridge-builder—the literal meaning of *pontifex*—who mediates between the divine and the human, transmitting the perennial wisdom through rite and tradition. Where the Magician wields the power of the moment, the Hierophant is the magus of *the eternal*: the custodian of the enduring mysteries, seated between the pillars, who confers initiation and translates the silent law into a living teaching.

the-magus-of-the-voice-of-power.term: The Magus of the Voice of Power
the-magus-of-the-voice-of-power.displayTerm: The Magus of the Voice of Power
the-magus-of-the-voice-of-power.summary: Part of the Hermit's title (Yod): the Magus of the Voice of Power—the seed-word in solitude.
the-magus-of-the-voice-of-power.description: ‘The Magus of the Voice of Power’ completes the Golden Dawn title of Atu IX, the Hermit (path of Yod, Virgo): ‘The Prophet of the Eternal; The Magus of the Voice of Power.’ Yod, the divine seed-letter and the spermatozoon of the alphabet, marks the Hermit as the hidden generative principle—the still point from which creative speech issues. His lamp is the light of the Logos carried into darkness; his ‘voice of power’ is the fertilising Word that, though uttered in solitude, sets worlds in motion. He is wisdom made potent and seminal.

the-maruts.summary: The Maruts, storm-gods of the sky — the tempestuous companions of Indra, at Air.
the-maruts.description: The Maruts are the Vedic storm-gods, a host of youthful, golden warriors who ride the winds and the thunderclouds as the companions of Indra. Referred to Aleph and Air and to Aquarius, they embody the swift, turbulent power of the moving sky — the gusts, gales, and lightning of the tempest. As a riding host of wind-spirits they are the very voice and fury of the storm.
tables: XXII. Small Selection of Hindu Deities

the-moon.summary: Atu XVIII — Qoph / Pisces; the dark night of illusion, instinct, and the journey before dawn.
the-moon.description: The Moon is trump XVIII, attributed to Qoph and Pisces, the path from Netzach to Malkuth. It is the dark night of the soul—the realm of illusion, fear, instinct, and the deep unconscious through which the initiate must pass before the dawn. Crowley’s card shows the scarab bearing the sun through the underworld between two black towers, watched by jackals and the menstrual moon. It is the perilous threshold of glamour and dream, but also the gateway of rebirth. The Moon teaches endurance through confusion and the courage to traverse the darkness without losing the way.
tables: XIV. General Attribution of the Tarot
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

the-names.summary: The words of power at Hod—the divine and angelic Names by which the forces are commanded.
the-names.description: The Names are attributed to Hod, the Mercurial sphere of language, intellect and magic, and they are the divine, angelic and spiritual Names of power—the words of God and the hierarchies by which the magician invokes, commands and constrains the forces of the work. In the Western tradition to know the true name of a thing is to hold authority over it, and the Names are the very keys of the art, vibrated and intoned to summon and to bind. Their place at Hod, the seat of Mercury and of the magical word, is exact. Esoterically the Names are the magician's instruments of command through sacred speech—the words of power that, rightly known and uttered, give authority over the unseen, the spoken keys by which the operator moves the hierarchies of force.

the-neck.summary: The neck of the Perfected Man, the supernal channel joining the head of the Tree to its body.
the-neck.description: The Neck is attributed to the three Supernals in the body of the Perfected Man. As the throat joins the head to the trunk, it is the narrow channel through which the influence of the Supernal triad pours down toward the lower Sephiroth—the passage across the throat of the Abyss. In the symbolism of Adam Kadmon it is the place of utterance and of breath, where the silent wisdom of the crown becomes the living word that descends to create the worlds below.

the-oath.summary: The binding vow of Scorpio—the magical obligation sworn unto death, the irreversible commitment of the Work.
the-oath.description: The Oath is attributed to Scorpio (the path of Nun, Death), and it is the binding magical vow—the obligation the aspirant swears, often upon pain of dreadful consequence, that fixes his commitment to the Work beyond any retreat. Its place at the sign of Death is exact, for the true oath is sworn unto death: it kills the old, divided self by committing the whole being irrevocably to a single course. To take the Oath is to burn the ships, to make return impossible. Esoterically the Oath is the magician's irreversible self-binding—the solemn vow that concentrates the entire will upon the goal and forbids all turning back, the death of every possibility but the one path chosen, the obligation that makes attainment a matter of necessity rather than mere desire.

the-outer-robe-of-concealment.summary: The dark veiling garment of Binah—the black robe that hides the glory, the concealment of the Mother.
the-outer-robe-of-concealment.description: The Outer Robe of Concealment is attributed to Binah, the supernal Mother and the sphere of dark understanding, and it is the black outer garment worn over the Inner Robe of Glory—the sombre robe that hides the inner light from the profane and shields the adept's splendour from the world. Binah is the sphere of form, limitation, and the concealing darkness of the Great Sea, and the dark robe is her emblem: the veil that contains and protects what is too holy or too bright to be shown. Esoterically the Outer Robe of Concealment is the magician's discretion and protective reserve—the dark garment of silence and concealment, worn over the inner glory, by which the attainment is guarded from the unworthy and the sacred kept hidden until its proper revealing.

the-pain-of-the-obligation.summary: The cost of the vow at Scorpio—the suffering that seals the magical oath, the price of irreversible commitment.
the-pain-of-the-obligation.description: The Pain of the Obligation is attributed to Scorpio (the path of Nun, Death), and it names the suffering that attends and seals the magical oath—the cost, the ordeal, the deliberate acceptance of pain by which the binding vow is made real and irrevocable. An oath without cost is no oath; it is the willingness to suffer for it that proves and fixes the commitment. Its place at Scorpio, the sign of death, transformation and the deep, marks it as the necessary anguish of the great change, the wound that cannot be undone. Esoterically the Pain of the Obligation is the price the magician knowingly pays for his vow—the accepted suffering that transmutes a mere intention into an unbreakable bond, the ordeal that is itself the gateway to the death-and-rebirth the oath commits him to.

the-pantacle.summary: The magical weapon of Earth—the disk of manifestation and the bread of the magician, the body of the Work.
the-pantacle.description: The Pantacle is the elemental weapon of Earth, attributed to the earthy 32nd path (Malkuth-as-element), and it is the disk or coin engraved with the figures of the Work—the implement of the body, of matter, and of all that has come into manifestation. Where the Wand wills, the Cup loves, and the Sword thinks, the Pantacle is: it is substance, the consecrated ground on which all is built and the bread by which the magician is nourished. It contains the whole universe in miniature, every force ordered upon its surface. Esoterically the Pantacle is the perfected body and the manifest world taken up as a sacred instrument—the field of earth made holy, the solid foundation in which the spirit's work becomes real and is fed.

the-perfumes.summary: The suffumigations of Yesod—the consecrated incense that conditions the astral atmosphere of the Work.
the-perfumes.description: The Perfumes are attributed to Yesod, the foundational and astral sphere, and they are the consecrated incenses and suffumigations burned in the rite—the fragrances chosen by correspondence to attract a given force and to condition the subtle atmosphere of the working. Paired in the table with the Sandals, the Perfumes belong to Yesod's office as the astral foundation: scent works directly upon the astral and the memory, shaping the unseen environment in which the operation unfolds. The right perfume calls the right power. Esoterically the Perfumes are the magician's means of attuning the astral plane—the fragrant offerings that prepare and charge the subtle atmosphere of Yesod, drawing the desired influence near and conditioning the foundation upon which the visible work is raised.

the-phallus.summary: The phallus of the Perfected Man, Yesod the Foundation and the generative root of the Tree.
the-phallus.description: The Phallus is attributed to Yesod, the ninth Sephirah, the Foundation. This is among the most exact of the correspondences in the body of Adam Kadmon: Yesod is traditionally the generative organ of the Tree, the reservoir of the astral and vital force, the channel through which the accumulated powers of the higher Sephiroth are gathered and discharged into Malkuth. As the phallus transmits the seed of life, so Yesod transmits the formative energy that makes the worlds fruitful—the foundation upon which manifestation is begotten.

the-plane.summary: The two-dimensional plane — Binah; extension into surface and form.
the-plane.description: The Plane is attributed to Binah, the third Sephirah. When the line is drawn sideways it generates the plane — the second dimension, surface and area, the first true 'form.' As Binah is the supernal Mother who gives shape and limit to the creative force of Chokmah, the plane is her geometrical emblem: extension that contains, the womb of figure within which solid bodies will be conceived.
tables: XLIX. Lineal Figures of the Planets, &c., and Geomany

the-pleiades.summary: The seven sisters — the star-cluster marking the lunar mansion of al-Thurayya.
the-pleiades.description: The Pleiades, the 'seven sisters' of myth, are the open star-cluster that the Arab tradition names al-Thurayya and which Liber 777 places in the path of Aries (Heh) among the Mansions of the Moon. Mythically the daughters of Atlas, set among the stars, they have marked the agricultural year for Greek, Polynesian, and Mesopotamian peoples alike — their heliacal rising and setting governing sowing and sailing. Esoterically they are a focus of multiplicity and of gathered light, a single radiant company.
tables: CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon

the-point.summary: The dimensionless point — Kether; the first and least manifestation of being.
the-point.description: The Point is attributed to Kether, the Crown. Having no dimension, no extension, no parts, it is the purest geometrical image of the first Sephirah — the unmanifest made just barely manifest, position without magnitude, the seed from which all extension unfolds. As the beginning of the dimensional series that descends the Tree, it is the mathematical emblem of the primal 'I am,' the one before all number.
tables: XLIX. Lineal Figures of the Planets, &c., and Geomany

the-priestess-of-the-silver-star.term: The Priestess of the Silver Star
the-priestess-of-the-silver-star.displayTerm: The Priestess of the Silver Star
the-priestess-of-the-silver-star.summary: The esoteric title of the High Priestess (Gimel): Priestess of the Silver Star, keeper of the lunar mysteries.
the-priestess-of-the-silver-star.description: ‘The Priestess of the Silver Star’ is the Golden Dawn title of Atu II, the High Priestess, on the path of Gimel (the Moon) that crosses the Abyss from Kether to Tiphareth—the longest and most secret of the paths. The Silver Star is Sirius, the star of the inmost initiation, and the order A∴A∴ (Argenteum Astrum) takes its name from her. She is the veiled lunar virgin who sits before the curtain of the sanctuary, holding the unopened book of the Law; her light is reflected, cool, and pure, the receptive memory of the cosmos. To pass her path is to ascend the central pillar by the silver thread of intuition toward the Crown.

the-prince-of-the-chariot-of-air-20-to-2.term: The Prince of the Chariot of Air. 20° ♑ to 20° ♒
the-prince-of-the-chariot-of-air-20-to-2.displayTerm: The Prince of the Chariot of Air. 20° ♑ to 20° ♒
the-prince-of-the-chariot-of-air-20-to-2.summary: Golden Dawn title and dominion of the Prince of Swords, ruling 20° Capricorn–20° Aquarius.
the-prince-of-the-chariot-of-air-20-to-2.description: ‘The Prince of the Chariot of Air. 20° ♑ to 20° ♒’ is the Golden Dawn (Book T) title and celestial dominion of the Prince of Swords, the airy, intellectual aspect of the airy suit—air of air, the most purely mental of the court—ruling from 20° Capricorn into Aquarius. Borne in his chariot through the heavens, the Prince is intellect in full and restless motion: brilliant, abstract, and tireless thought, the son who carries the cutting power of his element on wings of pure reason.
tables: LXIII. The Court Cards of the Tarot, with the Spheres of their Celestial Dominion Swords.

the-prince-of-the-chariot-of-earth-20-to.term: The Prince of the Chariot of Earth. 20° ♈ to 20° ♉
the-prince-of-the-chariot-of-earth-20-to.displayTerm: The Prince of the Chariot of Earth. 20° ♈ to 20° ♉
the-prince-of-the-chariot-of-earth-20-to.summary: Golden Dawn title and dominion of the Prince of Disks, ruling 20° Aries–20° Taurus.
the-prince-of-the-chariot-of-earth-20-to.description: ‘The Prince of the Chariot of Earth. 20° ♈ to 20° ♉’ is the Golden Dawn (Book T) title and celestial dominion of the Prince of Disks, the airy, intellectual aspect of the earthy suit, ruling from 20° Aries into Taurus. Borne in his chariot across the land, the Prince is matter governed by mind—the practical, deliberate, and competent son of the court, who carries the productive power of his earthy element forward with steady planning and material skill.
tables:
LXIV. The Court Cards of the Tarot, with the Spheres of 
their Celestial Dominion Pantacles.

the-prince-of-the-chariot-of-fire-rules-.term: The Prince of the Chariot of Fire. Rules 20° ♋ to 20° Virgo
the-prince-of-the-chariot-of-fire-rules-.displayTerm: The Prince of the Chariot of Fire. Rules 20° ♋ to 20° Virgo
the-prince-of-the-chariot-of-fire-rules-.summary: Golden Dawn title and dominion of the Prince of Wands, ruling 20° Cancer–20° Virgo (Leo).
the-prince-of-the-chariot-of-fire-rules-.description: ‘The Prince of the Chariot of Fire. Rules 20° ♋ to 20° Virgo’ is the Golden Dawn (Book T) title and celestial dominion of the Prince of Wands (the King in the Rider–Waite tradition), the airy, intellectual aspect of the fiery suit, ruling across the central degrees of Leo. Borne in his chariot of fire, the Prince is fire mastered and directed by mind—the questing, swift, and decisive son of the court, carrying the will of his element forward with disciplined, strategic force.
tables: LXXI. Court Cards of the Tarot, with the Spheres of their Celestial Dominion - Wands

the-prince-of-the-chariot-of-the-waters-.term: The Prince of the Chariot of the Waters. 20° ♎ to 20° ♏
the-prince-of-the-chariot-of-the-waters-.displayTerm: The Prince of the Chariot of the Waters. 20° ♎ to 20° ♏
the-prince-of-the-chariot-of-the-waters-.summary: Golden Dawn title and dominion of the Prince of Cups, ruling 20° Libra–20° Scorpio.
the-prince-of-the-chariot-of-the-waters-.description: ‘The Prince of the Chariot of the Waters. 20° ♎ to 20° ♏’ is the Golden Dawn (Book T) title and celestial dominion of the Prince of Cups, the airy, intellectual aspect of the watery suit, ruling from 20° Libra into Scorpio. Borne in his chariot upon the waters, the Prince is feeling governed by mind—the subtle, often secretive son of the court, who carries the powers of his watery element forward through intellect and will rather than mere emotion.
tables: LXII. The Court Cards of the Tarot, with the Spheres of their Celestial Dominion Cups

the-princess-of-the-echoing-hills-the-lo.term: The Princess of the Echoing Hills. The Lotus of the Palace of the Earth. Rules a 4th Quadrant of the Heavens about Kether
the-princess-of-the-echoing-hills-the-lo.displayTerm: The Princess of the Echoing Hills. The Lotus of the Palace of the Earth. Rules a 4th Quadrant of the Heavens about Kether
the-princess-of-the-echoing-hills-the-lo.summary: Golden Dawn title and dominion of the Princess of Disks: the Lotus of the Palace of Earth.
the-princess-of-the-echoing-hills-the-lo.description: ‘The Princess of the Echoing Hills. The Lotus of the Palace of the Earth. Rules a 4th Quadrant of the Heavens about Kether’ is the Golden Dawn (Book T) title and celestial dominion of the Princess of Disks, the earthy, culminating aspect of the earthy suit—earth of earth, the most material of the whole court. She rules the fourth quadrant of the heavens about the pole (Kether), the throne of the Ace. As the lotus of the palace of earth and mistress of the echoing hills, she is the power of matter brought to its fullest fruition, the threshold where one cycle ends and the seed of the next is sown.
tables:
LXIV. The Court Cards of the Tarot, with the Spheres of 
their Celestial Dominion Pantacles.

the-princess-of-the-rushing-winds-the-lo.term: The Princess of the Rushing Winds. The Lotus of the Palace of Air. Rules a 3rd Quadrant
the-princess-of-the-rushing-winds-the-lo.displayTerm: The Princess of the Rushing Winds. The Lotus of the Palace of Air. Rules a 3rd Quadrant
the-princess-of-the-rushing-winds-the-lo.summary: Golden Dawn title and dominion of the Princess of Swords: the Lotus of the Palace of Air.
the-princess-of-the-rushing-winds-the-lo.description: ‘The Princess of the Rushing Winds. The Lotus of the Palace of Air. Rules a 3rd Quadrant’ is the Golden Dawn (Book T) title and celestial dominion of the Princess of Swords, the earthy, culminating aspect of the airy suit. Like all the Princesses she governs a quadrant of the heavens about the pole, the throne of the Ace. As the lotus of the palace of air and the mistress of the rushing winds, she is the power of intellect brought down to earth—keen, wrathful, and decisive, the destroying and avenging aspect of the mind in action.
tables: LXIII. The Court Cards of the Tarot, with the Spheres of their Celestial Dominion Swords.

the-princess-of-the-shining-flame-the-ro.term: The Princess of the Shining Flame. The Rose of the Palace of Fire. Rules one Quadrant of Heavens round N. Pole
the-princess-of-the-shining-flame-the-ro.displayTerm: The Princess of the Shining Flame. The Rose of the Palace of Fire. Rules one Quadrant of Heavens round N. Pole
the-princess-of-the-shining-flame-the-ro.summary: Golden Dawn title and dominion of the Princess of Wands: the Rose of the Palace of Fire.
the-princess-of-the-shining-flame-the-ro.description: ‘The Princess of the Shining Flame. The Rose of the Palace of Fire. Rules one Quadrant of the Heavens round the North Pole’ is the Golden Dawn (Book T) title and celestial dominion of the Princess of Wands, the earthy, culminating aspect of the fiery suit. Unlike the Kings, Queens, and Princes—who rule bands of the zodiac—the Princesses govern a quadrant of the heavens about the celestial pole, the throne of the Aces. As the shining flame and the rose of the palace of fire, she is the energy of the element brought down to earth, vivid, fierce, and creative.
tables: LXXI. Court Cards of the Tarot, with the Spheres of their Celestial Dominion - Wands

the-princess-of-the-waters-the-rose-of-t.term: The Princess of the Waters. The Rose of the Palace of the Floods. Rules another Quadrant
the-princess-of-the-waters-the-rose-of-t.displayTerm: The Princess of the Waters. The Rose of the Palace of the Floods. Rules another Quadrant
the-princess-of-the-waters-the-rose-of-t.summary: Golden Dawn title and dominion of the Princess of Cups: the Lotus of the Palace of the Floods.
the-princess-of-the-waters-the-rose-of-t.description: ‘The Princess of the Waters. The Rose of the Palace of the Floods. Rules another Quadrant’ is the Golden Dawn (Book T) title and celestial dominion of the Princess of Cups, the earthy, culminating aspect of the watery suit. Like all the Princesses she rules a quadrant of the heavens about the pole, the throne of the Ace, rather than a band of the zodiac. As the rose (or lotus) of the palace of the floods, she is the power of water brought down to earth—gentle, dreaming, and infinitely receptive, the bride in whom feeling comes to its fruition.
tables: LXII. The Court Cards of the Tarot, with the Spheres of their Celestial Dominion Cups

the-prophet-of-the-eternal.summary: Part of the Hermit's title (Yod): the Prophet of the Eternal—the solitary bearer of inner light.
the-prophet-of-the-eternal.description: ‘The Prophet of the Eternal’ is part of the Golden Dawn title of Atu IX, the Hermit, on the path of Yod (Virgo) joining Chesed to Tiphareth; the full style is ‘The Prophet of the Eternal; The Magus of the Voice of Power.’ Yod is the first letter of the Tetragrammaton and the seed of all the others, and the Hermit—cloaked, lamp in hand—is the wise man who has withdrawn from the world to carry its hidden light. As *prophet of the eternal* he speaks not of the passing but of the enduring; his solitude is the fertile silence of the seed from which the Word will spring.

the-queen-of-the-thrones-of-air-20-to-20.term: The Queen of the Thrones of Air. 20° ♍ to 20° ♎
the-queen-of-the-thrones-of-air-20-to-20.displayTerm: The Queen of the Thrones of Air. 20° ♍ to 20° ♎
the-queen-of-the-thrones-of-air-20-to-20.summary: Golden Dawn title and dominion of the Queen of Swords, ruling 20° Virgo–20° Libra.
the-queen-of-the-thrones-of-air-20-to-20.description: ‘The Queen of the Thrones of Air. 20° ♍ to 20° ♎’ is the Golden Dawn (Book T) title and celestial dominion of the Queen of Swords, the watery, receptive aspect of the airy suit. Enthroned in the clear air, she rules from 20° Virgo into Libra. She is the keen, perceptive stillness of the element—intellect made graceful and discerning, the clear-eyed judge whose mind cuts cleanly yet sits in poise upon her throne.
tables: LXIII. The Court Cards of the Tarot, with the Spheres of their Celestial Dominion Swords.

the-queen-of-the-thrones-of-flame-20-to-.term: The Queen of the Thrones of Flame. 20° ♓ to 20° ♈
the-queen-of-the-thrones-of-flame-20-to-.displayTerm: The Queen of the Thrones of Flame. 20° ♓ to 20° ♈
the-queen-of-the-thrones-of-flame-20-to-.summary: Golden Dawn title and dominion of the Queen of Wands, ruling 20° Pisces–20° Aries.
the-queen-of-the-thrones-of-flame-20-to-.description: ‘The Queen of the Thrones of Flame. 20° ♓ to 20° ♈’ is the Golden Dawn (Book T) title and celestial dominion of the Queen of Wands, the watery, receptive aspect of the fiery suit. Enthroned upon flame, she rules from 20° Pisces into Aries, holding and steadying the fire that the King hurls abroad. She is the magnetic, enduring warmth of the element—fiery energy seated, sustained, and made constant in the form of the throned and gracious queen.
tables: LXXI. Court Cards of the Tarot, with the Spheres of their Celestial Dominion - Wands

the-queen-of-the-thrones-of-the-earth-20.term: The Queen of the Thrones of the Earth. 20° ♐ to 20° ♑
the-queen-of-the-thrones-of-the-earth-20.displayTerm: The Queen of the Thrones of the Earth. 20° ♐ to 20° ♑
the-queen-of-the-thrones-of-the-earth-20.summary: Golden Dawn title and dominion of the Queen of Disks, ruling 20° Sagittarius–20° Capricorn.
the-queen-of-the-thrones-of-the-earth-20.description: ‘The Queen of the Thrones of the Earth. 20° ♐ to 20° ♑’ is the Golden Dawn (Book T) title and celestial dominion of the Queen of Disks, the watery, receptive aspect of the earthy suit. Enthroned upon the fertile ground, she rules from 20° Sagittarius into Capricorn. She is the nurturing, fruitful repose of the element—matter as mother, the ambitious yet generous power that holds and ripens all that is planted in her.
tables:
LXIV. The Court Cards of the Tarot, with the Spheres of 
their Celestial Dominion Pantacles.

the-queen-of-the-thrones-of-the-waters-2.term: The Queen of the Thrones of the Waters. 20° ♊ to 20° ♋
the-queen-of-the-thrones-of-the-waters-2.displayTerm: The Queen of the Thrones of the Waters. 20° ♊ to 20° ♋
the-queen-of-the-thrones-of-the-waters-2.summary: Golden Dawn title and dominion of the Queen of Cups, ruling 20° Gemini–20° Cancer.
the-queen-of-the-thrones-of-the-waters-2.description: ‘The Queen of the Thrones of the Waters. 20° ♊ to 20° ♋’ is the Golden Dawn (Book T) title and celestial dominion of the Queen of Cups, the watery, receptive aspect of the watery suit—water of water, the most purely reflective of the court. Enthroned upon the still waters, she rules from 20° Gemini into Cancer. She is the tranquil, dreaming, mirror-like depth of the element: feeling at rest, the receptive vessel that holds and reflects all that is poured into it.
tables: LXII. The Court Cards of the Tarot, with the Spheres of their Celestial Dominion Cups

the-red-tincture.summary: The solar elixir of the alchemists, the red stone that transmutes base metal into gold.
the-red-tincture.description: The Red Tincture is set at Resh and the Sun, the radiant centre of gold and perfected power. In alchemy the red stone, or Rubedo, is the higher of the two great elixirs: the agent that transmutes base metals into gold and confers the fullness of the Work. Its solar attribution is exact, for it is the achievement of the golden, kingly perfection, the masculine and active culmination of the laboratory mystery that mirrors the soul made wholly luminous.

the-reins.summary: The reins of the Perfected Man—the loins and kidneys, the seat of inmost will and judgment.
the-reins.description: The Reins—an old word for the kidneys and loins—are attributed to Aquarius, Netzach, and Hod in the body of Adam Kadmon. In scriptural usage 'the reins' are the deepest seat of conscience and secret thought, that which God is said to try and search. As the kidneys filter and balance the inner waters, the reins of the Perfected Man are the place where the hidden motives are weighed, the inmost counsel of the soul that lies below the heart's awareness.

the-right-earh.summary: The right ear of the Perfected Man, attributed to constricting Saturn.
the-right-earh.description: The Right Ear is attributed to Tav and Saturn in the body of Adam Kadmon. Paired with the Jupiterian left ear, the right is given to grave and limiting Saturn—the ear attuned to the deep, slow tones of time, endurance, and the boundary of things. In the symbolic body it is the organ of sober, disciplined hearing, receiving the austere wisdom of the saturnine sphere that listens to silence and to the long counsel of the ages.

the-right-eye.summary: The right eye of the Perfected Man, the solar eye that mirrors the Sun.
the-right-eye.description: The Right Eye is attributed to Resh and the Sun in the body of Adam Kadmon. By the old doctrine of the lights the right eye is solar—the radiant, active organ of clear sight, the eye of day that perceives by its own brilliance, as the Eye of Ra blazes in the Egyptian myth. Paired with the lunar left, it forms with its fellow the two luminaries set in the countenance of the Perfected Man, the Sun and Moon gazing out upon the world.

the-right-nostril.summary: The right nostril of the Perfected Man, the breath of Mars.
the-right-nostril.description: The Right Nostril is attributed to Pe and Mars in the body of Adam Kadmon. Paired with the Venusian left, the right nostril is given to fiery, forceful Mars—the channel of the hot and active breath. In the symbolic body and in the yogic reading of the breath as paired currents of energy, it is the martial conduit, the solar-heated inhalation associated with vigour, heat, and the rousing of force.

the-root-of-the-powers-of-air.term: The Root of the Powers of Air
the-root-of-the-powers-of-air.displayTerm: The Root of the Powers of Air
the-root-of-the-powers-of-air.summary: Golden Dawn title of the Ace of Swords: the Root of the Powers of Air.
the-root-of-the-powers-of-air.description: ‘The Root of the Powers of Air’ is the Golden Dawn (Book T) title of the Ace of Swords, attributed to the Crown (Kether) and the realm of Spirit at the head of the airy suit. As an Ace it is the pure seed of its element—Air in its first, root form, the principle of intellect, discrimination, and force invoked. It is the sword of the divine mind crowned, the origin from which all the powers of the Swords descend into the world.
tables: CXXXV. Titles and Attributions of the Sword Suit.
LXIII. The Court Cards of the Tarot, with the Spheres of their Celestial Dominion Swords.

the-root-of-the-powers-of-earth.term: The Root of the Powers of Earth
the-root-of-the-powers-of-earth.displayTerm: The Root of the Powers of Earth
the-root-of-the-powers-of-earth.summary: Ace of Disks — Root of the Powers of Earth; the seed of the material world in Kether.
the-root-of-the-powers-of-earth.description: The Ace of Disks, the Root of the Powers of Earth, is the seed and origin of the suit of Earth, attributed to the first stirring of its element below the Crown. As all the Aces are the roots of their elements in Kether, this is the pure principle of matter, substance, and manifestation before it has divided into number. In the Thoth deck it bears the mark of the Beast and the magician's monogram, the whole material world in potential — the point from which all earthly wealth and form unfold.
tables: CXXXVI. Titles and Attributions of the Pantacle Suit

the-root-of-the-powers-of-fire.term: The Root of the Powers of Fire
the-root-of-the-powers-of-fire.displayTerm: The Root of the Powers of Fire
the-root-of-the-powers-of-fire.summary: Golden Dawn title of the Ace of Wands: the Root of the Powers of Fire.
the-root-of-the-powers-of-fire.description: ‘The Root of the Powers of Fire’ is the Golden Dawn (Book T) title of the Ace of Wands, attributed to the Crown (Kether) and the realm of Spirit at the head of the fiery suit. As an Ace it is the pure, undifferentiated seed of its element—Fire in its first, root form before it has flowed into the numbered cards. It is the primal will and energy, the spark of the divine fire from which all the active powers of the Wands proceed.
tables: CXXXIII. Titles and Attributions of the Wand Suit
LXXI. Court Cards of the Tarot, with the Spheres of their Celestial Dominion - Wands

the-root-of-the-powers-of-water.term: The Root of the Powers of Water
the-root-of-the-powers-of-water.displayTerm: The Root of the Powers of Water
the-root-of-the-powers-of-water.summary: Golden Dawn title of the Ace of Cups: the Root of the Powers of Water.
the-root-of-the-powers-of-water.description: ‘The Root of the Powers of Water’ is the Golden Dawn (Book T) title of the Ace of Cups, attributed to the Crown (Kether) and the realm of Spirit at the head of the watery suit. As an Ace it is the pure seed of its element—Water in its first, root form, the wellspring of love, feeling, and the fluid principle. It is the Holy Grail in potential, the fountain from which all the powers of the Cups flow into manifestation.
tables: CXXXIV. Titles and Attributions of the Chalice Suit
LXII. The Court Cards of the Tarot, with the Spheres of their Celestial Dominion Cups

LXIV. The Court Cards of the Tarot, with the Spheres of 
their Celestial Dominion Pantacles.

the-ruler-of-balance.summary: Part of Justice/Adjustment's title (Lamed): the Ruler of Balance—the principle that weighs all deeds.
the-ruler-of-balance.description: ‘The Ruler of Balance’ completes the Golden Dawn title of Atu VIII/XI, Justice—Adjustment in the Thoth deck—on the path of Lamed (Libra): ‘The Daughter of the Lords of Truth; The Ruler of Balance.’ The figure holds the scales and sword, and rules the great equilibrium of cause and effect by which nothing is ever truly out of account. Balance here is dynamic, not static—the dancer's poise, the ceaseless adjustment that keeps the cosmos true. Every action is weighed; every imbalance is, in time, corrected.

the-ruler-of-flux.summary: Part of the Moon's title (Qoph): the Ruler of Flux and Reflux—the tidal swing of the deep.
the-ruler-of-flux.description: ‘The Ruler of Flux’ opens the Golden Dawn title of Atu XVIII, the Moon, on the path of Qoph (Pisces) joining Netzach to Malkuth; the full style is ‘The Ruler of Flux and Reflux; The Child of the Sons of the Mighty.’ Pisces is the last sign, the deep of dreams and dissolution, and the lunar trump governs the ebb and flow of the tides—of the sea, of the blood, of the unconscious. As *ruler of flux and reflux* the Moon presides over all that waxes and wanes, the perilous, glamour-haunted passage through the gate where the waters of birth and death meet.

the-sceptre.summary: The rod of sovereign fortune at Jupiter—the king's staff of rule, dominion and the turning wheel.
the-sceptre.description: The Sceptre appears among the weapons at Jupiter (the path of Kaph, the Wheel of Fortune), and the attribution deepens its kingly meaning: Jupiter is the great benefic, the planet of expansion, sovereignty and good fortune, and the sceptre is the rod of that ruling power. As the Wheel turns and dispenses fortune, the one who holds the sceptre commands from the still centre, governing the changes rather than being tossed by them. It is authority joined to magnanimous abundance. Esoterically the Sceptre of Jupiter is the magician's sovereign command over the wheel of circumstance—the established rulership that, seated at the hub of fortune's turning, directs expansion and increase, the rod of the benevolent king who governs the very flow of luck and growth.

the-scythe-handle-is-a-tau.term: the scythe handle is a Tau
the-scythe-handle-is-a-tau.displayTerm: the scythe handle is a Tau
the-scythe-handle-is-a-tau.summary: Design detail of Death (Nun): the scythe-handle formed as a Tau.
the-scythe-handle-is-a-tau.description: ‘The scythe handle is a Tau’ is part of Liber 777's design for Atu XIII, Death (path of Nun, Scorpio): ‘A skeleton with a scythe mowing men; the scythe handle is a Tau.’ The skeletal reaper cuts down the living, but his implement is shaped as the letter Tau—the cross, the last letter of the alphabet and the sign of completion and of the path of the Universe. The detail teaches that death is not annihilation but the instrument of transformation: the Tau-handled scythe gathers life only to deliver it across the threshold into renewal.
tables: CLXXXI. Correct Design of Tarot Trumps

the-secret-force.summary: The hidden fire of Capricorn—the secret generative power of the horned god, the kundalini coiled in the dark.
the-secret-force.description: The Secret Force is attributed to Capricorn (the path of Ayin, the Devil), and it is the hidden, generative, serpent power that sleeps coiled in the depths—the secret fire of the horned god Pan, the kundalini at the base of the spine, the creative-sexual energy that the fearful brand diabolical and the wise revere as the very engine of life and of attainment. Its place at the Devil card is exact: what is called darkness here is in truth the concealed, irrepressible power of nature, dangerous only because it is so strong. To rouse and raise this force is the most perilous and the most fruitful of works. Esoterically the Secret Force is the magician's mastery of the hidden creative fire—the coiled power that, ignorantly feared but rightly awakened and directed upward, becomes the source of illumination and the secret strength of the whole Work.

the-secret-of-physical-strength.summary: The Taurean power of bodily strength, the magic of the enduring and rooted body.
the-secret-of-physical-strength.description: The Secret of Physical Strength is attributed to Vav and Taurus, the path of the Hierophant, the fixed earthy sign of the bull, emblem of solid, patient power. As a magical power it is the command of the body's vital force—endurance, vigour, the rooted strength of the ox—drawn from alignment with the steady, generative energy of Taurus. It is the most material of the powers, the foundation on which the subtler attainments must be built, for the temple of the spirit is the healthy and strong body.

the-self.summary: The Self — the divine 'I,' Yechidah, attributed to Kether.
the-self.description: 'The Self' renders, in the English column of the parts of the soul, the highest principle — the Yechidah, the unique divine spark, set at Kether. It is the true 'I' behind all the masks of personality, the indivisible point of pure being that is one with the source: the Self that the whole Work seeks to realise.
tables: XCVIII. Parts of the Soul English

the-shining-star.summary: The inner star of Binah—the point of light shining in the dark of understanding, the soul's guiding spark.
the-shining-star.description: The Shining Star is attributed to Binah, the supernal Mother and the sphere of the dark Great Sea, and it is the point of light that shines within that darkness—the guiding star of the soul, the inner spark that gleams in the deep of understanding and shows the way across the night. In a sphere all shadow and concealment, the star is the one luminous certainty, the light that is not of the daylight world but kindled in the depths. It recalls the Star of the magicians that goes before and leads to the holy place. Esoterically the Shining Star is the magician's inner guiding light—the spark of the higher self that shines unfailing within the darkness of Binah, the point of brilliance in the deep waters by which the soul orients itself and is led toward its source.

the-shoulders.summary: The shoulders of the Perfected Man, the Taurean yoke that bears the weight of action.
the-shoulders.description: The Shoulders are attributed to Vav and Taurus in the body of Adam Kadmon. As the shoulders are the strong, patient bearers of burdens—the yoke upon which the ox of Taurus labours—they answer to the fixed earthy strength of the bull, the steady endurance that supports the arms and carries the loads of the world. In the symbolic body they are the place of patient, rooted power, where the strength to act and to bear is seated.

the-slaughterer-s-luck.summary: The Slaughterer's Luck — the English meaning of the nineteenth lunar mansion (Sa'd al-Dhabih), in Capricorn.
the-slaughterer-s-luck.description: 'The Slaughterer's Luck' is the English gloss of Sa'd al-Dhabih (سعد الذابح, 'the luck of the slaughterer'), the nineteenth Arabic lunar mansion — named for the sacrificial knife of the priest who slaughters the ritual victim. Its principal stars are α and β Capricorni. In mansion-magic it is associated with cures from illness, the binding of evil, and the favourable concluding of difficult work — the 'luck' being that of the act that, however hard, completes the rite cleanly. Crowley places it at Capricorn (Ayin). See also: Sa'd al-Zábih.
tables: CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon

the-solid-figure.summary: The three-dimensional solid — Chesed; the first complete body in space.
the-solid-figure.description: The Solid Figure is attributed to Chesed, the fourth Sephirah. When the plane is extended in a third direction it generates the solid — the first body with volume, the complete figure of ordinary space. As Chesed is the sphere of stable, ordering Mercy, the foursquare builder of the manifest world, the solid is its geometrical emblem: form made full and substantial, the first 'thing' that can be measured and held.
tables: XLIX. Lineal Figures of the Planets, &c., and Geomany

the-son-of-the-morning.summary: Part of the Emperor's title (Heh): the Son of the Morning—the dawning solar-martial ruler.
the-son-of-the-morning.description: ‘The Son of the Morning’ opens the Golden Dawn title of Atu IV, the Emperor, on the path of Heh (Aries in Liber 777's older attribution). The phrase evokes the first light breaking in the east, the kindling fire of Aries that begins the zodiacal year, and the masculine, ordering power that establishes dominion over chaos. As the morning star heralds the sun, the Emperor heralds and frames the manifest world, fixing it within law, boundary, and rule. The full title continues ‘Chief among the Mighty,’ confirming his place as the sovereign of the active powers.

the-spirit-of.summary: The esoteric title of the Fool (Aleph): 'The Spirit of Aithêr'—the breath of pure spirit before form.
the-spirit-of.description: ‘The Spirit of Αιθηρ’ (Aithêr, the upper air or quintessence) is the Golden Dawn title of Atu 0, the Fool, the path of Aleph that joins Kether to Chokmah. Where the other trumps name powers and rulers, the Fool is named only as a *spirit*—the free, formless breath that moves over the face of the deep before any creation has condensed. Aithêr is the rarefied fire-air the Greeks set above the four gross elements, the substance of the gods themselves; to call the Fool its spirit is to place him at the very threshold of being, all potential and no fixity. He is the wind of which the wise say ‘thou knowest not whence it cometh,’ the holy madman whose emptiness is the precondition of every fullness to come.

the-spirit-of-the-mighty-waters.term: The Spirit of the Mighty Waters
the-spirit-of-the-mighty-waters.displayTerm: The Spirit of the Mighty Waters
the-spirit-of-the-mighty-waters.summary: The esoteric title of the Hanged Man (Mem): the Spirit of the Mighty Waters—sacrifice and immersion.
the-spirit-of-the-mighty-waters.description: ‘The Spirit of the Mighty Waters’ is the Golden Dawn title of Atu XII, the Hanged Man, on the path of Mem (elemental Water) joining Geburah to Hod. Mem is the maternal sea, and the trump is the soul suspended and inverted, drowned in the great deep that it may be reborn. The title names not a ruler but a *spirit*—the indwelling consciousness of the waters of sacrifice, the willing surrender by which the lower self is dissolved. The Hanged Man hangs in the posture of the slain-and-redeeming god, fertilising the world by his own immersion.

the-spirit-of-the-primal-fire.term: The Spirit of the Primal Fire
the-spirit-of-the-primal-fire.displayTerm: The Spirit of the Primal Fire
the-spirit-of-the-primal-fire.summary: The esoteric title of Judgement/The Aeon (Shin): the Spirit of the Primal Fire—the last trumpet and rebirth.
the-spirit-of-the-primal-fire.description: ‘The Spirit of the Primal Fire’ is the Golden Dawn title of Atu XX, Judgement (Crowley's Aeon), on the path of Shin (elemental Fire) joining Hod to Malkuth. Shin is the three-tongued letter of fire and spirit, and the trump is the great awakening—Israfel sounding the last trumpet, the dead rising from their tombs, the old order consumed and the new aeon born. As *spirit of the primal fire* it names the original, purifying flame that both destroys and resurrects, the call of judgement that is also the summons to a higher life.

the-star.summary: Atu XVII — Heh / Aquarius; hope, inspiration, and the pouring-out of cosmic grace.
the-star.description: The Star is trump XVII, attributed (in Crowley’s revision) to the letter Heh and the sign Aquarius, the path from Chokmah to Tiphareth. It is the image of hope, inspiration, and grace—the naked goddess Nuit pouring the waters of life from two cups beneath a sky of stars, renewing the world. Following the catastrophe of the Tower, the Star is the serene return of guidance and the promise of the infinite. Crowley’s declaration that ‘Tzaddi is not the Star’ swapped its attribution with The Emperor, one of the key reforms of the Thoth Tarot. The card teaches faith, openness, and the trust that the cosmos nourishes those who give themselves to it.
tables: XIV. General Attribution of the Tarot
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

the-sun.summary: Atu XIX — Resh / Sol; joy, clarity, vitality, and conscious illumination.
the-sun.description: The Sun is trump XIX, attributed to Resh and the Sun, the path from Hod to Yesod. It is the trump of joy, clarity, vitality, and the fully conscious self—light triumphant after the Moon’s darkness. Children dance in the unclouded radiance; the world is reborn in innocence and energy. As the letter Resh (‘head’) crowned by the solar disk, it marks the regeneration of consciousness and the simple, ecstatic affirmation of life. The Sun teaches that after the trials of the dark path comes the open, generous warmth of illumination, freedom, and renewed creative power.
tables: CLXXXI. Correct Design of Tarot Trumps
XIV. General Attribution of the Tarot
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

the-supreme-attainment.summary: The Supreme Attainment, the experience of the unmanifest beyond the Tree.
the-supreme-attainment.description: The Supreme Attainment is set at the Veils of the Negative, the boundless nothingness beyond Kether from which the whole Tree depends. It names the final goal toward which every Sephirah's vision is a stage: the dissolution of all attainment itself into the Unmanifest, the merging of the soul into the Naught that is the All. Beyond the Crown there is no longer experience of anything, for the experiencer and the experienced are gone; this is the last surrender, the attainment that is the cessation of attaining.

the-sword.summary: The magical weapon of Air and the intellect—the blade of analysis and severity, the implement of Geburah.
the-sword.description: The Sword is the elemental weapon of Air and of the discriminating intellect, attributed to Mars and to Geburah, the severe sphere of strength and judgement. It is the blade that divides, distinguishes and destroys—the analytic mind that cuts the true from the false, and the warrior's steel that strikes down what cannot stand. Where the Cup gathers, the Sword separates; its keenness is the rigour of reason and the cold courage of Geburah. In the magician's hand it banishes and defends, clearing the field of working by force. Esoterically the Sword is the trained, fearless intellect wielded with severity—the power to analyse, to judge, and to cut away all that is false or superfluous, the necessary harshness that purifies by division.

the-tao.summary: The Tao — the unnameable Way, attributed to the Veils of the Negative.
the-tao.description: The Tao, the 'Way' that cannot be named, is set in 777 at the Veils of the Negative — the three veils (Ain, Ain Soph, Ain Soph Aur) that precede and exceed even Kether. The attribution is exact: like the Ain, the Tao is the unconditioned source 'that was before Heaven and Earth,' empty yet inexhaustible, the nameless root from which the named ten thousand things arise.

the-tesseract.summary: The four-dimensional figure — Geburah; the solid extended beyond ordinary space.
the-tesseract.description: The Tesseract is attributed to Geburah, the fifth Sephirah. It is the four-dimensional analogue of the cube — the solid figure extended into a direction beyond the three of common experience, a body whose 'faces' are themselves solids. As Geburah is the sphere of severity and transcendent force, the tesseract is its geometrical emblem: form pushed past the bounds of the familiar world into a higher and more rigorous order of space.
tables: XLIX. Lineal Figures of the Planets, &c., and Geomany

the-throne.summary: The seat of majesty at Taurus—the chair of state on which the power is enthroned, stable and sovereign.
the-throne.description: The Throne is attributed to Taurus (the path of Vau, the Hierophant), and it is the seat of state—the chair upon which the god, the king, or the officiating power is enthroned, the emblem of established, seated authority and of the stability on which majesty rests. Its place at the fixed-earth sign of Taurus is fitting, for the throne is the very type of solid, immovable foundation raised into dignity: power not in motion but securely seated and at rest. The one who sits the throne rules from stillness. Esoterically the Throne is the magician's established and stable authority—the seat of settled power from which he presides over the work, the firm and dignified ground of being upon which the indwelling force is enthroned and from which it reigns.

the-thurible.summary: The vessel of sacred fire at Shin—the censer of the spiritual flame, incense rising in the element of fire.
the-thurible.description: The Thurible is attributed to the letter Shin and the element of Fire, and it is the censer in which the sacred fire burns and the incense is consumed—the vessel that carries the living coals and sends the fragrant smoke aloft. Where the same implement at Aquarius emphasises purification, here at Shin it is bound to the spiritual fire itself, the holy flame of the Aeon and of the descending tongues of fire. The thurible holds and dignifies that flame, making the fire portable and offering its smoke upward. Esoterically the Thurible is the magician's vessel of the spiritual fire—the bearer of the holy flame and the rising incense, the implement by which the sacred fire is contained, carried, and offered as the prayer and aspiration of the spirit ascend in its smoke.

the-tower.summary: Atu XVI — Pe / Mars; sudden destruction of false structures by divine force.
the-tower.description: The Tower is trump XVI, attributed to Pe and Mars, the path from Netzach to Hod. It is the lightning-stroke of sudden, liberating destruction—the false structure of the ego or the old order shattered by an irresistible higher force. Figures fall from the broken battlements as fire pours from the eye of Shiva or the mouth of the dragon. Martial and abrupt, the card marks the violent breaking-down that precedes real rebuilding. The Tower teaches that what is built on illusion must fall, and that catastrophe can be the merciful clearing of the ground.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

the-tripod.summary: The oracular seat of Gemini—the three-legged stand of the prophetess, the stable base of inspired vision.
the-tripod.description: The Tripod is attributed to Gemini (the path of Zayin, the Lovers), and it is the three-legged seat of the oracle—the Delphic tripod upon which the Pythia sat to deliver the god's inspired speech, the stand from which prophecy was uttered. Its three legs give perfect stability upon any ground, and its place at the airy, communicative sign of Gemini links it to the gift of inspired and divinely-prompted words. Upon the tripod the seer is steadied so that the voice of the god may speak clearly through her. Esoterically the Tripod is the magician's stable foundation for inspired utterance—the firm three-fold base, balanced upon any terrain, from which the oracular and prophetic word can be received and spoken without the seat itself being shaken.

the-twilight-of-the-place.summary: The conditioning dusk of Pisces—the half-light in which the astral grows visible, the gloom proper to vision.
the-twilight-of-the-place.description: The Twilight of the Place is attributed to Pisces (the path of Qoph, the Moon), and it names the dim, shadowy light deliberately created for the working—the deepening of the chamber into a half-darkness in which the ordinary daylight senses are quieted and the images of the astral can rise and be seen. Qoph is the lunar, dreaming path of vision and illusion, and twilight is its native condition: neither the full light of day nor utter dark, but the conditioning gloom in which the unseen draws near. The magician dims the place to open the inner eye. Esoterically the Twilight of the Place is the deliberate cultivation of the visionary state—the lowering of the outer light so that the inner light may dawn, the dusk in which the soul slips from waking certainty into the receptive condition where the astral becomes visible.

the-twin-merti.summary: The twin Merti — the double goddess of the two lands and the dawn, at Gemini.
the-twin-merti.description: The Merti are the twin goddesses of Egypt, often identified with Isis and Nephthys or with the tutelary goddesses of the two lands, here referred to Zayin and Gemini. As a doubled feminine power they preside over the pairing and balancing proper to the sign of the Twins — sister beside sister, the two crowns, the dawn and the dusk. They embody the sacred pair whose union completes a single divine office.

the-universe.summary: Atu XXI — Tav / Saturn & Earth; completion, the dancing whole, the Great Work accomplished.
the-universe.description: The Universe (the World) is trump XXI, the last, attributed to Tav and Saturn (with the element Earth), the path from Yesod to Malkuth. It is the trump of completion and fulfilment—the Great Work accomplished, the cosmos perfected and set dancing. The maiden of the world dances within the great serpent or the ellipse of the zodiac, surrounded by the four kerubic beasts, uniting all the elements and all the prior trumps in a single whole. As the final letter Tav, the ‘seal,’ it closes the alphabet and the journey. The Universe teaches that the end of the work is the joyous integration of every part—the One realised as the All.
tables: XIV. General Attribution of the Tarot
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

the-various-dhyanas.summary: 'the various Dhyanas' — Crowley's note at Malkuth in table XXIV for the Buddhist meditative absorptions.
the-various-dhyanas.description: In table XXIV ('Certain of the Hindu/Buddhist Results') Crowley closes the Malkuth cell with the phrase 'the various Dhyanas' — pointing to the four (or eight, or nine) jhana / dhyana states of Buddhist meditation: the successive absorptions in which the meditator passes from the first jhana (with applied and sustained thought) through the formless realms toward the cessation of perception. The phrase collects the full ladder at the foot of the Tree as the meditative ground from which the higher attainments rise. The entry preserves Crowley's pointer as it appears in the source.
tables: XXIV. Certain of the Hindu/Buddhist Results

the-virgin-mary.summary: The Virgin Mary — Theotokos, attributed to Binah the supernal Mother and to Malkuth the Bride.
the-virgin-mary.description: The Virgin Mary is set at once at Binah, the supernal Mother and Great Sea, and at Malkuth, the Bride and Queen of the manifest world — the two poles of the feminine on the Tree. As Theotokos, the God-bearer, she embodies Binah's dark, formative, sorrowful maternity; as the lowly handmaiden crowned in heaven she is Malkuth, the Daughter raised to the Mother's throne. The double attribution captures the whole arc of the divine feminine, from the heavenly Mother to the earthly Queen.
tables: XXXVI. Selection of Christian Gods (10); Apostles (12); Evangelists(4); and Churches of Asia (7)

the-vision-of-beauty-triumphant.summary: The Vision of Beauty Triumphant, the rapture of Netzach and the sphere of Venus.
the-vision-of-beauty-triumphant.description: The Vision of Beauty Triumphant is the spiritual experience of Netzach, the seventh Sephirah, the sphere of Venus, love, and the many-coloured fires of feeling. To attain it is to behold all things suffused with an overwhelming loveliness, the victory of beauty over the gross and the dead—nature, art, and desire revealed as radiant expressions of the divine. It is the characteristic ecstasy of the artist and the lover raised to a mystical pitch, the world seen as the body of the goddess.

the-vision-of-god-face-to-face.term: The Vision of God face to face
the-vision-of-god-face-to-face.displayTerm: The Vision of God face to face
the-vision-of-god-face-to-face.summary: The Vision of God Face to Face, the supernal experience of Chokmah.
the-vision-of-god-face-to-face.description: The Vision of God Face to Face is the spiritual experience of Chokmah, the second Sephirah, pure Wisdom and the supernal Father. To attain it is to stand in the unveiled presence of the Divine as a living force—not an idea or an image but the very face of God beheld directly, as Moses begged to see. It is among the highest of attainments below the Crown, the encounter with the godhead as Person and Power that transforms the seer utterly.

the-vision-of-love.summary: The Vision of Love, the merciful experience of Chesed.
the-vision-of-love.description: The Vision of Love is named as the spiritual experience of Chesed, the fourth Sephirah, the sphere of Jupiter, mercy, and the loving Father. To attain it is to be flooded with the boundless, generous love that pours from the higher Tree—the all-embracing benevolence of the king who gives without measure. It is the expansive, fatherly counterpart to the desirous beauty of Netzach: love not as longing but as overflowing grace, the cup that runs over upon the whole creation.

the-vision-of-power.summary: The Vision of Power, the Martian experience of Geburah.
the-vision-of-power.description: The Vision of Power is the spiritual experience of Geburah, the fifth Sephirah, the sphere of Mars, severity, and burning strength. To attain it is to know the tremendous force of the divine will in action—the awful, exhilarating power that destroys all that is false and upholds the cosmic order by the sword. It is the warrior's mysticism, the experience of being made an instrument of irresistible might, tempered always by the justice that distinguishes power from mere violence.

the-vision-of-sorrow.summary: The Vision of Sorrow, the dark supernal experience of Binah.
the-vision-of-sorrow.description: The Vision of Sorrow is the spiritual experience of Binah, the third Sephirah, the supernal Mother and the dark sea of Understanding. To attain it is to comprehend the whole grief of existence—the suffering inseparable from manifestation, the price of birth which is death, the sorrow of the Mother who brings forth only to lose. It is not despair but understanding: the deep, compassionate knowledge of the cost of being, which opens the heart toward the Abyss and the giving-up of self.

the-vision-of-splendour.summary: The Vision of Splendour, the Mercurial experience of Hod.
the-vision-of-splendour.description: The Vision of Splendour is the spiritual experience of Hod, the eighth Sephirah, the sphere of Mercury and of the ordering intellect. To attain it is to behold the glory of the divine as it shines through the structures of mind and form—the dazzling intricacy of the names, numbers, and systems by which the universe is rendered intelligible. It is the rapture of the philosopher and the magician of the word, the splendour of God revealed in the architecture of thought.

the-vision-of-the-harmony-of-things.term: The Vision of the Harmony of Things
the-vision-of-the-harmony-of-things.displayTerm: The Vision of the Harmony of Things
the-vision-of-the-harmony-of-things.summary: The Vision of the Harmony of Things, the solar experience of Tiphareth.
the-vision-of-the-harmony-of-things.description: The Vision of the Harmony of Things is the spiritual experience of Tiphareth, the sixth Sephirah, the harmonising heart of the Tree and the sphere of the Sun. To attain it is to perceive the perfect concord underlying all apparent discord—every force, however opposed, revealed as a note in a single unbroken music, the universe disclosed as a harmony rather than a war. It is the reconciling vision of the centre, where all the rays of the Tree converge in beauty.

the-vision-of-the-holy-guardian-angel.term: The Vision of the Holy Guardian Angel
the-vision-of-the-holy-guardian-angel.displayTerm: The Vision of the Holy Guardian Angel
the-vision-of-the-holy-guardian-angel.summary: The Vision of the Holy Guardian Angel, the redeeming experience of Malkuth.
the-vision-of-the-holy-guardian-angel.description: The Vision of the Holy Guardian Angel is named in the 777 column as the spiritual experience of Malkuth, the Kingdom—the first intimation, even amid ordinary life, of the divine guide who is one's true higher self. Though the full Knowledge and Conversation of the Holy Guardian Angel is the work of Tiphareth, its first vision dawns at the foot of the Tree, when the soul in the world of action glimpses that it is watched over and led. It is the seed of the whole Great Work, sown in the soil of the Kingdom.

the-vision-of-the-machinery-of-the-unive.term: The Vision of the Machinery of the Universe
the-vision-of-the-machinery-of-the-unive.displayTerm: The Vision of the Machinery of the Universe
the-vision-of-the-machinery-of-the-unive.summary: The Vision of the Machinery of the Universe, the lunar experience of Yesod.
the-vision-of-the-machinery-of-the-unive.description: The Vision of the Machinery of the Universe is the spiritual experience of Yesod, the ninth Sephirah, the astral foundation and sphere of the Moon. To attain it is to behold the vast interlocking mechanism by which the higher worlds are made manifest in the lower—the wheels within wheels, the subtle engine of cause and image that drives all phenomena. It is the engineer's mysticism of the astral plane, the revelation that the world of forms is a working machine of inconceivable intricacy and order.

the-wand.summary: The magical weapon of Fire and Will—the rod of authority and aspiration, the implement of Chesed.
the-wand.description: The Wand is the elemental weapon of Fire and the supreme instrument of the Will, attributed to Mercury, to the fiery letter Shin, and to Chesed, the sphere of rulership and benevolent power. It is the rod the magician raises to direct force, the sceptre of authority and the staff of aspiration that points the way upward—the disciplined, single-pointed Will made into a tool. Its fire is the ardour of the magician's purpose; its straightness is the rectitude of true intention. At Chesed it becomes the rod of just dominion, power wielded in mercy and order. Esoterically the Wand is the trained Will itself, the firm and upright purpose by which the adept commands the forces of the temple and ascends toward the source of his own authority.

the-waning-moon.summary: Liber 777's design for the Moon (Qoph): the waning moon.
the-waning-moon.description: ‘The waning moon’ is Liber 777's design for Atu XVIII, the Moon (path of Qoph, Pisces). The diminishing crescent presides over the trump of dream, illusion, and the perilous night-journey of the soul through the gate between the towers. As ruler of flux and reflux the Moon governs the ebbing tide, and the waning phase is the descent into the deep, the dimming light by which the soul must thread the dark waters of Pisces before the dawn of the Sun on the next path.
tables: CLXXXI. Correct Design of Tarot Trumps

the-waters-the-king-of-the-hosts-of-the-.term: the Waters. The King of the Hosts of the Sea. 20° ♒ to 20° ♓
the-waters-the-king-of-the-hosts-of-the-.displayTerm: the Waters. The King of the Hosts of the Sea. 20° ♒ to 20° ♓
the-waters-the-king-of-the-hosts-of-the-.summary: Golden Dawn title and dominion of the King/Knight of Cups, ruling 20° Aquarius–20° Pisces.
the-waters-the-king-of-the-hosts-of-the-.description: ‘The Waters. The King of the Hosts of the Sea. 20° ♒ to 20° ♓’ is the Golden Dawn (Book T) title and celestial dominion of the King of Cups (the Knight in the Thoth deck), the active, fiery head of the watery suit. His full style is ‘Lord of the Waves and the Waters, King of the Hosts of the Sea,’ and his rule spans the thirty degrees from Aquarius into Pisces. He embodies the moving sea—the dynamic, surging aspect of water, the warrior who rides and commands the deep of feeling and passion.
tables: LXII. The Court Cards of the Tarot, with the Spheres of their Celestial Dominion Cups

the-white-tincture.summary: The lunar elixir of the alchemists, the white stone that transmutes metal into silver.
the-white-tincture.description: The White Tincture, attributed to Gimel and the Moon, is the lunar counterpart of the red: the Albedo, the white stone that transmutes base metal into silver and marks the purification of the matter after its blackening. Its lunar attribution is apt—silver being the moon's metal and whiteness the colour of the washed and clarified soul. In the inner work it is the stage of attained purity, the moon's pale perfection, that precedes the final solar reddening of the Great Work.

the-whole-body-from-the-throat-to-the-ho.term: The whole body from the throat to the holy member
the-whole-body-from-the-throat-to-the-ho.displayTerm: The whole body from the throat to the holy member
the-whole-body-from-the-throat-to-the-ho.summary: The trunk of Adam Kadmon — Tiphareth, the heart and centre of the body.
the-whole-body-from-the-throat-to-the-ho.description: The whole body from the throat to the generative member is attributed to Tiphareth, the sixth Sephirah and the harmonising centre of the Tree. Just as Tiphareth gathers and balances the powers of the surrounding spheres, so the trunk — and pre-eminently the heart at its core — unites and sustains the limbs and organs of the macrocosmic Man. It is the solar centre of the body of Adam Kadmon, the seat of the reborn, integrating self.
tables: CIII. The Ten Divisions of the Body of God

the-whole-earth-is-full-of-his-glory.term: the whole earth is full of his glory
the-whole-earth-is-full-of-his-glory.displayTerm: the whole earth is full of his glory
tables: XCII. The Angelic Functions in the World of Yetzirah

the-wine.summary: The sacramental draught of Water—the blood of the god, the wine of communion and divine ecstasy.
the-wine.description: The Wine is attributed to the watery letter Mem (the path of the Hanged Man), and it is the sacramental draught—the blood of the god, the wine of the eucharist and of the Dionysian rite, drunk in communion to take the divine life into oneself. Its place at the still, sacrificial waters of Mem unites two of wine's meanings: the redeeming blood of the sacrificed god and the intoxicating draught that dissolves the boundaries of the self in ecstasy. To drink it is to partake of the god and to be loosened from the ordinary self. Esoterically the Wine is the sacrament of communion and ecstatic dissolution—the consecrated draught by which the magician takes the divine life into his own body and is, for a time, freed from the prison of the separate self, drowned and renewed in the god.

the-winged-egg.summary: The Orphic egg of Spirit—the winged cosmic seed containing all, the quintessence whence the worlds are hatched.
the-winged-egg.description: The Winged Egg is attributed to the quintessence, Spirit (31bis), and it is the Orphic Egg—the primordial cosmic egg, often depicted girt by a serpent or fledged with wings, from which the first-born god and the whole of creation are hatched. As the emblem of Spirit, the fifth element that is the root and reconciler of the other four, the Winged Egg contains all things in potential within its shell, the seed of the universe poised to unfold. Its wings show that this seed is itself living, spiritual, in motion. Esoterically the Winged Egg is the symbol of the quintessential spirit and the cosmic seed—the all-containing germ of being, fledged and ready to bring forth the worlds, the emblem of that spiritual root from which the four elements and all manifestation are born.

the-witches-sabbath-so-called.summary: The so-called Witches' Sabbath, the Capricornian gathering of the dark, earthbound rites.
the-witches-sabbath-so-called.description: The Witches' Sabbath, set at Ayin and Capricorn, the path of the Devil, names the legendary nocturnal assembly of witches with their horned lord—the Goat of Mendes who is the sign's own emblem. As a 'magical power' in the 777 column it stands for mastery of the chthonic, ecstatic, and transgressive currents that Capricorn governs: the fertility-rites and shadow-gatherings condemned by the Church yet rooted in older worship. Crowley read the Devil's path as the joyous, generative force of nature slandered into a demon, and the Sabbath as its maligned festival.

the-woman.summary: The Woman — a qliphothic shell at Malkuth, the harlot mirror of the Bride.
the-woman.description: Set at Malkuth in the table of averse orders, 'The Woman' is the qliphothic shadow of the Daughter and Bride who rightly crowns the foot of the Tree. Where Malkuth is the pure Queen, her shell is the harlot of illusion — the world embraced as an end in itself, matter mistaken for the whole, the false bride who is the husk of the true. It figures the great danger of the lowest sphere: the seduction of the merely material.
tables: CXXIII. Translation of the Orders of the Qliphoth

the-word.summary: The creative Logos of Chokmah—the first utterance by which all is made, the divine Word of the Father.
the-word.description: The Word is attributed to Chokmah, the supernal Father and the sphere of Wisdom, and it is the Logos—the first creative utterance by which the unmanifest light of Kether is sounded forth into being, the Word that was in the beginning and through which all things are made. Chokmah is the primal outpouring of force, and the Word is that force become articulate, the divine speech that gives form and law to creation. As a magical 'weapon' the Word is the operator's own creative utterance, his command that shapes reality in echo of the divine. Esoterically the Word is the supreme instrument of creative power—the magician's logos, the rightly-uttered command that, partaking of the Word of the Father, brings order out of the void and calls the intended thing into being.

the-yang.summary: The Yang — the active, light, masculine principle, attributed to Chokmah.
the-yang.description: The Yang, the bright, active, masculine, heaven-ward principle of Chinese cosmology, is set at Chokmah, the supernal Father and the sphere of dynamic, outgoing force. The attribution is precise: Chokmah is the great masculine fountain of energy on the Tree, exactly answering to the Yang that initiates, expands, and gives.

the-yin.summary: The Yin — the receptive, dark, feminine principle, attributed to Binah.
the-yin.description: The Yin, the dark, receptive, feminine, earth-ward principle, is set at Binah, the supernal Mother and the sphere of form, limitation, and the womb of manifestation. As Yang is to Chokmah, so Yin is to Binah: the receptive sea that gives shape and body to the formless force poured into it, the great cosmic mother of the Taoist polarity.

themeso.summary: Name of the first decan of Capricorn, the same Jovial face of fluctuating equilibrium.
themeso.description: Themeso is the name 777 records for the first decan of Capricorn (0°–10°), the Jovial face the gods-column calls Soda. Bearing the Two of Disks—Change—it marks the fluctuating equilibrium at the start of the Goat's ascent. Like its fellows it descends from the Egyptian decans, the ten-degree divisions of the ecliptic.
tables: CLXVIII. Egyptian Names of Asc. Decans.

themis.summary: Themis, the Titaness of divine law and order — the oracular embodiment of justice, at Libra.
themis.description: Themis is the Titaness of divine law, custom, and right order, an early holder of the Delphic oracle and counsellor of Zeus. Referred to Lamed and Libra, the sign of the scales, she is justice and natural law personified — the goddess who holds the balance and decrees what is fitting. Mother of the Horae and the Fates, she embodies the eternal order to which even the gods conform.

theoricus.summary: 2°=9, the grade of Yesod — the Theorist; mastery of the element of Air.
theoricus.description: Theoricus is the grade attributed to Yesod, the lunar Foundation. The aspirant masters the element of Air and is brought into contact with the astral plane, the treasure-house of images and the machinery that underlies the material world. The grade governs the imagination and the etheric body, the first ascent above the merely physical into the realm of formative force.

theregebon.summary: Diurnal angelic Lord of Libra within the Airy Triplicity.
theregebon.description: Theregebon is the day-governor of Libra among the angelic Lords of the Triplicities. As the cardinal member of the Air trine, Libra by day is the open weighing of justice and relation in the light of common sight; Theregebon presides over this daylight balancing of the scales, the public reckoning of fairness.

thesogar.summary: Presiding god of the first decan of Gemini, where mutable air first scatters into restless thought.
thesogar.description: Thesogar presides over the first decan of Gemini (0°–10°), the entry into mutable air. Jupiter rules this face and its card is the Eight of Swords—Interference—the crossed, over-busy mind of the Twins, thought tangling thought. In the decan system the Egyptians built as star-clocks and the Greeks turned into rulerships, this name marks where intellect first fragments into restless plurality.
tables: CLXVIII. Egyptian Names of Asc. Decans.

theta.summary: Theta — a letter of the Coptic alphabet (th), which Crowley attributes to the path of Teth (Leo).
theta.description: Theta is a letter of the Coptic alphabet — the script in which the Egyptian language was written in the Christian era, the Greek alphabet adapted to Egyptian speech. It is from Greek theta. Crowley folds the Coptic alphabet into the great correspondence of letters and paths in 777 (Table LI), assigning Theta to the path of Teth (Leo) on the Tree of Life, so that the Egyptian-Christian script takes its station among the Hebrew letters and the keys of the Tarot.
tables: LI. Names of the Coptic Letters

thighs.summary: The thighs, attributed to Sagittarius, the muscular drive of the centaur's stride.
thighs.description: The Thighs are attributed to Samekh and Sagittarius. With the hips, the thighs fall under the governance of the archer-centaur, whose lower body is the horse: the great muscles of locomotion that bear the body forward and lend the stride its power. Sagittarius, the mutable fire of journeying and aspiration, rules these limbs of movement, the strong thews by which the upright human travels its road.

this-column-is-reserved-for-the-addition.term: this column is reserved for the addition of other pantheons …
this-column-is-reserved-for-the-addition.displayTerm: this column is reserved for the addition of other pantheons …

thistle.summary: The armoured flower of Capricorn—the thistle, hardy and defended, thriving upon the goat's barren slopes.
thistle.description: The Thistle is attributed to Capricorn (Ayin, the Devil). Spiny, tenacious, and thriving upon poor and stony ground, it embodies the hardy, defended, ambitious endurance of the saturnine goat-sign—beauty and nourishment locked behind a wall of thorns. Esoterically the thistle is the well-armoured persistence of Capricorn, the flower that survives where the soil is hard, guarding its softness with iron defences.

thopibui.summary: Name of the second decan of Pisces, the same Jovial face of overflowing contentment.
thopibui.description: Thopibui is the name 777 records for the second decan of Pisces (10°–20°), the Jovial face the gods-column calls Sourut. Bearing the Nine of Cups—Happiness—it names the brimming emotional contentment at the heart of the Fishes' sign. Like its fellows it descends from the Egyptian decans, the ten-degree faces of the ecliptic.
tables: CLXX. Egyptian Names of the Succedent Decans

thoptius.summary: Name of the middle decan of Virgo, the Venusian face where discernment is rewarded with gain.
thoptius.description: Thoptius governs the middle decan of Virgo (10°–20°). Venus rules this face and it bears the Nine of Disks—Gain—material increase refined and made beautiful, the well-tended field at its most fruitful. One of the thirty-six decan-faces inherited from Egypt, it marks the rewarded discernment at the heart of the Virgin's sign.
tables: CLXX. Egyptian Names of the Succedent Decans

thor.summary: Thor, the thunder-god — wielder of the hammer Mjolnir, defender of gods and men, at Geburah.
thor.description: Thor is the Norse god of thunder, storm, and strength, the red-bearded son of Odin who guards Asgard and Midgard against the giants with his hammer Mjolnir.
