Referred to Geburah, the sphere of Mars and martial power, he is the very type of protective, crushing might — the thunderbolt made a champion. As the people's defender and the foe of chaos, he embodies courageous, world-guarding force.

those-of-triplicity.summary: 'Those of [Air] Triplicity' — Crowley's pointer in table XLIX to the lineal figures shared by the airy signs.
those-of-triplicity.description: Astrology divides the twelve zodiacal signs into four 'triplicities' of three signs each by element: Fire (Aries, Leo, Sagittarius), Earth (Taurus, Virgo, Capricorn), Air (Gemini, Libra, Aquarius), and Water (Cancer, Scorpio, Pisces). In table XLIX Crowley sometimes refers a position to 'those of [the] X triplicity' rather than restating the geometric figures cell-by-cell — a compact way of saying 'see the lineal forms of the other airy signs.' This entry covers the placement at path 11 (Aleph/Air) where the airy-triplicity reference appears.
tables: XLIX. Lineal Figures of the Planets, &c., and Geomany

those-of-y-triplicity.summary: 'Those of [Water] Triplicity' — Crowley's pointer in XLIX to the lineal figures shared across watery (and parallel) placements.
those-of-y-triplicity.description: A cross-reference label in Crowley's table XLIX — pointing to the lineal-figure set shared by signs and elements of a common triplicity. The slug here ('y' triplicity) is a transcription artefact for the elemental glyph 🜄 (Water) plus a stray 'y'; the entry encompasses positions where the formula appears in connection with the watery, fiery, and earthy triplicities. As with the airy version, it is shorthand: 'use the geometric figures already given for the other members of this elemental family.'
tables: XLIX. Lineal Figures of the Planets, &c., and Geomany

thoth.summary: Egyptian god of writing, magic, and wisdom; the divine scribe (Mercury).
thoth.description: Thoth (Egyptian Djehuti, Crowley’s Tahuti) is the ibis- or baboon-headed god of writing, language, magic, measurement, and wisdom—the divine scribe who records the judgement of souls and the inventor of the sacred letters themselves. In 777 he answers to Mercury and the sphere of Hod, the very patron of the magician’s art of names and correspondences. As the keeper of the ‘words of power,’ Thoth presides over the whole enterprise of esoteric knowledge; the Greeks identified him with Hermes, and from this fusion arose Hermes Trismegistus, legendary author of the Hermetic mysteries. He is the lord of the Tarot (the ‘Book of Thoth’) and of all magical speech.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

thought.summary: Thought — the mental function of the element Air, attributed to the path of Aleph.
thought.description: Thought is referred in 777 to Air (the path of Aleph), the swift, mobile, connecting element. As the mind moves, combines, and disperses like the wind, the airy element governs the function of thinking — the restless, mediating play of ideas in the microcosm.

tables: CLI. Magical Images of the Decans (Cadent)

thoum-aesh-neith.summary: Thoum-aesh-neith, Neith as the goddess of fire — the divine flame, at Shin.
thoum-aesh-neith.description: Thoum-aesh-neith is a form of the ancient goddess Neith in her fiery aspect, referred to Shin and the element of Fire. Neith is one of the oldest Egyptian deities, weaver of the world and goddess of war and wisdom; here her power is the primal flame, the creative and consuming fire. The name marks the fierce, igneous face of the great weaver-goddess, the fire at the root of the new Aeon's element.

three-stars-in-head-of-orion.term: three stars in head of Orion
three-stars-in-head-of-orion.displayTerm: three stars in head of Orion
tables: CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon

thrombosis.summary: Thrombosis at Samekh and Sagittarius — obstruction in the channels of the blood.
thrombosis.description: Thrombosis — the formation of an obstructing clot in the blood-vessels — is set on the path of Sagittarius, the mutable fire sign ruled by Jupiter. Sagittarius governs the hips and thighs and the great vessels of the lower body, and Jupiter the blood and its richness; thrombosis is the dangerous coagulation and blockage of that flow, abundance congealed into obstruction. Symbolically it is the arrow's path dammed, the coursing Jupiterian current stopped by its own thickening.

thrones.summary: Thrones — the English name of the angelic choir Aralim, the host of Assiah at Binah.
thrones.description: In the Qabalistic angelology each Sephirah commands its own choir of angels; “Thrones” (Table CI, the Angels of Assiah given in English) renders into the vernacular the Hebrew order Aralim, the host attributed to Binah. These are the Thrones, the strong and steadfast ones who uphold the seat of the divine, fitting the receptive stability of the supernal Mother. Crowley sets them at Binah on the Tree, where the choir gives angelic form to the energy of that sphere as it acts in Assiah, the world of action.

thrush.summary: The magical image of Caim — a thrush, then a man answering out of burning ashes — Goetic President of the second decan of Virgo (by night).
thrush.description: Caim (Camio, Caym), the fifty-third spirit of the Goetia and a great President, appears first in the form of a thrush, and then as a man bearing a sharp sword who seems to answer out of burning ashes or coals of fire. In 777 he is the nocturnal ruler of the second decan of Virgo. He is a good disputer who gives men the understanding of the voices of birds, the lowing of cattle, the barking of dogs, and the speech of the waters. The little songbird transformed into a swordsman speaking from the embers befits earthy, discerning Virgo — the keenness that reads meaning in the least of natural voices.

thuismis.summary: Traditional name of the last decan of Cancer, the same lunar face of emotional repletion.
thuismis.description: Thuismis is the name 777 records for the last decan of Cancer (20°–30°), the lunar face the gods-column calls Mercophta. Ruled by the Moon and bearing the Four of Cups—Luxury—it marks emotional repletion at the close of the Crab's sign. Like its fellows it descends from the Egyptian decans, the ten-degree faces used to divide the ecliptic into thirty-six watches.
tables: CLXXII. Egyptian Names of the Cadent Decans

thumis.summary: Name of the first decan of Virgo, a solar face of prudent labour echoing Thmei, goddess of truth.
thumis.description: Thumis is 777's name for the first decan of Virgo (0°–10°), the entry into mutable earth. The Sun rules this face and its card is the Eight of Disks—Prudence—the careful, skilful husbandry of the harvest-sign. The name echoes the Egyptian Thmei (Ma'at), goddess of truth and right measure, and this decan of discernment fittingly carries that note; among the thirty-six Hermetic faces it stands for diligent, exacting work.
tables: CLXVIII. Egyptian Names of Asc. Decans.

thyatira.summary: Thyatira — the church of works and love, attributed to Venus (Daleth).
thyatira.description: Thyatira, commended for its charity and service yet warned against the seductions of 'Jezebel,' is set in 777 in the path of Daleth and the sphere of Venus. The Venusian attribution captures both faces of the church — the genuine love and good works for which it is praised, and the carnal allurements against which it is cautioned.
tables: XXXVI. Selection of Christian Gods (10); Apostles (12); Evangelists(4); and Churches of Asia (7)

thyme.summary: The fragrant herb of Pisces—thyme, sweet and reviving, a perfume of courage, cleansing, and quiet dreams upon the path of Qoph.
thyme.description: Thyme is attributed here to Pisces (Qoph, the Moon). Its warm, sweet, reviving fragrance was burned to purify, laid among the dead, and used to bring courage and gentle, healing sleep—virtues that touch the dreamy, watery, threshold character of the Piscean path. Esoterically thyme is a perfume of the Piscean dream-gate—the clean sweet herb that purifies the air, steadies the heart, and eases the soul into the restorative waters of sleep.

ti.summary: Ti — a letter of the Coptic alphabet (ti), which Crowley attributes to 3 Binah.
ti.description: Ti is one of the Coptic letters drawn not from Greek but from Demotic Egyptian, added to the borrowed Greek alphabet to record sounds Greek could not write: it is the ti, a Demotic-derived sign standing for the syllable ti. Crowley folds the Coptic alphabet into the great correspondence of letters and paths in 777 (Table LI), assigning Ti to 3 Binah on the Tree of Life, so that the Egyptian-Christian script takes its station among the Hebrew letters and the keys of the Tarot.
tables: LI. Names of the Coptic Letters

tibetan.summary: Tibetan — a pantheon column Crowley reserved in 777 for future expansion, left unfilled.
tibetan.description: Crowley reserved a 'Tibetan' column in the pantheon tables (XXV-XXXII) for the Vajrayana Buddhist and Bön pantheon — Avalokiteshvara, Manjushri, Vajrapani, Tara, Padmasambhava, the wrathful yidams and protectors of the Tibetan tradition — but never filled it. He read widely in Buddhist sources (the table of 'Forty Buddhist Meditations' at XXIII attests to it), and the Tibetan pantheon would have mapped cleanly onto the Tree; in 777 itself, however, the column stands as an open editorial placeholder. The entry preserves it as such.

tiger.summary: The striped predator of Leo—solar ferocity and beauty, the ridden beast of Lust, splendour armed with claws.
tiger.description: The tiger is attributed to Leo, the fixed-fire sign of the Sun, and it is the most magnificent and terrible of the great cats: striped like living flame, supremely powerful, beautiful and merciless at once. It carries the leonine solar fire raised to its fiercest pitch—the devouring, ecstatic energy of the Lust card, the beast that is ridden and mastered rather than slain. Sacred in the East to gods of power and to the riding goddess, the tiger figures the splendour of force fully unleashed yet held in the hand. Esoterically the tiger is the blazing vital energy of Leo at its strongest—passion, courage and beauty fused into a single overwhelming power that the adept must learn to mount and to govern.

tiger-lily.summary: The flame-spotted lily of Aries—the tiger lily, bold and fiery, a flower of Martian ardour upon the Emperor's path.
tiger-lily.description: The Tiger Lily is attributed to Aries (Heh, the Emperor), the cardinal fire-sign of Mars. Its flame-orange petals flecked with dark spots and its proud, downward-flaring form give it a fierce, ardent character far from the white lily's chastity—a bold and burning bloom. Esoterically the tiger lily is fire and pride flowering together, the assertive, kindling energy of Aries made visible in a flower that seems to blaze.

tin.summary: The jovial metal of Chesed — expansion, sovereignty, and benign fortune.
tin.description: Tin is the metal of Jupiter and of Chesed, the merciful, expansive sphere — soft, bright, and anciently precious as the metal that, alloyed with copper, gave the world bronze and so an entire age of civilisation. Its jovial attribution carries the sense of beneficence and rule, the metal of the kindly king. Esoterically it belongs to the principle of magnanimous expansion and good fortune.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

tissues.summary: The tissues, attributed to Earth, the woven fabric of the body's substance.
tissues.description: The Tissues are attributed to Earth (32 bis). The woven fabrics of which the organs and the flesh are built—the very substance of the material body—belong to the earthy element, the principle of solid manifestation. As Earth is the ground in which all takes lasting form, so the tissues are the body made dense and tangible, the material weave through which the higher and subtler forces of the organism are clothed and brought to earth.

titan.summary: The Titans, elder gods of primordial power — the giant forces preceding the Olympians, at Gemini.
titan.description: The Titans are the elder race of Greek gods, children of Earth and Sky, who ruled before the Olympians overthrew them. Referred here to Zayin and Gemini, they embody the vast, primordial powers of nature — Kronos, Rhea, Oceanus, and their kin — the older order of cosmic forces. As the defeated elder gods they represent the titanic, pre-rational energies underlying the more ordered Olympian world.
tables: CLXXI. Egyptian Gods of the Zodiac (Cadent)

to-10.summary: Endpoint marker — paths terminating at Malkuth (Sephirah 10).
to-10.description: 'To 10' is the endpoint-marker for paths that descend all the way to Malkuth — the Kingdom, the manifest world, the foot of the Tree. Three paths arrive here: path 29 (Qoph/Pisces, the Moon, from Netzach), path 31 (Shin/Fire, Judgement/the Aeon, from Hod), and path 32 (Tav/Saturn, the Universe, from Yesod down the Middle Pillar). Together they are the three lowest paths, the threshold across which incarnated experience reaches up. The entry is the shared geometric address at the base of the Tree.
tables: XII. Position on the Glyph of the Tree of Life

to-2.summary: Endpoint marker — paths terminating at Chokmah (Sephirah 2).
to-2.description: In table XII Crowley specifies each of the 22 paths by its endpoints (e.g. '1 to 6,' '2 to 4'); the fragment 'to 2' is the endpoint indicator for any path running to Chokmah. The single path explicitly recorded here is path 11 (Aleph/Air, the Fool), which connects Kether to Chokmah down the supernal triad. The descriptor is a geometric pointer rather than a name: it tells you which Sephirah on the Tree the path enters at its lower terminal.
tables: XII. Position on the Glyph of the Tree of Life

to-3.summary: Endpoint marker — paths terminating at Binah (Sephirah 3).
to-3.description: The descriptor 'to 3' appears in Crowley's table XII as the endpoint-marker for paths whose lower terminal is Binah, the supernal Mother. Two paths arrive here: path 12 (Beth/Mercury, the Magus, from Kether) and path 14 (Daleth/Venus, the Empress, from Chokmah) — between them they form the upper supernal triangle's right and lower-right edges. As an entry the term is purely structural, a pointer to the position on the Tree at which the path enters.
tables: XII. Position on the Glyph of the Tree of Life

to-4.summary: Endpoint marker — paths terminating at Chesed (Sephirah 4).
to-4.description: The descriptor 'to 4' in table XII marks paths whose lower terminal is Chesed, the merciful Jupiterian sphere. Path 16 (Vav/Taurus, the Hierophant) descends from Chokmah across the Abyss to Chesed, crossing into the manifest world below the supernals. The term encodes only this geometric fact: the path's downward terminus is the fourth Sephirah.
tables: XII. Position on the Glyph of the Tree of Life

to-5.summary: Endpoint marker — paths terminating at Geburah (Sephirah 5).
to-5.description: In Crowley's geometric table XII, 'to 5' marks paths whose lower endpoint is Geburah. Two paths land here: path 18 (Cheth/Cancer, the Chariot, from Binah) and path 19 (Teth/Leo, Lust/Strength, from Chesed). Together they triangulate the upper Severity-side of the Tree. The entry is a structural pointer — the geometric address of the path's lower foot.
tables: XII. Position on the Glyph of the Tree of Life

to-6.summary: Endpoint marker — paths terminating at Tiphareth (Sephirah 6).
to-6.description: More paths flow to Tiphareth than to any other Sephirah, fitting its station as the harmonising solar centre of the Tree. The descriptor 'to 6' in table XII names this convergence: it collects path 13 (Gimel/Luna, the High Priestess, from Kether down the Middle Pillar across the Abyss), path 15 (Heh/Aries, the Emperor, from Chokmah), path 17 (Zayin/Gemini, the Lovers, from Binah), path 20 (Yod/Virgo, the Hermit, from Chesed), and path 22 (Lamed/Libra, Adjustment, from Geburah). The entry is the geometric address shared by all paths arriving at the heart of the Tree.
tables: XII. Position on the Glyph of the Tree of Life

to-7.summary: Endpoint marker — paths terminating at Netzach (Sephirah 7).
to-7.description: The 'to 7' descriptor in table XII marks paths whose lower terminus is Netzach, the Venusian Sephirah of feeling and victory. Two paths arrive here: path 21 (Kaph/Jupiter, Fortune, from Chesed) and path 24 (Nun/Scorpio, Death, from Tiphareth). The entry is purely structural — the geometric address at the foot of these paths on the right-hand astral level.
tables: XII. Position on the Glyph of the Tree of Life

to-8.summary: Endpoint marker — paths terminating at Hod (Sephirah 8).
to-8.description: 'To 8' in table XII names paths whose lower endpoint is Hod, the Mercurial Sephirah of intellect and form. Three paths arrive: path 23 (Mem/Water, the Hanged Man, from Geburah), path 26 (Ayin/Capricorn, the Devil, from Tiphareth), and path 27 (Pe/Mars, the Tower, from Netzach across the Tree). Together they ground the higher mind into Hod's analytic sphere — the entry is the shared geometric address.
tables: XII. Position on the Glyph of the Tree of Life

to-9.summary: Endpoint marker — paths terminating at Yesod (Sephirah 9).
to-9.description: 'To 9' is Crowley's geometric pointer in table XII for paths whose lower endpoint is Yesod, the lunar foundation Sephirah at the base of the Middle Pillar. Three paths converge here: path 25 (Samekh/Sagittarius, Art, from Tiphareth down the Middle Pillar), path 28 (Tzaddi/Aquarius, the Star/Emperor, from Netzach), and path 30 (Resh/Sol, the Sun, from Hod). The entry is the shared geometric address — Yesod, the dream-foundation of the astral plane.
tables: XII. Position on the Glyph of the Tree of Life
CL. Magical Images of the Decans (Succedent)

toad.summary: The chthonic creature of Aries and Yesod—witch's familiar, hidden poison and earthy transformation.
toad.description: The toad is set at Aries and at Yesod, an earth-bound, moisture-loving creature long bound up with witchcraft and the lower magics, the famed familiar of the cunning-folk. Squat and unlovely, it conceals a power of transformation—the fairy-tale beast that becomes a prince—and a real chemical potency in its glandular secretions, so that it has always been an emblem of the hidden virtue lurking in base and despised things. At Yesod, the lunar foundation and seat of the astral, the toad belongs to the world of dream, generation and the shaping of forms beneath the surface. Esoterically it figures the unglamorous matter that holds, concealed, the seed of metamorphosis.

tobacco.summary: The nicotine plant, attributed to Libra; sacred American herb and grave addiction.
tobacco.description:
Tobacco is set at the path of Lamed and Libra, the sphere of balance and offering — for among the peoples of the Americas it is one of the most sacred of all plants, the smoke borne upward as prayer, the herb of treaty, ceremony, and the balancing of relations between the human and spirit worlds. Stripped of that sacred frame and turned to habitual consumption, the same plant becomes one of the deadliest. Esoterically it is the offering-plant, the visible carrier of intention into the air.

Caution: tobacco is intensely addictive and a leading cause of cancer and cardiovascular death. This entry concerns its sacred symbolism, not its habitual use.
tobacco.caution: Intensely addictive; a leading cause of cancer and heart disease. Symbolic/historical entry only.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

toglas.summary: Treasures — the Nuctemeron genius of the eighth hour presiding over treasures, set by Crowley at Scorpio.
toglas.description: In the Nuctemeron — the “Day Illumined by Night” ascribed to Apollonius of Tyana and preserved by Éliphas Lévi — Toglas is numbered among the genii of the eighth hour, the spirit of treasures. He rules over treasure and the keeping and guarding of riches. Crowley arranges the twelve hours and their genii upon the paths of the Tree (777, Table CLXXIII), placing him at Scorpio (Nun).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

tolmophta.summary: Presiding god of the first decan of Sagittarius, the same Mercurial face of swift flight.
tolmophta.description: Tolmophta is the presiding god 777 assigns to the first decan of Sagittarius (0°–10°), the Mercurial face the names-column calls Eregbuo. Bearing the Eight of Wands—Swiftness—it marks the flight of the loosed arrow at the opening of the sign of the quest. It belongs to the Greco-Egyptian roster of thirty-six decan-rulers.
tables: CLXVII. Egyptian Gods of the Zodiac (Asc. Decans)

tomras.summary: Presiding god of the second decan of Sagittarius, the same lunar face of reserved strength.
tomras.description: Tomras is the presiding god 777 sets over the second decan of Sagittarius (10°–20°), the lunar face the names-column calls Sagen. Bearing the Nine of Wands—Strength—it names the reserved, tested power at the centre of the Archer's sign. The name comes from the Greco-Egyptian list of decan-rulers, the thirty-six faces of the night sky.
tables: CLXIX. Egyptian Gods of the Zodiac (Succedent)

tonics.summary: The strengthening, invigorating remedies, attributed to Leo — seat of vital force and the heart.
tonics.description: "Tonics" — the substances reputed to brace, strengthen, and restore the vital powers — are assigned to Teth, the path of Strength and the sign of Leo, the sun-ruled house of the heart and of vital fire. The attribution is one of pure symbolism: the sign of courage and inner force governs the drugs that fortify. Historically the category was a broad and uneven one, holding bitter botanical "bitters" and cinchona alongside the notoriously dangerous nerve-tonics of the nineteenth century — small doses of strychnine (nux vomica) and arsenic among them. Esoterically it figures the rallying and tempering of the life-force, Leonine strength as bodily resilience.
tonics.caution: Historical/symbolic entry only — not medical advice. Substances once sold as tonics included strychnine and arsenic, which are deadly poisons.

tooth.summary: Shin — 'tooth'; the triple flame of Spirit and Fire, path of The Aeon.
tooth.description: Shin means 'tooth' — the biting, grinding instrument — and its three-pronged form is universally read as a triple flame. In Liber 777 Shin is the path of The Aeon (Judgement), attributed to Fire and to Spirit, joining Hod to Malkuth. The three heads of the letter become the three mother-letters' fire, the threefold tongue of flame, the Holy Spirit's descent and the trumpet of the new aeon. The tooth that consumes is also the fire that purifies: Shin is the devouring, resurrecting flame.
tables: III. Translation of the Names of the Paths

topaz.summary: The golden solar stone of Tiphareth—the Sun, beauty, and the radiant heart.
topaz.description: The (yellow) topaz is attributed to Tiphareth and the Sun, its golden fire the perfect emblem of the solar centre of the Tree—beauty, harmony, and the radiant, integrating self. A fluorine aluminium silicate, golden topaz has been associated with the sun, with warmth, generosity, and clarity of will. In the Qabalistic scheme its solar gold marks it as the gem of the harmonised heart, the stone of the reborn god at the heart of the system.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

topmost-point.summary: The topmost point of the pentagram, attributed to Spirit, crowning the four elements.
topmost-point.description: In the Attribution of the Pentagram the Topmost Point is given to Spirit (31 bis), the fifth and highest member of the five-pointed star. The pentagram is the glyph of the rule of Spirit over the four elements: the single upward point lifted above the four below proclaims the supremacy of the quintessence, the divine spark that governs and unifies fire, water, air, and earth. It is the point of the will and of the indwelling god, the apex toward which the elemental forces are ordered.

tortoise.summary: The world-bearer of Yesod—the patient shelled beast on whose back the foundation rests.
tortoise.description: The tortoise is attributed to Yesod, the foundational sphere of the Tree, and it is the ancient cosmic emblem of the firm support beneath the world: in the old cosmologies the earth rests upon the back of a great tortoise, the slow, immovable creature that bears all things. Long-lived, patient, and armoured in its shell, the tortoise figures the steadfast foundation that endures while the swifter creatures pass—the base that does not move and does not fail. Its place at Yesod, the underpinning of the manifest world, is therefore exact. Esoterically the tortoise is the patient ground of all building, the slow imperishable support on which the higher structure stands, carrying its home and its protection with it through the long ages.

torvatus.summary: Discord — the Nuctemeron genius of the second hour presiding over discord, set by Crowley at Taurus.
torvatus.description: Among the genii of the second hour in the Nuctemeron of Apollonius of Tyana, Torvatus presides over discord. He sows quarrel and division, the breaking of accord between friends and allies. Lévi gives the roll of the hour-genii in his Transcendental Magic; Crowley tabulates them along the paths of the Tree (Table CLXXIII), assigning Torvatus to Taurus (Vav).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

totath.summary: Nocturnal angelic Lord of Taurus within the Earthy Triplicity.
totath.description: Totath is the night-governor of Taurus among the angelic Lords of the Triplicities, complement to the day-Lord Rayel. As the fixed ground of the Earth trine by night, Taurus is the patient earth at rest, the seed sleeping in the dark soil and gathering strength; Totath presides over this quiet, generative repose of matter.

touch.summary: The sense classically borne by Air/Vayu — the perception of contact and texture.
touch.description: Touch is the sense traditionally attributed to Vayu, the element of Air, in the Tattvic doctrine of the senses. Because contact and pressure are felt through movement and the meeting of surfaces — the province of the mobile airy element — touch is the faculty proper to Air. Diffused over the whole skin rather than localised in a single organ, it is the most pervasive of the bodily senses.

tourmaline.summary: The polychrome electric stone of Gemini — many colours and two charged poles.
tourmaline.description: Tourmaline is set on the path of Zayin and Gemini — a stone that grows in a greater range of colours than almost any other, often several within a single crystal (the 'watermelon' pink-and-green), and that becomes electrically polarised when heated, drawing and repelling at its two ends (pyro- and piezoelectricity). Its multiplicity and its charged dual poles both echo the Geminian theme of duality and exchange. The stone of the many-in-one and the living polarity.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

transformations.summary: The power of changing form, attributed to the all-pervading element of Spirit.
transformations.description: Transformations belong to Spirit (31 bis), the quintessence that contains and commands the four lower elements. As a magical power it is the art of changing one's own shape or apparent nature—the shamanic and witch-lore faculty of taking on the seeming of beast or other form. Because Spirit is the root of all the elements, the adept who governs it governs the boundaries between forms, and may put on or off the bodies of the lower world as a garment.

transmutations.summary: The Sagittarian power of changing the nature of things, the aim turned upon substance itself.
transmutations.description: Transmutations are set at Samekh and Sagittarius, the path of Temperance (Art), where opposites are combined and refined into a new and higher third. As a magical power it is the changing of one substance, condition, or quality into another—the alchemical reconciliation applied as a living art. The arrow of Sagittarius, shot from earth toward heaven, is the very image of the directed will that lifts the lower into the higher, the leaden into the golden.

travels-on-the-astral-plane.summary: The earthy yet boundless power of journeying in the body of light through the astral realms.
travels-on-the-astral-plane.description: Travels on the Astral Plane—astral projection—is attributed to Earth (32 bis), the ground from which the journey departs and the body that is left behind. As a magical power it is the disciplined sending-forth of the body of light to move through the visionary worlds, to test their gates with the proper signs and names, and to return with knowledge. That it is rooted in Earth is fitting: the firm foundation of a healthy, controlled organism is the launching-point of every safe ascent.

triangle.summary: The triangle of art at Malkuth and Saturn—the figure of constraint outside the circle, the geometry of manifestation.
triangle.description: The Triangle is attributed to Malkuth and to Saturn (the path of Tav), and in the magician's apparatus it is the triangle of art—the figure drawn outside the protective circle into which a summoned spirit is constrained to appear and be bound. As the simplest enclosed figure it is the geometry of manifestation, the first shape that bounds a space and makes a form possible; the three sides figure the threefold powers that hold a thing in being. Under Saturn it carries the meaning of limitation and the giving of form. Esoterically the Triangle is the principle of constraint that makes the formless visible—the disciplined boundary by which the operator compels the unseen to take a shape it can be commanded in, the form imposed upon force.
tables: XLIX. Lineal Figures of the Planets, &c., and Geomany

tristitia.summary: Geomantic figure 'Sorrow' — attributed to Saturn; grief, melancholy, downward weight.
tristitia.description: Tristitia, 'sorrow,' is one of the sixteen geomantic figures, attributed to Saturn and associated with Aquarius. Its downward-pointing form signifies grief, melancholy, suffering, and the heavy weight of Saturn — a figure of sadness, delay, and things sinking or buried. Unfortunate in most questions, it can yet favour matters that require patience, depth, or the slow working of time.
tables: XLIX. Lineal Figures of the Planets, &c., and Geomany

triumphal.summary: The Sixteenth Path — the Triumphal or Eternal Intelligence of Vav, the paradise of the just.
triumphal.description: The Sixteenth Path is the Triumphal or Eternal Intelligence (Sekhel Nitzchi), attributed to the letter Vav and the sign Taurus, the path of The Hierophant joining Chokmah to Chesed. The Sepher Yetzirah names it the pleasure of the Glory, the Paradise of Eden prepared for the righteous — the abiding delight in which the just find their reward. 'Triumphal' and 'eternal' share a root in the Hebrew Netzach (victory/eternity): this is the enduring, victorious sweetness of the higher Eden, the fixed and faithful bliss of the Bull-path.
tables: XIII. Paths of the Sefer Yetzirah

truce.summary: Four of Swords — Truce / Rest from Strife; Jupiter in Libra, Chesed of Air.
truce.description: The Four of Swords, Truce (Rest from Strife), is Chesed in the suit of Air and the third decan of Libra under Jupiter. The four blades arrange themselves point-to-point about a central rose, the warring mind brought to an ordered, merciful rest. It signifies the convalescence of the intellect — a negotiated peace, withdrawal and recovery, the settling of thought into a guarded but real repose.
tables: CXXXV. Titles and Attributions of the Sword Suit.

truthfulness.summary: The Mercurial virtue of truthfulness, the integrity of the speaking mind.
truthfulness.description: Truthfulness is the virtue of Hod, the eighth Sephirah, the sphere of Mercury and of the intellect and the word. As Hod governs speech, reason, and the systems of the mind, its proper virtue is the scrupulous honesty that keeps thought and word aligned with what is. Crowley regarded truthfulness, especially toward oneself, as the indispensable foundation of all magical progress: the mind that deceives itself can find no real attainment, and the first discipline of the aspirant is to record the truth without flattery.
tables: L. Transcendental Morality (10 Virtues; 7 Deadly Sins; 4 Magic Powers)

tt.summary: The 'Tt' double-stop sound-value — placed by Crowley at Binah, the third Sephirah.
tt.description: 'Tt' is one of the more obscure transcriptions in table LI, set opposite Binah — the great Mother Sephirah, the formative womb of all manifestation. The doubled stop most likely transcribes a Coptic letter whose value Crowley heard as a tightly geminated 'tt' (perhaps Ⲇ or a Bohairic variant); in Hebrew the closest analogue is the doubled Tav. Whatever the source-glyph, the entry's content is its placement alone: the heavy, time-bound, contained sound of the doubled dental, fixed at the sphere of Saturn and form.
tables: LI. English Equivalent of the Coptic Alphabet

tui.summary: Tui (Dui), the trigram of the Lake and joy — attributed to Venus and Water.
tui.description: Tui (two unbroken lines beneath a broken one) is the trigram of the Lake or Marsh — 'the joyous,' pleasure, the still gleaming water, the youngest daughter. In 777 it is referred to Venus (Daleth) and the element of Water (Mem): the gentle, reflective, delighting principle among the eight trigrams.

tuisco.summary: Tuisco (Tuisto), the earth-born ancestor of the Germani — the primal forefather, at Mars.
tuisco.description: Tuisco, or Tuisto, is the earth-born god named by Tacitus as the divine ancestor of the Germanic peoples, father of Mannus from whom the tribes descend. Referred to Pe and Mars, the planet of force and the warrior, he is the primal, vigorous progenitor of the nation. As the earth-sprung forefather he embodies the originating, martial vitality of the Germanic race.

tukiphat.summary: The schamir — the Nuctemeron genius of the eighth hour presiding over the schamir, set by Crowley at Scorpio.
tukiphat.description: In the Nuctemeron — the “Day Illumined by Night” ascribed to Apollonius of Tyana and preserved by Éliphas Lévi — Tukiphat is numbered among the genii of the eighth hour, the spirit of the schamir. His charge is the Shamir, the legendary stone-cleaving worm by which Solomon was said to have hewn the Temple without iron. Crowley arranges the twelve hours and their genii upon the paths of the Tree (777, Table CLXXIII), placing him at Scorpio (Nun).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

tum.summary: Tum (Atum), the self-created creator — the setting sun and the completed All, at Water.
tum.description: Tum is Atum, the primordial self-engendered god of Heliopolis who arose from the waters of Nu and brought forth the first gods from himself. Referred to Mem and the element of Water, he is associated with the setting sun and with completion — the totality of being returning to its source. As the “All” and the “Complete One,” Atum is both the first creator and the evening sun sinking back into the abyss from which it rose.

turquoise.summary: The sky-blue stone of Chokmah and Venus — heaven, protection, and the open sky.
turquoise.description: Turquoise, the sky-blue stone, is attributed to Chokmah and to Venusian Daleth — a sacred and protective gem across the Americas, Persia, and Tibet, worn as a guard against harm and an amulet of the open sky. Its serene heaven-colour binds it to the higher wisdom and to the gentle Venusian current; esoterically it is the stone of celestial protection and the blessing of the sky.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

turtle.summary: The shelled water-bearer of Cancer—the home carried through the deep, armoured shelter of the Chariot.
turtle.description: The turtle is attributed to Cancer, the watery path of the Chariot, and it shares with the crab the meaning of the protective shell carried always with the self—but the turtle is the creature of the open water, swimming the deep with its home upon its back. It joins the tortoise's symbolism of patient endurance and foundation to the lunar, maternal, sheltering nature of Cancer: the soft life sealed within a hard dome, moving slowly and safely through the great waters. Esoterically the turtle figures the self that bears its own sanctuary through the sea of feeling and dream, the armoured shelter of the Chariot advancing through the tides—security and tenderness carried together across the deep.

twin-deities.summary: The Twin Deities — the divine pair of Gemini, the doubled gods of the sign of the Twins.
twin-deities.description: “Twin Deities” names the principle of paired or doubled gods attributed to Zayin and Gemini, the sign of the Twins. Throughout mythology such pairs — Castor and Pollux, Isis and Nephthys, the two Horuses — express the Geminian theme of duality, complementarity, and the union of opposites. The twin gods stand for every divine pair whose tension and harmony mirror the two-fold nature of the sign.

twin-serpents.summary: The paired serpents of Mercury and Hod—the caduceus, polarity reconciled, the two currents twined upon the staff.
twin-serpents.description: The twin serpents are attributed to Mercury and to Hod, and they are the entwined snakes of the caduceus, Hermes's herald-staff about which the two opposed currents of force wind in balanced ascent. They figure the eternal polarity—light and dark, ida and pingala, the positive and negative streams—reconciled and made to climb together up the central rod. At Hod, the Mercurial sphere of mind and magic, this doubled serpent is the very emblem of the art: the magician's power to hold opposites in equilibrium and raise them as a single force. Esoterically the twin serpents are the kundalini in its dual aspect, polarity transmuted into ascent.

twins-of-god.summary: Thaumiel — the averse Crown; the divided godhead of the Qliphoth.
twins-of-god.description: The Twins of God (Thaumiel) are the Qliphothic counterpart of Kether, the highest of the averse orders. Their name marks the central horror of the shells: the divine unity perverted into a warring pair, the godhead doubled against itself. They are the demonic 'crown' from which the whole inverted Tree of unbalanced force depends.
tables: CXXIII. Translation of the Orders of the Qliphoth

two-beautiful-angels-sitting-in-chariot-.term: Two beautiful angels sitting in chariot of fire
two-beautiful-angels-sitting-in-chariot-.displayTerm: Two beautiful angels sitting in chariot of fire
two-beautiful-angels-sitting-in-chariot-.summary: The magical image of Belial — two beautiful angels seated in a chariot of fire — Goetic King of the second decan of Aquarius (by night).
two-beautiful-angels-sitting-in-chariot-.description: Belial, the sixty-eighth spirit of the Goetia and a mighty King said to have been created next after Lucifer, appears as two beautiful angels seated together in a chariot of fire, speaking with a comely voice. In 777 he is the nocturnal ruler of the second decan of Aquarius. He distributes preferments, senatorships and high offices, gives the favour of friends and foes and excellent familiars — but must be presented with gifts and sacrifices to give true answers. The twin radiant angels in their fiery car befit the airy sign of the Water-Bearer and its theme of dignities conferred — a fair seeming that conceals one of the greatest of the infernal kings. (For his fuller office see the entry on Belial.)

tables: CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon
CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon

tyler.summary: The guardian without the door, here at Malkuth — the outermost sentinel.
tyler.description: The Tyler (or Tiler) keeps the lodge from without, drawn sword in hand, ensuring that none but Masons approach and that the work proceeds unprofaned. Attributed to Malkuth, the outermost Sephirah and the boundary of the manifest Kingdom, the office is the final sentinel at the edge of the sacred space, dividing the temple from the world.
tables: CXV. Officers in a Masonic Lodge

typhon.summary: Typhon, the destroyer — the Greek name for Set, the chaos-monster, spread across the dark paths.
typhon.description: Typhon is the Greek monster of storm and chaos whom the Greeks identified with the Egyptian Set, the destroyer. Attributed in Liber 777 to Leo, Jupiter, and Scorpio, he is the violent, disruptive power of nature — the whirlwind, the volcanic fury, the adversary of the gods of order. In the Hermetic and Thelemic tradition Typhon-Set is the dark, dividing force whose opposition is woven into the very structure of the cosmic drama.
tables: CLXVII. Egyptian Gods of the Zodiac (Asc. Decans)
CLXXXI. Correct Design of Tarot Trumps

tzamiqiel.summary: Tzamiqiel, the angel set over Aquarius — the assisting intelligence of the sign on the path of Tzaddi.
tzamiqiel.description: Tzamiqiel is the angel attributed to Aquarius in the Golden Dawn and Crowley's 777 (Table CXLIII, the Twelve Lesser Assistant Angels of the Signs). The name carries the Hebrew theophoric ending ‑el, “of God,” marking him as a ministering intelligence rather than a ruling archangel: the lesser angel who carries the governance of the sign into act. Set over Aquarius (fixed Air), he embodies the patterning, water-bearing mind of the man; Crowley places him at the path of Tzaddi on the Tree of Life.
tables: CXLIII. Twelve Lesser Assistant Angels in the Signs (Transl).

udakkha.summary: Uddhacca — the Pali name for the ninth fetter, restlessness or mental agitation.
udakkha.description: Udakkha renders uddhacca, the ninth of the ten fetters, the agitation and unsettledness of mind that lingers as one of the higher fetters, set at Tiphareth. It is the subtle turbulence cut only at arahatship, the last disturbance of the central calm. (Its English face appears under 'Restlessness'.)

uncertainty.summary: Uncertainty — a qliphothic shell of the Veils, the negation of the unmanifest.
uncertainty.description: 'Uncertainty' is one of the translated names of the averse orders, set at the Veils of the Negative. As the divine Ain is the luminous, pregnant emptiness before all being, its qliphothic counterpart is mere uncertainty — the barren, formless doubt that is emptiness without promise, the void turned sterile. It marks the shadow-side of the negative veils: the abyss of meaninglessness mirroring the abyss of pure potential.
tables: CXXIII. Translation of the Orders of the Qliphoth

unchastity.summary: The Venusian vice of unchastity, the squandering of the generative fire.
unchastity.description: Unchastity is listed among the vices at Daleth and Venus, the path of the Empress and sphere of love and generation. As the shadow of Venus—goddess of desire and fertility—it is the dissipation of the sexual and creative force in mere indulgence, love debased to appetite. The Western tradition treats it not as the body's pleasure condemned but as the squandering of a sacred power: the same Venusian fire that, rightly used, creates and unites becomes, misused, the leak through which vitality and will are wasted.
tables: L. Transcendental Morality (10 Virtues; 7 Deadly Sins; 4 Magic Powers)

understanding.summary: Understanding—the third Sephirah; the Great Mother who gives form to force.
understanding.description:
Binah (בינה, ‘Understanding’) is the third Sephirah and the supernal Mother, the womb of form. Where Chokmah pours out undirected force, Binah receives, limits, and shapes it—the first imposition of structure, and therefore the origin of time, sorrow, and death. She wears the dual face of Marah, the bitter sea, and Ama, the bright fertile mother; the Qabalists call her both the Great Sea and the dark womb. Her planetary correspondence is Saturn, lord of limitation and form.

Binah completes the Supernal Triad (Kether–Chokmah–Binah) that lies ‘above the Abyss.’ To cross into her understanding is to accept the law of form: that to be anything is to be bounded, and that birth into form is also the beginning of mortality. Her virtue is silence.
tables: III. Translation of the Names of the Paths
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

undines.summary: The elementals of Water, set at Mem — the watery spirits of stream, lake, and sea.
undines.description: The Undines are the elemental spirits of Water among the Legendary Orders of Being, attributed to Mem, the path of the watery letter. In the Paracelsan scheme of the four elementals they are the inhabitants of water — fluid, emotional, beautiful beings dwelling in spring and river and ocean, the living soul of the element. Esoterically they govern the realm of feeling and the dissolving, reflecting currents of the magician's watery work.

undulating-ground.summary: An earth of the sevenfold scheme at Geburah — broken, hilly land of the Martial sphere.
undulating-ground.description: Among the Seven Earths, the 'Undulating Ground' is attributed to Geburah, the sphere of Mars and Severity. Its rising and falling, broken terrain answers to the Martial character of strife and unevenness — a rugged, troubled land of heights and hollows, the cosmic ground proper to the sphere of force, ordeal, and the rough discipline of strength.
tables: CV. Ten Earths in Seven Palaces English

unicellular-organisms.summary: The first life in the waters—the unicellular organisms of Pisces, primordial consciousness adrift in the deep of Qoph.
unicellular-organisms.description: Unicellular organisms are attributed to Pisces (Qoph, the Moon)—the most primitive life, single cells adrift in the primordial waters, the dim dawn of consciousness that Qoph and Pisces signify. As the 29th path is the darkest and most rudimentary, touching the animal and protoplasmic depths of the psyche, the single-celled creature is its perfect emblem: life and awareness at their first, formless stirring in the sea. Esoterically these organisms figure the beginning of incarnate consciousness, the faint flicker of the soul as it first takes a body in the waters of generation.

unicorn.summary: The pure beast of Aquarius and Chesed—the single horn of unity, untouchable virtue, the mercy that yields only to innocence.
unicorn.description: The unicorn is placed at Aquarius and at Chesed, the merciful sphere of Jupiter, and it is the supreme heraldic emblem of purity: a creature so wild and chaste that, by legend, it could be approached and tamed by nothing but a virgin. Its single spiralling horn is a figure of unity and of the concentrated power that streams from a single point—an apt token for the magnanimous, unifying mercy of Chesed. Under Aquarius, the sign of the ideal and the humane, it carries the dream of an incorruptible nobility. Esoterically the unicorn is the unblemished higher nature, the gentle yet untamable virtue that the soul must become pure to behold.

union-with-god.summary: Union with God, the crowning experience of Kether.
union-with-god.description: Union with God is the spiritual experience of Kether, the first Sephirah, the Crown and the nearest point to the unmanifest source. To attain it is to be made one with the Divine—the absorption of the individual will and being into the single point of pure existence from which all things flow. It is the summit of the manifest Tree, the mystic's final term below the Veils, where the drop returns to the ocean and the self is lost in the One.

uniting-intelligence.summary: The Thirteenth Path — the Uniting Intelligence of Gimel, consummation of spiritual truth.
uniting-intelligence.description: The Thirteenth Path is the Uniting Intelligence (Sekhel Manhig ha-Achduth, the Intelligence that conducts to Unity), attributed to the letter Gimel and the Moon, the long central path of The High Priestess crossing the Abyss from Kether to Tiphareth. The Sepher Yetzirah calls it the essence of Glory, the consummation of the truth of individual spiritual things. As the path that joins the Crown to the heart of the Tree, Gimel is the supreme uniter — the moonlit way of the soul's return, gathering the manifold into the One.
tables: XIII. Paths of the Sefer Yetzirah

unity-with-brahma.summary: Union with Brahman — the merging of the individual self in the Absolute, set at Kether.
unity-with-brahma.description: Unity with Brahma names, among the Hindu/Buddhist Results, the supreme attainment of union with Brahman — the dissolution of the apparent separate self into the one undivided reality — attributed to Kether. It is the goal of the Vedantic path, in which the drop returns to the ocean and 'That thou art' (tat tvam asi) is realised not as doctrine but as fact. Set at the Crown, it figures the final absorption beyond which lie only the negative veils; the ego-self is not improved but transcended utterly in the infinite.
tables: XXIV. Certain of the Hindu/Buddhist Results

unselfishness.summary: The Venusian virtue of unselfishness, the self-forgetting generosity of love.
unselfishness.description: Unselfishness is the virtue of Netzach, the seventh Sephirah, the sphere of Venus and of love. As the moral fruit of the sphere of feeling and desire, it is the turning of love outward—the forgetting of self in care for the other, the generosity that gives without counting. Where the vice of Netzach is lust, its grasping shadow, the virtue is the same force purified into selfless devotion: love that seeks the good of the beloved rather than the satisfaction of the lover.
tables: L. Transcendental Morality (10 Virtues; 7 Deadly Sins; 4 Magic Powers)

unstable-effort.summary: Seven of Swords — Unstable Effort; Moon in Aquarius, Netzach of Air: scattered will.
unstable-effort.description: Unstable Effort is the Golden Dawn name for the Seven of Swords, Netzach of the airy suit, the Moon in the last decan of Aquarius. The lunar instability undermines the resolve of the mind: a partial, hesitant attempt, force insufficient to its aim. The card warns of half-measures and the futility of effort that lacks conviction or support.
tables: CXXXV. Titles and Attributions of the Sword Suit.

uranus.summary: Uranus—sudden change, revolution, and awakening (modern planet).
uranus.description:
Uranus, discovered in 1781, is the first of the modern ‘trans-Saturnian’ planets and was absorbed into the esoteric scheme as the power of sudden change, revolution, genius, and awakening—the lightning-flash that shatters old forms. It resonates with the Fool and the uranian, electrical aspect of will, and is sometimes attributed to the element Air in its highest octave or to the path of Aleph.

Because Uranus lies beyond the visible seven of antiquity, its inclusion marks the living, evolving character of the correspondence system: as human knowledge of the heavens expanded, so the symbolic map was redrawn. Uranus brings the disruptive, liberating force that breaks the limits Saturn sets.
tables: CXXXIX. Planets Exalted in the Signs of the Zodiac
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

uthrodiel.summary: Angel of the third face of Scorpio, where pleasure decays into debauch and illusion.
uthrodiel.description: Uthrodiel presides over the closing decan of Scorpio (20–30°), where Venus meets the Seven of Cups, *Debauch* — corrupted desire, intoxication, the poisoned chalice. Venus drowned in Scorpio's waters becomes the lure of dissolution. Uthrodiel — whose theophoric ‑el marks it a servant of God even amid the mire — is the angel of the seductive descent that the soul must see through.

uvall.summary: The forty-seventh spirit of the Goetia, a camel-formed duke of Cancer who procures the love of women.
uvall.description: Uvall (Vual) is the forty-seventh spirit of the Goetia, a great and mighty duke of the decans of Cancer. He procures the love of women, tells things past, present and to come, and gains the friendship of friends and foes. He appears at first as a great dromedary or camel, then takes human form and speaks the Egyptian tongue, though not perfectly. A spirit of the watery sign, he is the winner of love and friendship.

vakabiel.summary: Vakabiel, the angel set over Pisces — the assisting intelligence of the sign on the path of Qoph.
vakabiel.description: Vakabiel is the angel attributed to Pisces in the Golden Dawn and Crowley's 777 (Table CXLIII, the Twelve Lesser Assistant Angels of the Signs). The name carries the Hebrew theophoric ending ‑el, “of God,” marking him as a ministering intelligence rather than a ruling archangel: the lesser angel who carries the governance of the sign into act. Set over Pisces (mutable Water), he embodies the dissolving, all-receiving compassion of the fishes; Crowley places him at the path of Qoph on the Tree of Life.
tables: CXLIII. Twelve Lesser Assistant Angels in the Signs (Transl).

valefor.summary: The sixth spirit of the Goetia, a duke of Taurus — a good familiar who tempts his keepers to theft.
valefor.description: Valefor is the sixth spirit of the Goetia, a mighty duke of the decans of Taurus. He makes a good and faithful familiar, yet his nature is to tempt those who keep his company to steal, and he is said to lead them at last to the gallows. He appears as a lion with the head of an ass, braying or bellowing. A spirit of the acquisitive earthy sign, he figures the thievish appetite that masquerades as a helpful companion.

valkyries.summary: The Valkyries, choosers of the slain — the warrior-maidens who bear heroes to Valhalla, at Air.
valkyries.description: The Valkyries are the Norse warrior-maidens, servants of Odin, who ride over the field of battle to choose the slain and bear the worthy dead to Valhalla. Referred to Aleph and Air, they are swift, sky-riding spirits, the winged choosers who decide the fate of warriors. As bearers of the heroic dead and pourers of the mead of the hall, they embody the glory and the cost of battle.

valor.summary: Seven of Wands — Valour; Mars in Leo, Netzach of Fire: courage against the odds.
valor.description: The Seven of Wands, Valour, is Netzach in the suit of Fire and the third decan of Leo, doubly martial with Mars in the Lion's sign. A single wand stands against six, the lone defender holding higher ground: it is courage drawn from a weaker position, the resolve to fight on though the advantage has been lost. Netzach's instability lends a note of desperation, but the title insists that boldness itself can carry the day.
tables: CXXXIII. Titles and Attributions of the Wand Suit

vampires.summary: The undead blood-drinkers, set at Cheth and Cancer — the night-feeders on the living.
vampires.description: The Vampires are an order of legendary beings, attributed to Cheth and the watery sign Cancer. Across the folklore of many nations they are the restless dead who rise to drain the blood and vitality of the living, repelled by the sun and warded by sacred signs. Set at the lunar, nocturnal sign of Cancer, they figure the parasitic clinging of the past upon the present — the unburied dead who will not relinquish life, feeding on the warmth of those who still possess it.

various-twin.summary: 'Various twin' — Crowley's category-note at Gemini for the twin-deity sub-class of the Geminian path.
various-twin.description: Beside 'hybrid Deities' in the Geminian cell of table XXII, Crowley adds 'Various twin' — collecting the explicitly paired twin gods of the world's mythologies under the Zayin/Gemini path: the Ashvins, Castor and Pollux, Apollo and Artemis, Romulus and Remus, the Egyptian Shu and Tefnut, the Yoruba Ibeji. The note is Crowley's editorial cross-reference at the path whose Tarot is The Lovers. The entry preserves it as the category-marker it is.
tables: XXII. Small Selection of Hindu Deities

varruna-avatar.summary: Varuna, the god of the cosmic waters and law — the all-seeing sky-ocean, at Geburah.
varruna-avatar.description: Varuna is the ancient Vedic god of the cosmic waters, the encompassing sky, and the moral order (rita), the all-seeing sovereign who binds wrongdoers with his noose. Referred to Geburah, the sphere of severity and judgement, he is the stern upholder of cosmic and ethical law, lord of the boundless deep. As the god who sees all and punishes the false oath, he embodies the inexorable justice of the waters and the heavens.
tables: XXII. Small Selection of Hindu Deities

vassago.summary: The third spirit of the Goetia, a good-natured prince of Aries who reveals the hidden and the lost.
vassago.description: Vassago is the third spirit of the Goetia, a mighty prince of the decans of Aries, of a nature good rather than malign. His office is to declare things past and to come and to discover what is lost or hidden; for this benign character he was sometimes favoured by scryers and crystal-gazers. Sharing the Arian decans with Bael and Agares, he represents the revealing, divinatory power of the fiery sign turned toward knowledge of secret and forgotten things.

vaya-bhawana.summary: Vāyu-bhāvanā — the meditation upon the air-element, set at the path of Air.
vaya-bhawana.description: Vaya-Bhawana is the 'cultivation of the air-element' among the Hindu/Buddhist Results, attributed to the path of Aleph and the element Air. It is the concentrative meditation upon air — its movement, lightness and pervading motion taken as the inward object — leading the mind into absorption and the powers proper to the element. One of the elemental bhāvanās, it answers to the air-kasiṇa; set at Air, it figures the meditator's union with the principle of motion and breath.
tables: XXIV. Certain of the Hindu/Buddhist Results

vayu.summary: The mediating element of intellect, breath, and communication.
vayu.description:
Air is the element of intellect, communication, and the breath of life—warm and moist, mobile, mediating between Fire and Water. In 777 it corresponds to the letter Aleph and path 11, to the Tatwa Vayu (a blue circle), and to the eastern quarter. Its weapon is the Dagger or Sword, its archangel Raphael, its elemental king Paralda, its creatures the sylphs.

The Hebrew Ruach means at once ‘air,’ ‘breath,’ and ‘spirit,’ and the same triple sense runs through pneuma and spiritus: the invisible medium of thought, word, and life. Air is the realm of ideas in motion, of analysis and exchange, the swift connective tissue that carries one thing to another.
tables: XXII. Small Selection of Hindu Deities
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

vedana.summary: Vedanā — the Pali name for feeling-tone, the second of the five skandhas.
vedana.description: Vedanā is the Pali term for the second skandha, the feeling-tone that colours every moment of experience as pleasant, painful or neutral, set at the element Fire. It is one of the most important links in the chain of dependent origination, for craving arises in dependence on feeling; the meditator who can rest awareness at the level of bare vedanā, neither clutching the pleasant nor fleeing the painful, cuts the process at its root. (Its English face appears under 'Feeling'.)

vehrin.summary: Angel of the second face of Sagittarius, where the fire gathers into tested strength.
vehrin.description: Vehrin governs the middle decan of Sagittarius (10–20°), attributed to the Moon and the Nine of Wands, *Strength* — power held in reserve, vigilant endurance. The Moon banks Sagittarius's fire into a guarded, ready force. Vehrin is the angel of the strength that has weathered every assault and still stands its watch.

veil-of-the-vault-of-heaven.term: Veil of the Vault of Heaven
veil-of-the-vault-of-heaven.displayTerm: Veil of the Vault of Heaven
veil-of-the-vault-of-heaven.summary: Vilon, the Curtain — the lowest heaven, the 'Veil' drawn and withdrawn at dawn and dusk.
veil-of-the-vault-of-heaven.description: Vilon, the Curtain or Veil, is the first and lowest of the seven heavens of the Talmud, here the 'Veil of the Vault of Heaven' attributed to Yesod and Malkuth. The Talmud says it serves no purpose but to be drawn back in the morning and rolled up at evening, renewing each day the work of creation — the simple curtain of the sky that divides day from night, threshold of the heavenly ascent.
tables: XCIV. The Heavens of Assiah English
CXX. Magical Images of the Sephiroth

velle.summary: 'To Will'—the fiery power of the Sphinx, the virtue of resolute will.
velle.description: Velle, 'to will,' is attributed to Shin and Fire, the fiery member of the Four Powers of the Sphinx—to Know, to Will, to Dare, to Keep Silent. As the power of Fire it is the burning, single-pointed resolution that drives the work to its end, the lion-faced strength of the magician's purpose. Crowley made the will the very axis of his philosophy—"Do what thou wilt shall be the whole of the Law"—and Velle names that flame: the determination that, kindled by knowledge, dares all and is sealed in silence.
tables: L. Transcendental Morality (10 Virtues; 7 Deadly Sins; 4 Magic Powers)

vengeance.summary: The Martian power of righteous destruction, the magic of the avenging sword.
vengeance.description: Vengeance is set at Pe and Mars, the path of the Tower, the lightning-stroke that throws down what is corrupt. As a magical power it is the wielding of destructive force against an enemy or an injustice—the operation of wrath made deliberate. Mars, lord of war and of severity, governs all such works, and the tradition is unanimous that they bind their worker most heavily: the sword of vengeance has two edges, and the avenger seldom escapes the recoil.

venus.summary: Venus—love, beauty, attraction, and art; ruler of Netzach and the path of Daleth.
venus.description:
Venus is the planet of love, beauty, harmony, and desire—the magnetic force of attraction that draws all things toward union. In 777 she rules the seventh Sephirah Netzach and the path of Daleth (the Tarot trump The Empress), governing art, pleasure, fertility, and the green growth of nature. Her metal is copper, her number seven, her emblems the rose, the dove, the girdle, and the myrtle.

As Aphrodite–Ishtar–Hathor she is at once the goddess of earthly passion and of the higher love that orders the cosmos. Brightest of the planets to the eye, Venus as both morning and evening star long carried a double symbolism of Lucifer the light-bringer and the gentle evening lamp—union of the high and the low under the single law of love.
tables: CXXXIX. Planets Exalted in the Signs of the Zodiac
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

vepar.summary: The forty-second spirit of the Goetia, a mermaid-formed duke of Taurus who rules the waters and festers wounds.
vepar.description: Vepar (Separ) is the forty-second spirit of the Goetia, a great duke of the decans of Taurus. He guides the waters and the ships laden with arms and armour; at command he makes the sea rough and stormy and causes it to appear full of ships, and he can make men die within three days by wounds that putrefy and breed worms. He appears in the form of a mermaid. A spirit of the earthy sign, he commands the perilous sea and the festering of mortal wounds.

verasua.summary: Name of the middle decan of Gemini, the Martial face where airy thought turns to a wounding edge.
verasua.description: Verasua is the name 777 keeps for the middle decan of Gemini (10°–20°). Mars rules this face, and it carries the Nine of Swords—Cruelty—the mind turned against itself, airy thought sharpened until it wounds. One of the thirty-six faces of the zodiac inherited from Egypt, it names the dark, anxious vigil at the centre of the sign of duality.
tables: CLXX. Egyptian Names of the Succedent Decans

versicles.summary: The sung verses of power at Hod—the short responsorial formulae by which the work is intoned and answered.
versicles.description: The Versicles are attributed to Hod, the Mercurial sphere of language and the magical word, and they are the short verses—the little spoken or chanted formulae, often call-and-response—that punctuate and drive the rite. Paired in the table with the Names, the Versicles belong to Hod's office of sacred speech: where the Names command by naming, the versicles invoke, affirm and answer in rhythmic, repeated phrases that build and focus the current of the working. Their brevity and repetition are their power, hammering the intention home. Esoterically the Versicles are the magician's rhythmic words of power—the brief, intoned formulae that carry and concentrate the force of the rite, the spoken verses by which the operator and the powers he addresses answer one another and the working is borne forward on the cadence of sacred speech.

vervain.summary: The sacred herb of Mercury—vervain, the Druids' and Romans' holy plant of enchantment, eloquence, and peace.
vervain.description: Vervain is attributed to Mercury (Beth, the Magus). The herba sacra of the Romans and a chief sacred herb of the Druids, it was gathered with rite for purification, oath, peace-making, and enchantment, and credited with virtues of eloquence, reconciliation, and protection—all proper to communicative, magical Mercury. Esoterically the vervain is the priest-magician's herb of the Magus, the sacred plant of articulate power, blessing, and the binding word.

tables: CXX. Magical Images of the Sephiroth

vesta.summary: Vesta, goddess of the hearth-fire — keeper of the sacred flame of home and state, at Virgo.
vesta.description: Vesta is the Roman goddess of the hearth, the home, and the sacred fire of the state, tended by the chaste Vestal Virgins whose flame must never go out. Referred to Yod and Virgo and to Capricorn, signs of purity and disciplined order, she is the pure, central fire of domestic and civic life. As the virgin of the hearth she embodies the warmth, continuity, and sanctity of the living flame.

via.summary: Geomantic figure 'Way' — attributed to the Moon; the road, journey, change.
via.description: Via, 'the way' or 'road,' is one of the sixteen geomantic figures, attributed to the Moon and associated with Cancer. Composed of a single column of four points, it is the image of a path or journey, signifying change, movement, and the course of events. Favourable for travel and for matters in transition, it is the lunar emblem of the road one must walk.
tables: XLIX. Lineal Figures of the Planets, &c., and Geomany

viaov.summary: The formula of Wisdom at Chokmah, the extended Word of the Father's outpouring.
viaov.description: VIAOV is attributed to Chokmah, the second Sephirah, the pure dynamic Wisdom and the supernal Father whose nature is the first outflashing of force from the Crown. Crowley gives it as a magical word of the highest masculine principle—a fivefold elaboration in the family of IAO, the seed-syllable of the god, lengthened to express the unbroken generative thrust of Chokmah, the Yod that fathers all the worlds. As the formula of the sphere of the Zodiac and the will-in-motion, it names the energy that is forever giving itself without diminution, the lightning-flash at the head of the Tree.

victory.summary: Victory—the seventh Sephirah; the sphere of Venus, emotion, desire, and nature.
victory.description:
Netzach (נצח, ‘Victory’ or ‘Endurance’) is the seventh Sephirah, the sphere of Venus and the first of the lower triad that governs the personality. It is the realm of the emotions, of desire, instinct, art, and the green force of nature—the victory not of the will but of feeling and longing. Its God-name is Jehovah Tzabaoth, its virtue unselfishness, its vice lust; its image a beautiful naked woman.

Netzach’s ‘victory’ is the persistence of life and love through endless cycles of nature. Paired with the cold intellect of Hod across the Tree, it supplies the warmth and impulse that reason alone cannot generate—the heart that drives the head.
tables: CXXXIII. Titles and Attributions of the Wand Suit
III. Translation of the Names of the Paths
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

vikkikika.summary: Vicikicchā — the Pali name for the second fetter, sceptical doubt.
vikkikika.description: Vikkikika (vicikicchā) is the Pali for the second of the ten fetters, the wavering doubt that divides and immobilises the mind, set at Chokmah. It is overcome at the first stage of awakening, when settled confidence replaces vacillation. (Its English face appears under 'Skeptical doubt'.)

vine.summary: The vine of ecstasy and sacrifice—Dionysus's gift and the True Vine, the blood of the god at Tiphareth.
vine.description: The Vine is attributed to Gemini (Zayin, the Lovers) and to Tiphareth. It is the plant of Dionysus and Bacchus, whose fermented blood is wine—the sacrament of divine intoxication, ecstasy, and the loosening of the bounded self. At Tiphareth, the place of the sacrificed-and-risen god, it becomes the True Vine whose crushed fruit is the blood of the saviour shared among his own. Esoterically the vine unites the two great mysteries of the solar centre: ecstasy that breaks the ego open, and the sacrifice by which the god gives his life that others may drink—the cup of joy and of redemption at once.

vinnanam.summary: Viññāṇa — the Pali name for consciousness, the fifth of the five skandhas.
vinnanam.description: Viññānam is the Pali term for the fifth skandha, consciousness or bare discernment, attributed in 777 to Spirit. It is the knowing that arises with each meeting of sense-faculty and object — eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness and the rest — the simple awareness 'that there is' an experience, prior to recognition or response. In the analysis of the aggregates it is not a permanent soul but a conditioned, momentary arising, dependent on the other aggregates as they are on it; its placement at Spirit marks it as the subtlest and most rarefied of the five. (Its English face appears under 'Consciousness'.)

virgin.summary: The pure maiden of Virgo—Isis and the wheat-bearing virgin, the untouched fertile potential of the sign.
virgin.description: The virgin is attributed to Virgo, whose very name and glyph she is, and she is the pure maiden of the harvest—Isis, Persephone, the celestial Virgin bearing the sheaf of wheat, the untouched yet fruitful figure who holds the seed of all increase in reserve. Hers is not barren purity but potential held inviolate, the consecrated wholeness from which, in its season, the harvest comes. Under Virgo, the sign of purity, discernment and sacred service, she figures the clean and dedicated vessel. Esoterically the virgin is the pure receptive matrix, the inviolate ground that must be kept undefiled so that the holy thing may be conceived within it—chastity understood as integrity, the untouched fullness ready to bear.

virgo.summary: Mutable Earth, ruled by Mercury—discernment, service, purity, and the harvest.
virgo.description:
Virgo, the Virgin, is mutable Earth ruled by Mercury—the sign of discernment, analysis, service, and the refining of matter toward purity. In 777 it corresponds to the letter Yod and the path of the Tarot trump The Hermit (path 20), the solitary sage bearing the lamp of inner light. It governs craft, health, work, and the careful perfecting of detail.

The celestial Virgin holding the sheaf of grain is an ancient image of the harvest mother and of spiritual purity—Isis, Demeter, the Madonna. Yod is the smallest letter, the seed-point of the Tetragrammaton, fitting for a sign concerned with the small, the precise, and the fertile potential hidden in the humble. Virgo’s gift is exact, devoted service; its shadow, anxious criticism.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

virile-force-reserved.summary: The conserved generative power of Virgo—continence as strength, the seed withheld and turned to the Work.
virile-force-reserved.description: 'Virile Force reserved' is attributed to Virgo, the sign of the Hermit and the Virgin, and it names the magical principle of continence: the generative power deliberately conserved rather than spent, the seed withheld and its energy redirected to the spiritual work. Virgo is the sign of purity and of the disciplined retention that gathers and refines, and here the virile force—the same creative fire figured by the lingam—is held in reserve, sublimated, raised. This is chastity understood not as denial but as the storing-up of power for transmutation. Esoterically 'virile Force reserved' is the conservation and sublimation of the creative-sexual energy—the deliberate withholding by which the force ordinarily spent in generation is gathered, refined, and turned upward to feed the Hermit's inner light and the Great Work.

virtue.summary: Three of Wands — Virtue; Sun in Aries, Binah of Fire: strength made steady.
virtue.description: Virtue is Crowley's title for the Three of Wands, Binah of the fiery suit, the Sun in the second decan of Aries. The raw will of the suit is here stabilised and matured: three wands firmly planted, the lotus-flames of pride turned to a calm and radiant confidence. It signifies established strength, generosity of energy, and the courage that comes from knowing one's own power.
tables: CXXXIII. Titles and Attributions of the Wand Suit

virvaso.summary: Traditional name of the second decan of Taurus, the same lunar face of fertile success.
virvaso.description: Virvaso is the name 777 records for the second decan of Taurus (10°–20°)—the same fixed-earth face the gods-column calls Helitomenos. Ruled by the Moon and carrying the Six of Disks—Success—it marks the point where the Bull's slow fertility yields a balanced harvest. Like all thirty-six decan-names it descends from the Egyptian division of the ecliptic into ten-degree faces used to tell the hours of the night.
tables: CLXX. Egyptian Names of the Succedent Decans

vishnu.summary: Vishnu, the great preserver — the all-pervading sustainer who descends as the avatars.
vishnu.description: Vishnu is the supreme preserver of the Hindu trinity, the all-pervading god who maintains cosmic order and descends into the world as the avatars to restore righteousness whenever it declines. His many attributions across the Tree reflect his universality — present at Chokmah, Geburah, Tiphareth and along numerous paths, each linked to one of his incarnations. Reclining on the cosmic serpent upon the sea of milk, blue-skinned and four-armed, he is the boundless sustaining love that upholds all that is.
tables: XXII. Small Selection of Hindu Deities

vishu-hari-krischna-rama.summary: Vishnu-Hari-Krishna-Rama — the preserver and his avatars gathered at the solar heart, Tiphareth.
vishu-hari-krischna-rama.description: This compound name gathers Vishnu (Hari) together with his great avatars Krishna and Rama, all referred to Tiphareth, the harmonising solar centre of the Tree. The grouping expresses the truth that the preserver and his incarnations are one — the single sustaining divine love manifesting through many radiant forms. At Tiphareth, the sphere of the sacrificed-and-risen god, these saviour-figures find their natural home as the beautiful, redeeming heart of the godhead.
tables: XXII. Small Selection of Hindu Deities

vishvarupa-darshana.summary: The Vision of the Universal Form (viśvarūpa-darśana) — the theophany of the Gita, set at Tiphareth.
vishvarupa-darshana.description: Vishvarupa-darshana is the 'vision of the universal form' among the Hindu/Buddhist Results, attributed to Tiphareth. It is the great theophany of the Bhagavad Gita, in which Krishna reveals to Arjuna his cosmic body — all the worlds, gods and devouring time blazing within a single overwhelming shape. Set at the solar heart of the Tree, the sphere of the redeeming god-form, it figures the beatific yet terrible vision of the whole universe beheld in and as the divine, the central revelation in which the many are seen gathered in the One.
tables: XXIV. Certain of the Hindu/Buddhist Results

vision-of-antinomies.summary: The Vision of Antinomies, the supernal experience of holding opposites as one.
vision-of-antinomies.description: The Vision of Antinomies is attributed to Chokmah, the sphere of supernal Wisdom. To attain it is to behold the great contradictions of existence—being and non-being, good and evil, motion and rest—not resolved into a bland middle but held together, each true, in a higher unity that transcends the law of contradiction. It is the wisdom of the second Sephirah, where the mind learns that the deepest truths are paradox, and that the One contains and reconciles all its own negations.

vision-of-chandra.summary: The Vision of Chandra — beholding the lunar deity, set at the path of the Moon.
vision-of-chandra.description: Vision of Chandra is the beholding of Chandra, the Hindu moon-god, among the Hindu/Buddhist Results, attributed to the path of the Moon. It is the inner vision of the lunar light — the cool, reflective, ever-waxing-and-waning luminary that governs the tides of the psyche and the soma of inspiration. Set at the lunar path, it answers to the visions of the astral and reflective realms, the silver counterpart to the solar splendour of Sūrya.
tables: XXIV. Certain of the Hindu/Buddhist Results

vision-of-no-difference.summary: The Vision of No Difference, the experience of the Unmanifest where all distinction dissolves.
vision-of-no-difference.description: The Vision of No Difference belongs to the Veils of the Negative, beyond the Crown. It is the realisation that, at the root, there is no real distinction between any thing and any other—self and other, this and that, all melting into the single undifferentiated ground of being. Where the lower visions reveal harmony among the many, this reveals that the many were never truly separate at all; it is the threshold of the absolute, where even unity gives way to the silence in which there is nothing left to distinguish.

vision-of-surya.summary: The Vision of Sūrya — beholding the solar deity, set at the path of the Sun.
vision-of-surya.description: Vision of Surya is the beholding of Sūrya, the Hindu sun-god, among the Hindu/Buddhist Results, attributed to the path of the Sun. It is the inner vision of the solar splendour — the radiant deity whose disc is the visible eye of heaven — answering to the solar attainments of clarity, harmony and self-luminous being. Set fittingly at the solar path, it figures the contemplative's encounter with the light at the centre, the kindling of the inward sun.
tables: XXIV. Certain of the Hindu/Buddhist Results

vision-of-the-genius.summary: The Vision of the Genius, the experience of Spirit and the encounter with the higher self.
vision-of-the-genius.description: The Vision of the Genius is attributed to Spirit (31 bis), the quintessence that crowns the elements. It is the beholding of one's daemon or genius—the higher tutelary self, the 'Augoeides' of the Neoplatonists—the radiant intelligence that guides the soul from above. Akin to the Knowledge and Conversation of the Holy Guardian Angel, it is the spirit-vision in which the magician meets the luminous companion who is both other and the truest self, the spark of divinity that presides over the whole work.

vision-of-the-higher-self.summary: The Vision of the Higher Self — the attainment, glimpsed at Malkuth and in Spirit, of one's own divine genius.
