vision-of-the-higher-self.description: The Vision of the Higher Self is among the magical and mystical results Crowley tabulates upon the Tree (Table XXIV), set at Malkuth and at Spirit. It is the moment in which the aspirant, working in the world of action, first perceives the indwelling divine self that stands above the personality — the Augoeides or Holy Guardian Angel in its earliest intimation. Coming at the foot of the Tree, it is the seed and promise of the whole Great Work: the realisation that behind the daily self there abides a higher, presiding identity toward whose knowledge and conversation the entire path ascends.
tables: XXIV. Certain of the Hindu/Buddhist Results

vision-of-universal-peacock.summary: The mystic vision of the cosmos as a single iridescent splendour of innumerable eyes — every part equally divine.
vision-of-universal-peacock.description: The Vision of the Universal Peacock is the magical attainment set by Crowley at Samekh, the path of Art (Temperance) and the sign of Sagittarius — the arrow shot from Yesod toward the sun of Tiphareth. In this vision the aspirant beholds the whole of creation as one shimmering, many-eyed glory, like the spread tail of a peacock whose every iridescent eye is a separate world and yet a facet of a single display. Every event, every being, every colour is seen to be necessary, beautiful, and equally divine — the apparent discords of existence resolved into one harmonious blaze. It is a vision of cosmic reconciliation native to the path of the Holy Guardian Angel, where the alchemical tempering of opposites (the work of Art) yields the perception that all things, fair and foul alike, are radiant members of one body. Esoterically it marks the dissolution of the partial, judging self into delighted acceptance of the totality — the peacock's plumage as the emblem of the universe rejoicing in its own infinite variety.

vision-of-wonder.summary: The Vision of Wonder, the supernal experience of awe before the Mother.
vision-of-wonder.description: The Vision of Wonder is attributed to Binah, the supernal Mother and dark sea of Understanding. To attain it is to be filled with boundless awe before the depth and majesty of being—the speechless astonishment of the soul confronted with the immensity of the divine womb from which all things are born and to which they return. It is wonder raised to a mystical pitch, the marvelling that, in Binah, opens into the deeper understanding of sorrow and of silence.

visuddhi.summary: Vishuddha — the throat chakra of ether and speech, attributed to Binah.
visuddhi.description: Vishuddha, the 'pure' chakra at the throat, is the fifth wheel, seat of the element Ether (Akasha) and of speech, hearing, and creative expression. Referred in 777 to Binah, the supernal Mother and the formative Word, it governs the bringing-forth of the inner into utterance — the purifying centre where thought becomes the spoken and the heard.

vitriol.summary: The alchemists' acrostic of inward descent, rooted at the foot of the Tree in Malkuth.
vitriol.description: At Malkuth, the Kingdom and the manifest earth, the formulae table sets VITRIOL—Visita Interiora Terrae Rectificando Invenies Occultam Lapidem, "Visit the interior of the earth; by rectification thou shalt find the hidden stone." It is the alchemists' command to seek the Philosopher's Stone not in the heavens but in the densest matter, by descending into the dark interior of one's own nature and there purifying what is found. Fittingly placed in the lowest Sephirah, the kingdom of dense body and ordinary life, VITRIOL teaches that the gold of attainment is hidden in the very ground beneath the feet, awaiting the one who dares to dig inward.

voices.summary: Voices — a class-image in CLXXXIII Legendary Orders of Being, the family of the disembodied auditory presences.
voices.description: 'Voices' (in 777 printed in quotation marks) appears in table CLXXXIII as one of the categories of Legendary Orders of Being — the disembodied vocal presences that occupy a long tradition from the bath kol of rabbinic Judaism to the daimon of Socrates to the angelic voices of Joan of Arc. The class is defined by mode of contact (heard, not seen) rather than by figure. The entry registers it as a Crowleyean category-header.

volac.summary: The sixty-second spirit of the Goetia (Valac), a child-formed president of Sagittarius who reveals treasure and serpents.
volac.description: Valac (here Volac) is the sixty-second spirit of the Goetia, a president of the decans of Sagittarius. He gives true answers concerning hidden treasures, and tells where serpents may be seen, delivering them harmless into the operator's hands. He appears as a small, poor-looking boy with the wings of an angel, riding upon a two-headed dragon. A spirit of the fiery sign, he is the revealer of buried treasure and the tamer of serpents.

vucula.summary: Presiding god of the second decan of Aquarius, the same Mercurial face of methodical intellect.
vucula.description: Vucula is the presiding god 777 sets over the second decan of Aquarius (10°–20°), the Mercurial face the names-column calls Astiro. Bearing the Six of Swords—Science—it names the methodical, problem-solving intellect at the centre of fixed air. It belongs to the Greco-Egyptian list of thirty-six decan-rulers.
tables: CLXIX. Egyptian Gods of the Zodiac (Succedent)

vulcan.summary: Vulcan, god of fire and the forge — the divine smith of the gods, at Fire.
vulcan.description: Vulcan is the Roman god of fire, volcanoes, and the forge, the lame master-smith counterpart of the Greek Hephaestus, who fashions the weapons and wonders of the gods. Referred to Shin and the element of Fire and to Libra, he is the controlled, creative fire of the smithy — the transforming flame that shapes metal into art and arms. As the divine craftsman he embodies fire harnessed to making, the heat that builds rather than merely destroys.

wand.summary: The Hermit's staff at Virgo—the will borne as a support on the solitary path, the rod of the lone seeker.
wand.description: The Wand appears among the weapons at Virgo, the path of the Hermit, where it takes the character of the staff carried by the solitary wayfarer—the rod that both supports the steps and directs the will along the lonely road. Paired here with the Lamp, it is the Hermit's companion: as the Lamp gives light, the Wand gives direction and stay. Virgo's wand is will refined by solitude and service, the disciplined purpose of one who walks apart. Esoterically the Wand of the Hermit is the seeker's tempered will made into a support and a guide—the staff of single-minded purpose that steadies the solitary on the upward path and points the way through the wilderness toward the light he carries and seeks.

warrior-on-black-horse.summary: The magical image of Cimejes — a valiant warrior upon a black horse — Goetic Marquis of the third decan of Capricorn (by night).
warrior-on-black-horse.description: Cimejes (Kimaris, Cimeies), the sixty-sixth spirit of the Goetia and a mighty Marquis who rules over all the spirits of the parts of Africa, appears as a valiant warrior riding upon a black horse. In 777 he is the nocturnal ruler of the third decan of Capricorn. He teaches grammar, logic and rhetoric, discovers lost and hidden things and treasures, and makes a man to bear himself like a warrior. The dark-mounted soldier befits the disciplined, ambitious sign of the Goat — eloquence and command won by martial bearing.

warrior-with-ducal-crown-rides-gryphon-t.term: Warrior with ducal crown rides gryphon. Trumpeters
warrior-with-ducal-crown-rides-gryphon-t.displayTerm: Warrior with ducal crown rides gryphon. Trumpeters
warrior-with-ducal-crown-rides-gryphon-t.summary: The magical image of Murmur — a crowned warrior riding a gryphon, his ministers sounding trumpets — Goetic Duke and Earl of the third decan of Virgo (by night).
warrior-with-ducal-crown-rides-gryphon-t.description: Murmur (Murmus), the fifty-fourth spirit of the Goetia, both Duke and Earl, appears as a warrior riding upon a gryphon (or vulture), wearing a ducal crown, while his ministers go before him sounding trumpets. In 777 he is the nocturnal ruler of the third decan of Virgo. He teaches philosophy perfectly and constrains the souls of the dead to come before the magician and answer whatever is asked. The crowned soldier borne upon the gryphon amid fanfare befits the discerning, service-minded sign of the Virgin — disciplined knowledge with power even over the dead.

water.summary: The passive, receptive element of emotion, intuition, and dissolution.
water.description:
Water is the element of emotion, intuition, memory, and the unconscious—cold and moist, receptive, descending, and formless save for the vessel that holds it. In 777 it answers to the letter Mem and path 23, to the Tatwa Apas (a silver crescent), and to the western quarter. Its weapon is the Cup, its archangel Gabriel, its elemental king Nichsa, its creatures the undines.

Mythically Water is the primordial deep from which creation rises and into which it dissolves—the waters of Genesis, the abyss of Tiamat, the river of forgetfulness. It governs the tides of feeling and the solvent power that breaks down rigid forms so that they may be reshaped. As the ‘universal solvent’ of nature it is also the alchemical agent of dissolution, the necessary death before reintegration.
tables: CX. Elements and Quarters per the Sepher Yetzirah
III. Translation of the Names of the Paths
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

water-nymphs.summary: The maiden-spirits of springs and streams, set at Aquarius — the living souls of fresh waters.
water-nymphs.description: Among the Legendary Orders of Being, the Water Nymphs are attributed to the path of Aquarius. They are the naiads and undine-kindred of classical and folk tradition — the beautiful maiden-spirits that inhabit and personify springs, rivers, lakes and fountains, the very life and consciousness of fresh water. As an order they figure the gracious, fertile, sometimes capricious soul of the waters; set at Aquarius, the Water-Bearer who pours forth the stream, they are the indwelling spirits of that life-giving flow.

water-of-lustration.summary: The consecrated cleansing water of Mem—the purifying flood that washes the temple and the operator clean.
water-of-lustration.description: The Water of Lustration is attributed to the watery letter Mem, and it is the consecrated water used to purify the temple, the implements and the magician before the work—the cleansing flood sprinkled with the aspergillus to wash away the profane and make all things holy. Its place at Mem, the still deep waters of the Hanged Man, is exact, for water is the natural agent of purification, dissolving and bearing away impurity. Before the fire of invocation can safely descend, the field must first be washed. Esoterically the Water of Lustration is the principle of purification by water in the magician's hand—the consecrating flood that cleanses both the place and the soul of the operator, dissolving the unclean so that the sacred work may proceed upon a purified ground.

water-turned-to-blood.summary: The Plague of Blood — the Nile turned to blood, attributed to Malkuth.
water-turned-to-blood.description: The first of the Ten Plagues of Egypt, the turning of the Nile and all the waters to blood, is set in 777 at Malkuth, the material Kingdom and the sphere of the elements. As the plagues are referred down the Tree, this corruption of the very waters of life belongs fittingly to the lowest sphere — the material world struck at its foundation.
tables: CXXII. The Ten Plagues of Egypt

watercress.summary: The pungent water-herb, attributed to Cancer; cleansing plant of the lunar element.
watercress.description: Watercress is set at the path of Cheth and Cancer, the cardinal-water sign ruled by the Moon — a pungent, mineral-rich herb of running streams, long valued as a spring tonic and blood-cleanser. Its watery habitat and cleansing virtue suit the lunar, tidal attribution of Cancer. A wholesome food requiring only the ordinary caution of clean water-sources.
watercress.caution: Safe as food; only wild harvest from clean water needs care.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

we-have-insufficient-knowledge-of-the-at.term: We have insufficient knowledge of the attributions of Assyrian
we-have-insufficient-knowledge-of-the-at.displayTerm: We have insufficient knowledge of the attributions of Assyrian

wealth.summary: Ten of Disks — Wealth; Mercury in Virgo, Malkuth of Earth: matter fully realised.
wealth.description: The Ten of Disks, Wealth, is Malkuth in the suit of Earth and the third decan of Virgo under Mercury. When earth descends wholly into earth, the suit reaches its completion: ten discs arranged as the Tree of Life, coined and stamped, the full and final realisation of material abundance. It is wealth in its most concrete form — and, being a ten, the point at which accumulation grows inert and must be returned to circulation.
tables: CXXXVI. Titles and Attributions of the Pantacle Suit

werewolves.summary: The men who become wolves, set at Qoph and Pisces — the eruption of the atavistic beast.
werewolves.description: The Werewolves are an order of legendary beings, attributed to Qoph and the sign Pisces. In folklore they are humans who, by curse or sorcery or the full moon's light, take on the form and savagery of the wolf. Set at Qoph — the path of the 'back of the head,' the atavistic hind-brain, and the Moon's dim animal light — they figure with great precision the eruption of the buried bestial nature, the older, instinctual creature rising up to overwhelm the human form.

west.summary: The quarter of the setting sun, attributed to the element Water.
west.description: The West is the quarter of the setting sun, of evening and the gathering dusk. In the elemental scheme of the Western mysteries it is attributed to Water, the element of feeling, reflection, and the deep — the realm into which the sun descends to be reborn. As the station of the closing day, it bears the receptive, flowing, and dissolving power within the magical circle.
tables: CX. Elements and Quarters per the Sepher Yetzirah

west-african.summary: West African — a pantheon column Crowley reserved in 777 for future expansion, left unfilled.
west-african.description: The 'West African' column in 777's pantheon tables (XXV-XXXII) was intended to receive the Yoruba Orisha (Olodumare, Eshu, Ogun, Shango, Yemaya, Oshun, Oya), the Fon Vodun, and the related deity systems of the Bight of Benin and the Niger valley — traditions whose precise attribution to the Tree would have repaid serious study. Crowley left the column blank, an honest acknowledgment that this synthesis was beyond what he had personally undertaken. The entry preserves the placeholder.

whale.summary: The leviathan of Cancer—the vast mother of the deep, the great sea-beast that swallows and shelters.
whale.description: The whale is attributed to Cancer, the watery, maternal path of the Chariot, and it is the greatest of the sea-creatures, the living vastness of the deep—the Leviathan of scripture and the great fish that swallowed Jonah, carrying him through the dark belly of the waters to be cast up reborn. As an immense, warm-blooded mother of the ocean it belongs to the sheltering, oceanic nature of Cancer, at once the engulfing depth and the womb that bears the soul through its night. Esoterically the whale figures the overwhelming maternal deep—the great unconscious that can swallow the self into darkness yet also carry it, transformed, back to the light, the belly of the deep that is both tomb and womb.

wheel-of-fortune.summary: Atu X — Kaph / Jupiter; the turning wheel of change, fate, and expansion.
wheel-of-fortune.description: Fortune (the Wheel of Fortune) is trump X, attributed to Kaph and Jupiter, the path from Chesed to Netzach. It is the ever-turning wheel of change, cycle, and destiny—the rise and fall of all fortunes under the expansive, fateful rule of Jupiter. Crowley’s wheel whirls with the alchemical trinity of sphinx, ape, and crocodile (the three gunas, the modes of nature) caught in perpetual revolution. Fortune teaches the law of cyclic flux: that nothing in manifestation is fixed, that the wise neither cling to the heights nor despair in the depths but find the still centre of the turning.
tables: XIV. General Attribution of the Tarot
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

wheels.summary: Wheels — the English name of the angelic choir Auphanim, the host of Assiah at Chokmah.
wheels.description: In the Qabalistic angelology each Sephirah commands its own choir of angels; “Wheels” (Table CI, the Angels of Assiah given in English) renders into the vernacular the Hebrew order Auphanim, the host attributed to Chokmah. These are the Wheels, the spinning galgalim of the chariot-throne, figuring the dynamic out-rushing force of the Zodiac and of primal Wisdom. Crowley sets them at Chokmah on the Tree, where the choir gives angelic form to the energy of that sphere as it acts in Assiah, the world of action.

whereon-revolve-the-triad-of-hermanubis.term: whereon revolve the triad of Hermanubis
whereon-revolve-the-triad-of-hermanubis.displayTerm: whereon revolve the triad of Hermanubis
whereon-revolve-the-triad-of-hermanubis.summary: Design detail of the Wheel of Fortune (Kaph): whereon revolve the triad of Hermanubis, Sphinx, and Typhon.
whereon-revolve-the-triad-of-hermanubis.description: ‘Whereon revolve the triad of Hermanubis’ is part of Liber 777's design for Atu X, the Wheel of Fortune (path of Kaph, Jupiter): ‘A wheel of six shafts, whereon revolve the triad of Hermanubis, Sphinx, and Typhon.’ The three figures are the powers of the turning wheel: Hermanubis rising (intelligence and aspiration), the Sphinx poised at the summit (equilibrium and the riddle of being), and Typhon descending (the destructive force that drags down). Their ceaseless revolution about an unmoving centre is the very mechanism of fortune—rise, balance, and fall endlessly renewed.

white.summary: The white kasiṇa of the Forty Meditations — the disc of pure white taken as the support of one-pointed absorption.
white.description: Among the Forty Buddhist Meditations (the kammaṭṭhāna), White is one of the colour-kasiṇas: a disc or field of pure white gazed upon until the mind, releasing the outward eye, holds the white as an inward 'counterpart sign' and sinks into absorption. Of the colour-discs the white is reckoned the most luminous and steadying, conducive to clarity and to the radiant mind; in the 777 scheme it stands among the practices that purify perception and lead the meditator from the gross object toward the formless. As a kasiṇa it is not symbolic adornment but a working tool — the simplest of objects made the doorway to jhāna.

CXLIX. Magical Images of the Decans (Ascendent)

white-sandal.summary: The cool white sandalwood of Mercury—a clean, serene wood-incense lending clarity to the airy path of Beth.
white-sandal.description: White Sandal (white sandalwood) is attributed here to Mercury (Beth, the Magus). Cool, sweet, and quieting, the true white sandal is among the great clarifying incenses; set upon the path of the Magus it lends its serene clarity to the mercurial mind. Esoterically white sandalwood is a perfume of lucid calm—the cool wood-scent that stills and clears the quick intellect of Mercury, serenity in the service of thought.

who-guides-parliament.summary: The Christian God at Chokmah — the supernal Father reduced, in Crowley's gloss, to the guide of governments.
who-guides-parliament.description: In Table XXXVI Crowley distributes the single Christian deity across the Sephiroth, supplying for each a wry English description that shows how the one God must take on, in turn, all the offices the pagans had shared among many gods. At Chokmah, the supernal sphere of the Father and of Wisdom, that God appears as the one 'who guides Parliament' — the paternal lawgiver and ruler, the supreme authority behind statecraft and counsel. The gloss is half-satirical, pointing up the diminution of a cosmic Father-principle into a constitutional patron; but it preserves a real correspondence, for Chokmah is genuinely the seat of overruling wisdom and sovereign direction.
tables: XXXVI. Selection of Christian Gods (10); Apostles (12); Evangelists(4); and Churches of Asia (7)

will-o-the-wisp.summary: The deceiving marsh-light, set at the Sun — the false flame that leads the traveller astray.
will-o-the-wisp.description: Among the Legendary Orders of Being, the Will-o'-the-Wisp (ignis fatuus) is attributed to the path of the Sun. It is the flickering light seen over bogs and marshes by night, which folklore made a mischievous spirit — a lantern-bearing sprite or wandering soul that lures the benighted traveller from the path into the mire. A false and counterfeit light, it stands in pointed contrast to the true solar radiance of its attribution: the deceptive gleam that apes the sun's guidance and leads only to loss, a caution that not every light is to be followed.

willow.summary: The weeping water-tree—the willow of Malkuth, mourning and pliant, rooted by the rivers of the Kingdom.
willow.description: The Willow is attributed here to Malkuth, the Kingdom, the manifest earth where the waters gather. Bending low over stream and pool, the weeping willow is the immemorial tree of grief and of yielding—the harps hung upon its boughs "by the waters of Babylon"—yet also of supple, unbreakable resilience and of fertile waterside life. Esoterically the willow is the pliant, sorrowing, water-fed tree of the lower world, bowing to the flow yet rooted fast in the soil of the Kingdom.

wind.summary: The air kasiṇa (vāyo) — the moving air taken as the support of meditative absorption.
wind.description: Wind is the air-element kasiṇa (vāyo-kasiṇa) of the Forty Meditations, attributed to the path of Aleph and the element Air. Rather than a disc, the meditator attends to the touch and movement of air — the stirring of leaves, the breath of wind upon the body — until that perception is gathered into a stable inner sign and the mind enters jhāna. As one of the four element-kasiṇas it teaches the practitioner to find the doorway to absorption even in the subtlest and least graspable of objects.

window.summary: Heh — 'window'; the aperture of breath and vision, path of The Star (or Emperor).
window.description: Heh means 'window' — an opening that lets in light and breath. Soft and aspirate, it is the letter of breathing, doubled in the Tetragrammaton to mark the supernal Mother and the bride. In Liber 777 Heh is attributed to Aries and, following Crowley's reordering after Liber AL, to the path of The Star (traditionally The Emperor), joining Chokmah to Tiphareth. As a window it is the threshold of revelation: the framed opening through which the higher light pours into the soul and through which the soul gazes out toward heaven.
tables: III. Translation of the Names of the Paths

wisdom.summary: Wisdom—the second Sephirah; the primordial dynamic, masculine Father force.
wisdom.description:
Chokmah (חכמה, ‘Wisdom’) is the second Sephirah, the first stirring of force out of the unity of Kether. It is the supernal Father, pure outgoing energy and will, the point set in motion into a line. As the archetypal active principle it corresponds to the Zodiac as a whole (the Sphere of the Fixed Stars, Mazloth) and to the energising Yod of the Tetragrammaton. Its virtue is devotion, its God-name Jah.

Chokmah is dynamic where Binah, its complement, is formative: it gives the seed-impulse that Binah receives and shapes. In Crowley’s reading it is the Logos, the creative Word, wisdom not as accumulated knowledge but as the very force of beginning.
tables: III. Translation of the Names of the Paths
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

witches.summary: The workers of folk-sorcery, set at Beth and Nun — wielders of the hidden art.
witches.description: The Witches are an order of legendary beings, attributed to Beth (Mercury) and Nun (Scorpio). Across folklore they are the practitioners of the hidden craft — herb and charm, curse and flight, congress with spirits and the powers of night. The double attribution is apt: Mercury gives the cunning, the word, and the magical skill, while Scorpio gives the dark, transformative, and sexual undercurrent. As an order they figure the folk-tradition of magical power, feared and persecuted yet enduring.

wizards.summary: The masters of arcane lore, set at Beth and Mercury — the male adepts of the magical art.
wizards.description: The Wizards are an order of legendary beings, attributed to Beth and the planet Mercury. They are the learned magicians of legend — Merlin and his kind — masters of arcane knowledge, conjuration, and the secret arts, the male counterpart to the witch. Set at the Mercurial path of the Magus, the very letter of the magical Word, they figure the disciplined, studied command of hidden power: wisdom and skill turned to the working of wonders.

wolf.summary: The predator of Scorpio and Mars—martial hunger, the death-instinct, the pack-fierce will to survive.
wolf.description: The wolf is attributed to Scorpio and to Mars, the sign and the planet of penetrating, destructive force, and it is the great predator of the northern imagination—lean, tireless, and merciless in the hunt. Sacred to Mars and to war-gods, ridden by death in the old myths (the wolves of Odin, the devouring Fenrir), it embodies the martial appetite and the death-dealing aspect of the life-force. Under Scorpio it is the instinct that kills in order to live, the desire that consumes its object. Esoterically the wolf is the raw survival-will and the hunger that drives transformation—a power to be acknowledged and harnessed, for it cannot be wished away.

wolf-with-a-gryphon-s-wings.term: Wolf with a gryphon s wings
wolf-with-a-gryphon-s-wings.displayTerm: Wolf with a gryphon s wings
wolf-with-a-gryphon-s-wings.summary: The magical image of Marchosias — a winged wolf with a serpent's tail, vomiting fire — Goetic Marquis of the second decan of Pisces.
wolf-with-a-gryphon-s-wings.description: Marchosias, the thirty-fifth spirit of the Goetia and a great and mighty Marquis, appears as a wolf with the wings of a gryphon and the tail of a serpent, vomiting fire from his mouth, and at command takes the shape of a man. In 777 he is set at the second decan of Pisces by day. A strong and valiant fighter who answers truly, he confided to Solomon that he hoped after a thousand and two hundred years to return to the seventh heavenly throne. The flaming winged wolf marks the fierce aspiration hidden in the yielding sign of the Fishes — the fallen spirit straining back toward the light.

wolf-with-serpent-s-tail.summary: The magical image of Amon — a wolf with a serpent's tail vomiting flame — Goetic Marquis of the first decan of Gemini.
wolf-with-serpent-s-tail.description: Amon, the seventh spirit of the Goetia and a mighty Marquis, appears first as a wolf with a serpent's tail breathing out fire, and at the operator's command takes the shape of a man with a raven's head and the teeth of a dog. In 777 he rules the first decan of Gemini by day. Most strong and powerful, he discerns things past and to come, procures love and reconciles enemies — and his composite beast-form, wolf married to serpent, fitly images the doubled, contrary nature of the Twins.

woman.summary: The feminine figure of Leo and Binah—Babalon astride the beast, and the Great Mother who gives all form.
woman.description: The figure of the woman is set at Leo and at Binah. At Teth/Leo she is the woman of the Lust card, riding and mastering the lion-serpent beast—Babalon enthroned upon the forces of life, the feminine that does not flee power but governs and consummates it. At Binah she is the Great Mother, the supernal feminine through whom the formless light first takes form, the womb and the grave of all things. Between these she spans the whole range of the feminine principle: ecstatic mistress of the life-force below, and the dark understanding Mother above. Esoterically the woman is the receptive-creative power without which no manifestation and no attainment is possible.

works.summary: Three of Disks — Works / Material Works; Mars in Capricorn, Binah of Earth.
works.description: The Three of Disks, Works (Material Works), is Binah in the suit of Earth and the second decan of Capricorn under Mars. The Mother gives form to matter through labour: three discs as a pyramid, the foundation of the Great Work laid in the wilderness. Mars in Capricorn lends industry and constructive force — building, craft, the establishment of material undertakings on a sound base.
tables: CXXXVI. Titles and Attributions of the Pantacle Suit

works-of-justice.summary: The Libran power of setting right, the magic that restores the broken balance.
works-of-justice.description: Works of Justice belong to Lamed and Libra, the path of Justice (Adjustment), whose scales and sword are the very emblems of righted wrong. As a magical power it is the operation undertaken to restore equilibrium—to compel fair dealing, to settle disputes, to make the crooked straight. Distinguished from the Martian works of wrath, justice acts not to destroy but to balance, returning to each exactly what is due, the law of Libra made an instrument of will.

works-of-malediction.summary: The Saturnian power of cursing, the dark magic of binding and blighting.
works-of-malediction.description: Works of Malediction are set at Tav and Saturn, the path of the Universe and the heaviest, most binding of the planetary forces. As a magical power it is the casting of curses—the laying of restriction, sterility, and decay upon a chosen object. Saturn, lord of limitation, time, and death, governs all such constricting operations. The tradition treats them as the gravest of the dark arts, fettering the worker in the same chains he forges, and most adepts renounce them entirely.

works-of-wrath.summary: The Martian power of burning destruction, the magic of the consuming assault.
works-of-wrath.description: Works of Wrath belong to Pe and Mars, the path of the Tower, whose blasted crown and falling figures depict the violence of destructive force unleashed. As a magical power it is the directed operation of rage—the assault, the breaking-down, the burning-away of an obstacle or foe. Mars rules all such fierce and martial workings; like its kindred works of vengeance and malediction it is held perilous, for the fire that is hurled outward scorches the hand that throws it.

worlds.summary: A content of the heavens at the lower Sephiroth — the worlds held within the cosmic order.
worlds.description: Among the contents of the heavens, the 'worlds' are reckoned at the lower Sephiroth of Yesod and Malkuth. They are the inhabited realms and orders of creation contained within the great frame of the heavens — the manifold worlds gathered at the foundation and kingdom, the lower terms of the cosmic descent in which spirit is housed in fact.
tables: XCV. Contents of the Heavens of Assiah

worm-eaten-corpse.summary: The contemplation of the worm-infested corpse — a cemetery meditation on decay.
worm-eaten-corpse.description: The Worm-eaten Corpse is the worm-infested stage (puḷavaka) of the ten foulness-contemplations of the Forty Meditations, set at the path of Cancer. The meditator steadies the mind upon the body crawling with maggots and worms, teeming with the life that feeds on death. The image, deliberately revolting, severs the fascination of the senses and the illusion that the body is clean, lovely or one's own; in the watery, nurturing sign of Cancer it makes plain that the body is itself a vessel and a feast for other lives.

wormwood.summary: The bitter silver herb—wormwood of Gemini, the artemisia whose bitterness sharpens wit and inspires vision.
wormwood.description:
Wormwood (Artemisia absinthium) is attributed here to Gemini (Zayin, the Lovers). Silver-leaved and intensely bitter—its very name a byword for bitterness, the star Wormwood of the Apocalypse—it was burned and steeped to clear the head, sharpen the wits, repel vermin, and (as the soul of absinthe) to kindle the mind toward vision. Its keen, clarifying bitterness has an airy, mercurial edge fitting Gemini. Esoterically wormwood is the bitter herb of clarified perception—the sharp silver scent that cuts through dullness and wakens the quick, divided mind of the Twins.

Caution: wormwood (thujone) is toxic in excess. This entry is symbolic and historical and is in no way advice for use.
wormwood.caution: Wormwood (thujone) is toxic in excess. Symbolic/historical entry only — not advice for use.

worry.summary: Five of Disks — Worry / Material Trouble; Mercury in Taurus, Geburah of Earth.
worry.description: The Five of Disks, Worry (Material Trouble), is Geburah in the suit of Earth and the first decan of Taurus under Mercury. The fives break their suit, and severity entering the realm of matter brings strain: five discs grind together as failing machinery, the engine of the world out of true. It is anxiety, want, and the gnawing fear of material loss — Mercury's restless intellect fretting over Taurus's solid ground.
tables: CXXXVI. Titles and Attributions of the Pantacle Suit

worshipful-master.summary: The Master of the Lodge, here at Chesed — the ruling light enthroned in the East.
worshipful-master.description: In the Craft lodge the Worshipful Master is the presiding officer, seated in the East and governing the work as the Sun governs the day. Attributed here to Chesed, the merciful, ordering sphere of Jupiter, he embodies benevolent authority and rule — the wise governor whose word opens and closes the labours of the brethren. His station mirrors the kingly, law-giving function on the Tree of Life.
tables: CXV. Officers in a Masonic Lodge

worthlessness.summary: Worthlessness — a qliphothic shell of the Veils, the void turned barren.
worthlessness.description: 'Worthlessness' (Crowley renders such shells also as 'vanity' or 'emptiness') is among the translated averse orders set at the Veils of the Negative. It is the qliphothic inversion of the boundless plenitude hidden in the Ain Soph: where the divine veils conceal an infinite richness, their shadow is sheer nullity and vanity — being drained of all value, the husk without the kernel.
tables: CXXIII. Translation of the Orders of the Qliphoth

wotan.summary: Wotan, the Germanic all-father — the storm-god of fury and wisdom, at Kether and Chesed.
wotan.description: Wotan is the continental Germanic form of Odin, the high god of the Wild Hunt, of fury (wod), wisdom, and the dead. Referred to Kether and Chesed — the Crown and the merciful sovereign sphere — he is the supreme paternal power of the Germanic gods, leader of the host of souls across the storm-sky. As Wotan he embodies the ecstatic, ruling, and far-roaming spirit of the all-father at the heights of the Tree.

wrapped-in-a-cloak.summary: Design detail of the Hermit (Yod): wrapped in a cloak.
wrapped-in-a-cloak.description: ‘Wrapped in a cloak’ opens Liber 777's design for Atu IX, the Hermit (path of Yod, Virgo): ‘Wrapped in a cloak and cowl, an ancient walketh bearing a lamp and staff.’ The enveloping cloak is the Hermit's withdrawal and concealment—the seclusion in which the inner light is guarded and the seed of wisdom matures in silence. Veiled from the world, he carries his illumination hidden within, the prophet of the eternal cloaked against the noise of the outer life.
tables: CLXXXI. Correct Design of Tarot Trumps
CLI. Magical Images of the Decans (Cadent)

wrath.summary: The Martian vice of wrath, the destructive rage of the unbalanced sword.
wrath.description: Wrath is the vice of Pe and Mars, the path of the Tower, the lightning-stroke of destruction. As the shadow of Mars—lord of force, courage, and severity—it is rage unmastered, the violent fury that lashes out and lays waste without justice or measure. Where the Martian virtue is energy and courage rightly directed, the vice is the same fire run wild, the blasting wrath that throws down the Tower not to purify but merely to ruin.
tables: L. Transcendental Morality (10 Virtues; 7 Deadly Sins; 4 Magic Powers)

yakasaganotz.summary: Angel of the third face of Taurus, where growth halts and labour seems to come to nothing.
yakasaganotz.description: Yakasaganotz governs the closing decan of Taurus (20–30°), where Saturn meets the Seven of Disks, *Failure* — the fallow pause, the promise unfulfilled. Saturn's weight stalls the Taurean field and the harvest appears to fail. Yakasaganotz is the angel of this discouraging interval, the necessary fallow that earth requires before it can bear again.

yama.summary: Yama, the god of death and lord of justice — the first to die, judge of the dead, at Libra.
yama.description: Yama is the Hindu god of death, the first mortal to die and so the ruler of the realm of the departed, who judges the dead and assigns their fate. Referred to Lamed and Libra, the sign of the balance, and to the dark paths of Scorpio and the Sun, he is the just measurer of deeds, the lord of dharma who holds the noose and the rod. Stern but righteous, he embodies the inescapable law that weighs every life.
tables: XXII. Small Selection of Hindu Deities

yasgedibarodiel.summary: Angel of the third face of Capricorn, where works consolidate into established power.
yasgedibarodiel.description: Yasgedibarodiel presides over the closing decan of Capricorn (20–30°), where the Sun meets the Four of Disks, *Power* (Earthly Power) — secured dominion, the fortress of wealth and authority. The Sun crowns Capricorn's long ambition. This longest of the angelic names carries the theophoric ‑el, marking the worldly power it governs as one held in stewardship under God; Yasgedibarodiel is the angel of consolidated earthly authority.

yasyasyah.summary: Angel of the second face of Capricorn, where labour is organised into constructive works.
yasyasyah.description: Yasyasyah governs the middle decan of Capricorn (10–20°), attributed to Mars and the Three of Disks, *Works* — skilled constructive labour, the master-builder at the scaffold. Mars drives Capricorn's industry into enduring structure. Yasyasyah is the angel of disciplined craftsmanship raised into lasting architecture.

yekh.summary: Yekh (Akh) — the shining spirit, the immortal radiance, attributed to Kether.
yekh.description: The Yekh (Akh, Khu), the 'shining one,' is the highest part of the Egyptian soul — the luminous, immortal spirit that, when the dead are justified, dwells among the imperishable stars. Set in 777 at Kether, the Crown and highest light, it is the divine spark of the being, the radiant intelligence that transcends body, shadow, and personal soul alike.
tables: CXVI. Egyptial Attribution of Parts of the Soul

yellow.summary: The yellow kasiṇa — the golden disc used as a support for meditative absorption.
yellow.description: Yellow is the yellow (pīta) colour-kasiṇa of the Forty Meditations, placed at the path of Mercury. The meditator fixes the mind upon a field of pure yellow until its inward image stabilises and the senses fall away into jhāna. Tradition links the golden disc with a warm, gladdening radiance; like all the kasiṇas it is a simple, concrete object deliberately chosen so that the mind, denied its usual scatter of impressions, may collect itself into single-pointed stillness.

yellow-diamond.summary: The golden diamond of Tiphareth — solar brilliance and the perfected heart.
yellow-diamond.description: The yellow diamond is set at Tiphareth, the solar centre — the supreme, incorruptible stone tinted with the gold of the Sun, uniting the diamond's perfection with the solar colour of the harmonised heart. It is the brilliance of the Crown brought down to the sphere of Beauty, the radiant, regenerate self made gem.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

yellow-square.summary: The Tattvic symbol of Prithivi — the yellow square of Earth.
yellow-square.description: The Yellow Square is the Tattvic symbol of Prithivi, the element of Earth. In Tattvic meditation each element bears a coloured geometric form, and the solid yellow square expresses the stable, supporting, enduring nature of Earth — density, foundation, and the medium of smell. It serves as the meditative gateway into the earthy quarter of the subtle world.

tables: CL. Magical Images of the Decans (Succedent)

yew.summary: The deathless death-tree of Saturn—the yew of the churchyard, poisonous and immortal, guardian of the grave.
yew.description:
The Yew is attributed to Saturn (Tav, the Universe). The dark evergreen of the churchyard, immensely long-lived yet wholly poisonous, it unites in one tree the saturnine mysteries of death and of immortality—planted among the graves it shadows, both bane and emblem of life unending; its wood made the deadliest of war-bows. Esoterically the yew is the saturnine tree of the death-threshold, the green that does not die standing watch over the dead, mortality and deathlessness grown into a single dark trunk.

Caution: nearly all parts of the yew are highly poisonous and can be rapidly fatal. This entry is symbolic and historical and is in no way advice for use.
yew.caution: Highly poisonous; can be rapidly fatal. Symbolic/historical entry only — never handle or ingest.

yohimba.summary: The aphrodisiac bark of the Devil and the Foundation—yohimbe, kindler of the sexual fire of Yesod and Capricorn.
yohimba.description:
Yohimbe (here "Yohimba") is set at Capricorn (Ayin, the Devil) and at Yesod, the lunar sphere of generation—a fitting double seat for the bark of a West African tree long used as a powerful aphrodisiac. Capricorn's trump is the Devil, lord of the goat and of unbridled creative-sexual force, and Yesod is the foundation of the sexual and astral life; the yohimbe belongs to both as the kindler of carnal fire. Esoterically it figures the raw generative energy that the Devil's path both embodies and tests—the lust that is the dark root of the same power which, raised, becomes spiritual will.

Caution: yohimbe is a potent vasoactive stimulant that can dangerously raise blood pressure and interact with other drugs. This entry is symbolic and historical.
yohimba.caution: Potent stimulant/aphrodisiac; can dangerously raise blood pressure and interact with medications. Symbolic/historical entry only.

yoni.summary: The receptive emblem of Binah—the womb-vessel of the Great Mother, the form that receives and bears the creative seed.
yoni.description: The yoni is the emblem of the female generative power, attributed to Binah the supernal Mother and to the earthy depth of Capricorn. As the womb and gate through which all things are born, it is the receptive vessel that takes in the creative seed and gives it form—the cosmic counterpart to the lingam, the Cup to its Wand. Its place at Binah is exact, for Binah is the Understanding that receives the formless light of the Father and shapes it into the first form. Esoterically the yoni is the sacred principle of receptivity and gestation, the holy matrix without which the projected force of the lingam remains barren; together they are the two halves of the one mystery of creation, reverenced in the tantric and Western traditions alike as the gate of life.
tables: XXII. Small Selection of Hindu Deities

yota.summary: Yota — a letter of the Coptic alphabet (i/y), which Crowley attributes to the path of Yod (Virgo).
yota.description: Yota is a letter of the Coptic alphabet — the script in which the Egyptian language was written in the Christian era, the Greek alphabet adapted to Egyptian speech. It is from Greek iota. Crowley folds the Coptic alphabet into the great correspondence of letters and paths in 777 (Table LI), assigning Yota to the path of Yod (Virgo) on the Tree of Life, so that the Egyptian-Christian script takes its station among the Hebrew letters and the keys of the Tarot.
tables: LI. Names of the Coptic Letters

young.summary: Design detail of the Lovers (Zayin): young.
young.description: ‘Young’ is a fragment of Liber 777's design for Atu VI, the Lovers (path of Zayin, Gemini): ‘A prophet, young, and in the Sign of Osiris Risen.’ The youth of the figure marks the freshness and vitality of the trump—the springtime of union, the dawning of love and discrimination under the twin sign of Gemini. Youth here is the unspoiled condition in which choice is still open and the marriage of contraries may be made anew.
tables: CLXXXI. Correct Design of Tarot Trumps

zachi.summary: Angel of the second face of Leo, where the lion's struggle is crowned with victory.
zachi.description: Zachi governs the middle decan of Leo (10–20°), attributed to Jupiter and the Six of Wands, *Victory* — triumph and acclaim. Jupiter's blessing upon Leo's fire brings the laurel and the rider's procession. Zachi is the angel of earned, radiant success, the moment when courage is publicly vindicated.

zagan.summary: The sixty-first spirit of the Goetia, a winged-bull king of Sagittarius who transmutes liquids and metals and makes fools wise.
zagan.description: Zagan is the sixty-first spirit of the Goetia, a great king and president of the decans of Sagittarius. He makes men witty, turns wine into water and water into wine, and blood into wine (or oil), and turns all metals into coin; he can make a fool wise. He appears as a bull with the wings of a griffin, then takes human form. A spirit of the fiery sign, he is the transmuter of liquids and metals and the giver of wit.

zahun.summary: Scandal — the Nuctemeron genius of the first hour presiding over scandal, set by Crowley at Aries.
zahun.description: In the Nuctemeron — the “Day Illumined by Night” ascribed to Apollonius of Tyana and preserved by Éliphas Lévi — Zahun is numbered among the genii of the first hour, the spirit of scandal. He rules over rumour and slander, the whispering tongue that disgraces a name. Crowley arranges the twelve hours and their genii upon the paths of the Tree (777, Table CLXXIII), placing him at Aries (Heh).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

zalberhith.summary: Nocturnal angelic Lord of Leo within the Fiery Triplicity.
zalberhith.description: Zalberhith is the night-governor of Leo among the angelic Lords of the Triplicities. As the fixed heart of the Fire trine by night, Leo's blaze becomes the hidden fire of the lion, fierce even when unseen, warmth guarded behind closed doors; Zalberhith presides over this nocturnal, undimmed strength.

zalburis.summary: Therapeutics — the Nuctemeron genius of the eighth hour presiding over therapeutics, set by Crowley at Scorpio.
zalburis.description: Zalburis is the Nuctemeron genius of therapeutics. That “Night-illumined Day”, ascribed to Apollonius of Tyana and handed down through Lévi's Transcendental Magic, sets a company of spirits over each of the twelve hours of the magical day, and Zalburis belongs to the eighth hour. His province is the healing art, the curing of the sick by remedy and regimen. In 777 (Table CLXXIII) Crowley redistributes these hour-genii across the zodiac, where this spirit falls at Scorpio (Nun).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

zaren.summary: Vengeance — the Nuctemeron genius of the sixth hour presiding over vengeance, set by Crowley at Virgo.
zaren.description: In the Nuctemeron — the “Day Illumined by Night” ascribed to Apollonius of Tyana and preserved by Éliphas Lévi — Zaren is numbered among the genii of the sixth hour, the spirit of vengeance. He is the avenger, the spirit of retribution and the requital of wrong. Crowley arranges the twelve hours and their genii upon the paths of the Tree (777, Table CLXXIII), placing him at Virgo (Yod).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

zarobi.summary: Precipices — the Nuctemeron genius of the third hour presiding over precipices, set by Crowley at Gemini.
zarobi.description: Among the genii of the third hour in the Nuctemeron of Apollonius of Tyana, Zarobi presides over precipices. He rules over cliffs, chasms and the danger of high and broken ground. Lévi gives the roll of the hour-genii in his Transcendental Magic; Crowley tabulates them along the paths of the Tree (Table CLXXIII), assigning Zarobi to Gemini (Zayin).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

zazer.summary: Angel of the first face of Aries, where the zodiac ignites and the naked Will seizes dominion.
zazer.description: Zazer is the first of the thirty-six Angels of the Decanates set by the Golden Dawn and tabulated by Crowley in 777, governing the opening ten degrees of Aries — the very threshold at which the wheel of the year strikes fire. This face is ruled by Mars within Mars' own sign, doubling the martial charge, and answers to the Two of Wands, *Dominion*: the bare spark of the Will asserting itself before any opposition can gather. Zazer is therefore the intelligence of beginnings that command rather than ask, the angelic pressure behind every act of pioneering self-assertion.

zebra.summary: The dual-striped horse of Gemini—black and white woven into one hide, the patterned duality of the Twins.
zebra.description: The zebra is attributed to Gemini, the dual sign of the Twins, and its very body declares the attribution: a wild horse barred all over in black and white, the two opposites not merely paired but interwoven into a single inseparable pattern. Where other Geminian creatures wear their duality as two halves, the zebra carries it as one fused design, an emblem of opposites so intermingled that they cannot be told apart. Swift, untamed, and dazzling in its stripes, it belongs to the airy, mercurial nature of the sign. Esoterically the zebra figures the perfect interweaving of light and dark, positive and negative, into a single living whole—duality not resolved by blending into grey but held vividly as alternating bands of one nature.

zeffar.summary: Irrevocable choice — the Nuctemeron genius of the ninth hour presiding over irrevocable choice, set by Crowley at Sagittarius.
zeffar.description: Among the genii of the ninth hour in the Nuctemeron of Apollonius of Tyana, Zeffar presides over irrevocable choice. His charge is the choice that cannot be unmade, the binding and final decision. Lévi gives the roll of the hour-genii in his Transcendental Magic; Crowley tabulates them along the paths of the Tree (Table CLXXIII), assigning Zeffar to Sagittarius (Samekh).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

zeirna.summary: Infirmities — the Nuctemeron genius of the fifth hour presiding over infirmities, set by Crowley at Leo.
zeirna.description: Among the genii of the fifth hour in the Nuctemeron of Apollonius of Tyana, Zeirna presides over infirmities. He rules over sickness and bodily weakness, the slow afflictions of the flesh. Lévi gives the roll of the hour-genii in his Transcendental Magic; Crowley tabulates them along the paths of the Tree (Table CLXXIII), assigning Zeirna to Leo (Teth).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

zelator.summary: 1°=10, the grade of Malkuth — the Zealous One; mastery of the element of Earth.
zelator.description: Zelator is the first true grade of the Golden Dawn and A∴A∴ above the Neophyte, attributed to Malkuth, the Kingdom. The 'zealous one' has gained a firm foothold in the material world and begins the work of the elements with Earth, learning steadiness, the disciplines of the body, and the foundations of practice. It is the ground floor of the Temple, where the long ascent of the Tree begins.

zend.summary: Zend — Crowley's reserved column in 777 for the Zoroastrian (Old Iranian) pantheon, left unfilled.
zend.description: 'Zend' is an older Western term for the Avestan / Zoroastrian tradition, taken from the Pahlavi 'Zand' (commentary on the Avesta). Crowley's reserved column under this heading in the pantheon tables (XXV-XXXII) was intended to receive the Iranian gods and angelic powers — Ahura Mazda, Ahriman, the Amesha Spentas (Vohu Manah, Asha Vahishta, Khshathra Vairya, Spenta Armaiti, Haurvatat, Ameretat), and the great Yazatas (Mithra, Anahita, Sraosha) — whose dualism strongly shaped both Hellenistic magic and the later Hermetic tradition. Crowley left the column blank; the entry preserves it as such.

zepar.summary: The sixteenth spirit of the Goetia, a duke of Virgo who joins lovers and renders women barren.
zepar.description: Zepar is the sixteenth spirit of the Goetia, a great duke of the decans of Virgo. His office is to make women love men and to bring them together in love, and also to make women barren. He appears in red apparel and armour, like a soldier. A spirit of the earthy sign, he governs the joining of lovers and the closing of the womb — the giving and withholding of fertility.

zeraph.summary: Presiding god of the third decan of Sagittarius, the same Saturnine face of over-strained ambition.
zeraph.description: Zeraph is the presiding god 777 attributes to the third decan of Sagittarius (20°–30°), the Saturnine face the names-column calls Chenen. Bearing the Ten of Wands—Oppression—it names the over-strained ambition at the end of the Archer's sign. It belongs to the Greco-Egyptian roster of thirty-six decan-rulers inherited by Western astrology.
tables: CLXXI. Egyptian Gods of the Zodiac (Cadent)

zeta.summary: Zeta — a letter of the Coptic alphabet (z), which Crowley attributes to the path of Zayin (Gemini).
zeta.description: Zeta is a letter of the Coptic alphabet — the script in which the Egyptian language was written in the Christian era, the Greek alphabet adapted to Egyptian speech. It is from Greek zeta. Crowley folds the Coptic alphabet into the great correspondence of letters and paths in 777 (Table LI), assigning Zeta to the path of Zayin (Gemini) on the Tree of Life, so that the Egyptian-Christian script takes its station among the Hebrew letters and the keys of the Tarot.
tables: LI. Names of the Coptic Letters

zeuda.summary: Presiding god of the first decan of Libra, the same lunar face of suspended balance.
zeuda.description: Zeuda is the presiding god 777 assigns to the first decan of Libra (0°–10°), the lunar face the names-column calls Serucuth. Bearing the Two of Swords—Peace—it marks the suspended balance at the opening of the scales. The name belongs to the Greco-Egyptian list of thirty-six decan-rulers underlying the Western faces.
tables: CLXVII. Egyptian Gods of the Zodiac (Asc. Decans)

zeus.summary: Jupiter—expansion, sovereignty, fortune, and mercy; ruler of Chesed and the path of Kaph.
zeus.description:
Jupiter is the planet of expansion, abundance, sovereignty, and benevolent order—the great fortune that enlarges and blesses. In 777 it rules the fourth Sephirah Chesed and the path of Kaph (the Tarot trump Fortune / the Wheel), governing kingship, law, generosity, and growth. Its metal is tin, its number four, its emblems the sceptre, the eagle, and royal blue and purple.

As Zeus–Jupiter–Marduk, the sky-father and king of the gods, this power presides over the just rule of the cosmos and the turning wheel of fortune. Its danger is excess—the expansion that becomes bloat or tyranny—but balanced by Martian severity it supplies the magnanimity and right rule that hold a world together.
sources: Crowley, Liber 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae

zira-a.summary: al-Dhira', 'the forearm' — the outstretched paws of the Lion, the lunar mansion in Gemini.
zira-a.description: al-Dhira', 'the forearm' or 'the paws' (the bright pair Castor and Pollux were read as the Lion's outstretched arm), is the mansion attributed in 777 to the path of Gemini (Zayin). The Arab tradition counted it a fortunate station for gain, for friendship, and for the increase of harvests — the reaching, grasping gesture answering well to the dexterity of the airy Twins.
tables: CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon

zizuph.summary: Mysteries — the Nuctemeron genius of the eighth hour presiding over mysteries, set by Crowley at Scorpio.
zizuph.description: Among the genii of the eighth hour in the Nuctemeron of Apollonius of Tyana, Zizuph presides over mysteries. His province is the hidden mysteries, the secrets veiled from the eyes of the profane. Lévi gives the roll of the hour-genii in his Transcendental Magic; Crowley tabulates them along the paths of the Tree (Table CLXXIII), assigning Zizuph to Scorpio (Nun).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

zodiac.summary: The Zodiac — the belt of the twelve signs, the sphere of the fixed stars, referred to Chokmah.
zodiac.description: The Zodiac is the band of twelve constellations through which the sun, moon, and planets appear to move, the great wheel of the heavens. Referred to Chokmah, the second Sephirah and the sphere of the fixed stars (the Mazloth), it represents the whole framework of celestial influence, the starry pattern that orders time and fate. As the totality of the signs it is the cosmic clock and the archetypal map of the soul's powers.

zophas.summary: Pentacles — the Nuctemeron genius of the eleventh hour presiding over pentacles, set by Crowley at Aquarius.
zophas.description: Zophas is the Nuctemeron genius of pentacles. That “Night-illumined Day”, ascribed to Apollonius of Tyana and handed down through Lévi's Transcendental Magic, sets a company of spirits over each of the twelve hours of the magical day, and Zophas belongs to the eleventh hour. His charge is the pentacles, the engraved talismans and figured seals of the art. In 777 (Table CLXXIII) Crowley redistributes these hour-genii across the zodiac, where this spirit falls at Aquarius (Tzaddi).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours

zubani.summary: al-Zubana, 'the claws' — the claws of the Scorpion that became the Scales, the lunar mansion in Libra.
zubani.description: al-Zubana, 'the claws' (anciently the claws of the Scorpion, before they were made the Balance), is the mansion set in the path of Libra (Lamed). The old astrologers held it an ill-omened, dividing station — good for separations, the undoing of enemies, and the redress of wrongs — fitting the keen weighing justice of the Scales.
tables: CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon

zubrah.summary: al-Zubra, 'the mane' — the haunch and mane of the Lion, the lunar mansion in Leo.
zubrah.description: al-Zubra, 'the mane' (the Lion's hindquarters and flowing mane), is the Mansion of the Moon in the path of Leo (Teth). Counted a fortunate, ascendant station — favourable for gain, for voyages, and for the bettering of one's estate — it carries the proud, radiant heat of high summer.
tables: CLXXIV. The Mansions of the Moon

zuphlas.summary: Forests — the Nuctemeron genius of the eleventh hour presiding over forests, set by Crowley at Aquarius.
zuphlas.description: Zuphlas is the Nuctemeron genius of forests. That “Night-illumined Day”, ascribed to Apollonius of Tyana and handed down through Lévi's Transcendental Magic, sets a company of spirits over each of the twelve hours of the magical day, and Zuphlas belongs to the eleventh hour. He rules the forests, the deep woods and their untamed life. In 777 (Table CLXXIII) Crowley redistributes these hour-genii across the zodiac, where this spirit falls at Aquarius (Tzaddi).
tables: CLXXIII. Genii of the Twelve Hours
